body: Consider a parametric model with parameter theta in an open subset of R^d, satisfying standard regularity (identifiability, smoothness, nonsingular Fisher information, true parameter interior to the space), and a null hypothesis restricting theta to a smooth submodel of codimension k. Let Lambda_n be the likelihood ratio: the supremum of the likelihood over the full model divided by its supremum over the null submodel, from n iid observations. Wilks' theorem states that under the null hypothesis, as n -> infinity, 2 log Lambda_n converges in distribution to a chi-squared distribution with k degrees of freedom, justifying the asymptotic chi-squared likelihood-ratio test. Due to Samuel S. Wilks.
title: Wilks' theorem

[Thm 6 (CLT for the normalized traces) of arXiv:2604.26499, 'Spectrum of Random Matrices with Exploding Moments'] Let $M$ be the matrix same as in Condition \ref{cond:matrixcond_1_NonHer} with $\alpha=1$. For any partition $\pi\in\bigcup_{k}\mathcal{P}(k)$, let $Z_N(T_\pi)$ be defined similar as in \eqref{eq:centered and normalized random variables Z_N} for matrix $M$.
Then the family
$
\big(Z_N(T_\pi)\big)_{\pi\in\bigcup_{k}\mathcal{P}(k)}
$
converges, as $N\to\infty$, to a centered Gaussian process
$\big(z(T_\pi)\big)_{\pi\in\bigcup_{k}\mathcal{P}(k)}$.
Moreover, for any two partitions $\pi_1,\pi_2$,
$$
\mathrm{Cov}\left(z(T_{\pi_1}),z(T_{\pi_2})\right)
=
\sum_{T\in\mathcal P^{\#}(T_{\pi_1},T_{\pi_2})}
\tau^{nh}[T],
$$
where $\mathcal{P}^{\#}(T_{\pi_1},T_{\pi_2})$ denotes the collection of graphs obtained by disjoint copies of the graphs $T_{\pi_1}$ and $T_{\pi_2}$ and gluing them with at least one common edge, and where $\tau^{nh}[T]$ is same as defined in the Theorem \ref{thm:Convergence of normalized trace for non-Hermitian matrices with independent exploding entries}.

[Lemma thm:stochastic_convergence of arXiv:2608.12056, 'Deviation inequalities for U-processes of growing order, with applications to half-space d'] Let $\mathcal{S}^d_q = \{x \in \mathbb R^d: \|x\| \leq q\}$ and $\mathcal{S}^{d-1} = \{x \in \mathbb R^d : \|x\| = 1\}$ be two sets, and denote $\bar{\mathcal{S}} = \mathcal{S}^{d-1} \times \mathcal{S}^d_q$. Under the assumptions of the theorem, the process 
\[
(u,z) \mapsto \sqrt{\frac{N}{m}} U_{N,m}\left(u,z\right)
\]
defined on $\bar{\mathcal{S}}$ converges weakly to $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{\left\lvert \dotp{z}{u}\right\rvert^2}{2}}\dotp{W}{u}$ where $W$ is a $d$-dimensional standard Gaussian vector. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Definition of arXiv:2412.02777, 'How to quantify the coherence of a set of beliefs'] A credence base $(\mathtt E, \boldsymbol q)$ is \textit{coherent} if there exists a probability distribution $\pi:2^\Omega\rightarrow [0, 1]$ where $\pi(E_i)=q_i$ for all $i\in\left\{1,\dots, n\right\}$. We also call $\boldsymbol q$ \textit{coherent} with respect to $\mathtt E$ if $(\mathtt E, \boldsymbol q)$ is coherent.

[Prop smash-well-based of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $G$ be a compact Lie group and let ${\mathcal{F}}_1,{\mathcal{F}}_2$ be two families of closed subgroups of $G$. If $X$ is ${\mathcal{F}}_1$-cofibrant, then $X\smashp-$ sends $({\mathcal{F}}_1\cap{\mathcal{F}}_2)$-weak equivalences between well-based $G$-spaces to ${\mathcal{F}}_2$-weak equivalences.
    \begin{proof}
       Let $f\colon Y\to Y'$ be an $({\mathcal{F}}_1\cap{\mathcal{F}}_2)$-weak equivalence of well-based $G$-spaces. We note that $(X\smashp f)^H$ agrees up to homeomorphism with $X^H\smashp f^H$ for any $H\subset G$. If $H\in{\mathcal{F}}_2\smallsetminus{\mathcal{F}}_1$, then $X^H=0$, so that $(X\smashp f)^H$ is a homeomorphism; on the other hand, if $H\in{\mathcal{F}}_1\cap{\mathcal{F}}_2$, then $X^H\smashp f^H$ is a weak equivalence as $f^H$ is a weak equivalence of well-based spaces and $X^H$ is well-based.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop smash-well-based of arXiv:2608.28504

[Theorem loiexpo of arXiv:2607.00753, 'Threatening excursions in large population\\ quasi-stationary birth and death systems.\\ O'] Let $A$ be an open subset of $\mathds R_{+}^{d}$ satisfying Assumption ${\bf (HS)}$.
For any $t\ge0$
$$
\lim_{K\to\infty}{{\mathds P}}^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}_{\nu_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}}\big(T^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}_{A}>t\, M_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(A)\, \eta_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(A)\big)=e^{-t}\;.
$$
In other words, the sequence  $\Big(\frac{T^{({\scriptscriptstyle K})}_{A}}{ M_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(A)\, \eta_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}(A)}\Big)$ issued from $\nu_{{\scriptscriptstyle K}}$ converges in law to the exponential law of parameter $1$, as $K$ tends to infinity.
title: Theorem loiexpo of arXiv:2607.00753

[Lemma l.list of arXiv:2411.12003, 'Central Limit Theorem for non-stationary random products of $\SL(2, \R)$ matrices'] Let the sequence $(\rho_n,\delta_n)_{n\ge n_0}$, \emr{where $n_0$ is given by Lemma~(l:var-lower of the paper)},
    be chosen in such a way that the following conditions hold:
    \begin{itemize}
        \item As $n\to\infty$, one has
        $  \rho_n\to \infty$ and  $\delta_n\to 0$.
        \item For some $n_1\ge 2n_0$, we have
        \[
        \rho_n=\rho'_0, \quad \delta_n= 3 \overline{C}^{\textcolor{black}{2+{\varepsilon}}} \quad \text{for all}\quad n=n_0,\dots,n_1,
        \]
        where $\overline{C}$ is given by Corollary~(c.3 of the paper),
        \[
            \rho'_0=\min \left(\rho_0, \frac{1}{20\overline{C}} \right)
        \]
        and $\rho_0$ is given by Lemma~(lm:Start of the paper).
        \item For every $m>2n_0$, taking $n=\lfloor\frac{m}{2}\rfloor$ and $n'=m-n$,
        one has
        
            \begin{gather}
                
                
                 \rho_{m} \le L \min(\rho_n, \rho_{n'}),
                \\
                
                \rho_m^{\textcolor{black}{2+{\varepsilon}}} \delta_m \le \frac{1}{100},
                
                \\
                 \left( \lambda \max(\delta_{n}, \delta_{n'}) + 2 \,\frac{K e^{\frac{\rho_{m}^2}{2}}}{m^{\textcolor{black}{{\varepsilon}/2}}} \right) \le \delta_{m},
            \end{gather}
            where constants $L$ and $\lambda$ are defined by the conclusion of Lemma~(lm:Contr of the paper) for $C=2\left(\frac{C_{\sigma}}{C_1}\right)^2$, where $C_1$ is given by Lemma~(l:var-lower of the paper), and $C_{\sigma}$ is given by~(equation eq:C-2 of the paper).
            
    \end{itemize}
    Then the conclusion of Proposition~(p.boot of the paper) holds for this sequence.

body:
[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2603.28226, '2603.28226'] Let \(f\ge0\) belong to \(L^1(\mathcal F_\infty)\), let \(\lambda>0\), and let
\(\theta\ge0\). Retain the notation of Section~\ref{sec:proof} and
\eqref{eq:s-theta}; thus
\[
r:=\inf\{n\ge1:\ f_n>\lambda\},
\qquad
\varepsilon_n:=d f_n\,\mathbf1_{\{r=n\}},
\qquad
\gamma_n:=d f_n\,\mathbf1_{\{r>n\}},
\]
\[
\Lambda_0:=0,
\qquad
\Lambda_m:=\sum_{k=1}^{m}\mathbb E_k[\varepsilon_{k+1}],
\qquad
s_\theta:=\inf\{m\ge1:\ \Lambda_m>\theta\lambda\},
\qquad
t_\theta:=r\wedge s_\theta.
\]
Also set
\[
r^-:=r-1 \ \text{on }\{r<\infty\},
\qquad
r^-:=\infty \ \text{on }\{r=\infty\}.
\]

Define
\[
g_\theta:=f-f_{t_\theta},
\]
\[
h_{\theta,n}:=
\sum_{j=1}^{n}
\bigl(\varepsilon_j-\mathbb E_{j-1}[\varepsilon_j]\bigr)\mathbf1_{\{s_\theta\ge j\}},
\qquad n\ge1,
\]
\[
k_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{st}}
:=
\sum_{j=1}^{n}\gamma_j\,\mathbf1_{\{s_\theta\ge j\}},
\qquad
k_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{pr}}
:=
\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathbb E_{j-1}[\varepsilon_j]\mathbf1_{\{s_\theta\ge j\}},
\qquad n\ge1.
\]
Then \(h_{\theta,n}\) converges almost surely and in \(L^1\) to a limit
\(h_\theta\in L^1(\mathcal F_\infty)\), and the sequences
\[
k_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{st}},
\qquad
k_{\theta,n}^{\mathrm{pr}}
\]
converge almost surely and in \(L^1\) to limits
\[
k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}},
\qquad
k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}
\in L^1(\mathcal F_\infty).
\]
Moreover,
\[
f=g_\theta+h_\theta+k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}+k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}.
\]

\medskip
\noindent\textup{(a)}
\[
\mathbb P\Bigl(\sup_{n\ge1}|\mathbb E_n[g_\theta]|>0\Bigr)
\le \frac{\|f\|_1}{\lambda},
\qquad
\|g_\theta\|_1\le 2\|f\|_1.
\]

\noindent\textup{(b)}
\[
\Bigl\|\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}
\bigl|\mathbb E_n[h_\theta]-\mathbb E_{n-1}[h_\theta]\bigr|
\Bigr\|_1
\le 2\|f\|_1.
\]
In particular,
\[
\|h_\theta\|_1\le 2\|f\|_1.
\]

\noindent\textup{(c)}
\[
k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}=f_{s_\theta\wedge r^-},
\qquad
0\le k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}\le \lambda
\quad\text{a.s.}
\]

\noindent\textup{(d)}
\[
k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}
=
\Lambda_{s_\theta-1}\,\mathbf1_{\{s_\theta<\infty\}}
+
\Bigl(\sup_{m\ge1}\Lambda_m\Bigr)\mathbf1_{\{s_\theta=\infty\}},
\qquad
0\le k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}\le \theta\lambda
\quad\text{a.s.}
\]

\noindent\textup{(e)}
\[
\mathbb E[h_\theta]=\mathbb E[\varepsilon_1],
\]
\[
\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}\|_1+\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}\|_1
=
\|f\|_1-\mathbb E[\varepsilon_1]
\le \|f\|_1,
\]
\[
\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}\|_2^2
\le \lambda\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}\|_1,
\qquad
\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}\|_2^2
\le \theta\lambda\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}\|_1,
\]
and
\[
\|k_\theta^{\mathrm{st}}+k_\theta^{\mathrm{pr}}\|_2^2
\le (1+\theta)\lambda\|f\|_1.
\]

body: Load-bearing hypothesis: finite speed of propagation and the domain-of-dependence cone are properties of the wave equation (and of symmetric hyperbolic systems), proved by a local energy identity on the cone. The Schrödinger equation has no such identity and propagates instantaneously. Concrete counterexample: let f ∈ L¹(R^n) be nonzero and compactly supported and let t ≠ 0. By the kernel formula, e^{itΔ}f(x) = (4πit)^{−n/2} e^{i|x|²/(4t)} · G(x/(2t)) where G is the Fourier transform of the compactly supported integrable function y ↦ e^{i|y|²/(4t)}f(y). By the Paley–Wiener theorem G extends to an entire function on C^n, and it is not identically zero, so its zero set contains no nonempty open set. Hence e^{itΔ}f is nonzero almost everywhere on every open subset of R^n at every t ≠ 0: compactly supported data instantly become globally supported. The same phenomenon rules out any cone-shaped domain of dependence, and the heat equation behaves the same way. What survives for Schrödinger are local smoothing, dispersive decay and (pseudo)locality statements about wave packets moving at velocity ≈ 2ξ, not a finite propagation speed; the wave equation's finite-speed argument must never be transplanted to a dispersive or parabolic equation.
title: Pitfall: Finite Speed of Propagation Is Hyperbolic, Not Dispersive — It Fails for Schrödinger

body: [Lemma 2.8 (Borel–Cantelli) of arXiv:2512.05720, 'First-passage percolation, non-positive curvature, and radial maps'] Let $(A_{n})_{n\geq 1}$ be a sequence of events in a probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$. (1) If $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\mathbb{P}(A_{n})<\infty$, then $\mathbb{P}\bigl(A_{n}\text{ i.o.}\bigr)=\mathbb{P}\Bigl(\limsup_{n\to\infty}A_{n}\Bigr)=0.$ (2) If the events $(A_{n})$ are independent and $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\mathbb{P}(A_{n})=\infty$, then $\mathbb{P}\bigl(A_{n}\text{ i.o.}\bigr)=1.$

[Proposition BTP of arXiv:2608.30747, 'Compact homogeneous complex manifolds'] If a Hermitian C-space is BTP, then the following conditions hold for any $\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta\in\Delta_\qg^+$:
\begin{enumerate}[{\rm (i)}] 
\item $x_{\alpha+\beta}=x_\alpha$ or $\tfrac{1}{x_\beta}A_\beta = \tfrac{1}{x_{\alpha+\beta}}A_{\alpha+\beta}$.  

\item $x_{\alpha+\beta}=x_\alpha+x_\beta$ or 
$
\tfrac{1}{x_\alpha}A_\alpha+ \tfrac{1}{x_\beta}A_\beta=\tfrac{1}{x_{\alpha+\beta}} A_{\alpha+\beta}.
$   
\item If $\alpha-\beta\notin\Delta_\qg^-$, then either $x_{\alpha+\beta}=x_\alpha+x_\beta$ or $x_{\alpha+\beta}=x_\alpha$. 

\item If $\alpha-\beta\notin\Delta_\qg^+$, then either $x_{\alpha+\beta}=x_\alpha+x_\beta$ or $x_{\alpha+\beta}=x_\beta$. 

\item If $\gamma, \alpha+\beta+\gamma \in \Delta_\qg^+$ and $\alpha+\gamma, \beta+\gamma \notin \Delta_\qg$, then $x_{\alpha+\beta} =x_{\alpha} + x_\beta$ or $x_{\alpha+\beta+\gamma}=x_\gamma$.  

\item If $\gamma, \beta+\gamma, \alpha+\beta+\gamma \in \Delta_\qg^+$ and $\alpha+\gamma \notin \Delta_\qg$, then 
\begin{align*}
\tfrac{1}{x_{\beta+\gamma}} & N_{\beta,\gamma} N_{\alpha, \beta+\gamma} (x_{\beta+\gamma} -x_\beta - x_\gamma)(x_{\alpha+\beta+\gamma} - x_{\alpha})\\
=& \tfrac{1}{x_{\alpha+\beta}} N_{\alpha, \beta} N_{\alpha+\beta, \gamma}(x_{\alpha+\beta}- x_\alpha)(x_{\alpha+\beta+\gamma} - x_{\alpha+\beta} - x_\gamma).  
\end{align*}
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

In two dimensions, it is equivalent to the divergence theorem.

[Proposition 9 (Weak stability of positive \(L^2\) Stein kernels) of arXiv:2608.27657, '\bfseries Stein Kernels and Normal Approximation\\ for Log-Concave Bilinear Forms'] Let \(\mu_k\Rightarrow\mu\) weakly on \(\R^n\), where each \(\mu_k\)
is centered and has finite second moments.  Let \(Y_k\sim\mu_k\), and
suppose that \(\mu_k\) admits a symmetric positive-semidefinite Stein
kernel \(\tau_k\) such that
\begin{equation}
  L:=\sup_k\E\|\tau_k(Y_k)\|_{\HS}^2<\infty.
  \tag{4.2}
\end{equation}
Then \(\mu\) is centered, \(\mu_k\to\mu\) in \(W_2\), and \(\mu\)
admits a symmetric positive-semidefinite Stein kernel \(\tau\) satisfying
\begin{equation}
  \E\tau(Y)=\Cov(Y),
  \qquad
  \E\|\tau(Y)\|_{\HS}^2
  \leq
  \liminf_{k\to\infty}\E\|\tau_k(Y_k)\|_{\HS}^2,
  \tag{4.3}
\end{equation}
where \(Y\sim\mu\).  The same kernel may be chosen with the following
additional permanence properties.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item
If \(F:\mathsf S_n\to[0,\infty]\) is convex and lower semicontinuous and
\(\sup_k\E F(\tau_k(Y_k))\leq C_F\), then
\[
  \E F(\tau(Y))\leq C_F.
\]

\item
If, for every \(A\in\mathsf S_n\),
\[
  \Var\!\left(\Tr(A\tau_k(Y_k))\right)
  \leq C_{\rm tr}\Tr(A^2),
\]
then
\begin{equation}
  \Var\!\left(\Tr(A\tau(Y))\right)
  \leq C_{\rm tr}\Tr(A^2)
  \qquad(A\in\mathsf S_n).
  \tag{4.4}
\end{equation}

\item
If, for every \(A\in\mathsf S_n\),
\[
  \E\Tr(A\tau_k(Y_k)A\tau_k(Y_k))
  \leq C_{\rm en}\Tr(A^2),
\]
then
\begin{equation}
  \E\Tr(A\tau(Y)A\tau(Y))
  \leq C_{\rm en}\Tr(A^2)
  \qquad(A\in\mathsf S_n).
  \tag{4.5}
\end{equation}

\item
If a constant \(C_{\rm wp}\) satisfies
\[
  \Var_{\mu_k}g
  \leq
  C_{\rm wp}\,
  \E\langle
    \tau_k(Y_k)\nabla g(Y_k),\nabla g(Y_k)
  \rangle
\]
for every \(k\) and every \(g\in C_c^\infty(\R^n)\), then
\begin{equation}
  \Var_\mu g
  \leq
  C_{\rm wp}\,
  \E\langle
    \tau(Y)\nabla g(Y),\nabla g(Y)
  \rangle
  \qquad(g\in C_c^\infty(\R^n)).
  \tag{4.6}
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Lemma long-range-percolation-coupling of arXiv:2608.00399, 'The Heavy-tailed Frog Model'] Let $d\ge1$, $\alpha \in (0, d)$, and $Q \in \mathcal{H}_{\alpha, K}$. 
    Fix $r \in \mathbb N^+$ and $\lambda > 0$. 
    Then, $\{ Y_{(u, v)}^{[L]} \}_{u \neq v}$ are mutually independent for each $L \ge r$.
    Moreover, there exist $\beta_1$ with $\beta_1 \to \infty$ as $r \to \infty$,
    such that, for any $L \ge r$ and any distinct $u, v \in \mathbb{T}^{[L]}$, we have
    \begin{align} 
        \mathbb P_{L}\left(Y_{(u, v)}^{[L]} = 1\right) \ge 1 - \exp\left(- \beta_1 |u - v|^{-s}\right),
    \end{align}
    where $|u - v|$ denotes the $\ell_\infty$-distance between $u$ and $v$ on $\mathbb{T}^{[L]}$ and $s := \alpha + d$.
title: Lemma long-range-percolation-coupling of arXiv:2608.00399

body:
Let T be a MINIMAL homeomorphism of a compact metric space X and let f be a continuous real function on X. Then the following are equivalent: (i) the Birkhoff sums S_n f(x) = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f(T^k x) are uniformly bounded in n for SOME point x; (ii) the Birkhoff sums are uniformly bounded in n and in x; (iii) f is a continuous coboundary, that is f = g composed with T minus g for some continuous g on X. In particular a cohomological equation with continuous data is solvable continuously precisely when its Birkhoff sums stay bounded at a single point - a striking upgrade from one orbit to the whole space, which is where minimality is used.
MINIMALITY of T and CONTINUITY of f.
Without minimality the equivalence fails;
with merely measurable data the corresponding statement is the Gottschalk-Hedlund analogue for measurable coboundaries and is different.

[Definition 31 of arXiv:2608.26628, 'Open Problems in Mathematical Logic'] We say a subgroup $G\leq S_\infty$ is \emph{finitely periodic} if 
    $\forall g\in G\setminus \{1\}$, $\langle g\rangle_{S_\infty}$ only has finitely many finite orbits.
    
    Similarly, we say a group $G\leq S_\infty$ is \emph{maximal finitely periodic} if for every proper extension $G\lneq G'\leq S_\infty$, $G'$ is not finitely periodic.

[Lemma 4 of arXiv:2607.25645, 'Estimates of the total variation distance between laws of Sobolev mappings on Gaussian spa'] Let $k\in\mathbb N$, let $p>2k-1$, and set
\[
q:=\frac{p}{p-2k+1}.
\]
Let $f=(f_1,\ldots,f_k)$ with $f_j\in W^{2,p}(\gamma)$ and
\[
\max_{1\le j\le k}\|f_j\|_{\dot{W}^{2,p}(\gamma)}\le b.
\]
Let $g\in W^{1,q}(\gamma)\cap L^\infty(\gamma)$, and let
$\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_k)\in\mathbb R^k$ satisfy $|\theta|=1$.
Then for every $\varepsilon>0$,
\[
\biggl|
\int_E \sum_{i,j=1}^k \theta_i (A_f)_{i,j}
\langle \nabla f_j,\nabla g\rangle_{H(\gamma)}
\Delta_f^{-1}\Phi_\varepsilon(\Delta_f)\,d\gamma
\biggr|
\le
32\bigl(\|\Phi'\|_\infty+2\bigr)k\|g\|_\infty b^{2k-1}
\bigl(h_{\gamma,q}(\Delta_f,\varepsilon)\bigr)^{1/q}.
\]

For m>=5 and q>=2, the arc-transitive graph C_m[empty_q] has mq vertices and degree 2q. Its mean hitting time from a target twin is mq, and from fiber j!=0 is j(m-j)+m(q-1). Its maximal commute time is 2 floor(m^2/4)+2m(q-1), its stationary mean hitting time is (m^2-1)/6+m(q-1), and its rate-one continuous-time relaxation time is 1/(1-cos(2*pi/m)). For fixed q their maximal-commute to twice stationary-hitting ratio tends to 3/2.
All hypotheses and scope restrictions in the statement apply.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:56fbe937b985212af54cac95ba016b633852bb232153be8e6b5b88a4ddec8c1f","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/56/56fbe937b985212af54cac95ba016b633852bb232153be8e6b5b88a4ddec8c1f.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:b6fe48a3609acff7cac38e87905ed070074475fda2593538887a0990dfc80d57","bundle_entry_key":"q-fold-cycle-hitting-times-and-relaxation","bundle_id":"population.w336-p0208-checked-attempt-20261010","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"w336/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.markov-chains:q-fold-cycle-hitting-times-and-relaxation","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# P0208: exact q-fold cycle calculation

Status: proof written by w336, independent KEEP pending. This extends the recorded q=2 campaign counterexample; it is not a new literature priority claim. The source's tau_star is a maximal commute time, not a maximal one-way hitting time. Relaxation here uses the rate-one continuous-time generator P-I.

Let m>=5, q>=2 and G=C_m[empty_q]. Its vertices are (i,a), with i modulo m and 1<=a<=q; two vertices are adjacent precisely when their first coordinates differ by one modulo m. G is simple, connected, 2q-regular, has n=mq vertices, and is not a cycle. Rotations, reflection of C_m and independent permutations inside each fiber act transitively on directed edges, so G is arc-transitive.

Fix target (0,1). Let a be the mean hitting time from a different vertex in fiber 0. Every visit to fiber 0 from elsewhere chooses a uniformly distributed vertex. If h_j is the mean from fiber j!=0, the quotient cycle's hitting-time equation gives

    h_j = j(m-j) + ((q-1)/q)a.

The identity j(m-j)=1+[(j-1)(m-j+1)+(j+1)(m-j-1)]/2 verifies that equation away from 0. From a twin of the target, a=1+h_1=m+((q-1)/q)a, so a=mq and h_j=j(m-j)+m(q-1). These values solve all first-step equations. A finite connected chain hits the target with finite mean, so uniqueness of the killed-chain linear system identifies them with the actual hitting times.

The graph automorphisms exchange any two vertices of a specified fiber separation, so hitting times are symmetric. For m>=5, floor(m^2/4)>m, hence the largest one-way hitting time is floor(m^2/4)+m(q-1), larger than the twin value mq. Consequently

    tau_star = 2 floor(m^2/4) + 2m(q-1),
    tau_0 = (m^2-1)/6 + m(q-1).

The second formula is the stationary mean hitting time of the fixed target, including its zero self-hitting time: sum_{j=1}^{m-1}j(m-j)=m(m^2-1)/6, and the remaining constant terms sum to m(q-1). A neighbor has mean hitting time m-1+m(q-1)=n-1.

P equals (A(C_m)/2) tensor (J_q/q). The fiber-constant subspace has eigenvalues cos(2*pi*k/m), 0<=k<m; its orthogonal complement has m(q-1) zero eigenvalues. Since cos(2*pi/m)>0 for m>=5, tau_2=1/(1-cos(2*pi/m)). This is the continuous-time relaxation time; for even m the non-lazy discrete-time absolute spectral gap vanishes, which is a different parameter.

For each fixed q>=2 and m tending to infinity,

    tau_star/n^2 -> 1/(2q^2),
    tau_2/n^2 -> 1/(2*pi^2*q^2),
    tau_star/(2*tau_0) -> 3/2.

Thus the same family refutes the three bounds recorded for Aldous-Fill Problem 7.27: O(n log n), O(n), and ratio 1+o(1). This statement relies on the cached problem's parameter definitions and does not establish whether the refutation was previously published.

Checks: scripts/check_p0208.py solves the full hitting-time systems, compares the full transition spectrum, checks the directed-edge orbit, and tests the stationary sum and neighbor identity. The proof covers all m>=5 and q>=2; finite checks supply validation, not the universal argument.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:6611f602491569522b255cbc2e27d93831a536afc7f6c21d6d129583b5b3eb06","revision_digest":"sha256:405c3edbd080e4ab09c7c9d7631f325297537e779f9158172ed4d856392c4891","source_id":"owner:campaign:w336:P0208:q-fold-cycle-hitting-times-and-relaxation","source_revision":"author-proof-2026-10-10; independent audit w346 pending","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

Method: Maximal stationary antivoter variance structural calculation Result: On the complete graph all distinct-pair correlations equal c. At stationarity, the generator applied to eta_i*eta_j gives c=-(1+(n-2)c)/(n-1), hence c=-1/(2n-3). Therefore Var(S)=n+n(n-1)c=n(n-2)/(2n-3). The general source inequality Var(S)<n/2 has the same leading term but leaves the exact gap n/[2(2n-3)]. Check: The correlation equation can also be obtained by conditioning on which member of the pair updates and whether it samples its partner. Each route gives the same c. In particular merely proving Var(S)<=n/2 cannot resolve the proposed finite-n optimizer. Obstruction: A sharp bound on the return-parity expression for the meeting chain, or on averaged spin correlations, is missing. Pairwise correlations need not all be bounded by the complete-graph value.

[Lemma 32 of arXiv:2608.12804, 'Scaling Limits for Ising Models on Inhomogeneous Random Graphs and Applications'] Let
\(
    K,K':[0,1]^2\rightarrow\mathbb R
\)
be symmetric, Riemann-integrable kernels, and suppose that
$\{\sigma_i\}_{i\geq1}$ and $\{\tau_i\}_{i\geq1}$ are two independent
sequences of i.i.d. Rademacher random variables. Let
$\{\lambda_r(K)\}_{r\geq1}$ and
$\{\lambda_r(K')\}_{r\geq1}$ denote the nonzero eigenvalues of
$T_K$ and $T_{K'}$, respectively, repeated according to
multiplicity. Then, we have:
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\displaystyle
\frac{1}{2N}
\sum_{1\leq i\neq j\leq N}
K\left(\frac{i}{N},\frac{j}{N}\right)
\bigl(\sigma_i\sigma_j+\tau_i\tau_j\bigr)
\\[4mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{1}{2N}
\sum_{1\leq i\neq j\leq N}
K'\left(\frac{i}{N},\frac{j}{N}\right)
\sigma_i\tau_i\sigma_j\tau_j
\end{pmatrix}
\xrightarrow{d}
\begin{pmatrix}
\displaystyle
\frac12\sum_{r=1}^{\infty}
\lambda_r(K)(X_r^2-1)
+
\frac12\sum_{r=1}^{\infty}
\lambda_r(K)(Y_r^2-1)
\\[4mm]
\displaystyle
\frac12\sum_{r=1}^{\infty}
\lambda_r(K')(Z_r^2-1)
\end{pmatrix},
\]
where
$\{X_r\}_{r\geq1}$,
$\{Y_r\}_{r\geq1}$, and
$\{Z_r\}_{r\geq1}$ are mutually independent sequences of
i.i.d. standard Gaussian random variables.
All three infinite series appearing in the distributional limit converge in $L^2$ and almost surely.

body:
[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2609.03669, 'Volterra Integral Reduction \\ for Boundary Diffusion Problems'] Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:smooth}--\ref{ass:func} and~\ref{ass:potential}, 
for each fixed $y$, the function $t \mapsto \partial_x f(t,y^+)$ 
is the unique solution in $C[0,T]$ of the following Volterra integral 
equation of the second kind with a continuous kernel
\begin{equation}
\alpha(t,y)\,\partial_x f(t,y^+)
=
G(t,y)
+
\int_0^t
\gamma_1(t-s,y)\,k(t,s)\,
\partial_x f(s,y^+)\,ds.
\end{equation}
Here,
\begin{equation}
G(t,y)
=
\partial_x g(t,y)
+
\frac{\beta(\psi(y))}{\sigma(y)}
\big(g(t,y)-f(t,y)\big),
\qquad
\gamma_1(\tau,y)
=
r_0(\tau,y,y)
+
\frac{\beta(\psi(y))}{\sigma(y)}
r_1(\tau,y,y),
\end{equation}
where $r_1(\tau,y,y)$ and $r_0(\tau,y,y)$ are continuous functions exhibiting $O_K(\tau^{1/2})$ behavior uniformly for $y$ in compact sets.

body:
[Definition def-adm of arXiv:2603.17861, 'Gaussian concentration, integral probability metrics, and coupling functionals\\ for infin'] A probability measure $\mu$ on $(\Omega,\mathfrak{F})$ is said to be asymptotically
decoupled if there exist $g:\mathds N\to\mathds N$ and $c:\mathds N\to [0,\infty)$ such that
$\lim_{n\to\infty}g(n)/n=0$, $\lim_{n\to\infty} c(n)/|\ensuremath{\Lambda}_n|=0$, and
\[
\forall j\in\mathds Z^d,\ \forall n\in\mathds N,\ \forall A\in\mathfrak{F}_{\ensuremath{\Lambda}_n+j},\ 
\forall B\in \mathfrak{F}_{(\ensuremath{\Lambda}_n+g(n)+j)^{\mathrm{c}}},
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
\e^{-c(n)}\mu(A) \mu(B)\leq \mu(A\cap B)\leq \e^{c(n)}\mu(A) \mu(B).
\end{equation}
If only the upper bound holds, one says that $\mu$ is asymptotically
decoupled from above.
title: Asymptotically decoupled measure

body:
[Thm equiv-flatness of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] If $X$ is a flat orthogonal $G$-spectrum, then the functor $X\smashp{-}\colon\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}\to\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}$ preserves $G$-equivariant weak equivalences. Moreover, for \emph{any} orthogonal $G$-spectrum $Y$ the functor ${-}\smashp Y$ preserves $G$-equivariant weak equivalences between flat orthogonal $G$-spectra.
    \begin{proof}
        For a published account of the first statement see [schwede2018global]*{Theorem 3.5.10}. For the second statement, we let $X_1\to X_2$ be any $G$-equivariant weak equivalence between flat orthogonal $G$-spectra and we pick a cofibrant replacement $Y'\to Y$. Then all maps in the induced square 
        \[
            \begin{tikzcd}
                X_1\smashp Y'\arrow[r]\arrow[d] & X_2\smashp Y'\arrow[d]\\
                X_1\smashp Y\arrow[r] & X_2\smashp Y
            \end{tikzcd}
        \]
        except possibly the bottom one are $G$-equivariant weak equivalences by the first part; thus, also the bottom map is a $G$-equivariant weak equivalence by 2-out-of-3.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Stolz

[Lemma l:brownian-properties of arXiv:2607.24640, 'The Yang-Mills measure on surfaces via Morse theory'] Let $\gamma$ be an admissible curve and $\psi\in L^\infty(\Sigma)$. One has that $\widetilde{\mathfrak{W}}_{\psi,\gamma}(0)=0$ almost surely and, for every $1\leq \ell\leq L$ and for every $0\leq s\leq t\leq 1$, $\widetilde{W}_{\psi,\gamma,\ell}(t)-\widetilde{W}_{\psi,\gamma,\ell}(s)$ follows a centered normal law with variance $\|\psi[\blacktriangle(\gamma_{[s,t]})]\|_{L^2_\upsilon(\Sigma)}^2$. 

If, in addition, $\gamma$ is primitive with respect to $V$, then, for every $p\geq 1$ and for every $0=t_0<t_1<t_2 <\ldots<t_p\leq 1$, $\widetilde{W}_{\psi,\gamma,\ell}(t_1)$, $\widetilde{W}_{\psi,\gamma,\ell}(t_2)-\widetilde{W}_{\psi,\gamma,\ell}(t_1)$,$\ldots$, $\widetilde{W}_{\psi,\gamma,\ell}(t_p)-\widetilde{W}_{\psi,\gamma,\ell}(t_{p-1})$ are independent. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma l:brownian-properties of arXiv:2607.24640

[Thm thm_meet_parity of arXiv:2608.29914, 'Fixed points in abstract provability structures'] Let $S$ be a meet APS satisfying \textup{(C3*)}, and let $\triangle v$ be a
one-variable APS term in the original language.
Then the following statements hold:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If $d(\triangle)$ is even, then $\mathsf{E}_S(\triangle)$ holds.

    \item If $d(\triangle)$ is odd, then
    $\mathsf{E}_S(\triangle) \iff \mathsf{E}_S(\boxtimes)$.
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 8 (Error bound for the realised volatility classifier) of arXiv:2609.00402, '2609.00402'] Suppose Assumption~\ref{ass:volatility} holds. Fix \(\alpha_V\in(0,1)\), define \(a_{V,\alpha_V}=U^2\sqrt{n\log(1/\alpha_V)/2}\), and set \(\lambda_{V,\alpha_V}=n\nu_0+a_{V,\alpha_V}\). Then the exact classifier \(h_{V,\lambda_{V,\alpha_V}}(\bm X)=\mathbb I\{V(\bm X)>\lambda_{V,\alpha_V}\}\) satisfies \(\mathbb P\{h_{V,\lambda_{V,\alpha_V}}(\bm X)=1\mid Y=0\}\leq\alpha_V\) and
\[
\mathbb P\{h_{V,\lambda_{V,\alpha_V}}(\bm X)=0\mid Y=1\}
\leq
\exp\left\{-\frac{2(n\kappa_V-a_{V,\alpha_V})_+^2}{nU^4}\right\}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{err}(h_{V,\lambda_{V,\alpha_V}})
\leq\pi_0\alpha_V+
\pi_1\exp\left\{-\frac{2(n\kappa_V-a_{V,\alpha_V})_+^2}{nU^4}\right\}.
\]

Now fix \(M>0\) and \(\epsilon_V>0\), and suppose that \(\sup_{\bm x\in\mathcal X_M}\lvert f_{\epsilon_V,M}^{RV}(\bm x)-V(\bm x)\rvert\leq\epsilon_V\). Define the clipped neural classifier $\overline h_V(\bm X)=\mathbb I\left\{f_{\epsilon_V,M}^{RV}(\operatorname{clip}_M(\bm X))>\lambda_{V,\alpha_V}+\epsilon_V\right\}.$ Then
\[
\operatorname{err}(\overline h_V)
\leq\pi_0\{\alpha_V+\tau_0(M)\}
+\pi_1\left[\exp\left\{-\frac{2(n\kappa_V-a_{V,\alpha_V}-2\epsilon_V)_+^2}{nU^4}\right\}+\tau_1(M)\right]
=:\mathfrak B_V(\alpha_V,\epsilon_V,M).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Error bound for the realised volatility classifier

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] There is an absolute constant $c>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large
$h$,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\left\{|hA|:A\subset\mathbb Z,\ |A|=4,
 \ \operatorname{ndiam} A<\frac{13}{20}h^2\right\}\right|\geq ch^3.
\end{equation}
More locally,
\begin{equation}
 \left|\mathcal R(h,4)\cap
 \left[\binom{h+3}{3}-\frac{h^3}{250},
       \binom{h+3}{3}-\frac{h^3}{400}\right]\right|\geq ch^3,
\end{equation}
where the endpoints may be rounded to integers.  Consequently
\[
 \boxed{|\mathcal R(h,4)|=\Theta(h^3)},
 \qquad
 \liminf_{h\to\infty}
 \frac{|\mathcal R(h,4)|}{|[3h+1,\binom{h+3}{3}]\cap\mathbb Z|}>0.
\]
The values counted in (equation eq:localmain of the paper) may be chosen with primitive
representatives having two independent homogeneous relations of degree at
most $h$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Positive-density four-point spectrum

\[
\int_{\mathbb R^n}\Delta_{\hat f}\,d\mu=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad

[Proposition prop:rectobs of arXiv:2608.28007, 'Exact Risk Ratios for Weighted Data Selection in Linear Regression'] In $\mathbb{R}^4$ let
\[
\begin{aligned}
&a_1=e_1,\quad a_2=e_2,\quad a_3=-e_1-e_2,\qquad
b_1=e_3,\quad b_2=e_4,\quad b_3=-e_3-e_4,\\
&h_1=-e_1-e_3,\qquad h_2=-e_2-e_4,
\end{aligned}
\]
and $G=\{a_1,a_2,a_3,b_1,b_2,b_3,h_1,h_2\}$. Then $G$ positively spans
$\mathbb{R}^4$; no subset of at most five vectors positively spans; the positive
circuits of $G$ are exactly
$\{a_1,a_2,a_3\}$, $\{b_1,b_2,b_3\}$, $\{a_1,b_1,h_1\}$,
$\{a_2,b_2,h_2\}$; and any cover of $G$ by circuit flats needs four planes,
of total dimension $8$.

body:
[Definition 20 of arXiv:2608.05931, 'Effective Lagrangian regularity and the uniqueness threshold for random H\"older velocity '] For a function $g : X \to Y$, where $X = \T^d$ or $\R^d$ and $Y$ is a Banach space, we define for $s \geq 0$ the (semi)norm space $\mathcal{C}^s$ as follows. For $s=0$, we let
    \[\|g\|_{\mathcal{C}^0(X) Y} := \sup_{x \in X} \|g(x)\|_Y.\]
    For $s \in (0,\infty)$---letting $s = n + r$ where $r \in (0,1]$ and $n \in \N$---we define $\mathcal{C}^s(X)$ as a seminorm on a subspace of $C^n(X)$ by
    \[\|g\|_{\mathcal{C}^s(X) Y} := \sup_{x,x' \in X, x \ne x'} \frac{\|\nabla^n g(x) - \nabla^ng(x')\|_Y}{|x-x'|^r}.\]
    We note in particular that $\mathcal{C}^1$ is the Lipschitz seminorm and that $\mathcal{C}^0$ is the natural norm on the space of bounded functions---rather than $C^1$ and $C^0$ which have additional qualitative regularity hypotheses that we do not want to require, as we will frequently be working with Lipschitz functions that are not $C^1$.

    We also consider for $p \in [1,\infty), s\geq 0$ the fractional Sobolev (semi)norm spaces $W^{s,p}$. For $s \in \N$, we just let $\|g\|_{W^{s,p}(X)Y} := \|\nabla^s g\|_{L^p(X)Y}$, and for $s>0$ and $s \not \in \N$, we again write $s = n+r$ where $r \in (0,1)$ and $n \in \N$ and define
    \[\|g\|_{W^{s,p}(X) Y} := \Big(\int_X \int_X \frac{\|\nabla^n g(x) - \nabla^n g(x')\|^p_Y}{|x-x'|^{d + rp}}\,dx\,dx'\Big)^{1/p}.\]

body: The halting problem is undecidable: there is no Turing machine H that, given as input an encoding of an arbitrary Turing machine M together with an input string w, always halts and correctly reports whether M halts on w. The halting set {(M, w) : M halts on w} is, however, computably enumerable (recognizable): a universal machine can simulate M on w and accept if the simulation halts.

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.27398, 'Strict Stability and Strict Minimality of Regular Area-Minimizing Hypercones: A Quantitati'] For $\nu\geq0$, let $J_\nu$ be the Bessel function of the first kind of
order $\nu$, and let $j_{\nu,1}$ denote its first positive zero.  Then, for
every $R>0$,
\begin{equation}
    \lambda_\C^D(R)
    =\frac{\lambda_\C^D(1)}{R^2}
    =\frac{j_{b_1,1}^2}{R^2}
    \geq\frac{4}{R^2}>0.
\end{equation}
Equivalently, $\frac{j_{b_1,1}^2}{R^2}$ is the optimal coefficient in
the quadratic inequality
\[
    Q_\C(\varphi)
    \geq\frac{j_{b_1,1}^2}{R^2}
      \int_\C\varphi^2\,d\cH^n,
    \qquad
    \varphi\in C^1(\C),\quad
    \spt\varphi\Subset B_R.
\]
Moreover, the sharp $|x|^{-2}$-weighted Jacobi inequality is
\[
    Q_\C(\varphi)
    \geq b_1^2
      \int_\C\frac{\varphi^2}{|x|^2}\,d\cH^n,
    \qquad
    \varphi\in C_c^1(\C\setminus\{0\}).
\]
In particular, $\C$ is strictly stable in the sense of
\cite{caffarelli1984minimal} if and only if $b_1>0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.27398

[Definition def: ample_Ban of arXiv:2412.07690, 'A law of large numbers concerning the distribution of critical points of random Fourier se'] An \emph{ample Banach space of sections} of $E$  is  a Banach space   ${\boldsymbol{U}}\subset   C^0(E)$   continuously embedded in $C^0(E)$  such that  \index{Banach space! ample}
\[
\forall t \in {\boldsymbol{T}},\;\;\spa\big\{\,u(t),\;\;u\in {\boldsymbol{U}}\,\big\}= E_t.
\]
Let $k\in {{\mathbb N}}$. We say that the Banach space ${\boldsymbol{U}}$ is \emph{$k$-ample} \index{Banach space! $k$-ample}  if for any \emph{distinct } points $t_1,\dotsc, t_k\in {\boldsymbol{T}}$ the map
\[
{\boldsymbol{U}}\ni u\mapsto  u(t_1)\oplus \cdots \oplus u(t_k)\in E_{t_1}\oplus \cdots \oplus E_{t_k}
\]
is onto.  \nobreak\hfill\penalty250 \hbox{}\nobreak\hfill$\rlap{$\sqcap$}\sqcup$\vskip\aline
title: Definition def: ample_Ban of arXiv:2412.07690

[Defi def_selfSimilarRiemann of arXiv:2608.17463, 'Persistence probabilities of fractional L\'evy fields indexed by hyperbolic space and othe'] Let $(X(\eta))_{\eta\in\mathcal{M}}$ be a weak stationary centred Gaussian field indexed by the Riemannian manifold $(M,\left\langle .,. \right\rangle_\mathcal{M})$ with Riemannian metric $\left\langle .,. \right\rangle_\mathcal{M}$ so that there is a function $g:\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ which determines the structure function of the process, i.e.\ $\mathbb{E}\left[(X(\eta)-X(\zeta))^2\right]=g(d_\mathcal{M}(\eta,\zeta))$ for all $\eta,\zeta\in\mathcal{M}$.
    
    The process is called self-similar (of order $H$), if for any $a>0$ and $\ol{\mathcal{M}} := (M, a^2 \left\langle .,. \right\rangle_\mathcal{M})$ the centred Gaussian field $(a^{-H} \mkern 1.5mu\overline{\mkern-1.5muX\mkern-1.5mu}\mkern 1.5mu(\eta))_{\eta\in\ol{\mathcal{M}}}$ determined by $\expec{(\mkern 1.5mu\overline{\mkern-1.5muX\mkern-1.5mu}\mkern 1.5mu(\eta) - \mkern 1.5mu\overline{\mkern-1.5muX\mkern-1.5mu}\mkern 1.5mu(\zeta))^2} = g(d_{\ol{\mathcal{M}}}(\eta,\zeta)) \\ = g(a ~d_\mathcal{M}(\eta,\zeta))$ exists and has the same finite dimensional distributions as $(X(\eta))_{\eta\in\mathcal{M}}$.
title: Defi def_selfSimilarRiemann of arXiv:2608.17463

            \pi_u\big(\sum_{i \leq d}\frac{\partial h}{\partial x_i}(0,x_z)x_i\big) + h(0,x_z) & r = 0 \,.
        \end{cases}$$
    In other words, $\tilde h$ is the unique continuous function such that
    \begin{equation}
        (r\pi_u + \pi_z)(\tilde h(r,x)) = h(rx_u,x_z) \,.
    \end{equation}
    
    

    For the functions $F$ and $G$ from (SPDE-F of the paper) and 
    (SPDE-G-sass of the paper) we also denote
    $$\tilde F(r,x,\theta)(\cdot) \coloneqq \tilde f(\cdot, r,x(\cdot),\theta) \,, \quad \tilde G(r,x,\theta) \coloneqq \tilde \sigma(\cdot, r,x(\cdot),\theta) \cdot H \,.$$

body:
[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] Let $z\in\mathbb C$ satisfy $\Re z>0$.  For every
$f\in L^2(\mathbb R^d)$ and $t>0$,
\begin{equation}
  (\mathrm e^{-tH_z}f)(x)
  =\mathbb E^{\prob_x}\left[
       \mathrm e^{-zA_t}f(W_t)
    \right]
  
\end{equation}
for almost every $x$.  The right-hand side defines a canonical pointwise
version whenever it is finite.  In particular, if $z=\beta-iu$, then
\begin{equation}
  |\mathrm e^{-tH_{\beta-iu}}f|(x)
  \leq (\mathrm e^{-tH_\beta}|f|)(x)
  \leq (P_t|f|)(x),
  
\end{equation}
where $P_t=\mathrm e^{t\Delta/2}$ is the free Brownian semigroup.

body:
[Lemma Polynomial basis identity of arXiv:2602.07920, 'On the position matrix of single-shelf shuffle and card guessing'] Let $N, m$ be a fixed positive integer. Then, 
    \[(N-x)^{\underline{m}} = \sum_{k=0}^{m}c_{N}(k, m) x^{\underline{k}},\]
    where \[c_N(k, m) = (-1)^{k}(N-k)^{\underline{m-k}}\binom{m}{k} = (-1)^{k}\frac{(N-k)!}{(N-m)!}\binom{m}{k},\qquad 0\leq k\leq m\;.\]
    In particular, $c_{N}(m, m)=(-1)^{m}$ and $ c_N(0, m)=N^{\underline{m}}$ for all $m$. Furthermore, $c_N(k, m)=0$ for $k>m$.
title: Lemma Polynomial basis identity of arXiv:2602.07920

body:
[Proposition 3 of arXiv:2608.18075, '2608.18075'] For
$(f,g)\in H^{-b}\oplus \mathsf p_T^\perp$, set
\begin{align}
 \beta_t&=U_w(T,t)^*(g/d_T),
\\
 \alpha_t&=U_w(T,t)^*f
 +\int_t^TU_w(s,t)^*\cS_{\rho_s}^*\beta_s\,\dd s.

\end{align}
In \eqref{eq:beta} the adjoint evolution acts on $H$, whereas the first
term in \eqref{eq:alpha} uses its extension to $H^{-b}$.  Then
\begin{align*}
 \beta\in C([0,T];H)\cap L^2(0,T;H^1),\quad 
 \cS_\rho^*\beta\in L^2(0,T;H^{-b}),
\end{align*}
and
\begin{align*}
 \alpha\in C([0,T];H^{-b}), \quad \widehat A_T'(f,g)(t)=Q^*\alpha_t
 \quad\text{in }L^2(0,T; H),
\end{align*}
where $\widehat A_T'$ denotes the Banach transpose of $\widehat A_T$. Moreover,
\begin{align}
 \Ker\widehat A_T'
 =\left\{(0,g):
 \begin{array}{l}
 g\in \mathsf p_T^\perp,\quad
 \beta_t=U_w(T,t)^*(g/d_T),\\
 \cS_{\rho_t}^*\beta_t=0
 \text{ in }H^{-b}\text{ for a.e. }t
 \end{array}\right\},
\end{align}
and $\langle\beta_t,\rho_t\rangle_2=0$ for all $t$.
title: Proposition 3 of arXiv:2608.18075

[Theorem 7 (van den Berg) of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186'] Suppose that $D$ is simply connected and that $\partial D$ is Minkowski nondegenerate with
Minkowski dimension $\msf d_M(\partial D)\in[1,2)$. That is,
\[0<\liminf_{r\to0}\frac{\msf{A}(\partial D_r)}{r^{2-\msf d_M(\partial D)}}\leq
\limsup_{r\to0}\frac{\msf{A}(\partial D_r)}{r^{2-\msf d_M(\partial D)}}<\infty,\]
where we define
\[\partial D_r=\left\{x\in\mbb R^2:\inf_{y\in\partial D}|x-y|<r\right\}.\]
There exists constants $c\in(1,\infty)$ and $\th>0$ such that
\begin{align}

c^{-1}t^{1-\msf d_M(\partial D)/2}\leq\msf{A}(D)-\msf M_0(t)\leq ct^{1-\msf d_M(\partial D)/2},\qquad t\in(0,\th).
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

1+\lVert \hat q\rVert^2\;\le\;1+\frac1d .
\]

[Lemma lem:single-send-bound of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix a \emph{send sequence}  
$\overline{p}$ and a non-negative integer~$\tau$.
Fix $\lambda \in (0,1/60)$.
Fix a positive integer~$j$ and a $j$-tuple
$\overline{a} \in (\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0})^j$.
Let $Z$ be
a generalised backoff process with  
send sequence~$\overline{p}$, start time~$\tau$,   and an initial population~$\overline{\mathbf{arr}}^Z(\tau)$ such that $\overline{\mathrm{arr}}^Y_{[j]}(\tau) = \overline{a}$. 
Fix a  set $S \subseteq [j]$ such that 
$|S| \geq 100 /\lambda^2$ and 
$\mathcal{N}^Z_{S}(\tau+1) = \sum_{i\in S} p_i a_i  \geq \lambda |S|/80$.
Let $q$ be the probability that
$\sum_{i\geq 1} s_i^Z(\tau+1) \leq 1$. 
Then $q \leq

body:
[Corollary Two centered radial initial vortices of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Under the assumptions of (thm:two-vortex of the paper), suppose in addition that, for
$i=1,2$,
\[
  \mathbf a_{i,\varepsilon}=\mathbf a_{*,i},
  \qquad
  \zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}(\mathbf x)
  =\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,0}^*
  (\mathbf x-\mathbf a_{*,i}).
\]
Then, for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon>0$,
\begin{equation*}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\left\{
  \sum_{i=1}^2\mathcal D(\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,t})
  +\sup_{(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)\in
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,t})\times
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,t})}
  \Bigl[W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)
  -W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}
  (\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})\Bigr]\right\}
  \leq C\varepsilon,
\end{equation*}
and
\begin{equation*}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\sum_{i=1}^2
  \mathcal A(\zeta_{i,\varepsilon,t})
  \leq C\varepsilon^{1/2}.
\end{equation*}
If the Hessian of $W_{\boldsymbol\kappa}^{(2)}$ at
$(\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})$ is positive definite, then, after
possibly decreasing $\rho$,
\begin{equation*}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)\in
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{1,\varepsilon,t})\times
  \mathsf C(\zeta_{2,\varepsilon,t})}
  |(\mathbf b_1,\mathbf b_2)
  -(\mathbf a_{*,1},\mathbf a_{*,2})|
  \leq C\varepsilon^{1/2}.
\end{equation*}
Here $C>0$ depends only on
$D,\rho$, and $\mathbf a_{*,i},\kappa_i,M_i,R_i$, $i=1,2$.

body:
[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2609.01190, 'Rough differential equations on manifolds via natural bundles'] Let $m,n,\ell\in\Nsf$, let $U\subseteq\Rsf^m$ be an open convex set, and let $\phi:U\to\Rsf^\ell$ be a smooth function. Let $p\in [1,3)$, let $\omega$ be a control function on interval $[S,T]$, and let $X=(X^\tau)$ be an $n$-dimensional branched rough path on interval $[S,T]$ with regularity $p$ and control $\omega$. Let $Y: [S,T]\to U$ be a continuous curve in $U$ and let $f_\tau^i:U\to\Rsf$ (for $\tau\in\Fcal_n^2$ and $i\in\llbracket 1,m \rrbracket$) be smooth functions. Assume that there exists $C\in (0,\infty)$ such that the inequality 
	\begin{equation}
	
		\bigg| 
			Y^i(t) - Y^i(s) 
			- f_{\ta}^i(Y(s)) X^{\ta}(s,t) 
			- \frac{1}{2} f_{\tab}^i(Y(s)) X^{\tab}(s,t) 
			- f_{\tc}^i(Y(s)) X^{\tc}(s,t) 
		\bigg| 
		\leq C \omega(s,t)^\frac{3}{p}
	\end{equation}
holds for every $i\in\llbracket 1,m \rrbracket$ and $(s,t)\in\Delta[S,T]$. Then there is a constant $\widetilde{C}\in (0,\infty)$ such that 
	\[
		\bigg|
			\phi^i(Y(t)) - \phi^i(Y(s)) 
			- g^i_{\ta}(Y(s))X^{\ta}(s,t) 
			- \frac{1}{2} g^i_{\tab}(Y(s)) X^{\tab}(s,t) 
			- g^i_{\tc}(Y(s))X^{\tc}(s,t) 
		\bigg| 
		\leq \widetilde{C}\omega(s,t)^\frac{3}{p},
	\]
where 
	\[
		g^i_{\ta} := \frac{\partial\phi^i}{\partial y^j}f_{\ta}^j, 
			\quad 
		g_{\tab}^i := \frac{\partial\phi^i}{\partial y^j}f_{\tab}^j + \frac{\partial^2 \phi^i}{\partial y^j\partial y^k} f_{\ta}^jf_{\tb}^k, 
			\quad\mbox{and}\quad  
		g_{\tc}^i := \frac{\partial\phi^i}{\partial y^j}f_{\tc}^j,
	\]
holds for every $i\in \llbracket 1,\ell \rrbracket$ and $(s,t)\in\Delta[S,T]$.
title: Lemma 3 of arXiv:2609.01190

In population dynamics, a Holling Type II functional response (or Michaelis-Menten / Monod saturation kinetics) is a per-predator consumption rate function h(N) = (s*N) / (1 + s*tau*N), where N is the prey density, s > 0 is the search / attack rate, and tau > 0 is the handling time per captured prey item. As N -> infinity, h(N) asymptotically saturates to the maximal kill rate 1/tau.
Prey density N >= 0
Attack rate s > 0 and handling time tau > 0
title: Holling Type II Functional Response

body: Let G = (V, E) be a finite simple undirected graph with V = {1, ..., n}. The adjacency matrix of G is the n by n matrix A with A_{ij} = 1 if {i,j} is in E and A_{ij} = 0 otherwise, including A_{ii} = 0 for all i. The (combinatorial) graph Laplacian is L = D - A, where D is the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees, D_{ii} = deg(i) = number of edges incident to vertex i. L is symmetric positive semidefinite, and its smallest eigenvalue is 0 with eigenvector the all-ones vector. [standard, e.g. Godsil and Royle, Algebraic Graph Theory]
title: Adjacency Matrix and Graph Laplacian

Fix a finite irreducible row-stochastic Q with stationary probability pi, p in [0,1]^d, c>0, f=cr^2 and 0<r with r+f<=1. For Z in the state space [0,1]^d, let X_i be conditionally independent Bernoulli((QZ)_i), and update Z prime=(1-r-f)Z+rX+fp. Put pbar=pi.p and K=sum pi_i^2. For 0<pbar<1, as r->0 the unique joint stationary law converges weakly to Y times the all-ones vector, where Y has Beta(2c*pbar/K,2c*(1-pbar)/K) law. At pbar=0 or 1 the stationary law is the corresponding point mass. This concerns stationary laws only; a functional diffusion limit and initial-layer analysis are not asserted.
All hypotheses and scope restrictions in the statement apply.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:5c5741603c5b376f3aac288187d5f79d59f80b507b8b34c0ee0372da284d74d5","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/5c/5c5741603c5b376f3aac288187d5f79d59f80b507b8b34c0ee0372da284d74d5.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:cbac8f169ff863a9595053ddefd9aa680d7116085e24b8a5c3f7297ee2ff2704","bundle_entry_key":"forced-network-urn-stationary-beta-law-quadratic-forcing","bundle_id":"population.w336-p0087-checked-attempt-20261010","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability theory","draft":"w336/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.reinforcement:forced-network-urn-stationary-beta-law-quadratic-forcing","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# P0087: stationary synchronization and covariance at f=c*r^2

Status: proof written; w346 KEEP pending. This proves a full stationary-law limit, stationary moments and a scalar generator limit under conditional independence. It does not prove the general network's functional diffusion limit or its initial layer.

Assume a fixed finite irreducible row-stochastic Q, its stationary probability row vector pi, p in [0,1]^d, c>0, r>0, f=c*r^2 and r+f<=1. Update

    Z'=(1-r-f)Z+r X+f p,

with conditionally independent X_i given Z, and P(X_i=1|Z)=(QZ)_i. There is a unique stationary law on [0,1]^d. Its mean is z*=f*((r+f)I-rQ)^(-1)p. Write pbar=pi.p and K=sum pi_i^2. As r decreases to zero, its stationary covariance satisfies

    Cov(Z) -> [K*pbar*(1-pbar)/(2c+K)]*1*1^T.

Proof of existence/uniqueness: the transition is Feller on a compact cube. Couple two states using the same independent uniforms for their Bernoulli coordinates. Because 1-r-f>=0, the weighted L1 distance has expected next value at most (1-f) times its present value; use pi Q=pi. Thus stationary laws are unique and the transition contracts in this Wasserstein distance. Taking expectations yields the displayed mean; the matrix is invertible because its eigenvalues have positive real part.

For synchronization, let D=diag(pi), S=pi.Z, and E_Q(z)=z^T D(I-Q)z=(1/2)sum pi_i Q_ij(z_i-z_j)^2. At stationarity, with Delta=r(X-Z)+f(p-Z),

    2r E[E_Q(Z)] = 2f E[<Z,p-Z>_D] + E[||Delta||_D^2]
                   <= 2f+(r+f)^2 = O(r^2).

Irreducibility makes E_Q(z)>=gamma*||z-1*(pi.z)||_D^2 for some fixed gamma>0: the finite symmetric quadratic form has kernel precisely the constants. Hence E||Z-1*S||_D^2=O(r). Also E[S]=pbar exactly, so z*_i tends to pbar.

The martingale innovation for S has conditional variance r^2 sum pi_i^2 (QZ)_i(1-(QZ)_i); conditional independence is used exactly here. Total variance at stationarity gives

    (2f-f^2) Var(S)=r^2 sum pi_i^2 E[(QZ)_i(1-(QZ)_i)].

Synchronization shows (QZ)_i-S tends to zero in L2. The variables are bounded, so for any subsequential limit V of Var(S), division by r^2 gives 2c V=K*(pbar*(1-pbar)-V). Its solution is unique. Every subsequence has that limit, and synchronization gives the full covariance limit.

For the scalar case Q=(1), stationarity gives the exact variance

    Var(Z)=r^2*p*(1-p)/(2f-f^2+r^2)
          =p*(1-p)/(1+2c-c^2*r^2).

For h in C^3([0,1]), the one-step scalar generator divided by r^2 converges uniformly to

    Lh(z)=c(p-z)h'(z)+(1/2)z(1-z)h''(z).

Indeed E[Delta]=c*r^2(p-z), E[Delta^2]=r^2*z(1-z)+c^2*r^4(p-z)^2, and |Delta|<=r+cr^2. Taylor's remainder, divided by r^2, is bounded by ||h'''||_infinity*r*(1+cr)^3/6, with the additional second-order drift term O(r^2). This identifies the candidate Wright-Fisher generator; path tightness and martingale-problem uniqueness are further steps.

Theorem (full stationary law). Under the same fixed-network assumptions and 0<pbar<1, the joint stationary law of Z converges weakly to Y*1, where

    Y ~ Beta(2c*pbar/K, 2c*(1-pbar)/K).

Proof: write S'=S+f*(pbar-S)+r*eta, where eta=pi.(X-QZ), E[eta|Z]=0, |eta|<=1 and E[eta^2|Z]=sum pi_i^2 (QZ)_i(1-(QZ)_i). For every polynomial h, the stationary Taylor identity divided by r^2 gives

    0=c E[(pbar-S)h'(S)]
      +(1/2)E[sum pi_i^2 (QZ)_i(1-(QZ)_i)*h''(S)] + O(r).

The drift-square contribution is O(r^2), and the third-order remainder is uniformly O(r). The proved L2 synchronization implies that the sum inside the second term differs from K*S*(1-S) by a quantity tending to zero in L1. Every subsequence has a further weakly convergent subsequence of S because [0,1] is compact. If its limiting moments are mu_k, use h(s)=s^k, k>=1, to obtain

    [2c+K*(k-1)]*mu_k = [2c*pbar+K*(k-1)]*mu_(k-1), mu_0=1.

These are exactly the moments of the displayed beta law: iterating gives the product of (2c*pbar/K+j)/(2c/K+j) for j=0,...,k-1, which also follows by integrating the beta density. A probability law on [0,1] is determined by its moments, since polynomials approximate continuous functions uniformly. Hence all subsequential limits agree and S converges weakly. Synchronization gives Z-S*1 tending to zero in probability, so the joint law converges to Y*1. If pbar=0 or 1, positivity of pi forces every p_i to be that endpoint and the unique stationary law is the corresponding point mass.

This proof uses all polynomial moments, not an inference from the first two moments. It proves convergence of stationary laws, not a limit for trajectories begun away from synchronization. Without conditional independence, the innovation variance changes. For example, Q=J_d/d, constant p, and one shared Bernoulli coin across all coordinates preserve a synchronized state and give the scalar beta parameters 2cp and 2c(1-p), rather than 2cdp and 2cd(1-p).

For reproducible finite checks, the exact covariance identity is

    V=B V B^T+r^2*diag(s*(1-s)-diag(Q V Q^T)),
    B=(1-r-f)I+rQ, s=Q z*.

Checks: the scalar exact formula; first four scalar stationary moments; exact polynomial generators; finite-network covariance systems; first four moments of the exact consensus Markov chain for Q=J_d/d at d=2,3,5; a common-coin control that changes the beta variance. The conditional-independence hypothesis is essential for K, the covariance formula and the stationary beta law.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:97f3a85196e873990e9567366e0506ef248b0ce7c5366d200c12cde129cf9cd6","revision_digest":"sha256:40d22fcda637f208570e3eca58d8253fc6efbc8c03ac8bb9324ce8528c678e9e","source_id":"owner:campaign:w336:P0087:forced-network-urn-stationary-beta-law-quadratic-forcing","source_revision":"author-proof-2026-10-10; independent audit w346 pending","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Corollary 7 (Pathwise convergence of threshold-separated jump atoms) of arXiv:2605.11783, 'Stability of Compensated Jump Integrals under Quadratic Variation Convergence'] Let $X$ and $\{X^n\}_{n\ge1}$ be c\`adl\`ag processes on $[0,t]$ such that
\[
[X^n-X]_t \to 0
\qquad \text{a.s.}.
\]

Let \(f_n\) and \(f\) be predictable functions on \(\Omega\times[0,t]\times\mathbb R\). Assume that there exists a set
\(\Omega_0\in\mathcal F\) with \(\mathbb P(\Omega_0)=1\) such that, for every
\(\omega\in\Omega_0\), every \(s\leq t\), and every compact set
\(K\subset\mathbb R\),
\[
        \sup_{x\in K}|f_n(s,x,\omega)-f(s,x,\omega)|\to0 .
\]

Fix \(r>0\), \(k\ge1\), \(a>0\), and let \(s\le t\). Assume moreover that
\[
        f(s,\cdot,\omega)
        \text{ is continuous at }\Delta X_s(\omega)
        \qquad\text{a.s.}
\]

Then
\[
1_{A_k(r)}
\left(
\int_{L(r,k)<|x|\le a} f_{n}(s,x)\,\mu_{n}(\{s\},dx)
-
\int_{L(r,k)<|x|\le a} f_{n}(s,x)\,\mu(\{s\},dx)
\right)
\longrightarrow 0
\]
almost surely on the event
\[
        \{(\Delta X)^*_t<a\}.
\]

[Lem diagonal-imaginary-part of arXiv:2605.13004, 'Orientation in Poisson Cluster Processes via Imaginary Bispectra'] Let $0<m<1$, let $h$ be a probability density on $(0,\infty)$, define
\[
U(t):=\int_0^\infty \cos(tu)h(u)\,du,
\qquad
V(t):=\int_0^\infty \sin(tu)h(u)\,du,
\]
and let $Q$ be the numerator term from Theorem~(thm:branching-bispectrum of the paper). Then $A(t):=\mathrm{Im} Q(t,t)$ satisfies
\begin{align}
A(t)
&=2(1-m)(2V(t)-V(2t)) \notag\\
&\quad+2(1-2m)\{(1-U(t))(V(2t)-V(t))-(1-U(2t))V(t)\} \notag\\
&\quad+2m\{[(1-U(t))^2-V(t)^2]V(2t)-2(1-U(2t))(1-U(t))V(t)\}.

\end{align}

Then, for $\mathrm{j} =1,2$, it holds that 
			\begin{align}
				\text{\upshape{(i)}}&\quad\E_x\bigl( \ee^{-q\tau_{b,Y}^-} \1_{\{\tau_{b,Y}^- < T_{a,Y}^{+,\lambda}\}} f^{(p)}_{1,\jj}(Y_{\tau_{b,Y}^-}) \bigr) = f^{(p,q)}_{2,\jj}(x) - \frac{\W^{(q)}(x-b)}{\Z^{(q)}(a-b,\varphi_{q+\lambda})}\lambda \int^\infty_0 \ee^{-\varphi_{q+\lambda}y}f^{(p,q)}_{2,\jj}(y+a)\dd y,   \\
				\text{\upshape{(ii)}}&\quad \E_x\bigl( \ee^{-q\tau_{b,Y}^-} \1_{\{\tau_{b,Y}^- < T_{a,Y}^{-,\lambda}\}} f^{(p)}_{1,\jj}(Y_{\tau_{b,Y}^-}) \bigr) = f^{(p,q)}_{2,\jj}(x) + \lambda \int^x_b \W^{(q+\lambda)}(x-y)f^{(p,q)}_{2,\jj}(y)\dd y \notag \\

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2608.07365, 'A pathwise Ito formula \\for weakly differentiable functions'] For any path $\omega\in Q_{\pi}([0, T], \Rr^d)$ the sequence $\mathcal{L}^{\pi_n}_{\omega}$ converges weakly to the weighted occupation  measure $\mu^T_{\omega}$ defined by 
\[
\forall A\in {\cal B}(\mathbb{R}^d),\qquad \mu^T_{\omega}(A):= {\rm tr}\int_0^T 1_A(\omega(t)) \d [\omega]_{\pi} (t).
\]
\begin{align*}\forall \phi\in C_c(\Rr^d),\qquad 
\int_{\Rr^d} \phi(x) \mathcal{L}^{\pi_n}_{\omega}(x) \d x  \xrightarrow{n \to \infty} \int_{\Rr^d} \phi(x) d\mu^T_{\omega}(x)
= {\rm tr}\int_0^T (\phi\circ\omega\,) \d[\omega]_{\pi}.
\end{align*}
title: Lemma 12 of arXiv:2608.07365

body:
Own-work METHOD DRAFT; proof (unaudited), attributed to w737 T385-C13 v1; no independent PASS or novelty claim. Fix L>0 and eta>0. For each n let X be a deterministic real n by n matrix with operator norm at most L, and w_1,...,w_n independent N(0,I_n) vectors. Put h_j=ReLU(Xw_j), mu=E h_j, z_j=h_j-mu, Phi=E[h_j h_j^T], and Sigma=E[z_j z_j^T]. Let R_j be real symmetric, measurable in X and the columns w_k with k!=j (and optionally auxiliary randomness independent of all feature weights), with operator norm at most 1/eta almost surely. The recorded unaudited derivation gives, for each fixed epsilon>0, P(max_j |z_j^T R_j z_j/n-Tr(Sigma R_j)/n|>epsilon)<=C n exp[-c n min(epsilon^2,epsilon)], with C,c depending only on L,eta. The centering step uses the exact identity z^T R z-Tr(Sigma R)=h^T R h-Tr(Phi R)-2 mu^T R(h-mu) for deterministic symmetric R. Louart-Liao-Couillet quadratic-form concentration controls the raw term. Gaussian Lipschitz concentration controls the mean correction. Indeed mu_i=||x_i||/sqrt(2 pi), ||mu||^2<=n L^2/(2 pi), and w->mu^T R ReLU(Xw) is Lipschitz with constant at most sqrt(n/(2 pi))*L^2/eta. Condition on all columns except j before applying those bounds; integrate and take a union bound, without asserting independence between deviation events. Thus the method allows correlations among coordinates within each feature column, but R_j must exclude the tested column. For X=I and eta=1, taking the same-column R=zz^T/||z||^2 makes z^T R z/n tend to kappa=1/2-1/(2 pi)>0 while Tr(Sigma R)/n=kappa/n, illustrating failure if this independence hypothesis is removed. For random X independent of all w_j with tight operator norm, conditioning first on ||X||<=L and then letting L grow gives convergence in probability, rather than a uniform unconditional exponential rate. This is a fixed-positive-ridge concentration ingredient; it supplies neither an edge law nor a justification for a ridge tending to zero. The underlying source-based proof draft and all proposed uses remain subject to independent review.
Fixed L>0 and eta>0; deterministic square X with operator norm at most L.
Independent standard Gaussian feature-weight vectors; coordinates of the resulting ReLU column need not be independent.
Each symmetric R_j excludes w_j from its measurability and has norm at most 1/eta.
Any auxiliary randomness is independent of all Gaussian feature weights.
Random-input extension requires independence from feature weights and a tight input norm; only convergence in probability is claimed there.
Owner-work proof (unaudited), w737 T385-C13 v1; no independent PASS or novelty claim.

body:
Internal demographic noise in continuous population models refers to stochastic fluctuations arising endogenously from the discrete, probabilistic birth, death, and predation interactions of individual agents. In the diffusion approximation, the infinitesimal diffusion matrix has entries whose magnitudes scale proportionally to the square root of the interaction rates (i.e., variance linear in the population state), distinct from external environmental noise where diffusion coefficients are proportional to the state itself.
Continuous diffusion approximation of discrete branching / birth-death processes
No fluctuating exogenous environmental drivers
title: Internal Demographic Noise in Population Models

[Theorem 12 (Wasserstein convergence for tRLMC) of arXiv:2605.24937, '2605.24937'] Assume \hyperref[ass:PJG]{\textup{(A1)}}--\hyperref[ass:LSI]{\textup{(A6)}}, and
let \(\lambda\in(0,\lambda_{\max}^{\mathrm{tRLMC}}].\)
There holds
\[
W_2(\mu_0\widetilde P^n,\pi_\beta)\;\le\; C_{W_2}\bigl(\lambda+e^{-c_0\lambda n}\bigr),
\]
where $C_{W_2}$ depends polynomially on the dimension and $c_0$ depends on $C_{\mathrm{LSI}}$.
As a result, for $\lambda\le \widetilde O({\varepsilon})$ one needs $N\ge \widetilde O\!\left(\frac{1}{\varepsilon}\right)$ to guarantee
\[
W_2(\mu_0\widetilde P^N,\pi_\beta)\le \varepsilon.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Wasserstein convergence for tRLMC

[Lemma 34 (Fourier recovery) of arXiv:2607.26377, '\textbf{Entire Logarithmic Signatures\\ of Bounded-Variation Paths in Finite Dimensions}'] Let $\beta^{(1)}:[0,T_1]\to V$ and $\beta^{(2)}:[0,T_2]\to V$ be continuous bounded-variation paths, translated to start at zero, with the same nonzero increment $v$.
Fix one functional $\ell\in V^*$ with $\ell(v)=1$, put $W=\ker\ell$, and write
\[
\beta_t^{(k)}=x_t^{(k)}v+X_t^{(k)},
\qquad x_t^{(k)}=\ell(\beta_t^{(k)}),
\qquad X_t^{(k)}\in W
\quad(k=1,2).
\]
Equip $W$ with an auxiliary Euclidean norm, define the decorated paths by \cref{eq:decorated-path}, and define the measures by \cref{eq:pushforward-measure}.
If
\[
S(B^{\Lambda}(\beta^{(1)}))
 =S(B^{\Lambda}(\beta^{(2)}))
\]
for every finite symmetric $\Lambda\subset 2\pi\Q$, then
\[
\mu_{\beta^{(1)}}^{\eta}
 =\mu_{\beta^{(2)}}^{\eta}
\]

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Reduce the intrinsic limit to a renewal-type statement for the branching-process comparison. Result: The intrinsic one-arm probability is bounded above and below by constants over n (Kozma-Nachmias), and the comparison object is the survival probability of a critical branching process with finite variance, for which n P(survive n generations) -> 2/sigma^2 (Kolmogorov). For the intrinsic arm event the analogous statement would be n P(intrinsic radius >= n) -> a_in where a_in should be 2/V with V the variance of the offspring distribution of the effective branching structure (the cluster explored by intrinsic distance is a branching process with dependent offspring). Existence of the limit therefore reduces to a Kolmogorov-type limit theorem for the intrinsic exploration, which needs the mean-field two-point asymptotics at the level of an exact constant (the lace expansion gives tau_{p_c}(x) ~ A/|x|^{d-2} with an exact constant A, Hara 2008), plus an exact constant for the 'variance' of the exploration, which is the sum of the three-point function's connected part, computable from the lace expansion in principle. The extrinsic limit is harder because the extrinsic arm event mixes intrinsic distance and Euclidean displacement; its bounded-ratio form comes from a second-moment argument that does not give constants. I could not complete either constant. Obstruction: Exact constants for the intrinsic branching structure require second-order lace expansion information.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0066-sharp-intrinsic-and-extrinsic-one-arm-exponents-in-high-dimensions

[Lemma of arXiv:2608.30212, 'A Painlev\'e equation for the H\"ormander-Bernhardsson constant'] Let $k$ be even, $c\in J_{k,0}$, and $m\ge 1$. Then
\begin{align*}
\mathcal{L}_c[Q_{k,c}/y^m] & = -(-1)^{m-1}\pi  \frac{Q_{k,c}^{(m-1)}(0) }{(m-1)!}\\
\mathcal{L}_c[Q_{k,c}^2/y^{2m}]&=0\\
\mathcal{L}_c[Q_{k,c}^2/(y^2-1)]&=0\\
\mathcal{L}_c[yQ_{k,c}^2/(y^2-1)]&=-\pi  Q_{k,c}(1) Q_{k,c}(-1)
\end{align*}

Let $A(x,t)$ be real measurable on $\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R$ and uniformly parabolic with constants $0<\lambda\le\Lambda<\infty$, and consider $\partial_tu=\mathrm{div}(A(x,t)\nabla u)$. The equation has a weak fundamental solution $\Gamma(x,t;y,s)$, defined for $s<t$, nonnegative, with $\int\Gamma(x,t;y,s)dx=1$ (conservation of mass; no symmetry of $A$ is needed, since constants solve the adjoint equation), and there is $C=C(n,\lambda,\Lambda)\ge1$ with $\frac{1}{C\,(t-s)^{n/2}}\exp\Big(-\frac{C|x-y|^2}{t-s}\Big)\ \le\ \Gamma(x,t;y,s)\ \le\ \frac{C}{(t-s)^{n/2}}\exp\Big(-\frac{|x-y|^2}{C(t-s)}\Big)$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb R^n$ and all $s<t$. The constants depend only on $n,\lambda,\Lambda$ and never on any modulus of continuity of $A$; in particular the bounds are stable under homogenization and rough coefficients. If bounded lower-order terms are present, or the equation is posed only for $0<t-s\le T$, the same two-sided bounds hold with $C$ depending in addition on $T$ and the bounds on those terms.

TECHNIQUE CARD. The alteration method, in Zhao's words: first make a random construction, and then fix the blemishes. A random object is shown to have few defects in expectation, the defects are removed or repaired deterministically, and the cost of the repair is bounded by the same expectation, often through Markov's inequality. Zhao, Chapter 3 (Alterations). Theorem 3.1.1: every graph on n vertices with minimum degree δ > 1 has a dominating set of size at most ((log(δ+1) + 1)/(δ+1)) n; the proof puts each vertex in X independently with probability p, adds the set Y of vertices that are neither in X nor adjacent to X, so that X ∪ Y dominates and E|X ∪ Y| ≤ (p + e^{−p(1+δ)}) n, and takes p = log(δ+1)/(δ+1). Theorem 3.4.1 (Erdős 1959): for all k and ℓ there is a graph with girth greater than ℓ and chromatic number greater than k; the proof takes a random graph G(n,p), uses Markov's inequality to make the number of cycles of length at most ℓ small, bounds the independence number, and deletes one vertex from each short cycle.
a random construction whose expected number of defects, or expected repair cost, can be computed
a deterministic repair step whose cost is bounded by the number of defects
Theorem 3.1.1: a graph on n vertices with minimum degree δ > 1; Theorem 3.4.1: positive integers k and ℓ

AUTHOR PROOF DRAFT; INDEPENDENT MATHEMATICAL REVIEW PENDING. For a fixed real beta, let N=ceil(8(1+abs(beta))), B_n=floor(n/2+beta*log_2(1+n/N)), and let T_beta be the rooted tree with 2^(B_(n+1)-B_n) children at each vertex at depth n. Contract unary corridors to the rooted binary branching skeleton. Each corridor and the initial stem have length at most 4; the resulting surjection pi obeys d_binary(pi(u),pi(v))<=d_T(u,v)<=4*d_binary(pi(u),pi(v))+8. Hence every T_beta is quasi-isometric to the rooted binary tree. T_0 and T_2 have equal critical probability 1/sqrt(2), yet only T_0 has critical extinction. Critical extinction is not a quasi-isometry invariant for arbitrary bounded-degree graphs, even with equal critical parameters. No claim is made about invariance within quasi-transitive graphs.

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a variable $f:X\to\mathbb R$ which follows the exponential law of parameter $\lambda>0$, its normalized central moments are given by the following formula,
$$M_k''=\sum_{s=0}^k(-1)^s\frac{k!}{s!}$$
with the small order normalized central moments being as follows,
$$M_1''=0\quad,\quad 
M_2''=1\quad,\quad
M_3''=2\quad,\quad
M_4''=9\quad,\quad\ldots$$
and with all this being, again, more complicated than for the usual moments.

On 0<epsilon<1/4, F(epsilon)=epsilon(2+sin(log epsilon)) is strictly increasing, lies between epsilon and 3epsilon, and satisfies log F(epsilon)/log epsilon ->1 as epsilon tends to zero. Nevertheless F(epsilon)/epsilon has no limit. Thus monotonicity plus bounded-ratio beta=1 alone cannot establish asymptotic equivalence to c epsilon. This analytic counterexample is a refuted inference, not a percolation counterexample.

[Coro 22 of arXiv:2609.03819, 'Stochastic damped wave and Euler-Bernoulli equations with singular locally H\"older contin'] Pathwise uniqueness holds for \eqref{concrete_damped_equation} in the following cases, which for reader's convenience we split according to the different intervals the parameter $\alpha$ belongs to. 

\vspace{1mm}
\begin{itemize}
\item Case $\displaystyle \alpha\in\left(\frac{d}{8k}+\frac14,\frac12\right]: \ 
\begin{cases}
&d<2k\\
&\theta\in \left(\max\left\{\frac23; \frac{d}{6k\alpha}+\frac{1-\alpha}{3\alpha}\right\}, 1\right),\\
&\beta\in \left[0,\min\left\{\frac\alpha2; \alpha-\frac d{4k}; \frac{\alpha(1+3\theta)}{2}-\frac{d}{4k}-\frac12\right\}\right),\\
&\delta\in \left(\frac d{4k}-\frac\alpha2,\frac\alpha2-\beta\right)\cap [0,\infty),
\end{cases}$\\[1mm]
\item Case $\displaystyle\alpha\in \left(\frac12, \frac34\right): \ 
\begin{cases}
&d<2k\\
&\theta\in \left(\max\left\{\frac23; \frac{2-3\alpha+\frac d{2k}}{3(1-\alpha)}\right\},1\right), \\
&\beta\in \left[0,\min\left\{\frac{1-\alpha}2; \alpha-\frac12+\frac{(1-\alpha)(3\theta-1)}2-\frac d{4k}\right\}\right), \\
&\delta\in \left(\frac d{4k}-\frac\alpha 2,\min\left\{\frac{1-\alpha}2-\beta; \frac32-2\alpha; \frac{1-\alpha(2-\theta)}{2(1-\theta)}\right\}\right)\cap [0,\infty),
\end{cases}$ \\[1mm]
\item Case $\displaystyle \alpha\in \left[\frac34, 1\right):
\ \begin{cases}
&d<2k\\
&\delta\in \left(\frac d{4k}-\frac{\alpha}2,\frac{1-\alpha}2\right)\cap [0,\infty), \\
&\theta\in \left(\max\left\{\frac23; \frac{2\delta+2\alpha-1}{2\delta+\alpha}; \frac{\alpha+2\delta-1+\frac d{2k}}{\alpha+2\delta}\right\},1\right), \\
&\beta\in \left[0,\min\left\{\frac{1-\alpha}2-\delta; \frac{1-\alpha(1-\theta)}2-\delta(1-\theta)-\frac{d}{4k}\right\}\right).
\end{cases}$
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Coro 22 of arXiv:2609.03819

$$V(f_1+\ldots+f_n)=nt$$

title: Lem 30 of arXiv:2607.27535

body:
STATUS: proof (unaudited). For the exact critical unshaped Gaussian tanh scalar chain with fixed K0>0, let Y=2L*K_L,t=L/n. For each fixed order k and c<infinity, uniformly n>=n0 and 1<=L<=cn, E Y^j=m_j(t)+(5j/12)J_j(t)*log(L)/L+O(1/L), 1<=j<=k. Here m_j=E A_t^(-j), J_j=E[H_t A_t^(-j-1)] using the same Brownian path, A_t=int_0^1 exp(tr+sqrt(2t)B_r)dr,H_t=exp(t+sqrt(2t)B_1). Therefore kappa_k(Y)=F_k(t)+(5/12)G_k(t)*log(L)/L+O(1/L), F_k=P_k(m), G_k=sum_j j J_j partial_j P_k(m). Both coefficient functions have arbitrary finite small-t Taylor expansions with explicit Gaussian-integral remainder bounds. At fixed t>0 this supplies the first log(n)/n width term and an O_t(1/n) remainder. Assumptions: Zero bias; independent standard Gaussian rows/layers; weight variance exactly1/n, no activation shaping or normalizer; K0>0 fixed; fixed cumulant order and finite positive depth-ratio cap c. Constants depend on k,K0,c; threshold n0 large enough for the stated inverse moments. Scope: First logarithmic finite-width order only; the full all-orders 1/n expansion of C019 is NOT proved. The uniform O(1/L) constant is finite but not given as a numerical closed form. Analytic proof and dependencies C044-C046 await independent audit. Higher-order printed Hanin constants disagree with the Brownian-functional coefficients; explicit discrepancy retained for reviewer, not used as a premise.
Zero bias; independent standard Gaussian rows/layers; weight variance exactly1/n, no activation shaping or normalizer; K0>0 fixed; fixed cumulant order and finite positive depth-ratio cap c. Constants depend on k,K0,c; threshold n0 large enough for the stated inverse moments.
