body:
[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2607.09246, 'Scaling limit of 1+1 dimensional directed polymer with power-law tail and spatial correlat'] Assume that conditions \textbf{(A)} and \textbf{(B)} hold, with
\(\alpha>2\).  Recall \( \beta_N \) and \(k_N\) in \eqref{beta_N} and \eqref{k_N}, and fix $\theta\in(2,\alpha\wedge4)$.
Define
\[
        \Delta\hat\omega(i,x):=\hat\omega(i,x)-\bar\omega(i,x),
        \qquad
        \hat\omega(i,x)
        :=
        \frac{
        e^{\beta_N\bar\omega(i,x)-\bar\lambda(\beta_N)}-1}
        {\beta_N}.
\]
Then there exists a sequence \(\varepsilon_N\downarrow0\) such
that, uniformly in \(i\) and \(x,z\in\mathbb Z\),
\begin{equation}
        \left|
        \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q}
        [\hat\omega(i,x)\hat\omega(i,z)]
        \right|
        \le C\gamma(x-z),
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
        \left|
        \mathbb E_{\mathbb Q}
        [\Delta\hat\omega(i,x)\Delta\hat\omega(i,z)]
        \right|
        \le \varepsilon_N\gamma(x-z).
\end{equation}
More precisely, one may take
\[
        \varepsilon_N=C(\beta_N^{\theta-2}+\beta_N^2).
\]

	Then

	Y^1_t\geq Y^2_t,

	$$

body: [Defn of arXiv:2608.27939, 'Entropy and domination for quasi-Hitchin representations'] A \emph{weighted planar network} $(\Gamma, \omega)$  is a finite acyclic directed planar graph $\Gamma$, with $n$ sources on the left boundary and $n$ sinks on the right boundary, and with a weight function $\omega:\mathcal{E} \to \mathbb{C}$ defined on the set of directed edges. The \emph{weight matrix} $\mathcal{W}(\Gamma, \omega)$ of such a network is the $n\times n$ matrix whose $(i,j)$--entry is the sum of the weights of all directed paths from source $i$ to sink $j$, where the weight of a path is the product of the weights of its edges.

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2605.17155, '2605.17155'] Let \(B\) be a Banach space and let \(f:\Nzero\to B\).  

\begin{enumerate}
\item A positive integer \(\tau\) is a
\emph{Bohr \(\varepsilon\)-translation number}, or simply an \emph{\(\varepsilon\)-translation number} of \(f\), if
\[
   \sup_{n\ge0}\norm{f(n+\tau)-f(n)}<\varepsilon .
\]
The sequence \(f\) is \emph{(Bohr) almost periodic}, if for every
\(\varepsilon>0\), the set of Bohr \(\varepsilon\)-translation numbers is
relatively dense.

\item The sequence \(f:\Nzero\to B\) is \emph{limit periodic} if
it is a uniform limit of periodic sequences, equivalently if for
every \(\varepsilon>0\) there is a periodic sequence \(g:\Nzero\to B\) such
that
\[
   \sup_{n\ge0}\norm{f(n)-g(n)}<\varepsilon .
\]

\item The sequence \(f:\Nzero\to B\) is
\emph{asymptotically almost periodic} if
\[
   f(n)=g(n)+c(n),\qquad n\ge0,
\]
where \(g:\Nzero\to B\) is almost periodic and \(c(n)\to0\) in \(B\).

\item For \(q\ge1\), define the \emph{Weyl \(q\)-seminorm} of a sequence
\(u:\Nzero\to B\) by
\[
   \norm{u}_{W^q}
   :=
   \limsup_{L\to\infty}\sup_{N\ge0}
   \left(\frac1L\sum_{n=N}^{N+L-1}\norm{u(n)}^q\right)^{1/q}.
\]
A positive integer \(\tau\) is a
\emph{Weyl \(q\)-\(\varepsilon\)-translation number} of \(f\) if
\[
   \norm{\,f(\cdot+\tau)-f(\cdot)\,}_{W^q}<\varepsilon .
\]
The sequence \(f\) is \emph{Weyl \(q\)-almost periodic} if, for every
\(\varepsilon>0\), the set of Weyl \(q\)-\(\varepsilon\)-translation numbers is
relatively dense.

\item For \(q\ge1\), define the \emph{Besicovitch \(q\)-seminorm} by
\[
   \norm{u}_{B^q}
   :=
   \limsup_{L\to\infty}
   \left(\frac1L\sum_{n=0}^{L-1}\norm{u(n)}^q\right)^{1/q}.
\]
A positive integer \(\tau\) is a
\emph{Besicovitch \(q\)-\(\varepsilon\)-translation number} of \(f\) if
\[
   \norm{\,f(\cdot+\tau)-f(\cdot)\,}_{B^q}<\varepsilon .
\]
The sequence \(f\) is \emph{Besicovitch \(q\)-almost periodic} if, for every
\(\varepsilon>0\), the set of Besicovitch \(q\)-\(\varepsilon\)-translation
numbers is relatively dense.
\end{enumerate}

[Proposition 13 (Principal curvatures for weighted $\ell_p$-balls) of arXiv:2605.11995, 'Intrinsic volumes of \(\ell_p\)-balls and a continuum of Maxwell--Poincar\'e--Borel laws f'] Let $x\in \partial \mathbb B_p^n(a)$ be such that $x_i\neq 0$ for all $i=1,\dots, n$.  Then the principal curvatures of $\mathbb B_p^n(a)$ at $x$, denoted by $\lambda_1(x),\dots,\lambda_{n-1}(x)$, are precisely the solutions of the degree $n-1$ polynomial equation
\[
\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^{2p}|x_i|^{2p-2}
\prod_{\substack{j=1\\ j\ne i}}^n
\left((p-1)a_j^p|x_j|^{p-2}
-
\left(\sum_{r=1}^n a_r^{2p}|x_r|^{2p-2}\right)^{1/2}\lambda
\right)=0.
\]
For $m=1,\ldots, n$ the $(m-1)$-st elementary symmetric polynomial of the principal curvatures is given by
\[
\sigma_{m-1}\bigl(\lambda_1(x),\dots,\lambda_{n-1}(x)\bigr)
=
\frac{(p-1)^{m-1}}
{\left(\sum_{r=1}^n a_r^{2p}|x_r|^{2p-2}\right)^{(m+1)/2}}
\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^{2p}|x_i|^{2p-2}\sum_{\substack{I\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}\setminus\{i\}\\ |I|=m-1}}
\prod_{j\in I} a_j^p|x_j|^{p-2}.
\]

Let sigma be a translation-invariant mean-zero +/-1 field on Z^3 or a finite abelian group, with 0<=G(x)=E[sigma_0 sigma_x]<=1 and finite chi=sum_x G(x). Put B=sum_x G(x)^2. For the ordered triples D such that (0,x2,x3,x4) has at least two equal sites, sum_D[-U4(0,x2,x3,x4)]=12chi^2-16chi-6B+12, between 0 and 12chi^2. Here U4 is the mean-zero fourth cumulant. For any xi>0 the contact contribution normalized by chi^2 xi^3 is at most 12/xi^3, and therefore vanishes if xi diverges. Since B<=chi, the unnormalized contact mass divided by chi^2 tends to 12 when chi diverges. The coefficient is sharp over the stated class, as N perfectly correlated spins on a cyclic group give 12N^2-22N+12. Exact coincident tuples only are controlled; the distinct-site mass required for C0052 is not lower-bounded.

[Defn def:formal_qMPL of arXiv:2609.01458, 'Confluence relations for $q$-analogues of multiple zeta values'] We denote by $\hat{\mathcal{F}}$ the set
of formal symbols
\[
\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,k_{d}}(x_{1},\dots,x_{d}),
\]
where $d\geq0$, $k_{1},\dots,k_{d}\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq1}$, and
\[
x_{i}\in\{z^{h}q^{m}\mid h\in\{0,\pm1\},m\in\mathbb{Z}\}\qquad(1\leq i\leq d),
\]
satisfying
\begin{equation}
x_{i}\cdots x_{d}\in zq^{\mathbb{Z}}\cup q^{\mathbb{Z}_{>0}}\qquad(1\leq i\leq d).
\end{equation}
We write the case $d=0$ as $\mathbb{L}(\emptyset)$. We call the
elements of $\hat{\mathcal{F}}$ formal $q$MPLs. We call $k_{1}+\cdots+k_{d}$
the weight. We also call $k_{i}$ the weight of the $i$-th position.
In this section, we introduce several subsets of $\hat{\mathcal{F}}$.
Although each subset is defined when it first appears, their definitions
and inclusion relations are collected in (app:notation-summary of the paper)
for the reader's convenience. For $\mathcal{X}\subset\hat{\mathcal{F}}$,
we denote by $\mathbb{Q}\mathcal{X}$ the $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space
with basis $\mathcal{X}$.
title: Formal $q$MPLs

[Corollary cor:sine of arXiv:2411.15830, 'Deformations of biorthogonal ensembles and universality'] For any compactly supported continuous function $h:\mathbb{R}\to [0,+\infty)$, we have the limits
\[
\lim_{n\to\infty}\mathcal G_n^{\sigma_n}[h]=\begin{cases}
\mathcal G_{\sin}^{\sigma}[h],&t=0,\\
\mathcal G_{\sin}[h],&t>0.\end{cases}
\]

 where $\mathcal G_{\sin}$ and $\mathcal G_{\sin}^\sigma$ are the probability generating functionals of the sine point process and its $\sigma$-deformation,
 
\[
\mathcal G_{\sin}[h]=\det(\mathsf{1}- \sqrt h\mathbf K_{\sin}\sqrt h),\qquad \mathcal G_{\sin}^{\sigma}[h]=\det(\mathsf{1}- \sqrt h\mathbf K_{\sin}^\sigma\sqrt h),
\]

with 

\[
\mathbf K_{\sin}^\sigma=\sqrt{1-\sigma}\mathbf K_{\sin}(\mathsf{1}-\sigma\mathbf K_{\sin})^{-1}\sqrt{1-\sigma}.
\]

In particular, the deformed orthogonal polynomial ensemble $\mathcal X_n^{\sigma_n}$ converges weakly as $n\to\infty$ to the deformed sine point process $\mathcal X_{\sin}^{\sigma}$ if $t=0$, and to the sine point process $\mathcal X_{\sin}$ if $t>0$. [Proposition prop:ik-nnbox-to-boxnn of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] For every $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}$,
  $\textbf{IK} \vdash \neg \neg \Box \varphi \to \Box \neg \neg \varphi$.
  \begin{proof}
    By completeness, it suffices to prove validity in every IK-model.
    Let $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$ be an IK-model,
    and fix $x_0 \in W$ such that $x_0 \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \neg \neg \Box \varphi$.
    To prove $x_0 \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \Box \neg \neg \varphi$,
    fix $x_1, y_0 \in W$ such that $x_0 \leq x_1$ and $x_1 \sqsubset y_0$.
    We show that $y_0 \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \neg \neg \varphi$.

    Fix any $y_1 \in W$ such that $y_0 \leq y_1$.
    By FS2 applied to $x_1 \sqsubset y_0$ and $y_0 \leq y_1$,
    there is $x_2 \in W$ such that $x_1 \leq x_2$ and $x_2 \sqsubset y_1$.
    By persistency, $x_2 \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \neg \neg \Box \varphi$.
    By the $\leq$-reflexivity of $x_2$ and the fact that no world forces $\bot$,
    it follows that
    $x_2 \not \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \neg \Box \varphi$.
    Hence there is $x_3 \in W$ such that $x_2 \leq x_3$ and
    $x_3 \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \Box \varphi$.

    By the $\Diamond$-p condition applied to $x_2 \sqsubset y_1$ and $x_2 \leq x_3$,
    there is $y_2 \in W$ such that $x_3 \sqsubset y_2$ and $y_1 \leq y_2$.
    By the $\leq$-reflexivity of $x_3$ and the forcing clause for $\Box$,
    we have $y_2 \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$.
    Therefore, $y_1 \not \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \neg \varphi$.
    Since $y_1$ was arbitrary, $y_0 \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \neg \neg \varphi$.
    Since $x_1$ and $y_0$ were arbitrary,
    $x_0 \Vdash^{\text{h}}_\mathfrak{M} \Box \neg \neg \varphi$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:ik-nnbox-to-boxnn of arXiv:2608.29708

[Def 26 of arXiv:2609.01389, 'K-stability and birational rigidity of Fano 3-fold weighted complete intersections'] Let $X$ be a $\mbQ$-Fano variety of dimension $n$.
For a prime divisor $E$ over $X$, we define
\[
S_X (E) \coloneq \frac{1}{(-K_X)^n} \int_0^{\infty} \vol (-f^*K_X - t E) d t,
\]
where $f \colon \tilde{X} \to X$ is a projective birational morphism such that $E$ is a prime divisor on $\tilde{X}$, and
\[
\delta_X (E) \coloneq \frac{A_X (E)}{S_X (E)},
\] 
where $A_X (E)$ is the log discrepancy of $X$ at $E$.
The \textit{global delta invariant} of $X$ is defined as
\[
\delta (X) \coloneq \inf \Set{ \delta_X (E) | \text{$E$ is a prime divisor over $X$}}.
\]
For a closed point $\msp \in X$, the \textit{local delta invariant} of $X$ at $\msp$ is defined as
\[
\delta_{\msp} (X) \coloneq \inf \Set{ \delta_X (E) | \text{$E$ is a prime divisor over $X$ such that $\msp \in C_X (E)$}}.
\]
title: Definition 26 of arXiv:2609.01389

\operatorname{Var}_\mu(-\log q_\mu)
\leq
\frac{\pi^2}{6s^2}.
\]
In particular, for the uniform probability measure on a convex body,
\[
\operatorname{Var}_{\mu_K}(-\log q_K)
\leq
\frac{\pi^2}{6}n^2.

[Defi 42 of arXiv:2608.28148, 'Flows and homotopies of Banach Lie algebroids'] Consider a manifold $M$ and a subset $\mathcal{S} \subseteq C^0(M,\R)$ of continuous functions. We say that $M$ 
\begin{enumerate}
\item admits $\mathcal{S}$-bump functions or is ($\mathcal{S}$ -regular) if for every $x\in M$ and every open $x-$neighborhood $U \subseteq M$ there exists $\chi \in \mathcal{S}$ such that $\chi (M) \subseteq [0,1], U = \chi^{-1} (]0, 1])$ and $\chi (x) = 1$.
\item is $\mathcal{S}$-paracompact if every open cover $(U_i)_{i \in I}$ of $M$ admits a subordinate partition
of unity $(\chi_i)_{i\in I}$ of functions $\chi_i \in \mathcal{S}, i \in I$.
\end{enumerate}
If $\mathcal{S} = C^k(M, \R)$ for some $k\in \N_0 \cup \{\infty\}$, we shorten the notation and say that $M$ admits $C^k$-bump functions or is $C^k$
-paracompact. Note that $C^0$-paracompactness is equivalent to the usual topological notion of paracompactness.
title: Definition 42 of arXiv:2608.28148

[Lemma 9 of arXiv:2607.16017, 'On large networks of integrate-and-fire neurons with short-term synaptic plasticity'] We have that 
\begin{equation}
R_{s,t}^a (v, x) = K^v_a (s, t) \psi_{ t-s}(x) + \int_s^t K^v_a (s, u) R_{u, t }^a ( (1- U) \psi_{ u-s } (x) ) \d u . 
\end{equation}
As a consequence, 
\begin{equation} R_{s, t }^a (v, x) = S^{a, 1 }_{s, t} (v) + S_{s, t}^{a,2} (v) x , 
\end{equation}
where 
$$ S^{a, 1 }_{s, t} (v) = K_a^v ( s, t) \psi_{t-s} (0) + \int_s^t K^v_a (s, u ) R^{a, 1}_{u,t} \d u + (1 - U) \int_s^t K_a^v (s, u ) \psi_{u-s} ( 0)  R^{a, 2 }_{u, t } \d u $$
and 
$$ S^{a, 2 }_{s, t } ( v) = K^v_a (s, t) e^{ (t-s)/\tau} + (1- U) \int_s^t K^v_a (s, u ) e^{ - (u-s)/\tau} R^{a, 2 }_{u, t} \d u . $$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem th: stability_t_dependent of arXiv:2609.00257, 'Stability estimates for the initial-to-final-state inverse problem'] Let $0<T<\infty$ and $n\geq 2$. Consider two time-dependent potentials $V_1, V_2 \in L^1((0,T);L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n))$ with decay of the form $\|V_j\|_{\delta, \varepsilon}< \infty$ and $\|\mathop\mathrm{Im} V_j\|_{\delta, \varepsilon}\leq \frac{1}{4T} $ for $j\in\{1, 2\}$. Assume also that the potentials satisfy the a priori assumption $\|V_1 - V_2\|_{\delta, \varepsilon} \leq R_0$ for some fixed constant $0<R_0<\infty$.
	 
	Let $\mathcal{U}_T^1$, $\mathcal{U}_T^2$ denote the corresponding initial-to-final-state maps. Then, for any $\delta >1/2$ and $ \varepsilon>0$, there holds 
	\begin{equation}
	\|V_1 - V_2\|_{H^{-1}(\mathbb{R}^n)} \lesssim \omega_\varepsilon(\mathrm{dist}_{\delta,\varepsilon} (\mathcal{U}_T^1, \mathcal{U}_T^2)),
	\end{equation}
	under the condition that $\mathrm{dist}_{\delta,\varepsilon} (\mathcal{U}_T^1, \mathcal{U}_T^2)$ is sufficiently small. Here $\omega_\varepsilon$ is a modulus of continuity satisfying that
	\[
	\omega_\varepsilon(t)\leq\left(\frac{|\log(t)|}{5\varepsilon}\right)^{\frac{-\varepsilon}{n(n+3)(1+\varepsilon)}},\quad 0<t<1/e.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem th: stability_t_dependent of arXiv:2609.00257

PROOF OF A SPECIAL CASE; independent audit pending. Fix a,b in [0,1] and let K(z)=[[a,z],[conjugate(z),b]]. On the disk |z|^2<=min(ab,(1-a)(1-b)), the Shannon entropy of the determinantal subset measure with kernel K(z) is concave as a function of the complex number z. Its four atom probabilities are ab-|z|^2, (1-a)(1-b)-|z|^2, a(1-b)+|z|^2, and (1-a)b+|z|^2. This covers all two-site Hermitian positive contractions with common diagonals, including boundary kernels, but does not settle jointly varying diagonals or larger kernels.

A predictor $\hat{p}(X) \in [0, 1]$ is perfectly calibrated for binary outcome $Y \in \{0, 1\}$ if $P(Y = 1 \mid \hat{p}(X) = p) = p$ for all $p \in [0, 1]$. The Expected Calibration Error (ECE) partitions predictions into $M$ bins $B_m$ and computes the weighted average difference $\text{ECE} = \sum_{m=1}^M \frac{|B_m|}{N} |\operatorname{acc}(B_m) - \operatorname{conf}(B_m)|$.
Y \in {0, 1} is a binary label
B_m partitions the probability interval [0, 1]
title: Probability Calibration and Expected Calibration Error (ECE)

Let X be a centered real random variable (E[X] = 0). The following properties are equivalent up to universal multiplicative constants: (1) Tail bound: P(|X| >= t) <= 2 * exp(-c1 * t^2) for all t >= 0; (2) Moment bound: (E[|X|^p])^{1/p} <= c2 * sqrt(p) for all p >= 1; (3) MGF bound: E[exp(lambda * X)] <= exp(c3 * lambda^2) for all lambda in R; (4) Orlicz norm: ||X||_{psi_2} <= c4.

For nonempty closed A set d_n=dist(K_n,A). Suppose P(d_n>0)->r>0 and P(d_n>epsilon_j)->r_j for epsilon_j decreasing to zero, with r_j->r. Then P(K avoids A)=r and the conditional law of K_n given avoidance converges weakly to K conditioned on avoidance. body:
[Lem 9 of arXiv:2609.02040, '\Large Quantum Landau Damping with Coulomb Repulsion in the Whole Space'] For any $h\in[0,1]$ and $t>0$, it holds that
        
		\begin{align*}
			\Nrm{\Gr_\h(t,\cdot)}{L^\infty} &\lesssim \frac{1}{t^2\weight{t}^4} \,  ,
			&
			\Nrm{\Gr_\h(t,\cdot)}{L^1} &\lesssim \frac{1}{t^{1/8}\weight{t}^{3-1/8}} \,  ,
			\\
			\Nrm{\GrE_\h(t,\cdot)}{L^\infty} &\lesssim \frac{1}{t\weight{t}^4} \,  ,
			&
			\Nrm{\GrE_\h(t,\cdot)}{L^1} &\lesssim \frac{1}{\weight{t}^{2}} \, . 
		\end{align*}
		Moreover, we have
		\begin{align*}
			\Nrm{\Gr_\h(t,\cdot) - \Gr_0(t,\cdot)}{L^\infty} &\lesssim \frac{h^2}{t^4\weight{t}^4} \, ,
			&
			\Nrm{\Gr_\h(t,\cdot) - \Gr_0(t,\cdot)}{L^1} &\lesssim \frac{h^{2}}{t\weight{t}^{4}} 
			\\
			\Nrm{\GrE_\h(t,\cdot) - \GrE_0(t,\cdot)}{L^\infty} &\lesssim \frac{h^2}{t^3\weight{t}^4} \, ,
			&
			\Nrm{\GrE_\h(t,\cdot) - \GrE_0(t,\cdot)}{L^1} &\lesssim \frac{h^{2}}{t^{3/8}\weight{t}^{4-3/8}} \, .
		\end{align*}

[Proposition 68 (Compatibility of spectral, Gaussian, and dyadic approximations) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Fix $(a;b,c)\in\mathfrak L$, admissible exponents
\[
 0<s<1-\beta_{b,c},
 \qquad
 \beta_{b,c}<\sigma<1-\beta_{b,c},
\]
and $2\le p<\infty$.  Let $(\Lambda_j)_{j\ge1}$ be any admissible cofinal
spectral cutoff sequence.  On each of the four Hilbert legs in
\eqref{eq:abstract-flat-1}--\eqref{eq:abstract-flat-4}, fix increasing
finite-rank orthogonal projections converging strongly to the identity; in
the equal-color case use the same projection on the two copies of the common
Gaussian space.  For dyadic $L\ge2$, let
$\mathcal B_{j,m,L}^{a;b,c}$ be the finite sum of the principal centered
blocks over $\mathfrak F_L$ in \eqref{eq:anisotropic-finite-set}, with spectral
cutoff $\Lambda_j$ and simultaneous four-leg compression at level $m$.
Write $j=\infty$ for the uncut synthesis maps and $m=\infty$ for the
uncompressed centered Wiener operator.  Set
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr X_T^{s,\sigma}:=
 \mathcal L\!\left(
 C_TL^2\cap L_T^\infty B_{2,\infty}^{\sigma},
 C_TH^{s-1}\cap L_T^1B_{2,\infty}^{\sigma-1}
 \right).
\end{equation}
Then the following assertions hold.

First, for finite $j,m,L$, the operator
$\mathcal B_{j,m,L}^{a;b,c}$ is a finite Gaussian polynomial with values in a
finite-dimensional subspace of $\mathscr X_T^{s,\sigma}$.  For each $j,m$,
including the uncut or uncompressed values, its limit as $L\to\infty$ exists
in $L^p(\Omega;\mathscr X_T^{s,\sigma})$; denote it by
$\mathcal B_{j,m}^{a;b,c}$.  For every $\gamma$ below the strict margins in
\eqref{eq:assembly-tail-gamma},
\begin{equation}
 \sup_{j,m}
 \|\mathcal B_{j,m}^{a;b,c}-\mathcal B_{j,m,L}^{a;b,c}\|_
 {L^p(\Omega;\mathscr X_T^{s,\sigma})}
 \lesssim_{p,\gamma}L^{-\gamma}.
\end{equation}
Here and below the suprema include $j=\infty$ and $m=\infty$.

Second, the three-parameter family has a joint limit:
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal B_{j,m,L}^{a;b,c}
 \longrightarrow
 \mathcal B_{\infty,\infty}^{a;b,c}
 \quad\text{in }L^p(\Omega;\mathscr X_T^{s,\sigma})
 \quad\text{as }j,m,L\to\infty
\end{equation}
with the product ordering on $\N^3$.  Consequently every iterated limit in
the spectral cutoff, Gaussian compression, and dyadic assembly parameters
exists and gives the same centered operator.  In the equal-color case, the common limit is the centered second Wiener
chaos obtained after removing the deterministic covariance distribution.

body:
[Lemma 1 of arXiv:2606.23896, 'The one-point Schreier Poisson boundary of Thompson's group \(F\)'] Let \((X_n)\) be a Markov chain on a countable state space
\(E\), with transition kernel \(P\). Let \(A\subset E\) be nonempty. Assume
that, starting from every \(x\in E\), the chain hits \(A\) almost surely, and
that, starting from every \(a\in A\), it returns to \(A\) infinitely often
almost surely.

Define

\[
\tau_0=\inf\{n\ge 0:X_n\in A\},
\]

and, for \(k\ge 0\),

\[
\tau_{k+1}=\inf\{n>\tau_k:X_n\in A\}.
\]

The trace chain on \(A\) is

\[
Y_k=X_{\tau_k}
\]

with transition kernel

\[
P_A(a,b)=\mathbb P_a(X_{\tau_1}=b),
\qquad a,b\in A .
\]

Then restriction gives an isometric order-isomorphism

\[
H^\infty(E,P)\cong H^\infty(A,P_A).
\]

Consequently the Poisson boundaries of \((E,P)\) and \((A,P_A)\) are
isomorphic.

[Thm 2 of arXiv:2511.18861, 'Correlation Decay for Maximum Weight Matchings on Sparse Graphs'] Let $G$ be a connected graph whose degree is bounded above by $D$. Suppose that the edge weights are i.i.d.\ exponential random variables with mean $1$. Let $e \in E(G)$ and $r\geq 3$ be such that $\bB_e^r(G)$ is a tree. 
    
    Then we have
    \[
    \varrho_r(G, e)  \leq 2D(1 - (2D)^{-D})^{r-2}.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:KP_vec of arXiv:2604.28068, 'Mean-square Stability and Bifurcations for Dissipative SDEs'] Let $A$, $B$, $C$, $D$ be real matrices.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item If the matrices $A+B$ and $C+D$ exist, then 
    $$(A+B)\otimes (C+D)=A\otimes C+A\otimes D+B\otimes C+B\otimes D.$$ 
    \item  If $A$, $B$, $C$ are three matrices, such that the matrix product $ABC$ exists, then $$\mathrm{vec}(ABC)=(C^T\otimes A)\mathrm{vec}(B).$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:corr of arXiv:2607.20956, 'Sharp moduli of continuity for Gaussian fields and stochastic PDEs via correlation bounds'] Suppose (equation alphaH=3/2 of the paper), and fix $0<t_1<t_2$.
	Then, for any $\varepsilon \in (0\,,1)$, there exist $\rho \in (0\,,1)$ such that $\rho = O(\varepsilon^2)$ and $r_\rho \in (0\,,1)$ such that
	\begin{align*}
		|\mathbb{E}[(u(t\,,x)-u(t\,,y))&(u(t\,,x') - u(t\,,y'))]| \\
		&\le \varepsilon \|u(t\,,x)-u(t\,,y)\|_2 \|u(t\,,x') - u(t\,,y')\|_2
	\end{align*}
	uniformly for all $t\in [t_1\,,t_2]$, $r \in (0\,,r_\rho]$ and $x,y,x',y' \in \mathbb{R}$ with $|x-y| \le r$, $|x'-y'| \le r$ and $|x-x'| \ge 2r^\rho$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Definition 172 (Gluing of trapezoids) of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Take trapezoids $\mathcal{T}_1,\ldots,\mathcal{T}_m$ with long bases $\llbracket D_i,U_i\rrbracket$, $i\in[m]$, equipped with type maps \eqref{eq:typemap} and containing a total of $2H$ (maximal) blue segments. We say that the trapezoids are glued into a domain $\mathcal D$, if for each trapezoid $\mathcal T_i$ and each of its blue segment $\llbracket A_h,B_h\rrbracket\subset \llbracket D_i,U_i\rrbracket$ there exists exactly one other trapezoid $\mathcal T_{i'}$, $i'\neq i$ and a blue segment in it $\llbracket A_{h'},B_{h'}\rrbracket\subset \llbracket D_{i'},U_{i'}\rrbracket$, such that $\llbracket A_{h'},B_{h'}\rrbracket$ coincides with $\llbracket A_{h},B_{h}\rrbracket$. In this situation, the trapezoids $\mathcal T_i$ and $\mathcal{T}_{i'}$ are \emph{adjacent}, and we identify indices $h$ and $h'$. We require the gluing to be connected: any two trapezoids can be linked by a chain of adjacent ones.
title: Gluing of trapezoids

body: When one ensemble of $M$ members predicts $D$ output coordinates (spectral bands, pixels, reduced coefficients) and a separate affine stack is fitted per output, the $D$ least-squares weight vectors form a matrix $\hat W \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times (M+1)}$ with $\hat W = W + Z$: row $d$ of the noise $Z$ has covariance $\sigma_d^2 (X_d^T X_d)^{-1}$, $X_d$ the calibration design of output $d$ and $\sigma_d^2$ its residual variance, while the true $W$ has low effective rank whenever the optimal weighting varies smoothly across outputs (neighbouring bands weight the same members similarly). The relevant random-matrix ratio is then $\beta = (M+1)/D$ - not $M/n_{\mathrm{cal}}$ - and the problem is low-rank matrix denoising: after scaling row $d$ by $1/\sigma_d$ (and, when the designs $X_d$ are nearly common across outputs, right-whitening by $\bar G^{1/2}\sqrt{n}$ with $\bar G$ the average of $X_d^T X_d / n$), the Gavish-Donoho optimal singular-value shrinkage selects the rank as the number of singular values above the Marchenko-Pastur edge $1 + \sqrt\beta$ and debiases each retained singular value, with no cross-validation. Shrinking every row toward one global weight vector by a cross-validated scalar - the best heuristic found on the EMIT/OCO-2 pools, beating per-output least squares on 69 of 70 cells by 3.1 percent - is the rank-one special case of this estimator with the direction fixed and the amount tuned by hand. For EMIT ($M = 23$, $D = 285$) $\beta = 0.084$; for OCO-2 ($M = 18$, $D = 40$) $\beta = 0.475$, a wide bulk in which only strong structure clears the edge.

[campaign status: candidate_full_solution - author-checked, unrefereed, prior art searched but not cleared] Let f_R be the plus/minus-one indicator of the left-right crossing of the square [0,R]^2, for critical bond percolation on Z^2 or critical site percolation on the triangular lattice. Let S(f_R) be its spectral sample and P(f_R) its pivotal set, and I(f_R) = E|P(f_R)| the total influence. CLAIM: there is a constant C depending only on the lattice such that for every R >= 2, H(S(f_R)) <= C I(f_R) and H(P(f_R)) <= C I(f_R); equivalently Ent(f_R) = O(R^2 alpha_4(R)). This is Kalai, Three puzzles on mathematics, computation and games, ICM 2018, arXiv:1801.02602, Section 3.3.2, Conjecture 8, and the first open problem of Garban, Pete and Schramm, The Fourier spectrum of critical percolation, Acta Mathematica 205 (2010), Section 11. The general entropy-influence conjecture for arbitrary Boolean functions is NOT claimed; this is the percolation crossing case only. The general principle the argument isolates: the inequality holds for every Boolean function on a planar array whose spectral sample satisfies sum_{k>=1} E|S_{2^k}| = O(E|S|), i.e. whose spectral sample is a fractal of dimension strictly below two.

the quoted GPS inputs (Lemma 3.2, (2.6), the half-plane three-arm bound) are literature dependencies, not proved here

NEW STEP, a quadtree coding bound. For a random subset A of the bits write A_r for the set of dyadic r-squares that meet A. Describe A from the coarsest scale down: one bit for emptiness, then four bits per hit square of side 2^k naming which of its four children are hit, and a bounded number of bits per hit unit square. The decoder always knows how many bits to read, so the code is uniquely decodable and Shannon source coding gives H(A) <= 1 + 4 sum_{k=1..K} E|A_{2^k}| + C_0 E|A_1|. Since E|A| = I(f_R) for both S and P, the finest term is a multiple of the influence and everything rests on the coarser scales. QUOTED INPUTS: (1) Garban-Pete-Schramm Lemma 3.2, P[S intersect B nonempty] <= 4 alpha_box(B,Q_R), which follows in one line from the identity P[S intersect B nonempty] = E[Var(f_R | bits outside B)], with the same bound and no constant for the pivotal set; (2) their (2.6), quasi-multiplicativity with the polynomial lower bound alpha_4(r,R) >= C^{-1} (r/R)^{2-eps}; (3) the half-plane three-arm bound alpha_3^+(r,R) <= C (r/R)^2. ONE-SCALE SUM. Classify an r-square B by its distance d to the boundary of Q_R and the distance D to the second nearest side. For d >= 2r and D >= 8d the four-arm event from B forces four alternating arms from B to radius d/2 and three alternating half-plane arms from 2d to D/2, on disjoint bits, so alpha_box(B,Q_R) <= alpha_4(r,d/2) alpha_3^+(2d,D/2) <= C alpha_4(r,d) (d/D)^2. At most C (d/r)(D/r) squares have d and D in given dyadic ranges, so E|A_r| <= C (R/r)^2 alpha_4(r,R) + C. Inserting this and using (R/r)^2 alpha_4(r,R) <= C R^2 alpha_4(1,R) r^{-eps} makes the scale sum geometric, and I(f_R) >= c R^2 alpha_4(1,R) absorbs the additive logarithm. THE EXPONENT CONDITION IS WHERE THE RESULT COMES FROM: the scale sum converges exactly when r^2 alpha_4(1,r) grows polynomially. With the five-arm bound alone, whose exponent is exactly two, the same argument gives only the trivial O(I log R). On the triangular lattice alpha_4(r,R) is of order (r/R)^{5/4}, so the scale-r term is (R/r)^{3/4+o(1)} and the bound is dominated by its finest term. CHECKS ON RECORD: exact Walsh-Hadamard spectra on the 2x2 and 3x3 squares (H(S) = 2.000 bits at I = 1.000; H(S) = 5.331 bits at I = 1.719) confirm the coding inequality, a control on the definitions and not evidence for the asymptotics; a Monte Carlo run on the pivotal set for R = 16 to 256, with the pivotal rule brute-force-verified against flipping on all 49,152 edge cases of the 3x3 square, gives E|P_r|/E|P| stable in R at 0.575, 0.356, 0.214, 0.127, 0.075 for r = 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, decaying like r^{-0.74}, with the scale-sum ratio climbing from 1.25 to 1.44 toward the predicted sum_k 2^{-3k/4} = 1.46. WHAT IS NOT DONE: independent referee of the memo; general quads checked only in outline. [Lem 108 of arXiv:2507.08909, 'Annealed almost periodic entropy'] If $\phi$ is unital and $\cal{O}$ is any base of neighbourhoods of $\phi$ in $\S^{\rm{u}}_k(\G)$, then
\[\hann(\phi) = \inf_O\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\log \bbP(\Phi^{\pi_n}_V \in O).\]
The analogous formula holds for $\ul{\rmh}^\ann$ if `$\limsup$' is replaced by `$\liminf$'.

[Definition def.scvec of arXiv:2412.05698, 'Controlled rough SDEs, pathwise stochastic control and dynamic programming principles'] {FHL21}}]
   Let $\beta, \beta' \in (0,1]$ and $\gamma >1$ be some fixed parameters.
   We call $(f,f')$ {\em stochastic controlled vector field on \( \mathbb{R}^d \)} and write \( (f,f')\in \ensuremath{{\mathbf D}}^{\beta,\beta'}_XL_{p,q}{\mathcal{C}}^\gamma_{b}\)
   if the following conditions are satisfied.

   \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
      \item
      The pair
      \[
      (f,f')\colon\Omega \times  [0,T] \to {\mathcal{C}}^\gamma_{b}(\mathbb{R}^{d}; \mathbb{R}^m) \times {\mathcal{C}}^{\gamma-1}_{b} (\mathbb{R}^d ; \mathrm{Lin}(\mathbb{R}^{d_X},\mathbb{R}^m))
      \]
      is  progressively measurable in the strong sense and uniformly $n$-integrable in the sense that
      \begin{align}
         \|(f,f')\|_{\gamma;q}:=\sup_{s\in [0,T]}\||f_s|_{\gamma}\|_q +  \sup_{s\in [0,T]}\||f'_s|_{\gamma-1}\|_q 
      \end{align}
      is finite.

      \item
      Letting
      \begin{align}
         \llbracketZ\rrbracket_{\zeta;p,q}:=\sup_{(s,t)\in \Delta_T:s\neq t}\frac{\Big\|\big\|\sup_{y\in {\mathbb{R}^d}}|Z_{s,t}(y)|\,\big|\,{\mathfrak F}_s \big\|_p\Big\|_q}{(t-s)^\zeta}\,,

Let d>=2 and let the iid undirected nearest-neighbor weights on Z^d have a nondegenerate law supported in [r,R] with 0<r<=R<infinity. Put mu=E t_e. Choose separated positive-mass support intervals with low upper bound a, high lower bound b>a, and k>=1 with k*b>(k+2)*a. Let S be the sum of k axial weights, H the sum of the k+2 edges of its disjoint height-one detour, and delta=E[(S-H)_+]>0. Then E T(0,n*e1)<=n*mu-floor(n/(k+1))*delta and almost surely limsup_n T(0,n*e1)/n<=mu-delta/(k+1). The coordinate-monotone axial sum divided by n tends to mu, so its raw same-environment difference from unrestricted FPP has asymptotic liminf at least delta/(k+1)>0. This does not compare centered fluctuations or exponents.

[Corollary 26 of arXiv:2608.30752, '2608.30752'] Let \(M=S\) be a closed oriented surface of genus at least two and
\(u_0=\mathrm{id}: M=S\to S,
X_t=\gamma_q(t)\). Let \(X_g\in\mathcal T(S)\)
with  the metric \(g\) on $M=S$. Let
\(\Phi_{\Delta_q,X_g}\in\mathcal Q(X_g)\) be the Hubbard--Masur
differential whose vertical measured foliation is \(\Delta_q\) \cite{HubbardMasur1979}. For each
\(i\), let \(A_i\) be its characteristic Jenkins--Strebel cylinder with
 conformal modulus
\(M_i=\mathrm{Mod}(A_i)\). Then
\begin{equation}
  \mathscr E_{\Delta_q}(\mathrm{id}_S)
  =\frac12\Ext_{X_g}(\Delta_q)
  =\frac12\int_{X_g}|\Phi_{\Delta_q,X_g}|
  =\sum_{i=1}^r\frac{1}{2M_i}.
  
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{t\to\infty}
  \frac{\mathcal E_{\mathrm{id}_S}(X_t)}{t^2}
  =8\Ext_{X_g}(\Delta_q)
  =\sum_{i=1}^r\frac{8}{M_i}.
  
\end{equation}

[Proposition 4 (Stability near a compact family of flat metrics) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Let \(M\) be a fixed torus and let \(\mathcal F\) be a compact set of
flat metrics on \(M\) (not modulo diffeomorphisms).  For a fixed
\(\rho\in(0,1)\), there is a uniform
\(h^{2+\rho}\)-neighborhood of \(\mathcal F\), measured using one fixed smooth
reference metric on \(M\), such that the Ricci flow starting from any
metric in this neighborhood exists for all future time and, without applying a
time-dependent pullback, converges exponentially as a tensor field on \(M\) to
a flat metric.  Here \(h^{2+\rho}\) is the little H\"older space, namely the
closure of smooth metrics in the \(C^{2,\rho}\)-norm.  The exponential rate and
the constants may be chosen uniformly on \(\mathcal F\), and parabolic
bootstrapping gives convergence in every fixed \(C^m\)-norm.

[Proposition 5 (Bonferroni bounds and second-order graph decomposition) of arXiv:2609.03466, 'Least-Favorable Location for Binomial Top-$t$ Selection'] Set
\[
 N_H=t\binom{k-t}{2},\qquad
 N_L=(k-t)\binom t2,\qquad
 N_D=2\binom{k-t}{2}\binom t2.
\]
Then, for every $n,p,k,t,\delta$,
\begin{equation}
 t(k-t)a_n(p)-N_HH_n(p)-N_LL_n(p)-N_Da_n(p)^2
 \le Q_n(p)\le t(k-t)a_n(p).
 
\end{equation}
Moreover, inclusion--exclusion gives the exact decomposition
\begin{equation}
 Q_n(p)
 =t(k-t)a_n(p)-N_HH_n(p)-N_LL_n(p)-N_Da_n(p)^2+\mathcal R_n(p),
 
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal R_n$ is the alternating sum over edge sets containing at least three edges.

[Proposition 3 of arXiv:2608.22693, 'Uniformity of extremal behaviour along geodesics in Liouville quantum gravity'] (\cite[Theorem~2]{BK25})

Fix $\gamma \in (0,2)$ and consider a whole-plane GFF $h$ and the associated LQG metric $D_h$. Then the following holds almost surely. For any points $u,v \in \CC$, any $D_h$-geodesic $P$ from $u$ to $v$ and any sequence of $D_h$-geodesics $\{P_n\}_{n \in \NN}$ converging to $P$ in the Hausdorff sense with respect to the Euclidean metric (or equivalently, the metric $D_h$), for all $n$ large enough, we have 
\begin{equation*}
    (P_n \setminus P) \cup (P \setminus P_n) \subseteq B_{\varepsilon}(u) \cup B_{\varepsilon}(v).
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 3 of arXiv:2608.22693

Own-work research draft; status: proof (unaudited); independent review pending. On any fixed compact embedded C2 closed k-manifold of surface volume V with a chart F of inverse-Lipschitz constant a and Jacobian >=j>0, densities in [(1-delta)/V,(1+delta)/V] have finite-codebook minimax error >=a*delta*j/[V*(k+1)*2^(2k+6)*8^(1/k)]*(S+1)^(-1/k). Reach and volume are unchanged. Explicit constants are supplied for spheres. Assumptions: k>=1; compact embedded C2 manifold without boundary; positive finite V; chart extends C1 past the cube and is bi-Lipschitz; 0<delta<1; S counts the complete output description; containing target class permits density slack around uniform density on this admissible fixed manifold. Limits: No identified proof gap. Constants depend on a chosen admissible manifold; no uniformly smooth density class or unrestricted-real-weight sharp-rate assertion. The proof uses the bounded-density cube Hamming packing and signed tents.

Let A generate a C_0-semigroup (T(t)) on a Banach space X with ‖T(t)‖ ≤ M e^{ωt}, and let B ∈ B(X) be bounded and everywhere defined. Then A + B with domain D(A + B) = D(A) generates a C_0-semigroup (S(t)) satisfying ‖S(t)‖ ≤ M e^{(ω + M‖B‖)t}. The perturbed semigroup solves the variation-of-constants equation S(t)x = T(t)x + ∫_0^t T(t − s) B S(s)x ds for all x ∈ X, and is given by the Dyson-Phillips series S(t) = Σ_{n ≥ 0} S_n(t) with S_0(t) = T(t) and S_{n+1}(t)x = ∫_0^t T(t − s)B S_n(s)x ds, converging in operator norm uniformly on compact time intervals. In particular boundedness of the perturbation is enough; no relative-boundedness smallness is needed, and D(A) is unchanged.
X is a Banach space
A generates a C_0-semigroup
B is bounded and defined on all of X

[Defi gie of arXiv:2507.20324, 'Non-existence of several random fractals in Brownian motion and Brownian loop soup'] Let $X_{0},X_{1},\ldots,X_{k}$ be independent Brownian motions started uniformly from $\mathcal{C}_0$, and stopped upon reaching $\partial\mathcal{B}(0,e^{r})$. Let $\Gamma$ be a Brownian loop soup with intensity $\mathbf{c}\in (0,1]$ in the plane, and $\Gamma_{r}$ be the collection of loops in $\Gamma$ which are fully contained in $\mathcal{B}(0,e^{r})$. We write $\widetilde{X}_{i}$ for the union of $X_{i}$ and the clusters in $\Gamma_{r}\backslash\Gamma_{0}$ that it intersects. Let $\Pi_{r}$ be the $\sigma$-algebra generated by $X_{1},\ldots,X_{k},\Gamma_{r}\backslash\Gamma_{0}$. Define
\[\widetilde{Z}_{r}:=\mathbb{P}(X_{0}\cap(\cup_{j=1}^{k}\widetilde{X}_{j})=\varnothing|\Pi_{r}).\]
For all $\lambda>0$, let $p(\mathbf{c},k,r,\lambda)=\mathbb{E}[\widetilde{Z}_{r}^{\lambda}]$. Then the generalized intersection exponent $\xi_{\mathbf{c}}(k,\lambda)$ is defined by
\[\xi_{\mathbf{c}}(k,\lambda):=-\log\lim_{r\to\infty}(p(\mathbf{c},k,r,\lambda))^{1/r}.\]
title: Defi gie of arXiv:2507.20324

Let k>=0 be an integer. A sample compression scheme maps a finite labeled sample S to a subset kappa(S) of at most k observations and reconstructs a classifier h_S. Assume stability: whenever kappa(S) is contained in S_prime and S_prime is contained in S, reconstruction on S_prime equals h_S. For any input-label distribution P, n>2k IID observations S, and 0<delta<1, with probability at least 1-delta the following implication holds: if h_S has zero empirical classification error on S, then its population error is at most 2[k ln4+ln(1/delta)]/(n-2k). The bound is distribution-free and contains no extra log n factor.

IID labeled observations
Stable reconstruction after retaining the compressed subset
0<delta<1
Risk is 0-1 classification error; consistency appears in the implication

Let N=N(n) with N/n->c in (0,infinity). For all n,i,j let X_ij^(n) be real independent identically distributed random variables with mean zero, variance one, and E|X_ij^(n)|^(4+epsilon)<infinity for some epsilon>0. Let sigma_ij(n) be deterministic real numbers uniformly bounded in absolute value. Let A_n be deterministic real N-by-n matrices whose row Euclidean norms and column Euclidean norms are uniformly bounded over all n and all rows and columns. Put (Y_n)_ij=sigma_ij(n) X_ij^(n)/sqrt(n) and Sigma_n=Y_n+A_n. For the relevant N,n, write A=A_n and sigma_ij=sigma_ij(n), D_j=diag(sigma_1j^2,...,sigma_Nj^2), and Dtilde_i=diag(sigma_i1^2,...,sigma_in^2). Let S_plus consist of the functions z->integral_[0,infinity) (lambda-z)^(-1) nu(dlambda) for probability measures nu on [0,infinity), analytically continued to C minus [0,infinity). Define the unique S_plus-valued solution psi_i,psitilde_j by psi_i(z)=-1/[z(1+tr(Dtilde_i Ttilde(z))/n)] and psitilde_j(z)=-1/[z(1+tr(D_j T(z))/n)], where Psi=diag(psi_i), Psitilde=diag(psitilde_j), T(z)=[Psi(z)^(-1)-z A Psitilde(z) A^T]^(-1), and Ttilde(z)=[Psitilde(z)^(-1)-z A^T Psi(z) A]^(-1). Both trace terms in these canonical equations use division by n. Set Q_n(z)=(Sigma_n Sigma_n^T-z I_N)^(-1) and Qtilde_n(z)=(Sigma_n^T Sigma_n-z I_n)^(-1). Almost surely, for every z in C minus [0,infinity), tr(Q_n(z)-T_n(z))/N->0 and tr(Qtilde_n(z)-Ttilde_n(z))/n->0 as n->infinity. The conclusion is for normalized unweighted resolvent traces of this independent-entry variance-profile model. The canonical measures can vary with n; convergence of the variance profiles to a limiting distribution is not an assumption.

uniformly bounded deterministic variance profile sigma_ij

noise normalization Y_ij=sigma_ij X_ij/sqrt(n)

[Theorem eq:conditional-remainder-cost of arXiv:2607.27613, 'Regularized Bulk Universality versus Bounded-Disorder Nonuniversality\\for Annealed Comple'] \label[theorem]{thm:one-spike}
Assume that \(J_{1\cdots1}\) has law \(\mu\).  Fix \(M<\infty\),
\(a>2M\), and \(\eta>0\).  Assume that the spike event below has
positive probability for all sufficiently large \(N\) and that
\begin{equation}
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
 \log\mathbb P\left(
 \left.\left\lVertR_N\right\rVert_\infty\le M\,\right|\,
 \frac{J_{1\cdots1}}{\sqrt N}\in[a,a+\eta]\right)=0.
\end{equation}
No assumptions of independence, centering, identical distribution, or
existence of a density are needed beyond this conditional-rate
hypothesis.  Then
\begin{equation}
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Crt}_{N,\max}^J([a-M,a+\eta+M])
 \ge-\overline I_\mu(a,\eta).
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log
 \mathbb E\operatorname{Crt}_N^J([a-M,a+\eta+M])
 \ge-\overline I_\mu(a,\eta).
\end{equation}

[Cor 2 of arXiv:2506.21829, 'Some notes on Lamperti's recurrence of stochastic sequences'] (Lamperti \cite{L}.)
Assume that a nonegative stochastic sequence $X_n$ satisfies \eqref{1}, and assume that for $x\to\infty$, we almost surely have
\begin{eqnarray}
\mu(x)&=&\mathsf{E}\{X_{n+1}-X_n~|~X_n=x, X_{n-1},\ldots,X_0\}=\frac{\xi}{2x}+O\left(\frac{1}{x^{1+\epsilon}}\right), \\
v(x)&=&\mathsf{E}\{(X_{n+1}-X_n)^2~|~X_n=x,  X_{n-1},\ldots,X_0\}=r^2+O\left(\frac{1}{x^{\epsilon}}\right),\nonumber\\
&&\text{where}\ \xi \ \text{is a positive value}.\nonumber
\end{eqnarray}
Then the stochastic sequence is recurrent, if for almost all $x\to\infty$,
\[
\mu(x)\leq \frac{v(x)}{2x}+O\left(\frac{1}{x^{1+\epsilon}}\right).
\]
If instead for some $\theta>1$ and  almost all large $x$,
\[
\mu(x)\geq\frac{\theta v(x)}{2x},
\]
then the stochastic sequence is transient. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cor 2 of arXiv:2506.21829

[Lemma 18 (Stable generator identity) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] Let $\mathcal S(\R)$ denote the Schwartz space and let $\mathcal S'(\R)$ denote the space of tempered distributions. Let $L^\alpha$ be the generator of the one-dimensional symmetric $\alpha$-stable process, with sign convention
\[
L^\alpha f(x)=\int_{\R\setminus\{0\}}\left(f(x+z)-f(x)-\1_{\{|z|\le1\}}zf'(x)\right)c_\alpha |z|^{-1-\alpha}\dd z.
\]
Then
\[
  L^\alpha u_{\delta,\eps}(x)=C_\alpha\psi_{\delta,\eps}(x)
\]
in the sense of distributions and pointwise for the mollified function, for some constant $C_\alpha>0$. Consequently, for a scale parameter $\gamma\in\R$,
\[
  L^\alpha_\gamma u_{\delta,\eps}(x)=C_\alpha |\gamma|^\alpha\psi_{\delta,\eps}(x),
\]
where
\[
L^\alpha_\gamma f(x):=\int_{\R\setminus\{0\}}\left(f(x+\gamma z)-f(x)-\1_{\{|z|\le1\}}\gamma z f'(x)\right)\nu(\md z).
\]

body:
[Proposition prop:first-cumulants of arXiv:2607.05693, 'Free multiplicative convolution and Erlang moments in monitored quantum transport'] The first three charge-transfer cumulants per channel are
\[
  \kappa_1(\tau)=\mathrm{e}^{-\tau},
\]
\[
  \kappa_2(\tau)=\left(\mathrm{e}^\tau-1-\tau\right)\mathrm{e}^{-2\tau},
\]
and
\[
  \kappa_3(\tau)
  =
  \left(
    \mathrm{e}^{2\tau}
    -3(1+\tau)\mathrm{e}^\tau
    +2+4\tau+3\tau^2
  \right)\mathrm{e}^{-3\tau}.
\]

body:
Fix alpha>0, rho>0 and lambda>0, all independent of the positive integer N. For each N let M_N=floor(exp(alpha N)), and let epsilon_(1,N),...,epsilon_(M_N,N) be independent centered Gaussian variables, each of variance rho^2/N. Define phi_N=(1/(lambda N)) log(sum_(mu=1)^(M_N) exp(lambda N epsilon_(mu,N))). On any common probability space for these arrays, phi_N converges almost surely to alpha/lambda+lambda rho^2/2 when lambda<=lambda_c=sqrt(2alpha)/rho, and to rho sqrt(2alpha) when lambda>=lambda_c. The two expressions agree at lambda_c. Independence is required within each N; no independence across different N is needed. Equivalently, for independent Gaussian patterns xi_mu~N(0,I_N) and a state x_N of norm rho sqrt(N), chosen independently of these patterns, one may take epsilon_(mu,N)=<x_N,xi_mu>/N. The result applies to that fixed state or independently chosen state sequence. It does not assert a uniform limit over pattern-dependent states or along an adaptive retrieval trajectory. This is the classical Gaussian random energy model condensation formula, used as a noise free-energy computation, not a retrieval or basin theorem. Source: Lucibello--Mezard, arXiv:2304.14964v4, equations (4)--(5), PDF p2; variational derivation Appendix A, PDF pp7--9. The exponentially large count may equally be exp(alpha N)-1 with the usual integer rounding, since its logarithmic rate is unchanged.
alpha,rho,lambda are fixed strictly positive real numbers
M_N=floor(exp(alpha N)); the energies within each N are independent N(0,rho^2/N)
All arrays are on a common probability space; arbitrary dependence across different N is permitted
For the pattern interpretation, x_N has norm rho sqrt(N) and is independent of every competing Gaussian pattern

Suppose that $\{X_t\}_{t=1}^{\infty}$ is an $(m-1)$th order regular Markov chain on state space $S$. Let $Q$ be the transition matrix of its reduced first order chain $\{Y_t\}_{t=1}^{\infty}$. If $\omega \in \mathbb R^N$ is a normalized nonnegative right eigenvector of $Q$ associated with dominant eigenvalue $1$, i.e. $Q\omega=\omega$, $\omega_i \ge 0$ for $i=1,2, \ldots, N$, and $\sum_{i=1}^{N} \omega_i=1$. Then,
\be

\pi = P^{(0)}\omega
\ee 
is a probability distribution in $\mathbb{R}^n$, which is a constant vector for any choice of $\omega$. Moreover, this $\pi$ is the unique limiting probability distribution satisfying (\ref{prob}). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 20 (The i.i.d.\ entry model) of arXiv:2608.04824, 'Strong Convergence for a General Class of Random Matrix Models'] Fix \(d\in\mathbb N\).  Given a probability space, let
\[
 \bigl(\xi^{(\kappa)}_{ij}\bigr)_{i,j\geq1},
 \qquad 1\leq\kappa\leq d,
\]
be mutually independent infinite arrays.  Within each color \(\kappa\), the
entries are i.i.d.\ copies of a complex random variable \(\xi^{(\kappa)}\)
satisfying
\[
 \E\xi^{(\kappa)}=0,
 \qquad
 \E|\xi^{(\kappa)}|^2=\sigma_\kappa^2,
 \qquad
 \E|\xi^{(\kappa)}|^4<\infty.
\]
For \(n\geq1\), set
\[
 X_{\kappa,n}
 =\frac1{\sqrt n}
   \bigl(\xi^{(\kappa)}_{ij}\bigr)_{1\leq i,j\leq n}.
\]
Thus, for each color, the unnormalized entry blocks are nested upper-left
corners of one infinite array; the matrix at size \(n\) is obtained by applying
the normalization \(n^{-1/2}\) to the corresponding corner.  This coupling
across \(n\) is used for every almost-sure statement below.  No restriction is
placed on
\(\E[(\xi^{(\kappa)})^2]\).
title: The i.i.d.\ entry model

body:
[Proposition 27 of arXiv:2604.20514, 'Macroscopic loops in the random loop model on sparse random graphs'] Fix \(u\in[0,1]\) and \(\theta>0\). Define
\[
C_\theta:=
\begin{cases}
1, & \theta=1,\\[1ex]
\dfrac{\theta |\log \theta|}{|\theta-1|}, & \theta\neq 1.
\end{cases}
\]

Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite graph with \(|V|=n\), and assume that for some \(\eta,\varepsilon>0\),
\[
e_G(S)\le (1+\varepsilon)|S|
\qquad\text{for every }S\subset V\text{ with }|S|\le \eta n.
\]
Assume moreover that
\[
\frac{|E|}{n}\in [m_-,m_+]
\]
for some \(m_-,m_+>0\).
Then for every \(a\ge 0\) and every \(s>0\),
\[
\frac1s\int_a^{a+s}\Pbb^G_{\theta,t,u}(A_\eta)\,\dd t
\ge
\frac{
m_- - c_{\theta,u}(1+\varepsilon)-C_\theta/s
}{
(1+\theta)m_+ - c_{\theta,u}(1+\varepsilon)
},
\]
provided the denominator is positive.

[Proposition 22 of arXiv:2608.18834, 'The Parabolic Anderson Model's Total Mass at Small Times: Geometry, Fluctuations, and Reno'] Suppose that Assumption \ref{Assumption} holds.
For every $t>0$ and $x\in(\mbb R^d)^2$,
there exists a random variable $\al_t(x)$ such that
\begin{align}

\lim_{\eps\to0}\al^\eps_t(x)=\al_t(x)
\qquad\text{in $L^p$ for all $p\geq1$}.
\end{align}
Moreover, for every $c>0$, there exists $\th_c>0$
such that for every $t\in(0,\th_c)$,
\begin{align}

\sup_{\eps>0,~x\in(\mbb R^d)^2}\mbf E\Big[\exp\big(c\al^\eps_t(x)\big)\Big],\sup_{x\in(\mbb R^d)^2}\mbf E\Big[\exp\big(c\al_t(x)\big)\Big]<\infty.
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:hypercube-entropy of arXiv:2605.17082, 'Spectral Purification in Reversible Markov Chains: Hidden Parameters, Observable Equivalen'] As $n \to \infty$ with $k = \frac{n}{4}\log n + \alpha n$, the spectral entropy satisfies
\[
S_{\mathrm{spec}}(k) =
\begin{cases}
\Omega(\log n), & \alpha \to -\infty, \\[2pt]
e^{-4\alpha} + O(e^{-8\alpha}), & \alpha = O(1), \\[2pt]
e^{-4\alpha} + o(1) \to 0, & \alpha \to +\infty.
\end{cases}
\]
The collapse from $\Omega(\log n)$ to $0$ occurs continuously over the window $\alpha = O(1)$, corresponding to $\Delta k = O(n)$ steps---precisely the cutoff phenomenon.

body:
Two distributions on a Euclidean space are (tau,delta)-close if they admit a coupling (X,X_hat) such that Pr(||X-X_hat||_2>tau)<delta. For a joint distribution of (X,Y), an algorithm taking y and outputting law p_hat_(.|y) is a (tau,delta)-posterior sampler if, with probability at least 1-delta over Y, its output law and the true conditional law p(.|Y) are (tau,delta)-close in this coupling sense. There are two failure probabilities: the exceptional-measurement probability delta, and the conditional coupling-failure probability delta on good measurements. The definition is not a TV-error bound or an every-fixed-observation guarantee. In the paper's linear model Y=A X+eta, ||A||_op<=1 and eta is independent N(0,beta^2 I_m); beta is the noise standard deviation.
Euclidean norm
conditional laws and the sampler's output laws are defined
nonnegative tau; delta in (0,1)
linear measurements only in the final model clause

[Defn def-fppray of arXiv:2412.03067, 'Geodesic Trees and Exceptional Directions in FPP on Hyperbolic Groups'] For  $\omega \in \Omega$, a semi-infinite (resp.\ bi-infinite) path $\sigma_\omega$ is said to be an $\omega-$geodesic ray (resp.\ a bi-infinite
		$\omega-$geodesic, or simply a bigeodesic) if every finite subpath of   $\sigma_\omega$ is an $\omega-$geodesic.
	
	A path $\sigma$ is said to  accumulate on $\xi \in {\partial G}$ if there exist $v_n \in  \sigma$ such that $v_n \to \xi$ as $n \to \infty$. 
		An $\omega-$geodesic ray $\sigma_\omega$ accumulating on $\xi\in {\partial G}$  has direction $\xi$ if its only accumulation point  in ${\partial G}$ is $\xi$.
title: Defn def-fppray of arXiv:2412.03067

[Lemma upper_bound_on_expected_number_of_occupation of arXiv:2505.07145, 'Nonamenable Poisson zoo'] Under the assumptions of 	Lemma~(lemma:size_biasing_for_Poisson_zoo of the paper),
let $\mathcal{X} = \sum_{i \in I} \delta_{(x,H)_i} \sim \mathcal{Q}_{\nu}^\lambda$.
Given any $A \in \mathcal{Z}$, let us denote the restricted zoo by $\bar{ \mathcal{X} } = \mathcal{X} \, \mathds{1} \left[ A \right]$ and the corresponding total occupation measure by $ \bar{\mu}(x) := \mu^{ \bar{ \mathcal{X} } }(x)$.

	
	
	
	
	
Then we have
\begin{equation}
	
	\sup_{x \in V(G)} \mathbb{E} \left. \left[ \bar{\mu}(x) \, \right| \, \bar{\mu}(x) > 0 \right] \leq \lambda \cdot m_1 + 1.
\end{equation}
If $\bar{ \mathcal{X} }$ and $x$ are such that $\bar{\mu}(x)=0$ a.s., we consider the conditional expectation to be 0.

[Corollary 19 (Local inverse regularity of the selected maps) of arXiv:2606.09121, 'Truncated Signature Information for Mixed Fractional Brownian Paths'] Let $\theta_0\in\mathcal P_K$ and let the scales in $\mathcal H$ be distinct.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item If $L\ge2K$, then there exist $r_2,c_2>0$ such that
\[
    \|\Psi_{\mathcal H}(\theta)-\Psi_{\mathcal H}(\theta_0)\|
    \ge c_2\|\theta-\theta_0\|
\]
for every $\theta\in\mathcal P_K$ with $\|\theta-\theta_0\|\le r_2$.
\item If $L\ge K$, then there exist $r_3,c_3>0$ such that
\[
    \|\Gamma_{\mathcal H}(\theta)-\Gamma_{\mathcal H}(\theta_0)\|
    \ge c_3\|\theta-\theta_0\|
\]
for every $\theta\in\mathcal P_K$ with $\|\theta-\theta_0\|\le r_3$.
\end{enumerate}

[Prop intersection of arXiv:2606.30517, '\textsc{Convergence towards Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations with a focus on Diestel--'] The pairwise intersections of the cells of ${\rm IPVT}({\rm DL}(p,q))$ satisfy the following almost surely:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
			\item  Two cells of different type have finite or empty intersection (resp.~adjacency). 
			\item  Two cells of the same type have infinite or empty intersection (resp.~adjacency).
			\item  In addition, every cell attains each of these intersection/adjacency types infinitely often.
		\end{enumerate}

body:
The alternative 'injective implies surjective' for operators of the form lambda I - K is carried entirely by two hypotheses: K is compact, and lambda is nonzero. (1) Compactness is load-bearing. On l^2 the unilateral shift S(x_1, x_2, ...) = (0, x_1, x_2, ...) is bounded and injective but not surjective, and S = I - K with K = I - S bounded but not compact; its index is -1, not 0. So for a general bounded perturbation of the identity the two alternatives can both fail to be the right dichotomy: the equation x - K x = y can be uniquely solvable for some y and unsolvable for others, with no finite-dimensional solvability condition of equal dimensions on the two sides. What actually powers the alternative is that the index is 0, which compactness guarantees; a Fredholm operator of nonzero index (like S) is a counterexample to the dichotomy but not to Fredholm theory. (2) lambda nonzero is load-bearing. Take K = diag(1, 1/2, 1/3, ...) on l^2, which is compact and injective, with dense but proper range (the sequence (1/n) is not in ran K, since it would need preimage (1, 1, 1, ...)). So for lambda = 0, 'injective' does not give 'surjective', the range is not closed, and 0 is in the spectrum of every compact operator on an infinite-dimensional space. (3) In the Hilbert-space version the solvability condition uses the conjugate: lambda x - K x = y is solvable exactly when y is orthogonal to ker(conjugate of lambda times I - K*), not to ker(lambda I - K*); forgetting the conjugation is a common slip for complex lambda. (4) The dimension identity dim ker(lambda - K) = dim ker(lambda - K') is an identity of the two kernels, not a claim that the kernels correspond naturally, and it fails for non-compact perturbations (for S, ker S = 0 while ker S' is one-dimensional).
the perturbation K is compact
lambda is a nonzero scalar
the ambient space is a Banach space (Hilbert space for the adjoint form with conjugated lambda)
title: Pitfall: The Fredholm Alternative Needs a Compact Perturbation and a Nonzero lambda

[Defn 6 (Sphere condition) of arXiv:2608.19104, 'Record times for coverage thresholds and maximal spacings'] Suppose $\partial A \in C^{1,1}$.
        For $z \in \partial A$ let $\hat n_z$ be the unit normal to $\partial A$ at $z$ pointing inside $A$.

        Given $\tau \geq 0$,
        let us say $\tau $ satisfies the {\em sphere condition}
         for $A$ if, for all $x \in \partial A$,
        we have $B(x+ \tau \hat n_x , \tau) \subset A$
        and  $B(x -\tau \hat n_x, \tau) \cap A = \{x\}$.

Let $\tau(A)$ denote the supremum of the set of all $\tau$ satisfying
the sphere condition for $A$.
title: Sphere condition

[Proposition prop:thin-box-upper-frame-obstruction of arXiv:2609.03264, 'Certified Spherical MUSIC for 3D Localization under Adversarial Subspace Perturbations'] There exist absolute constants \(c_0,\varepsilon_0>0\) with the
following property. For every \(0<\varepsilon\le\varepsilon_0\) and
every sufficiently large integer \(n\), there is a point cloud
\(X_n\subset B_1(0)\) with
\[
    s_n:=|X_n|=n^6,
    \qquad
    \delta_{X_n}=n^{-4},
\]
and a wavenumber
\[
    \kappa_n=\varepsilon n^6
\]
such that
\[
    \kappa_n\delta_{X_n}
    =
    \varepsilon n^2
    =
    \varepsilon s_n^{1/3},
\]
whereas the associated spherical Gram matrix satisfies
\[
    \lambda_{\max}(G_{X_n})
    \ge
    \frac{c_0}{\varepsilon}.
\]
Consequently, an arbitrary-cloud spherical frame upper bound cannot hold under a separation threshold
\(o(s^{1/3})\).

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2510.24244, 'Statistical properties of Markov shifts: part II-LLT'] Under Assumptions \ref{MixAss} and \ref{Assss} the following conditions are equivalent.
\vskip0.2cm
(1) $\liminf_{n\to\infty}\text{Var}(S_nf)<\infty$;
\vskip0.2cm
(2) $\sup_{n\in\bbN}\text{Var}(S_n f)<\infty$;

\vskip0.2cm
(3) we can write 
$$
f_j=\bbE[f_j(X_j,X_{j+1},...)]+M_j(X_j,X_{j+1},...)+u_{j+1}(X_{j+1},X_{j+2},...)-u_j(X_j,X_{j+1}...),\,\ \text{a.s.}
$$
where $\sup_j\|u_j\|_{j,\om}<\infty,$\;
$\sup_j\|M_j\|_{j,\om}\!\!<\!\!\infty$, \, $u_j$ and $M_j$ have zero mean and $M_j(X_j,X_{j+1},...),j\geq 0$ is a reverse martingale difference  with respect to the reverse filtration $\cG_j=\sigma\{X_k: k\geq j\}$ and\footnote{Note that by the martingale convergence theorem we get that the sum $\sum_{k=0}^\infty M_k(X_k,X_{k+1},...)$ converges almost surely and in $L^p$ for all finite $p$.} 
$$
\sum_{j\geq 0}\text{Var}(M_j(X_j,X_{j+1},...))\!\!<\!\!\infty.
$$
\vskip0.1cm
(4) there exist measurable functions $H_j:\cX_{j,\infty}\to\bbR$ such that 
$$
f_j(X_j,X_{j+1},...)=H_{j+1}(X_{j+1},X_{j+2},...)-H_j(X_j,X_{k+1},...)\,\,\text{ a.s.}
$$
In fact, we must have $H_j\in L^s(\ka_j)$ for all finite $s\leq b$ and, in fact, $H_j=\mu_j(H_j)+u_j(X_j,X_{j+1},...)+\sum_{k\geq j}M_k(X_k,X_{k+1},...)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\rho_{K_j}=|H_j\backslash G/H_j|.

Assume GRH for $\zeta_L$, and let
$V_j\asymp\sqrt{\log\log T}$.  Then
\begin{align*}

body:
DEFINITIONS. For a class C of subsets of X and points x_1, ..., x_n, the number of distinct traces |{ A intersect {x_1, ..., x_n} : A in C }| is at most 2^n; the growth (shatter) function is s(C, n) = max over all n-point sets of this number; the VC dimension d = VC(C) is the largest n with s(C, n) = 2^n (infinite if s(C, n) = 2^n for all n). Sauer-Shelah: if d < infinity then s(C, n) <= sum_{i <= d} binom(n, i) <= (e n / d)^d for n >= d. THEOREM (Vapnik and Chervonenkis, 1971). Let X_1, ..., X_n be i.i.d. from P and P_n the empirical measure. For every eps > 0 and n >= 2 / eps^2, P( sup_{A in C} |P_n(A) - P(A)| > eps ) <= 4 s(C, 2n) exp( -n eps^2 / 8 ); a form valid for all n is P( sup_{A in C} |P_n(A) - P(A)| > eps ) <= 8 s(C, n) exp( -n eps^2 / 32 ). COROLLARIES. If VC(C) = d < infinity, then sup_A |P_n(A) - P(A)| -> 0 almost surely for EVERY P (C is a uniform Glivenko-Cantelli class), with E sup_A |P_n(A) - P(A)| <= C_0 sqrt(d / n) for an absolute constant C_0 (Talagrand's sharpening of the log-free bound); the sample size n = O( (d log(1/eps) + log(1/delta)) / eps^2 ) makes the sup at most eps with probability 1 - delta; and the condition is also necessary: if VC(C) = infinity there is a distribution P for which the sup does not converge to 0 in probability (Vapnik-Chervonenkis; Assouad; Dudley). In learning: for a class of classifiers of VC dimension d, every classifier's true error is within eps of its training error simultaneously once n is of order d / eps^2 (up to logarithms), so empirical risk minimisation is consistent exactly for finite VC dimension (the fundamental theorem of statistical learning, PAC learnability iff finite VC dimension).
C a class of measurable sets (or of {0,1}-valued functions); the suprema are assumed measurable (a countable class, or the standard measurability conditions)
i.i.d. sampling from an arbitrary P on X
the constants 4, 8 and 8, 32 are the classical ones; several textbooks state slightly different constants from the same proof

(1) Ghost-sample symmetrisation. Let X_1', ..., X_n' be an independent copy of the sample and P_n' its empirical measure. If sup_A |P_n(A) - P(A)| > eps, fix a set A attaining more than eps; conditionally on the first sample, |P_n'(A) - P(A)| <= eps/2 with probability at least 1/2 whenever n eps^2 >= 2 (Chebyshev: Var P_n'(A) <= 1/(4n) <= eps^2 / 8), and then |P_n(A) - P_n'(A)| > eps/2. Hence P( sup_A |P_n(A) - P(A)| > eps ) <= 2 P( sup_A |P_n(A) - P_n'(A)| > eps / 2 ). (2) Random signs. The 2n points are exchangeable in pairs (X_i, X_i'), so swapping each pair by an independent Rademacher sign sigma_i does not change the law: P( sup_A |P_n(A) - P_n'(A)| > eps/2 ) = P( sup_A |(1/n) sum_i sigma_i (1_A(X_i) - 1_A(X_i'))| > eps/2 ). (3) Reduction to finitely many sets. Condition on the 2n points. The supremum over A depends only on the trace of A on these 2n points, so there are at most s(C, 2n) distinct events to control. For a fixed A, the variables sigma_i (1_A(X_i) - 1_A(X_i')) are independent, mean zero, valued in [-1, 1], so Hoeffding's inequality gives P_sigma( |(1/n) sum_i sigma_i (1_A(X_i) - 1_A(X_i'))| > eps/2 ) <= 2 exp( -2 n (eps/2)^2 / 4 ) = 2 exp( -n eps^2 / 8 ). (4) Union bound over the at most s(C, 2n) traces, then remove the conditioning and multiply by the factor 2 from step 1: P( sup_A |P_n(A) - P(A)| > eps ) <= 4 s(C, 2n) exp( -n eps^2 / 8 ). [Prop th-on-corep-sym-mon of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] There exists a unique strong symmetric monoidal structure on $\textbf{\textup{th}}$ such that the isomorphism from Construction~(constr:th-on-corep of the paper) becomes an isomorphism of symmetric monoidal functors.
    \begin{proof}
        As $\textbf{\textup{y}}_{/\textbf{\textup{Gr}}}$ contains the monoidal unit $0\colon\textbf{\textup{L}}(0,-)\to\textbf{\textup{Gr}}$, there is a unique isomorphism $\smash{S^0\cong\textbf{\textup{th}}(0)}$ compatible with the identification from Construction~(constr:th-on-corep of the paper); similarly, there is a unique compatible isomorphism $\textbf{\textup{th}}(-)\mathbin{\raise.5pt\hbox{\rlap{\lower.5pt\hbox{$\square$}}\kern.55pt$\smashp$\kern.55pt}}\textbf{\textup{th}}(-)\to\textbf{\textup{th}}(-\boxtimes-)$ on $(\textbf{\textup{y}}_{/\textbf{\textup{Gr}}})^{\textup{op}}$. By Lemma~(lemma:extend-nat-trafo of the paper) the latter uniquely extends to a transformation on all of $\cat{$\textbf{\textup{L}}$-Top}_{/\textbf{\textup{Gr}}}$, which is then necessarily an isomorphism. Moreover, appealing to uniqueness multiple times shows that this satisfies all the coherence conditions necessary for the structure map of a strong symmetric monoidal functor.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition \bf Quasi-leaf of arXiv:2603.28936, 'Composition of random functions and word reconstruction'] Let $w\in\{a,b\}^k$. A vertex $x\in [n]$ is a \emph{$w$-leaf} (or just \emph{leaf} if $w$ is clear from the context) if $\mathbf{w}^{-1}(x)=\emptyset$, or equivalently if there are no vertices at distance $k$ from $x$ in $B_{w}(x)$. A vertex $x\in [n]$ is a \emph{$w$-quasi-leaf} (or just \emph{quasi-leaf} if $w$ is clear from the context) if $\mathbf{w}^{-1}(x)$ is a subset of leaves, or equivalently if there are no vertices at distance $2k$ from $x$ in $B_{w^2}(x)$. 
We denote by $\mathcal{Q}_n=\mathcal{Q}_n^w$ the (random) set of quasi-leaves.
title: \bf Quasi-leaf

body: [Definition 253 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] A \emph{connectoid} is a symmetric $H \times H$ positive semi-definite matrix $\boldsymbol{\Theta}$ with entries in $\{0,\frac{1}{2},1\}$ and having the following connectedness property: for any $h,h' \in [H]$ there exists a finite sequence $h_0,\ldots,h_s$ with $h_0 = h$, $h_d = h'$ and for any $c \in [d]$ we have $\theta_{h_{c - 1},h_c} \neq 0$. A connectoid is \emph{realizable} if it comes from a graph $\mathsf{G}$ as in \eqref{ThetaGeq}; we can also ask for bipartite or non-bipartite realizability.

Let $A$ be measurable and uniformly parabolic with constants $\lambda,\Lambda$ and let $u\ge0$ be a local weak solution of $\partial_tu=\mathrm{div}(A\nabla u)$ in $B_{2r}(x_0)\times(t_0-4r^2,t_0)$. Set $Q^-=B_r(x_0)\times(t_0-3r^2,t_0-2r^2)$ and $Q^+=B_r(x_0)\times(t_0-r^2,t_0)$. Then $\sup_{Q^-}u\ \le\ C\,\inf_{Q^+}u$ with $C=C(n,\lambda,\Lambda)$. The time lag is essential and so is the direction: the past cylinder's supremum is controlled by the future cylinder's infimum, never the reverse, and no inequality of this form holds on a single time slice. Nonnegativity on the whole cylinder $B_{2r}\times(t_0-4r^2,t_0)$ is required. Consequences: interior Holder continuity of solutions, the near-diagonal lower bound for the fundamental solution, and (through chaining) Aronson's Gaussian lower bound; the inequality is equivalent to the conjunction of the volume doubling property and a Poincare inequality in the Grigor'yan-Saloff-Coste characterization on manifolds and graphs.
A measurable, uniformly parabolic with constants lambda, Lambda; divergence form
u >= 0 and a local weak solution on the whole cylinder B_{2r} x (t_0 - 4r^2, t_0)
the two cylinders are separated in time, with Q^- earlier than Q^+

[Corr FRSB of arXiv:2605.05631, 'Wandering Exponents and the Free Energy of the High-Dimensional Elastic Polymer'] Consider the model $B(x)=(1+x)^{-\gamma}$ for $\gamma<1$ at some fixed $(\beta,t)$. The Larkin mass $\mu_{Lar}(\beta;t)$ exists and is given by the unique $\mu$ which solves the equation
		\[2\gamma(\gamma+1)\left(1+\frac{2}{\beta \sqrt{\mu t}}\right)^{-\gamma-2}=\sqrt{\mu^3t}.\] 
		For all $\mu\ge \mu_{Lar}(\beta;t)$ the model is RS, and for all $\mu<\mu_{Lar}(\beta;t)$ the model is FRSB.\\
		
		\noindent Moreover, in the FRSB case, the Parisi pair, $(q_c,\zeta_c)$, in Theorem (theorem:intro:1-d continuum T>0:FRSB of the paper) may be found explicitly. The value for the unique triple $(q_0,q_*,q_c)$ immediately follows from the equations
		\[q_c-q_0=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{c_0}{\mu^{\frac{3}{2(2+\gamma)}}}-1\right),\;\;\; q_0=c_1\mu^{\frac{3(\gamma+1)}{2(2+\gamma)}+3},\;\;\; q_c-q_*=\frac{1}{\beta\sqrt{\mu_{Lar}(\beta;t)t}}, \]
		with constants given by $c_0=(\frac{2\gamma(\gamma+1)}{\sqrt{t}})^{1/(\gamma+2)}$ and $c_1=\frac{\gamma t}{c_0^{1+\gamma}}$. The measure $\zeta$ can then be found from its CDF, which is given for $s\in [q_0,q_*)$ by 
		\[\zeta_c([0,s])=\frac{\gamma+2}{3\beta}\left(\frac{4}{t\gamma(\gamma+1)}\right)^{1/3}(1+2q_c-2s)^{\frac{\gamma-1}{3}}, \]
		and otherwise by $\zeta_c([0,s])=0$ if $s\in [0,q_0)$ and $\zeta_c([0,s])=1$ if $s\in [q_*,q_c]$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corr FRSB of arXiv:2605.05631

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The orthogonal polynomials for $L^2(\mathbb R)$, with scalar product
$$<f,g>=\int_0^\infty f(x)g(x)e^{-x^2}\,dx$$
are the Hermite polynomials $\{P_k\}$, satisfying the following differential equation,
$$P_k''(x)-2xP_k'(x)+P_k(x)=0$$
as well as the following order $2$ recurrence relation,
$$P_{k+1}(x)=2xP_k(x)-2kP_{k-1}(x)$$
and which are given by the following formula,
$$P_k(x)=(-1)^k e^{x^2}\cdot\frac{d^k}{dx^k}\big(e^{-x^2}\big)$$
called Rodrigues formula for the Hermite polynomials.
title: Unnumbered theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'

[Proposition prop:CSPI of arXiv:2509.04155, 'An Approach to Sub-Gaussian Heat Kernel Estimates via Analysis on Metric Spaces'] Let $p^* \in (p,\infty]$ be given by
    \[
    p^* := 
    \begin{cases}
        pQ_U/(Q_U - \beta_L) & \text{ if } \beta_L < Q_U\\
        \infty & \text{ if } \beta_L \geq Q_U.
    \end{cases}
    \]
    Then the reference measure $\mu$ satisfies the following Sobolev--Poincar\'e inequality for all $q \in [1,p^*)$.
    There are constant $C,\sigma \geq 1$ such that for all $f \in \mathcal{F}_p$,
    \[
        \left( \vint_{B(x,r)} \abs{f - f_{B(x,r)}}^q \, d\mu \right)^{\frac{1}{q}} \leq C \left(\frac{\Psi(x,r)}{\mu(B(x,r))} \int_{B(x,\sigma r)} \, d\Gamma_p\Span{f} \right)^{\frac{1}{p}}.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:CSPI of arXiv:2509.04155

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2607.25949, 'Block-hierarchical covariance decompositions for finite-block additive functionals'] (Shift-inherited eigenvalues).
Let \(\{X_t\}_{t\in\mathbb Z}\) be a stationary Markov chain. Let \(2\le m\le k\) and let $h\in \mathcal I_m$.
Define
\[
\widehat{h}_{m,k}(x_1,\ldots,x_k)
=
\sum_{i=1}^{k-m+1}
h(x_i,\ldots,x_{i+m-1}).
\]
For this function the Green--Kubo series is finite, and
\[
B_k \widehat{h}_{m,k}=(k-m+1) \widehat{h}_{m,k}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 4 of arXiv:2607.25949

[Corollary cor:growth-bound-partition-functions of arXiv:2509.04333, 'The limiting law of the Discrete Gaussian level lines'] For any $A', B'$ in $Q$, we have
		\begin{equation*}
			Z^n_{Q, \mathbb Z^2; F, \mu}(A', B') = \sum_{\gamma \in \ensuremath{\mathcal P}_Q(A', B')} q^n_{\mathbb Z^2; F, \mu}(\gamma) \leq \exp({\ensuremath{\mathscr G}}^n_\mu(\ell_{A', B'}, \theta_{A', B'}) + O((\log L)^{2a}))\,.
		\end{equation*}
		Let $W$ be any region containing the infinite vertical strip between the lines $x = A'_1 + (\log L)^2$ and $x = B'_1 - (\log L)^2$. The same bound holds if we replace the weight $q^n_{\mathbb Z^2; F, \mu}(\gamma)$ with $q^n_{W; F, \mu}(\gamma)$, or with 
		\[\exp\big(-{\ensuremath{\mathscr E}}^*_\beta(\gamma)+ \frac{\mu}{N_n}\ensuremath{\mathcal A}_F(\gamma) + \mathfrak{I}_W(\gamma) -\Delta\mathfrak{I}_W(\gamma, \gamma_\mathsf{left})\big)\]
		uniformly over all $\gamma_{\mathsf{left}} \in \ensuremath{\mathcal P}_Q(A, A')$, with $\Delta\mathfrak{I}_W(\gamma, \gamma_\mathsf{left})$ defined as in (eq:correction-term of the paper).

body: [Lemma compatible sequence of arXiv:2605.03151, 'Giants through Higher-Order paths in Random Simplicial Complexes'] Let $\left( (X_r, \sigma_r) \right)_{r \geq 0}$ be a sequence of $(k+1)$-connected $k$-rooted simplicial complexes locally finite above dimension $k$. Assume that the sequence $\left( (X_r, \sigma_r) \right)_{r \geq 0}$ is compatible in the sense that $B_{X_s}(\sigma_s; r) \cong (X_r, \sigma_r)$ for all $s \geq r$. Then there exists a $(k+1)$-connected $k$-rooted simplicial complex $(X, \sigma)$ that is locally finite above dimension $k$ and $(X_r, \sigma_r) \cong B_X(\sigma; r)$ for every $r \geq 0$. Moreover, $(X, \sigma)$ is unique up to isomorphisms.

\begin{equation}
\E_{\nu^r_T}\Big[ \Phi(\psi)\E_{\mu^{N,\psi}_T}[G(x)]\Big]

\E_{m^{N}_T}\Big[G(x)\,  \E_{\gamma^{\bbH,x}_{T/N}}[\Phi(\psi)]\Big]
,
\end{equation}

where $\gamma^{\bbH,x}_{T/N}$ is the Gaussian measure on $\bbH$ with variance $T/N$ (as in (equation eq: Gaussian H of the paper)) and mean 
$\big( \frac{1}{N}\sum_i n_k(x_i) \big)_{k \geq -d}$.

[Theorem of arXiv:2604.04747, 'Scaling limit and density conjecture for activated random walk on the complete graph'] \thlabel{thm:density}  Suppose that $m_n = \lceil \mu n\rceil $ for $\mu \in (0,1]$. 
    \begin{enumerate}[label = (\alph*)]
        \item If $\mu >p$, then $\mathfrak{J} \geq e^{cn}$ w.h.p.\ for some $c = c(\mu,p)>0$.
        \item If $\mu =p$, then $\mathfrak{J} / (n \log n) \overset{\mathbf{P}} \to 1/2$.
        \item If $\mu <p$, then $\mathfrak{J} \leq C n$ w.h.p.\ for some
        $C = C(\mu,p)< \infty$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Cor 36 of arXiv:2605.26664, 'Mixing times for Glauber dynamics of lozenge tilings of the hexagon'] { There exists a constant $C>1$ such that the following holds.} Fix $z = (x,y) \in \mathfrak{L}_{q;a,b,c}$, such that $x \ge x^{SW}_{q;a,b,c}$ and $\ell_z$ is the southwest edge of $\mathfrak{X}_{a,b,c}$. {Then, for any nonnegative $h \in [\mathcal{H}_{q;a,b,c} (z) - N^{-1}, \mathcal{H}_{q;a,b,c} (z) + N^{-1}]$ and $\textbf{V} \in \{ \bm{v}_z^{\perp}, \bm{w}_{z;q} \}$, we have $\dist_{\textbf{V}} (z, \mathcal{U}_{q;a,b,c}^h) \le C (\md_z \me_{z;q}^{-1})^{1/2} N^{-1}$.}

body: Let 1 <= p < infinity and let Omega be a bounded connected open subset of R^n with Lipschitz boundary. Poincare-Wirtinger form: there is a constant C depending only on p and Omega such that ||u - u_Omega||_{L^p(Omega)} <= C ||grad u||_{L^p(Omega)} for every u in W^{1,p}(Omega), where u_Omega denotes the average of u over Omega. Zero-boundary form: for u in W_0^{1,p}(Omega), with Omega merely bounded in one direction, ||u||_{L^p(Omega)} <= C ||grad u||_{L^p(Omega)}, so the gradient term alone is an equivalent norm on W_0^{1,p}(Omega). The inequality says a Sobolev function is controlled by its gradient once its mean (or boundary value) is pinned; it is the engine behind coercivity of variational problems, spectral gaps for the Laplacian, and compactness arguments.
title: Poincare inequality

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2609.01166, 'Nonparametric inference for density-dependent McKean--Vlasov diffusions'] For every candidate $\xi$, and \(M>v_\star\),
\begin{eqnarray}
 \KL(\pi_0\Vert\pi_\xi)
 &=& (1-\tau_0(M))\KL(\pi_0^M\Vert\pi_\xi^M) + (1-\tau_0(M))\log\frac{1-\tau_0(M)}{1-\tau_\xi(M)} + R_\xi(M)\\
 &\leq& \KL(\pi_0^M\Vert\pi_\xi^M)+d_m(M)+\bar R_m(M),
\end{eqnarray}
where $R_\xi(M):=\int_{A_M^c}\pi_0(x) \log(\pi_0(x)/\pi_\xi(x))\,\dd x$. Moreover, 
\begin{equation}
\KL(\pi_0^M\Vert\pi_\xi^M)
\leq \frac{1}{c_M}\left(
\KL(\pi_0\Vert\pi_\xi)+d_m(M)+\bar R_m(M)
\right)
\end{equation}
with \(c_M:=\int_{A_M} e^{-K(V(x)-v_\star)}\,dx\left(\int_{\R^d} e^{-\kappa(V(x)-v_\star)}\,dx\right)^{-1}\in(0,1)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 5 of arXiv:2609.01166

time-\((-1)\) model of every tangent space at \(\xi\) splits globally,
isometrically, and biholomorphically as

 (Z,d,J)\cong(\C^m,g_{\rm E},J_0)\times(Z',d',J').

[Theorem thm:multil of arXiv:2411.10829, 'Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble and its Laplace transform'] Choose $m\in \mathbb N$, $\vec \mathbf k \in \mathbb R^m_+ $, and $\vec \boldsymbol{\tau}\in \mathbb R_{\ge 0}^m$ such that $\boldsymbol{\tau}_1\le \cdots \le \boldsymbol{\tau}_m$, any real $C_1>0$, and a large enough $N\in \mathbb N$. We take the rank $N$ G$\beta$E corners process $\{y^n_i\}_{1\leq i\leq n\leq N}$, with variance $\tau=2N/\beta$; and $\vec k \in \mathbb Z^m$, and integers $N\ge N_1\ge \cdots \ge N_m$,  such that
\begin{equation} 
|k_\ell-\mathbf k_\ell N^{2/3}|<C_1, \qquad  |N - \boldsymbol{\tau}_\ell N^{2/3}-N_\ell|<C_1, \qquad \text{for each }\ell\in\llbracket 1,m\rrbracket.
\end{equation}
Then as $N\to\infty$, uniformly over the ($N$--dependent) choices of $\vec k$ and $\vec N$ satisfying (equation eq_x1 of the paper):
\[
 \mathbb E \left[ \prod_{\ell=1}^m \left(\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{N_\ell} \left(\frac{y^{N_\ell}_i}{2\sqrt{N_\ell N}}\right)^{k_\ell}+\left(\frac{y^{N_\ell}_i}{2\sqrt{N_\ell N}}\right)^{k_\ell+1}\right) \right]\to \mathbf L_\beta(\vec \mathbf k, \vec\boldsymbol{\tau}).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:multil of arXiv:2411.10829

body: [Proposition 2.6 (Lemma 2.4 [BT17]) of arXiv:2512.05720, 'First-passage percolation, non-positive curvature, and radial maps'] Let $X$ be an infinite connected graph with bounded degree and assume that $\nu({0})=0.$ There exists an increasing function $\alpha:(0,\infty)\to(0,1]$ such that $\lim_{t\to 0}\alpha(t)=0,$ and such that for all finite path $\gamma$ and all $\epsilon>0,$ $\mathbb{P}(|\gamma|_{\omega}\leq\epsilon|\gamma|)\leq\alpha(\epsilon)^{|\gamma|}.$

body:
Hanin-Nica, Finite Depth and Width Corrections to the Neural Tangent Kernel, arXiv1909.05989v1, Section2 and Theorem1 (PDFp4), is a source for initialization moments of the diagonal NTK of a fully connected ReLU network. Its setting uses a scalar output, zero-initialized but trainable biases, independent identically distributed raw weights with a Lebesgue density, symmetry about zero, variance one and finite fourth moment. Its Theorem1 gives an exact first-moment formula and a two-sided comparison for the second moment, including an exponential factor in a sum of inverse widths and a multiplicative error involving a sum of inverse squared widths. A comparison E[K^2] comparable to (E[K])^2 exp(5 beta) does not by itself establish Var(K)=O(1/n), even if beta tends to zero: the unspecified comparison constants prevent subtracting (E[K])^2 to obtain that rate. This comparison is also not a quantitative theorem for arbitrary smooth activations or transposed/reused-matrix Tensor Programs. Before using the exact formulas, resolve these printed-v1 conventions: Section2 prose says the output is linear but Eq2 applies ReLU for i=1,...,d; Eq3 prints reciprocal square-root normalization factors; beta is defined by a sum through d while n_d=1 is specified, whereas the equal-hidden-width consequence writes beta=d/n. These are unresolved source-interpretation questions, not a refutation of the authors intended theorem. This card records source scope and the limitation of a second-moment comparison; it does not assert a corrected NTK theorem or an NTK nonconcentration inference from moments alone.
Source-v1 scope note; intended endpoint and normalization conventions remain for independent source review.

body: Lemma (campaign status: proved): For twelve nonzero coefficients, an affine atom which is not the central atom of twelve equal magnitudes has size at most $792$. Unequal-magnitude case: reorient positively and condition on an unequal pair; its four signed sums are distinct, and the ten-coordinate subsets hitting one of the four required targets form a four-Sperner family, so their total is at most $\binom{10}{5}+2\binom{10}{4}+\binom{10}{3}=252+210+210+120=792$. Equal magnitudes with noncentral target: largest noncentral layer is $\binom{12}{5}=792$. A three-sign affine atom has size three only for three equal magnitudes at a one-minority target; otherwise at most two. Notes: VERIFIED: $252+420+120=792$. Consequence: more than $2592$ joint states forces both own-layer rows to be equimodular, since otherwise the joint count is at most $3\cdot792=2376$ or $2\cdot924=1848$. The four-Sperner step is the reusable device.

[Proposition 46 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Assume $q\in C([-L,L])$, $q\ge q_0>0$, $a\in C([-L,L])$, $m\ge0$ and $J(0)>0$. Put
\[
T_q=\int_{-L}^{L}\frac{dx}{q(x)},\qquad
A_q=\int_{-L}^{L}\frac{a(x)}{q(x)}\,dx,
\]
and
\[
C_m:=\mathbf 1_{\{m=0\}}
+\frac1{T_q}\left[
2\log\frac{m+1}{T_q}-\log\big(J(0)q(-L)\big)-A_q
\right].
\]
Then
\[
\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})
=\frac{m+1}{T_q}\log\sigma
+\frac{2}{T_q}\log\log\sigma
+C_m+o(1)
\qquad(\sigma\to+\infty).
\]
In particular, $\Lp(\cA_{\sigma,m,L})\to+\infty$.

[Theorem theorem-energy-equality of arXiv:2411.04500, '\LARGE Probabilistic Approaches to The Energy Equality in Forced Surface Quasi-Geostrophic'] Assume further that $ \beta=\alpha/2.$	Let $\mathcal{C}_0\subset \mathbb{X}_{\alpha,\alpha/2}$ be a weak-strong uniqueness class of (equation PDE-SQG of the paper) such that $\mathcal{C}=\overline{\mathcal{C}_0}^{\mathcal{I}}$ contains non-empty time-reversible subsets. Let $\mathcal{R} \subset \mathcal{C}$ satisfy  $\mathcal{R}=\mathfrak{T}_T \mathcal{R}.$  Suppose that $ \theta\in \mathcal{R} $ is  a weak solution of (equation PDE-SQG of the paper) for some $g \in L^2([0, T];H)$ in the sense of Definition (def-weak-solution-skeleton-equation of the paper). Then the kinetic energy equality holds:
	\begin{equation}

	\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition conv of arXiv:2412.06701, 'Matsumoto-Yor processes on Jordan algebras'] Let $T\ge 0$. If $\widetilde{G}_k^n=P(w_1^n)\dots P(w_k^n)$, for $k\ge 0$, then 
 
the sequence of processes 
$$ \widetilde{g}^{(n)} = \left(\widetilde{g}^{(n)}_t := \widetilde{G}_{\lfloor nt\rfloor}^n \ ; \ t\in [0,T] \right), \, n\ge 1, $$ 
converges in law in $\mathcal D([0,T],G)$ equipped with the Skorokhod topology towards the diffusion $(\widetilde{g}_t \ ; \ t \in [0,T])$. Moreover, the sequence of processes $$\left(\Lambda_{\lfloor nt\rfloor}^n,L_{\lfloor nt\rfloor}^n,I_{\lfloor nt\rfloor}^n \ ; \ t\in [0,T]\right), \, n\ge 1,$$ converges in law in $\mathcal D([0,T],E^{\times 3})$ towards $\left(\widetilde\lambda_t,\widetilde\ell_t,\widetilde\iota_t \ ; \ t\in [0,T]\right)$.
title: Proposition conv of arXiv:2412.06701
