[Theorem 9 (Abbreviated version of the main results) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] \hfill
		
		\begin{itemize} 
			\item \underline{\textbf{Assumptions.}} Let $(\LogDensity^1|_{\Sigma_0},v^1|_{\Sigma_0}, v^2|_{\Sigma_0},v^3|_{\Sigma_0},\Ent|_{\Sigma_0}) \in C^\infty(\Sigma_0)^{\times 5}$ be  smooth functions satisfying the same assumptions (e.g. quantitative transversal convexity, Sobolev regularity, etc.) as in \cite{abbrescia2022emergence}. In particular, there exists an acoustical eikonal function $u$ solving the eikonal equation $(\gfour^{-1})^{\alpha\beta}\p_\alpha u \p_\beta u = 0$, and a rough time function 
				$\timefunctionarg{0} = \timefunctionarg{0}(t,u,x^2,x^3)$ solving $\muX \timefunctionarg{0} =0$
				with range $[\timefunction_0,0] = [-\mupositive,0]$ such that $(\timefunctionarg{0},u,x^2,x^3)$ form a global coordinate system on 
				$\twoargMrough{[\timefunction_0,0],[- \rightu,\leftu]}{0}
				= \bigcup_{\timefunction \in [\timefunction_0,0]} \hypthreearg{\timefunction}{[- \rightu,\leftu]}{0}
				$. This is a compact portion of the maximal classical development 
				of the data up to its boundary with respect to the differential structure of the geometric coordinates $(t,u,x^2,x^3)$, where $\rightu,\leftu > 0$ depend only on the background solution. With respect to this differential structure of the geometric coordinates, the $C^{3,1}$-norm of the solution variables $\wavearray = (\RRiemann,\LRiemann,v^2,v^3,\Ent)$ remain bounded on $\twoargMrough{[\timefunction_0,0],[- \rightu,\leftu]}{0}$, and $\upmu > 0$ everywhere on  $\twoargMrough{[\timefunction_0,0],[- \rightu,\leftu]}{0}$ except for the crease $\twoargmumuxtorus{0}{0} = \crease$, where it vanishes: $\upmu|_{\twoargmumuxtorus{0}{0}} = 0$. The change of variables map $\Upsilon(t,u,x^2,x^3) = (t,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ is a diffeomorphism everywhere on $\twoargMrough{[\timefunction_0,0],[- \rightu,\leftu]}{0}$ onto its image except for the crease $ \crease$, where it is merely a homeomorphism. There is gradient blow-up along $\crease$ relative to Cartesian differential structure of $(t,x^1,x^2,x^3)$ in that the following estimate holds on $\Upsilon\left(\twoargMrough{[\timefunction_0,0],[- \interestingu,\interestingu]}{0} \right)$, where $0 < \interestingu <  \min\{1,\leftu,\rightu,\frac{1}{22}\blowupdelta^{-1}\}$:
				\begin{align}
					|\partial_{x^\alpha} \RRiemann|, |\partial_{x^\alpha} v^1|,|\partial_{x^\alpha} \LogDensity| \gtrsim \frac{1}{\upmu}. 
				\end{align}
				The solution is smooth on 	$\Upsilon\left(\twoargMrough{[\timefunction_0,0],[- \interestingu,\interestingu]}{0} \setminus \crease \right)$, while for $\alpha = 0,1,2,3$, $i=1,2,3$, and $A=2,3$,
		the fluid quantities 
		$\LogDensity$,

		$\Ent$, 
		$\Flatcurl v^i$, 
		$\partial_i \Ent$, 
		and 
		$\gfour_{ab} \Yvf{A}^a \partial_{\alpha} v^b$
		remain bounded on all of $\Upsilon(\twoargMrough{[\timefunction_0,0],[- \interestingu,\interestingu]}{0})$. 
			\item \underline{\textbf{Ingoing eikonal function, double-null coordinates, and the characteristic diamond.}}
				There exists an \emph{ingoing} acoustical eikonal function $\ubar$ solving $(\gfour^{-1})^{\alpha\beta}\p_\alpha \ubar \p_\beta \ubar = 0$ with initial data $\ubar|_{\datahypfortimefunctiontwoarg{0}{[\timefunction_0,0]}} = - \upmu|_{\datahypfortimefunctiontwoarg{0}{[\timefunction_0,0]}}$. [Theorem 1 of arXiv:2609.04155, 'The subconvexity problem for symmetric square\\ $L$-functions in Level aspect'] Let $\pi\simeq\bigotimes_\nu^\prime\pi_\nu$ be a cuspidal automorphic representation for $\GL_2(\Q)$ of arithmetic conductor $q(\pi)=p^2$, with the central character $\omega_\pi$, the adelic lift of a primitive non-quadratic Dirichlet character $\chi_\pi$ modulo $p$. If $\pi_\nu$ is tempered for all $\nu<\infty$, $\pi_p\in\mathcal S$, and the spectral parameters of $\pi_\infty$ be bounded, then we have the following subconvex bound, 
         \[
         L\left(\frac{1}{2},\, \sym^2\pi\right)\ll_{\eps, \pi_\infty}q(\sym^2\pi)^{\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{168}+\eps},
         \]
         where the implied constants depends on $\eps$, and polynomially on spectral parameters of $\pi_\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop 13 of arXiv:2609.03185, 'Uniqueness of tangent flows in free boundary flow'] There are $C, L, \epsilon > 0$ and $\gamma \in (0,1)$ with the following property. Suppose that 
$$\tau_0^{-1}, \sup\limits_{s\in [0,1]} d_V(\mu_{\mathscr{C}_+}, \mu_{M_{\tau_0-s}}), \mathcal A^\gamma (M_{\tau_0 - 1}) - \lim\limits_{\tau \to \infty} \mathcal A^\gamma(M_\tau) \leq \epsilon.$$
Then one of the following holds:
\begin{enumerate} [label=\normalfont(\roman*) ]
\item $\mathcal{D}(M_{\tau_0 + L}, M_{\tau_0 + 2L}) \leq Ce^{-\frac{\tau_0}{8}}.$
\item $\mathcal{D}(M_{\tau_0 + L}, M_{\tau_0 + 2L}) \leq \frac{1}{2} \mathcal{D}(M_{\tau_0}, M_{\tau_0 + L}).$
\item $\mathcal{D}(M_{\tau_0 + L}, M_{\tau_0 + 2L}) \leq C \Big(\mathcal A^\gamma(M_{\tau_0 + L}) -\mathcal A^\gamma(M_{\tau_0 + 2L}) \Big).$
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Prop ProdContSing of arXiv:2609.01501, 'Singularities of star cluster algebras'] Let $ \mathfrak{X} := V(h) \subseteq \ensuremath{\mathbb{A}}_\kappa^{\ell_1+\cdots + \ell_m} $,
	where
	\[
		h := \prod_{\alpha=1}^m P_{\ell_\alpha} (z_1^{(\alpha)}, \ldots, z_{\ell_\alpha}^{(\alpha)}) + \delta 
		\in \kappa [ z_1^{(\alpha)}, \ldots, z_{\ell_\alpha}^{(\alpha)} \mid \alpha \in \{ 1, \ldots, m \}]
	\]
	with 
	$ \delta \in \kappa $. 
	If $ \delta $ is invertible, 
	then $ \mathfrak{X} $ is singular if and only if the following two conditions hold:
	\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
		\item[(a)] 
		$ \ell_\alpha = 2 k_\alpha $ is even, 
		with $  k_\alpha \geq 1 $,
		for all $ \alpha \in \{ 1, \ldots, m \} $, and 
		
		\item[(b)] 
		$ (-1)^{k_1 + \cdots + k_m} + \delta  = 0 $.
	\end{enumerate}
	In the singular case, $ \Sing (\mathfrak{X}) $ is the origin and the hypersurface $ \mathfrak{X} $ has an isolated singularity of type $ A_1 $ at the origin. 
	\\
	On the other hand, if $ \delta = 0 $, then 
	$ \mathfrak{X} $ is a simple normal crossing divisor with $ m $ disjoint irreducible components, 
	i.e., after a suitable choice of coordinates $ h $ is of the form $ x_1 \cdots x_m $ with $ (x_1, \ldots, x_m) $ part of the chosen coordinates.

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.26996, 'A note on shifting distributions via Poisson races'] Let $P,Q$ be two distributions over the same finite set.
If $D(Q||P) < \infty$ then
there is a $P$ to $Q$ simulator $I$ such that
\begin{align*}
\E [\log I] 
\leq D(Q||P) + 1.45 \|Q-P\|_1.
\end{align*}
On the other hand, for every $P$ to $Q$ simulator $I$,
\[\E[\log I] \geq \frac{1}{2} \max \{ D(Q||P),  \|Q-P\|_1 \}.\]
In particular, if $D(Q||P)=\infty$ then there is no $P$ to $Q$ simulator. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.26996

[Lemma small-class-of-colimits-cc of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $\textbf{\textup{U}}\subset\ul\Cat_T$ be small. Then the $\infty$-category $\Cat_T^\textup{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}$ of $\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cocomplete small $T$-$\infty$-categories and $\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cocontinuous functors has small colimits, and for any small diagram ${\mathcal{C}}_\bullet\colon I\to\Cat_T^\textup{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}$ and any ${\mathcal{D}}\in\Cat_T^\textup{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}$ the induced map
    \begin{equation}
        \ul{\textup{Fun}}_T^\textup{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}(\mathop{\textup{colim}}\nolimits_I {\mathcal{C}}_\bullet,{\mathcal{D}})\to\lim\nolimits_{I^{\textup{op}}}\ul{\textup{Fun}}_T^\textup{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}({\mathcal{C}}_\bullet,{\mathcal{D}})
    \end{equation}
    is invertible.
    \begin{proof}
        Fix any small diagram ${\mathcal{C}}_\bullet\colon I\to\Cat_T^\textup{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}$ and an extension to a colimit diagram $I^\triangleright\to\Cat_T$. Writing $\infty$ for the terminal object of $I^\triangleright$, it follows that for any $\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cocomplete ${\mathcal{D}}$, the induced equivalence
        \[
            {\textup{Hom}}_{\Cat_T}({\mathcal{C}}_\infty,{\mathcal{D}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}\lim\nolimits_{I^{\textup{op}}}{\textup{Hom}}_{\Cat_T}({\mathcal{C}}_\bullet,{\mathcal{D}})
        \]
        then restricts to an equivalence between the union of those path components of the left-hand side given by functors $F\colon{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{D}}$ such that each ${\mathcal{C}}_i\to{\mathcal{C}}\to{\mathcal{D}}$ is $\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cocontinuous and $\lim_{I^{\textup{op}}}{\textup{Hom}}_{\Cat_T^\textup{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}}({\mathcal{C}}_\bullet,{\mathcal{D}})$. On the other hand, [martiniwolf2022presentable]*{Proposition~A.4.2 and Remark~A.4.3} yield a map ${\mathcal{C}}_\infty\to{\mathcal{C}}_\infty'$ to a small $\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cocomplete $T$-$\infty$-category such that ${\textup{Hom}}_{\Cat_T^\textup{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}}({\mathcal{C}}_\infty',{\mathcal{D}})\to{\textup{Hom}}_{\Cat_T}({\mathcal{C}}_\infty,{\mathcal{D}})$ defines an equivalence of the union of the same set of path components. This provides the desired colimit.
        
        To see that $((eq:internal-colimit of the paper))$ is an equivalence, it suffices by the (non-parametrized) Yoneda lemma, that the induced map on ${\textup{Hom}}({\mathcal{K}},-)$ is an equivalence for every ${\mathcal{K}}\in\Cat_T$. However, this induced map may be identified with the equivalence
        \[
            {\textup{Hom}}_{\Cat_T^\text{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}}(\mathop{\textup{colim}}\nolimits_I{\mathcal{C}}_\bullet,{\textup{Fun}}({\mathcal{K}},{\mathcal{D}}))\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}
            \lim\nolimits_{I^{\textup{op}}}{\textup{Hom}}_{\Cat_T^\text{$\textbf{\textup{U}}$-cc}}({\mathcal{C}}_\bullet,{\textup{Fun}}({\mathcal{K}},{\mathcal{D}})).
            \qedhere
        \]        
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma small-class-of-colimits-cc of arXiv:2608.28504

[Definition 5 of arXiv:2607.02777, 'Hypocoercivity for Hamiltonian Diffusions \\ with Singular Drift'] A probability measure $\P$ on $\sZ$ is said to be a solution to the martingale problem associated with $(\sL, \core)$ if for every $f\in \core=C^2_c(\Omega_1\times \Omega_2)$
        \[
            M^f_t:= f(X_t , Y_t ) - f(X_0, Y_0) - \int_0^t \sL f (X_s, Y_s) \,\textup{d}s , \quad t\geq 0, 
        \]
       where $f(\partial)\defeq 0$ and $(\sL f)(\partial)\defeq  0$, is a continuous martingale under $\P$ with respect to the filtration $(\sF_{t+})_{t\geq 0}$.
title: Definition 5 of arXiv:2607.02777

body:
[Def D2.1 of arXiv:2609.03848, 'The mean-field limit of the Schr\"{o}dinger-Lohe model\\ and emergent dynamics'] \emph{[C-C-H]}
Let $\Psi := \{ \psi_k \}$ be a global smooth solution to (equation SL of the paper). 
\begin{enumerate}
\item
The ensemble $\Psi$ exhibits {\em complete synchronization}, if the following estimate holds:
\[ 
\lim_{t \to \infty} \max_{1\le k,l\le N} \| \psi_l(t) - \psi_k(t) \|_{\mathfrak{H}} = 0. 
\]
\item
The ensemble $\Psi$ exhibits {\em practical synchronization},  if the following estimate holds:
\[ 
\lim_{\kappa \to \infty} \limsup_{t \to \infty} \max_{1\le k,l\le N} \| \psi_l(t) - \psi_k(t) \|_{\mathfrak{H}} = 0. 
\]
\end{enumerate}
title: Def D2.1 of arXiv:2609.03848

[Theorem 31 (Law of large numbers) of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] Suppose that Assumptions~\ref{Assumptions_Theta} and \ref{Assumptions_basic} hold.
Fix $h \in [H]$ and let $f$ be a bounded continuous function
defined on $\amsmathbb{A}_h^{\mathfrak{m}}$ for $\N$ large enough. Then
\[
 \lim_{\N\rightarrow\infty} \Bigg| \frac{1}{\N} \sum_{i=1}^{N_h} f\bigg(\frac{\ell_i^h}{\N}\bigg) -\int_{\hat
{a}'_h}^{\hat{b}_h'} f(x) \dd\mu_h(x)\Bigg|=0\qquad \text{in probability.}
\]
 In terms of the Stieltjes transform (Definition~\ref{def_empirical_mes}) for each $\N$-independent  $\varepsilon > 0$ and compact set $\amsmathbb{K}_h$ containing $[\hat{a}_h,\hat{b}_h]$  in its interior for $\N$ large enough, we have
\[
\lim_{\N\rightarrow\infty} \sup_{z\in \amsmathbb{C} \setminus \amsmathbb{K}_h}\,\P\Bigg[\bigg| \frac{G_h(z)}{\N} - \Gm_{\mu_h}(z)\bigg|>\eps\Bigg] =0.
\]
Both limits are uniform over the ensembles satisfying Assumptions~\ref{Assumptions_Theta} and \ref{Assumptions_basic} with fixed constant $C$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma failstep of arXiv:2412.04284, 'Approximately jumping towards the Origin'] Let $k \equiv -1$ modulo 4. Suppose that $z_k$ exists and that $|z_k|=r>1$. If $z_{k}=z_{k+2}$, then 
    $$|z_k|-|z_{k+4}|>r-\sqrt{r^2+4-4\sqrt{r^2-1}}.$$ Furthermore, if $\sqrt{2}<|z_k|<2$, then $z_k \neq z_{k+4}$ and $|z_{k+4}|<\sqrt{2}$.

body:
[Proposition prop:joint-system of arXiv:2507.12502, 'Quantitative Edge Eigenvector Universality for Random Regular Graphs: Berry-Esseen Bounds '] The vector process $\mathbf{X}(t)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\mathrm{d}\mathbf{X}(t) = A(t)\mathbf{X}(t)\mathrm{d} t + \Sigma(t)\mathrm{d}\mathbf{B}(t) + \boldsymbol{\mathcal{E}}(t)\mathrm{d} t
\end{equation}
where:
\begin{itemize}
\item $A(t)$ is the drift matrix with entries $A_{ij} = -\frac{1}{2}\delta_{ij} + (1-\delta_{ij})(\lambda_i - \lambda_j)^{-1}$
\item $\Sigma(t)$ is the diffusion matrix with $\Sigma\Sigma^* = \text{Cov}(\mathrm{d}\mathbf{X}/\mathrm{d} t)$
\item $\mathbf{B}(t)$ is a $K$-dimensional Brownian motion
\item $\|\boldsymbol{\mathcal{E}}(t)\| \leq C_1 K^{1/2} N^{-5/6+\varepsilon}$
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Joint Overlap System

[Theorem of arXiv:2412.04284, 'Approximately jumping towards the Origin'] For each dimension $d \geq 2$, the random variable $\|x_n\|$ has a unique, invariant measure $\pi_d$ on $[0, \infty]$. This invariant measure $\pi_d$ has expectation 
$$ \int_{0}^{\infty} x ~d\pi_d(x) = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2} \frac{ \Gamma(\frac{d+1}{2})}{\Gamma(\tfrac{d}{2})} = \sqrt{\frac{\pi}{8}} \sqrt{d} + o(\sqrt{d})$$
which is asymptotically $(\sqrt{\pi/8} + o(1)) \cdot \sqrt{d}$.
The invariant measure $\pi_d$ has faster than Gaussian decay: for every $\alpha > 0$
$$ \int_{0}^{\infty} e^{\alpha x^2} d\pi_d(x) < \infty.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma calcdim of arXiv:2505.11721, 'Variational principles for Hausdorff and packing dimensions of fractal percolation on self'] Let $\mu$ be a positive and finite Borel measure supported on $[0,1]^d$. Let $(\mathcal G_N)_{N\ge 1}$ a sequence of finite families of closed parallelepipeds included in $[0,1]^d$ and such that for all $N\ge 1$ two elements of $\mathcal G_N$ are equal or have disjoint interior. 

Suppose that for each $N\ge 1$ and each $Q\in\mathcal G_N$ one has $\mu(\partial Q)=0$ and  the elements of $\mathcal G_N$ form a covering of $\supp(\mu)$. In particular, $\mu$-almost every $z\in \supp(\mu)$ is contained in a unique element $Q_N(z)$ of $\mathcal{F}_N$ for all $N\ge 1$. 
 
Let $\epsilon_1>0$, $\epsilon_2\in (0,1)$, $\delta_2\ge \delta_1\ge 0$ and $\Delta_2\ge \Delta_1\ge 0$. Let $(N_j)_{j\ge 1}$ be an increasing sequence of integers. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item Suppose that  for $\mu$-almost every $z$ one has $\liminf_{N\to+\infty} \frac{\log(\mu(Q_N(z)))}{-N}\ge \delta_1$ and for~$N$ large enough the sides lengths of $Q_N(z)$ are larger than $e^{-N(1+\epsilon_1)}$. Then,  $\underline\dim_H(\mu)\ge \frac{\delta_1}{1+\epsilon_1}$.

\item Suppose that for $\mu$-almost every $z$ one has $\liminf_{j\to+\infty} \frac{\log(\mu(Q_{N_j}(z)))}{-N_j}\le \delta_2$ and  the  sides lengths of $Q_{N_j}(z)$ are smaller than $e^{-N_j(1-\epsilon_2)}$. Then, $\overline\dim_H(\mu)\le \frac{\delta_2}{1-\epsilon_2}$.

\item  Suppose that for $\mu$-almost every $z$ one has $\limsup_{j\to+\infty} \frac{\log(\mu(Q_{N_j}(z)))}{-N_j}\ge \Delta_1$  and the  sides lengths of $Q_{N_j}(z)$ are larger than $e^{-N_j(1+\epsilon_1)}$. Then, $\underline\dim_P(\mu)\ge \frac{\Delta_1}{1+\epsilon_1}$.

\item Suppose that for $\mu$-almost every $z$ one has $\limsup_{N\to+\infty} \frac{\log(\mu(Q_N(z)))}{-N}\le \Delta_2$  and for~$N$ large enough the sides lengths of $Q_N(z)$ are smaller than $e^{-N(1-\epsilon_2)}$.  Then,  $\overline\dim_P(\mu)\le \frac{\Delta_2}{1-\epsilon_2}$. 
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma calcdim of arXiv:2505.11721

body: In mathematics, the Kolmogorov continuity theorem is a theorem that guarantees that a stochastic process that satisfies certain constraints on the moments of its increments will be continuous. It is credited to the Soviet mathematician Andrey Nikolaevich Kolmogorov.

body:
[Corollary 18 of arXiv:2608.30059, 'Multihomogeneous Measures and Stochastic Polar Representations'] If  \(\nu=\nu_Z\in M_{\chi_\alpha,\sigma}(E)\), then   the following are
equivalent: 
\begin{enumerate}[\rm(i)]
\item
\(\nu\) is \(B\)-invariant.

\item
For every \(a\in\mathsf T\)
\[
\nu_{B^aZ}=\nu_Z;
\]
equivalently, every random element \(B^aZ\) is another stochastic representer of
\(\nu\).

\item
For every \(a\in\mathsf T\) and every
\(\Gamma\in\mathcal H_\alpha(E)\)
\[
\E{\Gamma(B^aZ)}=\E{\Gamma(Z)}.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:Lipschitzquotient of arXiv:2609.01557, '$L^\infty$ Variational Approximation of the Aubry Set'] Let \(v_1,v_2\) be two critical subsolutions and set
\[
    z:=v_1-v_2.
\]
Then for all \(x,y\in\mathbb T^n\),
\begin{equation}
    |z(y)-z(x)|
    \leq \delta_M(x,y).
\end{equation}
Consequently, \(z|_\mathcal A\) descends to a \(1\)-Lipschitz function
\[
    \overline z:(\mathcal A_M,\delta_M)\to\mathbb R.
\]
If
\[
    \mathcal H^1(\mathcal A_M,\delta_M)=0,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
    \mathcal H^1(z(\mathcal A))=0.
\end{equation}
In particular, \(z(\mathcal A)\) contains no nontrivial interval.

[Definition def3_1 of arXiv:2607.26169, 'Scaling and partial universality of the height zero probability in the 2D Abelian sandpile'] Let \(U\subset\mathbb{C}\) be a simply connected region. Let \(z\in U\) and let \(\varphi : U \rightarrow \mathbb{D}\) be the unique conformal mapping to the unit disk \(\mathbb{D}\coloneqq \{w \in \mathbb{C} : |w| < 1\}\) satisfying \(\varphi(z) = 0\), \(\varphi'(z) > 0\). The conformal radius of \(U\) viewed from \(z\) is defined to be 
    \[
        \mathrm{rad}_U(z) = \frac{1}{\varphi'(z)}.
    \]

body: Ding-Lee-Peres Question 5.2 (arXiv:1004.4371, Section 5: when t_hit = o(t_cov), are the cover-time fluctuations of order t_hit?) is answered in the negative. On the clique-star G_k (a k-clique with one pendant leaf at each clique vertex; t_hit = 2k^2 + k + 1) the cover time satisfies Var(tau_cov) ~ t_hit t_cov and (tau_cov - E tau_cov)/sqrt(Var tau_cov) converges to a standard Gaussian; on the double star D_k (two adjacent centres, each with k pendant leaves; t_hit = 6k + 3) the cover time centred at 4k log k and divided by 2 sqrt(2) k sqrt(log k) converges to |Z|, a half-normal law, with t_cov = 4k log k + (4/sqrt(pi)) k sqrt(log k) + o(k sqrt(log k)) and Var(tau_cov) = 8(1 - 2/pi) k^2 log k (1 + o(1)). Centred at its mean instead, (tau_cov - t_cov)/sqrt(t_hit t_cov) converges to (|Z| - sqrt(2/pi))/sqrt(3), and the standardized cover time (tau_cov - E tau_cov)/SD(tau_cov) converges to (|Z| - sqrt(2/pi))/sqrt(1 - 2/pi), not to a half-normal law; SD(tau_cov)/t_hit ~ (sqrt(2)/3) sqrt(1 - 2/pi) sqrt(log k) -> infinity. The proofs use exact first-step hitting systems, an excursion transform f_k with mu = k^2 - k + 2 and sigma^2 = k^4 - 4k^2 + 5k - 2, stage and coupon-clock closed forms, a residual lemma (the trap is last with probability 1/(r+1)), second-order expansions with explicit error 3k log k + 5k, moderate deviations by Gartner-Ellis at speed a_k^2, an operational-time construction exact in law (tau = 2P + J - 1), and an occupation CLT with covariance (2/q) L^+.

[Definition 73 (Algebraic ancestry and analytic critical cost) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] For a cutoff \(N\ge2\), the split ancestry Rees module is
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr R^{\rm anc}_{\le N}(H)
 :=H\oplus
 \bigoplus_{n=2}^N\ \bigoplus_{r=1}^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}
 z^{-r}\operatorname{Ran}P_{n,r}.
 
\end{equation}
The symbol \(z^{-r}\) records the algebraic normal order
\(F_rL_n/F_{r+1}L_n\).

For tensors set
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr K_0^{[0]}:=\mathbb R,
 \qquad \mathscr K_1^{[0]}(H):=H,
 \qquad \mathscr K_n^{[0]}(H):=\mathfrak A_1^{(n)}(H)\quad(n\ge2),
 
\end{equation}
and, for \(n\ge2\), \(r\ge1\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr K_n^{[r]}(H):=
 \mathfrak W_{\rm mf}^{[r]}(H^{\otimes n}).
 
\end{equation}
Thus cost zero means trace class in every cut, while cost \(r\) permits the
critical profile \(\phi_r(N)\).  The inclusions
\(\mathscr K_n^{[r-1]}\subseteq\mathscr K_n^{[r]}\) define the analytic
critical boundary
\begin{equation}
 \partial_{\rm cr}^0\mathscr K_n(H):=\mathscr K_n^{[0]}(H),
 \qquad
 \partial_{\rm cr}^r\mathscr K_n(H)
 :=\mathscr K_n^{[r]}(H)/\mathscr K_n^{[r-1]}(H),
 \quad r\ge1.
 
\end{equation}
The truncated analytic Rees space is
\begin{equation}
 \mathscr R^{\rm cr}_{\le N}(H)
 :=\bigoplus_{n=0}^N
   \bigoplus_{0\le r\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor}
   z^{-r}\mathscr K_n^{[r]}(H),
 
\end{equation}
with the degree-one summand understood as \(H\).  The direct Rees sum carries
its product quasi-topology.  By contrast, the quotients
\(\partial_{\rm cr}^r\mathscr K_n\) are used as algebraic associated-graded
spaces; no Hausdorff quotient topology is implicit.
title: Algebraic ancestry and analytic critical cost

[Theorem thm:main of arXiv:2609.02234, 'An $n(\log n)^{o(1)}$ bound for nested cycles without geometric crossings'] For every fixed integer $k\ge3$, there are constants $K_k>0$ and $n_k$ such that every graph $G$ on $n\ge n_k$ vertices with $e(G)>K_k\Phi(n)=K_kn\omega(n)$ contains $k$ nested cycles without geometric crossings. Consequently,
\[
  f_k(n)=O_k\!\left(n\frac{(\log\log n)^2}{\log\log\log n}\right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 3 (Dobrushin-Major-Taqqu in Hölder topology) of arXiv:2606.04179, 'Functional Scaling Limits of Interpolated Correlated Random Walks in Hölder Topology'] Assume the correlation function \(\rho\) is a regularly varying 
    function of index \(-\alpha\) with \(\alpha \in (0,\frac1{\hermRank})\), that is
    \[
        \tag{regularly-varying ``fat tail''}
        \rho(k) = k^{-\alpha} \slowVar(k)
        \qquad \forall k\in \nat 
    \]
    for a slowly varying function\footnotemark
    \(\slowVar\colon (0, \infty) \to \real\)
    and \(\feature \in L^p(\gamma)\) for some \(p > 2\). Then the rescaled interpolated random
    walk converges in distribution in the Hölder topology. That is
    for the variance \(\sigma^2 \coloneq c_\hermRank^2\hermRank!/(\hurst(2\hurst-1))\)
    \[
        \hat\interpF^n \coloneq\tfrac{n^{-\hurst}}{\slowVar(n)^{\frac{\hermRank}2}}\interpF^n \xrightarrow{d} \sigma Z^{\hermRank,\hurst}, \qquad \text{in the space } C^{\beta}([0,T]) \text{ for any } \beta \in (0,\hurst - \tfrac1p),
    \]
    where \(Z^{\hermRank,\hurst}\) is a ``Hermite process'' (Definition \ref{def: Hermite process}) with Hurst index
    \(\hurst = 1-\frac{\alpha \hermRank}{2}\in (\frac12, 1)\),
    and \(C^{\beta}([0,T])\) is the space of \(\beta\)-Hölder continuous functions on \([0,T]\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Dobrushin-Major-Taqqu in Hölder topology

[Lem of arXiv:2411.15724, 'Wasserstein Convergence Rates for Empirical Measures of Random Subsequence of $\{nα\}$'] Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be i.i.d. random variables, and let $\alpha \in \mathbb R$. \footnote{Note that in this lemma, $X_1$ is not required to be integer-valued, and $\alpha$ is not required to be irrational.} Set $\mu_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{j = 1}^{n} \delta_{\{ S_j \alpha \}}$, $n \geq 1$. Then the event
$$
E : = \bigg\{  \limsup_{n \rightarrow \infty}   B_n^{-1} \mathbb W_1(\mu_n, \mu) \geq 1    \bigg\}
$$
has probability $0$ or $1$, where $(B_n)_{n \in \mathbb N}$ is a sequence of non-negative numbers and satisfies $\lim_{n \rightarrow \infty} n B_n = \infty$.
title: Unnumbered lem of arXiv:2411.15724, 'Wasserstein Convergence Rates for Empirical Measures of Rand'

[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2608.22112, '2608.22112'] \textbf{(Accumulating prediction errors increase the multi-step loss)}
Let $\mathrm{MAE}_h$ and $\mathrm{Loss}_H$ be defined as in
\cref{MAE} and \cref{loss}. Suppose that
\[
\mathrm{MAE}_{H+1}
>
\frac1H \sum_{h=1}^H \mathrm{MAE}_h.
\]
Then
\[
\mathrm{Loss}_{H+1}
>
\mathrm{Loss}_H.
\]
In particular, if the sequence $\{\mathrm{MAE}_h\}$ is increasing,
then extending the optimization horizon increases the loss.

[Theorem 4 (Antisymmetric maximum principle) of arXiv:2609.01403, '2609.01403'] Let $n\ge2$, $s\in(0,1)$,
\[
    H=\{x_1>0\},
    \qquad
    \widetilde x=(-x_1,x'),
\]
and let $B_r(x_0)\subset H$ and
$c\in L^\infty(B_r(x_0))$. Assume
$u\in\mathcal L^{2s}(\mathbb R^n)$ is antisymmetric with respect to
$\partial H$, namely
\[
    u(\widetilde x)=-u(x)
    \qquad
    \text{for a.e. }x\in H,
\]
and $u\ge0$ a.e. in $H$. Suppose
\[
    \mathscr{L}_su+cu\ge0
    \qquad
    \text{in }\mathcal D'(B_r(x_0)\setminus\{x_0\}),
\]
and
\[
    u\ge m>0
    \qquad
    \text{a.e. in }
    B_r(x_0)\setminus B_{r/2}(x_0).
\]
Then
\[
    u\ge\alpha m
    \qquad
    \text{a.e. in }B_r(x_0)\setminus\{x_0\},
\]
where
\[
    \alpha
    =
    \alpha\!\left(
        n,s,
        r^{2s}\|c^+\|_{L^\infty(B_r(x_0))}
    \right)>0.
\]
As above, for $0<r\le1$ the constant may be chosen uniformly in $r$,
while for $c\le0$ it depends only on $n$ and $s$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Antisymmetric maximum principle

[Defi 8 of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] Let $m \in \mathbb{R}$. A function $a : \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{C}$ is said to belong to $S^m$ if $a$ is smooth and satisfies for all multi-indices $\alpha, \beta$: 
\[
    |\partial_{\xi}^{\alpha}\partial_x^{\beta}a(x,\xi)| \leq C(\alpha,\beta) \langle \xi \rangle^{m-|\alpha|}.
\]
Similarly, we say that a function $a : \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}$  belongs to $C_*^{\rho}S^m$ if $a(x,\xi)$ is smooth in $\xi$ and for all multi-indices $\alpha$:
\[
    \|\partial_{\xi}^\alpha a(\cdot, \xi)\|_{C_*^{\rho}} \leq C(\alpha) \langle \xi \rangle^{m-|\alpha|},
\] 
where $C_*^{\rho}$ denotes the Zygmund space \cite[Appendix A]{TaylorPDE}.
title: Definition 8 of arXiv:2609.01105

[Theorem thm:whole-plane-persistence of arXiv:2609.00645, 'Global persistence of nearly radial concentrated vortices in a bounded domain'] Fix $\kappa,M,R>0$.  Then there exists $C=C(\kappa,M,R)>0$ such that the following
holds.  For $\varepsilon>0$, let
$\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\in L^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ satisfy
\begin{equation}
  \omega_{\varepsilon,0}\geq0,\qquad
  \int_{\mathbb R^2}\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\,\mathrm d\mathbf x=\kappa,
  \qquad
  \|\omega_{\varepsilon,0}\|_\infty\leq M\varepsilon^{-2},
  \qquad
  \operatorname{supp}\omega_{\varepsilon,0}
  \subset B_{R\varepsilon}(\mathbf0).
\end{equation}
Let $\omega_{\varepsilon,t}$, $t\in\mathbb R$, be the corresponding Yudovich
solution of the two-dimensional Euler equation in $\mathbb R^2$.  Then
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})^2
  \leq C\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,0}).
\end{equation}
If, in addition,
\begin{equation}
  \mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,0})\leq\frac{\kappa^2}{C},
\end{equation}
then, with
\[
  \mathbf X_\varepsilon
  :=\frac1\kappa\int_{\mathbb R^2}\mathbf x
  \omega_{\varepsilon,0}(\mathbf x)\,\mathrm d\mathbf x,
\]
one has
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})}
  |\mathbf b-\mathbf X_\varepsilon|
  \leq (1+\sqrt2)R\varepsilon.
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{\mathbf b\in\mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})}
  |\mathbf b|
  \leq(2+\sqrt2)R\varepsilon.
\end{equation}
In particular, for any family of initial data satisfying
(equation eq:whole-plane-initial-data of the paper) with the same $\kappa,M,R$, if
$\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,0})\to0$ as $\varepsilon\to0$, then
\[
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\mathcal A(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})\longrightarrow0,
  \qquad
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}\ \sup_{\mathbf b\in
  \mathsf C(\omega_{\varepsilon,t})}|\mathbf b|\longrightarrow0.
\]

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2609.01851, 'Minimum Weakly Saturated Graphs and Bootstrap Percolation in General Host Graphs'] Consider $H$-bootstrap percolation in a host graph $X$ of two order $n$ graphs $G$ and $G'$.
    If $G_{t} \subseteq G'_{s}$ for some time steps $t$ and $s$, then $G$ $H$-percolates $\implies G'$ $H$-percolates. Moreover, if $G$ percolates in $k\geq t+1$ steps, then $G'$ percolates in at most $k-t+s$ time steps.

If a_1 >= a_2 >= ... >= a_n and b_1 >= b_2 >= ... >= b_n (both sequences sorted the same way), then (1/n) sum a_i b_i >= ((1/n) sum a_i) ((1/n) sum b_i); if one sequence is increasing and the other decreasing, the inequality reverses. The integral form: for f and g both monotone in the same direction on [0,1], the integral of f g is at least the product of the integrals. This is the one-dimensional case of the Harris-FKG inequality (a product of two increasing functions of one uniform variable has nonnegative covariance), and its proof is the identity 2(n sum a_i b_i - sum a_i sum b_j) = sum_{i,j} (a_i - a_j)(b_i - b_j) >= 0.
both sequences (or functions) monotone in the same direction; opposite directions reverse the inequality
no independence or product structure needed beyond the single variable; the n-variable generalization is Harris-FKG

body: In mathematics, the polar decomposition of a square real or complex matrix $A$ is a factorization of the form $A=UP$, where $U$ is a unitary matrix, and $P$ is a positive semi-definite Hermitian matrix ( $U$ is an orthogonal matrix, and $P$ is a positive semi-definite symmetric matrix in the real case), both square and of the same size.

[Corollary 39 of arXiv:2608.25785, 'Proper Actions on Homogeneous Spaces of the Upper Triangular Matrix Group via Coarse Geome'] Let $S$ be a nonempty set, $I$ a finite set with $\# I\geq 2$, $J_1,J_2$ subsets of $I$, 
    $\{f_i\mid i\in I\}$ a family of functions from $S$ to $\R_{\geq 0}$,
    $\{a_{(\sigma,i)} \mid \sigma =1,2, \, i\in I\setminus J_\sigma\}$ a family of elements of $\R_{>0}$, and $\mathcal{P},\mathcal{Q}$ partitions of $I$.
    Assume that there exists $i_0\in I\setminus (J_1\cup J_2)$ such that $f_{i_0}$ values on $\R_{>0}$, and for each $\sigma\in \{1,2\}$ and $j\in J_\sigma$, there exists $C_j\geq 1$ such that $f_j\leq C_j\max\{f_i\mid i\in I\setminus J_\sigma \}$.
    Then the following two functions are pairwise close:
    \[
    \max\left\{\sum_{i\in P\setminus J_1}a_{(1,i)}f_i\middle| P\in \mathcal{P}\text{ with }P\neq J_1\right\},\quad 
    \max\left\{\sum_{i\in Q\setminus J_2}a_{(2,i)}f_i\middle| Q\in \mathcal{Q} \text{ with }Q\neq J_2\right\}.
    \]
    Here, $\R_{>0}$ is equipped with the LR-coarse structure. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: For the biased Bernoulli convolution at ratio 2/3 - the law of sum_k B_k (2/3)^k with B_k i.i.d., P(B_k = 1) = p - the measure is singular for every p < p* = 0.140277, where p* solves H(p) = log(3/2) in natural logarithms (H(p)/log(3/2) = 0.4896, 0.8018, 1.2341, 1.7095 at p = 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 1/2). Proof: the dimension of the measure is at most the entropy-over-Lyapunov ratio H(p)/log(3/2), and a measure on the line of dimension below one is not absolutely continuous; Hochman's theorem is needed only for the matching lower bound dim = min(1, H(p)/log(3/2)), which this does not use. Two further thresholds govern the Fourier criterion at this ratio. The biased factor |(1-p) + p e^{i phi}|^2 = 1 - 2p(1-p)(1 - cos phi) has arithmetic mean 1 - 2p(1-p) over the phase, which gives the annealed (main-term) exponent alpha(p) = 1 + log(1 - 2p(1-p))/log(3/2), zero at p(1-p) = 1/6, i.e. p = (1 - 3^{-1/2})/2 = 0.211325; and log-mean 2 log(1-p), which gives the quenched (typical) threshold (3/2)(1-p)^2 = 1 at p = 0.183503. As a calibration control for statistics on the unbiased Bernoulli convolution at 2/3 (the same ratio, frequencies and arithmetic, only the weights changed): below p* the measure is singular and a detection is expected; above 0.2113 the main term decays and a pass is expected; between 0.1403 and 0.2113 the measure has dimension one while the main term already diverges, so a reading there means nothing - controls belong at p <= 0.12 and p >= 0.35. Unlike the Pisot control lambda = 1/phi, where one localised cell forces the reading a priori, the absence of such a cell at ratio 3/2 is Mahler's open problem on ||(3/2)^m xi||, so the control's genuineness rests on an empirical extensiveness test: a flat per-step rate means one cell forces the reading, a wobbling rate means a real measurement (flat to 0.0005 at 1/phi from K = 8; wobbling by 0.028 at the unbiased 2/3).

[Definition 6 of arXiv:2605.02002, 'Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI'] (Approximate conservation of $\phi$-entropy) We say that a distribution $\mu$ on $\{0,1\}^n$ satisfies $K$-approximate tensorization of $\phi$-entropy if for any function $f:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ and any $X\sim\mu$,
$$
\operatorname{Ent}^\phi[f(X)]\leq K\cdot\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbb{E}[\operatorname{Ent}^\phi[f(X)\mid X_{-i}]],
$$where we denote by $X_{-i}$ the configuration $X$ restricted to $[n]\setminus\{i\}$.

Own work draft; proof (unaudited), conditional reduction, no novelty claim. Let alpha>0, beta=alpha+1, p_t=A*t^(-beta) sum to one on t=1,...,n, H>0, ell0>0. Suppose comparison task losses h_t satisfy 1{s<(1-delta)H/p_t}-eta_t <= h_t/ell0 <= 1{s<(1+delta)H/p_t}+eta_t with 0<=delta<1, eta_t>=0, and actual losses satisfy sum_t p_t*abs(ell_t-h_t)/ell0<=e. Set E=e+sum_t p_t*eta_t. Then ell0*(A*T_n(floor((A*s/((1-delta)*H))^(1/beta)) clipped to n)-E) <= sum_t p_t*ell_t <= ell0*(A*T_n(floor((A*s/((1+delta)*H))^(1/beta)) clipped to n)+E), where T_n(m)=sum_{t=m+1}^n t^(-beta). If r=(A*s/H)^(1/beta) tends to infinity, n/r tends to infinity, delta tends to zero, and E=o(A*r^(-alpha)), then total loss is asymptotic to ell0*A/alpha*r^(-alpha). This supplies the exponent alpha/(alpha+1) conditionally; proving the transition and error hypotheses for a network remains open.

[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2609.03185, 'Uniqueness of tangent flows in free boundary flow'] There exist constants $C>0$ and $\epsilon>0$ such that the following holds. Suppose that $|\alpha|, |\widehat{\alpha}|, |\mathscr{R}-Id|, D_{\mathscr{T}^{\alpha,\mathscr{C}_+}_\tau}(M_{\tau_0}), D_{\mathcal{W}^{\alpha(\tau),\mathscr{C}_+}}(M_{\tau_0}), D_{\mathscr{T}^{\alpha,\mathscr{C}_+}_{\tau+L}}(M_{\tau_0+L})\leq\epsilon,$ and $ D_{\mathscr{T}^{\alpha,\mathscr{C}_+}_\tau}(M_{\tau_0})>e^{-\tau_0/8}.$
Then
\[
D_{\mathscr{T}^{\widehat{\alpha},\mathscr{RC}_+}_{\tau+1}}(M_{\tau_0+1}),\ 
D_{\mathcal{W}^{\widehat{\alpha}(\tau+1),\mathscr{RC}_+}}(M_{\tau_0+1}) \leq C\bigg(D_{\mathscr{T}^{\alpha,\mathscr{C}_+}_\tau}(M_{\tau_0}) +|\mathscr{R}-Id| +|\alpha-\widehat{\alpha}|
+e^{-\frac{(R_{\widehat{\alpha}}-1)^2}{8p_0}}\bigg),
\]
\vspace{-\baselineskip}
\[
D_{\mathscr{T}^{\widehat\alpha,\mathscr{RC}_+}_\tau}(M_{\tau_0}) \leq C\bigg(D_{\mathcal{W}^{\alpha(\tau),\mathscr{C}_+}}(M_{\tau_0}) +|\mathscr{R}-Id| +|\alpha-\widehat{\alpha}|
+e^{-\frac{(R_{\widehat{\alpha}}-1)^2}{8p_0}}\bigg).
\]
If $|\widehat{\alpha}|\geq|\alpha|$, the exponential error terms are bounded by the corresponding distance terms. Finally,
$$ D_{\mathcal{W}^{\alpha(\tau+1),\mathscr{C}_+}}(M_{\tau_0+1}) + D_{\mathcal{W}^{\alpha(\tau+1),\mathscr{C}_+}}(M_{\tau_0+L+1})
\leq C\Big(D_{\mathscr{T}^{\alpha,\mathscr{C}_+}_\tau}(M_{\tau_0}) +
D_{\mathscr{T}^{\alpha,\mathscr{C}_+}_{\tau+L}}(M_{\tau_0+L}) +|\alpha|^2 \Big).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma of arXiv:2512.09219, 'Strong confluence of geodesics in Liouville quantum gravity'] ([GM21])
Let $h$ be a whole plane GFF and fix $s>0$.  Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $\mathcal{Z}$ be a collection of $n$ points in $\mathbb{C}$ such that $|z-w| \geq 2(1+s)$ for all distinct points $z,w \in \mathcal{Z}$.  For $z \in \mathcal{Z}$, let $E_z$ be an event measurable with respect to $\sigma(h|_{B_1(z)}-h_{1+s}(z))$.  Then, for all $p,q \in (0,1)$,  there exists $n_* = n_*(s,p,q) \in \mathbb{N}$ such that if $\mathbb{P}(E_z) \geq p$ for all $z \in \mathcal{Z}$,  then $\mathbb{P}\left(\cup_{z \in \mathcal{Z}} E_z \right) \geq q$ for all $n \geq n_*$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let $f: X \rightarrow S$ be a projective surjective morphism of integral excellent schemes with $X$ normal. Let $D$ be a $\Q$-Cartier $\Q$-divisor on $X$, and let $v$ be a divisorial valuation over $X$.
Take a projective birational morphism $\mu :Y \rightarrow X$ from a normal integral scheme, a prime divisor $\Gamma$ on $Y$, and $\lambda\in\R_{>0}$ such that $v=\lambda\cdot\ord_{\Gamma}$ (Remark~\ref{excval}).
We define the asymptotic vanishing order $v(\| D/S \|)$ of $D$ along $v$ as
\[ v(\| D/S \|) := \lambda\cdot\ord_{\Gamma}(Y/S,\|\mu^{*}D\|) = \lambda\cdot\ord_{\Gamma}(\|\mu^{*}D\|,Y/S). \]
This definition is independent of the choice of $Y$ and $\Gamma$ by Lemma~\ref{ordaffine} and Remark~\ref{ordrem}.
When $S$ is affine, we write $v(\| D/S \|)$ by $v(\| D\|)$ since it is independent of the choice of $S$ by Remark~\ref{ordrem}.

body:
[Theorem thm3.4 of arXiv:2508.12951, '\textbf{On the central limit question for strictly stationary, reversible Markov chains}'] Suppose $(q_1, q_2, q_3, \dots)$ is a sequence of positive
numbers such that $q_n \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.
Then there exists a (real) strictly stationary, countable-state,
irreducible, aperiodic (hence $\beta$-mixing) Markov chain 
$X := (X_k, k \in \mathbb Z)$ which is reversible and has
the following properties: \hfil\break
(i) There exists a positive constant $C$ such that
$P(|X_0| \leq C) = 1$; \hfil\break
(ii) there exists a positive integer $N$ such that 
$\textrm{\rm Var}(\, \sum_{k=1}^n X_k) \geq q_n \cdot n^2$ for all 
$n \geq N$; \hfil\break 
(iii) eqs.\ ((eq3.21 of the paper)), ((eq3.22 of the paper)), and ((eq3.23 of the paper))
hold; and \hfil\break
(iv) there exists a strictly increasing sequence 
$\bigl(J(1), J(2), J(3), \dots\bigl)$ of positive integers, 
and a sequence $(b_1, b_2, b_3, \dots)$ of positive constants
satisfying $b_n \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$, such that
\begin{equation}

b_n^{-1} \sum_{k=1}^{J(n)}X_k\ \to \mu_{\rm P1sL}\ \
{\rm in\ distribution\ as}\ n \to \infty.   
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm3.4 of arXiv:2508.12951

body:
[Lem small-frequency-abelian-estimates of arXiv:2605.13004, 'Orientation in Poisson Cluster Processes via Imaginary Bispectra'] Let $\overline H(x):=\int_x^\infty h(u)\,du\sim x^{-\alpha}L(x)$ with $0<\alpha\le2$, where $L$ is slowly varying. Write $L_t:=L(1/t)$,
\[
U(t):=\int_0^\infty \cos(tu)h(u)\,du,
\qquad
V(t):=\int_0^\infty \sin(tu)h(u)\,du.
\]
Then, as $t\downarrow0$, the following estimates hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $0<\alpha<1$, then
\[
1-U(t)\sim S(\alpha)t^\alpha L_t,
\qquad
V(t)\sim C(\alpha)t^\alpha L_t,
\]
where
\[
S(\alpha)=\frac{\pi/2}{\Gamma(\alpha)\sin(\pi\alpha/2)},
\qquad
C(\alpha)=\frac{\pi/2}{\Gamma(\alpha)\cos(\pi\alpha/2)}.
\]
\item If $\alpha=1$, then
\[
1-U(t)\sim \frac{\pi}{2}tL_t,
\qquad
2V(t)-V(2t)\sim 2(\log2)tL_t.
\]
More explicitly, with $J(x):=\int_1^x u^{-1}L(u)\,du$, the potentially larger slowly varying contribution to $V(t)$ is of order $tJ(1/t)$, and it cancels in $2V(t)-V(2t)$ because
\[
J(1/t)-J(1/(2t))\sim (\log2)L_t.
\]
\item If $1<\alpha<2$, then $\mu_1:=\int_0^\infty u h(u)\,du<\infty$, and
\[
1-U(t)\sim S(\alpha)t^\alpha L_t,
\qquad
V(t)-\mu_1t\sim C(\alpha)t^\alpha L_t.
\]
\item If $\alpha=2$, then $\mu_1:=\int_0^\infty u h(u)\,du<\infty$,
\[
V(t)-\mu_1t\sim -\frac{\pi}{2}t^2L_t,
\qquad
2V(t)-V(2t)\sim \pi t^2L_t.
\]
Moreover, if $R_2(x):=1+\int_1^x u^{-1}L(u)\,du$, then
\[
1-U(t)=O(t^2R_2(1/t)),
\qquad
 tR_2(1/t)=o(L_t).
\]
\end{enumerate}

Bijection and monotonicity are essential to this obstruction

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2605.21424, 'A dice game, a multinomial walk, and the inverted Dirichlet distribution'] Let \(\Delta_{m-1}\) denote the \(m-1\) dimensional simplex in \(\R^m\).
Then the function $\pi\colon \Delta_{m-1}\to\Delta_{m-1}, p=(p_1,\dotsc,p_m)\mapsto(\pi_1(p),\dotsc,\pi_m(p))$ is a bijection.
The restriction of  $\pi$ to the relative interior of \(\Delta_{m-1}\) is a diffeomorphism.

[Lemma PCM-invariance of arXiv:2507.01406, '{\Large On Iterated Lorenz Curves with Applications: The Multivariate Case }'] \noindent  Let $d=2m$, and let $F$ be PCM with respect
to the fixed pairing ((2050 of the paper)). Assume the relevant marginals are
continuous and the Lorenz normalizer is positive. Then $L_{F}$ is again PCM
with respect to the same pairing. Consequently, if $L^{0}=L^{F}$ and $
L^{n+1}=L_{L^{n}}$, then $L^{n}$ is PCM for all $n\geq 0$, as long as the
iterates remain in the regular atom-free regime. \medskip

body:
Let $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu)$ be a probability space (a finite or even $\sigma$-finite measure suffices here), $T: X \to X$ measure-preserving, $f \in L^1(\mu)$ real-valued. Write $S_n f = \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} f \circ T^k$ and $F_N = \max_{1 \le n \le N} S_n f$. Then
$$\int_{\{F_N > 0\}} f\,d\mu \ \ge\ 0 \quad \text{for every } N \ge 1,$$
and consequently $\int_{\{\sup_n S_n f > 0\}} f\,d\mu \ge 0$. The maximal inequality follows: for $\alpha > 0$, $\mu\big(\{ \sup_{n} \tfrac{1}{n} S_n f > \alpha \}\big) \le \tfrac{1}{\alpha} \int_{\{\sup_n S_n f / n > \alpha\}} f\,d\mu \le \tfrac{1}{\alpha}\|f\|_1$ (apply the first statement to $f - \alpha$; for the last step in infinite measure one needs $f \ge 0$ or $\mu$ finite, since $\int (f - \alpha)$ over the set is where $\mu$ finite is used). This is the only analytic input needed for the pointwise ergodic theorem. It fails if $T$ does not preserve $\mu$.
T is measure-preserving
f is integrable
the sets are defined through the partial sums S_n f, n >= 1

[Definition 34 of arXiv:2609.03962, '$L^p$ isomorphisms for the fractional Laplacian on $\mathbb{R}^n$ and their application'] Let $s\in(0,2)$. For $(u,P)\in(\cL_s)^n\times\mathscr S'(\R^n)$ we define
\[
  T(u,P):=\big(\flap u+\nabla P,\ -\mathrm{div}\,u\big)\in
  \mathscr D'(\R^n)^n\times\mathscr D'(\R^n)
\]
by its action on test fields: for all $\phi\in C_{\mathrm{c}}^\infty(\R^n)^n$ and
$\psi\in C_{\mathrm{c}}^\infty(\R^n)$,
\[
  \langle \flap u+\nabla P,\ \phi\rangle
  :=\int_{\R^n} u\cdot\flap\phi\,dx-\langle P,\ \mathrm{div}\,\phi\rangle,
  \qquad
  \langle -\mathrm{div}\,u,\ \psi\rangle:=\int_{\R^n} u\cdot\nabla\psi\,dx .
\]

body:
[Theorem 1 (Limiting bulk spectrum) of arXiv:2606.20816, 'Spectral Properties of Dense Barab\'asi--Albert Graphs'] Let $M$ be the adjacency matrix of the Barab\'asi--Albert multigraph with $m = c n$ and fixed $c \in \left(0, \frac12\right)$, and define the centered and rescaled matrix
\[
Y
\ = \
\frac{M - \E[M]}{\sqrt{m}}.
\]
Then the empirical spectral distribution of $Y$ converges weakly in probability,\footnote{A sequence of probability measures $\mu_n$ on $\R$ converges weakly in probability to a probability measure $\mu$ if, for all bounded continuous functions $f : \R \to \R$ and all $\varepsilon > 0$,
\[
\P \left[
\abs{
\int f \, d \mu_n - \int f \, d \mu
}
>
\varepsilon
\right]
\ \to \
0
\]
as $n \to \infty$.} as $n \to \infty$, to a deterministic probability measure $\mu_c$.

The Stieltjes transform
\[
G_c \left(z\right)
\ = \
\int_{\R} \frac{1}{\lambda - z} \, d \mu_c \left(\lambda\right),
\quad z \in \mathbb{H},
\]
is given by
\[
G_c \left(z\right)
\ = \
c m_A \left(z\right) - \int_c^1 \frac{1}{z + u \left(x\right) K \left(z\right)} \, d x,
\quad
u \left(x\right)
\ = \
\left(2 x - c\right)^{-1 / 2},
\]
where the pair $\left(K \left(z\right), L \left(z\right)\right)$ is the unique solution in $\mathbb{H}^2$ of the system
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
K \left(z\right)
&\ = \
L \left(z\right) - \frac{\sqrt{c}}{z + L \left(z\right) / \sqrt{c}},\\[4pt]
L \left(z\right)
&\ = \
-\int_c^1 \frac{u \left(y\right)}{z + u \left(y\right) K \left(z\right)} \, d y,
\end{aligned}
\quad z \in \mathbb{H},
\end{equation}
and
\[
m_A \left(z\right)
\ = \
-\frac{1}{z + L \left(z\right) / \sqrt{c}}.
\]

The limiting density $\rho_c$ is recovered by Stieltjes inversion:
\[
\rho_c \left(\lambda\right)
\ = \
\frac{1}{\pi} \lim_{\eta \downarrow 0} \Im G_c \left(\lambda + i \eta\right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Limiting bulk spectrum

[Lemma Lemma_appendix_D of arXiv:2608.30548, 'Finite speed of propagation and waiting time phenomena for stochastic porous media equatio'] Let $u$ be the unique kinetic solution to (equation Eq_SPME_intro of the paper) with initial value $u_0$. For a given $x_0\in \mathbb T^d\setminus\mathrm{supp}(u_0)$ define the process $G:[0,T] \times \Omega\times \left[0,\frac{1}{2}\right) \rightarrow \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ by 
    \[
        G(t,\omega, r): = \sup_{s\in (0,t)} \, \int_{B_r(x_0)} u_s^{\alpha+1}(\omega).
    \]
    Let $(\mu,r)\in \mathbb{R}_+\times \left[0,\frac{1}{2}\right)$. Then for any $t\in (0,T)$, the random time 
    \[
        \tau:= \inf\left\{ s>0, \, G(s,r)>\mu\right\}
        \wedge t
    \]
    is a stopping time.

body: Measured on a frame spread in three dimensions (the 8 sign vectors divided by sqrt 8, leverages 3/8, two irrational rotations), comb laws with N teeth of width 1/N at the integers, Gaussian cells, lattice part exact: the two-dimensional frame integral J_2(kappa) = int int |E e^{i(yL + tV + kappa LP)}| dy dt that the Theorem H route needs grows with N at every fixed kappa (kappa = 1: 15.4, 18.6, 23.4, 28.2, 32.5 at N = 4..12; untwisted value about 32/N). The hub-conditioned integral with twist proportional to the partner frequency grows too. The mixed norms int dt ||T(., t)||_{L^p(dy)} with p >= 3/2 stay flat on one rotation but grow for every p <= 2 on the other. For fine combs of bounded range (teeth of width 1/N at spacing 2/N in [0, 2]) all of these stay flat, so the growth is driven by the spread of the laws. The density of the single hub 2 X_h (L + beta) + V^2 + 2 eps L P falls with N and does not feel eps, and its characteristic function is integrable uniformly in eps (fine combs: |eta|^{3/2}|phi_Q| in [1.0, 1.4], integral 3.0 at eps = 0, 0.03, 0.003). Lesson: every bound that takes moduli of the twisted light transform at a fixed hub value and a fixed Fresnel frequency loses; a proof must pair the hub with the light transform before any modulus, or be real-variable.

body:
[Thm two-sided of arXiv:2411.15724, 'Wasserstein Convergence Rates for Empirical Measures of Random Subsequence of $\{nα\}$'] Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots$ be integer-valued i.i.d. random variables with characteristic function $\varphi$, and let $S_j = \sum_{i = 1}^{j} X_i$. Let $\alpha$ be an irrational number. Suppose that
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item there exists $0 < \beta \leq 2$ such that in an open neighborhood of $0$,\footnote{Throughout the paper $A \asymp B$ means that there exists an absolute constant $C > 0$ such that $C^{-1} B \leq A \leq C B$.}
$$
|1 - \varphi(x)| \asymp |x|^\beta;
$$

\item there exists $\gamma \geq 1$ such that
\begin{align} 
0 < \liminf_{q \rightarrow \infty} q^\gamma \| q \alpha \| < \infty.
\end{align}
\end{enumerate}
Set $\mu_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{j = 1}^{n} \delta_{\{ S_j \alpha \}}$, $n \geq 1$. Then for any $1 \leq p < \infty$,
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item if $\beta \gamma < 2$, assume furthermore that $X_1$ is non-constant, then

$$\mathbb E \big[  \mathbb W_p(\mu_n, \mu)  \big] \asymp \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}};$$

\item if $\beta \gamma = 2$, assume furthermore that $X_1$ is non-constant, then there exist $c_1, c_2 > 0$ such that for any $n \in \mathbb N$,

$$\frac{c_1}{\sqrt{n}} \leq \mathbb E \big[  \mathbb W_p(\mu_n, \mu)  \big] \leq \frac{c_2 (\log n)^{1 - \frac{1}{p \vee 2}} }{\sqrt{n}};$$

\item if $\beta \gamma > 2$, then

$$
0 < \limsup_{n \rightarrow \infty} n^{1/(\beta \gamma)} \mathbb E \big[ \mathbb W_p(\mu_n, \mu) \big] < \infty,
$$
\end{enumerate}
where all constants and implied ones depend on $p$ and conditions on $\varphi$ and $\alpha$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm two-sided of arXiv:2411.15724

[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2607.25986, 'Asymptotics of a two-species particle system associated to the doubly parabolic Keller-Seg'] Let $\gamma \in (\frac 32,2)$ and $\alpha>0$. Assume that $\chi>0$ and 
$\theta>0$ are such that~\eqref{condistar} holds true.
For all $\sigma\in (0,\frac12]$, all $T>0$, there exist a constant $A_{\sigma,T}$  
(also depending on $\chi,\lambda,\alpha,\gamma,\theta,c_0$) such that for all $(N,M,\e)\in \Aa_\sigma$,
\begin{gather}
\E \Big[\int_0^T \int_{\R^2} \frac{1}{|X_s^{1,N,M,\e}-X_s^{2,N,M,\e}-\sqrt\e y|^{2(\gamma-1)}} \phi(y)\dd y\dd s\Big ]\leq A_{\sigma,T},
\\
\E \Big[\int_0^T  \int_0^s \int_{\R^2}\frac{1}{(s-u+ |X_s^{1,N,M,\e}-X_u^{2,N,M,\e}-\sqrt\e y|^{2})^\gamma} \phi(y) \dd y 
\dd u \dd s \Big ]\leq A_{\sigma,T},  \\
\E \Big[\int_0^T \Big|(\nu^{1,N,M,\e}_s \ast \nabla \phi_{\e})(X^{1,N,M,\e}_s)\Big|^{2(\gamma-1)}\dd s
\Big]\leq A_{\sigma,T}, \\
\E \Big[\int_0^T  \int_0^s \int_{\R^2}
\Big|\nabla K^{\theta,\lambda}_{s-u}(X_s^{1,N,M,\e}-X_u^{2,N,M,\e}-\sqrt\e y)\Big|^{\frac{2\gamma}3} \phi(y)\dd y
\dd u \dd s \Big ]\leq A_{\sigma,T}. 
\end{gather} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Own work draft; proof (unaudited). Target 2 bound. In the C006 small-total-reference-leakage ensemble with independent unique-witness background, almost surely C003 A, if true, forces every fixed uniform deterministic polynomial-time witness finder to miss a superpolynomial multiple of h_n background inputs eventually; more precisely sampler accuracy and residual count at most p(n)h_n coincide only finitely often for every fixed polynomial p. This does not solve Target 2 and has no novelty priority claim.
C006 v2 protected bits and witness locations; independent unique-witness background
Polynomial bound on logarithm of full auxiliary reference-oracle count conditional on other blocks and independent background
R is one fixed deterministic uniform polynomial-time oracle procedure; p is a fixed polynomial
metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:e1d154ab0e5e2822f3938d40219ab6f1ac2ce223d2bf58a9891f5208441eb083","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/e1/e1d154ab0e5e2822f3938d40219ab6f1ac2ce223d2bf58a9891f5208441eb083.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:58d0a1c13624564312f217a40a040ad33d187d5d06207c755edc8f37f97277ed","bundle_entry_key":"t410-w739-c009-v1","bundle_id":"population.t410-w739-background-obstructions-v1","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"oracle computational complexity; weighted sampling; hidden witnesses; average-case inversion","draft":"w739/bundle_009.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:complexity.cryptography:t410-w739-c009-v1","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Sparse background: sampling requires many residual search failures

C009 v1. Target 2. Kind: bound. Status: proof (unaudited).
This is a necessary compatibility condition for a proposed oracle architecture,
not a proof of either target. No novelty priority is claimed.

## Setup and statement

Use the C006 v2 protected blocks, h_n=2^floor(n/2), M_n=2^(n^2).
At every unprotected input y put exactly one accepted n^2-bit witness u_y.
These locations may be arbitrary, but are fixed independently of the protected
bits and locations, including after other independent background data is fixed.
The auxiliary oracle obeys the same conditional full-reference condition:
after fixing other blocks and independent background it has at most 2^a(n)
references independent of this block's protected variables, with a polynomial.
Selection among references may depend arbitrarily on protected variables.

Fix a deterministic uniform polynomial-time oracle procedure R(y) returning
an n^2-bit candidate or failure. Define Z_R(n) as the number of unprotected
inputs y at length n for which R(y) fails to return an accepted witness.
R may query both the witness table and the selected auxiliary oracle. Fix
any positive integer-valued polynomial upper bound p(n)>=1.

There is one uniform efficiently weighted family W_R such that, for every
fixed uniform polynomial-time sampler S, almost surely the following two
events hold simultaneously at only finitely many n:

  (i) S approximates W_R at L(n)=1+n+n^2 within
      TV tau_n=1/[100(p(n)+1)L(n)];
 (ii) Z_R(n)<=p(n) h_n.

The probability-one set can be chosen simultaneously for all R, all such
polynomial bounds p, and all S, by countability. Hence on this set, IF C003 A
holds, every such R has Z_R(n)/h_n eventually greater than every polynomial.
This is a conditional necessity, not an existence claim for such an oracle.

## Efficient residual filter

Let G_R(y)=1 when R(y) does not return an accepted witness; verify every
candidate with the actual witness table, treating malformed outputs as failure.
At distinguished length L(n), give dummy 0^L weight 1 and word 1 y w
weight 4 iff G_R(y)=1 and (y,w) is accepted. Give all other words weight zero.
At other lengths give just the dummy weight 1. R is fixed code, so this is a
single uniform polynomial-time oracle weight family. It does not recognize H_n
and it does not contain S or a description/compiler for every weight family.

Write d=p(n)+1 and h=h_n. On event (ii), at most p(n)h unprotected accepted
words remain, and at most h protected accepted words remain. Therefore the
number N of accepted nondummy words in W_R is at most d h. Each has exact
target mass v=4/(1+4N). No assumption about their distribution over inputs or
their dependence on the selected auxiliary oracle has been made.

## A learner combines R with samples of the residual law

For analysis, evaluate R on every input in the fixed protected set H_n and
verify its output. Set the corresponding guessed bit to one on a successful
verification, otherwise zero. This has no false positive protected bits.
It may use H_n as fixed information: C006 allows unrestricted computation and
fixed descriptions independent of the sampled bits and locations. The weight
family and S do not get H_n. Any protected yes bit not found by this step has
its unique witness in the support of W_R, by the definition of G_R.

If N=0 there are no such missed yes bits, so this learner already recovers the
whole bit vector. Otherwise suppose (i) and (ii) hold for this fixed oracle.
Call a supported word bad if S emits it with probability less than v/2.
The positive-part characterization of total variation gives

    number of bad words < 2 tau_n/v
       = tau_n (1+4N)/2 <= (1+4dh)/(200dL) < h/8.

Every other supported word has S-probability at least

    v/2 >= 2/(1+4dh) >= 1/(3dh).

Run S independently t=6dh(n+2) times. Verify each output's residual filter
and witness predicate and set its protected bit to one if it is accepted.
Background outputs can simply be ignored when restricting to the fixed
protected coordinates. At most h good protected witnesses need be observed.
The probability that any is missed is at most

    h (1-1/(3dh))^t <= h exp(-2(n+2))
       <= h 2^(-2(n+2)) <= 1/16.

Thus on each oracle satisfying (i) and (ii), the learner guesses the protected
vector within floor(h/8) errors with probability at least 15/16 over the
independent S tapes. This remains valid even if R found some protected yes
witnesses: those were recorded before sampling. No assumption that R fails
on every protected input is needed.

## Unconditional direct-product bound and quantifiers

Let r(n) bound witness queries for R plus verifying its output, and let s(n)
bound witness queries per S call at this inverse-polynomial accuracy. These
are polynomials for fixed R,S,p. The learner uses at most

    Q <= h r(n) + 6dh(n+2)[s(n)+r(n)+1]

direct witness queries. Fix its random tapes, other blocks, and all independent
background information. C006 v2 followed by the C007 Hamming-ball union bound
gives unconditional success probability at most

    2^(a(n)-h/4) (1+1/M_n)^Q <= 2^(a(n)-h/4) exp(Q/M_n).

Average over the tapes and independent data. In particular, do NOT condition
the protected posterior on the residual-count event or the accuracy event.
Since success is at least 15/16 on their intersection, its probability is at
most (16/15) times this displayed upper bound. It is summable in n: Q is h
times a polynomial, Q/M_n tends to zero, and a(n)<=h/8 eventually. Tail union
bounds imply that intersection occurs only finitely often almost surely.

There are countably many fixed uniform R and S and integer-coefficient
polynomial upper bounds p. Taking the intersection of these probability-one
statements is legitimate, even when their codes are selected after O.
Now suppose A holds for an oracle in this intersection. For each fixed R,p,
A supplies a uniform sampler for W_R at the inverse-polynomial schedule
tau_n above (use any polynomial in L dominating 100(p(n)+1)L; n<=L).
An arbitrarily smaller error also suffices. This sampler is eventually accurate.
The intersection bound forces Z_R(n)>p(n)h_n eventually. Taking all p proves
the conditional superpolynomial ratio claim. A does not imply a uniform
compiler over R, and none has been used.

## Consequence and precise remaining gap

A sparse-background inversion interface cannot simply return a valid witness
at every unprotected input while ignoring the protected inputs. Its verified
failure predicate would be a residual filter with Z_R=0, contradicting the
necessary condition together with A almost surely. Even polynomially many
background failures per protected input are insufficient. A compatible
construction needs a much larger background failure set for every fixed
efficient deterministic search routine, despite requiring accurate law sampling.

This does not refute C003 B: B gives randomized average-case distributional
inversion, not a deterministic routine with the residual guarantee assumed
here. A residual set much larger than h_n can still have negligible fraction
among all 2^n inputs. Whether a hierarchy of such residual sets supports all
oracle-dependent weight families and inversion maps remains OPEN. No common
oracle, independent audit, formal proof certificate, or scored movement is claimed.

For n in [0, 2] and x = 1/sqrt(2 + sqrt(2 - n)) the honeycomb O(n) loop-model interface converges to SLE(kappa) with kappa = 4 pi/(2 pi - arccos(-n/2)); for x above that value it converges to SLE(kappa) with kappa = 4 pi/arccos(-n/2). Known only for n = 1 at the critical point (site percolation, Smirnov) and for the n = 0 boundary in the trivial sense. Source: Bauerschmidt, Duminil-Copin, Goodman, Slade: Lectures on self-avoiding walks, Clay 2012, Conjecture 3.7, p. 25. Status notes: The n = 0 critical case is the SLE(8/3) conjecture for SAW (the source's Conjecture 1.5), which the Codex campaign already records as P0003 (hexagonal SAW scaling limit); this record covers n in (0,2] and the dense phase, and the n = 0 dense case (x above critical, kappa = 8).
Posed in Bauerschmidt, Duminil-Copin, Goodman, Slade: Lectures on self-avoiding walks, Clay 2012
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07
title: Open problem: Interfaces of the honeycomb O(n) loop model converge to SLE(kappa)

For every prime power q = p^k there is a field with exactly q elements, unique up to isomorphism, denoted F_q; it is the splitting field of x^q - x over F_p. Every finite field has prime-power order, and the multiplicative group F_q* is cyclic of order q - 1.

body: [Theorem T:half-space-log-gamma-horizon of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] Let $\theta > 0$ and $\alpha \in (-\theta, \infty)$. Then there exists a random function $\mathcal{H}^{\mathsf{LG}}$, such that $-\log \mathcal{H}^{\mathsf{LG}}\in \mathcal{D}((-\theta, \alpha \wedge 0], \mathbb{Z}, \alpha \wedge 0)$, and for any finite set $I = (\gamma_1 < \cdots < \gamma_k) \subset (-\theta, \alpha \wedge 0]$, the restriction $\mathcal{H}^{\mathsf{LG}}|_I$ is equal in law to the half-space log-gamma joint stationary measure given in Proposition (P:stationary-existence of the paper). In particular, $\mathcal{H}^{\mathsf{LG}}$ gives a coupling of all the log-gamma joint stationary measures identified above. We call $\mathcal{H}^{\mathsf{LG}}$ the \textbf{(extended) half-space log-gamma horizon}.
title: Theorem T:half-space-log-gamma-horizon of arXiv:2604.10020

[Definition 7 of arXiv:2605.30616, 'Brownian motion: the hyperbolic number setting'] Let $\left(X,\sigma\left(X\right),\mu\right)$ be a $\mathbb{H}$-valued-probability
space where 
\[
\mu=\mu_{1}+\mu_{2}k=\left(\mu_{1}+\mu_{2}\right)e_{+}+\left(\mu_{1}-\mu_{2}\right)e_{-}.
\]
For $A,B\in\sigma\left(X\right)$, define the conditional $\mathbb{H}$-valued
probability $\mu\left(A\mid B\right)$ by 
\[
  \mu\left(A\mid B\right)\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\frac{\left(\mu_{1}+\mu_{2}\right)\left(A\cap B\right)}{\left(\mu_{1}+\mu_{2}\right)\left(B\right)}e_{+}
  +\frac{\left(\mu_{1}-\mu_{2}\right)\left(A\cap B\right)}{\left(\mu_{1}-\mu_{2}\right)\left(B\right)}e_{-},
\]
where 
\[
\frac{\left(\mu_{1}+\mu_{2}\right)\left(A\cap B\right)}{\left(\mu_{1}+\mu_{2}\right)\left(B\right)}=\left(\mu_{1}+\mu_{2}\right)\left(A\mid B\right),
\]
and 
\[
\frac{\left(\mu_{1}-\mu_{2}\right)\left(A\cap B\right)}{\left(\mu_{1}-\mu_{2}\right)\left(B\right)}=\left(\mu_{1}-\mu_{2}\right)\left(A\mid B\right),
\]
are the usual $\mathbb{R}$-valued non-negative conditional measures
with axiomatization: 
\[
\mu\left(B\right)=0=0+0k\;\;\overset{\mathrm{axiom}}{\Longrightarrow}\;\;\mu\left(A\mid B\right)=\mu\left(A\right).
\]

body:
[Corollary 5 of arXiv:2608.26662, 'Boundary–Moment Universality and Curvature Corrections in Random Geometric Graphs on Riema'] Assume $d=2$ and $f\equiv V^{-1}$, where
$V:=\Vol_g(M)$.  Then
\[
J_{P_3}(2)=M_{P_3}(2)=\frac{9\sqrt3\pi}{4},
\quad
J_{K_3}(2)=\frac{\pi(4\pi-3\sqrt3)}4,
\quad
\gamma_2=\frac{\pi}{4\pi-3\sqrt3}.
\]
Let
\[
\widehat F_{3,n}(r)
:=\frac{U_{K_3}(r)}
{\binom n3 r^4J_{K_3}(2)},
\qquad
\widehat V_n(r):=
\begin{cases}
\widehat F_{3,n}(r)^{-1/2},
&\widehat F_{3,n}(r)>0,\\
1,
&\widehat F_{3,n}(r)=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Define
\begin{equation}
\widehat\chi_n(r)
:=\frac{3}{2\pi}\widehat V_n(r)^3
\widehat{\mathcal G}_{3,n}(r)
=-\frac{3(4\pi-3\sqrt3)}{2\pi^2}
\frac{\widehat V_n(r)^3C_n(r)}
{\binom n3r^6}.

\end{equation}
If $r_n\downarrow0$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
n^2r_n^6\rightarrow\infty,

\end{equation}
then
\[
\widehat V_n(r_n)\xrightarrow{\Pp}V,
\qquad
\widehat\chi_n(r_n)\xrightarrow{\Pp}\chi(M).
\]
Consequently, since $\chi(M)$ is integer-valued, rounding
$\widehat\chi_n(r_n)$ to the nearest integer recovers $\chi(M)$

Let U ⊂ C be open, let A ⊂ U have no accumulation point in U (so A is discrete and closed in U, hence at most countable), and for each a in A let P_a(z) = Σ_{j=1}^{m_a} c_{a,j} (z - a)^{-j} be a given nonzero polynomial in 1/(z - a) with no constant term and finite m_a ≥ 1. Then there exists a function f meromorphic on U, holomorphic on U minus A, whose set of poles is exactly A and whose principal part at each a in A is P_a, i.e. f - P_a extends holomorphically across a. Any two such functions differ by a function holomorphic on all of U, so the general solution is f + h with h holomorphic on U. A standard instance is the pole structure of the Gamma function: U = C, A = {0, -1, -2, ...}, with prescribed principal part (-1)^n / (n! (z + n)) at the point z = -n for n = 0, 1, 2, ....
U ⊂ C is open
A ⊂ U has no accumulation point in U
each prescribed principal part is a finite polynomial in 1/(z-a) without constant term

Own-work draft, T419-C032 v1, proof (unaudited), novelty unresolved. Let r>=2, N>=1024r(r+1), p=N+r and G=[Q Z] be r-by-p iid standard Gaussian with r-by-r signal block Q. Put M=GG^T, S0=M^(-1/2)Q, w0=sigma_min(S0)^2 and delta=||M/p-I||_op. For any 0<mu<=1, the event 0<delta<1/2 and delta>(mu^2/2)sqrt(w0) has probability at least (3/64)(1/(256r))^(r^2), uniformly in N. For the reduced flow Ydot=M^(-1)Y H(I-Y^T Y), H=diag(lambda_i^2,0), lambda_i in [mu,1], a worst-case sufficient condition preserving minimum signal-overlap square above w0/4 is gamma<(mu^2/2)sqrt(w0), gamma=delta/(1-delta). The event violates that condition even as input dimension grows. Thus Gram concentration alone cannot justify arbitrary-confidence convergence through this sufficient criterion. This is a certificate failure, not optimization failure or a target solution. The proof uses independent signal/null Gaussian blocks, exact second/fourth moments, Paley-Zygmund and a Frobenius variance bound; no simulation or asymptotic approximation.

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:e29b92d8877120363e7811b9beeba48202fa7eb4bfa672af84795c9ffa43db71","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/e2/e29b92d8877120363e7811b9beeba48202fa7eb4bfa672af84795c9ffa43db71.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:facc2f72471ee7e906f476a4d1074b1dad0340eba462b514508969e458399e97","bundle_entry_key":"gram-overlap-barrier-failure","bundle_id":"population.t419-gram-overlap-barrier-route-failure-018","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian matrix initialization and low-rank gradient dynamics","draft":"w705/bundle_018.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:optimization.lowrank:gaussian-gram-concentration-insufficient-signal-overlap-barrier","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T419-C032 v1 — why a Gram-concentration overlap barrier is insufficient

Kind: route-failure. Target1. Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty or target-progress claim. This tests one sufficient criterion, not LoRA convergence, and builds on rather than reproves C030's rank-crossing obstruction.

## Proposed criterion

Write p=N+r, G=[Q Z] with r-by-r signal block Q and r-by-N null block Z. Let M=GG^T, Y0=M^(-1/2)G, S0 its first r columns and w0=sigma_min(S0)^2. Let

    delta=||M/p-I||_op<1, gamma=delta/(1-delta).

For the reduced Stiefel flow Y'=M^(-1)Y H(I-Y^T Y), H=diag(lambda_i^2,0) with lambda_i in [mu,1], set S=Y[:,1:r], W=S^T S, w=lambda_min(W), t=lambda_max(W)<=1. Its exact signal equation is

    S'=M^(-1) S D(I-S^T S), D=diag(lambda_i^2).

Write p M^(-1)=I+K with ||K||<=gamma. For every unit minimum eigenvector v of W, direct differentiation gives

    v^T W'v >= (2(1-w)/p) [mu^2 w-gamma sqrt(w t)].

Indeed S^T M^(-1)S=(W+S^T K S)/p. The main term is w v^T Dv, while the error is bounded by gamma ||S Dv|| ||Sv|| <=gamma sqrt(t w). This works for repeated minimum eigenvalues by taking the minimum over their unit eigenvectors.

In particular gamma<(mu^2/2)sqrt(w0) is a sufficient barrier for w>=w0/4: the lower derivative is strictly positive at a potential first crossing, unless w0=0. The non-strict version follows by continuity or a slightly smaller barrier. This route would need a high-probability guarantee of this criterion; a claim merely that delta->0 is insufficient because w0 also tends to zero.

## Uniform positive-probability failure of the sufficient criterion

For every r>=2, N>=1024r(r+1), and every 0<mu<=1, iid Gaussian G has

    P[0<delta<1/2 and delta>(mu^2/2)sqrt(w0)]
      >= (3/64) (1/(256r))^(r^2) >0.

Consequently, without further ideas, this criterion cannot deliver arbitrary confidence 1-rho merely by taking p large. The lower bound is extremely small and is an obstruction to the certificate, not a lower bound on optimization failure. No Gaussian asymptotic approximation is used.

Put epsilon=1/(128r). Restrict all r^2 entries of Q to [-epsilon,epsilon], an event A of probability at least (epsilon/2)^(r^2). To justify the bound, the standard Gaussian density exceeds1/4 on [-epsilon,epsilon] (use sqrt(2pi)<3 and exp(-epsilon^2/2)>3/4). Except on a null subset Q is nonsingular. Also ||Q||_F<=r epsilon and |(QQ^T)12|<=r epsilon^2.

Independently, let U=(ZZ^T)12=sum_(j=1)^N Z_1j Z_2j. Gaussian integration by parts gives E Z^2=1 and E Z^4=3, so

    E U^2=N, E U^4=3N^2+6N.

The elementary Paley-Zygmund inequality (obtained by Cauchy-Schwarz on the event X>theta EX) applied to X=U^2 yields

    P[|U|>=sqrt(N)/2] >= (9/16)/(3+6/N) >=1/16.

Entrywise moment calculation also gives

    E||ZZ^T-NI||_F^2=N r(r+1).

Markov's inequality therefore bounds P[||ZZ^T-NI||_op>N/4] by 16r(r+1)/N<=1/64. The intersection B of the two good events has probability at least3/64, with no independence assumption between them. A and B are independent, because Q and Z are independent column blocks.

On A intersect B,

    lambda_min(M)>=3N/4,
    delta >= |M12|/p >= (sqrt(N)/2-r epsilon^2)/p >=sqrt(N)/(4p),
    sqrt(w0) <=||M^(-1/2)Q||_F <=2r epsilon/sqrt(3N).

N>=r and the displayed assumptions imply

    delta/sqrt(w0) >=sqrt(3) N/(8p r epsilon)
                       >=sqrt(3)/(16r epsilon)=8sqrt(3)>mu^2/2.

The ratio is well defined off the null singular-Q set. Finally

    delta <= [N/4+r^2 epsilon^2+r]/p <1/2.

These inequalities prove the probability claim. Since gamma>=delta, the proposed inverse-Gram criterion fails on this event too. Its failure persists for arbitrarily large p, despite the usual unconditioned relative Gram concentration.

## Interpretation and provenance

This does not say that no other perturbation argument works. It rejects the specific worst-case minimum-overlap barrier with arbitrary-confidence Gaussian initialization, even at large aspect ratio. A successful quantitative argument could exploit correlations, avoid minimum-overlap barriers entirely, or control passage through their zero sets as allowed by C030. Both whole targets remain open.

then $x = x^*$ (resp. $y = y^{**}$) and $\gamma_1(x^*, Y^{-}(x^*)) = 0$ (resp. $\gamma_2(X^-(y^{**}),y^{**}) = 0$). Furthermore, $x^*$ is a pole of $\phi_2$ (resp. $y^{**}$ is a pole of $\phi_1$)  if and only if $(r_{2} + 1)\mu_2 > 2 \quad (resp. \quad (r_{1} + 1)\mu_1 > 2).$
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 22 of arXiv:2609.01190, 'Rough differential equations on manifolds via natural bundles'] Let $f:\Rsf^m\to\Rsf$ be a smooth, compactly supported function and let $\varepsilon, \tilde{\varepsilon}, \delta, \zeta\in [0,\infty)$ and $a,b, \tilde{a},\tilde{b}\in\Rsf^m$ be such that 
	\[
		|b-a|\leq \varepsilon, 
			\quad 
		|\tilde{b}-\tilde{a}|\leq \tilde{\varepsilon}, 
			\quad 
		|\tilde{a}-a|\leq \delta, 
			\quad\mbox{and}\quad 
		|\tilde{b}-\tilde{a} - (b-a)| \leq \zeta.
	\]
Let also $T_0,T_1: \Rsf^m\times\Rsf^m\to\Rsf$ be defined by 
	\begin{align*}
		& T_0(x,y):= f(y)-f(x),\\
		& T_1(x,y):= f(y)-f(x)- \frac{\partial f}{\partial x^j}(x)(y^j-x^j)
	\end{align*}
for $x,y\in\Rsf^m$. Then
	\[
		\left|T_0(a,b)\right|  \lesssim \varepsilon 
		\quad\mbox{and}\quad
		|T_0(\tilde{a},\tilde{b})-T_0(a,b)| \lesssim \varepsilon(\delta + \zeta) + \zeta,
	\]
and
	\[
		 |T_1(a,b)| \lesssim \varepsilon^2
		 \quad \mbox{and}\quad 
		 |T_1(\tilde{a},\tilde{b})-T_1(a,b)| \lesssim \varepsilon^2(\delta + \zeta) + (\varepsilon + \tilde{\varepsilon})\zeta
	\]
where the constants are non-decreasing functions of $C^1$, $C^2$, $C^2$, and $C^3$ norm of $f$, respectively. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:antisym-sob of arXiv:2608.17022, 'Sharp hypocoercive convergence estimates for underdamped Langevin dynamics with specular r'] Let $f\in\mathscr C$ and let
\[
g(x,v)=g_0(x)+v\cdot G(x),\qquad g_0\in H^1(\Omega),\quad G\in H^1(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^d),
\]
and assume the trace condition
\begin{equation}
n(x)\cdot G(x)=0\qquad\text{for $\sigma$-a.e.\ }x\in\partial\Omega ,
\end{equation}
where $G$ on $\partial\Omega$ means the trace of $G$. Then $g\in\Lmu$, $\mathscr{L}_a g\in\Lmu$, and
\begin{equation}
\ip{\mathscr{L}_a f}{g}=-\ip{f}{\mathscr{L}_a g}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 243 of arXiv:2601.16377, '2601.16377'] \cite{MumTata}
 Let $\Sigma$ be a compact Riemann surface of genus $\mathsf{g}$ equipped with a lagrangian sublattice $\mathcal{L} \subset H_1(\Sigma,\amsmathbb{Z})$. There exists a unique meromorphic bidifferential $\mathcal{B}^{\Sigma,\mathcal{L}}$ with the following properties.
\begin{itemize}
\item It is symmetric in its two variables.
\item It has double poles on the diagonal with biresidue $1$, \textit{i.e.} for any $p \in \Sigma$ and local coordinate $\zeta_p$ near $p$, we have
\[
\mathcal{B}^{\Sigma,\mathcal{L}}(z_1,z_2)\,\, \mathop{=}_{z_1,z_2 \rightarrow p}\,\, \frac{\dd\zeta_{p}(z_1)\dd\zeta_{p}(z_2)}{(\zeta_p(z_1) - \zeta_p(z_2))^2} + O(1).
\]
\item It is normalized on $\mathcal{L}$, \textit{i.e.} for any $\mathsf{a} \in \mathcal{L}$ we have $\oint_{z \in \mathsf{a}} \mathcal{B}^{\Sigma,\mathcal{L}}(z_0,z) = 0$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 18 of arXiv:2609.03054, 'The classes of bivariate Schur and Herglotz matrix-valued rational functions: realizations'] Let $p(z_1, z_2)$, with $p(0, 0)=1$, be a non-constant 
bivariate polynomial with real coefficients. Then $p$ admits a representation 
\begin{equation} p(z_1,z_2)=\det (I_{|n|} - K Z_n ),
\end{equation}
with $n=(n_1,n_2)=\deg p$ and $K\in {\mathbb R}^{|n|\times |n|}$ a contraction, where $|n|=n_1+n_2$ and
$Z_n=z_1I_{n_1}\oplus z_2I_{n_2}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] Assume that $Q\colon\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty)$ is continuous,
$Q(x)\to\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$, and is not constant.  Then
\[
    \lim_{\beta\downarrow0}\lambda'(\beta)=\infty,
    \qquad
    \lim_{\beta\uparrow\infty}\lambda'(\beta)=q_*.
\]
Consequently,
\[
    \beta\longmapsto\lambda'(\beta)
\]
is a continuous strictly decreasing bijection from $(0,\infty)$ onto
$(q_*,\infty)$.  In particular, for every $\theta>q_*$ there is a unique
$\beta_\theta>0$ such that $\lambda'(\beta_\theta)=\theta$.

[Definition def:consistent of arXiv:2510.13572, 'Coalescence in Markov chains'] A probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathcal{F}_S$ is \emph{consistent} with $P\in\mathcal{P}_S$,
in which case we say that the pair $(P,\mu)$ is \emph{consistent},  if
\begin{equation}
p_{i,j} = \mu\bigl(\{f\in\mathcal{F}_S: f(i)=j\}\bigr), \qquad  i,j\in S.
\end{equation}
Let $\mathcal L_P$ denote the set of probability measures $\mu$ on $\mathcal{F}_S$ 
that are consistent with $P\in\mathcal{P}_S$.  \hfill $\blacktriangleleft$

body:
[Lemma lem:regularization of arXiv:2608.30888, 'Three-term asymptotics for discrete\\ Hardy--Rellich constants in high dimension'] Let $\gamma\geq1$, let $\alpha<0$, and let $\phi$ be smooth on $\mathbb T^N$.  Put
$V=\omega^\gamma$ and
\[
 f_\varepsilon=(\omega+\varepsilon)^\alpha,
 \qquad h_\varepsilon=(\rho+\varepsilon)^{\gamma/2}.
\]
The first-order ground-state identity and the second-order periodic Rellich
identity are valid with $f_\varepsilon$, and the conjugation identity for
$\int h_\varepsilon^2|\nabla\phi|^2$ is valid with $h_\varepsilon$.  As
$\varepsilon\downarrow0$, all coefficient terms converge in $L^1$, while the
non-negative square terms are lower semicontinuous.  Consequently the
inequalities obtained by discarding those squares remain valid for
$f=\omega^\alpha$ and $h=\rho^{\gamma/2}$.

 \mathbb{P}\!\left(
   \abs{\sum_{i=1}^N\varepsilon_i a_i-x}\leq \rho
 \right)
 \leq \frac{C}{\sqrt K}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 1 (Gittins Index, Gittins index policy) of arXiv:2606.24703, 'Scheduling jobs with unknown size distribution in a M/G/1 queue: the shifted empirical Git'] \ \\
   The Gittins index function at age $x$ of a job with  size
   measure $\phi$ and remaining probability function $\bar{F}$ is

    \begin{equation}
      
      \nu(x) := \sup_{y > x}\frac{\pr (X \leq y | X>x)}{\E(\min(X,y) -x | X>x)} =  \sup_{y > x} \frac{\int_{x}^{y}  d\phi(u)}{\int_{x}^{y} \bar{F}(u) du}.
    \end{equation}
    The corresponding Gittins index policy works as follows:
    Whenever the  age $x$ of the current active job is preemptable ($x\in \XP$), the Gittins index policy activates one  job with the maximal current Gittins index.
title: Gittins Index, Gittins index policy

body:
planar first-passage percolation
conditions known to be met for a large class of absolutely continuous edge-weight distributions - the abstract does not list them
the quantity bounded is the NON-RANDOM fluctuation E T - n mu, not the variance

PAIRS WITH THE UPPER BOUND: the Alexander-method state of the art gives E T(0,x) - mu(x) <= C(|x| log|x|)^{1/2}. This gives the other side, sqrt(log n). The gap between sqrt(log n) and sqrt(n log n) is where the whole question of the non-random fluctuation lives.
METHOD: an application of Dembin-Elboim-Peled's work on the BKS midpoint problem, plus Mermin-Wagner type estimates - the same estimate family Dembin-Elboim use for the crossing noise-sensitivity result.
SOURCE: arXiv:2511.06166v2, 'Lower bounds on non-random fluctuations in planar first passage percolation', submitted 2025-11-08, last revised 2026-06-01. Official arXiv API record retrieved by lane P4 on 2026-08-22; no journal reference as of that date.
VERIFICATION STATUS: theorem-checked-against-source for the conclusion and its scope; the hypothesis set is NOT pinned by the abstract ('some conditions that are known to be met for a large class of absolutely continuous edge weight distributions'), so nothing is asserted here about which laws qualify.
title: Hassler (2025, revised June 2026): the NON-RANDOM fluctuation in planar first-passage percolation is at least of order sqrt(log n), under conditions known to hold for a large class of absolutely continuous edge-weight distributions. This improves Nakajima's log log n bound and is the first result showing divergence of the non-random fluctuation in ARBITRARY directions.

body: In mathematics, the Weierstrass elliptic functions are elliptic functions that take a particularly simple form. They are named for Karl Weierstrass. This class of functions is also referred to as ℘-functions and they are usually denoted by the symbol ℘, a uniquely fancy script p. They play an important role in the theory of elliptic functions, i.e., meromorphic functions that are doubly periodic. A ℘-function together with its derivative can be used to parameterize elliptic curves and they generate the field of elliptic functions with respect to a given period lattice.
title: Weierstrass elliptic function
