- s(s+2)(s+4) (delta_ij w_k w_l + the five other pair placements) |w|^{-s-6}
+ s(s+2) (delta_ij delta_kl + delta_ik delta_jl + delta_il delta_jk) |w|^{-s-4}.

Contracting against any four vectors v1,...,v4 and applying Cauchy-Schwarz bounds its absolute value by

s(s+2)[(s+4)(s+6)+6(s+4)+3] |w|^{-s-4} product_j |vj|
= C4(s)|w|^{-s-4} product_j |vj|.

The path stays away from zero. The two remainder weights integrate to 1/4. Finite total variation, compact supports, and this uniform derivative bound justify Fubini and give the asserted inequality, including for atomic signed measures.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:cc39eb09a6500e905ff79273369c99c1df7a527ede643ddffe64991092a31494","revision_digest":"sha256:4eb244dbc974c74481eac9eeb5dad04d17298fa77901ad3660fc75e243618166","source_id":"own-work:w528:p0309-dipole-free-fourth-derivative-bound","source_revision":"campaign-2026-10-10-w528-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Definition 3 of arXiv:2609.02019, '2609.02019'] Let $s>\frac{3}{2}+\max\{2\delta_{\mathcal Q},1\}$.Let $\tau^*$ be a stopping time with $\mathbb P(\tau^*>0)=1$.
		An $H^s$-valued progressively measurable process
		\[
		v=(v(t))_{0\le t<\tau^*}
		\]
		is called a maximal $H^s$ classical solution to \eqref{Target problem SCCF} if the
		following conditions hold:
		
		\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=0.79cm]
			\setlength\itemsep{0.2em}
			
			\item  For a.e. $\omega\in\Omega$, and for every $T<\tau^*(\omega)$,
			$v\in C([0,T];H^s)$.
			
			\item $\pas$, for every $t\in[0,\tau^*)$,  \eqref{Target problem SCCF}
			holds as an identity in $C_b^1(\mathbb R)$.
			
			\item On the event $\{\tau^*<\infty\}$,
			$\limsup_{t\uparrow\tau^*}\|v(t)\|_{H^s}=\infty.$
			
		\end{itemize}
		
		If $\mathbb P(\tau^*=\infty)=1$, the maximal solution is called global.

[Prop 66 of arXiv:2604.00635, 'Large deviations of the periodic Toda chain'] Let $\boldsymbol{\lambda}^+_N \in \mathbb{R}^N_{<}$. Then the following are equivalent.
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\boldsymbol{\lambda}^+_N \in \mathcal{A}_N$.
    \item There exists a vector $\boldsymbol{\eta}_N \in \mathbb{R}^N_{<}$ such that the following holds. Let

$$P(x) := \prod_{k=1}^N ( x - \eta_k)$$ and let $\zeta_1, \dots, \zeta_{N-1} \in \mathbb{R}$ be the roots of $P^\prime$. Then $|P(\zeta_k)| > 2\veps_N$ for all $k \in \intn{1}{N-1}$ and $\lambda_1^+, \dots, \lambda_N^+$ are the roots of $P - 2\veps_N$.
\end{enumerate}

\[
  U_\pi\rho^N U_\pi^*=\rho^N,
  \qquad
  \mbox{ for all } \pi\in\mathfrak S_N.
\]
This is the labelled-particle analogue of the symmetry appearing in bosonic
closed quantum systems, although we do not restrict the state space to the symmetric
tensor product.

body:
For the planar walk that chooses a fair horizontal step on a first visit and a fair vertical step on a repeat visit, its horizontal and vertical departure counts H_n and V_n both tend to infinity almost surely. The coordinates admit X_n=S^H_(H_n), Y_n=S^V_(V_n), where S^H and S^V are independent simple symmetric walks, and each clock visits every nonnegative integer. Consequently each coordinate is unbounded in both signs and hits zero infinitely often. The clocks depend jointly on the visited set; independence of the time-changed coordinates and infinitely many visits to a single planar site are not asserted.
All hypotheses and scope restrictions in the statement apply.

Each clock is integer-valued, starts at zero, increases only by zero or one, and is unbounded, so it attains every integer value. The underlying walk's arbitrarily large positive and negative values and infinitely many zero indices are attained at arbitrarily late global times. This proves the coordinate claims. The two clocks depend on the entire visited set; their zero indices need not coincide. Synchronization of coordinate returns is the missing recurrence step.

[Defn 29 of arXiv:2608.13976, 'Boundary Harnack principle for diffusion with jumps on metric measure spaces'] Let $B$ be a ball in $\R^d.$
Suppose that $U$ is an open subset of $B$. A Borel function $u$ on
$B$ is said to be:
\begin{itemize}
\item harmonic in $U$ with respect to $X^{b, B}$ if
\begin{equation}
u(x) = \E_x[u(X^{b, B}_{\tau^b_{V}})],\qquad
x\in V,
\end{equation}
for every bounded open set $V$ with $\overline{V}\subset U$;

\item excessive with respective to $X^{b, B}$ if $u$ is
nonnegative and for every $t > 0$ and $x\in B$
\[
u(x) \geq \E_x[u(X^{b, B}_{t})]
\quad\mbox{and}\quad u(x) = \lim_{t \downarrow0}
\E_x[u(X^{b, B}_t)];
\]

\item a potential with respect to $X^{b, B}$ if it is excessive
with respect to $X^{b, B}$ and for every sequence $\{U_n\}_{n \ge1}$
of open sets with
$\overline{U}_n \subset U_{n+1}$ and $\bigcup_n U_n = B$,
\[
\lim_{n \to\infty}
\E_x[u(X^{b, B}_{\tau^b_{U_n}})] = 0,\qquad
\xi_B\mbox{-a.e. } x\in B;
\]

\item a pure potential with respect to $X^{b, B}$ if
it is a potential with respect to $X^{b, B}$ and

\[
\lim_{t \to\infty} \E_x[u(X^{b, B}_t)] = 0,\qquad
\xi_B \mbox{-a.e. } x\in B.
\]

\end{itemize}
title: Definition 29 of arXiv:2608.13976

[Theorem thm:main1 of arXiv:2608.11084, 'Sharp Frobenius-Norm Concentration for Sample Moment Tensors'] Let \(X_1,\ldots,X_N\) be i.i.d. copies of a centered sub-Gaussian random
vector \(X\in\mathbb R^d\) with covariance matrix \(\Sigma\) and
sub-Gaussian constant \(K\). Let \(p\ge 2\) be an integer. Then, for every
\(q\ge1\),
\[
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(
\mathbbm{E}
\bigg\|
\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^{\otimes p}
-
\mathbbm{E} X^{\otimes p}
\bigg\|_{\mathsf F}^q
\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)^{1/q}
\lesssim_p
K^p
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(
\frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt N}
+
\rho_p(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q\land N}{N}}
+
\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N}
\aftergroup\egroup\originalright),
\]
where
\[
\rho_p(\Sigma)
:=
\begin{cases}
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{p/2},
& p \text{ even},\\[3pt]
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf F}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2},
& p \text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\]
Moreover, if $X$ is Gaussian, then
\[
\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft(\mathbbm{E} \bigg\|
\frac{1}{N}
\sum_{i=1}^N
X_i^{\otimes p}-\mathbbm{E} X^{\otimes p}
\bigg\|_{\mathsf{F}}^q\aftergroup\egroup\originalright)^{1/q}
\asymp_p
\frac{\mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma)^{p/2}}{\sqrt{N}}
+
\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)\sqrt{\frac{q}{N}}
+
\|\Sigma\|^{p/2}\frac{q^{p/2}}{N},
\]
where
\[
\rho_{p,G}(\Sigma)
:=
\begin{cases}
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf{F}}^{p/2-1}\|\Sigma\|, & p \text{ even},\\[3pt]
\|\Sigma\|_{\mathsf{F}}^{(p-1)/2}\|\Sigma\|^{1/2}, & p \text{ odd}.
\end{cases}
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Concentration of sample moment tensors

Consider the Gaussian field $X_\varepsilon^\alpha$ defined in (equation eqModel: X epsilon alpha white noise integral of the paper). There exist constants $C,c>0$ and $T_*,\lambda_*>0$ such that
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbb{P}\Bigl(
		\sup_{x\in[0,1)^d}X_\varepsilon^\alpha(x)
		\leq A_\alpha(T)-\lambda
		\Bigr)
		\leq Ce^{-c\lambda},
		\qquad T\geq T_*,\quad\lambda\geq\lambda_*,

	where $A_\alpha(T)$ is defined in (equation eqIntroduction: A(t) of the paper).

OWNER RESULT DRAFT: proof (unaudited), T336-w727-C014 v1; no novelty claim. Let N,D,A,H be positive integers, L>=0 an integer, W,K0>=1. Each layer first applies residual N-normalized ReLU attention with A heads, each having D-by-D Q,K,V matrices, and then a tokenwise residual ReLU MLP a -> a+U2 ReLU(U1 a), with U1 of size H-by-D and U2 of size D-by-H. All matrix entries and the final two-output readout entries are in [-W,W]. The fixed input encoding is parameter independent and every coordinate is bounded by K0. The readout acts on a fixed token and may use fixed coordinatewise output interval clips. Put P=L(3AD^2+2DH)+2D. Starting K_0=K0,E_0=0, set Kbar_l=K_l+AD^4W^3K_l^3, Ebar_l=(1+3AD^4W^3K_l^2)E_l+3AD^4W^2K_l^3, K_(l+1)=(1+HDW^2)Kbar_l, and E_(l+1)=(1+HDW^2)Ebar_l+2HDW Kbar_l. Then Lambda=DW E_L+DK_L>0 bounds uniform parameter-to-output sensitivity: for every theta,theta' in the parameter cube at sup distance delta, the maximum coordinate difference of the two outputs is <=Lambda delta uniformly over the stated inputs. For every gamma>0, q=max(1,ceil(2W Lambda/gamma)) gives a fixed output gamma-cover of size at most (q+1)^P and log size at most P log(2+2W Lambda/gamma). No token/layer independence is assumed; the constants do not grow with N. The factor 2HDW Kbar accounts separately for perturbing BOTH trainable MLP matrices, and the MLP acts on post-attention Kbar,Ebar. Biases must use a preserved constant coordinate already counted in D, or be counted separately. Fixed output clipping is used only as a nonexpansive map here; no assertion that variance clipping decreases KL is made. C006's saved deterministic attention-stage estimate is used; its statistical theorem and C007 remain unaudited. This supplies the deterministic cover needed for C013's architecture with A=5, P=L(15D^2+2DH)+2D and clipped-context input bound K0=max(1,B,s). An explicit W containing C013's comparator coefficients, and the correct statistical task-law/output-range hypotheses, still must be established before claiming the full raw-input ERM theorem.
N,D,A,H positive integers; L>=0; W,K0>=1; all trainable matrix/readout entries bounded by W
Parameter-independent input encoding bounded by K0; normalized ReLU attention followed by a residual ReLU MLP in each layer
Fixed token readout and optional fixed output clips; biases only through a counted constant register or separately counted
C006 saved attention-stage estimate used as ground; no new concentration theorem or independent audit claimed

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:7a7544c4fc173cfc087cd0d6fbac6987264deae806a48320ba0721184614efca","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/7a/7a7544c4fc173cfc087cd0d6fbac6987264deae806a48320ba0721184614efca.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:ca55a27068c97123eb5befea4d75f47723f483cbd1d8e084684a75368e1ebb2f","bundle_entry_key":"t336-w727-c014","bundle_id":"population.w727-t336-residual-mlp-parameter-cover-009","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Transformer generalization; neural-network parameter covers","draft":"w727/bundle_009.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:learning.transformers:draft-normalized-relu-attention-residual-mlp-parameter-cover","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C014 v1: parameter covers with residual ReLU MLP blocks included

Kind: bound. Target: none (reviewer-authorized prior-averaged generalization).
Status: proof (unaudited). No novelty claim. This supplies the architecture
hypothesis missing when applying the saved attention-only C006 cover to the
raw-input C013 model. It does not claim a new concentration theorem.

## 1. Architecture and statement

Let N,D,A,H be positive integers, L a nonnegative integer, and W,K0>=1.
There are N tokens of width D, A normalized ReLU-attention heads in each
layer, and a tokenwise residual ReLU MLP of hidden width H AFTER attention.
Unused heads/hidden units may be padded with zeros. For each layer define

    a_i = h_i + (1/N) sum_{b=1}^A sum_{j=1}^N
                   ReLU(<Q_b h_i,K_b h_j>) V_b h_j,
    h_i^+ = a_i + U_2 ReLU(U_1 a_i),

with Q_b,K_b,V_b of size D by D, U_1 of size H by D, U_2 of size D by H.
All matrix entries and the entries of a final two-output linear readout
lie in [-W,W]. The fixed input encoding is independent of the parameter
vector and uniformly bounded by K0 in coordinate sup norm. The readout
acts on a fixed token. It may be followed by fixed coordinatewise interval
clips, including mean clipping to [-U,U] and variance clipping to [v0,v1]
with 0<v0<=v1. Those clips have no trainable parameters. Biases, if used,
are implemented by a preserved constant register included in D, as in C004.

The dense trainable scalar count (or an upper bound with fixed masks) is

    P=L(3 A D^2+2 D H)+2D.

Define nonnegative deterministic recurrences, starting with K_0=K0,E_0=0:

    Kbar_l=K_l+A D^4 W^3 K_l^3,
    Ebar_l=(1+3 A D^4 W^3 K_l^2) E_l+3 A D^4 W^2 K_l^3,
    K_{l+1}=(1+H D W^2) Kbar_l,
    E_{l+1}=(1+H D W^2) Ebar_l+2 H D W Kbar_l.

Put Lambda=D W E_L+D K_L>0. For every two parameter vectors theta,theta'
of coordinate sup distance delta,

    sup_inputs max(|mu_theta-mu_theta'|,|v_theta-v_theta'|)
       <=Lambda delta.

The supremum is over all encoded inputs satisfying the displayed fixed
K0 bound; no independence among tokens or layers is assumed. The bound
is valid for every N and its constants do not grow with N.

For gamma>0 let q=max(1,ceil(2W Lambda/gamma)). There is a fixed output
gamma-cover of cardinality at most (q+1)^P, hence log cardinality at most

    P log(2+2W Lambda/gamma).

These estimates concern a bounded parameter cube, not unbounded weights.
They are uniform deterministic bounds, not probabilistic training claims.

## 2. Attention stage: use the saved deterministic estimate

C006 Section 2 establishes exactly the attention-stage norm and joint
input/parameter perturbation estimate used here. Substituting head count
A for its H, if all entering states have norm <=K_l and the two entering
states differ by <=E_l delta, then their attention outputs have norm
<=Kbar_l and differ by <=Ebar_l delta. Its proof bounds transformed
coordinates by D W K_l and uses the three factors in each head; normalized
summation cancels N. This saved deterministic estimate is taken as ground,
not re-audited in this extension. C006 itself remains independently unaudited.

The new issue is that these outputs then pass through TWO trainable MLP
matrices. Omitting that stage is not a valid architecture specialization
for the trainable raw-input encoder.

## 3. New residual-MLP stage and its two parameter contributions

Write a,a' for one token's attention outputs. Assume both are bounded by
Kbar and their difference by Ebar delta. Let U_1,U_2 and U_1',U_2' have
entries bounded by W, with entrywise differences at most delta. In the
coordinate sup norm, the hidden activation r=ReLU(U_1 a) satisfies

    ||r||<=D W Kbar,
    ||r-r'||<=D(W Ebar+Kbar) delta.

The second statement follows by splitting
U_1 a-U_1'a'=U_1(a-a')+(U_1-U_1')a' and using ReLU's 1-Lipschitz property.
There are D summands per hidden coordinate. This accounts for perturbing
U_1 as well as a; no derivative of ReLU at zero is required.

There are H hidden summands per output coordinate, so

    ||U_2 r||<=H D W^2 Kbar,
    ||U_2 r-U_2' r'||
       <=H W ||r-r'||+H delta ||r'||
       <=H D W^2 Ebar delta+2 H D W Kbar delta.

The first H D W Kbar parameter term comes from U_1 and the second from
U_2. Adding the identity residual a proves

    ||a+U_2 r||<=(1+H D W^2)Kbar,
    ||(a+U_2 r)-(a'+U_2'r')||
       <=[(1+H D W^2)Ebar+2H D W Kbar]delta.

This proves the new K/E recurrence after the full attention-then-MLP layer.
Induct on layers, with E_0=0 because the input encoding is parameter
independent. The order matters: the MLP sees Kbar_l,Ebar_l, not K_l,E_l.

## 4. Readout and finite cover

For the final readout R and R', split
R h-R'h'=R(h-h')+(R-R')h'. Its two output coordinates therefore differ
by at most (D W E_L+D K_L)delta. Fixed scalar interval clipping is
1-Lipschitz and preserves this bound. This use of clipping does NOT assert
that clipping a variance decreases Gaussian KL.

Use the same fixed parameter grid as C006: divide each [-W,W] coordinate
into q equal intervals. A grid vector is within 2W/q<=gamma/Lambda of
every parameter vector. It gives output error <=gamma uniformly, before
observing any training tasks. The full cube grid has (q+1)^P points.
Since q=max(1,ceil(x)), x=2W Lambda/gamma>0, one has q+1<=x+2,
giving the logarithmic bound in Section 1. For L=0 the assertion reduces
to the linear readout, with K_L=K0,E_L=0 and P=2D, as required.
Fixed masks can only reduce the free coordinate count; retaining P as
an upper bound is harmless. All actual trainable encoder coefficients
must be included in these parameter coordinates.

## 5. Consequence for the T336 statistical route and its unpaid step

For C013 the architecture substitution is A=5, and D,H,L are its displayed
raw-input widths and depth. Thus P=L(15D^2+2DH)+2D exactly matches its dense
parameter upper bound. With context labels clipped to [-B,B], its fixed
raw-coordinate/label/role/constant input encoding has K0=max(1,B,s).
The grid feature samples are coefficients of the trainable MLP, NOT an
unaccounted parameter-dependent input map.

The C006/C007 concentration arguments use the architecture through a
fixed uniform output cover and P,Lambda. This lemma supplies those objects
for attention PLUS residual MLPs. Their respective statistical task-law,
output-range and clipping assumptions must still be satisfied; this
deterministic lemma neither verifies nor weakens those assumptions.
In particular C006's attention-only P=3ALD^2+2D cannot be used when the
encoder MLP matrices are trainable. C006/C007 remain unaudited statistical
claims; no new independent PASS or concentration proof is asserted here.

The next unpaid step is an explicit entry bound W for C013's constructed
encoder and C002 attention matrices, ensuring comparator membership in
the bounded parameter cube. One must then set output clip ranges that
contain that comparator's outputs and apply the correct original-task
or conditioned-task version of the prior-averaged log-loss bound.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:8bd1052f0e37a97b383e243ca16b39049739ef3febde09fc99222865928973e6","revision_digest":"sha256:4ee349df73592768c4ef1d3c9bfd4243a04c2eac0b50e99a389cdfb144e594fe","source_id":"owner:T336-w727-C014-v1","source_revision":"T336-w727-C014-v1","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2609.01402, 'Parabolic Lie algebroid connections on parabolic principal bundles over curves'] \mbox{}
\begin{enumerate}
\item There are natural equivalences of categories $\Phi\,:\,\mathscr{C}_{\Gamma}\,\overset{\sim}\longrightarrow
\, \mathscr{C}$ and $\Psi\,:\,\mathscr{V}_{\Gamma}\,\overset{\sim}\longrightarrow \,\mathscr{V}$. 

\item The following equalities of functors hold:
$$\Psi\circ\mathbb{A}\ = \ \mathbb{A}_{*}\circ\Phi\ \ \text{ and }\ \ \Psi\circ\mathrm{ad}\ =\ \mathrm{ad}_{*}\circ\Phi .$$

\item There is a natural isomorphism $\zeta\,:\,TX_{*}\, \overset{\sim}\longrightarrow\, \Psi(TY)$
given by the differential of $\sigma$. Moreover, for any $E_{G}\,\in\, \mathscr{C}_{\Gamma}$,
$\Psi$ takes the equivariant Atiyah exact sequence for 
$E_{G}$ to the parabolic Atiyah exact sequence for $\Phi(E_{G})\,\in\,\mathscr{C}$.

\item There is an equivalence of categories between the parabolic Lie algebroids on $(X,\,S)$ and the
$\Gamma$--equivariant Lie algebroids on $Y$. 

\item Take $E_{G}\,\in\, \mathscr{C}_{\Gamma}$ and a $\Gamma$--equivariant Lie algebroid
$(V,\,\phi)$ on $Y$. Giving a $\Gamma$--equivariant holomorphic $(V,\,\phi)$--connection on $E_{G}$ is equivalent
to giving a parabolic $(V_{*},\, \phi_{*})$--connection on $\mathcal{E}_{G}\,:=\,\Phi(E_{G})\,\in
\, \mathscr{C}$, where $(V_{*},\, \phi_{*})$ is the parabolic Lie algebroid on $X$ corresponding to
$(V,\, \phi)$.
\end{enumerate}

body: In mathematics, the spectral gap is the difference between the moduli of the two largest eigenvalues of a matrix or operator; alternately, it is sometimes taken as the smallest non-zero eigenvalue. Various theorems relate this difference to other properties of the system. The spectral gap gets its name from the matrix spectrum, that is, for a matrix, the list of its eigenvalues. It provides insight on diffusion within the graph: corresponding the spectral gap to the smallest non-zero eigenvalue, it is then the mode of the network state that shows the slowest exponential decay over time.

[Theorem 52 (Poisson boundary) of arXiv:2608.03575, '2608.03575'] Conditionally on \((G,\rho,\Theta)\), almost surely the unit circle
\(\partial\D\), equipped with the exit measures
\((\nu_v)_{v\in V(G)}\), realizes the Poisson boundary of \(G\).

Equivalently, for every bounded harmonic function \(h\) on \(G\), there
exists a bounded Borel function \(g:\partial\D\to\mathbb R\) such that
\begin{equation}
    h(v)
    =
    \mathbb E_v^G[g(\Xi)]
    =
    \int_{\partial\D}g(\xi)\,d\nu_v(\xi).
\end{equation}

Assume there exists an open interval $I\subset \mathbb{R}$ such that $J=[a,b)$, $(a,b]$ or $[a,b]\subset I$ on which the function $F$ is a strictly convex function and subsequently the Bregman divergence $\phi_{_F}$  is well defined as well. Let $\pi: I \to  J$ defined by $\pi(u) =a$ if $u< a$, $\pi(u)=b$ if $u> b$ and $\pi = I_d$ on $J$ (projection from $I$ onto $J$). Assume ${\cal H}\big({\rm supp}(P)\big)= [a,b]\cap \mathbb{R}$ (convex hull of the support of $P$). Then $\phi_{_F}$ and the distortion functions $G_n$ can  be extended on $I^2$ and $I^n$ respectively and
\[
\forall\, x=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\!\in I^n, \quad G_n\big(\pi(x_1),\ldots,\pi(x_n) \big)\le G_n(x_1,\ldots,x_n). 
\]
In particular, $\inf_{I^n\cap {\cal S}_n}G_n = \inf_{{\cal S}_n([a,b])}G_n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition ascending.def of arXiv:2609.00163, 'Decompositions and diagrams of symplectic surfaces in Weinstein domains'] Let $(W, \lambda)$ be a Weinstein domain with a compatible Morse function $\rho:W\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$.
A smoothly embedded oriented surface $(S, \partial S) \subset (W, \partial W)$ is \emph{ascending} if 
\begin{itemize}
    \item $S$ contains no critical points of $\rho$,
    \item $\rho|_S$ is a Morse function, and

[Lemma 23 (Sign--Dirichlet representation) of arXiv:2605.11451, '2605.11451'] Let $X^{(n)}$ be uniform on $B_p^n$. Then
\[
 X_i=\eps_iT_i^{\alpha},\qquad i=1,\ldots,n,
\]
where $\eps_1,\ldots,\eps_n$ are independent Rademacher signs and
\[
 (T_0,T_1,\ldots,T_n)\sim\operatorname{Dirichlet}(1,\alpha,\ldots,\alpha),
\]
independently of the signs. Here $T_0=1-\sum_{i=1}^n |X_i|^p$.

[Proposition 28 of arXiv:2609.02064, 'Coalescence and fluctuations of O'Connell--Yor polymers\\ via the free-energy correlation '] Fix $\wt x\in\R$ and a compact set
  $K\Subset\R\setminus\{\wt x\}$.  Then,
  we have 
  
  \noi
  \begin{align}
    \sup_{u\in K}\bigg|
      \frac1\be T_{2,\eps}(u,\wt x)  - 
   \frac12\EE\bigg[  \int_{\DN^2} Q_{\wt x}(d\wt\ga)Q_u(d\ga) 
    \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}   \mathfrak D_i(\wt x+\wt\ga_i,u+\ga_i)    \bigg]    \bigg|
    \xrightarrow{\eps\to 0} 0 .
    
    \end{align}
Recall from \eqref{T1_pre} that
\[
      \frac1\be T_{1,\eps}(u,\wt x)
    =\al^2\EE\bigg[\int_{\DN^2}
      \Bigl(
        \Psi^\eps(\wt x+\wt\ga_n-u-\ga_n)
        +\Psi^\eps(u+\ga_n)
      \Bigr)
      Q_{\wt x}^\eps(d\wt\ga)Q_u^\eps(d\ga)
    \bigg].
        \]
Then, we have
    
    \noi
  \begin{align}  
  \begin{aligned} 
    \sup_{u\in K}
      \bigg| \frac{\al^2}{2}\EE\bigg[
        \int_{\DN^2} Q_{\wt x}(d\wt\ga)Q_u(d\ga)
        & \Bigl(   \sgn(\wt x+\wt\ga_n-u-\ga_n)   +\sgn(u+\ga_n)     \Bigr)      \bigg]  \\
     & \qquad  -   \frac1\be T_{1,\eps}(u,\wt x)
        \bigg|
      \xrightarrow{\eps\to 0} 0. 
      \end{aligned} 
    
  \end{align}

[Pro 25 (Local group quotient) of arXiv:2608.30990, 'Convergence of symmetries: nilpotency, dimension, and perfectness'] Let $G$ be a local group, $H \subset G $ a normal sub-local group with normalizing neighborhood $V$, and $W \subset G$ an open symmetric set. Assume $W^{6} \subset V$ and $V^6 \subset G$. Then
 \begin{itemize}
     \item The binary relation defined by 
     \[  x \sim y \text{ if and only if  } x^{-1} y \in H          \]
     is an equivalence relation on $W$.  
     \item Setting  
     \[     \Omega _{W, H } : = \{ \, ( a , b ) \in (W/\sim) ^{\times 2} \, \vert \,  xy \in  W \text{ for some }x \in a, \, y\in b \, \}   ,      \]
    the local group structure of $G$ induces a well defined inverse map $W / \sim  \to W / \sim $ and a well defined product $\Omega _{W,H} \to W/ \sim$, turning $W/ \sim$, equipped with the quotient topology, into a local group. 
 \end{itemize}
The local group obtained in Proposition \ref{pro:local-quotient} is denoted by   $(G/ H)_W$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:P_t^n roots of arXiv:2512.17808, 'Zeros of polynomial powers under the heat flow'] For any fixed $t>0$, the zeros of $P_t^n$ remain within a distance of $2\sqrt t+o(1)$ from the initial zeros $\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_d$, more precisely, for all $n\in \mathbb{N}$,
\begin{align} \supp(\mu_{n,t})\subset \cup_{j=1}^d B_{2\sqrt t \sqrt{1+\frac{1}{2n\alpha}}} (\lambda_j).
\end{align}
Consequently, the family $(\mu_{n,t})_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ forms a tight sequence of probability distributions.
Moreover, if $t>0$ is sufficiently small so that (equation eq:support_mu_nt of the paper) is a disjoint union, then $$\mu_{n,t}\left(B_{2\sqrt{t}\sqrt{1+\frac{1}{2n\alpha}}}(\lambda_j)\right)=\frac{\alpha_j}{\alpha}, \qquad j=1,\ldots, d.$$
title: Lemma lem:P_t^n roots of arXiv:2512.17808

[Prop 7 of arXiv:2603.27433, 'The $k$-cycle shuffling with repeated cards'] Let $r:=n-\l_1$. Suppose that one of the following holds:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $r\in[\log n,n^{5/6}]$, and $2\le k\le o(n/\log n)$. 
\item $r\in[n^{5/6},0.499 n]$, and $6\log n\le k\le o(n/\log n)$. 
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, suppose that $t':=t-\frac{n\log n}{k}$ satisfies $|t'|\le \frac{n(\log\log n-\omega(1))}{2k}$. Then, we have 
$$|s_\l(k)|^{2t}\le \exp\left(-2r\log n+r\log r-\omega(r)\right).$$
title: Prop 7 of arXiv:2603.27433

[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2605.02002, 'Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI'] (\cite{chen2025rapid1}, Theorem 3.16) Given $C:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$. Assume that a denoising process $(Y_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ is $\phi$-entropically stable with rate $C(t)$ throughout $t\in[0,1]$. Then for each given $\theta\in[0,1]$, the process $(Y_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ will satisfy $R$-approximate conservation of $\phi$-entropy up to time $\theta$ where we take 
$$
R=\exp\left(\int_0^\theta \frac{C(t)}{1-t}dt\right).
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 12 of arXiv:2605.02002

For the semicircle density (1/(2 pi)) sqrt(4 - x^2) on [-2, 2] (mean 0, variance 1), all odd moments vanish and the 2k-th moment equals the Catalan number C_k = (1/(k+1)) binom(2k, k): 1, 2, 5, 14, 42, 132, ... . A semicircle of radius R has 2k-th moment C_k (R/2)^{2k}. In the moment method for a Wigner matrix W = X / sqrt n, where X is real symmetric with independent entries above the diagonal, mean 0 and variance 1, the normalized traces satisfy E tr(W^{2k}) / n -> C_k: expanding the trace as a sum over closed walks of length 2k on the index set, only walks whose edges are each traversed exactly twice and whose underlying graph is a tree survive as n grows, and such walks are counted by C_k; the Catalan numbers determine the semicircle law uniquely because it has compact support. Wigner's theorem then follows from convergence of moments plus a variance bound (or a concentration bound on the trace) giving weak convergence of the empirical spectral distribution in probability.
entries independent up to symmetry with mean 0 and variance 1 before scaling by 1/sqrt n
moments bounded uniformly in n (finite fourth moment suffices for the semicircle limit of the empirical spectral distribution; the diagonal entries may have a different variance)
the moment method identifies the limit because the semicircle law is determined by its moments (compact support)
title: Moments of the Wigner semicircle law are the Catalan numbers (the moment method)

[Mydef of arXiv:2411.08430, 'The Restricted Isometry Property of Block Diagonal Matrices Generated by $\varphi$-Sub-Gau'] A random vector $X$ is called a $\varphi$-sub-Gaussian random vector if all one-dimensional marginals of $X$, i.e., the random variables $\langle X, x\rangle$ for any $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, are $\varphi$-sub-Gaussian. The $\varphi$-sub-Gaussian norm of $X$ is defined as
$$
\tau_{\varphi}(X):=\sup _{x \in \mathrm{S}^{n-1}} \tau_{\varphi}(\langle X, x\rangle),
$$
where $S^{n-1}$ denotes the Euclidean unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^n$.
title: Unnumbered mydef of arXiv:2411.08430, 'The Restricted Isometry Property of Block Diagonal Matrices '

CAMPAIGN RESULT [independently checked proof; E0095-REV v1; no novelty claim]. Consider the connected cubic graph on vertices 0,...,9 with edges (0,3),(0,4),(0,5),(1,2),(1,5),(1,6),(2,3),(2,8),(3,8),(4,6),(4,7),(5,7),(6,9),(7,9),(8,9). Its ordinary SRW gap is simple. Among all 30 absent pairs, the exact derivative-maximizing edges at added weight zero are (2,4) and (2,7). Both yield a strictly smaller ordinary gap at weight one than edge (3,4): their unit gap lies in (47694555/10^8,47694557/10^8), whereas (3,4) lies in (48117795/10^8,48117798/10^8). Thus choosing a unit edge by maximizing infinitesimal gain can fail even with a simple initial gap. This variant changes stationary law; it is not a stationary-preserving Metropolis or total-variation result.

Let X_1, ..., X_N be k-wise independent and let Y_1, ..., Y_N be mutually independent with Y_i equal in law to X_i. For distinct indices i_1, ..., i_s with s <= k and positive integers a_1, ..., a_s with E|X_{i_j}|^{a_j} finite, E[X_{i_1}^{a_1} ... X_{i_s}^{a_s}] = prod_j E[X_{i_j}^{a_j}] = E[Y_{i_1}^{a_1} ... Y_{i_s}^{a_s}], and by linearity the same holds for every polynomial whose monomials each involve at most k distinct coordinates. The bound k is sharp: for the uniform signs with product one and N = k + 1, E[X_1 ... X_{k+1}] = 1 while independent unbiased signs give 0.

Let pi be a probability mass function on a nonempty finite set E with rational masses, and D the least common multiple of the denominators of its masses in lowest terms (denominator 1 for a zero mass). For U uniform on {1, ..., N}, a map F with F(U) distributed exactly as pi exists if and only if D divides N, so D is the least such N. Applied to a rational coupling on S x T, the coordinates of F(U) give the coupled pair from a single uniform seed.

body:
Let f be holomorphic on a punctured disc D' = { 0 < |z - a| < r } and suppose a is an essential singularity of f (neither removable nor a pole; equivalently the Laurent series at a has infinitely many negative-power terms). Then for every 0 < rho < r the image f({ 0 < |z - a| < rho }) is dense in C: for every w in C and every eps > 0 there are points z arbitrarily close to a with |f(z) - w| < eps. Equivalently, every complex number is a limit of f along some sequence z_n -> a. The three singularity types are thereby characterised by the behaviour of |f| near a: bounded (removable, Riemann), tending to infinity (pole), neither (essential). Picard's great theorem sharpens density to: f takes every complex value with at most one exception infinitely often in every punctured neighbourhood of a (exp(1/z) omits 0).
f holomorphic on a punctured disc around a, a an isolated essential singularity
the conclusion is density, not surjectivity: Picard's great theorem is the stronger, deeper statement

body:
[Proposition pro:covering-packing-1 of arXiv:2606.21556, 'Mean field limit of non-exchangeable interacting diffusions on co-evolutionary networks'] Consider a metric space $(\mathcal{X},d_\mathcal{X})$ and a subset $A\subset \mathcal{X}$. Then, we have:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item If $\{y_1,\ldots,y_m\}\subset A$ is a $2\varepsilon$-separated set of $A$ and $\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}$ is a $\varepsilon$-net of $A$, then $m\leq n$.
    \item If $\{y_1,\ldots,y_m\}\subset A$ is a $\varepsilon$-separated set of $A$ such that $m=\mathcal{M}_\varepsilon(A)$, then it also a $\varepsilon$-net of $A$.
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Lemma lem:Fs of arXiv:2607.08551, 'Weighted-threshold Coupon Collection'] Fix $s\in[0,1)$ and define
\[
F_s(\alpha):=
(1-s)\int_0^1 x^{-s}\Bigl(1-e^{-(1-s)\alpha x^{-s}}\Bigr)\,dx,
\qquad
\alpha\ge 0.
\]
Then $F_s$ is continuous, strictly increasing, satisfies $F_s(0)=0$, and
\[
\lim_{\alpha\to\infty}F_s(\alpha)=1.
\]
Hence, for every $\theta\in(0,1)$ there exists a unique $\alpha_{s,\theta}>0$ such that
\[
F_s(\alpha_{s,\theta})=\theta.
\]

body: [Theorem 2.3 (de Finetti’s Theorem) of arXiv:2603.10190, 'Hoeffding-Type Concentration Bounds for Exchangeable Random Variables'] Let $X$ be a standard Borel space. A probability measure $p$ on $X^{\mathbb{N}}$ is exchangeable if and only if there exists a unique probability measure $\rho$ on $PX$ such that, for every $A\in\mathcal{B}(X^{\mathbb{N}})$, $p(A)=\int_{PX}q^{\otimes\mathbb{N}}(A)\rho(\mathrm{d}q).$ In particular, for every $M\in\mathbb{N}$ and every $A\in\mathcal{B}(X^{M})$, $p_{M}(A)=\int_{PX}q^{\otimes M}(A)\rho(\mathrm{d}q),$ where $p_{M}$ denotes the $M$ -dimensional marginal of $p$.

Let p_s(x)=sum_i p_s(x,i) and q_s(i|x)=p_s(x,i)/p_s(x). Fix a class y, finite horizon T>0 and a constant guidance increment eta>=0. In increasing sampling time t, s=T-t, define guided DDIM by dX_t/dt=b_eta(X_t,t), b_eta(x,t)=x+grad_x log p_s(x,y)+eta*grad_x log q_s(y|x). Unguided DDIM is dZ_t/dt=b_0(Z_t,t). body:
[Defi 4 of arXiv:2511.10535, 'Eigenvalues of Brownian Motions on $\mathrm{GL}(N,\mathbb{C})$'] Let $(\A,\tau)$ be a $W^\ast$-probability space, and let $a\in\A$ (just $L^2(\A,\tau)$ suffices).  Then $a^\ast a = |a|^2$ is selfadjoint, and so has a spectral measure $\mu_{|a|^2}$: the unique compactly-supported probability distribution on $\R_+$ whose moments are given by $\int x^k \mu_{|a|^2}(dx) = \tau[(a^\ast a)^k]$ (see \eqref{eq.spectral.meas}).  Denote by $\nu_a$ the push-forward of $\mu_{|a|^2}$ under $x\mapsto\sqrt{x}$; in other words, $\nu_a$ is the spectral measure of $|a|:=\sqrt{a^\ast a}$.

For $z\in\C$, define the {\bf log potential} $U_a\colon\C\to\R\cup\{-\infty\}$ by
\[ U_a(z):= \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^\infty \log(x)\,\nu_{a-z}(dx). \]
It is a subharmonic function, and so its (weak) Laplacian is a positive Radon measure.  In this case it is a probability measure: the {\bf Brown measure of $a$}
\[ \mu_a:= \Delta U_a \quad \text{i.e.} \quad
\int_{\C} \psi\,d\mu_a = \int_{\C} \Delta\psi(z)\, U_a(z)\,dz \qquad \forall\,\psi\in C^\infty(\C). \]
The Brown measure is then also uniquely defined by 
\[ \int_{\C} \log |\lambda-z|\,\mu_a(d\lambda) = U_a(z). \]

body: The Weierstrass convergence theorem (a locally uniform limit of holomorphic functions is holomorphic and derivatives converge locally uniformly) has no real-variable analogue and does not upgrade to uniform convergence on the whole domain. (1) Real failure: f_n(x) = sin(n^2 x)/n converges to 0 uniformly on R, but the derivatives f_n'(x) = n cos(n^2 x) do not converge to the derivative of the limit — at x = 0, f_n'(0) = n → ∞ — so uniform convergence of real functions carries no information about derivatives. More dramatically, by the Weierstrass approximation theorem every continuous nowhere differentiable function on [0,1] is a uniform limit of polynomials, so uniform limits of real-analytic functions need not be differentiable anywhere. The complex proof uses the Cauchy estimates, which need holomorphy on a two-dimensional neighborhood: a bound on |g| on a disk controls all derivatives at the center. (2) Only locally uniform: f_n(z) = z^n/n converges to 0 uniformly on all of D, yet f_n'(z) = z^{n-1} has supremum 1 on D for every n and does not converge uniformly on D. So the derivative statement must be quoted with 'uniformly on compact subsets'; deducing a uniform derivative bound up to the boundary from a uniform bound on the functions is a genuine error, and controlling it requires extra input (a larger domain of holomorphy, or boundary regularity). (3) The hypothesis is convergence on compact subsets of the open set, not convergence on the closed set: a sequence converging uniformly on the closed unit disk still gives derivative convergence only on |z| ≤ r < 1 unless the functions are holomorphic on a larger disk.
title: Pitfall: differentiating a uniform limit is a complex-analytic phenomenon, and only locally uniform

[Definition def:level of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] A map $f\colon X\to Y$ in $\cat{$\bm{G}$-OrthSp}$ is called an \emph{$G$-equivariant level fibration} if for every finite-dimensional inner product space $V$, $f(V)\colon X(V)\to Y(V)$ is a fibration in the $\mathcal G_{G,{\textup{O}}(V)}$-equivariant model structure, i.e.~if $f(V)^H$ is a Serre fibration for every closed subgroup $H\subset G$ and every continuous group homomorphism $H\to O(V)$. Analogously, we define the \emph{$G$-equivariant level weak equivalences} as those $f$ such that $f(V)$ is a $\mathcal G_{G,{\textup{O}}(V)}$-weak equivalence for all finite-dimensional inner product spaces $V$. 

    A map is called a \emph{$G$-equivariant cofibration} if it has the left lifting property against all maps that are simultaneously $G$-equivariant level fibrations and $G$-equivariant level weak equivalences.
title: Definition def:level of arXiv:2608.28504

body:
[Definition def: partition procedure in sle of arXiv:2606.13147, 'Scaling limits of the single-curve interface and outermost loops in the planar random fiel'] Fix a sufficiently small constant $\iota>0$, and set
$M=\iota r^{3\kappa}N.$
For a box $\mathsf{B}$, write
$S_\gamma(\mathsf{B}):=\sum_{x\in\mathsf{B}}{\operatorname{dist}}(x,\gamma)^{-1/4}.$
We define the following recursive partition procedure. We first partition $\Lambda_N$ into boxes of side length $M$. Given a current box $\mathsf{B}$, we proceed as follows.

If
$
S_\gamma(\mathsf{B})<M^{7/4},
$
we leave $\mathsf{B}$ unchanged.
If
$
S_\gamma(\mathsf{B})\ge M^{7/4},
$
we divide $\mathsf{B}$ into two sub-boxes according to the following rule. Suppose, after translation and rotation if necessary, that
$
\mathsf{B}=[1,a]\times[1,b],
1\le a\le b.
$
For \(0\le c\le b\), let
$
\mathsf{C}_1(c)=[1,a]\times[1,c],
\mathsf{C}_2(c)=[1,a]\times[c+1,b],
$
with the convention that empty boxes are omitted. We choose \(c\) so that
$
\big|S_\gamma(\mathsf{C}_1(c))-S_\gamma(\mathsf{C}_2(c))\big|
$
is minimized, and replace \(\mathsf{B}\) by the two boxes \(\mathsf{C}_1(c)\) and \(\mathsf{C}_2(c)\).

We repeat this procedure until every current box \(\mathsf{B}\) satisfies
$
S_\gamma(\mathsf{B})<M^{7/4}.
$
The resulting collection of boxes is denoted by
$
\mathsf{B}_1,\ldots,\mathsf{B}_n.
$
Finally, we set
$
\mathsf{B}_i^+=\mathsf{B}_i\cap\Lambda^+,
\mathsf{B}_i^-=\mathsf{B}_i\cap\Lambda^-.
$
title: Definition def: partition procedure in sle of arXiv:2606.13147

body: Publication record. For a conditioned Galton-Watson tree, or more generally a simply generated tree, T_n with n vertices and l_k(T_n) its number of vertices at distance k from the root, Conjecture 21.1 of S. Janson, Simply generated trees, conditioned Galton-Watson trees, random allocations and condensation (Probab. Surveys 9, 2012) states that E l_k(T_n)^r -> E l_k(T^)^r for every integer r >= 1 and every k >= 1, T^ the local limit, and the same for real r > 0. Y. Shmalo, Moments of level widths in conditioned Galton-Watson trees (October 2026) shows that if the offspring law xi is critical and E xi^(r+1) < infinity for a real r >= 1, then l_k(T_n)^r, n >= 1, is uniformly integrable for every k, so E l_k(T_n)^r -> E Z_k^(r+1) with Z_k the size of generation k of the unconditioned process; with the cases that follow from Fatou's lemma this proves the conjecture for every integer r >= 1, and for every real r > 0 except when 0 < r < 1 and xi is critical with infinite variance and E xi^(r+1) < infinity. Paper: https://github.com/yspennstate/level-width-moments (commit dd48a4b11b9d). Not refereed.
title: Janson Conjecture 21.1 (arXiv 20.1) proved: moments of level widths in conditioned Galton-Watson trees converge to those of the local limit (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/level-width-moments)

body:
[Defn def:D of arXiv:2609.01458, 'Confluence relations for $q$-analogues of multiple zeta values'] For adjacent $u,v\in\hat{\mathcal{F}}$, define
\[
D(u,v)\in\mathbb{Q}\hat{\mathcal{F}}\otimes\Omega
\]
as follows. When
\[
u=\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,k_{d}}(x_{1},\dots,x_{d}),v=\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,k_{d}}(x_{1},\dots,qx_{j},\dots,x_{d}),
\]
we put
\[
D(u,v)\coloneqq\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,k_{j}-1,\dots,k_{d}}(x_{1},\dots,x_{d})\otimes e_{0}
\]
for $k_{j}>1$, and
\begin{align*}
D(u,v) & \coloneqq-\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,\widehat{k_{j}},\dots,k_{d}}(x_{1},\dots,x_{j-1}x_{j},\dots,x_{d})\otimes e_{q^{-m}}\\
 & \qquad+\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,\widehat{k_{j}},\dots,k_{d}}(x_{1},\dots,x_{j}x_{j+1},\dots,x_{d})\otimes(e_{q^{-m}}-e_{0})
\end{align*}
for $k_{j}=1$ and $x_{j}=q^{m}z$, and
\begin{align*}
D(u,v) & \coloneqq\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,\widehat{k_{j}},\dots,k_{d}}(x_{1},\dots,x_{j-1}x_{j},\dots,x_{d})\otimes(e_{q^{-m}}-e_{0})\\
 & \qquad-\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,\widehat{k_{j}},\dots,k_{d}}(x_{1},\dots,x_{j}x_{j+1},\dots,x_{d})\otimes e_{q^{-m}}
\end{align*}
for $k_{j}=1$ and $x_{j}=q^{-m}z^{-1}$. Here, we understand that
\[
\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,\widehat{k_{j}},\dots,k_{d}}(x_{1},\dots,x_{j-1}x_{j},\dots,x_{d})=\mathbb{L}_{k_{2},\dots,k_{d}}(x_{2},\dots,x_{d})
\]
when $j=1$, and
\[
\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,\widehat{k_{j}},\dots,k_{d}}(x_{1},\dots,x_{j}x_{j+1},\dots,x_{d})=0
\]
when $j=d$. When
\[
u=\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,k_{d}}(x_{1},\dots,x_{d}),v=\mathbb{L}_{k_{1},\dots,k_{d}}(x_{1},\dots,q^{-1}x_{j},\dots,x_{d}),
\]
we define $D(u,v)$ by
\[
D(u,v)\coloneqq-D(v,u).
\]
title: Formal single-position $q$-difference

[Definition newCminus of arXiv:2607.19651, 'Metastability and phase transition in a social network model with multiple opinions'] For any opinion $o\in\mathcal{O}$, a consensus set for $o$ is defined in the following way
\begin{equation}
    \mathcal{C}^o = \{u \in \mathcal{S}:u\neq 0, u(a,o)\geq 0 ,u(a,p)\leq 0, \forall a\in\mathcal{A}, \forall p\in\mathcal{O}\setminus\{o\}\}.
\end{equation}
Note that for any $u\in \mathcal{C}^o$, there exists at least one actor $a\in \mathcal{A}$ such that $u(a,o)>0$.
    A consensus set for another opinion than $o\in\mathcal{O}$ is defined as follows:
    \[
    \mathcal{C}^{-o}=\bigcup_{p\in\mathcal{O}\setminus\{o\}}\mathcal{C}^p .
    \]
title: Consensus sets

[Corollary 15 of arXiv:2605.14206, 'The clumsy coupon collector's problem'] As a formal power series, the generating function of
the distribution is
\[
  \sum_{n=0}^\infty \PP\left(T_{m,p} \leq n\right) z^n =
    \left[(1-z)
      \sum_{\ell=0}^m
      \binom{m-m/z}{\ell}
      (-1)^\ell
      \left(\frac{1}{1-p}\right)^\ell
    \right]^{-1}
\]
while the generating function of the tails is
\[
  \sum_{n=0}^\infty \PP\left(T_{m,p} > n\right) z^n = 
  \frac{1}{1-z} - \left[(1-z)
      \sum_{\ell=0}^m
      \binom{m-m/z}{\ell}
      (-1)^\ell
      \left(\frac{1}{1-p}\right)^\ell
    \right]^{-1}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Definition of arXiv:2605.02226, 'Finitely Dependent Processes on Subshifts'] A subshift $X $ is \textbf{strongly irreducible} (SI) if there exists $k \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for any two subsets $F$ and $F'$ in $G$ with $d(F, F') > k$ and any pair of globally allowed patterns $ a \in A^F$ and $ b \in A^{F'}$, we have $[a] \cap [b] \neq \emptyset$, that is, there exists $ x \in X$ such that $ x|_{F} = a$ and $ x|_{F'} =b$. The smallest such $k$ is called the SI distance for $X$.

The simplest forms of Brouwer's theorem are for continuous functions from a closed interval in the real numbers to itself or from a closed disk to itself. A more general form than the latter is for continuous functions from a nonempty convex compact subset of Euclidean space to itself.
title: Brouwer fixed-point theorem

\[
  n^{\star}(d,m)=(m+1)d .
\]
Moreover, for every dataset with feature rank $r$, some
$(m+1)r$ weighted points already recover a full-data optimum exactly, and
there is an explicit integer dataset on $(m+1)d$ points for which every
selection of $(m+1)d-1$ weighted points has ratio exactly
$1+\frac{m+1}{2md(m^2+m-1)}>1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:sec5-mellin of arXiv:2607.18070, 'The Brownian loop-catcher'] Let \(\mathsf P,\mathsf Q\) be laws on one-sided filling hulls such that
\(\mathsf P[\xi\in H]=\mathsf Q[\xi\in H]=0\).  Suppose
\[
 \int\mathbf 1_{\{H\cap C=\varnothing\}}e^{-\lambda m_\mathbb{D}(H,C)}
 \,\mathsf P(\,\mathrm d H)
 =\int\mathbf 1_{\{H\cap C=\varnothing\}}e^{-\lambda m_\mathbb{D}(H,C)}
 \,\mathsf Q(\,\mathrm d H)
\]
for every radial filling hull \(C\) from \(\xi\) to an interior point.
Then, for every \(z\in\mathbb{D}\),
\[
 \mathsf P[z\in\mathbb{D}\setminus H]
 =\mathsf Q[z\in\mathbb{D}\setminus H].
\]
title: Lemma lem:sec5-mellin of arXiv:2607.18070

While external environmental noise (multiplicative state noise) typically drives predator or prey populations to extinction in finite time or asymptotically, internal demographic noise proportional to the square root of event rates preserves strict positivity of population trajectories almost surely for all t >= 0. Internal fluctuations diminish as populations approach boundary states, preventing boundary hitting and ensuring global persistence.
Internal demographic noise model where diffusion vanishes at zero with square-root rate
No multiplicative environmental brownian fluctuations
title: Persistence Under Internal Demographic Noise Versus Environmental Noise

$\mathbb{P}\bigl(\bigcup_{k=1}^{N}A_{k}\bigr)\ge1-\exp(-\Psi)$, where
\[
  \Psi:=\sup_{L\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}}\frac{1}{L+1}
  \sum_{k=1}^{N}\bigl(\mathbb{P}(A_{k})-\varphi(L+1)\bigr)_{+}.
\]
In the finite restricted reading the supremum may be taken over
$0\le L\le N-1$.

belongs to $C_b(\mathbb{R}^{d_y})$.

body: [Definition Extreme points of arXiv:2604.04672, 'Connected components and topological ends of stationary planar forests'] For any subset $X\subset\mathcal D$, denote by $\partial_{\mathcal D}(X)$ its set of extreme points, that is, elements $x\in X$ which are either a maximum or a minimum in $X$ with respect to $<_\mathcal D$. [Definition def:tridiag of arXiv:2412.04579, 'Solvable Families of Random Block Tridiagonal Matrices'] Let $r, n\ge 1$. An $(rn)\times(rn)$ matrix $\mathbf{T}$ is called an ${\mathbb{F}}$-valued $r$-block Jacobi matrix if it is a ${\mathbb{F}}$-Hermitian block tridiagonal matrix built from $r\times r$ blocks satisfying the following conditions. The diagonal blocks $\mathbf{A}_1, \dots, \mathbf{A}_n$ are $r\times r$ ${\mathbb{F}}$-Hermitian matrices. The off-diagonal blocks $\mathbf{B}_1, \dots, \mathbf{B}_{n-1}$ above the diagonal are lower triangular with positive diagonal entries, see (equation eq:T of the paper).
 We denote the set of such matrices by $\mathfrak{M}_{n,\beta, r}$,
 \begin{align}
 \mathbf{T}=
 \left[\begin{array}{ccccc}
 \mathbf{A}_1& \mathbf{B}_1 & 0 &\dots & \\
 \mathbf{B}_1^{\dag} & \mathbf{A}_2 &\mathbf{B}_2 &\dots \\
 0&\ddots & \ddots & \ddots &0 \\
 & 0 & \mathbf{B}_{n-2}^\dag &\mathbf{A}_{n-1} &\mathbf{B}_{n-1} \\
 & & 0 & \mathbf{B}_{n-1}^\dag & \mathbf{A}_n\\
 \end{array} \right].
 \end{align}
title: Definition def:tridiag of arXiv:2412.04579

For stationary ergodic strictly elliptic static nearest-neighbor RWRE, p=P_0(A_l)>0 implies q(omega)=P_0^omega(A_l)>0 almost surely; p<1 implies q<1 almost surely. Thus a mixed p would have 0<q<1 almost surely. Positivity alone does not prove p=1: the zeros of q and 1-q propagate by harmonicity, while their values need not be translation invariant. body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, Heat across an edge of an arc-transitive graph (October 2026), addresses Aldous and Fill, Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, Open Problem 7.30, which asks for a monotonicity property of random walk on arc-transitive graphs stronger than P_i(X_{2t} = j) <= P_i(X_{2t} = i). It proves that on every finite connected 1-walk-regular graph, in particular every finite connected arc-transitive graph and every distance-regular graph, the heat-kernel ratio H_t(x,y)/H_t(x,x) is strictly increasing in t for every edge xy, where H_t = exp(-t(I - A/d)); the derivative is the variance of the Laplacian eigenvalue under the exponentially tilted spectral measure of x. The same holds for the lazy walk in discrete time. On a regular graph that is not 1-walk-regular the ratio across an edge can exceed 1 and decrease (an exact rational certificate on a 4-regular graph of Regev and Shinkar), while its average over the neighbours of x is always increasing. A Lean 4 file checks the finite inequality behind the variance bound. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/arc-transitive-edge-heat (commit 258ba70a8fd2). Not refereed.
title: Heat across an edge of a 1-walk-regular graph: H_t(x,y)/H_t(x,x) is strictly increasing in t, on Aldous-Fill Open Problem 7.30 (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/arc-transitive-edge-heat)

body: Let alpha, beta, gamma, delta be nonnegative functions on the subsets of a finite set such that for all A, B: alpha(A) beta(B) <= gamma(A union B) delta(A intersect B). Then for all families X, Y: alpha(X) beta(Y) <= gamma(X join Y) delta(X meet Y), where f(X) = sum of f over X, X join Y = {A union B}, X meet Y = {A intersect B}. This single inequality implies FKG, Kleitman, and much of correlation theory on distributive lattices.

[Lemma 4 (Partition estimate for exponentially-weighted sums) of arXiv:2512.04646, '\textbf{Canonical Rough Path over Tempered Fractional Brownian Motion: Existence, Construc'] Let $\alpha > 1$, $\beta > 0$, and let
$\mathcal{P} = \{0=t_0 < t_1 < \cdots < t_N=T\}$ be a partition of
$[0,T]$ with mesh $\delta := \max_{0\le i\le N-1}(t_{i+1}-t_i)$.
Write $\Delta_i := t_{i+1}-t_i$. Then
\begin{equation}

\Sigma(\mathcal{P}) :=
\sum_{i,j=0}^{N-1} \Delta_i^{\alpha}\,\Delta_j^{\alpha}\,
e^{-\beta|t_i-t_j|}
\le C(\alpha,\beta,T)\,\delta^{2\alpha-2},
\end{equation}
where
\begin{equation}

C(\alpha,\beta,T)
= T + \frac{2T}{\beta}(1+c_0)
\end{equation}
for some absolute constant $c_0>0$, and $C(\alpha,\beta,T)$ is
bounded uniformly in $\delta\in(0,1]$.
title: Partition estimate for exponentially-weighted sums

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2605.25715, '2605.25715'] Let $\mathbf{G} \in L^p_{loc}(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathbb{R}^d)$ for some $p\in(d,\infty)$, $A=(a_{ij})_{1\le i,j\le d}$ be a symmetric and positive definite matrix of real numbers,  and let $(P_t)_{t>0}$ be the regularized semigroup associated with the $L^1$-closed extension of $(L^{A,\mathbf{G}}, C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d))$, defined by
$$
L^{A,\mathbf{G}}f = \frac12 \mathrm{trace}(A\nabla^2 f) + \langle \mathbf{G}, \nabla f \rangle, \quad f \in C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d)
$$
(see \cite{LST22}). Let $T$ be a $d \times d$ strictly positive definite symmetric matrix. If there exist constants $N_0\in \N$ and $M>0$ such that
$$
\langle \mathbf{G}(x), Tx \rangle \leq M \|x\|^2, \quad \text{for a.e. } x \in \mathbb{R}^d \setminus \overline{B}_{N_0},
$$
then $(P_t)_{t>0}$ is conservative.

Let n>=2 be finite and V be a real symmetric 3 by 3 matrix with eigenvalues lambda1>lambda2>0>lambda3. Consider self-inclusive normalized attention dot x_i=(I-x_i*x_i^T) sum_j exp(beta*x_i^T*V*x_j)*V*x_j / sum_j exp(beta*x_i^T*V*x_j) on (S^2)^n, so Q^T K=V. Fix a unit top eigenvector e1. There exists B(V,n)>0 such that for every beta>B(V,n), all 2^n configurations x_i=s_i*e1, s_i in {+1,-1}, are locally asymptotically stable and have open positive-volume basins. For a nonconstant sign pattern with r=n_plus/n_minus, a sufficient criterion from Remark 5.3 is lambda1>|log r|/(2 beta) and lambda_k<lambda1*((c-r)*(c*r-1))/(r*(c^2-1)) for k=2,3, where c=exp(2 beta lambda1). This is a known local stability result; it neither classifies all attracting equilibria nor proves an almost-everywhere limit theorem.

Let f be a nonconstant entire function and M(r) = max_{|z| = r} |f(z)|. The order of f is ρ = limsup_{r→∞} (log log M(r))/(log r) in [0, ∞]; equivalently ρ = inf{λ ≥ 0 : M(r) ≤ exp(r^λ) for all sufficiently large r}, with the infimum of the empty set taken to be ∞. Constant functions are assigned order 0. If 0 < ρ < ∞ one further distinguishes the type σ = limsup_{r→∞} log M(r)/r^ρ. Examples: every nonconstant polynomial has order 0; exp(z), sin z, cos z and 1/Γ have order 1; exp(z^n) has order n; cos(sqrt z) has order 1/2; exp(exp(z)) has infinite order. If f has finite order ρ and nonzero zeros (a_n) listed with multiplicity, then Σ_n |a_n|^{-s} < ∞ for every s > ρ; the exponent of convergence of the zeros, λ = inf{s > 0 : Σ_n |a_n|^{-s} < ∞}, satisfies λ ≤ ρ, and the inequality can be strict (exp(z) has order 1 and no zeros at all).
f is entire
M(r) denotes the maximum modulus on the circle of radius r

      \mathbb{P} \left( d_{G_p}(x,y) \ge K t , x \xleftrightarrow{G_p} y \right) \le \exp(- c t).

[Lemma 5 (Mixed edge) of arXiv:2607.23887, '2607.23887'] Let $S\subset\N^2$ be finite and $\Delta=\mathrm{conv}(S)\subset\mathbb
R_{\ge0}^2$. Suppose the weight $w(a,b)=a-b$ takes both a positive and a
negative value on $S$. Then there is an integral linear form
$\ell(a,b)=ca+db$ with $c+d>0$ such that, writing
$\lambda=\min_{\alpha\in S}\ell(\alpha)$ and $F=\{\alpha\in S:\ell(\alpha)=\lambda\}$,
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $\lambda/(c+d)\ge0$, and
\item[(ii)] $w$ does not have one strict sign on $F$: either $w$ vanishes
somewhere on $F$, or $w$ takes both signs on $F$.
\end{enumerate}

[Proposition prop:secondorder of arXiv:2412.01995, 'Exciting games and Monge-Amp\`{e}re equations'] Fix $x^0 \in \partial \Delta$ with $x^0_1=\dotso=x^0_k=0$,  $x^0_{k+1},\dotso,x^0_d > 0$, and $\sum_{j=k+1}^d x_j^0<1$. Taking $r= (1-\sum_{i=k+1}^d x^0_i)/{(2d)}$,  there exist two positive constants $c_1(x^0)$, $c_2(x^0)$ such that for any $x_1,\dotso, x_k \in (0,r)$,
    \begin{align*}
    c_1(x^0) Diag(1/x^2_1,\dotso,1/x^2_k, 1,\dotso, 1) 
  &\leq \nabla^2 g(x_1,\dotso, x_k, x^0_{k+1},\dotso,x^0_d) \\
  &\leq  c_2(x^0)Diag(1/x^2_1,\dotso,1/x^2_k, 1,\dotso ,1),
  \end{align*}
    where $Diag(1/x^2_1,\dotso,1/x^2_k, 1,\dotso, 1)$ denotes a diagonal matrix with the $(i,i)$-th entry being $1/x^2_i$ for $1\leq i \leq k$ and $1$ for $k+1 \leq i \leq d$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition D_TWGroot of arXiv:2510.26724, 'Sharp Fuss-Catalan thresholds in graph bootstrap percolation'] A graph $T$ is called a 
{\em tree witness graph (TWG)} for  the 
edge $e$ if either 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $T=e$; or else 
\item for some copy 
$H^{(e)}$ of $K_r$ 
with $e\in E(H^{(e)})$ there are TWGs 
$T_f$ for each edge $f\in E(H^{(e)}\setminus e)$
such that $T_f$ and $T_{f'}$ are vertex disjoint
outside of $H^{(e)}$ 
for all $f\neq f'\in E(H^{(e)}\setminus e)$, 
and $T=\bigcup_{f\in E(H^{(e)}\setminus e)}T_f$.
\end{enumerate}
In case (2) we call $H^{(e)}$ the {\it root} of $T$
and the $T_f$ its {\it primal branches}.

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.23960, 'Learning from Uncertainty-dependent Missing Labels for Semi-supervised Classification'] Let \(\theta_0\) denote the true parameter of the augmented complete-data model
\(p_{\theta_0}(Y,Z,M)\), where \(M\) is the mechanism-generated missingness
indicator. Let
\[
  S_{\rm aug}(Y,Z,M;\theta_0)
  =
  \nabla_\theta \log p_\theta(Y,Z,M)\big|_{\theta=\theta_0}
\]
be the corresponding augmented complete-data score, and define
\[
  \mathcal I_{\rm aug}(\theta_0)
  =
  \operatorname{Var}\{S_{\rm aug}(Y,Z,M;\theta_0)\}.
\]
Let \(\mathcal G\) be any observed sigma-field obtained by coarsening the
augmented data, for example
\[
  \mathcal G=\sigma(Y,M,Z^{\rm obs},R),
\]
where \(R\) denotes any design randomization. Define the design information
\[
  \mathcal I_{\rm des}(\theta_0)
  =
  \operatorname{Var}\!\left[
    E\{S_{\rm aug}(Y,Z,M;\theta_0)\mid \mathcal G\}
  \right].
\]
Then
\[
  \mathcal I_{\rm des}(\theta_0)
  \preceq
  \mathcal I_{\rm aug}(\theta_0).
\]
Consequently, no regular estimator based on the coarsened observed experiment
can have asymptotic variance below the information bound for the augmented full
experiment, whenever the relevant information matrices are nonsingular. Equality
can occur only when the augmented complete-data score is
\(\mathcal G\)-measurable almost surely. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.23960

body:
[Proposition prop:fr-rotation of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] For the symmetric urn started at $\pi_0=\delta_n$, for every $t\ge0$ and
every $k$,

\begin{equation}
\sqrt{\pi_t(k)}=\langle k\rvert\,e^{-i\theta(t)J_y}\,\lvert n\rangle,\qquad
\theta(t)=\arccos\bigl(e^{-2t}\bigr),

\end{equation}

and the right side is real and nonnegative. Consequently
$\sigma^{\mathrm{FR}}_t=e^{-i\theta(t)J_y}\,\ketbra{n}{n}\,e^{i\theta(t)J_y}$, so the
Fisher--Rao lift of the relaxing law is itself a rigid rotation of a spin
coherent state, about the $y$ axis, run on exactly the Ehrenfest quantum
clock.

C_\mu

\lVert \bar{\mu}-\bar{\nu}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}
+
C_\mu H(\nu\mid\mu).

\]

The link patterns with $n$ boundary points and $m$ links are called $(n,m)$-links, denoted by ${\rm LP}(n,m)$.

Let A be a self-adjoint operator on a separable complex Hilbert space H. Multiplication form: there exist a finite measure space (M, μ), a unitary U: H → L²(M, μ) and a real-valued μ-measurable function f on M, finite μ-a.e., such that x ∈ D(A) iff f·(Ux) ∈ L²(M, μ), and U A U^{-1} g = f g for all g ∈ U D(A). Projection-valued measure form: there is a unique projection-valued measure E on the Borel sets of ℝ with A = ∫_ℝ λ dE(λ), meaning D(A) = {x ∈ H : ∫ λ² d⟨E(λ)x, x⟩ < ∞} and ⟨Ax, y⟩ = ∫ λ d⟨E(λ)x, y⟩ for x ∈ D(A), y ∈ H; E is supported on σ(A) ⊂ ℝ. Borel functional calculus: for Borel φ: ℝ → ℂ, φ(A) = ∫ φ(λ) dE(λ) is defined on D(φ(A)) = {x : ∫ |φ|² d⟨E x, x⟩ < ∞}; the map φ ↦ φ(A) is a *-homomorphism, φ(A) is bounded with ‖φ(A)‖ = sup of |φ| on σ(A) when φ is bounded and continuous, φ(A) is self-adjoint iff φ is real-valued a.e., and φ(A) is unitary if |φ| = 1. In particular e^{itA} (t ∈ ℝ) is unitary and, when A ≥ 0, e^{-tA} (t ≥ 0) is a self-adjoint contraction.

[Conjecture of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'] For $\phi\in\bR$, let $\cC_\phi$ be the full subcategory of the localized
category
\[
Nov\otimes_{Nov_+}\mathsf C_B
\]
consisting of objects $E$ with the following property: for every
$\varepsilon>0$, $E$ admits a constructible metrized model
$\widetilde E\in\mathsf C_B$ such that
\[
\phi-\varepsilon<
\phi_-(\Lambda_{\widetilde E})
\leq
\phi_+(\Lambda_{\widetilde E})
<
\phi+\varepsilon .
\]
Here the phases are normalized using the graded microlocal coefficient
system $\cV_{\widetilde E}$ on
$\Lambda_{\widetilde E}^{\mathrm{sm}}$.

The collection of subcategories $\{\cC_\phi\}_{\phi\in\bR}$ is the slicing
of a Bridgeland stability condition with central charge $Z_\Omega$.
Equivalently, together with $Z_\Omega$ it uniquely determines this
stability condition. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Unnumbered conjecture of arXiv:2609.00978, 'Towards Categorical K\"ahler Geometry'

body:
[Proposition 7 of arXiv:2608.26038, 'Rotated semicircle laws for permanental roots of Gaussian random matrices'] For every \(x\in\R\),
\begin{align}
  H_N\sim\Pp_{2,N}:\qquad
  &\E[P_N(\ii x)P_N(-\ii x)]
  =
  \int_{\R^2}
  \prod_{\ell=1}^2(x-\ii y_\ell)^N
  \,\dd\Gamma_{2,N}(y_1,y_2),
  \\
  H_N\sim\Pp_{1,N}:\qquad
  &\E[P_N(\ii x)P_N(-\ii x)]
  =
  \int_{\R^2}
  \prod_{\ell=1}^2(x-\ii y_\ell)^N
  \,\dd\Gamma_{4,N}(y_1,y_2).
  
\end{align}
The integrals are absolutely convergent.

[Lemma lem:parity of arXiv:2608.01253, 'The pseudo-quantum representation of \\finite reversible Markov chains'] Run the uniformised chain of (sec:setup of the paper), a Poisson$(\Lambda)$ clock with
$P$-moves at the ticks, and start the doubled chain at $(i,+)$. At time $t$ the
doubled chain is at $(j,+)$ if the original chain is at $j$ after an even number of
ticks, and at $(j,-)$ if after an odd number. Consequently, for the embedding
$\widehat\pi_0=\binom{\pi_0}{0}$,

\begin{equation}
\widehat T_t\binom{\pi_0}{0}
=\binom{\,e^{-s}\cosh(sP^{T})\,\pi_0\,}{\,e^{-s}\sinh(sP^{T})\,\pi_0\,},
\qquad s=\Lambda t,

\end{equation}

so the two sheets carry the even and odd halves of the Poisson representation
(equation eq:poisson-rep of the paper), and their sum returns $T_t\pi_0$.

[Theorem 4 of arXiv:2605.25715, '2605.25715'] Let $\widetilde{\mathbf{G}}\in L^p_{loc}(\mathbb{R}^d, \mathbb{R}^d)$ for some $p\in(d,\infty)$. Suppose that $(L^{\widetilde{\mathbf{G}}}, C_0^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^d))$ admits a unique infinitesimally invariant measure $\mu$. (Here unique is meant up to a multiplicative constant.) Write $\mu=\exp(2 \Phi)\,dx$, with $\Phi \in H^{1,p}_{loc}(\R^d)$ (cf. Remark \ref{definvaranrem}), and set $\mathbf{B}:=\widetilde{\mathbf{G}}-\nabla \Phi$. Then it holds:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] $\widetilde{\mathbf{G}}=\nabla \Phi+\mathbf{B}$ is the unique WHHD for $\widetilde{\mathbf{G}}$.
  \item[(ii)] If there exists an OHHD for $\widetilde{\mathbf{G}}$, then it is unique and 
 \[
 \widetilde{\mathbf{G}}=\nabla \Phi+\mathbf{B}
 \]
is the unique OHHD for $\widetilde{\mathbf{G}}$.
\item[(iii)] An OHHD for $\widetilde{\mathbf{G}}$ exists, if and only if $\mathrm{div}_{dx}(\mathbf{B})=0$ or $\langle \nabla \Phi, \mathbf{B} \rangle = 0$.\\
(In particular, if $\langle \nabla \Phi, \mathbf{B} \rangle \not =0$ on $V$ for some measurable set $V$ with $dx(V)>0$ or if $\mathrm{div}_{dx }(\mathbf{B})\not =0$, then there is no OHHD for $\widetilde{\mathbf{G}}$.)
\end{itemize}

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact integral manipulation, Palm calculus, mass transport, limiting obstruction or conditional construction Result: For a finite weighted edge set, choosing an edge proportionally to its weight and then a uniform endpoint samples vertices with probability proportional to weighted degree. Thus a uniform-vertex limit need not equal the endpoint limit when degrees or weights vary. Even knowledge of both endpoint marginals does not identify their joint boundary law: an equal mixture of pairs (0,0),(1,1) and an equal mixture of (0,1),(1,0) have the same marginals but disjoint supports. Product-edge convergence must retain the endpoint-pair measure and horizontal/vertical edge weights. Check: Each incident edge contributes half its sampling weight to a vertex, proving the degree bias. The two binary pair laws both have Bernoulli(1/2) marginals, checking the independent loss of correlation information. Obstruction: No convergence estimate for the actual product-graph endpoint measure is proved. The pair-law example is an information diagnostic, not a constructed graph counterexample.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0421-convergence-of-edge-measured-product-graph-voronoi-diagrams
No independent review

[Lemma lem:uniform-approximate-Goh of arXiv:2609.02710, 'Asymptotic Mean Value Laplacian\\ on equiregular sub-Riemannian manifolds'] Let $X^\lambda=(X_1^\lambda,\ldots,X_k^\lambda)$ be a jointly smooth
family of vector fields on $\mathbb R^n$, all supported in one fixed compact set,
with $\lambda\in\Theta$.  Let $\mathcal A\subset\Theta\times
L^2([0,1];\mathbb R^k)$ be compact for the strong $L^2$ topology, and assume
that every $(\lambda,u)\in\mathcal A$ is energy minimizing between its
endpoints and that
\[
 \sup\{\|u\|_{L^\infty}:(\lambda,u)\in\mathcal A\}<\infty.
\]
Write $E_\lambda$ for the endpoint map from $0$, set
\[
 J(u):=\frac12\|u\|_{L^2}^2,\qquad F_\lambda:=(E_\lambda,J),
\]
and let $\operatorname{ind}_{-}(Q)$ denote the maximal dimension of a
subspace on which a quadratic form $Q$ is negative definite.  For every
$\kappa>0$ and integer $N\ge1$, there is $\Lambda>0$ with the following
property.  If $(\lambda,u)\in\mathcal A$ and
$(\bar p,\bar p_0)\in(\mathbb R^n)^*\times\mathbb R$ is nonzero and satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \bar pD_uE_\lambda=\bar p_0D_uJ,\qquad
 |\bar p|\ge\Lambda|\bar p_0|,
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{ind}_{-}\!\left(
  \left.(\bar p,-\bar p_0)\cdot D_u^2F_\lambda
  \right|_{\ker D_uF_\lambda}\right)<N,
\end{equation}
then the adjoint covector $p(t)$ with terminal value $p(1)=\bar p$

[Lemma lem:disconnect_interior of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] {amy-cle-resampling}}]

Suppose that $\Gamma$ is a nested ${\rm CLE}_{\kappa}${} in a simply connected domain $D$, and let $\Upsilon_\Gamma$ be its gasket. For each $a\in(0,1)$, $b>0$ there exists $p > 0$ such that the following holds. 

Let $z\in D$ and $j_0\in\mathbf{Z}$ be such that $B(z,2^{-j_0})\subseteq D$. There exists a resampling $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ of $\Gamma$ within $A(z,2^{-j},2^{-j+1})$ for each $j>j_0$ with the following property. Let $G^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ be the event that $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ has a loop $\widetilde\mathcal {L}$ that
\begin{itemize}
 \item disconnects every point in $\Upsilon_{\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}} \cap B(z,2^{-j})$ from $\partial B(z,2^{-j+1})$,
 \item the gasket and the collection of loops of $\Gamma$ and $\Gamma^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j}$ remain the same in each connected component of $\mathbf{C} \setminus \widetilde\mathcal {L}$ that intersects $B(z,2^{-j})$.
\end{itemize}
For $k\in\mathbf{N}$, let $\widetilde G_{z,j_0,k}$ be the event that the number of $j=j_0+1,\ldots,j_0+k$ so that
\[ \mathbf{P}[ G^{\mathrm{res}}_{z,j} \,|\, \Gamma ] \geq p\]
is at least $(1-a)k$.  Then
\[ \mathbf{P}[(\widetilde G_{z,j_0,k})^c] = O(e^{-b k}) \]
where the implicit constant does not depend on $z,j_0,k$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:spec-ind of arXiv:2411.09075, 'Weak Poincar{\'e} Inequalities, Simulated Annealing, and Sampling from Spherical Spin Glas'] The following \emph{local-to-global principle} reduces proving a \Poincare inequality to establishing bounds on the spectrum of \emph{influence matrices}.
    Suppose for {\bf every} $S\subseteq [N]$, and {\bf every} pinning $x_S$ of coordinates in $S$, the spectral norm of its \emph{influence matrix} $\Psi_{S,x_S}$ is at most $\alpha$, then the Glauber dynamics chain satisfies a $n^{-O(\alpha)}$-\Poincare inequality.
    Here, the influence matrix $\Psi_{S,x_S}$ is an $(n-|S|)\times(n-|S|)$ matrix indexed by vertices $v\notin S$, where
    \[
        \Psi_{S,x_S}[a,b] \coloneqq \Pr[x_a = +1 | x_b = +1] - \Pr[x_a = -1 | x_b = +1]\mper
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Given measurable spaces (X, F) and (Y, G), a function f : X -> Y is measurable if the preimage of every set in G lies in F. For real-valued f it suffices that {x : f(x) > a} in F for every real a (the sets (a, infinity) generate the Borel sigma-algebra). Measurability is preserved under sums, products, sups/infs of countable families, and pointwise limits - which is why it is the right regularity class for integration.

# Unrestricted random-mean DDPM learning for equilateral three-Gaussian teachers

This is a restricted-case candidate theorem, dependent on unaudited C06--C10. It removes the zero-centroid optimization constraint from C08/C09. It does not claim the general well-separated K=3 target, established novelty, or finite-precision complexity.

## 1. Statement

Let d>=2, R>=1 be known, E have two orthonormal columns, and u_1,u_2,u_3 be the unit equilateral vertices in R^2. The original law is the equal-weight mixture of N(R E u_j,I_d). The plane E is unknown to the algorithm. Choose the small noisy radius a according to C10: for a sufficiently small fixed absolute rho,

    sigma_0=1/(80 sqrt(d)),
    S=10 log(100/(sigma_0 rho)),
    a^2<=c rho exp(-76(S+1)).                         (1)

For a polynomial upper runtime bound, choose equality in (1) with sufficiently small absolute c, rather than allowing arbitrarily smaller a. Put tau=a/R and sigma=sqrt(1-tau^2)>=1/2. For independent original samples X_i and Gaussian noises Y_i, set W_i=tau X_i+sigma Y_i. Optimize the ordinary empirical DDPM loss

    Lhat(M)=n^(-1)sum_i ||s_M(W_i)+Y_i/sigma||^2,
    s_M(x)=-x+sum_j softmax_j(m_j.x-||m_j||^2/2)m_j.

All d-by-3 means are free parameters. Initialize their entries iid N(0,3a^2/(2d)), independently of data/noise. Use physical Euclidean GD with step one.

For 0<epsilon<1, 0<eta<=1/100, sufficiently many polynomially many samples yield

    min_pi ||M_T-a E U_pi||_F<=a epsilon             (2)

with probability at least 553/1600-eta>1/3, at

    T=O(a^(-2)log d+a^(-4)log(C/epsilon)).            (3)

The population version succeeds with probability at least 553/1600. These are real-arithmetic statements, counting exponentials as score evaluations. Sampling and arithmetic costs are polynomial in d,1/epsilon,1/eta, with an enormous fixed dimension exponent from (1). To estimate the original law, rescale means by R/a, and choose epsilon=2 epsilon_TV/R (or smaller than one); matching implies TV error at most R epsilon/2 by Gaussian KL, Pinsker and mixture convexity. Consequently costs are also polynomial in R and the inverse prescribed original-law error. Unknown radius and finite-precision implementation remain outside the statement.

## 2. Population trajectory

Use C10's exact decomposition M=a b 1^T+a c Z V^T, c=sqrt(3/2), V=sqrt(2/3)U^T. C10 proves entry, except on a set of initialization probability at most 1-79/200. Conditional on that good event, the covariance surrogate's entry angle is uniform in either determinant branch. Removing the three unstable sectors of total angular measure 1/8 leaves probability 553/1600.

At entry, the actual mean configuration is in the full tube around the equilateral subspace, projected radius in [0.9,1.1], angular margin from each unstable boundary bounded below by a fixed delta, and normal error at most C rho. Reduce the fixed rho and the constant c in (1) as needed to preserve the margins of C08. C10's full normal contraction and quadratic tangent forcing give, in normalized Euclidean mean coordinates J=M/a,

    ||w_k||<=C rho exp(-c_1 a^2 k),
    tangent error per step <=C a^2 ||w_k||^2.         (4)

Its accumulated size is at most C rho^2. The same sector-barrier and radial-inward arguments in C08 therefore apply. The restricted dynamics in the equilateral subspace are unchanged by allowing additional coordinates: invariance makes them exactly the C02/C03 radius-angle dynamics, up to fixed coordinate normalization constants. In particular normal and radial rates are order a^2, angular rate order a^4, and the angular maximum stays outside the chosen sector. Thus

    |r_k-1|+alpha_k+||w_k||<=C exp(-c_2 a^4 k).       (5)

Here alpha is distance to the nearest matching angular minimum; the radial estimate tracks that minimum exactly, as established in C08, rather than claiming an O(a^2) radius floor. Equation (5) yields (2),(3) for the population loss. The fastest centroid direction causes no loss: its order-one contraction was included in C10's normal Hessian argument, and its divergent rescaled linear field has zero tangent projection.

## 3. Uniform empirical approximation with a free centroid

The finite-sample argument needs no symmetry of the empirical objective. Work on ||b||<=11, ||Z||_F<=5 and define the two rescaled fields

    h_b=-a^(-4) partial_b F_a,
    h_Z=-a^(-4) grad_Z F_a,

and their empirical analogues. For any 0<zeta<1, with probability at least 1-eta,

    sup ||(hhat_b-h_b,hhat_Z-h_Z)||<=zeta            (6)

when n is a sufficiently large polynomial in d,1/a,1/zeta,1/eta. Although h_b itself contains -2a^(-2)b, this is polynomially bounded on the parameter box; no uniform-in-a boundedness of the population field is asserted.

Here is a direct extension of C09's concentration proof. Let

    B=C_0(d+1/a+1/zeta+1/eta+1)^2,
    n=ceil(B^100),                                  (7)

with sufficiently large absolute C_0. Both ||W|| and ||Y|| exceed B only with probability at most C exp(-c B^2), uniformly in the teacher plane. This follows by their Gaussian norm moment generating functions and the bounded mean shifts ||a E u_j||=a. The mean parameter norm is at most C a on the fixed b,Z box. Softmax derivatives of fixed order are bounded combinations of probabilities; logit derivatives are polynomials in W and bounded means. Differentiating the per-pair loss once or twice in the normalized b,Z coordinates therefore gives a polynomial envelope. More explicitly, a first score derivative is bounded by C a(1+||W||), its second derivative by C a^2(1+||W||)^2, and the score norm by ||W||+C a. Hence rescaled loss gradient is bounded by C a^(-3)(1+||W||)(1+||W||+||Y||), and its derivative by a fixed polynomial bounded by C B^12 on ||W||,||Y||<=B. Fixed-coordinate factors c, sqrt(3) and the three means change only C. The same bounds hold for a slightly enlarged fixed parameter box, allowing Lipschitz extension along segments.

Truncate the per-pair fields to zero outside this safe event for the proof only. Their expectation differs from the untruncated population field by at most polynomial(d,1/a) exp(-c B^2), using the polynomial envelope, Gaussian moments and Cauchy--Schwarz. This is smaller than zeta/10 for sufficiently large C_0. All n actual sample pairs are safe with probability at least 1-eta/4; the algorithm uses the original untruncated objective.

Parameter nets now have dimension 3d instead of 2d. A mesh zeta/(100 C B^12) in the fixed parameter box and a 1/2 direction net have combined log cardinality at most C d log B. The elementary bounded-scalar MGF inequality proved in C09 gives per-net tail at most 2 exp[-c n zeta^2/B^24]. Since zeta>=1/B and n>=B^100, this exponent is at least c B^74 and dominates both net entropy and log(1/eta). The direction net converts scalar bounds to Euclidean field bounds, and the parameter Lipschitz bound extends to all points. Allocating failures and adding expectation bias proves (6). This event is simultaneous over parameters and therefore covers all iterates without a data/iterate independence assumption. Choosing B^100 instead of B^80 only loosens the polynomial sample bound.

## 4. Entry with persistent empirical perturbations

Take zeta=c_* a^2 epsilon with sufficiently small absolute c_*. The exact coordinate metric gives

    b_+=b-(partial_b F_a)/(3a^2)+(a^2/3)e_b,
    Z_+=Z-(2 grad_Z F_a)/(3a^2)+(2a^2/3)e_Z,
    ||(e_b,e_Z)||<=zeta.                            (8)

In particular

    ||b_k||<=2^(-k)||b_0||+C(a^4+a^2 zeta).

Since zeta<=a^2, its floor remains O(a^4). The transient centroid impulse into Z is still O(a^2||b_0||^2). The additional direct shape error contributes C zeta exp(76(S+1)) to the entry comparison. Thus, reducing c in (1), the total comparison error C(a^2+zeta)exp(76(S+1)) stays below the entry tolerance. The full parameter box is retained by the same stopped induction as C10. The good initialization-and-surrogate-angle event remains of probability 553/1600; actual empirical rotational invariance is neither assumed nor needed.

## 5. Full tube with persistent empirical perturbations

In normalized Euclidean J coordinates, (8) adds an error of size at most C a^2 zeta per physical step. C10's integrated physical normal Hessian therefore implies

    ||w_{k+1}||<=(1-c a^2)||w_k||+C a^2 zeta,
    ||w_k||<=C rho exp(-c a^2 k)+C zeta.             (9)

The population tangent forcing remains quadratic. Together with the direct empirical error, it has a decaying contribution C a^2 rho^2 exp(-c a^2 k) and a persistent contribution C a^2 zeta. The first has summable total C rho^2. The second must not be summed over all time: near the sector boundary, the restricted angular drift is inward by c a^4 delta, whereas the persistent perturbation is at most C a^2 zeta. Our choice zeta=c_* a^2 epsilon makes the former dominate. Exactly the moving barrier in C09, decreased only by partial sums of the transient errors, keeps a fixed angular margin. The radial annulus has an order-a^2 inward margin, also dominating these perturbations. This closes the normal/radial/angular tube induction together.

Inside the retained sector, the resulting recurrences are

    alpha_{k+1}<=(1-c a^4)alpha_k
                 +C a^2 rho^2 exp(-c' a^2 k)+C a^2 zeta,
    |r_{k+1}-1|<=(1-c a^2)|r_k-1|
                 +C a^4 alpha_k^2+C a^2||w_k||^2+C a^2 zeta.

Geometric convolution gives

    alpha_k+|r_k-1|+||w_k||
       <=C exp(-c'' a^4 k)+C' zeta/a^2.             (10)

The normal floor is O(zeta), the radial floor O(zeta+zeta^2/a^2), and the angular floor O(zeta/a^2); thus (10) uses the largest. Choose c_* to make the final term a sufficiently small multiple of epsilon, and take the time in (3). The Euclidean coordinate metric yields (2).

## 6. Probability and limitations

The initialization-and-angle event has probability at least 553/1600. Uniform empirical control fails with probability at most eta. A union bound, without multiplying dependent probabilities, yields success at least 553/1600-eta. At eta=1/100 this is 537/1600>1/3. Population control sets empirical error to zero and uses the larger probability. A repeated-run selection guarantee is not claimed.

The teacher is still centered, equilateral, equally weighted and spherical, with known radius and covariance. There is no imposed centering on learned parameters or initialization and no known plane or orbit augmentation. General triangles, unknown radius/covariance, unequal weights, finite precision and the full T309 target remain open. C06's anisotropic population local minimum prevents treating equilateral geometry as innocuous. The result is an unaudited candidate restricted theorem, not a finding of novelty.

Least trusted steps: C10's free-centroid analytic estimates, the uniform gradient/Lipschitz envelope over all free means, and the persistent-error tube barrier. Exact symbolic probability and metric checks support only their finite algebra. body: In abstract algebra, a composition series provides a way to break up an algebraic structure, such as a group or a module, into simple pieces. The need for considering composition series in the context of modules arises from the fact that many naturally occurring modules are not semisimple, hence cannot be decomposed into a direct sum of simple modules. A composition series of a module M is a finite increasing filtration of M by submodules such that the successive quotients are simple and serves as a replacement of the direct sum decomposition of M into its simple constituents.
