[Thm smasympexGOEGSE of arXiv:2412.00593, 'A new approach to strong convergence II.\\The classical ensembles'] There exist universal constants $C,c>0$, and a compactly supported 
distribution $\nu_k$ for every $k\in\mathbb{Z}_+$, such that the following 
hold. Fix any bounded $h\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R})$, and define
$$
	f(\theta):= h(K\cos\theta)
	\qquad\text{with}\qquad
	K := (Cr)^{q_0}\|X_{\rm F}\|.
$$
Then for every $m, N\in \mathbb{N}$ with $m\le\frac{N}{2}$, we have
\begin{multline*}
       \left| \mathbf{E}[\mathop{\textnormal{tr}} h(X^N)]
	- \sum_{k=0}^{m-1} \frac{\nu_k(h)}{N^k} \right| 
	~\vee~
       \left| \mathbf{E}[\mathop{\textnormal{tr}} h(Y^N)]
	- \sum_{k=0}^{m-1} \frac{\nu_k(h)}{(-2N)^k} \right| 
\\
       \le
	\frac{(Cq_0)^{2m}}{m! N^m} \|f^{(2m+1)}\|_{[0, 2\pi]} 
	+
	Cre^{-cN}\big(\sobnorm{h}{0}{(-\infty,\infty)}
		+ \sobnorm{f^{(1)}}{0}{[0, 2\pi]} \big).
\end{multline*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Smooth asymptotic expansion for GOE/GSE

[Theorem thm:loclim of arXiv:2512.17747, 'On exponentially height-penalized random trees'] Let $\mu=\mu_n$ be a sequence admitting a limit $\alpha \in [0,\infty)$.
Let $\mathbf{T}_n$ be a $\mu$-height-biased tree of size $n$. If $\alpha>0$, then the random rooted tree $(\mathbf{T}_{n},\varnothing)$ converges locally to the infinite \emph{Poisson tree} of parameter $\alpha$ as defined in [abraham2020very]. Otherwise, if $\alpha=0$, equivalently $\mu=o(1)$, then the random rooted tree $(\mathbf{T}_{n},\varnothing)$ converges locally to Kesten's tree as defined in [kesten1986subdiffusive]. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Local limit in the local regime

[Thm 20 (Theorem~\ref{thm:micro}-(\ref{thm:sl})) of arXiv:2607.28865, 'First-Passage Percolation on Spread-out line graphs: Microscopic Regime'] Suppose Assumption~\textup{A.\ref{ass:A2}} holds and $0<\ga:=\gc\lc<2$.
Let $m_n:=\left\lfloor n/\mu_{\sfP} \right\rfloor$ and define
\begin{align}
    a_n :=\inf\left\{x>0:m_n\pr(\sfT_1>x)\le1\right\},
    \quad\text{and}\quad
    b_n :=m_n\,\E\left[\sfT_1\ind_{\{\sfT_1\le a_n\}}\right],
\end{align}
where $\sfT$ is the renewal-block passage time defined in~\eqref{eq:block-variable-notation}.
Then
\begin{align*}
    \frac1{a_n}\cdot (T_n-b_n)
    \Longrightarrow
    Z_\ga,
\end{align*}
where $Z_\ga$ is the totally right-skewed $\ga$-stable random variable characterized by
\begin{align}
    \E\left[e^{itZ_\ga}\right]
    =
    \exp\left(
        \int_0^\infty
        \left(
            e^{itx} - 1 - itx\ind_{\{x\le1\}}
        \right)
        \ga x^{-\ga-1}\,dx
    \right),
    \quad
    t\in\dR.
\end{align}
title: Theorem~\ref{thm:micro}-(\ref{thm:sl})

[Definition Doubling metric spaces of arXiv:2609.03129, 'A Closed-Form Formula for Consistent Lipschitz Regression on Metric Spaces with Sparse Neu'] A metric space $(X,\rho)$ is called doubling if there exists
$\lambda_X\in\mathbb N_+$ such that every ball $B(x,r)\subseteq X$ can be covered by at most $\lambda_X$ balls of radius $r/2$.  The smallest such $\lambda_X$ is called the doubling constant of $(X,\rho)$, and the doubling dimension is
$
    \operatorname{ddim}(X,\rho)
\ensuremath{\stackrel{\mbox{\upshape\tiny def.}}{=}}
    \log_2(\lambda_X)
$.
title: Doubling metric spaces

Define the heat kernel Phi: R^n x (0,infinity) -> R by Phi(x,t) = (4 pi t)^{-n/2} exp(-|x|^2/(4t)). Then Phi is smooth and satisfies partial Phi/partial t = Delta_x Phi for all x in R^n, t>0. For every bounded uniformly continuous g: R^n -> R, u(x,t) = integral_{R^n} Phi(x-y,t) g(y) dy is smooth on R^n x (0,infinity), solves partial u/partial t = Delta u there, and u(x,t) -> g(x) uniformly on R^n as t -> 0+. Moreover Phi(.,t) is an approximate identity: integral_{R^n} Phi(x,t) dx = 1 for every t>0.

body:
Let Ω ⊂ ℝⁿ be open and F: Ω × ℝ × ℝⁿ → ℝ continuous; consider the equation F(x, u(x), Du(x)) = 0 in Ω. A function u ∈ C(Ω) is a viscosity SUBsolution if for every φ ∈ C¹(Ω) and every point x₀ ∈ Ω at which u − φ has a local maximum, F(x₀, u(x₀), Dφ(x₀)) ≤ 0. It is a viscosity SUPERsolution if for every φ ∈ C¹(Ω) and every local minimum point x₀ of u − φ, F(x₀, u(x₀), Dφ(x₀)) ≥ 0. It is a viscosity solution if it is both. (Equivalent reformulations: replace 'local' by 'strict local' or 'global' max/min, or use C^∞ test functions, or use super-/subdifferentials D⁺u(x₀) and D⁻u(x₀): the conditions read F(x₀, u, p) ≤ 0 for all p ∈ D⁺u(x₀) and ≥ 0 for all p ∈ D⁻u(x₀).) Every classical C¹ solution is a viscosity solution, and a viscosity solution that is differentiable at x₀ satisfies the equation pointwise there. For time-dependent equations u_t + H(x, Du) = 0 on Ω × (0,T) apply the same definition with the gradient variable (u_t, Du) and test functions of (x,t). SHARP EDGE — the sign of F matters: writing the same equation as −F = 0 interchanges the roles of sub- and supersolutions, so the two forms have DIFFERENT viscosity solutions. Example: on (−1,1) with boundary values u(±1) = 0, the function 1 − |x| is a viscosity solution of |u'| − 1 = 0 but NOT of 1 − |u'| = 0, while |x| − 1 is a viscosity solution of 1 − |u'| = 0 but not of |u'| − 1 = 0 (at the kink x = 0, a concave kink admits only test functions touching from above, and a convex kink only test functions touching from below). Viscosity solutions are in general only continuous, are stable under uniform limits, and for convex H coincide with Lipschitz solutions that are semiconcave; the notion is designed so that comparison/uniqueness theorems hold where classical and a.e. solutions are non-unique.
F is continuous
u is continuous on Ω
the equation is written in the form F = 0 with a fixed sign convention

body:
[Theorem result of arXiv:2607.01463, 'Two Multi--Draw Coupon Collector models with different retention rules'] Consider the  $d$ coupon collector's problem (d--CCP), where in each run we keep \textbf{all} the new observed coupons. Let $T_{N,d}$ be the number of trials until all $N$ different types of coupons, which are uniformly distributed, are collected (at least once). Then, as $N\rightarrow \infty$
\begin{equation}
\mathbb {E}\left[T_{N,d}\right]=
\frac{N}{d}\log N
+\frac{\gamma N}{d}
-\frac{d-1}{2d}\log N
+\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{d-1}{2d}\gamma\right)
+\mathcal{O}\left(\frac{\log N}{N}\right).

\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Over connected unweighted graphs on n vertices with simple random walk, max_G tau_0(G) = n^3/54 + O(n^{19/7}), settling the Kemeny half of Aldous-Fill Open Problem 6.13. The balanced barbell attains n^3/54 + 0.056 n^2 + o(n^2), so the maximum's second-order term is positive and of order n^2 and the n^{19/7} is the upper bound's looseness. Ingredients: the bridge-tree identity, a deletion comparison, the mass-capacity inequality A <= gamma (s+a_n)^2 / (2 P S^2), a distance budget, a Rayleigh test function, a stability squeeze, and the Alev-Anari-Lau-Oveis Gharan cut/resistance-diameter theorem (balance 3-a = 1+6a, a = 2/7). Exhaustively for n <= 7 every maximizer is a barbell; the optimal block fraction is 1/3 at n = 60, 120, 240.

[Lm 28 of arXiv:2512.02286, 'Pfaffian Transition Probability and Correlation Kernel of TASEP in Half-space'] Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be two kernels defined on $\mathbb{N}\times\mathbb{N}$, which are given by
\[
S_i(x,y)=\frac1{2\pi\ii}\oint_{\gamma}\dd w\,w^{x-y-1}g_i(w), 
\]
where $g_1,g_2$ are complex functions which are both analytic on the disk $\{z\in\mathbb{C}\!:|z|<r\}$ for some $r>0$ and $\gamma$ is any simple closed contour contained in that disk.
Then the sum defining the convolution $S_1\conv S_2$ is absolutely convergent and
\begin{equation}
S_1\conv S_2(x,y)=\frac1{2\pi\ii}\oint_{\gamma}\dd w\,w^{x-y-1}g_1(w)g_2(w)
\end{equation}
for all $x,y\in\mathbb{N}$.

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2506.10256, 'Clustering of large deviations events in heavy-tailed moving average processes: the catast'] Let $(Z_i)$  be i.i.d.  zero mean one-dimensional random variables that are 
  regularly varying with index $\alpha>1$. For each $n=1,2,\ldots$ let
  $\{\beta_{in}\}_{i =
    -\infty}^\infty $ be a sequence satisfying $\sum_{i =
    -\infty}^\infty |\beta_{in}| \leq nL$ for some $L > 0$ independent
  of $n$. If $\alpha\leq 
  2$, assume also that for some $B>0$ we have $|\beta_{in}|\leq B$ for
  all $i,n$. 
(a) \  For any $\delta, \tau> 0$ and $0<\vep\leq 1$, for all $n\geq
n_0(\vep,\tau/B)$ (that may also depend on the distribution of $Z$), we have 
    \[
    P\left( \left| \sum_{i=-\infty}^\infty \beta_{in} Z_i
        \one(|\beta_{in}Z_i|\leq \tau n)\right| > n\delta\right)  \leq
    \left\{ \begin{array} {ll}
    \left( \frac{n^2\tau\delta}{ E(Z_0^2)\sum_{i=-\infty}^\infty
        \beta_{in}^2}\right)^{-\delta/(8\tau)} & \text{if} \
                                                 \alpha>2,\\
       \left(\frac{n^2\tau\delta  B^{\alpha-2-\vep}} {g(\tau n/B) \sum_{i=-\infty}^\infty
        |\beta_{in}|^{\alpha-\vep}}\right)^{-\delta/(8\tau)} & \text{if} \
                                                 1<\alpha\leq 2,
\end{array} \right.
    \]
    where $g$ is regularly varying with exponent $2-\alpha$ and it
    depends only on the law of $Z$ and $\vep$. 
 

(b) \  For any $\delta, \tau> 0$ and $0<\vep\leq 1$, for all $n\geq
n_0(\vep,\tau/B)$ (that may also depend on the distribution of $Z$), we have 
    \begin{align*}
    P\left( \left| \sum_{i=-\infty}^\infty \beta_{in} Z_i
       \right| > n\delta\right)  \leq& \left( \frac{n^2\tau\delta}{ E(Z_0^2)\sum_{i=-\infty}^\infty
                                       \beta_{in}^2}\right)^{-\delta/(8\tau)} \\
                                       +& 2 B^{-\alpha +\vep} P(|Z_0|>n\tau/B) \sum_{i}
     |\beta_{in}|^{\alpha-\vep}
       \end{align*}
       if $\alpha>2$, and
    \begin{align*}
    P\left( \left| \sum_{i=-\infty}^\infty \beta_{in} Z_i
       \right| > n\delta\right)  \leq&     
  \left(\frac{n^2\tau\delta  B^{\alpha-2-\vep}} {g(\tau n/B) \sum_{i=-\infty}^\infty
      |\beta_{in}|^{\alpha-\vep}}\right)^{-\delta/(8\tau)} \\
+& 2 B^{-\alpha +\vep} P(|Z_0|>n\tau/B) \sum_{i}
     |\beta_{in}|^{\alpha-\vep} 
\end{align*}
if $1<\alpha<2$, where $g$ is as in part (a). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\]

[Corollary 13 of arXiv:2608.03922, 'Absolute continuity of two-dimensional polynomial random vectors'] Let $M,R>0$ and $d\in\mathbb N$. Let
$\mu=\bigotimes_{j=1}^\infty\mu_j$,
where $\mu_j\in\mathcal M_d(M,R)$ for every $j\in\mathbb N$.
Then, for every $f\in\mathcal P_d(\mu)$ and every sequence of cylindrical
polynomials $\{f_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$ of degree at most $d$ such that
$f_n\to f$ in $L^2(\mu)$, the sequence $\{\nabla f_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$
converges in $L^2(\mu;\ell^2)$, and its limit does not depend on the choice
of $\{f_n\}_{n=1}^\infty$. Consequently, the gradient extends uniquely to a
bounded linear operator
$\nabla\colon\mathcal P_d(\mu)\to L^2(\mu;\ell^2)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 13 of arXiv:2608.03922

[Thm thm41 of arXiv:2411.13099, 'Long time behavior of killed Feynman-Kac semigroups with singular Schr{ö}dinger potentials'] ([guillinqsd]) Assume, in addition to the three previous assumptions $\mathfrak 1$, $\mathfrak 2$, and $\mathfrak 3$ above, that $Q$ has a spectral gap in $b\mathcal B_{\mathbf W_\star} (\mathscr S)$, i.e. 
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf r_{ess}(Q|_{b\mathcal B_{\mathbf W_\star} (\mathscr S)})<\mathsf r_{sp}(Q|_{b\mathcal B_{\mathbf W_\star} (\mathscr S)}).
\end{equation}
Then, there exist  a unique couple $(\mu, \varphi) \in \mathcal P_{\mathbf W_\star}(\mathscr S)\times \mathcal C_{b\mathbf W_\star}(\mathscr S)$, where  $\varphi>0$ over $\mathscr S$ and  $\mu(\varphi)=1$, and constants $r\in ]0,1[, C\ge 1$, such that
$$
 \mu Q=\mathsf r_{sp}(Q|_{b\mathcal B_{\mathbf W_\star}}(\mathscr S))\mu, \ Q\varphi= \mathsf r_{sp}(Q|_{b\mathcal B_{\mathbf W_\star} (\mathscr S)}) \varphi
$$ 
 and
\begin{equation}
\Big \|\frac {1}{\mathsf r_{sp}(Q|_{b\mathcal B_{\mathbf W_\star}(\mathscr S)})^n}Q^n f - \varphi \mu(f)\Big \|_{b\mathcal B_{\mathbf W_\star}(\mathscr S)} \le C r^n \|f \|_{b\mathcal B_{\mathbf W_\star} (\mathscr S)}, \ \forall f\in b\mathcal B_{\mathbf W_\star}(\mathscr S).
\end{equation}
Moreover, $\mu(O)>0$ for all nonempty open subset $O$ of $\mathscr S$. 
In particular, we have: 
 \begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item[$\mathfrak a$.] If  $\nu\in \mathcal M_{b\mathbf W_\star}(\mathscr S) $  satisfies for some $\lambda \in \mathscr R$, $\nu Q= \lambda\nu$ and $\nu(\varphi)\ne0$, then $\lambda=\mathsf r_{sp}(Q|_{b\mathcal B_{\mathbf W_\star} (\mathscr S)})$ and $\nu=c\mu$ for some constant $c$.
 \item[$\mathfrak b$.] If $f\in b\mathcal B_{\mathbf W_\star}(\mathscr S)$ satisfies for some  $\lambda \in \mathscr R$,  $Qf=\lambda f$  and  $\mu(f)\ne 0$, then $\lambda=\mathsf r_{sp}(Q|_{b\mathcal B_{\mathbf W_\star}(\mathscr S)})$ and $f=c\varphi$ for some constant $c$.
 \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm thm41 of arXiv:2411.13099

[The 33 of arXiv:2609.02879, 'On the cut locus of Hamilton--Jacobi equations I: structure and propagation via the touchi'] Let $H$ be a Tonelli Hamiltonian on $\T^n$ and $\phi\in\SCL(\T^n)$. Then there exist $C_1>0$ and $C_2>0$ (depending on the local $C^2$ modulus and the Tonelli modulus of $H$ and the Lipschitz and semiconcavity constants of $\phi$) such that for any $x\in\operatorname{Alex}(\phi)$
	\begin{align*}
		\|D^2\phi(x)\|\leqslant\max\Big\{\ \frac{C_1}{\tau_{\phi,H}(x)},C_2\ \Big\}.
	\end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition prop:gibbs cond of arXiv:2603.01322, 'Gibbs conditioning, atypical consensus and splitting Gibbs measures on random regular grap'] Let $c\in \R$ and let ${\mathcal M}(c)  \subset\P(\TkaXinf)$ be the set of minimizers of the constrained optimization problem 
    \begin{align}
 {R} (c) :=   \min_{\rho \in {\mathcal A} (c)} I^\k (\rho), 
   
   \end{align}
   where $I^\k$ is the large deviation rate function of $\{U_n\}$ from Theorem (\oldref{thm:ldp-Un}). 
Then for any open set ${\mathcal O} \subset\P(\TkaXinf)$ with ${\mathcal M} (c) \subset {\mathcal O}$, the conditional limits (equation eq:general cond limit of the paper)-(equation eq:general cond limit other way of the paper) hold. In other words, if $c > \sref$ (resp. $c < \sref$)  
then $\{U_n\}$ asymptotically lies in ${\mathcal M}(c)$ given $\{\mathbb{E}_{L_n}\sqpr{S_h}\geq c-\delta\}$ (resp. $\{\mathbb{E}_{L_n}\sqpr{S_h}\leq c-\delta\}$).
title: Gibbs conditioning principle

body: [Definition 15 ($\mathcal{E}^f$-expectation) of arXiv:2605.04359, 'Well-posedness of reflected BSDEs with default time and irregular barrier: An application '] Let $T^{\prime} \in [0,T]$ be a deterministic time. Let $\xi \in \mathbb{L}^2_{\beta}(\mathcal{F}_{T'})$. The $\mathcal{E}^f$-expectation of $\xi$ denoted by $\left(\mathcal{E}^f_{t,T'}(\xi)\right)_{t \in [0,T']}$ is defined as the the first component of the BSDE \eqref{basic equation : classical BSDE} with default jump associated with terminal time $T'$ and data $(\xi,f)$. More generally, for each time $T'\in [0,T]$ and each terminal condition $\xi \in \mathbb{L}^2_{\beta}(\mathcal{F}_{T'})$, due to Theorem \ref{Existence and uniqueness unconstrained BSDE}, we may define an operator $\mathcal{E}^f: \left(T',\xi\right) \to \mathcal{E}^f_{\cdot,T'}(\xi)$, and we say that $\mathcal{E}^f_{\cdot,T'}(\xi)$ is the $\mathcal{E}^f$-expectation process of $\xi$.

body:
[Lem 162 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Let $I$ be a finite, nonempty index set. Let 
  \[
    \lt(\Theta, 
    \vec{\hat{Z}}\equiv
    (\hat Z_i)_{i\in I},
    \vec{\tilde{Z}}
    \equiv(\tilde Z_i)_{i\in I}\rt)
  \]
  be a random variable where
  $(\vec{\hat{Z}},\vec{\tilde{Z}})$
  are centered, jointly gaussian, and independent of $\Theta$. 
  Assume that $\vec{\hat{Z}}$ and $\vec{\tilde{Z}}$ are equidistributed,
 and that, for distinct $i,k\in I$,
  \[
    \bbE[\hat Z_i\hat Z_k]
    =\bbE[\tilde Z_i\tilde Z_k]
    =\bbE[\hat Z_i\tilde Z_k]=0.
  \]
Let $F$ and $G$ be measurable functions
such that $F(\Theta,\hat Z)$ and 
$G(\Theta,\hat Z)$ have finite variance, and such that
	\beq
    \bbE\Big[F(\Theta,\hat Z) 
    	\,\Big|\, \Theta\Big] = 0 = 
    \bbE\Big[G(\Theta,\tilde Z) 
    	\,\Big|\, \Theta\Big]\,,
    \eeq
  $\Theta$-almost surely.
Then the covariance between $F(\Theta,\hat{Z})$ and $G(\Theta,\tilde{Z})$ is bounded by
  \beq
    \lt| \bbE[F(\Theta,\hat Z) G(\Theta,\tilde Z)] \rt|
    \le
    \rho_{\max} \cdot
    \bbE[F(\Theta,\hat Z)^2]^{1/2}
    \bbE[G(\Theta,\tilde Z)^2]^{1/2}\,, 
    
  \eeq
where $\rho_i\in[-1,+1]$ denotes the correlation between $\hat{Z}_i$ and $\tilde{Z}_i$, and 
$\rho_{\max} 
   \equiv\max\{|\rho_i|: i\in i\}$.
 
\begin{proof}
Let $\sigma_i$ denote the standard deviation of $\hat{Z}_i$, and denote
  \[
    \hat W_i \equiv 
    \frac{\hat Z_i}{\sigma_i}\,, \quad
    \tilde W_i 
    \equiv \frac{\tilde Z_i}{\sigma_i}\,,
  \]
which are marginally standard gaussians. It follows from the assumptions that
$(\hat W_i,\tilde W_i)$ are independent over $i\in I$, and $\bbE[\hat W_i\tilde W_i]=\rho_i$.
Let $(h_m)_{m\geq 0}$ denote the orthonormal Hermite polynomials for the
one-dimensional standard gaussian measure. We note that if $W$ and $\tilde{W}$ are marginally standard gaussians, and $(W,\tilde{W})$ is jointly gaussian and $\rho$-correlated, then it is straightforward to verify that
	\beq
	\E[ h_n(W) h_m(\tilde{W})]
	= \ind\{n=m\} \rho^n\,.\eeq
 For a multi-index $\vec n=(n_i)_{i\in I}\in\bbZ_{\ge 0}^I$, define the multivariate Hermite polynomial
  \[
    H_{\vec n}(w)
    \equiv\prod_{i\in I}h_{n_i}(w_i).
  \]
  We expand $F,G$ in the Hermite bases of $\hat W$ and $\tilde W$ respectively, conditional on $\Theta$, to obtain Hermite coefficients $a_{\vec n}(\Theta)$ and $b_{\vec n}(\Theta)$ such that
  \begin{align*}
    F(\Theta,\hat Z)
    &= \sum_{\vec n}a_{\vec n}(\Theta)
        H_{\vec n}(\hat W)\,, \\
    G(\Theta,\tilde Z)
    &= \sum_{\vec n}b_{\vec n}(\Theta)
        H_{\vec n}(\tilde W)\,.
  \end{align*}
  The assumption \eqref{e:conditional-centering} ensures $a_{\vec 0}(\Theta)=b_{\vec 0}(\Theta)=0$, $\Theta$-almost surely.
  Consequently, expanding in the Hermite bases and applying \eqref{e:hermite.corr.ip} gives
  \begin{align*}
    &\bigg|
      \bbE\Big[
        F(\Theta,\hat Z)G(\Theta,\tilde Z) \,\Big|\, \Theta
      \Big]
    \bigg|
    \le
      \sum_{\vec n\neq\vec 0}
         |a_{\vec n}(\Theta)b_{\vec n}(\Theta)|
         \prod_{i\in I}|\rho_i|^{n_i}\\
    &\qquad\le
      \rho_{\max}
      \bigg(\sum_{\vec n\neq\vec 0}
        a_{\vec n}(\Theta)^2
        \bigg)^{1/2}
      \bigg(\sum_{\vec n\neq\vec 0}
        b_{\vec n}(\Theta)^2
        \bigg)^{1/2}
    =\rho_{\max}
      \bbE\Big[F(\Theta,\hat Z)^2 
      	\,\Big|\, \Theta\Big]^{1/2}
      \bbE\Big[G(\Theta,\tilde Z)^2 
      	\,\Big|\, \Theta\Big]^{1/2}\,.
  \end{align*}
  Taking expectation over $\Theta$ and again applying the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality proves the conclusion.
\end{proof}

[Theorem 16 (The branching rule in $\U(n)$) of arXiv:2603.00353, 'Aldous-type Spectral Gaps in Unitary Groups'] Let $\mu=(\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_n)\in\mathbb{Z}^n$ be a non-increasing vector. Then the restriction of $\rho_\mu$ to $\U_{[n-1]}\cong\U(n-1)$ is given by 
\[
    \rho_\mu|_{\U_{[n-1]}} \cong \bigoplus_{\pi\,\colon\,\pi,\mu~\mathrm{interlace}} \rho_\pi,
\]
where the sum is over the non-increasing vectors $\pi\in\mathbb{Z}^{n-1}$ such that $\pi$ and $\mu$ \textit{interlace}. In particular, the decomposition of $\rho_\mu|_{\U_{[n-1]}}$ is multiplicity-free. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: The branching rule in $\U(n)$

body:
[Theorem th:Foster-Liapunov of arXiv:2603.20078, '\bf \Large Gated Infinite Server Queues in Light Traffic'] Suppose 
	that a Markov Chain with countable state space, say $\mathbb{Z}_+$, and transition
	probability matrix $P_{ij}$ is irreducible and let $N$ be a given natural
	number. If $V:\mathbb{Z}_+\to \mathbb{R}_+$, is a non-negative and $h:\mathbb{Z}_+\to \mathbb{R}_+$ a
	strictly positive function on the state space such that
	\begin{eqnarray}
		\sum_{j\in \mathbb{Z}_+} P_{ij}V(j) &\leq  & b,\hspace{1.14in}i \leq  N,
		 \\
		\sum_{j\in \mathbb{Z}_+} P_{ij}V(j) &\leq  & V(i)-h(i) ,\hspace{0.4in} i>N,  
	\end{eqnarray}
	where $b>0$, then the Markov Chain is positive recurrent and its (unique, 
	due to its irreducibility) stationary distribution, $\pi$, satisfies $\sum_j\pi(j) h(j) <\infty$. 
	Furthermore we have 
	$\sum_{j}P_{ij}^n h(j) \rightarrow \sum_j \pi_j h(j)$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Foster--Lyapunov Criterion
Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.13631

body:
[Proposition 1 (Martingale Trilemma) of arXiv:2607.12365, 'Bernoulli--Doob representation, asymptotic limits and boundary behavior of bounded homogen'] Let $Z$ be a continuous process on $[0,1]$ with $\sigma(0)=0$.
The following three conditions cannot hold simultaneously:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm(a)] \textit{Startability:} $\Pr(Z_t>0)>0$ for some $t>0$ when
      $Z_0=0$.
\item[\rm(b)] \textit{Bounded domain:} $Z_t\ge0$ for all $t\ge0$.
\item[\rm(c)] \textit{Martingale property:} $\E[Z_t]=Z_0=0$ for all
      $t\ge0$.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, within the class of processes satisfying
\textnormal{(b)} and \textnormal{(c)}, the only admissible boundary
behaviour at $0$ is absorption: $Z_t=0$ for all $t\ge\tau_0$ on
$\{\tau_0<\infty\}$.

[Proposition 30 (Scaling) of arXiv:2607.24561, 'Range convergence and sharp one-arm asymptotics\\for the critical percolation cluster in h'] For $\lambda>0$ define $\Phi_\lambda:\cM\to\cM$ by
$(\Phi_\lambda\mu)(A):=\lambda^{-4}\mu(\lambda A)$. Then
\[
\bN\circ\bigl(\mu\mapsto\Phi_\lambda\mu\bigr)^{-1}
\;=\;\lambda^{-2}\,\bN
\qquad\text{as measures on }\cM .
\]
In particular $\supp(\Phi_\lambda\mu)=\lambda^{-1}\Ran$, so  the family
$K\mapsto\bN(\Ran\not\subset\overline B_K)$ scales as $K^{-2}$; see
Proposition~\ref{prop:range}.

[Lemma 14 (Properties of \(\psi_{s,m}\)) of arXiv:2609.01436, '2609.01436'] The function \(\psi_{s,m}\) is bounded, nonnegative, nonincreasing,
convex, and belongs to \(C_b^{1,1}([0,\infty))\), with \(\operatorname{supp}\psi_{s,m}\subset[0,L]\).  Moreover,
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item
for \(0\leq x\leq s/2\), \(
 \psi_{s,m}(x)\geq(e^{-1/2}-e^{-4})^2\);
\item if \(0\leq d\leq s\) and \(0\leq x\leq L-2s\), then
\[
 \psi_{s,m}(x+d)\geq\frac{1}{(e+1)^2}\psi_{s,m}(x);
\]
\item for every finite nonnegative Borel measure \(F\) of mass \(N\),
\[
 \int_{(L-2s,\infty)}\psi_{s,m}(x)\,dF(x)
 \leq (e^2-1)^2Ne^{-2m};
\]
\item if \(L\leq\varepsilon'\), for \(x\ge 0\),
\(
 \psi_{s,m}(x)\leq\varphi_{\varepsilon'}(x).
\)
\end{enumerate}

[Theorem thm:portal-degradation of arXiv:2608.20480, 'When Clean Data Hurts: Learning with Monotone \\ Corruptions Beyond Binary Classification'] There is a countable multiclass hypothesis class $\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{portal}}$ with
$d_{\mathrm{DS}}(\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{portal}})=1$ such that
\[
    R^{\mathrm{imp}}_{\mathrm{iid}}(n;\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{portal}})
    =
    O(1/n),
    \qquad
    R^{\mathrm{imp}}_{\mathrm{ad},n}(n;\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{portal}})
    =
    \Omega(\log n/n).
\]
For every $d\ge1$, a $d$-fold product gives a class of DS dimension $d$ with
clean risk $O(d/n)$ and adaptive risk
$\Omega(d\log(1+n/d)/n)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:portal-degradation of arXiv:2608.20480

[Proposition 3 of arXiv:2608.12839, 'Spiking Neural Networks with Elephant Reinforcement'] Let \(\boldsymbol\mu(t)\) be a solution of the nonlinear RMF equation. Then, for
all \((v,s,k)\in E\), the coordinate probabilities are absolutely continuous
in time and satisfy the following equations for almost every \(t\geq0\).

For \(v\geq1\),
\begin{align}
\frac{d}{dt}p_i(t;v,s,k)
=
a_i(t)p_i(t;v-1,s,k)

-
\bigl[a_i(t)+\gamma+\lambda(v,s,k)\bigr]
 p_i(t;v,s,k).
\end{align}

For \(v=0\),
\begin{align}
\frac{d}{dt}p_i(t;0,s,k)
=&
-a_i(t)p_i(t;0,s,k)

+
\gamma\sum_{u\geq1}p_i(t;u,s,k)
\\
&+
q^{+}(s-1,k-1)
\sum_{u\geq0}
\lambda(u,s-1,k-1)
 p_i(t;u,s-1,k-1)
\nonumber\\
&+
q^{-}(s+1,k-1)
\sum_{u\geq0}
\lambda(u,s+1,k-1)
 p_i(t;u,s+1,k-1).
\nonumber
\end{align}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}

\beta_i(t)
=
\sum_{(v,s,k)\in E}
\lambda(v,s,k)p_i(t;v,s,k).
\end{equation}
For the hard-threshold intensity,
\begin{equation}

\beta_i(t)
=
\sum_{s,k}
\sum_{v>\alpha s^+}
p_i(t;v,s,k).
\end{equation}

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2603.25615, 'Fourier dimension of Mandelbrot cascades on planar curves'] For any $\delta>0$, almost surely,
\[\left|\widehat{\mu_{n+1}}(\xi)-\widehat{\mu_n}(\xi)\right|\lesssim_\delta 
b^{2n \delta} \left( \sum_{1 \leq \ell \leq k} b^{2(\ell-k)} \sum_{\iii\in\Lambda^n,D_\iii\subseteq (\mathcal{S}_\ell(\xi))_{b^{1-n}}} \mu_n(D_\iii)^2 \right)^{1/2}+b^{-n}\,,\]
for all $1\le k\le n$ and $b^{n+k-1} \leq |\xi| \leq b^{n+k}$. Here, the implicit constant is random, but independent of $n,k$ and $\xi$.

Independent review pending. Let D_N have diagonal grid v_j=-1+(2j+1)/N, let u_N be the normalized all-ones vector, and let B_N,h_N be the cavity blocks in a basis starting with u_N. On J=(-1/2,1/2), eta_N=N^(-1/4), N>=16, the scalar resolvent g_N has Im g_N>=pi/8 and |g_N|<=C+1/4, C=(log3)/2+pi/2. Hence b_N=Im g_N/|g_N|^2>=pi/[8(C+1/4)^2]>0 and its integrated log(1+1/b_N) is uniformly bounded along eta_N. At every fixed N the same functional diverges as eta->0. Thus fixed-size divergence does not force successive limits. This is an abstract finite-cavity example, not an Anderson proof.

[Lemma lem:fixed-cutoff-product-approx of arXiv:2608.23135, 'Graph distance and effective resistance of the random walk trace in four and five dimensio'] For every fixed $R\ge2$, let
\[

        \qquad
        \mathcal E_{\vartheta,R}:=\mathcal E_\vartheta\cap\mathcal P_{\vartheta,R}.
\]
Let $\Gamma_{\vartheta,R}^{q}$ be the independent Bernoulli edge set on
$\mathcal P_{\vartheta,R}$ with edge probabilities $(q_e)_{e\in\mathcal P_{\vartheta,R}}$.
Then
\begin{equation}

        d_{\rm TV}\bigl(\mathcal L(\mathcal E_{\vartheta,R}),
        \mathcal L(\Gamma_{\vartheta,R}^{q})\bigr)\longrightarrow0,
\end{equation}
where $\mathcal L_Y$ is the law with respect to $\mathbb P_Y$.

[Theorem thm:n-leaves of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] On $\mathcal{D}_{+}(R)$ with $R = \prod_{i} I_{i}$ bounded and
		$\log f$ bounded, the coordinate modulation distribution integrates
		to the foliation by separable tilting classes
		$\{\prod_{i}\varphi_{i}(x_{i})\,f\}$, each law reachable from each
		leaf-mate in at most $n$ moves, one per coordinate; the complete
		leaf invariant is the interaction potential, the class of $\log f$
		modulo additive functions of single coordinates; the product laws
		form the unique leaf on which all coordinate actions commute; and
		marginal-matching transport is again flat, realized by
		multidimensional iterative proportional fitting with local cycle
		rate governed by the principal angles among the $n$ rank subspaces,
		through the operator matrix of pairwise conditional expectations
		$(P_{ij})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma cones of arXiv:2608.30747, 'Compact homogeneous complex manifolds'] Let $\{ Z_i\}_{i=1}^n$ be a basis of $\RR^n$ satisfying the following properties:  
\begin{enumerate}[{\rm (i)}]
\item $\la Z_i,Z_j\ra\leq 0$ for all $i\ne j$, 

\item for each $j$ there exists $i$ such that $\la Z_i,Z_j\ra< 0$.  
\end{enumerate}
If a nonzero vector $Z=\sum\limits_{i=1}^n x_iZ_i$ satisfies that $\la Z,Z_i\ra\geq 0$ for all $i=1,\dots,n$, then $x_i>0$ for all $i=1,\dots,n$.

[Lemma lem:good_scales_for_event of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] Suppose that $h$ is a GFF on $D$ with some bounded boundary values. For $p > 0$, let $G^p$ be an event that is measurable with respect to the restriction of a GFF to $A(0,1/4,3/4)$, and suppose that $\lim_{p \to 0} \mathbf{P}[G^p] = 1$. Let $G^p_{z,r}$ denote the event that $\widetilde{h}_{z,r}(z+r\cdot) \in G^p$ (so that $G^p_{z,r}$ is an event measurable with respect to the restriction of $\widetilde{h}_{z,r}$ to $A(z,r/4,3r/4)$).

For any $b>0$ and $q \in (0,1)$ there exist $M>0$, $p > 0$ so that the following holds. Let $z \in D$ and $r>0$ such that $B(z,r) \subseteq D$. For $k\in\mathbf{N}$ let $E$ denote the event that the fraction of $1 \leq j \leq k$ so that the scale $(z,2^{-j}r)$ is $M$-good for $h$ and $G^p_{z,2^{-j}r}$ occurs is at least $q$. Then $\mathbf{P}[E^c] = O(e^{-bk})$.

[Thm 16 of arXiv:2608.23450, 'The Oldest Allele in a Moran Model'] Let $f, f^1, f^2, \dots$ be continuous functions in the Skorohod space $D_E[0,\infty)$ taking values in a metric space $(E, d)$. Let $\{\tau^i\}_{i\geq 0}$ be a sequence of strictly positive times such that $\sum_{i=0}^\infty \tau^i = \infty$.  Define the following concatenation with $t \in [0,\infty)$:
    
\[
(f\star f^1\star f^2\star \dots)(t) =
\begin{cases}
f(t) & \text{if } \quad 0\leq t<\tau^0 \\
f^1(t-\tau^0) & \text{if } \quad \tau^0\leq t<\tau^0 + \tau^1 \\
\vdots \\
f^n\left(t-\sum \limits_{i=0}^{n-1}\tau ^i\right)  & \text{if } \quad\sum \limits_{i=0}^{n-1}\tau ^i \leq t < \sum \limits_{i=0}^{n}\tau ^i\\
\vdots
\end{cases}
\]

\noindent Suppose that there exists a collection of sequences of functions $(f_n), (f_n^1), (f_n^2), \dots$ with corresponding sequences of strictly positive times $(\sigma^0_n), (\sigma^1_n), \dots$ representing the concatenation times for the pre-limit paths. Suppose that as $n \to \infty$, we have convergence in the product space $D_E[0,\infty) \times (0,\infty)$ given by:
\[ (f_n, \sigma_n^0) \longrightarrow (f, \tau^0) \quad \text{and} \quad (f_n^i, \sigma_n^i) \longrightarrow (f^i, \tau^i) \quad \text{for all } i \ge 1. \]

If the concatenated pre-limit path is defined as:
\[
(f_n\star f^1_n\star f^2_n\star \dots)(t) =
\begin{cases}
f_n(t) & \text{if } \quad 0\leq t<\sigma_n^0 \\
f_n^1(t-\sigma_n^0) & \text{if } \quad \sigma_n^0\leq t<\sigma_n^0 + \sigma_n^1 \\
\vdots \\
f_n^k\left(t-\sum \limits_{i=0}^{k-1}\sigma_n^i\right)  & \text{if } \quad\sum \limits_{i=0}^{k-1}\sigma_n^i \leq t < \sum \limits_{i=0}^{k}\sigma_n^i\\
\vdots
\end{cases}
\]
and if $f, f^1, f^2, \dots$ are continuous at the endpoints of their respective concatenated intervals, then there is convergence $(f_n\star f^1_n\star f^2_n\star \dots)\longrightarrow (f\star f^1\star f^2\star \dots)$ in the Skorokhod topology.

\(0<\sigma^\xi<\infty\) almost surely, and its law is atomless.  Let

body:
Let Omega be a bounded open set in R^n with C^1 boundary and outward unit normal nu, and let F be a vector field in C^1(closure of Omega) (or in W^{1,1}(Omega) with an integrable trace). Then the integral over Omega of the divergence of F equals the boundary integral of F dotted with nu with respect to (n-1)-dimensional surface measure. Two standard consequences: integration by parts, the integral over Omega of u_{x_i} v = minus the integral of u v_{x_i} plus the boundary integral of u v nu_i; and Green's identities, for instance the integral over Omega of ( u Laplacian v - v Laplacian u ) equals the boundary integral of ( u times the normal derivative of v minus v times the normal derivative of u ). The theorem extends to Lipschitz domains, where the normal exists at almost every boundary point, and to sets of finite perimeter with the reduced boundary and measure-theoretic normal in place of the classical ones.
Boundary regularity (C^1, or Lipschitz, or finite perimeter) and enough integrability of the field and its derivative up to the boundary.
On an arbitrary bounded open set the statement is false - the boundary can be too wild to carry a normal.

[Definition 1 (Causality and extendibility of curves) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $\mathcal{M} \subset \R^{1+3}$ be an open subset of spacetime on which the fluid variables
	$\vec{\Psi} := \{s,\uprho,v^1,v^2,v^3\}$ are defined and $C^1$,
	and let $\gfour(\vec{\Psi})$ be the acoustical metric defined in \eqref{E:ACOUSTICALMETRICANDMATERIALDER}. Let $\upgamma : I \to \mathcal{M}$ be a $C^1$ curve, where $I \subseteq \R$ is an interval of the form $[a,b], (a,b), [a,b)$, or $(a,b]$ where $-\infty \le a < b \le \infty$.
		\begin{itemize}
			\item We say that $\upgamma$ is $\gfour$-timelike ($\gfour$-null) if $\gfour(\dot \upgamma(s), \dot \upgamma(s)) < 0$ $(\gfour(\dot \upgamma(s), \dot \upgamma(s)) =0)$ for all $s \in I$. We say $\upgamma$ is $\gfour$-causal if it is either $\gfour$-timelike or $\gfour$-null.
			\item We say that $\upgamma$ is \emph{extendible} in $\mathcal{M}$ if at least one of the limits $\lim_{s \to a} \gamma(s)$ or $\lim_{s \to b} \gamma(s)$ exist \emph{in $\mathcal{M}$}. We note that this notion of extendibility is with respect to the \emph{domain} $\mathcal{M}$. 
			\item If $\upgamma$ is not extendible, it is called inextendible.
		\end{itemize}
title: Causality and extendibility of curves

[Theorem th:Friedman of arXiv:2510.10299, '\Large Sparse graphs and their Benjamini-Schramm limits: a spectral tour'] Let $d \geq 3$ be an integer,  $G$ a random graph distributed according to the uniform measure on $ \mathbb{G}(n,d)$, and let  $d = \mu_1 \geq \mu_2 \geq \cdots \geq \mu_n$ be the eigenvalues of its adjacency operator $A$. Then for every $\epsilon >0$, the event 
$$
 \max (\mu_2 , -\mu_n) \leq 2 \sqrt{d-1} + \epsilon,
$$
has probability tending to $1$ as $n$ tends to infinity (and  $nd$ is even). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Friedman's Theorem, adjacency version

[Theorem 13 of arXiv:2608.17374, '\textbf{On the Pseudo-Mixing of Kac's Walk}'] For $n\in \mathbb{N}$, fix $1\leq k<n$ and $T\geq0$. Then fix a function $f= f_{n}$ with $f \, : \: \So{n} \mapsto \mathbb{R}$ of the form 
\[
f(X) = \prod_{r=1}^{k} X[i_{r},j_{r}].
\]

Let $C > 0$ be the constant appearing in the statement of Theorem \ref{LemmaMainContractionEstimate} and let 
\be 
\omega_{n} = C_{\mathrm{diam}}\,k\, n^{- \left\lfloor \frac{T}{C n (k+\log(n))\log(n)} \right\rfloor}
\ee 
be the upper bound obtained in that theorem.\footnote{Here we replace $D(X,Y)$ with the upper bound $C_{\mathrm{diam}} \, k$, where $C_{\mathrm{diam}}$ is a universal constant chosen so that the diameter of $\mathrm{St}(n,k)$ with respect to the Riemannian distance $D$ is at most $C_{\mathrm{diam}}k$.}

There exists some universal constant $N_{0}$ so that, for all $n > N_{0}$ and all $x \in \So{n}$,
\be 
| \kacdist_{n,T,x}(f) - \haarOdist_{n}(f) | \leq 2\sqrt{2k\,\omega_{n}}.
\ee

Let $\mathcal U$ be a collection of affine open subsets of $Y$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\arabic*)}]
\item A subset $Z\subseteq \bigcup_{U\in \mathcal U} U$ is {\it $\mathcal U$-invariant} if $Z\cap U$ is $\SAut(U)$-invariant for every $U\in\mathcal U$.
\item The collection $\mathcal U$ is {\it transversal} if $\bigcup_{U\in\mathcal U}U$ has no nonempty proper $\mathcal U$-invariant subset.
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Lemma 6 (Weighted cancellation) of arXiv:2606.25204, 'Exponential Rank Bounds for Random Matrices'] Let \(\Omega\) be a measurable space, let \(\nu\) and \(\sigma\) be finite
measures on \(\Omega\), and let \(w:\Omega\to(0,\infty)\) be bounded and
Borel.  Suppose
that for some \(C>0\),
\[
   \int_A w\,d\nu\leq C\int_A w\,d\sigma
\]
for every Borel set \(A\subseteq\Omega\).  Then
\[
   \nu(A)\leq C\sigma(A)
\]
for every Borel set \(A\subseteq\Omega\).

body:
[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2604.08127, 'Asymptotics of Brownian occupation measures \\ with unusually large intersections'] For any $q > 1$ and $0 < \gamma < \frac{2q}{q-1}$, consider the Gibbs measure
    \begin{equation}
    
        \mathrm{d} \widehat{\mathbb{P}}_{t} = \frac{1}{Z_t} \exp \left\{ t^{1 - \gamma} \beta([0, t]^q)^{\gamma/q} \right\} \mathrm{d} \mathbb{P}.
    \end{equation}
    Then, the Brownian occupation measures $\widetilde{L}_t$ under the law $\widehat{\mathbb{P}}_t \circ \widetilde{L}_t^{-1}$ converge to
    \[  
    \lim_{t \to \infty} \widetilde{L}_t = \widetilde{\mu}_{1, q, \gamma} \quad \text{in } \widetilde{\mathcal{M}}_1(\mathbb{R}),
    \]
    where $\mu_{1, q, \gamma}$ has density $\psi_{1, q, \gamma}^2$ and $\psi_{1, q, \gamma}$ is the unique (up to shifts) solution to the variational problem
    \begin{equation}
        
    \rho_{1, q, \gamma} = \sup_{\substack{\psi \in H^1(\mathbb{R}) \\ \| \psi \|_2 = 1}} \left\{\| \psi \|_{2q}^{2\gamma} - \frac{1}{2} \| \nabla \psi \|_2^2 \right\}.
    \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 3 of arXiv:2604.08127

[Lemma convexity of arXiv:2604.20660, 'The Legendre structure of the TAP complexity\\ for the Ising spin glass'] Let $g:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be $C^2$ with $g''\ge \kappa$ for some $\kappa\in\mathbb{R}$, and let
		$\Phi_\zeta$ be the solution of the Parisi PDE run backward on $[t,1]$ with terminal
		condition $\Phi_\zeta(1,\cdot)=g$, where $\xi''\ge 0$ and $\zeta\ge 0$.
		Then for every $s\in[t,1]$,
		\[
		\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\,\partial_{xx}\Phi_\zeta(s,x)
		\;\ge\;
		\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}}\,g''(x)
		\;\ge\;
		\kappa.
		\]
		In particular, $x\mapsto\Phi_\zeta(s,x)$ is everywhere at least as convex as $g$.

[Lemma le:cyc_layer of arXiv:2606.16259, 'Super-Arrhenius relaxation of the triangular plaquette model in any dimension'] Let $d,n\in \mathbb N$, and let $1\leqslant k\leqslant d$.
  Denote by $S_0$ and $S_1$ the sets of points in $\Lambda_{d,n}$ whose $k$-th coordinate is equal to $0$ and $1$ respectively.
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item If $X\in \mathcal{C}_{d,n}$ and $X\cap S_0=\emptyset$, then $X=\emptyset$.
  \item If $X\in \mathcal{C}_{d,n}$ and $X\cap S_1=\emptyset$, then $X\subseteq S_0$.
    Moreover, $X\in \mathcal{C}_{(T',S_0)}$, where $T'=T_d\setminus\{e_k\}$.
  \end{enumerate}

[Defn def:misordered of arXiv:2604.12963, 'Shocks, instability, and the twenty networks\\ of infinite geodesics in the Directed Lands'] Let $\theta\in\Theta^\omega$. For $(z,t)\in\mathbb{R}^2$, let $\tau^-$ and $\tau^+$ be, respectively, $\theta-$ and $\theta+$ shock interfaces emanating from $(z,t)$. We say that $\tau^-$ and $\tau^+$ are \emph{misordered} if there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that
$\tau^-(r)<\tau^+(r)$ for all $r\in(t-\varepsilon,t)$.

\begin{align*}
\fint_{a}^{b}\Vert P_\tau^{\omega}\Vert_{2,2}^2 \drm \tau
\leq \euler^{-2\Lambda a+\gamma(\kappa S)b},
\end{align*}
and 
\[
h(\omega)\leq \gamma(\kappa S)
:=\frac{2}{S^2}\left(\cosh\left(\kappa S\right)-1\right).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let gamma be the standard normal probability measure on R and g be a real function in L^2(gamma). Use the orthonormal probabilists Hermite basis H_k=He_k/sqrt(k!) and coefficients a_k=E[g(Z)*H_k(Z)], Z~gamma. For jointly standard normal X,Y with correlation q in (-1,1), define C_g(q)=Cov(g(X),g(Y)) and V=Var_gamma(g). Then C_g(q)=sum_(k>=1) a_k^2*q^k and V=sum_(k>=1) a_k^2. In particular, lim_(q up to 1) [V-C_g(q)]/(1-q)=sum_(k>=1) k*a_k^2, allowing the value +infinity. This sum is finite exactly when g has a weak derivative g_prime in L^2(gamma), that is, g belongs to H^1(gamma); weak derivative means the usual distributional derivative with respect to Lebesgue measure. In that case ||g_prime||_(L^2(gamma))^2=sum_(k>=1) k*a_k^2 and V-C_g(q)=||g_prime||_(L^2(gamma))^2*(1-q)+o(1-q). These are Gaussian analytic identities used in the authors' activation-smoothness calculation. They do not require the replica ansatz and do not assert a rigorous storage-capacity threshold.
Real g in L^2 of the standard Gaussian measure; orthonormal probabilists Hermite convention.
For the finite-energy first-order expansion, also g in H^1(gamma).

Let (D,d) be a Polish metric space and let mu_i,nu_i be Borel probability measures with finite second moments, for i=1,...,k with finite k>=1. Let t_i>=0 and sum_i t_i=1. Then W_2(sum_i t_i mu_i,sum_i t_i nu_i)^2<=sum_i t_i W_2(mu_i,nu_i)^2. The same weights occur on both sides of the coupling. In particular, for r in [0,1] and mu,nu,tau in P_2(D), W_2((1-r)mu+r tau,(1-r)nu+r tau)^2<=(1-r)W_2(mu,nu)^2. Thus the corresponding contraction factor for W_2 itself is sqrt(1-r). Joint convexity is asserted for the squared distance. The unsquared version is false: on R take mu_1=mu_2=nu_2=delta_0, nu_1=delta_1, and weights r,1-r with 0<r<1; the distance between mixtures is sqrt(r), whereas the weighted sum of the two unsquared distances is r. Source: Ambrosio--Stra--Trevisan, A PDE approach to a 2-dimensional matching problem, Section 2.1, equation (2.4).
Polish metric space (complete and separable)
Finite collection of probability-measure pairs, each with finite second moment
Nonnegative weights summing to one, identical for the two mixtures

[Thm 5 of arXiv:2605.26669, '2605.26669'] Let $Y^1_0$ and $Y^2_0$ be non-negative integers such that $T_0:=Y^1_0+Y^2_0>0$.  Define the proportion of balls of type 1 in the urn as $Z_n:=\frac{Y^1_n}{T_n}$, as indicated in (\ref{Z-1}).
For any positive integers $a,b,c$ and any $p\in (0,1)$,  if the condition $3 b p+c p>a p+c$ is satisfied, we have
\beq
\sqrt{n} \left(Z_n-\frac{1}{2}\right)\stackrel{\dd}{\longrightarrow} \nn\left(0,\frac{\sigma^2}{2\Gamma-1}\right),
\deq
where
$$
\sigma^2:=\frac{p(a-b)^2+c^2(1-p)}{4\big((a+b)p+c(1-p)\big)^2}
$$
and
$$
\Gamma:= \frac{2b p}{(a+b)p+c(1-p)}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop Lyapunov-arguemnt-fails of arXiv:2511.10223, 'Stochastic Reaction Networks Within Interacting Compartments with Content-Dependent Fragme'] Let $N$ denote the compartment model in (equation eq:potentially-explosive of the paper), let $\mathcal N$ denote its state space, and for $n\in\mathcal N$ define
\begin{align*}
    C(n)&:=\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^2} n_x\\
    S(n)&:=\sum_{(e,s)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^2} sn_{(e,s)}\\
    E(n)&:=\sum_{(e,s)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^2} en_{(e,s)}.
\end{align*}
These represent, respectively, the total numbers of compartments, substrate molecules, and enzymes when the system is in state $n$. Let $\mathcal L$ and $\mathcal A$ denote the generators of $N$ and  of the CRN in (equation eq:CRN-projection of the paper), respectively. Suppose that $f$ is some function $f:\mathbb Z^3_{\ge0}\to[0,\infty)$, and suppose $V:\mathcal N\to[0,\infty)$ is defined by $V(n):=f(E(n),S(n),C(n))$.
If $V$ has finite sublevel sets and there exists $c,d$ such that $\mathcal LV(n)\le cV(n)+d$ for all states $n$, then $f$ has finite sublevel sets and $\mathcal Af(e,s,y)\le cf(e,s,y)+d$ for all states $(e,s,y)$.
title: Prop Lyapunov-arguemnt-fails of arXiv:2511.10223

[Theorem general-positive-integralrep-dunkl of arXiv:2512.10625, 'Bessel and Dunkl processes with drift'] For each $x\in\mathbb R^N$ there exists a unique probability measure $\mu_x\in M^1(\mathbb R^N)$ with
  $$E_k(x,\lambda)= \int_{\mathbb R^N} e^{\langle y,\lambda\rangle}\> d\mu_x(y) \quad\text{ for all}\quad \lambda\in \mathbb C^N.$$
  The measures $\mu_x$ have the folowing properties:
  \begin{enumerate}\itemsep=-1pt
\item[\rm{(1)}] The support $supp\>\mu_x $ is contained in the convex hull of the Weyl group orbit $\{gx: \> g\in W\}$ of $x$.
 \item[\rm{(2)}]  $x\in supp\>\mu_x $, and for $k>0$,  $\{gx: \> g\in W\}\subset  supp\>\mu_x $.
\item[\rm{(3)}] For $t>0$ and $x\in\mathbb R^N$,
  $\mu_{tx}$ is the image of $\mu_x$ under the mapping $y\mapsto ty$ on $\mathbb R^N$.
  \end{enumerate}

body: In probability theory, if a large number of events are all independent of one another and each has probability less than 1, then there is a positive probability that none of the events will occur. The Lovász local lemma allows a slight relaxation of the independence condition: As long as the events are "mostly" independent from one another and aren't individually too likely, then there will still be a positive probability that none of them occurs. This lemma is most commonly used in the probabilistic method, in particular to give existence proofs.

[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2607.19176, 'Exponential Convergence of the Sinkhorn Algorithm for the Schrödinger Bridge with Regime S'] Assume that the cost function \(c\) is bounded, with
\[
\|c\|_{L^\infty(E\times E)} \le M.
\]
Let \((\varphi,\psi)\) be optimal Schrödinger potentials, and let
\((\varphi^n,\psi^n)_{n\ge0}\) be the Sinkhorn iterates defined above. Then the following holds:

\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Optimal potentials.}
    \[
    \operatorname{osc}_E(\varphi)\le 2M,
    \qquad
    \operatorname{osc}_E(\psi)\le 2M.
    \]

    \item \textbf{Sinkhorn iterates.} For every \(n\ge0\),
    \[
    \operatorname{osc}_E(\varphi^{n+1})\le 2M,
    \qquad
    \operatorname{osc}_E(\psi^{n+1})\le 2M.
    \]
\end{enumerate}

[Thm 15 of arXiv:2607.06745, 'Regularization and asymptotic behaviour of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck evolution operators in infin'] Let the system satisfy Assumption $\text{\ref{assu: periodicita}}.$
Then $P_{0,T}\left(Im\Pi_{0}\right)\subseteq Im\Pi_{0}$, and the
spectral radius of $P_{0,T\mid Im\Pi_{0}}$ is less than or equal
to $e^{\omega_{0}T}$.

Consequently, for every $\omega\in\left(\omega_{0},0\right)$, there
exists $N_{\omega}\in\mathbb{N}$ such that:
\begin{equation}
\left\Vert P_{0,T\mid Im\Pi_{0}}^{N}\right\Vert _{\mathcal{L}\left(L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{0}\right)\right)}\leq e^{\omega NT}\quad\forall N\geq N_{\omega}.
\end{equation}
Further, there exists also $C_{T,\omega}>0$ such that:
\begin{align}
\left\Vert P_{s,t}f-\int_{X}f\left(y\right)\mu_{t}\left(dy\right)\right\Vert _{L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{s}\right)}\leq C_{T,\omega}e^{\omega\left(t-s\right)}\left\Vert f\right\Vert _{L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{t}\right)}\\
\forall s<t,\ f\in L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{t}\right),\nonumber 
\end{align}
where $\left\{ \mu_{t}\mid t\in\mathbb{R}\right\} $ is the family
of Gaussian measures defined in $\text{\eqref{def misura inv}}$.

body:
Load-bearing hypothesis: 'take the closure of T' presupposes that T is closable, i.e. that x_n ∈ D(T), x_n → 0 and Tx_n → y force y = 0; equivalently (in a Hilbert space) that D(T*) is dense. What fails: without closability the closure of the graph is not a graph, and 'the smallest closed extension' does not exist. Counterexample: H = ℓ², D(T) = finitely supported sequences, T x = (Σ_n x_n) e_1. T is densely defined and linear. Take x^{(k)} = (1/k, ..., 1/k, 0, 0, ...) with k entries: ‖x^{(k)}‖ = 1/√k → 0 while T x^{(k)} = e_1 for every k, so the graph closure contains both (0,0) and (0, e_1) and T is not closable. Consistently, ⟨Tx, y⟩ = (Σ x_n) conj(y_1) is ℓ²-bounded in x only if y_1 = 0, so D(T*) = {y : y_1 = 0} is not dense - exactly the criterion. The same phenomenon occurs for pointwise evaluation f ↦ f(0)g on L²(ℝ) restricted to continuous L² functions. Related traps: (i) an operator can be closable while its closure has strictly larger domain on which a defining formula no longer holds pointwise, so identities proved on D(T) must be re-derived by continuity in the graph norm; (ii) symmetry rescues closability (a symmetric operator is always closable, since T ⊂ T* and T* is closed), which is why this pitfall bites mainly for non-symmetric operators such as first order operators with unbalanced boundary conditions or multiplication-composition operators; (iii) a core argument ('it suffices to verify on a dense subspace') is valid only if the subspace is dense in the graph norm of the closed operator, not merely dense in the ambient space.

[Prop ent of arXiv:2411.09640, 'Random Lipschitz functions on graphs with weak expansion'] The following holds for discrete random variables $X$, $Y$, $Z$, and $X_1, \dots X_n$.
\begin{enumerate}[(a)]
\item $H(X) \le \log |\mathrm{Image}(X)|$, where $\mathrm{Image}(X)$ is the set of values $X$ takes with positive probability, with equality iff $X$ is uniform from its image.
\item $H(X,Y)=H(X)+H(Y|X)$
\item $H(X|Y) \le H(X)$
\item if $Z$ is determined by $Y$, then
$H(X|Y) \le H(X|Z)$ and $H(Y,Z|X) = H(Y|X)$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop ent of arXiv:2411.09640

[Definition 12 of arXiv:2604.03213, 'Asymptotic expansion for transport maps \\ between laws of multimatrix models'] Define $\tr\left(\C \la \cB \ra\right)$ to be the vector space 
    $$ \bigslant{\C \la \cB \ra}{\spn\left\{ PQ-QP : P,Q\in \C \la \cB \ra \right\}}. $$
    The equivalence class in $\tr\left(\C\la\cB\ra\right)$ of an element $P \in \C\la\cB\ra$ is denoted by $\tr\left(P\right)$.
    Also, define $\Tr^0(\cB)$ to be the symmetric tensor algebra of $\tr\left(\C \la \cB \ra\right)$ modulo the relation $\tr\left(1\right) = 1$.
    Finally, define $\Tr^{\ell}(\cB) \coloneqq H_c^{\otimes \ell-1}\otimes \C \la \cB \ra^{\otimes \ell} \otimes \Tr^0(\cB)$ for all $\ell \in \N$.

[Lemma 9 (Lexicographic sign rule (fair $s$-die)) of arXiv:2601.16580, 'Coin flipping and waiting times paradoxes \\ Why fair coins are exceptional'] Put $y=s/x>1$ and $H_T(y):=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{B}(T)} y^\ell$. Let $\ell^\star$ be the largest index on which the border-indicator vectors of $T_A,T_B$ differ. Then, for all $x\in(0,1)$,
\[
\operatorname{sign}\!\big(h_A(x)-h_B(x)\big)
=\operatorname{sign}\!\big(H_A(y)-H_B(y)\big)
=\operatorname{sign}\!\big(\mathbf{1}_{\{\ell^\star\in\mathcal{B}(T_A)\}}-\mathbf{1}_{\{\ell^\star\in\mathcal{B}(T_B)\}}\big),
\]
hence the sign is constant on $(0,1)$. Evaluating at $y=s$ gives $H_T(s)=\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal{B}(T)} s^\ell=\mathbb{E}[\tau_T]$.

[Theorem prop2 of arXiv:2608.00295, 'Quadratic Perturbations of Markov Systems'] Let ${\bf A}=(A_i)_{1\leq i\leq n}$ such that   $A_i=(a_{i}^{(s,t)})_{1\leq s,t\leq d}\in M_d(\mathbb{R})$ is a stochastic $d\times d$ matrix for each $1\leq i\leq n$, and ${\bf b}=(b_{i,j})_{1\leq i, j\leq n}$ such that each $b_{i,j}=(\alpha_{i,j}^{(s)})_{1\leq s\leq d}\in \mathbb{R}^d$ is a null-sum vector for each $1\leq i, j\leq n$ (with the convention  that $b_{i,i}=0$ for all $1 \leq i\leq n$).  We define the nonlinear operator 
$$T({\bf A};{\bf b}):\overbrace{\mathbb{R}^d \times  \mathbb{R}^d \times \dots \times \mathbb{R}^d}^{n \text{ times}}\to \overbrace{\mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{R}^d \times \dots \times \mathbb{R}^d}^{n \text{ times}},$$ 
determined by 
$$T({\bf A};{\bf b})\begin{bmatrix}
v_1\\
v_2\\
\vdots\\
v_n
\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}
{\displaystyle A_1v_1+\sum_{j=1}^n\langle v_1,v_j\rangle b_{1,j}}\\
{\displaystyle A_2v_2+\sum_{j=1}^n \langle v_2,v_j\rangle b_{2,j}}\\
\vdots\\
{\displaystyle A_nv_n+\sum_{j=1}^n \langle v_n,v_j\rangle b_{n,j}}
\end{bmatrix}.$$
The following are equivalent. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item For all the possible combinations of $\pm$ sign of the null-sum vectors $b_{i,j}$ we have that $T({\bf A};{\bf \pm b})$ induces a well defined operator from $\Delta_{d-1}^n$ to  $\Delta_{d-1}^n$. 
\item For each $1\leq i\leq n$ and $1\leq s\leq d$ we have $${\displaystyle \sum_{j=1}^n|\alpha_{i,j}^{(s)}|\leq \min_{1\leq t\leq d} \{a_{i}^{(s,t)}\}}.$$  
\end{enumerate}
title: Theorem prop2 of arXiv:2608.00295

[Defi construction of mu of arXiv:2604.23890, 'The Cutoff Profile for Random Transpositions on Repeated Cards in the Full Range of Parame'] Suppose $t\in\mathbb{Z}$. Set $t':=t-\lfloor\frac{n\log n}{2}\rfloor$, and $\gamma_t:=\exp(-2t'/n)$, which is the same as in (defi: construction of nu of the paper). Let $\mu_n^t$ denote the measure on $\mathfrak{S}_n$ defined by the following sampling process: first, sample $M_t\in\{0,1,\ldots,n\}$ according to the distribution 
$$\mathbf{P}[M_t=k]=\begin{cases}\mathbf{P}(\Pois(\gamma_t)=k)/\mathbf{P}(\gamma_t-l^{1/3}\le\Pois(\gamma_t)\le \gamma_t+l^{1/3})&\gamma_t-l^{1/3}\le k\le \gamma_t+l^{1/3}\\
0 & \text{else}

then sample a uniformly random subset $S_t$ of size $M_t$ in $[n]$. Finally, sample a uniformly random element of $\mathfrak{S}_{[n]\backslash S_t}$ and view it as an element of $\mathfrak{S}_n$ by fixing all of the elements in $S_t$.

body:
[Defn loc_conv of arXiv:2607.25428, 'The local weak limit of the minimum spanning arborescence in the complete graph'] A sequence of random rooted marked graphs $\{(G_n,o_n,\mathfrak m_n)\}_{n\ge 0}$ converges locally weakly to $(G,o,\mathfrak m)$ if for all $(H,u,\mathfrak q)\in\mathcal{G}^{\bullet}$ and $r\ge 0$,
$$\mathbb{P}(B_{(G_n,o_n,\mathfrak m_n)}(r)\simeq (H,u,\mathfrak q))\to\mathbb{P}(B_{(G,o,\mathfrak m)}(r)\simeq (H,u,\mathfrak q)),$$
as $n\to\infty$, where $a \simeq b$ means $a$ is isomorphic to $b$ as rooted marked graphs.
title: Defn loc_conv of arXiv:2607.25428

body:
[Lemma 2605121130 of arXiv:2609.02626, 'Comparison principles and symmetry for subquadratic fractional $p$-Laplacian equations'] Given $N\ge 1$, $s\in (0, \frac12)$, $\frac{1}{1-s}<p<2$, an open set $U\subset \mathbb{R}^N$, and $g\in C_c^2(U)$. Then there is $C>0$ depending only on $N$, $p$ and $s$, such that for any $u\in \widetilde{W}^{s, p}(U)$ and $t\in [-1, 1]$, in weak sense
\[
\Big|(-\Delta)_p^s (u-t g)-(-\Delta)_p^s u\Big|\le C\|g\|_{C^2(\mathbb{R}^N)}^{p-1}|t|^{p-1}\quad \mbox{in } {\rm supp} (g),
\]
where $\|g\|_{C^2(\mathbb{R}^N)}=\Sigma_{|\alpha|\le 2}\|\partial^\alpha g\|_{L^{\infty}(\mathbb{R}^N)}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 2605121130 of arXiv:2609.02626

body: In probability theory, the de Moivre–Laplace theorem, which is a special case of the central limit theorem, states that the normal distribution may be used as an approximation to the binomial distribution under certain conditions. In particular, the theorem shows that the probability mass function of the random number of "successes" observed in a series of $n$ independent Bernoulli trials, each having probability $p$ of success (a binomial distribution with $n$ trials), converges to the probability density function of the normal distribution with expectation $np$ and standard deviation ${\textstyle {\sqrt {np(1-p)}}}$, as $n$ grows large, assuming $p$ is not $0$ or $1$.

body: [Definition 1 (Asymmetric shelf-shuffle) of arXiv:2606.18047, 'Analysis of the asymmetric shelf shuffle'] Let $m\in \mathbb{N}$ be a natural number and $p\in (0, 1)$. An $(m, p)$-shelf shuffler has $m$ labelled shelves. A deck of cards labelled $1, \ldots, n$ is dealt from the bottom sequentially and assigned a shelf independently and uniformly at random. Each card is placed at the top or bottom of the existing pile, on the assigned shelf, with probability $p$ and $1-p$, respectively, independently of everything else. The shuffled deck is then formed by joining the piles in shelf order.
title: Asymmetric shelf-shuffle

body: [Definition def: mean_coexist of arXiv:2504.04792, 'Uniqueness and Longtime Behavior of the Completely Positively Correlated Symbiotic Branchi'] Let $\phi,\psi \in C_{\text{tem}}^+ \cap \mathcal{M}$ and let $(U^1,U^2)$ be the solution of $((eq: formal of the paper))$ with initial conditions $(U^1_0, U^2_0) = (\phi, \psi)$. We say that local coexistence is possible if for any limit point $(U^1_{\infty}, U^2_{\infty}) \in M_{\text{tem}}^2$, and for all $g_1, g_2 \in C_{\text{exp}}$, $\mathbb{P}\left(\langle U^1_\infty, g_1 \rangle \cdot \langle U^2_\infty, g_2 \rangle > 0 \right) > 0$. Otherwise, we say that local coexistence is impossible.
title: Definition def: mean_coexist of arXiv:2504.04792

body:
[Theorem 16 (Kac's walk applied to the Johnson--Lindenstrauss transform) of arXiv:2608.17374, '\textbf{On the Pseudo-Mixing of Kac's Walk}'] There is a universal constant $C_{\mathrm{JL}}<\infty$ such that the following holds. Let $n\geq 2$, let $x\in\So{n}$, and let $M\sim\kacdist_{n,T,x}$ be the endpoint of $T$ steps of Kac's walk started from $x$. Let $\mathcal X\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ have $N\geq2$ points, and let $0<\varepsilon,\delta<1/2$. Set
\be 
r=\left\lceil \log\frac{N}{\delta}\right\rceil,
\ee
and assume $4r<n$. Let $\ell$ be an integer satisfying
\be 
C_{\mathrm{JL}}\varepsilon^{-2}r\leq \ell<n.
\ee

If
\be 
T\geq
C_{\mathrm{JL}}\,n(4r+\log n)\left(r\log\frac{n}{\varepsilon}+\log\frac{N}{\delta}\right),
\ee
then, with probability at least $1-\delta$ over $M\sim\kacdist_{n,T,x}$,
\be 
(1-\varepsilon)\|x_i-x_j\|_2^2
\leq
\|A_M(x_i-x_j)\|_2^2
\leq
(1+\varepsilon)\|x_i-x_j\|_2^2
\ee
for every pair $1\leq i<j\leq N$.

In particular, for fixed $\varepsilon$ and $N/\delta\leq n^A$, with $A<\infty$ fixed, the usual Johnson--Lindenstrauss target dimension $\ell=O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log(N/\delta))=O_A(\varepsilon^{-2}\log n)$ \vnote{Isn't the JL target dimension $\epsilon^{-2}\log N$? EDIT: Ah, I see what's going on, $N$ is set to polynomial in $n$. But see below.} is achieved by taking $T\geq C_A n\log^3 n$. \vnote{I am worried that this is not the best illustration of our bound. In particular, when $N$ is polynomial in $n$, the JL embedding dimension $\ell$ is already $O(\log n)$ and so applying the matrix already only costs $O(n\log n)$. Shouldn't we be thinking about very large point sets of size, say $2^{n^{\epsilon'}}$ for some constant $0 < \epsilon' < 1$.} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Kac's walk applied to the Johnson--Lindenstrauss transform

body:
[Lemma 1 (Expectation under independent site occupation $D3$) of arXiv:2605.04048, 'Catastrophe--dispersion models in random and varying environments across generations'] Let $d\ge1$ and let $Y:=N_{\eta(T)}$ be an $\mathbb N_0$-valued random variable with probability generating function
\[
G_Y(s)=\mathbb E[s^Y], \qquad |s|<1.
\]
Under dispersal mechanism $D3$, the expected number of founded colonies is
\[
\mathbb E\!\left[\Delta^{(3)}(Y)\right]
=
d\left(1-G_Y\!\left(1-\frac1d\right)\right).
\]

Conditionally on $Y=r$, each of the $r$ surviving individuals independently chooses one of the $d$ sites with probability $1/d$ each.

For $j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$, define
\[
I_j:=\mathbf 1_{\{r_j\ge1\}},
\]
where $r_j$ is the number of individuals assigned to site $j$. Then
\[
\Delta^{(3)}(r)=\sum_{j=1}^d I_j.
\]

By linearity of expectation and symmetry, $\mathbb E[\Delta^{(3)}(r)]=\sum_{j=1}^d \mathbb E[I_j]=d\,\mathbb E[I_1]$. Now, $\mathbb E[I_1]=\mathbb P(r_1\ge1)=1-\mathbb P(r_1=0)$. The event $\{r_1=0\}$ means that none of the $r$ individuals chooses site $1$. Since choices are independent,
\[

body: Let dx/dt = f(x) be a C^1 vector field on R^n with an equilibrium x_0 (f(x_0) = 0) that is hyperbolic, meaning the Jacobian Df(x_0) has no eigenvalue with zero real part. The Hartman-Grobman theorem states that there is a neighborhood U of x_0 and a homeomorphism h: U -> R^n with h(x_0) = 0 conjugating the nonlinear flow near x_0 to the linear flow generated by Df(x_0): h(phi_t(x)) = exp(t Df(x_0)) h(x) whenever both sides are defined. So near a hyperbolic equilibrium the qualitative behavior of the nonlinear system matches its linearization; an analogous statement holds for hyperbolic fixed points of diffeomorphisms.
title: Hartman-Grobman theorem

[Definition 5 of arXiv:2608.19396, '\bf Penalisation of Two-Dimensional Brownian Motion'] Let $(F_{t})_{t \geq 0}$ denote an $(\mathcal{F}_t)$-adapted, nonnegative process. We shall say that this process belongs to the class $\mathcal{C}$ if and only if the following conditions hold:

\begin{enumerate}
    \item  $(F_{t})_{t \geq 0}$ is a nonnegative and nonincreasing process. In particular, since $0 \leq F_{t} \leq F_{0}$ and $F_{0}$ is a.s. constant ($\mathcal{F}_0$ is trivial), this process is $W^{(2)}$-almost surely bounded by a constant $C = F_{0}$.
     \item 
    There exists $a>0$ such that for every $t \geq \sigma_a$, where $
    \sigma_a := \sup \{ t \geq 0 :  |X_{t}|\le a \}$, 
    we have $$F_{t} = F_{\sigma_a} = F_{\infty} := \underset{s \rightarrow \infty}{\lim} F_s.$$
    \item We have 
    $$ \mathbf{W}^{(2)}(F_{\infty}) = \mathbf{W}^{(2)}(F_{\sigma_a}) < \infty.$$ 
    \end{enumerate}
title: Definition 5 of arXiv:2608.19396

[Lemma lem:higher-rank-variance-gain of arXiv:2606.21006, 'Law of the Iterated Logarithm for Weighted Sums of Functionals of Long-Memory Gaussian Seq'] Assume \(((A1 of the paper))\), \(((A3 of the paper))\), and \(((A4 of the paper))\), \(\alpha m<1\), and \(2d+\alpha m<1\). Let
\(
    \widetilde G(x):=G(x)-\frac{J_m}{m!}H_m(x).
\)
Then \(\widetilde G\) has Hermite rank at least \(m+1\). Moreover, there exist
\(C<\infty\), \(\delta>0\), and \(\gamma\ge1\) such that, for every sufficiently
large \(N\) and every interval \(I\subset\{N+1,\ldots,2N\}\),
\[
    \operatorname{Var}\left(\sum_{t\in I}a_t\widetilde G(X_t)\right)
    \le
    C v_N^2N^{-2\delta}\left(\frac{|I|}{N}\right)^\gamma .
\]
In particular, after decreasing \(\delta\) if necessary,
\[
    \left\|\sum_{t=1}^n a_t\widetilde G(X_t)\right\|_2
    \le C v_n n^{-\delta},
    \qquad n\ge3,
\]
and hence
\(
    \operatorname{Var}\bigl(\sum_{t=1}^n a_t\widetilde G(X_t)\bigr)
    =o(v_n^2).
\)

[Theorem thm:abstract-square-transversality of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] Let $\nu_{\rm ref}$ be a sigma-finite positive Radon measure on $S$, and let
$(\Lambda_i,\phi_i)_{i=1}^M$ be real eigenpairs of $A_\mu$ with continuous
representatives.  Assume that the following three conditions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=0pt,topsep=0.35em,parsep=0pt,partopsep=0pt]
\item The eigenpairs satisfy
\begin{equation}
 A_\mu\phi_i=\Lambda_i\phi_i,
 \qquad
 \Lambda_i>0,
 \qquad
 \Lambda_i\ne\Lambda_j\ (i\ne j),
 \qquad
 \left\|\phi_i\right\|_{L^2(\mu)}=1.
 
\end{equation}
\item The measures satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \mu\perp\nu_{\rm ref},
 \qquad
 \operatorname{supp}\mu=S,
 \qquad
 \rho=0\ \text{or}\ \rho\ll\nu_{\rm ref}.
 
\end{equation}
\item There exist $c_0>0$, finite signed measures $b_i\ll\nu_{\rm ref}$, and a
linear map
\begin{equation}
 L:
 \operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{\phi_1^2,\ldots,\phi_M^2\}
 \longrightarrow\mathcal M_{\rm fin}(S),
 
\end{equation}
such that
\begin{equation}
 L(\phi_i^2)
 =c_0\Lambda_i\phi_i^2\mu-b_i,
 \qquad 1\le i\le M.
 
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
Then, for every $a\in\mathbb R^M$,
\begin{align}
 \sum_{i=1}^Ma_i\Theta_\mu(\phi_i,\phi_i)=0
 &\Longrightarrow a=0,
 \\
 \sum_{i=1}^Ma_i\Lambda_i\Theta_\mu(\phi_i,\phi_i)=0
 &\Longrightarrow a=0.
 
\end{align}

[Proposition 5 (Continuity / Cauchy--Schwarz) of arXiv:2608.30589, 'Vector-Valued Wavelet Bases as Hilbert $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$-Module Bases: A Construc'] Fix $f\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)$. The map
\[
T_f:\ L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)\to \mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R}),\qquad
T_f(g):=\langle f,g\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})},
\]
is linear and bounded. More precisely, for any matrix norm $\|\cdot\|$ on $\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})$,
there exists a constant $C_m>0$ (depending only on $m$ and on the chosen norm) such that
\[
\|\langle f,g\rangle_{\mathbb{M}_m(\mathbb{R})}\|
\le C_m\,\|f\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)}\,\|g\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m)}
\qquad\forall\,g\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^d,\mathbb{R}^m).
\]
In particular, $T_f$ is continuous.

[Corollary cor:inverse-weight-linear-dynamics of arXiv:2608.16119, 'Fully nonlinear parabolic equations under a fixed reference diffusion: weighted \texorpdfs'] Let $0\leq\alpha<1$ and assume
Assumption~(ass:reference-diffusion of the paper).  Let
\begin{equation*}
 F\in L_\alpha^2,\qquad \psi\in L^2(\mu_T),\qquad u=\mathcal U(F,\psi),
\end{equation*}
and put $Y=u(\cdot,X)$ and $P=D_xu(\cdot,X)$.  There exists a universal numerical
constant $C>0$ such that
$Y\in\mathbb S^2(\mathbb R)$, $P^\top\in\mathbb H^2(\mathsf M^X;\mathbb R)$,
\begin{equation}
 Y_t=\psi(X_T)+\int_t^TF(s,X_s)\,\mathrm d s
      -\int_t^TP_s^\top\,\mathrm d\mathsf M_s^X,
 
\end{equation}
The accompanying estimate is
\begin{equation}
 \left\lVert Y\right\rVert_{\mathbb S^2(\mathbb R)}^2
 +\left\lVert P^\top\right\rVert_{\mathbb H^2(\mathsf M^X;\mathbb R)}^2
 \leq C\left(
   \norm\psi_{L^2(\mu_T)}^2
   +\frac{T^{1-\alpha}}{1-\alpha}\left\lVert F\right\rVert_\alpha^2\right).
 
\end{equation}
If, in addition, Assumption~(ass:drift-multiplier of the paper) holds,
$F\in H_{x,\alpha}^1$, and $\psi\in H^1(\mu_T)$, set
\begin{equation*}
 \mathsf H=D_x^2u(\cdot,X),\qquad
 \mathfrak A_t=-\int_0^t\mathfrak g[u,F](s,X_s)\,\mathrm d s.
\end{equation*}
Then $P\in\mathbb S^2(\mathbb R^d)$,
$\mathsf H\in\mathbb H^2(\mathsf M^X;\mathbb R^d)$, and
$\mathfrak A\in\mathbb V^2(\mathbb R^d)$, with
\begin{equation}
 P_t=P_0+\mathfrak A_t
       +\int_0^t\mathsf H_s\,\mathrm d\mathsf M_s^X,
 \qquad
 P_T=D_x\psi(X_T).
 
\end{equation}
The gradient processes satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \left\lVert P\right\rVert_{\mathbb S^2(\mathbb R^d)}^2
 +\left\lVert \mathsf H\right\rVert_{\mathbb H^2(\mathsf M^X;\mathbb R^d)}^2
 +\left\lVert \mathfrak A\right\rVert_{\mathbb V^2(\mathbb R^d)}^2
 \leq C\left(
   \left\lVert D_x\psi\right\rVert_{L^2(\mu_T)}^2
   +\frac{T^{1-\alpha}}{1-\alpha}
       \left\lVert \mathfrak g[u,F]\right\rVert_\alpha^2\right).
 
\end{equation}

[Definition def:function_d of arXiv:2510.21186, 'Weingarten Calculus with Virtual Isometries'] Let $k$ and $n$ be positive integers such that $k \le n$.
We define the \emph{descension function} $\Lower_{k,n}$ in $\mathbb{C}[S_k]$ by
 \[
\Lower_{k,n}(\sigma)= (\sgn \sigma) \sum_{t=0}^{\mathsf{f}(\sigma)} \binom{\mathsf{f}(\sigma)}{t} \frac{1}{n^{\downarrow (k-t)}},
\qquad \sigma \in S_k,
 \]
 where $n^{\downarrow t}$ is the falling factorial defined by
 \[
n^{\downarrow t} = \begin{cases}
 n(n-1) \cdots (n-t+1) & \text{for $t=1,2,\dots$}, \\
1 & \text{for $t=0$}.
\end{cases}
\]

[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The normal law of parameter $1$ is the following measure:
$$g_1=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\,e^{-x^2/2}dx$$
More generally, the normal law of parameter $t>0$ is the following measure:
$$g_t=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi t}}\,e^{-x^2/2t}dx$$
These are also called Gaussian distributions, with ``g'' standing for Gauss.

[Theorem 1 (Main theorem, condensed form) of arXiv:2606.26065, 'Localized Centered Second-Chaos Operators'] Assume the localized continuous Gaussian model described in Section~\ref{sec:setup}, together with the time-regularity and cutoff convergence hypotheses used in Section~\ref{sec:global}.  Suppose that the centered dyadic amplitude obeys the power-law envelope
\[
 \mathcal G(N)\le C_GN^{-\Gamma},\qquad \Gamma>\frac d2.
\]
Let $\lambda>0$ and choose exponents $s,\sigma$ in the strict window
\[
 s<\lambda+\Gamma-d,\qquad
 \max\{0,d-\Gamma\}<\sigma<\lambda+\Gamma-d.
\]
Then the localized centered Galerkin operators are uniformly bounded in every finite $L^p(\Omega)$ as maps
\[
 \mathbb X_T^\sigma
 \longrightarrow
 C_TH^{s-\lambda}\cap L_T^1B^{\sigma-\lambda}_{2,\infty},
\]
where $\mathbb X_T^\sigma$ is the dyadic model of $C_TL^2\cap L_T^\infty B^\sigma_{2,\infty}$ defined in~\eqref{eq:Xspace}.  They converge in $L^p(\Omega)$ in the corresponding operator norm.  Under the finite-state Galerkin stabilization hypothesis, the full cutoff sequence also converges pathwise on one probability-one event.  The same operator estimate applies to same-family Wick squares after complete Wick centering and order-two decoupling. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 11 of arXiv:2609.01473, 'Keller sequences of exact $\infty$-categories'] An extension-closed full inclusion $i\colon \cal{A} \hookrightarrow \cal{C}$ of exact categories is \emph{left-special} if for every projection $p\colon y \epi i(a)$ in $\cal{C}$ with $a \in \cal{A}$ there is a projection $q\colon b \epi a$ in $\cal{A}$ and a factorization $i(b) \to y \to i(a)$ of $i(q)$ through $p$.
Dually, $i\colon \cal{A} \hookrightarrow \cal{C}$ is \emph{right-special} if $i^{\op}$ 
is left-special. We say that $i$ is a \emph{Keller inclusion} if it is closed under retracts and both left and right-special.

body: [Proposition prop:conditional_law_of_strands of arXiv:2609.04140, 'The conformally invariant metric on $\CLE_4$ III:\\ uniqueness'] Suppose that we have the same setup as in Proposition~(prop:bi_chordal_sle_4_two_arm_exponent of the paper).  Let $E$ denote the event that $P_1$ and $P_2$ merge and that $P_3$ and $P_4$ merge,  in each case before either of the two curves in question reaches its continuation threshold. body: Tonelli's theorem needs BOTH measures sigma-finite and the integrand nonnegative and product-measurable; it then asserts that the double integral and both iterated integrals agree in [0, infinity], with no integrability assumption. Fubini's theorem needs both measures sigma-finite and f in L^1(mu tensor nu); it then asserts the same equality with all three quantities finite. Two failure modes are standard and are NOT the same failure. (1) Integrability dropped, sigma-finiteness kept: on (0,1)^2 with Lebesgue measure take f(x,y) = (x^2 - y^2)/(x^2 + y^2)^2. Since d/dy [ y/(x^2+y^2) ] = (x^2 - y^2)/(x^2+y^2)^2, the inner integral over y in (0,1) is 1/(1+x^2), so integrating in x afterwards gives pi/4; f is antisymmetric under swapping x and y, so the other order gives -pi/4. Both iterated integrals exist and are finite and they differ, so f cannot be in L^1 of the product. (2) sigma-finiteness dropped, nonnegativity kept: let mu be Lebesgue measure on [0,1], nu counting measure on [0,1], and f the indicator of the diagonal. Then integral over x of (integral over y of f dnu) dmu = integral 1 dmu = 1, while integral over y of (integral over x of f dmu) dnu = integral 0 dnu = 0. Tonelli's conclusion fails although f >= 0, because nu is not sigma-finite. A third, quieter caveat: for COMPLETE measure spaces the correct statement is that ALMOST every section is measurable, not every section, since a null set in the product can have non-measurable sections; the theorem for the completed product measure is stated that way. In practice the usable recipe is: apply Tonelli to |f| first to decide integrability, then apply Fubini to f. [standard; e.g. Folland, Real Analysis, 2nd ed., Theorems 2.37 and 2.39]

body:
[Thm 2 of arXiv:2606.21759, 'A Note On Gaussian Random Fields \& Underlying Markov Processes Through a Central Limit Th'] {(Universal Gaussian Random Field (UGRF) Limit)}

The sequence of space-time 
random fields $\{\mathcal{I}_n(\cdot,\cdot)\}_{n=1}^\infty$
converges in distribution to a space-time generalized
Brownian motion $\{B(f,t):f\in\mathcal{R}(A),t\ge 0\}$
with spatial covariance $C$ given by (\ref{rbcov})
in the sense that 
\begin{itemize}
\item For fixed $(f_1,\dots,f_m)\in\mathcal{R}(A)^m, m\ge 1$,
$(\mathcal{I}_n(f_1,\cdot),\dots,\mathcal{I}_n(f_m,\cdot)), n\ge 1$, converges weakly to $(B(f_1,\cdot),\dots,B(f_m,\cdot))\in C([0,\infty);\mathbb{R}^m)$,
\item For fixed but arbitrary 
 $t_1<\cdots<t_m, f_1,\cdots f_m\in\mathcal{R}(A), m\ge 1$, the $m$-dimensional random vector
 $(\mathcal{I}_n(f_1,t_1),\cdots,\mathcal{I}_n(f_m,t_m))\in\mathbb{R}^m$, 
converges in distribution to the Gaussian random vector $(B(f_1,t_1),\dots,B(f_m,t_m))$.

\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: A nonroot block carries incoming boundary signs W and private signs Q = (Q_1, ..., Q_q). The conditional entropy loss is L_{Q|W} = q - H(Q | W). Boundary-only forms are assigned to the parent; conditional defects then telescope down the recursive block tree. Notes: Telescoping is why a uniform rooted theorem would globalize with one absolute constant (p.8).

[Theorem thm: borne asymptotique r fini pour les caractères peu de points fixes of arXiv:2605.28770, 'Cutoff profiles for conjugacy invariant random walks on symmetric groups'] Let $r\geq 0$. For each $n\geq 1$, let $\sigma_n\in {\ensuremath{\mathfrak{S}}} _n$.
Assume that $f_1(\sigma_n) = o(\sqrt{n})$ and $f_2(\sigma_n) = o(n)$. Then as $n\to \infty$, uniformly over all $\lambda \vdash n$ such that $\lambda_1 = n-r$, we have
\begin{equation}
    \chi^{\lambda}(\sigma_n) = o_r(n^{-r/2}).
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Review the failure of perturbation theory and test a restricted version on a tree-like subgraph. Result: On the Bethe lattice a.c. spectrum is known (Klein; Aizenman-Warzel) because the self-consistent equation for the Green function has a stable solution; on Z^3 the corresponding equation is not closed. A known partial statement is that the rescaled disorder-averaged Wigner distribution evolves diffusively up to times lambda^{-2-kappa} for a small kappa > 0 (Erdos-Salmhofer-Yau), beyond the kinetic time scale lambda^{-2} but still finite, so it does not reach the infinite-time statement. I tested the possibility of transferring the tree result through a spanning tree of Z^3: the operator restricted to a spanning tree is not the operator on Z^3, and removing the edges changes the spectrum non-perturbatively, so no transfer. No result; the problem is recorded as attempted with the explicit obstruction that the only tools proving a.c. spectrum are tree-specific. Obstruction: Absence of a closed self-consistency equation on Z^3; kinetic-regime results stop at finite times.

body:
[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.06523, 'On the Gardner Transition in the Ising Pure $p$-Spin Glass II'] For every $p\geq3$, there are unique numbers
\[
 0<\beta_1^p<\beta_2^p<\infty
\]
such that the model is:
\begin{enumerate}
\item  RS, i.e. $\mu_\beta=\delta_0$ if and only if
      $0<\beta\leq\beta_1^p$.
\item   1-RSB, i.e. $\mu_\beta=m \delta_0 +(1-m)\delta_q$
      if and only if
      $ \beta_1^p<\beta\leq\beta_2^p.$
\item  FRSB if and only if $\beta>\beta_2^p$.  More precisely,  there are $0<q_\beta<q'_\beta<1$ such that
      $ \operatorname{supp}\mu_\beta=\{0\}\cup[q_\beta,q'_\beta]$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.06523

[Definition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given variables $f_1,f_2,f_3,\ldots\,$, we say that $f_n\to f$ in law when 
$$E(\varphi(f_n))\to E(\varphi(f))$$
for any continuous function $\varphi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$.

body: [Theorem 1 (Perron-Frobenius Perron (1907) of arXiv:2503.19927, 'Fully personalized PageRank and algebraic methods to distribute a random walker'] Let A ∈RN×N be a non-negative, irreducible square matrix. Then the following statements are true: 1. ρ(A) ∈σ(A) and its algebraic multiplicity is 1. 2. There exists a vector c ∈Rn with c > 0 such that it is an eigenvector of A associated to the eigenvalue ρ(A). 3. The eigenvector c is unique up to scaling. The eigenvector c is sometimes referred to as the Perron eigenvector of A.

body: [Prop critstab of arXiv:2608.25865, 'Instability of Böhm's Einstein metrics'] Let $g$ be an Einstein metric with an Einstein constant $\Lambda$. Then $g$ is stable if and only if $$\Delta_L\geqslant 2\Lambda.$$

[Definition 12 ($\ivgff$) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Fix $d=2$ and $\beta \in \R_{>0}$. For any domain $\Lambda$ and any $\zeta: \Z^2 \mapsto \Z$, the \emph{two-dimensional lattice integer-valued Gaussian free field} (2D IV-GFF) --- also known as \emph{discrete Gaussian model} --- on $\Lambda$ with boundary conditions $\zeta$ at inverse temperature $\beta$ is the probability measure on $\phi: \Z^2 \mapsto \Z$ given by 
\[ \mu^\zeta_{\ivgff, \Lambda, \beta} [\phi =f ]  = \frac{1}{Z_{\ivgff, \Lambda, \beta}^\zeta} \e^{- \beta H^\zeta_{\ivgff, \Lambda}(f)}, \]
where $Z^\zeta_{\ivgff, \Lambda, \beta}$ is the normalising constant and 
\[ H^\zeta_{\ivgff, \Lambda}(f) = \sum_{\substack{\{x,y\}\subset \Lambda \\ x \sim y}}(f_x - f_y)^2 + \sum_{\substack{x \in \Lambda, y \in \Lambda^c \\ x \sim y}}(f_x - \zeta_y)^2.  \]

[Lem average of gaussians of arXiv:2602.22342, 'Sum of Gaussian vectors and large sets'] Let $\Psi:\R^n\to \R^n$ be a Lipschitz map with Lipschitz constant at most $C_{\mathrm{Lip}}>0$, and let $G$ be a standard Gaussian random vector in $\R^n$.

Then there are two standard Gaussian random vectors $X,Y$ in $\R^n$ such that 
 $$\Psi(G)-\E[\Psi(G)]=C_{\mathrm{Lip}}\frac{X+Y}{2}.$$

[Corollary 90 (Low degrees, long hooks, and arbitrary depth) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] For every controlled critical entrance the following assertions hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item In degree three, the unique primitive sector
$\mathbf S_{(2,1)}H_{\mathbb C}$ has exact ancestry one.  Every nontrivial
flattening satisfies the universal $N^{-1}$ upper bound, and some labelled
native Hall coordinate $T$ satisfies $s_N(T)\sim C/N$ with $C>0$.
\item In degree four,
\[
 L_4(H_{\mathbb C})
 \cong\mathbf S_{(3,1)}H_{\mathbb C}
 \oplus\mathbf S_{(2,1,1)}H_{\mathbb C},
\]
and the two sectors have exact ancestries one and two.  Their universal upper
profiles are respectively
\[
 \frac1N,
 \qquad
 \frac{\log(e+N)}N.
\]
Each profile is attained, up to a positive asymptotic coefficient, by a
labelled native Hall coordinate.
\item For every $n\ge2$, the long-hook sector
$\mathbf S_{(n-1,1)}H_{\mathbb C}$ has exact ancestry one.  Its universal
critical upper profile is $N^{-1}$, and the native Hall family attains this
profile.
\item For every $r\ge1$, some partition $\lambda_r\vdash2r$ has exact
ancestry $r$; a native coordinate then satisfies
\[
 s_N(T)\sim C\frac{(\log N)^{r-1}}N,
 \qquad C>0.
\]
Thus finite-order critical depths are unbounded.
\end{enumerate}
Under a replicable natural grade-one source the same grades are minimax sharp
on arbitrarily long finite windows.  If the input area is little weak trace,
every upper membership improves to the corresponding little logarithmic
grade.

$$
\lim_{D\to\infty}\sup_{n\geq 1}\E\left[(\deg P_n^S)^m
\mathbf{1}_{{\deg P_n^S>D}}
\right]=\lim_{D\to\infty}
\sup_{n\geq 1}\E\left[
(\deg P_n^{\Haar,S})^m\mathbf{1}_{{\deg P_n^{\Haar,S}>D}}\right]=0.
$$
