body: [Corollary 15 (Law of Robustness for Infinite Function Classes) of arXiv:2603.02806, 'The Price of Robustness: Stable Classifiers Need Overpar'] Assume (H1) and (H3), and fix $\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1)$. Consider the $0$ - $1$ loss $\ell_{\text{0--1}}$. There exists an absolute constant $K>0$ such that, if 1. the minimal risk $R^{*}:=\inf_{f\in\mathcal{F}}R_{\text{0--1}}(f)$ satisfies $R^{*}\geq\varepsilon$, and 2. the sample size $n$ is large enough so that (i) $\tfrac{K}{\sqrt{n}}<\tfrac{\varepsilon}{3}$ and (ii) $\sqrt{\tfrac{2\log(2/\delta)}{n}}<\tfrac{\varepsilon}{2}$, then with probability at least $1-\delta$, for all $\tilde{\varepsilon}>0$, the following holds uniformly for all $g\in\mathcal{G}$ and $f_{g}=sgn\circ g$: $\hat{R}_{\text{0--1}}(f_{g})\leq R^{*}-\varepsilon\;\;\implies\;\;\frac{S^{*}(g)}{L(g)}<\max\left\{\frac{3K}{\varepsilon}\sqrt{\frac{p}{nd}}\sqrt{c\log\!\left(1+60WJ\tilde{\varepsilon}^{-1}\right)},\;\sqrt{\frac{8c}{d}\log\!\left(\frac{6K}{\varepsilon}\right)}\right\}.$

[Proposition prop:poisson_explicit of arXiv:2601.09976, 'Stochastic Calculus as Operator Factorization:\\ An Operator--Covariant Derivative and Uni'] For $\mathcal{F}_T^N$-measurable $F \in L^2(\Omega)$, the operator--covariant derivative is
\[
(D_{\tilde{N}} F)_t = \mathbb{E}[\mathcal{D}_t^+ F \mid \mathcal{F}_{t-}]
\]
$d t \otimes dP$-a.e., where $\mathcal{D}_t^+$ is the add-a-point operator~(equation eq:diff_op of the paper). In particular, $D_{\tilde{N}} F$ is the predictable projection of the discrete gradient. This identification is well known in the discrete Malliavin calculus~[Privault2009,DiNunno2009]; what is new here is not the operator itself, but its characterization as an instance of the general adjoint construction $D_X = \delta_X^*$.

[Prop generator_continuous_process of arXiv:2411.13964, 'Long-time analysis of a pair of on-lattice and continuous run-and-tumble particles with ja'] Let $\mathcal L$ be
  the generator of the continuous process. Its domain $D(\mathcal L)$
  is the set of bounded measurable functions
  $f : E_D \rightarrow \mathbb R$ such that
\begin{itemize}
\item for $\sigma \in \Sigma_+ \setminus \Sigma_-$ the function
  $f( \cdot, \sigma)$ is absolutely continuous on $[0, \ell)$ and
  $\lim_{x \rightarrow \ell} f(x, \sigma) =
  f\left(\ell,*_\sigma^\ell\right)$,
\item for $\sigma \in \Sigma_+ \setminus \Sigma_-$ the function
  $f(\cdot, \sigma)$ is absolutely continuous on $(0, \ell]$ and
  $\lim_{x \rightarrow 0} f(x, \sigma) = f\left(0, *_\sigma^0\right)$.
\end{itemize}

For $f \in D(\mathcal L)$ one has that
\begin{itemize}
\item in the bulk $\cup_{\sigma \in \Sigma} E_\sigma$ the generator
  comprises a transport term and a jump term
\begin{align*}
\mathcal L f(x, (\sigma^1, \sigma^2)) = &\underbrace{(\sigma^2 - \sigma^1) \partial_x f(x, (\sigma^1, \sigma^2))}_{\text{\normalfont transport term}} \\
&\quad + \underbrace{\lambda(x,\nu) \int_{E_D} \left(f(\tilde x, \tilde \nu) - f(x, (\sigma^1, \sigma^2))\right) dQ\left((x, (\sigma^1, \sigma^2)); (\tilde x, \tilde \nu)\right)}_{\text{\normalfont jump term}},
\end{align*}
\item whereas for boundary states
  $(x, \nu) \in \cup_{\nu \in \partial K} E_\nu$ the generator is
  given only by the jump term
$$
\mathcal L f(x, \nu) = \lambda(x, \nu) \int_{E_D} \left(f(\tilde x, \tilde
  \nu) - f(x, \nu)\right) dQ((x, \nu); (\tilde x, \tilde \nu))
$$
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: For a weighted sum S = sum a_i x_i of independent Rademacher signs with all |a_i| >= 1, the probability that S lands in any interval of length 2 is at most C n^{-1/2} (Erdos's sharpening via Sperner's theorem: for an open or half-open interval of length 2 the sharp bound is the middle binomial coefficient over 2^n; a closed interval of length 2 can carry more, e.g. n = 2, a = (1, 1) and [0, 2] has probability 3/4). Inverse Littlewood-Offord theory (Tao-Vu, Nguyen-Vu) characterizes when the concentration probability is large - the weights must have rich additive structure (generalized arithmetic progressions) - and powers the least-singular-value and universality results for discrete random matrices.

[Theorem 1 (Main a priori estimate) of arXiv:2608.29726, '\LARGE A Priori Estimates for Singular Fractional Stochastic Burgers Equations'] Let \((\alpha,\gamma)\) satisfy
\eqref{eq:admissible-alpha-gamma}, fix \(T>0\), and let \(m\) be a smooth
transformed solution on \([0,T]\), associated with a smooth enhancement in
the class of \Cref{prop:fractional-enhancement} and obtained through the
Da Prato--Debussche, linear response, and Zvonkin transformations of
\Cref{sec:enhanced-zvonkin}.  Initialize all stochastic coordinates at zero
and assume that \(m(0)=u_0\in C^\infty(\T)\).  Then
\[
 \norm m_{L^\infty(0,T;L^1)}
 {}+\norm m_{L^\infty(0,T;L^2)}
 {}+\norm m_{L^2(0,T;H^{\gamma/2})}
 {}+\norm m_{L^3(0,T;B^s_{3,3})}
\le C_{T,s}
\]
for every \(0<s<1/3\).  At \(\gamma=2\), the Besov term may be taken with
any \(0<s<1/2\).  The constant depends locally uniformly on \(T\), \(s\),
\(\norm{u_0}_{L^2}\), the enhanced-model norm, the uniform norm of the resolvent family,
and the resulting coefficient and Zvonkin norms.  If the resolvent parameter is
selected locally uniformly as in \Cref{prop:zvonkin}, the bound is therefore
uniform over bounded families of enhanced inputs.

[Theorem 12 (Jacobian master identity) of arXiv:2605.26107, 'Radial Extremality for LRU Caching and the Fill--Holst Conjecture'] Let $N\ge2$, $1\le C<N$, and let $q\in\Delta_N^\circ$ be nonuniform.  Put
$\lambda(\theta)=u+\theta(q-u)$ and
$\mathcal H(\theta)=H_C(\lambda(\theta))$.  Then, for $0<\theta\le1$,
\begin{equation}
        \mathcal H'(\theta)
        =
        \frac{1}{\theta}\left(H_C(\lambda(\theta))-\frac{C}{N}\right)
        +
        \frac{1}{N\theta}
        \sum_{1\le i<k\le N}
        G_{ik}(\lambda(\theta))
        (\lambda_i(\theta)-\lambda_k(\theta))^2.
\end{equation}
In particular $\mathcal H'(\theta)>0$ for $0<\theta\le1$.

[Lem properties_of_the_discrete_continuous_coupling of arXiv:2411.13964, 'Long-time analysis of a pair of on-lattice and continuous run-and-tumble particles with ja'] Let $X$ and the sequence of stochastic processes $(Y^L)_{L \ge 2}$ be
  as in definition~(def:discrete_continuous_coupling of the paper).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] Each $Y^L$ is a DITP (resp. DFTP).
\item[(ii)] Let $0 = T_0 < T_1 < \cdots$ be the jump times of the
  couple $(\sigma^1, \sigma^2)$. For all $t \ge 0$ one has
\begin{align*}
\left| i_L(y^L(t)) - x(t) \right| \le &\left| i_L(y^L(0)) - x(0) \right| + \frac{1}{\gamma_L} \sum_{k = 1}^{n(t)} \left| D_k(t) \right|
\end{align*}
where $n(t) = 1 + \sum_{k = 1}^{+\infty} 1_{\{T_k \le t\}}$ and
$$
D_k(t) = \sum_{i = 1, 2} (-1)^i \sigma^i(T_{k-1}) \Big[ N_i^L(T_k \wedge t) - N_i^L(T_{k-1} \wedge t) - \gamma_L \left( T_k \wedge t - T_{k-1} \wedge t \right)\Big].
$$
\end{itemize}

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] We have the following formula,
$$\sqrt{1+t}=1-2\sum_{k=1}^\infty C_{k-1}\left(\frac{-t}{4}\right)^k$$
with $C_k=\frac{1}{k+1}\binom{2k}{k}$ being the Catalan numbers. Also, we have
$$\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+t}}=\sum_{k=0}^\infty D_k\left(\frac{-t}{4}\right)^k$$
with $D_k=\binom{2k}{k}$ being the central binomial coefficients.

[Lemma 14 (Interpolation bounds for the cubic Besov functional) of arXiv:2608.29726, '\LARGE A Priori Estimates for Singular Fractional Stochastic Burgers Equations'] Let \(1<\gamma\le2\), \(1-\gamma/2<\beta<1\), and let \(m\) be smooth
with \(\sup_{t\le T}\norm{m(t)}_{L^1}\le M\).
Let \(E_T\) and \(Z_T^\beta\) be as in
\Cref{prop:energy-cubic}.  For every \(\varepsilon>0\), the following
bounds hold with a finite constant \(C_\varepsilon\), whose value may
change from line to line and may depend on \(T,M,\gamma,\beta\), but not on
\(m\).
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=*]
\item If \(\beta>2-\gamma\), then
 \begin{equation}
 Z_T^\beta
 \le\varepsilon E_T+C_\varepsilon.

\item If \(1<\gamma<2\) and
\(1-\gamma/2<\beta\le2-\gamma\), then there exists
\(s_0\in(1/12,1/3)\), depending only on
\(\gamma\) and \(\beta\), such that
 \begin{equation}
 Z_T^\beta
 \le\varepsilon\bigl(E_T+K_T^{s_0}\bigr)
 +C_\varepsilon.
 \end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

body:
Nam-Fonseca-Lee-Mingard-Louis Lemma1: exact balanced gradient-flow skill dynamics. Use the finite fixed-basis noiseless model in the companion definition, with f(i,x)=sum_{k=1}^N a_k*b_k*g_k(i,x), target amplitude S>0 and 1<=N<=n_s. Fix D>=1 training examples and let d_k be the number whose task is k, so sum_{k=1}^{n_s} d_k=D. The source samples them iid from its task/bit distribution; the identity below holds conditional on any realized sample. Run continuous-time gradient flow with eta>0 on empirical half squared loss L_D=(1/(2D))*(sum_{k<=N} d_k*(S-a_k*b_k)^2+sum_{k>N} d_k*S^2). For each represented k assume a_k(0)=b_k(0) and 0<R_k(0)=a_k(0)*b_k(0)<S. Then for every T>=0, a_k(T)=b_k(T), R_k(T)=a_k(T)*b_k(T)=S/[1+(S/R_k(0)-1)*exp(-2*eta*S*(d_k/D)*T)], and L_k(T)=(S-R_k(T))^2/2. In particular d_k=0 leaves R_k constant; d_k>0 gives R_k(T) increasing to S. Omitted skills k>N retain conditional loss S^2/2. This is a continuous gradient-flow identity for trainable scalar factors of fixed skill functions, not a convergence theorem for feature learning or finite-step stochastic gradient descent. Without balance the scalar product derivative is eta*(d_k/D)*(a_k^2+b_k^2)*(S-a_k*b_k), which does not generally reduce to the displayed logistic equation.
Same fixed-basis model and empirical half squared loss; D>=1 and eta>0.
Equal scalar factors at initialization with product strictly between zero and S; continuous gradient flow.

body:
[Theorem T:Markov-process of arXiv:2604.10020, 'The directed landscape in half-space'] For $\rho \in \mathbb{R} \cup \{-\infty\}$, take any half-space pre-landscape $\mathcal{M}^\rho$, continuously extended to $\mathbb{H}^2_\uparrow$.
 Consider a function $f \in \operatorname{UC}_{0,+}$.
For each $t > 0$, define the process
$\mathfrak{h}^\rho_t f = f \diamond \mathcal{M}^\rho_{0, t}$, and set $\mathfrak{h}^\rho_0 f = f$.
Then $(\mathfrak{h}^\rho_t, t \ge 0)$ is a time-homogeneous Markov process on $\operatorname{UC}_{0,+}$, whose law does not depend on the choice of pre-landscape. Moreover, for almost surely $\mathcal{M}^\rho$, $(t,f)\mapsto \mathfrak{h}^\rho_tf$ is continuous on $\operatorname{UC}_{0,+}$, and $\mathfrak{h}^\rho_t f$ is a continuous function for each $t > 0, f \in \operatorname{UC}_{0,+}$. Lastly, for any finite set $Y \subset \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}, t > 0$ and any function $f \in \operatorname{UC}_{0,+}$  satisfying
\begin{equation}
    
    \limsup_{x \to \infty}\frac{f(x)}{x} < \infty,
\end{equation}
the marginal
$
(\mathfrak{h}^\rho_t f(y) : y \in Y)
$
is given by Theorem (T:half-space-fixed-point of the paper). 
The Markov process $(\mathfrak{h}^\rho_t, t \ge 0)$ is the \textbf{KPZ fixed point in half-space} with parameter $\rho$.

body:
Let $x_1,\dots,x_N$ be random points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose joint law is invariant under reflection of any subset of them through the origin, and which are almost surely in general position. Then the probability that all of them lie in a single open halfspace whose boundary contains the origin, equivalently the probability that the origin is not in their convex hull, equals $2^{-N+1}\sum_{k=0}^{d-1}\binom{N-1}{k}$. In particular this probability is $1$ whenever $N \le d$. Note that symmetry alone does not suffice: general position is needed, since for instance two points i.i.d. uniform on $\{\pm e_1\} \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ are symmetric yet give probability $0$.
the joint law of the points is invariant under reflection of any subset through the origin
the points are almost surely in general position (every d or fewer are linearly independent)
independence of the points is not required

body: [Lem Lemma: Measurable selection subnilmanifolds of arXiv:2605.16921, '${\ASL_n}(\mathbb Z)$ invariant random subsets of $\mathbb Z^n$'] Let $N/\Gamma$ be a nilmanifold and let $S$ be a standard Borel space. Let $\omega \mapsto \eta_\omega$ be a Borel map from $S$ into the space of Haar measures on subnilmanifolds of $N/\Gamma$, equipped with the weak-$*$ topology. Then there exist Borel maps $u: S \to N$ and $H: S \to \mathcal{H}$, where $\mathcal{H}$ denotes the (countable) set of rational subgroups of $N$, such that for every $\omega \in S$, $u(\omega)^* \eta_\omega$ is the Haar measure on $H(\omega) \cdot \overline{e}$.

body:
[Theorem 2 (Exact supercritical second moment) of arXiv:2604.05760, '\bfseries The volume of hyperbolic Poisson zero cells:\\ critical divergence and exact sec'] Consider a hyperbolic Poisson hyperplane tessellation in $\HH^d$ with intensity $\gamma > \gamma_c^{(d)}$. The second moment of the volume of the zero cell is given by
\[
\EE\cH^d(Z_o)^2\!
=\! \frac{\gamma^3 \pi^{d-2}}{32} \Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2\!\!
G_{10, 10}^{5, 5} \left(
1 \middle| \begin{matrix}
	1-a,\,1-a,\,1-a,\,\frac{5-d}{4},\,\frac{3-d}{4},\,a+\frac{d+1}{2},\,a+\frac{d+1}{2},\,a+\frac{d+1}{2},\,0,\,\frac{1}{2} \\
	a,\,a,\,a,\,\frac{d-1}{4},\,\frac{d+1}{4},\,\frac{1-d}{2}-a,\,\frac{1-d}{2}-a,\,\frac{1-d}{2}-a,\,1,\,\frac{1}{2}
\end{matrix}
\right)\!,
\]
where $a = \frac{1}{4} \big( \frac{\gamma}{\sqrt{\pi}} \frac{\Gamma\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)}{\Gamma\left(\frac{d+1}{2}\right)} - d + 1 \big)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Exact supercritical second moment

body:
[Proposition 2 of arXiv:2608.27634, 'Curvature-Aware Radius Shrinkage for Adaptive Nearest Neighbor Classification'] Let $x_{(1)}, x_{(2)}, \dots, x_{(k_{\mathrm{base}})}$ denote the
	$k_{\mathrm{base}}$ nearest training neighbors of $x$, sorted by increasing
	distance $d(x, x_{(1)}) \le d(x, x_{(2)}) \le \dots \le d(x,
	x_{(k_{\mathrm{base}})})$, and let $r^{(0)}(x) = d(x, x_{(k_{\mathrm{base}})})$
	be the reference radius of Eq.~(3). Then restricting the voting set to the
	$k(x)$ closest neighbors, as in Eq.~\eqref{eq:ki}, is equivalent to voting
	within the closed metric ball of radius
	\begin{equation}
		r(x) = d\big(x, x_{(k(x))}\big) \le r^{(0)}(x),
		
	\end{equation}
	i.e., $\{x_{(1)}, \dots, x_{(k(x))}\} = B(x, r(x)) \cap \mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{train}}$
	(up to distance ties), with $r(x) = r^{(0)}(x)$ exactly when $k(x) =
	k_{\mathrm{base}}$ (i.e., $s(x) = 1$).

Let $Y=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m)$ be any centered Gaussian vector with covariance
matrix $S$, and let $Z_1,\ldots,Z_m$ be independent standard Gaussian random
variables.  Then
\[
  \max_iY_i\stackrel{d}{=}\max_iZ_i
  \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
  S=I_m.
\]

[Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.30178, '2608.30178'] Assume that the model $(X, Y)$ in \eqref{eq:noimm-system} is
source-conservative.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item If \(r_1\ge0\), then \(\Pp_{x,y}(\tauX<\infty)=0\).
\item If \(r_2\ge0\) and \(\theta_2\ge1\), then
\(\Pp_{x,y}(\tauY<\infty)=0\).
\item If \(0\le\theta_2<1\), then
\beqlb 
 a_2(1-\theta_2)\E_{x,y}\int_0^{\tau_0}X_s^{\kappa_2}\dd s
 =a_2(1-\theta_2)\E_{x,y}\int_0^{\tauY}X_s^{\kappa_2}\dd s \le y^{1-\theta_2}.
\eeqlb
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 \left\{\int_0^\infty X_s^{\kappa_2}\dd s=\infty\right\}
 \subseteq\{\tauY<\infty\}
 \qquad\text{almost surely}.
 
\end{equation}
Moreover, for every \(T,L>0\),
\beqnn
 \Pp_{x,y}\left(
 \tauY>T,
 \ \int_0^T X_s^{\kappa_2}\dd s\ge L
 \right)
 \le\frac{y^{1-\theta_2}}{a_2(1-\theta_2)L}.
 \eeqnn
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 3 of arXiv:2608.30178

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2506.15736, 'Coming down from infinity for coordinated particle systems'] Suppose that a coordinated particle system $(X(t))_{t \geq 0}$ on a finite set of sites $V$ with no reproduction. Suppose $(X(t))_{t \geq 0}$ stays infinite. Then the following three conditions must be met.

    \begin{enumerate}
        \item[(a)] There exists a site $v_1 \in V$ with $X_{v_1}(0) = \infty$.
        
        \item[(b)] There exists a site $v_k \in V$ such that the $\Lambda_{v_k}$-coalescent does not come down from infinity. 

        \item[(c)] There exist sites $v_2, \ldots, v_{k-1}$ such that for every $i = 1, \ldots, k-1$ either $M_{v_iv_{i+1}}(dz)$ or $R_{v_iv_{i+1}}(dz)$ is $\Lambda_{v_i}$-strong.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition 44 (Uniform lifted linear Schauder estimate) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Fix \(m\geq2\) and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\).  Let \(s(t)\), \(a\leq t\leq b\),
be a Ricci flow satisfying \(\PBG_m(s;\Lambda;[a,b])\) for some \(\Lambda\geq1\).
Let \(E\) be a fixed finite-rank tensor bundle and consider,
on the universal cover and in the charts of
Lemma~\ref{lem:uniform-parabolic-atlas}, a system
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal P U
 =\partial_tU-a^{ij}\nabla_i\nabla_jU-B^i\nabla_iU-CU=F.
\end{equation}
Assume that the second-order part is diagonal in the bundle components and
uses the same coefficient matrix \(a^{ij}\) on every component.  For fixed
constants \(0<\lambda_-\leq\lambda_+<\infty\), suppose that
\[
 \lambda_- s^{ij}\xi_i\xi_j\leq a^{ij}\xi_i\xi_j
 \leq\lambda_+ s^{ij}\xi_i\xi_j,
\]
and that the local
\(C^{m-2+\sigma,(m-2+\sigma)/2}\)-norms of \(a,B,C\) are bounded by
\(A_0\).

Every smooth bounded solution on the universal cover satisfies, for
\(\theta>0\) with \(a+\theta\leq b\),
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 \|U\|_{C^{m+\sigma,(m+\sigma)/2}_{\mathrm{uloc}}
          (\widetilde M\times[a+\theta,b],s)}
 \leq C_\theta\bigl(&
       \|U\|_{C^0(\widetilde M\times[a,b],s)}\\
       &+\|F\|_{C^{m-2+\sigma,(m-2+\sigma)/2}_{\mathrm{uloc}}}\bigr).
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
For the global estimate, assume in addition that \(\mathcal P\) is
deck-invariant, equivalently that the coefficient fields \(a,B,C\) descend to
\(M\).  If \(U\) and \(F\) are deck-invariant and descend to tensors \(u\)
and \(f\) on \(M\), with \(u(a)\in C^{m,\sigma}\) and
\(f\in Y_s^m[a,b]\), then
\begin{equation}
 \|u\|_{X_s^m[a,b]}
 \leq C\left(
      \|u(a)\|_{C^{m,\sigma}(M,s(a))}
      +\|f\|_{Y_s^m[a,b]}\right).
\end{equation}
The constants depend only on
\(m,\sigma,\Lambda,\lambda_-,\lambda_+,A_0\), on \(\theta\) in the interior
estimate, and on an upper bound for \(b-a\).  The interior and initial-face
estimates are based, respectively, on Lieberman's interior Schauder theorem
\cite[Theorem~4.9, p.~59]{Lieberman} and his Cauchy--Dirichlet Schauder theorem
\cite[Theorem~4.28, p.~77]{Lieberman}.  All atlas-radius, overlap, and cutoff
constants, fixed-coordinate ellipticity constants, localized initial-face
boundary-chart constants, and coefficient H\"older constants are uniform over
the admissible family specified by \(\PBG_m\) and the displayed bounds.  In
particular, the constants are independent of collapse of the compact quotient.

The transductive covariance-penalty criterion of the label-free blend selects by the cross-validated relative squared loss, while the pools score by the mean per-row ratio. On the benchmark corpora the two orderings part on pkanrtm (24,000 calibration rows, a near-zero-target tail): the squared-loss criterion picks the simplex, the worst vertex, on every cell. The same criterion written in the score's own metric, R_1(w) = mean_i sqrt(max(r_i + delta(w), 0)), repairs it. Measured 2026-09-06: P39 (a) REFUTED: the ratio-metric blend vs the best vertex on pkanrtm = -0.93 (within 0.3); (b) REFUTED: vs the registered blend on the other corpora = advection -0.02, darcy +0.40, burgers -1.74 (within 0.2); (c) HELD: it beats least squares on 48 of 55 cells (87 pct); falsifier (worse than the registered blend by more than 0.3 on any corpus, or worse than the best vertex on pkanrtm by more than 1.0) TRIGGERED. On the pools the blend was built on (EMIT, OCO-2, both splits): P40 (a) HELD: the R_1 blend vs the registered blend = B-emit +0.48, B-oco +0.14, C-emit +1.52, C-oco +0.16 (within 0.2); (b) HELD: wins over least squares R_1 vs registered = B-emit 38/39, B-oco 30/30, C-emit 40/36, C-oco 30/30 (at least the registered count less three); (c) REFUTED: the two selections coincide on B-emit 3 of 40, B-oco 0 of 30, C-emit 0 of 40, C-oco 0 of 30 cells (at least half); falsifier (R_1 worse than the registered blend by more than 0.3 on either corpus on either split) not triggered. P43: the metric on the third family, fresh split (P43): P43 (a) HELD: on the fresh split the registered blend reads -46.02 vs the best vertex on pkanrtm (the P38 falsifier fires again); (b) REFUTED: the R_1 blend vs the best vertex = advection -0.02, darcy +0.80, burgers -0.98, pkanrtm -0.28 (within 0.3 everywhere); (c) HELD: R_1 vs the registered blend on the other three = advection -0.02, darcy +0.56, burgers -0.13 (within 0.2); (d) HELD: the simplex-vs-least-squares signs by corpus match the first split; falsifier (R_1 worse than the best vertex by more than 1.0 on any corpus) not triggered.
the score is the mean per-row ratio ||e|| / max(||y||, floor); the criterion's cross-validated loss is the mean squared ratio; the transductive variance shift delta(w) = V_ev(w) - V_cal(w) is estimated by the pairs bootstrap of the fitted predictor at both row sets
measured on the benchmark corpora (advection, Darcy at four betas, Burgers at four viscosities, pkanrtm and pkanrtm-lowfi) with the three vertices simplex / least squares / pool heuristic and the 0.1 barycentric grid; the EMIT / OCO-2 check is P40

Write rho_i = ||f(x_i) - y_i|| / m_i for the per-row ratio. Then S = mean rho_i and Q = mean rho_i^2 = (mean rho_i)^2 + var(rho_i). Two estimators f and g with the same S can differ in Q by the difference of their ratio variances, and an estimator with the smaller Q can have the larger S whenever its ratios are less dispersed but larger on average - the ordering by Q is the ordering by S only when the ratio dispersion is comparable across candidates. [Lemma lem:truncated-var-damage of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] Let $Q_{t^*,D}$ be the inner matrix with inner truncation parameter $D$ and termination at iteration level $t^*$; we have
\[
 \mathrm{Var}(Q_{t^*,D} ) = \frac{\gamma}{1-\gamma}\left( 1 - \varepsilon_{D,t^*} \right).
\]
for \[ 
\varepsilon_{D,t^*} = O( \frac{1}{(t^*)^2} + \frac{1}{D^2})\,\,.
\]
Notice this quantity is $1-o_{D,t^*}(1)$ at the threshold $\gamma=1/2$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Truncated Variance is still almost $1$ (Lemma~D.11 of \cite{PotechinXu2026Theta})

body: [Lem count-long-edges of arXiv:2411.14336, 'Finding the root in random nearest neighbor trees'] This algorithm satisfies the property that, for all $\varepsilon > 0$ sufficiently small and all $n \in \mathbf{N}$, $\mathbf{P} \{ 1 \in H(\varepsilon,n)\} \geq 1 - \varepsilon \text{ and } |H(\varepsilon,n)| \leq {2^{d}}/{\varepsilon}$. The algorithm runs in $O(n)$ time. Furthermore, there exists $c > 0$ such that with probability at least $1 - \varepsilon$, $|H(\varepsilon,n)| \subseteq \{1, \dots, \tau\}$ for $\tau = \exp(cd)\cdot (1/\varepsilon)\log(1/\varepsilon)$.

    The first edge added to the graph is long with probability $1 - B_d(\ell) = 1 - \varepsilon$.

for which one has the estimate uniform over $t\in (0,1]$ and $N\ge 1$: $$\sup_{a\in \mathbb R^d} | (\mathfrak m_N, G_t(a-\bullet))_{L^2(\mathbb R^d)} | \leq C(t\vee N^{-1})^{\e-1}$$ for some $\e>0$. Here $G_t(x) = (2\pi t)^{-d/2} e^{-|x|^2/2t}$ is the $d$-dimensional heat kernel.

[Lemma lem:singularinvariance2 of arXiv:2608.30973, 'Pseudo-Anosov flow and dynamics on guts'] Let \(T\) be a ladderpole tube.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If more than one components of \(F_{\tau}\cap T\) meet \(v_{i}\), then between two adjacent components, a product annulus connects them near \(v_{i}\).
\item If \(v_{i}\) and \(v_{i+1}\) have opposite coorientation, then there is an edge connecting \(v_{i}\) and \(v_{i+1}\).
\item If \(v_{i}\) and \(v_{i+1}\) have same coorientation, then no edge connects \(v_{i}\) and \(v_{i+1}\).

\end{enumerate}

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2608.29427, '\small Positive mass and rigidity \\ for asymptotically flat tangent bundles'] Let $(M,g)$ be a contractible AF manifold. Suppose that $g$ is weakly trace-majorizing, has decay rate
	\[
	\sigma\geq n-2,
	\]
	and has nonnegative integrable scalar curvature. Let $\widetilde g$ be an admissible metric on $TM$. Then the connecting metric $\mathdutchcal g$ is flat and
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item[\small \textbf{\textsf{(a)}}] \emph{\small \textsf{\textbf{Positivity of mass.}}}
		\[
		0\leq
		\underline{\m}(TM,\widetilde g,\zeta)
		\leq
		\overline{\m}(TM,\widetilde g,\zeta)
		<\infty,
		\]
		for any set of preffered coordinates $\zeta$.
		If, in addition, $g$ is weakly trace-rigid, then the ADM mass of $\left(TM, \widetilde g\right)$ in the preffered coordinates exist and
		\[
		 \m(TM,\widetilde g, \zeta) =
		\frac{(n-1)\omega_{n-1}}
		{(2n-1)\omega_{2n-1}}
		\m(M,g).
		\]
		\item[\small \textbf{\textsf{(b)}}] \emph{\small \textsf{\textbf{Rigidity.}}}
		If in a set of preferred coordinates,
		\[
		\underline{\m}(TM,\widetilde g,\zeta)=0,
		\]
		then
		\[
		(M,g)\cong_{\mathrm{isom}}(\mathbb R^n,\delta).
		\]
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

For a measurable f on a measure space (X, Sigma, mu), the distribution function is d_f(t) = mu({x : |f(x)| > t}) for t > 0; it is nonincreasing and right-continuous. For 0 < p < infinity the weak L^p quasi-norm is ||f||_{L^{p,infinity}} = sup_{t>0} t * d_f(t)^{1/p}, and weak L^p = L^{p,infinity}(mu) is the set of (a.e.-classes of) measurable f with this quantity finite; by convention L^{infinity,infinity} = L^infinity. It is a quasi-norm: ||f+g||_{L^{p,infinity}} <= max(2, 2^{1/p}) (||f||_{L^{p,infinity}} + ||g||_{L^{p,infinity}}), from d_{f+g}(t) <= d_f(t/2) + d_g(t/2). Chebyshev's inequality gives L^p contained in L^{p,infinity} with ||f||_{L^{p,infinity}} <= ||f||_p, and the inclusion is strict in general: on R^n, |x|^{-n/p} lies in L^{p,infinity} but not in L^p. For 1 < p < infinity, L^{p,infinity} admits an equivalent norm; L^{1,infinity}(R^n) admits none.

[Theorem thm:extremal of arXiv:2608.11931, '\texorpdfstring{Nonlinear parabolic characterizations of stochastic completeness at infini'] Let $u_0\in\ell^\infty(X)$.  Choose constants
\[
    A\le \min\{0,\inf_X u_0\}
    \qquad \text{and} \qquad
    B\ge \max\{0,\sup_X u_0\}.
\]
Then, there exist global bounded pointwise solutions $u^A,u^B$ of
the (eq:GPME of the paper) with initial datum $u_0$ satisfying
\[
    A\le u^A\le u^B\le B
    \qquad\text{on }[0,\infty)\times X.
\]
For every $T>0$, the restriction of $u^A$ to $[0,T]\times X$ is minimal
among all bounded pointwise solutions on that time interval lying above $A$
while the restriction of $u^B$ is maximal among all bounded pointwise
solutions lying below $B$.  In particular, if $v$ is any bounded pointwise
solution on $[0,T]\times X$ with $A\le v\le B$, then
\begin{equation}
    u^A\le v\le u^B
    \qquad\text{on }[0,T]\times X.
\end{equation}
If $u_0\ge0$, the choice $A=0$ gives a global minimal positive solution $u^0$
satisfying
\[
    0\le u^0(t,x)\le \|u_0\|_\infty
    \qquad\text{on }[0,\infty)\times X.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 23 of arXiv:2603.27433, 'The $k$-cycle shuffling with repeated cards'] Let $(n_N)_{N\ge 1},(m_N)_{N\ge 1},(l_N)_{N\ge 1},(k_N)_{N\ge 1}$, and $(t_N)_{N\ge 1}$ be sequences of positive integers that satisfy the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $n_N=m_N\cdot l_N$ for all $N\ge 1$.
\item $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}l_N=\infty$, but $\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}\frac{l_N}{\log n_N}=0$.
\item $k_N\ge 2$ for all $N\ge 1$, and $\limsup_{N\rightarrow\infty}\log n_N k_N\le c_0$, where $c_0\in[0,1)$ is an absolute constant.
\item $t_N=\frac{n_N}{k_N}(\log n_N-\frac 12\log l_N+c)$ for all $N\ge 1$, where $c\in\R$ is an absolute constant.
\end{enumerate}
Then, we have
$$\lim_{N\rightarrow\infty}d_{TV}(\sim_{l_N}\backslash P_{n_N,k_N}^{*t_N},\sim_{l_N}\backslash U_{\S_{n_N}})=2\Phi(\exp(-c)/2)-1.$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: In the mathematics of chaos theory, a horseshoe map is any member of a class of chaotic maps of the square into itself. It is a core example in the study of dynamical systems. The map was introduced by Stephen Smale while studying the behavior of the orbits of the van der Pol oscillator. The action of the map is defined geometrically by squishing the square, then stretching the result into a long strip, and finally folding the strip into the shape of a horseshoe.
title: Horseshoe map

body:
[Lemm 17 of arXiv:2609.01105, 'Obstruction to quasi-invariance of Gaussian measures under transport flows on Riemannian M'] Let $(M,g)$ be a smooth boundaryless complete Riemannian manifold. Assume that the flow $X_{t,t_0}$ of a vector field $u \in L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R},\mathcal{C}^{1,\varepsilon}(M))$, as defined in \eqref{eq:defX}, satisfies the following property: for all $t_0 \in \Rr$ and all $x \in M$ there exists $\delta=\delta(t_0,x)>0$ such that for all $t\in \Rr $ satisfying $|t-t_0|\leq \delta$, 
\[
    \Jac X_{t,t_0}(x) : (T_xM,g(x)) \longrightarrow (T_{X_{t,t_0}(x)}M,g(X_{t,t_0}(x)))
\]
is an isometry. 
Then, for almost every $t$, the vector field $u(t)$ is a Killing field, namely: 
\[
    	\nabla_i u_j(t)+\nabla_j u_i(t) = 0.
\]
Conversely, if for almost all~\(t\), we have 
\[
    	\nabla_i u_j(t)+\nabla_j u_i(t) = 0,
\]
then for all~\(t\in \Rr\) and all~\(x\in M\), we have that~\(\Jac X_t (x)\) is an isometry.

A finite irreducible Markov-modulated Poisson process can have time-stationary forward-wait SCV below one, although its event-stationary interarrival SCV is at least one. On a unit-rate directed n-cycle with uniform stationary phase, arrival rate h>0 at one phase and zero at all others, m=E[X]=(n-1)/2+n/h and SCV(X)=1-(n-1)(n-5)/(6*m*m). Hence SCV(X)<1 for n>=6. For n=6,h=100 it equals 21451/24576. With rates (100,1/1000,1/1000,1/1000,1/1000,1/1000), exact arithmetic gives about0.8740277570. Across all finite irreducible MMPPs with nonzero nonnegative arrival rates the infimum of time-stationary SCV is1/3. This is a mathematical derivation with novelty unverified; it refutes the time-stationary proposal in He2021 section4.3, not his proved event-stationary theorem.
Q is a finite irreducible continuous-time Markov generator
D is a nonzero nonnegative diagonal arrival-rate matrix
Time-stationary initial phase is pi; event-stationary initial phase is pi D/(pi D 1)

\[

For the regularized Gaussian/ReLU reciprocal-angle transition, fixed K>0, bounded C5 tests with bounded derivatives, sufficiently small fixed theta_star>0 and theta=1/(nu)<=theta_star, 0<u<=K, the complete C032 operators A,B obey |n(P_n f-f)-Af-Bf/n| <= C_K[(u+sqrt(u))/n^(3/2)+(1+1/u+1/u^2)/n^2+n exp(-cn)]. The same bound holds for the exact killed kernel with bounded cemetery test value. The permitted u interval extends down to 1/(n theta_star). Independent Gaussian rows, zero-bias ReLU, width n sufficiently large; A=(2u+a)D+u^2 D^2 and B=(10u+6a/5+b/u)D+(11u^2+12au/5+a^2/2)D^2+(4u^3+au^2)D^3+(u^4/2)D^4, a=1/(3pi), b=1/(6pi^2); regularization is C032 normalized-Gram self-loop off a small concentration box. Construction: use n iid rows (x,y)=(max(g,0),max(cos(theta)g+sin(theta)h,0)), g,h independent standard Gaussians. The output angle is the angle between the two n-vectors; kill if either norm or the angle is zero. For regularization, self-loop when the sample averages of (x^2+y^2,(x-y)^2/theta^2,(x^2-y^2)/theta) leave a sufficiently small fixed box about their population mean. on n and tends to zero. The bound becomes large near that endpoint; this

## Proof: retain the factors lost in compact notation

Use C032's normalized row coordinates Z_theta, means mu_theta and fixed
concentration box, with T_theta the reciprocal angle multiplier. All
coordinate derivatives of T_theta through order five are bounded there,
uniformly for 0<=theta<=theta_*. The same is true of the smooth coefficients
in its theta expansion T_theta=T0+theta^2 H+O(theta^4).

Each nonzero coordinate derivative of Phi_theta(z)=f(uT_theta(z)) has at
least one factor u. The remaining powers of u are bounded using u<=K.
Consequently each of its derivatives of orders one through five is bounded
by C_K u, not merely by an unspecified compact constant. The fifth-order
Taylor remainder for the sample average is at most C_K u n^(-5/2).
Polynomial terms deleted outside the concentration box have exponentially
small expectations, by uniform normalized Gaussian moments and Holder;
bounded transition terms have error at most C exp(-cn). After multiplying
by n these errors are bounded by C[u n^(-3/2)+n exp(-cn)].

deterministic, covariance and higher centered-moment terms, is

    n(P_n f-f)
      = n[f(uT_theta(mu_theta))-f(u)]
        + Q(theta) + H0(u)/n

and coordinate derivatives is O(u theta/n), which is smaller. Replacing
T_theta by T0 in the covariance term costs O(u theta^2). The O(n^-3)
fourth-cumulant term before scaling is also absorbed by u n^(-3/2).

the differing factor has L2 norm O(sqrt(theta)) on the Gaussian sign-flip
strip and off it by Taylor expansion; all other factors have uniformly
bounded joint L2 products. Cauchy-Schwarz then bounds each difference.

       +(10u f'+11u^2 f''+4u^3 f'''+u^4 f''''/2)/n,

                                                    +O_K(u theta^2). (3)

body:
[Lemma 22 of arXiv:2606.11994, 'Sample Path Properties of the\\ Fractional Wiener--Weierstrass Bridge II'] Assume $H>1/2$, and put $p=1/H$.  For step functions $f,g$ on
$[0,1]$, the inner product on $\calH$ has the concrete
representation
\begin{equation}   \left\langle f,g\right\rangle_{\calH}   =   H(2H-1)\int_0^1\int_0^1   f(x)g(y)|x-y|^{2H-2}\,\dd x\,\dd y .   
\end{equation}
Moreover, $L^p[0,1]$ embeds continuously into $\calH$: there is a finite
constant $C_H$ such that
\begin{equation}   \norm{f}_{\calH}   \le C_H\norm{f}_{L^p[0,1]},   \qquad f\in L^p[0,1].   
\end{equation}
Under this embedding, \eqref{eq:calH-inner-product} remains valid for all
$f,g\in L^p[0,1]$.  Finally,
\begin{equation*}   \norm{f}_{\calH}=0,\quad f\in L^p[0,1],   \quad\Longrightarrow\quad   f=0\text{ Lebesgue-a.e.}
      
\end{equation*}
In particular, the embedding $L^p[0,1]\hookrightarrow\calH$ is injective.

body: [Lemma 6 (Polynomial entropy implies a local bound) of arXiv:2602.20971, 'Does Order Matter : Connecting The Law of Robustness to Robust Gener'] Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a measurable class of functions bounded in $[0,b]$, where $b>0$. Assume that for some $p>2$ and $A>0$, $\sup_{Q}\log\mathcal{N}\left(\eta,\mathcal{G},L_{2}(Q)\right)\leq A\eta^{-p}\qquad\text{for all }0<\eta\leq b,$ where the supremum is over all finitely supported probability measures $Q$. For $r\geq 0$, define $\mathcal{G}(r)=\{g\in\mathcal{G}:Pg^{2}\leq r\}.$ Let $\bar{A}:=1\vee A$. Then there is a constant $C_{p,b}>0$, depending only on $p$ and $b$, such that $\mathfrak{R}_{n}(\mathcal{G}(r))\leq C_{p,b}\left(\bar{A}^{1/p}n^{-1/p}+\sqrt{\frac{r}{n}}\right).$ In particular, if $A\geq 1$, then $\mathfrak{R}_{n}(\mathcal{G}(r))\leq C_{p,b}\left(A^{1/p}n^{-1/p}+\sqrt{\frac{r}{n}}\right).$

[Proposition thm:GeoBM of arXiv:2605.28430, 'Limit theory for Lipschitz-localized statistics in random geometric models'] Let $M = \{M(x)\}_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d}$ be a non-negative, real-valued random field on $\mathbb{R}^d$ having fast $\mathbb{B} $-mixing correlations as in Definition~(d.omegatmixing-field of the paper)(i.B-mixing-field of the paper)-(i.mixing-field-fast of the paper).
Assume that $M$ is bounded by some constant $R$, that is,
$\sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d} M(x) \le R < \infty$.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a simple point process on $\mathbb{R}^d$ having 
fast mixing correlations  as in Definition~(d.omegamixing of the paper)(i.mixing-ground-fast of the paper), bounded reduced  Palm intensity function~(equation bdedreduced of the paper),
 and independent of the random field $M$.
Consider the  edge length measure $\sigma_{n}^{\textnormal{}}$ of the geostatistical graph $\Psi(\mathcal{P}_n, M)$ as in (equation e:Geo-edges of the paper).
\begin{enumerate}[wide, label=(\roman*), labelindent=0pt]
\item 
A central limit theorem holds for the family $\big(\sigma_{n}^{\textnormal{}}(f)\big)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$; that is, as $n \to \infty$,
\[
  \big({\rm Var} \, \sigma_{n}^{\textnormal{}}(f)\big)^{-1/2}
  \Big( \sigma_{n}^{\textnormal{}}(f) - \mathbb {E}  \, \sigma_{n}^{\textnormal{}}(f) \Big)
  \stackrel{d}{\Rightarrow} Z,
\]
for all $f \in \mathbb{B} (W_1)$, provided ${\rm Var} \, \sigma_{n}^{\textnormal{}}(f) = \Omega(n^{\nu})$ for some $\nu > 0$.

\item 
Further, if the random field $M$ and the point process $\mathcal{P}$ are stationary, with $\rho$ denoting the intensity of $\mathcal{P}$,
then the expectation and variance asymptotics
hold for 
$\big(\sigma_{n}^{\textnormal{}}(f)\big)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$,
as stated in Proposition~(expvar of the paper). 
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma lem:green-form-inverse of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] Fix $x\in\Omega_{\rm op}$ and $\theta\in L^2(M_x)$.  The potential
$u:=U_D(\theta M_x)$ belongs to $V_x$ and is the unique solution of
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal E(u,v)=\int_D\theta\widetilde v\,dM_x,
 \qquad v\inV_x.
 
\end{equation}
Its $L^2(M_x)$ representative and its energy are given by
\begin{align}
 \widetilde u&=G_x\theta\quad\text{in }L^2(M_x),
 \\
 I_D(\theta M_x)&=\langle\theta,G_x\theta\rangle_{L^2(M_x)}.
 
\end{align}
Equivalently,
\[
 G_x\theta\in\operatorname{Dom}(A_x),
 \qquad A_xG_x\theta=\theta.
\]

[Corollary 33 of arXiv:2608.27372, 'Universality and sharp thresholds for ellipsoid fitting'] Assume $(x_i)_{i\leq n}$ satisfy the hypotheses of
	Proposition~\ref{prop:light-tail-quotient}, and $n/d^2 \to \alpha\in (0,\infty)$. 
    
    There exists an absolute constant $\mu>0$ such that the following holds. For every fixed $L\geq 2$ and $\eps\in(0,1)$, there exist $
	K_0=K_0(\alpha,K_x,L,\eps)>0$ and $C=C(K_x,L)>0$ such that for every $K\ge K_0$,
	with probability $1-o(1)$, the following holds: for every
	$\ell=2,\ldots,L$, every $\mathcal I\subset[n]$, and every
	$t\in\R^n$ supported on $\mathcal I^c$ satisfying
	$\|t\|_2=1$ and $\|t\|_\infty\le(Kd)^{-1/2}$, let
	$\mathsf V_{t,\ell}$ be the span of the eigenvectors of
	$\Sigma_{t,\ell}$ whose eigenvalues are at least $\mu$, where
	\[
    \Sigma_{t,\ell}\equiv\sum_{i\notin \mathcal{I}} t_i^2 u_{i,\ell} u_{i,\ell}^\top,\qquad m_{t,\ell}:=\dim\mathsf V_{t,\ell}.
    \]
    Then for every such $\mathcal{I}, t$, the $\mathcal{F}_{\ell-1}^{\mathcal I}$-measurable event
	\begin{equation}
	\mathcal G_\ell^{\mathcal I}(t)
	:=
	\left\{
	\max_{i\le n}\|u_{i,\ell}\|_2^2\le Cd,
	\quad
	m_{t,\ell}\ge(1-\eps)p_\ell
	\right\}
	\end{equation}
	occurs, and $P_{\mathsf V_{t,\ell}}\Sigma_{t,\ell}P_{\mathsf V_{t,\ell}}
	\succeq\mu P_{\mathsf V_{t,\ell}}$ holds.

[Lemma 1 of arXiv:2608.17493, 'Integrals of some compound processes'] Let $X, Y$ two stochastic processes on $\mathcal{D}[0,\infty)$. Assume that $X(t)\stackrel{d}{=}Y(t), \ t\ge0$. 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item[($i$)] If both $X$ and $Y$ have independent and stationary increments, then $X\stackrel{d}{=}Y$ on $\mathcal{D}[0,\infty)$.
		\item[($ii$)] If both $X$ and $Y$ have independent increments and $X(t)-X(s)\stackrel{d}{=}Y(t)-Y(s), \ t>s\ge0$, then $X\stackrel{d}{=}Y$ on $\mathcal{D}[0,\infty)$.
	\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact conditioning, spectral integral estimate, deterministic graph comparison or order-statistic asymptotics Result: One spectral step only needs finite mean. Put g2(x)=exp(-x)*sum_(j>=2)P(j)*x^(j-2)/(j-2)!, and consider Kf(x)=integral min(x,y)*f(y)*g2(y)dy on L2(g2 dx). Tonelli gives integral x*g2(x)dx=sum_(j>=2)(j-1)P(j)=E[K_degree]-1. Since min(x,y)^2<=x*y, the squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm is at most (E[K_degree]-1)^2. Thus finite mean already makes this symmetric integral operator compact. The kernel is also positive semidefinite because min(x,y)=integral_0^infinity 1_(t<x)*1_(t<y)dt. This removes an exponential moment from the compactness step, while leaving the stronger population conclusions untouched. Check: The gamma integral of x^(j-1)*exp(-x)/(j-2)! equals j-1. For compactly supported test functions, Fubini expresses the quadratic form as integral (integral_(x>t) f(x)g2(x)dx)^2 dt; continuity extends positivity to L2. Obstruction: No assertion that every source growth/extinction theorem survives under finite mean. Identifying the branching eigenfunctions, integrability of the spine, and uniform integrability of martingales still require proof.

[Corollary 8 of arXiv:2604.24392, 'Numerical approximation of Markovian BSDEs in infinite horizon and elliptic PDEs'] Let $p\in (1,+\infty]$. 
Assume  \eqref{as:generatorf}, \eqref{as:b:sigma} and \eqref{as:int:X:nablaX}.
\begin{description} 
\item [(case $p=+\infty$)]: Assume \eqref{as:suprho}, $a>\theta$, $\ta>\ttheta$,  $\kappa_\infty < 1$ and $\normr{\Phi(0)}<+\infty$,
then there is a unique continuous function $v: \bR^d \to \bR^{d'}\times \bR^{d'\times d}$ with  $\displaystyle\sup_{x\in \bR^d}\dfrac{\norm{v(x)}}{{\rho}(x) }<+\infty$  satisfying  $v=\Phi(v),$
i.e. solving \eqref{prop:eq:u} and \eqref{prop:eq:baru}. Moreover the solution $v$ satisfies the following bound: $\displaystyle\normr{v}\leqslant \frac{1}{1- \kappa_\infty} \normr{\Phi(0)}$.
\item [(case $p \in (1,+\infty)$)]: Assume that there exists a probability measure $\meas$ on $\bR^d$ satisfying $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} |x|^r \meas(\dx)<+\infty$ and such that \eqref{eq:condition:stability:rho} holds. Assume also  $\kappa_p < 1$ and $\left(\displaystyle\int_{\bR^d} |\Phi(0)(x)|^p \meas(\dx)\right)^\frac{1}{p } < +\infty$.
\end{description}
Then, there is a unique measurable function $v: \bR^d \to \bR^{d'}\times \bR^{d'\times d}$ with   $\left(\displaystyle\int_{\bR^d}\norm{v(x)}^p \meas(\dx)\right)^\frac{1}{p }<+\infty$ satisfying  $v=\Phi(v)$, i.e. solving \eqref{prop:eq:u} and \eqref{prop:eq:baru}.
Moreover the solution $v$ satisfies the following bound: $\displaystyle\left(\int_{\bR^d}\norm{v(x)}^p \meas(\dx) \right)^\frac{1}{p }\leqslant \frac{1}{1- \kappa_p} \left(\int_{\bR^d}\norm{\Phi(0)(x)}^p \meas(\dx)\right)^\frac{1}{p }$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Lemma lem:shape of arXiv:2510.05850, 'Three-point connectivity constant for $q$-state Potts spin clusters'] For a loop $\eta$ sampled from $\widetilde\SLE_\kappa^\mathrm{sep}(\mathcal{C})$ (resp.\ $\SLE_\kappa^\mathrm{sep}(\mathcal{C})$), there is a unique decomposition $\eta = \eta^0 + \mathbf{t}$ with $\eta^0 \in \mathrm{Loop}_0(\mathcal{C})$ and $\mathbf{t} \in \mathbb{R}$, and there exists a probability measure $\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_\kappa(\mathcal{C})$ (resp.\ $\mathcal{L}_\kappa(\mathcal{C})$) on $\mathrm{Loop}_0(\mathcal{C})$ and constants $\widetilde C,C>0$ such that the joint law of $(\eta^0,\bf t)$ equals $\widetilde C\widetilde{\mathcal{L}}_\kappa(\mathcal{C})\times dt$ (resp.\ $C\mathcal{L}_\kappa(\mathcal{C})\times dt$). Moreover, $\widetilde C=(\mathbb{E}[\log \mathsf{R}_{R\to B}]+\mathbb{E}[\log \mathsf{R}_{B\to R}])^{-1}$ and $C=(\mathbb{E}[\log \mathsf{R}_{R\to B}])^{-1}$.

[Prop prop coefficient functional of arXiv:2512.20338, 'Up-down chains and scaling limits: \\ application to permuton- and graphon-valued diffusio'] There exists a unique bounded linear functional $ [  h _ \varnothing ^o ] \colon C(  E  ) \to  \mathbb R  $ satisfying
    \begin{equation}
        
        [  h _ \varnothing ^o ]  d _s^o
        		=
        			 M _{ | s | }( s )
				,
					\qquad
					s \in   \mathbb S  
				.
	\end{equation}
	\noindent	
	Moreover, this functional is contractive, positive, and satisfies the following conditions:
    \begin{enumerate}[ label = (\roman*) ]

		\item
		
		$
			[  h _ \varnothing ^o ] f^o
    			=
			[  h _ \varnothing  ]
			f
		$
		for $ f \in  H  $
        (in particular, $
        	[  h _ \varnothing ^o ]  h _s^o
        		=
        			 \mathbbm 1 ( s =  \varnothing  )
        $
        for $ s \in   \mathbb S   $),

        \item
		
        $
        	[  h _ \varnothing ^o ] f
        		=
        			\lim_{ t \to \infty }
        				{\textstyle \int_ E  }
           					  \mathcal T  ( t )
           					f
        					\,
        					d \nu
        $
        for $ f \in C(  E  ) $ and any probability measure $\nu$ on $ E $,
		and
		
		\item
		
    	$
			[  h _ \varnothing ^o ] f
				=
        			\lim_{ n \to \infty }
        				{\textstyle \int_{   \mathbb S  _n } }
            				 \pi _n f \,
            				d  M _n
    	$
    	for $ f \in C(  E  ) $.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Prop 9 of arXiv:2607.06745, 'Regularization and asymptotic behaviour of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck evolution operators in infin'] Let $-\infty<s<t<+\infty$. The image
of the operator
\[
P_{s,t}:L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{t}\right)\to L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{s}\right)
\]
is contained in $W^{1,p}\left(X,\mu_{s}\right)$ and $P_{s,t}$ is
continuous as an operator with values in $W^{1,p}\left(X,\mu_{s}\right)$.
Consequently, $P_{s,t}$ is compact as an operator with values in
$L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{s}\right)$.

\vspace{1mm}

In particular, the continuity estimate for the gradient has the form:
\begin{equation}
\left\Vert \nabla P_{s,t}f\right\Vert _{L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{s};X\right)}\leq C_{p}\left\Vert \Lambda\left(t,s\right)\right\Vert _{\mathcal{L}\left(X\right)}\left\Vert f\right\Vert _{L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{t}\right)}\quad\forall f\in L^{p}\left(X,\mu_{t}\right),
\end{equation}
where $\Lambda\left(t,s\right)$ is the operator defined in Remark
$\text{\ref{rem:def Lambda}}$.

Furthermore, relation $\text{\eqref{eq: formula grad C1}}$ also holds
for $\varphi\in W^{1,p}\left(X,\mu_{t}\right)$ and for $\mu_{s}$-almost
every $x\in X$.

Suppose that A is a subset of V satisfying 0 < |A| < |V |. Let W be the set of all vertices of the embedded graph of X. Then, there exists a subset B of W that satisfies the following conditions: |E(B, W \ B)| ≤k(n + 1 −k)|F(A, V \ A)|, 1 ≤|B|, |V \ A| ≤n|W \ B| δmin .
title: Lemma 4.2 of arXiv:2309.11785: Cheeger type inequalities for high dimensional simplicial complexes

[Theorem 2 (Cameron--Martin formula) of arXiv:2608.02417, 'A Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula for linear stochastic evolution equations in Banach spaces'] Let \(R\in\gamma(\scrH,E)\), let \(W\) be an \(\scrH\)-isonormal Gaussian
process, and let \(X_R\) be the centred \(E\)-valued Gaussian random variable
canonically associated with \(R\). Then, for every bounded Borel function
\(g:E\to\R\), every \(h\in\scrH\), and every \(\varepsilon\in\R\),
\begin{equation}
    \E g(X_R+\varepsilon Rh)
    = \E\Bigl[ g(X_R)\exp\Bigl(\varepsilon W(h) -\frac{\varepsilon^2}{2}\|h\|_\scrH^2\Bigr)\Bigr].
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Cameron--Martin formula

[Lemma 6 of arXiv:2609.01498, 'A Tight Erd\H{o}s-Stone Bound for All Graph Densities'] For every $0 < \eta < 1$ and $n > 4/\eta$ the following holds. If $\epsilon < 1/2$ and $G$ is a graph with $n$ vertices and
$(1-\epsilon){n \choose 2}$ edges, then $G$ has a subgraph $H$ with $p > (\eta/2)^{1/2}n$ vertices and with minimum degree at least
$(1-\epsilon-\eta)p$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let $(X, d)$ be a compact metric space. A homeomorphism $f: X \to X$ is expansive with expansivity constant $\varepsilon > 0$ if whenever $x \ne y$ there is some $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ (positive OR negative) with $d(f^n x, f^n y) > \varepsilon$; equivalently, $d(f^n x, f^n y) \le \varepsilon$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ forces $x = y$. A continuous map $f: X \to X$ (not necessarily invertible) is positively expansive (forward expansive) with constant $\varepsilon$ if $d(f^n x, f^n y) \le \varepsilon$ for all $n \ge 0$ forces $x = y$. Positive expansiveness is much stronger than expansiveness: a positively expansive HOMEOMORPHISM of a compact metric space exists only when $X$ is finite (Schwartzman; Keynes-Robertson), so for an infinite compact space the notion is meaningful only for genuinely non-invertible maps such as expanding maps and one-sided shifts. On a compact space the property (with some constant) does not depend on the choice of compatible metric, though the constant does. Expansiveness is preserved by passing to $f^{-1}$ and to $f^k$, $k \ne 0$; positive expansiveness is preserved by passing to $f^k$, $k \ge 1$.
X is a compact metric space
for the homeomorphism notion f is invertible; for positive expansiveness f is only assumed continuous

body:
[Theorem 6 of arXiv:2604.13819, 'Convolution, cumulants and infinitesimal generators in the formal power series ring'] The $t$-deformed cumulants $\{\kappa_{i}^{t}(A)\}_{i \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}}$ are unique maps satisfying the following conditions:
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (i)]
\item $\kappa_{i}^{t}(A)$ is a polynomial in $p_{1}(A), \dots, p_{i}(A)$ with leading term $\frac{t^{i-1}}{(t)_{i}} p_{i}(A)$. 
That is, there exists a polynomial $F_{i}$ in $i-1$ variables such that 
$$
\kappa_{i}^t(A) = \frac{t^{i-1}}{(t)_{\underline{i}}}p_{i}(A) + F_{i}(p_{1}(A), \dots, p_{i-1}(A)).
$$ 
\item Homogeneity: $\kappa_{i}^{t}(D_{r}[A]) = r^{i}\kappa_{i}^{t}(A)$ for any $r \in \mathbb{R}$ and $i \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}$.
\item Additivity: $\kappa_{i}^{t}(A \boxplus^{t} B) = \kappa_{i}^{t}(A) + \kappa_{i}^{t}(B)$. 
In other words, 
$$
C^t[A \boxplus^{t} B](z) = C^{t}[A](z) + C^{t}[B](z).
$$ 
\end{enumerate}

[Lem mobius-primitive of arXiv:2607.00311, 'Thermal Concentration and Poisson--Dirichlet Edge Statistics for Random-Lattice Gibbs Ense'] Let $\mu:\mathbb N\to\{-1,0,1\}$ be the M\"obius function. 
Thus $\mu(1)=1$, $\mu(d)=0$ if $d$ is divisible by the square of a prime, and
$\mu(d)=(-1)^r$ if
$$
d=p_1p_2\cdots p_r
$$
with distinct primes $p_1,\ldots,p_r$.

The elementary M\"obius inversion identity is
$$
\sum_{d|N}\mu(d)=
\begin{cases}
1, & N=1,\\
0, & N\ge2.
\end{cases}
$$
Consequently, for every nonzero vector $\bm q\in\mathbb Z^n$,
$$
\chi_{\mathbb Z^n_{\operatorname{prim}}}(\bm q)=\sum_{d|\bm q}\mu(d),
$$
where $d|\bm q$ means that $d$ divides every coordinate of $\bm q$.

body:
[Prop pt of arXiv:2411.07809, 'Pirogov--Sinai Theory Beyond Lattices'] Suppose $G$ is an infinite bipartite graph satisfying the hypotheses
  of Theorem~(thm:transitive of the paper) or~(thm:matched of the paper). Let $v_{\textsf{o}}$
  and $v_{\textsf{e}}$ denote fixed vertices in $V_{\textsf{o}}$ and
  $V_{\textsf{e}}$. If $\lambda\geq\lambda_{\star}(C_{\text{iso}},D,\Delta)$, then
  \begin{equation}
    
    \lim_{n\to\infty}  \mu^{\textsf{e}}_{\Lambda_{n}}[\textrm{$v_{\textsf{e}}$
      is occupied}] >\frac{1}{2}, \quad \text{and} \quad 
    \lim_{n\to\infty}  \mu^{\textsf{o}}_{\Lambda_{n}}[\textrm{$v_{\textsf{o}}$ is
      occupied}] >\frac{1}{2}  \,.
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 29 of arXiv:2608.28991, 'Jigsaw-CRL: Recovering Global Latent Causal Order from Fragmented Multi-Client Interventio'] Fix a client $k\in[K]$. Let $\cI\subseteq \cC_k$ be a collection of blocks that is closed under block ancestors, namely
\[
C\in \cI,\ C'\in Anc_k^\rblk(C)\quad \Longrightarrow\quad C'\in \cI.
\]
Define
\[
W \;\triangleq\; \Big\langle [\bQ_k]_{\rho_k(i),:}\ \Big|\ i\in \bigcup_{C\in\cI} C \Big\rangle .
\]
Let $j_1,\dots,j_\ell$ be intervention indices such that
\[
C_k(j_r)\notin \cI,\qquad r=1,\dots,\ell,
\]
where $C_k(j_r)$ denotes the block in $\cC_k$ containing the target $t_{j_r}$. Define
\[
\cS_{\cI}
\;\triangleq\;
\Big( \bigcup_{r=1}^\ell Anc_k^\rblk\big(C_k(j_r)\big)\Big)\setminus \cI,
\qquad
S
\;\triangleq\;
\rho_k\!\Big(\bigcup_{C\in\cS_{\cI}} C\Big).
\]
For each $s\in S$, let $[\bar{\bH}_k]_{s,:}$ be the projection of $[\bH_k]_{s,:}$ onto $W^\perp$, and let $[\bar{\bH}_k]_{S,:}$ be the matrix formed by stacking these projected rows.

Then
\[
\Pi_{W^\perp}\!\left(
\row\Big(\{\bTheta_k^{(j)}-\bTheta_k^{(0)}\}_{j\in\{j_1,\dots,j_\ell\}}\Big)
\right)
\]
is contained in
\[
\Big\langle
[\bar{\bH}_k]_{S,:}^{T}
(\bI-[\bA_k]_{S,S})^{T}
[\bSigma_k]_{S,S}^{-1}
[\be_{\rho_k(t_j)}]_{S},
\ 
[\bar{\bH}_k]_{S,:}^{T}
\Big(
(\bI-[\bA_k]_{S,S})^{T}
[\bSigma_k]_{S,S}^{-1}
[\bu_k^{(j)}]_{S}
+
[\bd_k^{(j)}]_{S}
\Big)
\ \Big|\ 
j\in\{j_1,\dots,j_\ell\}
\Big\rangle .
\]

body: [Proposition 8 of arXiv:2512.19517, 'Spiking and Resetting'] Let $0<a\leq b<1$ and $A=[a,b]$. For any $n\geq 0$ and any real numbers $0=s_{0}<s_{1}<s_{2}<s_{n}<t=s_{n+1}$, conditionally to the event $\{e_{1}^{\varepsilon}\geq t\}$, the random vector $\begin{split}\big(N^{\varepsilon}_{(s_{i},s_{i+1}]}(A)\big)_{0\leq i\leq n}\end{split}$ converges in law, as $\varepsilon$ goes to $0$, to the random vector $\begin{split}\big({\bar{N}}_{i}\big)_{0\leq i\leq n}\end{split}$ composed of independent random variables such that for any $i\in\{0,\ldots,n\}$, $N_{i}$ is a Poisson random variable with parameter $(s_{i+1}-s_{i})\lambda_{*}(A)$.

,\\

    $$\mathbb{P}(\|R_K^\epsilon(t)\| >  \epsilon^{(K+1)(1/2 - 2a)}e^{(\lambda + a)t}\|x_0\|) \leq \delta \,,$$

[Lemma lem-decomp-cone of arXiv:2411.19810, 'Radial conformal welding in Liouville quantum gravity'] Let $W \in (0, \frac{\gamma^2}2)$. Let $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa^\mathrm{wp}(\rho)$ denote the law of whole-plane $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa(\rho)$ from $0$ to $\infty$. Sample $(z, \psi_0, \eta_0^\mathrm{wp}) \sim \mathcal{A}_{\psi_0}(dz) P_W(d\psi_0) \mathrm{SLE}_\kappa^\mathrm{wp}(W-2)$. For each connected component $B$ of $\mathbb{C} \backslash \eta_0^\mathrm{wp}$, let $p_B$ and $q_B$ be the first and last points of $\partial B$ hit by $\eta_0^\mathrm{wp}$. Let $\tilde \mathcal{W}$ be the collection of all quantum surfaces $(B, \psi_0, p_B, q_B)/{\sim_\gamma}$, and  endow $\tilde \mathcal{W}$ with the ordering where $(B_1, \psi_0, p_{B_1}, q_{B_1})/{\sim_\gamma}$ precedes $(B_2, \psi_0, p_{B_2}, q_{B_2})/{\sim_\gamma}$ if $\eta_0^\mathrm{wp}$ hits $q_{B_1}$ for the last time before it hits $q_{B_2}$ for the last time. 
	
	    
	    Let $B_\bullet$ be the connected component of $\mathbb{C} \backslash \eta_0^\mathrm{wp}$ containing $z$, and let $\mathcal{B}_\bullet = (B_\bullet, \psi_0, z, p_{B_\bullet}, q_{B_\bullet})/{\sim_\gamma}$. Let $ \mathcal{D} \subset \tilde \mathcal{W}$ (resp.\ $\mathcal{W} \subset \tilde \mathcal{W}$) be the ordered collection of elements that come before (resp.\ after) $(B_\bullet, \psi_0, p_{B_\bullet}, q_{B_\bullet})/{\sim_\gamma}$. Then the joint law of $(\mathcal{D}, \mathcal{B}_\bullet, \mathcal{W})$ is $(1 - \frac{2W}{\gamma^2})^2 {\mathcal{M}}^\mathrm{disk}_{0,2}(W) \times {\mathcal{M}}^\mathrm{disk}_{1,2}(\gamma^2 - W)  \times \mathcal{M}^\mathrm{wed}(W)$.

body: There is a Boolean function f: {-1,1}^2 -> {0,1}, f(x) = (1 + x_1 x_2)/2, that is not unate, has fhat({1}) = fhat({2}) = 0 but q_1 = q_2 = 1 (both coordinates are pivotal everywhere), and has Var(f) = 1/4 < 1/2 = (1/4)(q_1^2 + q_2^2). So the unate hypothesis cannot be dropped from either the identity q_i = 2|fhat({i})| or the lower bound of the variance sandwich.

[Definition 2 of arXiv:2604.23656, 'Doubly Reflected Backward SDEs Driven by $G$-Brownian Motion with Quadratic Generator'] Let $M_{G}^{0}(0,T)$ be the collection of processes in the
	following form: for a given partition $\{t_{0},\cdot\cdot\cdot,t_{N}\}$ of $[0,T]$,
	\[
	\eta_{t}(\omega)=\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}\xi_{j}(\omega)\mathbf{1}_{[t_{j},t_{j+1})}(t),
	\]
	where $\xi_{i}\in L_{ip}(\Omega_{t_{i}})$, $i=0,1,2,\cdot\cdot\cdot,N-1$. For each
	$p\geq1$ and $\eta\in M_G^0(0,T)$, let $\|\eta\|_{H_G^p}:=\{\hat{\mathbb{E}}[(\int_0^T|\eta_s|^2ds)^{p/2}]\}^{1/p}$, $\Vert\eta\Vert_{M_{G}^{p}}:=(\mathbb{\hat{E}}[\int_{0}^{T}|\eta_{s}|^{p}ds])^{1/p}$ and denote by $H_G^p(0,T)$,  $M_{G}^{p}(0,T)$ the completion
	of $M_{G}^{0}(0,T)$ under the norm $\|\cdot\|_{H_G^p}$, $\|\cdot\|_{M_G^p}$, respectively.

[Proposition prop:existence_vw of arXiv:2609.01984, 'Instantaneous shrinking of supports for stochastic PDEs\footnote{JY was supported by a KIA'] For each $n\ge1$, there exists a filtered probability space
$(\bar\Omega,\bar{\mathcal F},\{\bar{\mathcal F}_t\},\bar\mathbb{P})$
carrying:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm(i)] an $\bar{\mathcal F}_0$-measurable nonnegative random
function $\bar u_0$ and a coefficient field $(\bar a,\bar b,\bar c)$
satisfying Assumption (asp:coefficients of the paper), with
$\mathcal L(\bar u_0,\bar a,\bar b,\bar c)
 =\mathcal L(u_0,a,b,c)$;
\item[\rm(ii)] two independent space-time white noises
$\xi_1,\xi_2$ relative to $\{\bar{\mathcal F}_t\}$;
\item[\rm(iii)] nonnegative processes
$v_n,w_n\in C([0,T];C_{\rm tem}(\mathbb{R}))$ solving
(equation eq:spde_v_n of the paper) and (equation eq:spde_w_n of the paper) with
$(u_0,a,b,c)$ replaced by $(\bar u_0,\bar a,\bar b,\bar c)$.
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, for every $p\ge2$, $\varepsilon\in(0,\delta/2)$, and $a>0$, there
exists $N=N(a,\varepsilon,p,T)>0$, independent of $n$, such that
\[
    \mathbb{E}\|\Psi_a v_n\|_{C^{\varepsilon}([0,T]\times\mathbb{R})}^p
    + \mathbb{E}\|\Psi_a w_n\|_{C^{\varepsilon}([0,T]\times\mathbb{R})}^p
    \le N,
    \qquad
    \Psi_a(x):=\zeta(ax)=\frac1{\cosh(ax)}.
\]

Let U subset R^n be open and u harmonic on U. If closure(B(x,r)) subset U, then u(x) equals both the average of u over the sphere partial B(x,r) and the average of u over the ball B(x,r): u(x) = (1/|partial B(x,r)|) integral_{partial B(x,r)} u dS = (1/|B(x,r)|) integral_{B(x,r)} u dV. Conversely, any locally integrable function on U satisfying the sphere mean-value property for every such ball is, after modification on a null set, smooth and harmonic on U.
U is open in R^n

[Defi def:stochasticcontrolledroughpaths of arXiv:2412.05698, 'Controlled rough SDEs, pathwise stochastic control and dynamic programming principles'] {FHL21}}]   
A pair \((Z,Z')\) is called \textit{stochastic controlled rough path} of $(p,q)$-integrability and $(\kappa,\kappa')$-H\"older regularity if 
\begin{enumerate} \renewcommand{\alph{enumi})}{\alph{enumi})}
\item \(Z=(Z_t)_{t \in [0,T]}\) is progressively measurable such that

\[
    \|\delta Z\|_{\kappa;p,q} := \sup_{0 \leq s < t \leq T} \frac{\|\|\delta Z_{s,t}|{\mathfrak F}_s\|_p\|_q}{|t-s|^\kappa} < +\infty;
\]
\item \(Z'=(Z'_t)_{t \in [0,T]}\) is progressively measurable such that
\[
    \sup_{t \in [0,T]} \|Z'_t\|_q < +\infty \quad \text{and} \quad \|\delta Z'\|_{\kappa';p,q} := \sup_{0 \leq s < t \leq T} \frac{\|\|\delta Z'_{s,t}|{\mathfrak F}_s\|_p\|_q}{|t-s|^{\kappa'}} < +\infty;
\]
\item writing \(R^Z_{s,t} = \delta Z_{s,t} - Z'_s \delta X_{s,t}\) for \((s,t)\in\Delta_T\), we have
\[
    \|\mathbb{E}_\cdot R^Z\|_{\kappa+\kappa';q} := \sup_{0 \leq s < t \leq T} \frac{\|\mathbb{E}_s(R^Z_{s,t})\|_q}{|t-s|^{\kappa+\kappa'}} < + \infty.
\]
\end{enumerate}
We write \((Z,Z') \in \mathbf{D}_X^{\kappa,\kappa'} L_{p,q}\); and also \(\mathbf{D}_X^{2\kappa} L_{p,q}\), \(\mathbf{D}_X^{\kappa,\kappa'} L_p\) if \(\kappa = \kappa'\) and \(p=q\), respectively.

[Proposition propclassbd of arXiv:2604.07227, 'Transition probabilities of step-reinforced random walks'] Let $S$ be a generalized SRRW on a countably infinite $G$ with parameter $\alpha \in [0,1)$ and step distribution $\mu$ being a class function. We denote its law by $\mathbb{P}^{(\alpha)}$ to indicate the dependence on $\alpha$. Let $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ and $m \in \mathbb{N}_+$ be such that 
$$
\max_{x\in G} \mathbb{P}^{(0)}(S_n=x) \leq \varepsilon, \quad \forall  n\geq m.
$$
Then there exists a positive constant $\rho \in (0,\alpha)$ depending only on $\alpha$ such that
$$
\max_{x\in G} \mathbb{P}^{(\alpha)}(S_n=x) \leq \varepsilon + 5\rho^{n}, \quad \forall  n\geq \frac{8 m}{1-\alpha}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let Omega = {0,1}^E for a finite set E (the coordinates e in E are 'edges' or 'bits'), and let P_p denote the product measure under which the coordinates omega_e are independent Bernoulli(p_e) variables, p = (p_e) in [0,1]^E; write P_p also for the case p_e = p for all e. For an event A (a subset of Omega) and a coordinate e write A^e = { omega : omega^e in A } and A_e = { omega : omega_e in A }, where omega^e and omega_e are omega with the coordinate e set to 1 and to 0 respectively; A^e and A_e do not depend on the coordinate e. The coordinate e is PIVOTAL for A at omega if exactly one of omega^e, omega_e lies in A; Piv_A(omega) is the set of pivotal coordinates and its size |Piv_A| is the number of pivotal coordinates. THEOREM (Margulis 1974, Russo 1981). For every event A, p |-> P_p(A) is a polynomial in the p_e and, for every coordinate e, d/dp_e P_p(A) = P_p(A^e) - P_p(A_e). With a single parameter p, d/dp P_p(A) = sum over e in E of ( P_p(A^e) - P_p(A_e) ). If A is INCREASING (closed under raising coordinates) then A_e is contained in A^e, A^e minus A_e is exactly the event that e is pivotal for A, and the formula reads d/dp P_p(A) = sum over e of P_p( e is pivotal for A ) = E_p |Piv_A| = sum over e of I_e^p(A), where I_e^p(A) = P_p(e pivotal for A) is the influence of e on A under P_p. In particular an increasing event's probability is nondecreasing in p (and in every p_e), and its derivative is the expected number of pivotal coordinates. The formula holds verbatim for an event on an infinite product space that depends on finitely many coordinates; for a general increasing event depending on infinitely many coordinates the right-hand side is only known to bound the derivative from below in the appropriate one-sided sense, and the finite-dimensional form is the one used in practice (finite boxes, then limits).
E finite (or the event depends on finitely many coordinates of an infinite product space)
the measure is a product of Bernoulli(p_e) coordinates; the single-parameter form takes p_e = p for all e
the pivotal (influence) form of the right-hand side needs A increasing; the general form P_p(A^e) - P_p(A_e) holds for every event
the sharp-threshold consequences are cited, not proved

[Proposition 22 of arXiv:2608.30752, '2608.30752'] Let \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{id}}\) denote the marking-preserving homotopy class
of Lipschitz maps \(v:X_0\to Y\). In a \(q\)-natural coordinate
\(z=x+iy\), define
\[
  H_q(v)
  :=
  \frac12
  \int_{X_0\setminus Z(q)}
  |v_x|_{u_0^*h}^2\,dx\,dy,
  \quad
  V_q(v)
  :=
  \frac12
  \int_{X_0\setminus Z(q)}
  |v_y|_{u_0^*h}^2\,dx\,dy.
\]
These quantities are globally well-defined because the transition maps
between \(q\)-natural coordinates are of the form
\(z\mapsto\pm z+c\), and \(Z(q)\) has measure zero. Set
\begin{equation}
  \mathscr V_q(Y)
  :=
  \inf_{v\in\mathscr H_{\mathrm{id}}}V_q(v).
  
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
  e^{-2t}E(t)
  \searrow
  \mathscr V_q(Y)
  \qquad
  \text{as }t\to\infty.
  
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{t\to\infty}
  \frac{E(t)}{e^{2t}}
  =
  \mathscr V_q(Y),
  \qquad
  E(t)
  =
  \mathscr V_q(Y)e^{2t}+o(e^{2t}).
  
\end{equation}

Suppose, in addition, that \(q\) is Jenkins--Strebel and that its vertical
foliation is the contracting foliation of the ray. Write the complementary
components of its vertical critical graph as maximal flat cylinders
\(
  C_i
  \cong
  (0,h_i)\times
  \bigl(\mathbb R/c_i\mathbb Z\bigr),
\) \(
  i=1,\ldots,r,
\)
where \(q=dz^2\), \(z=x+iy\), the vertical trajectories
\(x=\mathrm{constant}\) are closed, \(c_i\) is their \(q\)-length, and
\(h_i\) is the transverse height of \(C_i\). Let \(\delta_i\) be the core
curve of \(C_i\), and put
\(
  M_i:=\operatorname{Mod}(C_i)=\frac{h_i}{c_i}.
\)
Then
\begin{equation}
  \mathscr V_q(Y)
  =
  \frac12
  \sum_{i=1}^r
  M_i\,\ell_Y(\delta_i)^2
  =
  \frac12
  \sum_{i=1}^r
  \frac{h_i}{c_i}\,
  \ell_Y(\delta_i)^2.
  
\end{equation}
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
  \lim_{t\to\infty}
  \frac{E(t)}{e^{2t}}
  =
  \frac12
  \sum_{i=1}^r
  \operatorname{Mod}(C_i)\,
  \ell_Y(\delta_i)^2.
  
\end{equation}

[Theorem thm:int-3 of arXiv:2510.06891, 'Multivariate CLT for L\'evy processes: convergence rates without moment assumptions'] Let $\bm{X}
$ be a genuinely $d$-dimensional L\'evy process and $\bm{Z}$ be a $d$-dimensional standard Gaussian random vector with $\mathscr{A}$ equal to either $\mathscr{K}$ or $\mathscr{C}$. Assume there exist measurable functions $\bm{A}:[1,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $\bm{B}:[1,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ such that
\[
t \mapsto t^{-1}d_\mathscr{A}(\bm{X}_t-\bm{A}(t)), \bm{B}(t)\bm{Z} )\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(+\infty).
\]
Assume also that $\bm{B}(t)$ is invertible for all sufficiently large $t$ and that the limits $\bm{e}_j^\intercal\bm{B}(t)^\intercal \bm{B}(t) \bm{e}_j \to \infty$, for $j\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$, and
$\bm{B}(t)^{-1}\bm{B}(f(t))\to \bm{I}_d$, for any non-decreasing function $f$ with $f(t)/t\to 1$, hold as $t \to \infty$. Then $\mathds{E}[|\bm{X}_1|^2]<\infty$ and $d_\mathscr{C}(\bm{X}_t-t\mathds{E}\bm{X}_1, \bm{B}(t)\bm{Z} )\to 0$ as $t\to\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:int-3 of arXiv:2510.06891

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, Maximal flow through thin boxes with heavy-tailed capacities (October 2026), addresses Question 36 of Auffinger, Damron and Hanson, 50 Years of First-Passage Percolation: does the limit of Phi/(kl) for the maximal flow from bottom to top of a box in Z^3 exist without Kesten's finite exponential moment assumption? It need not. For every height function m(N) with liminf m(N)/log N = 0 there is a capacity law with no atom at 0 (and infinite mean) such that the maximal flow through [0,N]^(d-1) x [0,m(N)] in Z^d, d >= 2, satisfies limsup Phi/N^(d-1) = +infinity almost surely, and Phi/N^(d-1) exceeds N^(1/2)/2 with probability tending to one along a sequence of N; the heights may grow like (log N)^(1/2), inside Kesten's range. For m(N)/log N -> infinity, Rossignol and Theret (Electron. J. Probab. 23 (2018), paper 99) proved convergence for every capacity law, so for these laws the limit depends on how fast the height grows. The argument counts vertical columns whose edges all carry a very large capacity. Finite-mean and finite-variance laws are not addressed. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/maxflow-thin-boxes (commit 4ebcec43a73a). Not refereed.
title: Maximal flow through thin boxes with heavy-tailed capacities need not have a limit, answering Auffinger-Damron-Hanson Question 36 (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/maxflow-thin-boxes)

[Definition of arXiv:2512.06640, 'Existence and sharpness of the phase transition for the frog model on transitive graphs'] Let $(X_{1},d_{1})$ and $(X_{2},d_{2})$ be two metric spaces. A map $f: X \rightarrow Y$ is called a \textbf{quasi-isometry} if there exists $K>0$ such that 
    \begin{itemize}
        \item For all $z,y \in X_{1},$ we have that 
        $$ K^{-1}d_{1}(z,y) - K \leq d_{2}(f(z),f(y)) \leq Kd_{1}(z,y) + K \, . $$
        \item For all $x_{2} \in X_{2}$ there exists some $x_{1} \in X_{1}$ such that $d_{2}(x_{2},f(x_{1})) \leq K.$
    \end{itemize}
We say that $X_{1}$ is quasi-isometric to $X_{2}$ if there exists a quasi-isometry $f:X_{1}\rightarrow X_{2}.$

[Definition of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] We say $\mathfrak{F} = (W, W_\bot, \leq, \sqsubset)$ is a \emph{CK-frame} if $(W, \leq, \sqsubset)$ is an f-frame and $W_\bot \subseteq W$,
  where $W_\bot$ is upward closed with respect to both $\leq$ and $\sqsubset$ (i.e. $\forall x,y\, (x \in W_\bot \mathrel{\text{\&}} (x \leq y \mathrel{\text{or}} x \sqsubset y) \mathrel{\Rightarrow} y \in W_\bot)$)
  and is $\sqsubset$-serial (i.e. $\forall x\, (x \in W_\bot \mathrel{\Rightarrow} \exists y\, (y \in W_\bot \mathrel{\text{\&}} x \sqsubset y))$).
  Each $x \in W_\bot$ is called a \emph{fallible} world.

[Theorem thm:production-controlled-lyapunov of arXiv:2608.22910, 'A Commutator Framework for Selective Spectral Alignment in Deep Neural Networks'] Assume that, along the gradient-flow trajectory,
\begin{equation}
\mathscr D(t)
\geq
2\mu\mathscr E(t),
\qquad
\mu>0,
\end{equation}
and, for every \(i\in\mathcal I\),
\begin{equation}
q_i(t)
\leq
K_i\mathscr E(t),
\qquad
K_i>0.
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
\mathscr E(t)
\leq
e^{-2\mu t}\mathscr E(0),
\qquad
q_i(t)
\leq
K_i e^{-2\mu t}\mathscr E(0),
\quad
i\in\mathcal I.
\end{equation}
The same conclusion holds with \(q_i\) replaced by a localized gate defect
whenever the corresponding error bound is available.

If m=0, all trajectories and approximation errors are zero.
