[Proposition prop:diafree-vi-is-veb of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] $\mathcal{V}^i \cap \mathscr{L}_\Box = \mathcal{V}^e_\Box$.
  \begin{proof}
    ($\subseteq$)
    It suffices to show that for any $\Box$-p model $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$, $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_\Box$, and $w \in W$,
    $w \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$ iff $w \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$.
    This can easily be proven by induction on the construction of $\varphi$,
    reusing the proofs of Proposition (prop:int-ext-coincides of the paper) ($\Box \Leftrightarrow$) by replacing persistency with $\Box$-persistency.

    ($\supseteq$) Suppose that there are $\varphi \in \mathscr{L}_\Box$, $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$, and $w \in W$ such that $w \nVdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$.
    We construct a new f-model $\mathfrak{M'} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset', V)$ by letting
    $\mathord{\sqsubset'} = \mathord{\sqsubset} \cup \set{ (x, y'); \exists x'\, (x \leq x' \sqsubset y') }$,
    then $\mathfrak{M'}$ is clearly a $\Box$-p model.
    \begin{claim*}
      $x \Vdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \psi \iff x \Vdash^e_\mathfrak{M'} \psi$ for every $\psi \in \mathscr{L}_\Box$.
      \begin{subproof}[Proof of claim]
        We use an induction on the construction of $\psi$.
        We shall only prove the case when $\psi = \Box \chi$.

        ($\Rightarrow$)
        Suppose $x \nVdash^e_\mathfrak{M'} \Box \chi$, then
        there is $y$ such that $x \sqsubset' y \nVdash^e_\mathfrak{M'} \chi$.
        Here, $y \nVdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \chi$ by the induction hypothesis.
        Also, $x \sqsubset' y$ implies either $x \leq x \sqsubset y$ or $x \leq x' \sqsubset y$ for some $x'$.
        In any case, $x \nVdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Box \chi$ holds.

        ($\Leftarrow$)
        Suppose $x \nVdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \Box \chi$, then
        there are $x', y'$ such that $x \leq x' \sqsubset y' \nVdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \chi$.
        Here, $y' \nVdash^e_\mathfrak{M'} \chi$ by the induction hypothesis.
        Also, $x \leq x' \sqsubset y'$ implies $x \sqsubset' y$ by definition.
        Therefore, $x \nVdash^e_\mathfrak{M'} \Box \chi$ holds.
      \end{subproof}
    \end{claim*}
    By the claim, $w \nVdash^i_\mathfrak{M} \varphi$ implies $w \nVdash^e_\mathfrak{M'} \varphi$.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:diafree-vi-is-veb of arXiv:2608.29708

On one uniform bit let rho != 0 and a = |rho|. (i) For 1 < q < infinity and f = 1 + sgn(rho) x, ||f||_1 = 1 while ||T_rho f||_q^q = ((1 + a)^q + (1 - a)^q)/2 > 1. (ii) For 1 <= p < infinity, eps = a/(p + a^2) and f = 1 + sgn(rho) eps x, 0 < eps <= 1/2 and ||T_rho f||_infinity = 1 + a eps > ||f||_p. So neither L^1 -> L^q nor L^p -> L^infinity contracts with constant 1 for any rho != 0.

body: [Lemma lem:scale_free_degree of arXiv:2605.19835, 'Reemergence of the Epidemic Threshold in SIRS Infections on Connected Stars'] Let $G$ be a random scale-free graph with $n\in \mathOrText{\mathds{N}}_{\geq 1}$ vertices that follows a power-law degree distribution with power-law exponent $\gamma \in \mathOrText{\mathds{R}}_{>2}$. Let a_l(theta0) be the constant-word INTERIOR no-upward-cut coefficient for l vertices, summing theta0^B 2^(l-R) over paths starting at their minimum and ending at their maximum. [Lem lem_NonPersistenceOnDomainsWithoutZeroRiemann of arXiv:2608.17463, 'Persistence probabilities of fractional L\'evy fields indexed by hyperbolic space and othe'] Let $(X_H(\eta))_{\eta\in\mathcal{M}}$ be a fractional L\'evy field with Hurst parameter $0<H\leq 1/2$ and let $A$ be a relatively compact subset of $\mathcal{M}$, such that $\inf_{\eta\in A} \mathbb{E}\left[X_H(\eta)^2\right] > 0$. Then with positive probability the field is non-positive on $A$, i.e.
    \begin{align*}
        \mathbb{P}\left(X_H(\eta) \leq 0 ~ \forall \eta\in A\right) > 0.
    \end{align*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm Thm_monotonicity of arXiv:2606.22183, 'Expected loss of quasi-arithmetic means of exchangeable random variables'] Let $I\subseteq \mathbb{R}$ be a nonempty open interval, $f:I\to\mathbb{R}$ be a continuous and strictly increasing function, and $(\xi_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of exchangeable random variables with values in $I$.
If $L:I\to\mathbb{R}$ is a function such that the function $L\circ f^{-1}$ is convex on $f(I)$
 and $\operatorname{\mathbb{E}}(\vert L(\xi_1)\vert)<\infty$, then $\operatorname{\mathbb{E}}\big(L\big(\mathscr{A}_n^{f}(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n)\big) \big)\in[-\infty,\infty)$, $n\in\mathbb{N}$, and
 the sequence $\Big(\operatorname{\mathbb{E}}\big(L\big( \mathscr{A}_n^{f}(\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n) \big)\big)\Big)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is decreasing.

[Theorem 3 (Worst-line pressure in higher dimension) of arXiv:2607.07014, '2607.07014'] Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a compact convex polytope, and let \((\Phi_{\omega_n})_{n\ge1}\) be i.i.d. random piecewise affine self-maps of \(K\). Set \(\Phi_n:=\Phi_{\omega_n}\circ\cdots\circ\Phi_{\omega_1}\) and \(L_n:=L(\Phi_n;K)\). Assume that \(L_n\) is measurable for every \(n\ge1\), and that 
\[\sup_{\omega}L(\Phi_{\omega};K)\le B\] 
for some deterministic \(B\ge1\). Then the conclusions of Theorem~\ref{thm:main-pressure} remain valid after replacing \(N_n\), \(X_n\), \(\Lambda\), \(I_\pm\), and \(\log 2\) by \(L_n\), \(Z_n:=n^{-1}\log L_n\), \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{line}}\), \(I_{\mathrm{line},\pm}\), and \(\log B\), respectively, where
\[
\Lambda_{\mathrm{line}}(q):=\lim_{n\to\infty} n^{-1}\log\mathbb E[L_n^q]
\]
and \(I_{\mathrm{line},\pm}\) are defined from \(\Lambda_{\mathrm{line}}\) exactly as in Theorem~\ref{thm:main-pressure}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Worst-line pressure in higher dimension

[Lem 9 of arXiv:2606.27078, 'Semimartingale Optimal Transport with Jumps: A General Framework and Equivalent Formulatio'] Let $\Theta \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d \times \mathbb{S}_+^d \times \mathcal{L}$ be measurable. For any $\overline{\mathbb{P}} \in \overline{\mathfrak{P}}_{\Theta}^{t,x,b,c,v}$ and any $\overline{\mathbb{F}}$-stopping time $\overline{\tau}$ taking values in $[t,1]$, the following hold.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(1)]\text{(Conditioning property.)} There exists a family of regular conditional probability measures $(\overline{\mathbb{P}}_{\overline{\omega}})_{\overline{\omega}\in\overline{\Omega}}$ of $\overline{\mathbb{P}}$ given $\overline{\mathcal{F}}_{\overline{\tau}}$ such that for $\overline{\mathbb{P}}$-almost every $\overline{\omega} \in \overline{\Omega}$,
\[
\overline{\mathbb{P}}^{\overline{\tau},\overline{\omega}}(\cdot)
:=\overline{\mathbb{P}}_{\overline{\omega}}\bigl(\overline{\omega}\otimes_{\overline{\tau}}\tilde{\omega}\mid\tilde{\omega}\in\cdot\bigr)
\]
belongs to 
$\overline{\mathfrak{P}}_{\Theta}^{\overline{\tau}(\overline{\omega}), \overline{\omega}_{\overline{\tau}(\overline{\omega})}}$.
\item[(2)]\text{(Concatenation property.)} Let $\{\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{\omega}}\}_{\overline{\omega}\in\overline{\Omega}}$ be a family of probability measures such that
\[
\overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{\omega}} \in \overline{\mathfrak{P}}_{\Theta}^{\overline{\tau}(\overline{\omega}), \overline{\omega}_{\overline{\tau}(\overline{\omega})}}
\quad \text{for } \overline{\mathbb{P}}\text{-a.e. } \overline{\omega},
\]
and the mapping $\overline{\omega} \mapsto \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{\omega}}$ is $\overline{\mathcal{F}}_{\overline{\tau}}$-measurable. Then the concatenated measure
\[
(\overline{\mathbb{P}} \otimes_{\overline{\tau}} \overline{\mathbb{Q}})(\cdot) := \int_{\overline{\Omega}} \overline{\mathbb{Q}}_{\overline{\omega}}(\cdot) \, \overline{\mathbb{P}}(\mathrm{d}\overline{\omega})
\]
satisfies $\overline{\mathbb{P}} \otimes_{\overline{\tau}} \overline{\mathbb{Q}} \in \overline{\mathfrak{P}}_{\Theta}^{t,x,b,c,v}$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 9 of arXiv:2606.27078

[Lemma lem:gen-error-polynomial-regression of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] Suppose that $\{(x_i,y_i)\}_{i\le n}$ is an i.i.d. dataset drawn from the distribution $\mu$, such that $\EE_\mu[y^4]<\infty$ and $\EE_\mu[|x^\alpha|]<\infty$ for all multi-index $\alpha$. 
Let $\cH$ be a class of functions from $\RR^d$ to $\RR$ such that any $f\in \cH$ is in $L^2(\mu)$.  
Suppose that for every $f\in \cH$, there is a polynomial $p$ of degree $D$ such that $\EE[|f(x) - p(x)|^2]^{1/2} \le \varepsilon$. 
Then there exists an algorithm that takes $O\Big( \varepsilon^{-3} d^{D} \log(1/\varepsilon) \cdot \log(1/\delta)\Big)$ samples and computes a hypothesis $\hath$ in $\mathrm{poly}(d,D,1/\varepsilon)$ time such that, with probability at least $1-\delta$ over the dataset, it holds that $\EE[\ell (y, \hat h(x))] \le \mathrm{opt}_\cH + \varepsilon$, where $\mathrm{opt}_\cH = \inf_{f\in \cH} \EE[\ell(y,f(x))]$.
title: Lemma lem:gen-error-polynomial-regression of arXiv:2512.04371

[Definition 24 of arXiv:2606.31455, 'Discrete time-multidimensional renewal theory and applications'] Let $\lambda_1,\lambda_2>0$ and $0\le \rho<1$.
A random vector $(X_1,X_2)$ taking values in $\mathbb{R}_+^2$ is said to follow the
Moran--Downton bivariate exponential distribution if it has joint density
\begin{equation}
f_{X_1,X_2}(x_1,x_2)
=
\frac{\lambda_1\lambda_2}{1-\rho}
\exp\!\left(-\frac{\lambda_1 x_1+\lambda_2 x_2}{1-\rho}\right)\,
I_0\!\left(\frac{2\sqrt{\rho\,\lambda_1\lambda_2\,x_1x_2}}{1-\rho}\right),
\qquad x_1,x_2\in\mathbb{R}_+,
\end{equation}
where $I_0$ is the modified Bessel function of the first kind of order $0$,
\[
I_0(z)=\sum_{m=0}^\infty \frac{1}{(m!)^2}\left(\frac{z}{2}\right)^{2m}.
\]
Under the rate parametrization used in \eqref{eq:downton-pdf}, the marginals are exponential
with rates $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2$, and $\rho=0$ yields independence.
(Alternative scale parametrizations appear in the literature; see, e.g.,
\cite{downton1970bivariate,hanandeh2013inference}.)

Let X have joint density or pmf f(x;theta) for a scalar parameter theta in an open subset of R, satisfying regularity conditions under which differentiation with respect to theta may be passed under the integral/sum sign, both for the normalization condition and for computing E_theta[T(X)]. Let T(X) be any statistic with finite variance used to estimate g(theta) for a differentiable function g, and let b(theta) = E_theta[T(X)] - g(theta) be its bias, assumed differentiable in theta. Then Var_theta(T(X)) >= (g'(theta) + b'(theta))^2 / I(theta), where I(theta) = E_theta[ (d/dtheta log f(X;theta))^2 ] is the Fisher information, assumed finite and positive. In particular, if T is unbiased for theta itself (g(theta)=theta, b=0), then Var_theta(T(X)) >= 1/I(theta).

body:
Standard approximation arguments in L^p silently use p < infinity. On R^n with Lebesgue measure: (1) DENSITY. Continuous compactly supported functions are dense in L^p for 1 <= p < infinity, but their closure in L^infinity is C_0(R^n) (continuous functions vanishing at infinity), a proper closed subspace; L^infinity(R^n) is not separable, while L^p(R^n) is for p < infinity. (Simple functions are dense in L^p for every p including infinity; simple functions with support of FINITE measure are dense only for p < infinity.) (2) MOLLIFICATION. If phi is an approximate identity then phi_eps * f -> f in L^p for 1 <= p < infinity, but not in L^infinity: for f = 1_{[0,infinity)} each phi_eps * f is continuous, and any continuous g satisfies ||g - f||_infinity >= 1/2, so the convergence fails; in L^infinity one only gets convergence at points of continuity (and weak-* convergence). (3) TRANSLATION. h -> f(. - h) is continuous from R^n to L^p for p < infinity; in L^infinity it is not: for f = 1_{[0,infinity)}, ||f(. - h) - f||_infinity = 1 for every h not equal to 0. Consequences for proofs: any argument that proves an estimate for nice functions and 'passes to the limit by density', or that uses continuity of translation (Riemann-Lebesgue, convolution identities, Lebesgue differentiation via density), must be carried out in L^p with p < infinity, or re-done by a separate weak-* / pointwise argument at p = infinity.
Lebesgue measure on R^n (for a general Radon measure on a locally compact Hausdorff space, density of C_c in L^p, p < infinity, still holds)
1 <= p <= infinity as indicated
title: Pitfall: density, mollification and continuity of translation require p < infinity

[Lemma 19 (Maximal moment estimate for stable stochastic integrals) of arXiv:2608.17540, 'Pathwise stability for one-dimensional SDEs driven by Brownian motion and a symmetric stab'] Let $\gamma=(\gamma_s)_{0\le s\le T}$ be predictable and satisfy
\[
  \E\int_0^T |\gamma_s|^\alpha\dd s<\infty.
\]
Define
\[
  M_t:=\int_0^t\int_{\R\setminus\{0\}}\gamma_s z\,\wt N(\md s,\md z).
\]
Then, for every $p\in(0,\alpha)$, there is a constant $C_{p,\alpha}$ such that
\[
  \E\sup_{0\le t\le T}|M_t|^p
  \le C_{p,\alpha}\left(\E\int_0^T |\gamma_s|^\alpha\dd s\right)^{p/\alpha}.
\]

body:
[Lemma aux-lem of arXiv:2507.01406, '{\Large On Iterated Lorenz Curves with Applications: The Multivariate Case }'] Let $f(x,v)$ be a family of probability densities on $
\mathcal{X}\times \mathcal{V}$, where $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{V}$ are
intervals in $R$. Assume the following:

($RR_{2}$ Property) For any $v_{1},v_{2}\in \mathcal{V}$ with $v_{1}<v_{2}$,
the likelihood ratio $L(x)=f(x,v_{2})/f(x,v_{1})$ is non-increasing in $x$.

(Regularity and Strict Log-Concavity) For each fixed $v\in \mathcal{V}$, the
log-density $g(x,v)=\log f(x,v)$ is a real-analytic and strictly log-concave
function of $x$ on the interior of its support.

(Non-degeneracy) For every pair $v_{1}<v_{2}$, the function $x\mapsto
g(x,v_{2})-g(x,v_{1})$ is not constant over the interior of the common
support.

Then the kernel $f(x,v)$ has the strict $RR_{2}$ property ($SRR_{2}$). That
is, for any $v_{1}<v_{2}$, the ratio $L(x)$ is strictly decreasing in $x$
over the interior of their common support.

[Definition 1 of arXiv:2608.30223, 'Fairness in Multi-class Multi-group Classification Problems via Contextual Coherent Risk M'] A lower semi-continuous functional $\varrho: \Lc_p(\Omega, \Fc, P;\Rb^M) \to \Rb\cup\{+\infty\}$ is a systemic coherent risk measure with preference to small outcomes if it satisfies the following properties:
        \begin{itemize}
            \item[A1.] \emph{Convexity:} For all $Z, Z' \in \Lc_p(\Omega, \Fc, P;\Rb^M)$ and $ \alpha \in (0,1)$, the following holds\\
                $ ~ \varrho[\alpha Z + (1-\alpha)Z'] \leq \alpha \varrho[Z] + (1 - \alpha)\varrho[Z']. $
            \item[A2.] \emph{Monotonicity:} For all $Z, Z' \in \Lc_p(\Omega, \Fc, P;\Rb^M)$, if $Z_i \geq Z'_i$ for all components $i = 1, \dots, M$, $P$-a.s., then $\varrho[Z] \geq \varrho[Z']$.
            \item[A3.] \emph{Positive homogeneity:} For all $Z \in \Lc_p(\Omega, \Fc, P;\Rb^M)$ and all constants $t > 0$, the relation $\varrho[tX] = t\varrho[X]$ holds.
            \item[A4.] \emph{Translation equivariance:} For all $Z \in \Lc_p(\Omega, \Fc, P;\Rb^M)$ and for all constants $a \in \Rb$, the following relation holds $\varrho[Z + a\one] = \varrho[Z] + a\varrho[\one].$
        \end{itemize}

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2604.22257, 'On necessary and sufficient conditions for the local large deviation principle'] {\rm (i)}~In the general case, if  the LDP is satisfied for a family of random vectors then the LLDP with the same rate function~$D$ is also satisfied for that family.

{\rm (ii)}~The converse implication holds true provided that the following condition is met{\rm :}  for any $N>0$ there exists a $v>0$ such that

[Definition 2 of arXiv:2609.04139, 'The conformally invariant metric on CLE$_4$ II:\\ existence of geodesics'] We define a \emph{geodesic CLE$_4$ metric coupling} to be a family of couplings
	\begin{equation*}
	 	D = \left\{\left( \Gamma_U, D_{\Gamma_U}^U \right)\right\}_U
	\end{equation*}
	where $U \subsetneq \BC$ ranges over all simply connected domains and $\Gamma_U$ is a non-nested CLE$_4$ in $U$, such that:
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\Roman*), ref=\Roman*]
		\item {\bfseries (Geodesic metric)} $D_{\Gamma_U}^U$ is a.s.\ a metric on $\Gamma_U$ such that the following hold.
			\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), ref=\roman*]
				\item For each $\SCL_1, \SCL_2 \in \Gamma_U$, there exists an admissible path $P$ (which we refer to as a \emph{$D_{\Gamma_U}^U$-geodesic}) connecting $\SCL_1$ and $\SCL_2$ such that $D_{\Gamma_U}^U(\SCL_1, \SCL_2) = \len(P; D_{\Gamma_U}^U)$. The same is true with a deterministic connected arc (resp.\ two deterministic and disjoint connected arcs) of $\partial U$ in place of $\SCL_1$ (resp.\ $\SCL_1$ and $\SCL_2$).
				\item Let $\phi\colon U \to \BD$ be a conformal mapping. For every $\SCL \in \Gamma_U$, the process $(\phi(\SCB_t(\SCL; D^U_{\Gamma_U}){)})_{t\ge 0}$ is c\`adl\`ag for the Hausdorff distance, and the same is true with a deterministic connected arc of $\partial U$ in place of $\SCL$.
				\item For all $t, s\ge 0$, if $\SCB_t(\SCL_1; D^U_{\Gamma_U}) \cap \SCB_s(\SCL_2; D^U_{\Gamma_U}) \neq \emptyset$, then $D^U_{\Gamma_U} (\SCL_1, \SCL_2) \le t+s$. The same is true with a deterministic connected arc (resp.\ two deterministic and disjoint connected arcs) of $\partial U$ in place of $\SCL_1$ (resp.\ $\SCL_1$ and $\SCL_2$).
			\end{enumerate}
			Note that $\len(P; D_{\Gamma_U}^U) \ge D_{\Gamma_U}^U(\SCL_1,\SCL_2)$ for every admissible path $P$ connecting $\SCL_1$ and $\SCL_2$, by the triangle inequality along the chains in the definition of $\len$; a path attaining equality is thus 
			what the term geodesic refers to. 
		\item {\bfseries (Locality)} Let $V \subset U$ be a deterministic simply connected subdomain. Let $I \subset \partial U$ be a deterministic connected arc. Let $\{V_j\}_j$ be the connected components of $V^\star$. Then, conditionally on
				\begin{multline}
					\bigl\{\SCL \in \Gamma_U : \SCL \not\subset V\bigr\}, \quad \bigl\{\SCB_t(\SCL; D_{\Gamma_U}^U) : \SCL \in \Gamma_U, \ \SCL \not\subset V, \ t \in [0, D_{\Gamma_U}^U(\SCL, \partial V^\star)]\bigr\}, \\
					\text{and} \quad \bigl\{\SCB_t(I; D_{\Gamma_U}^U) : t \in [0, D_{\Gamma_U}^U(I, \partial V^\star)]\bigr\},
				\end{multline}
			the $(\Gamma_U|_{V_j}, D_{\Gamma_U}^U(\bullet, \bullet; V_j))$'s are independent and their conditional laws are those of $(\Gamma_{V_j}, D_{\Gamma_{V_j}}^{V_j})$, respectively. 
		\item {\bfseries (Conformal invariance)} Let $\phi \colon U \to \phi(U)$ be a deterministic conformal mapping. Then,
		\begin{equation*}
			\left(\phi(\Gamma_U), \left( D_{\Gamma_U}^U\left(\phi^{-1}(\SCL_1), \phi^{-1}(\SCL_2) \right) \right)_{\SCL_1, \SCL_2 \in \phi(\Gamma_U)} \right)
			 \overset{(\mathrm{d})}{=} \left( \Gamma_{\phi(U)}, \left(D_{\Gamma_{\phi(U)}}^{\phi(U)}(\SCL_1, \SCL_2) \right)_{\SCL_1, \SCL_2 \in \Gamma_{\phi(U)}} \right).
		\end{equation*}
		The equality in law is understood as in \Cref{def:weak_axioms}.
		
			
				
				
			
		
		
			
			
		\item {\bfseries (Uniform exploration)} The collection $\{(\SCL, D_{\Gamma_U}^U(\SCL, \partial U))\}_{\SCL \in \Gamma_U}$ has the law of a uniform exploration of $\Gamma_U$ (cf.~\cite{CoInCLEExpl}), in the sense of \Cref{def:weak_axioms}.
	\end{enumerate}
title: Definition 2 of arXiv:2609.04139

[Thm 8 (CLT for the normalized traces) of arXiv:2604.26499, 'Spectrum of Random Matrices with Exploding Moments'] Let $M$ be the block diagonal matrix defined in 
\eqref{eqn: main definition of block matrix M} satisfying 
Condition \ref{cond: Correlated Block matrix} with $\alpha=1$. 
For any partition $\pi\in \bigcup_{k\ge1}\mathcal P(k)$, let $Z_N(T_{\pi})$ be defined as in \eqref{eq: Z_N T pi}. Then the family of random variables
$
\big(Z_N(T_\pi)\big)_{\pi\in\bigcup_{k}\mathcal{P}(k)}
$
converges to a centered Gaussian process $\big(z(T_\pi)\big)_{\pi\in\bigcup_{k}\mathcal{P}(k)}$ as $N \rightarrow \infty$. 
Moreover, for any two partitions $\pi_1,\pi_2$, the limiting covariance is given by
\begin{align}
\mathrm{Cov}\left(z(T_{\pi_1}),z(T_{\pi_2})\right)
&=
\sum_{r_1,r_2 \in \{1,2\}}\sum_{T \in\mathcal{P}^{\#}(T_{\pi_1}^{(r_1)},T_{\pi_2}^{(r_2)})} \tau^b[T],
\end{align}
where the expression of $\tau^b[T]$ is given in \eqref{eq:covariance kerne for block matrix model}. Here $\mathcal{P}^{\#}(T_{\pi_1}^{(r_1)}, T_{\pi_2}^{(r_2)})$ denotes the collection of graphs obtained by disjoint copies of the graphs $T_{\pi_1}^{(r_1)}$ and $T_{\pi_2}^{(r_2)}$ and gluing them with at least one common edge.

[Proposition 34 of arXiv:2506.10494, 'Geometric Jensen-Shannon Divergence Between Gaussian Measures On Hilbert Space'] [\textbf{Normalizing factor}]
	
	Assume the hypothesis of Theorem \ref{theorem:geometric-interpolation-equivalent-Gaussian-Hilbert-space}.
	Assume further that $S_i \in \SymTr(\Hcal)_{< I}$, $i=0,1$. Then the normalizing factor $Z_{\alpha}^G(p_0:p_1)$ is given by
	\begin{align}
		&Z_{\alpha}^G(p_0:p_1) \doteq \int_{\Hcal}p_0^{1-\alpha}(x)p_1^{\alpha}(x) \; d\mu_{*}(x)
		\nonumber
		\\
		& =  [\det(I-S_0)]^{-\frac{1-\alpha}{2}}[\det(I-S_1)]^{-\frac{\alpha}{2}}
		\nonumber
		\\
		& \quad \times \exp\left[-\frac{1-\alpha}{2}||(I-S_0)^{-1/2}C_{*}^{-1/2}(m_0 - m_{*})||^2\right]
		\nonumber
		\\
		& \quad \times 
		\exp\left[-\frac{\alpha}{2}||(I-S_1)^{-1/2}C_{*}^{-1/2}(m_1 - m_{*})||^2\right]
		\nonumber
		\\
		&\quad \times \det(I-S_{\alpha})^{1/2}\exp\left(\frac{1}{2}||(I-S_{\alpha})^{-1/2}C_{*}^{-1/2}(m_{\alpha} - m_{*})||^2\right).
		
	\end{align}
Equivalently, with $I + A = (I-S_1)^{-1/2}(I-S_0)(I-S_1)^{-1/2} > 0$, with $A =(I-S_1)^{-1/2}(S_1-S_0)(I-S_1)^{-1/2}$, then $Z_{\alpha}^G(p_0:p_1)$ is given by
\begin{align}
	&Z_{\alpha}^G(p_0:p_1)
	\nonumber
	\\
	
	
	&= \det[(1-\alpha)(I+A)^{-\alpha} + \alpha (I+A)^{1-\alpha}]^{-1/2}
	\nonumber
	\\
	& \quad \times \exp\left[-\frac{1-\alpha}{2}||(I-S_0)^{-1/2}C_{*}^{-1/2}(m_0 - m_{*})||^2\right]
	\nonumber
	\\
	& \quad \times 
	\exp\left[-\frac{\alpha}{2}||(I-S_1)^{-1/2}C_{*}^{-1/2}(m_1 - m_{*})||^2\right]
	\nonumber
	\\
	& \quad \times \exp\left(\frac{1}{2}||(I-S_{\alpha})^{-1/2}C_{*}^{-1/2}(m_{\alpha} - m_{*})||^2\right).
	
\end{align}
Furthermore, this expression is valid for $S_i \in  \SymHS(\Hcal)_{< I}$, $i=0,1$.

body:
Let lambda* denote Lebesgue outer measure on R^d, defined by lambda*(E) = inf of sum of volumes of countably many open boxes covering E, let L be the sigma-algebra of Caratheodory-measurable (Lebesgue measurable) sets, and let lambda = lambda* restricted to L. Then: (1) OUTER REGULARITY, valid for EVERY set E contained in R^d, measurable or not: lambda*(E) = inf { lambda(U) : U open, U contains E }. (2) MEASURABILITY CRITERION: E is in L if and only if for every eps > 0 there is an open U containing E with lambda*(U \ E) < eps, if and only if there is a G_delta set G containing E with lambda(G \ E) = 0, if and only if there is an F_sigma set F contained in E with lambda(E \ F) = 0. (3) INNER REGULARITY by compact sets, valid for every E in L: lambda(E) = sup { lambda(K) : K compact, K contained in E } (both sides may be +infinity). Equivalently, for E in L with lambda(E) < infinity and eps > 0 there is a compact K contained in E with lambda(E \ K) < eps. Thus lambda is a Radon measure: it is finite on compacta, outer regular and inner regular. (4) COMPLETENESS: if lambda*(N) = 0 then N is in L and lambda(N) = 0, and hence every subset of a null set is measurable with measure zero. Equivalently, (R^d, L, lambda) is the completion of (R^d, Borel, lambda|Borel): L = { B union Z : B Borel, Z a subset of a Borel null set }. SHARP EDGES. (a) The Borel sigma-algebra itself is NOT complete: the Cantor set is Borel and null, it has 2^continuum subsets, all of them Lebesgue null and hence Lebesgue measurable, while there are only continuum many Borel sets; so L is strictly larger than the Borel sigma-algebra, and 'measurable' must never be silently upgraded to 'Borel'. (b) Regularity statements about the MEASURE are for measurable sets. Outer regularity in the form (1) does hold for arbitrary sets because it is the definition of the outer measure, but inner regularity fails badly for non-measurable sets: a Vitali set has inner measure 0 and positive outer measure, so the two approximations do not meet. It is exactly the meeting of the two that measurability expresses. (c) Completeness is what makes 'a.e. defined' harmless: if f = g almost everywhere and f is measurable then g is measurable. That inference is FALSE in the Borel sigma-algebra, and is a frequent silent error. (d) Regularity is not automatic for general Borel measures: on a non-sigma-compact or non-locally-compact space a finite Borel measure need not be inner regular by compact sets. Lebesgue measure is regular because R^d is sigma-compact, locally compact and second countable, and because lambda is finite on boxes. (e) Not every set is measurable: the existence of a non-measurable set uses the axiom of choice, and translation invariance plus countable additivity forbid extending lambda to all subsets of R^d.
the ambient space is R^d with Lebesgue outer measure defined by countable covers by boxes
L is the sigma-algebra of Caratheodory-measurable sets and lambda = lambda* restricted to L
R^d is sigma-compact, locally compact and second countable, and lambda is finite on bounded sets - this is what drives regularity
the axiom of choice is used only for the remark that non-measurable sets exist

In the stipulated planar Gaussian displacement-increment model with Fourier covariance beta^{-1}1_{0<|k|<=Lambda}[P_L(k)/(a|k|^s)+P_T(k)/(b|k|^2)] and inverse Fourier measure d^2k/(2pi)^2, let delta rho=-rho div u. Then Var(delta rho(0))=rho^2 Lambda^{4-s}/[2pi beta a(4-s)]>0; rho+delta rho is negative infinitely often on any fixed equally spaced ray almost surely. Therefore it cannot have the exact one-point law of a finite smoothing sum of any locally finite point configuration with a nonnegative kernel. This concerns only the auxiliary Gaussian model, not an actual Riesz Gibbs law or a controlled approximation.

[Theo eq:coupling-intro-node of arXiv:2607.01877, 'Coupling some conditioned L\'evy trees with the Kesten tree'] We assume the infinite variation setting and the Grey condition, as well as the Lévy measure $\pi$ has no atom and full support in $(0, + \infty)$. 
The (sub-)critical Lévy tree ${\mathcal T}$ conditioned under the excursion measure to have maximal vertex ``size'' $\delta$, say ${\mathcal T}^{\mathbf{\mathrm{node}}}_\delta$, with its only vertex $X_\delta$ of ``size'' $\delta$
is distributed as $({\mathcal K}^{\mathbf{\mathrm{node}}}_\delta,H_\delta)$:
\begin{equation}
    
({\mathcal T}^{\mathbf{\mathrm{node}}}_\delta, X_\delta)
   \, \overset{\text{(d)}}{=} \,
   ({\mathcal K}^{\mathbf{\mathrm{node}}}_\delta, H_\delta)
   \quad\text{and}\quad
   {\mathcal T}^{\mathbf{\mathrm{node}},*}_\delta
   \, \overset{\text{(d)}}{=} \,
{\mathcal K}^{\mathbf{\mathrm{node}},*}_\delta.
\end{equation}
Furthermore in the critical case, 
 the ``increasing'' sequence $({\mathcal K}^{\mathbf{\mathrm{node}},*}_\delta)_{h\ge 0}$  converges  to the Kesten tree ${\mathcal K}$ in $({\mathbb T}, {d_\mathrm {LGH}})$, and we have the following  local   convergence in distribution:
 \begin{equation}
   
      {\mathcal T}^{\mathbf{\mathrm{node}}}_\delta  \xrightarrow[\delta \rightarrow
   +\infty]{\text{(d)}}
      {\mathcal K}
     \quad\text{in}\quad
  ({\mathbb T}, {d_\mathrm {LGH}}).
 \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Conditioning w.r.t.\ the maximal vertex ``size''

 =\bigl(E_{\Lambda}\otimes_{\R}\C\bigr)^*.

\[
\zeta_{\omega_1,\eta_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes
\zeta_{\omega_r,\eta_r}
\]
with $\omega_j\in\Lambda$ and $\eta_j\in W^*$ separate $E_{\Lambda}^{\otimes r}$.

[Definition 9 (Angle conditions (Z1)--(Z4)\cite{GeRCP}) of arXiv:2608.03575, '2608.03575'] Let $(G,\Theta)$ be an ADT. When needed, the following conditions are imposed
\begin{enumerate}[(Z1)]
\item If $e_1,e_2,e_3$ are the three edges forming the boundary of a triangular face and
\[\Theta(e_1)+\Theta(e_2)+\Theta(e_3)>\pi,\]
then for every permutation $\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}$ we have
\[\Theta(e_i)+\Theta(e_j)<\pi+\Theta(e_k).\]

\item If $e_1,e_2,\dots,e_s$ form a simple closed curve in $G$ that is not the boundary of any triangular face, then
\[\sum_{i=1}^s \Theta(e_i) < (s-2)\pi.\]

\item If $e_1$ and $e_2$ are \emph{homologically non-adjacent} edges in $G$, then
\[\Theta(e_1)+\Theta(e_2)<\pi.\]
where an arc $\Gamma$ formed by two adjacent edges in $E$ is called homologically adjacent if there is an edge in $E$ that connects the two endpoints of $\Gamma$. Conversely, we call it homologically non-adjacent.

\item If $e_1,e_2,e_3$ are the three edges forming the boundary of a triangular face, then for every permutation $\{i,j,k\}=\{1,2,3\}$ we have
\[\cos\Theta(e_i)+\cos\Theta(e_j)\cos\Theta(e_k)\ge 0.\]
\end{enumerate}
title: Angle conditions (Z1)--(Z4)\cite{GeRCP}

      \max_{0\leq s\leq T}
      \abs{\mathscr H_{T_\eta+s}^{(N)}-h_+}>\eta
    \right)
    \leq
    C(1+T)\exp(-c_0N).

    \Pp\left(
      \tau_\varrho^{(N)}
      >
      T_\eta+\lfloor\exp(c_1N)\rfloor
    \right)
    \to1 .
  \end{equation}
  For every fixed $N$, however, the chain is eventually absorbed almost surely
  from every deterministic initial state.

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For the Ising model, or more generally ferromagnetic spin systems with finite-range or summable interactions, let G(x,y) = <sigma_x sigma_y> be the two-point function. The Simon-Lieb inequality bounds G(x,y) across any finite set Lambda separating x from y (x in Lambda, y outside Lambda) by G(x,y) <= sum_{u in Lambda, v not in Lambda, u~v} G(x,u) J_{uv} G(v,y), a one-step recursive bound relating the two-point function across a separating surface to the two-point function up to the boundary of Lambda times the coupling crossing it. Iterating the inequality over a sequence of nested separating sets, such as concentric boxes, yields exponential decay of G(x,y) once the associated generating function drops below its self-consistency threshold, giving a classical route, predating and complementary to the Duminil-Copin-Tassion approach, to sharpness of the phase transition and analyticity of the free energy in the high-temperature regime. It does not determine the exact critical temperature directly, only characterizing it implicitly through the inequality's self-consistency condition, and it applies specifically to ferromagnetic spin systems with a workable notion of finite separating surfaces; it does not transfer automatically to percolation, which uses combinatorially different, though philosophically related, inequalities. Typical failure: Iterating the Simon-Lieb inequality across many nested separating surfaces while implicitly assuming a geometric decay rate that has not actually been verified to be summable; turning the one-step recursive bound into exponential decay requires checking that the relevant generating function, summing G times J over the boundary, lies strictly below its self-consistency threshold, and this check is exactly where the difficulty of locating beta_c resides, so skipping it silently assumes the conclusion. Canonical reference: Simon, 1980, Communications in Mathematical Physics; Lieb, 1980, Communications in Mathematical Physics.

[4 10 of arXiv:2607.12303, 'Marginal Stationary Distributions and Convergence Rates of Higher Order Markov Chains'] Suppose that $\mathcal{W}$ is a joint stationary distribution of an $(m-1)$th order Markov chain  $\{X_t\}_{t=1}^{\infty}$ on state space $S$ with transition tensor $\mathcal{P}$ and $\pi$ is the  marginal stationary distribution defined by $\mathcal{W}$. If the chain starts with $Y_1=(X_{m-1}, \ldots, X_1)$ that has the joint distribution $\mathcal{Z}^{(1)}=\mathcal{W}$, then the joint distribution ${\cal Z}^{(t)}$ of $Y_t=(X_{t+m-2}, \ldots, X_t)$ satisfies
$$
\mathcal{Z}^{(t)} = \mathcal{W}
$$
for all $t \ge 1$. Furthermore, let $\beta^{(t)} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ be the marginal distribution of $X_{t+m-2}$ in $Y_t$, that is, 
$$
\beta^{(t)}_i=\sum_{i_2, \ldots, i_{m-1} \in S} z^{(t)}_{i i_2 \ldots i_{m-1}}, \ \ i \in S.
$$
Then we have
$$
\beta^{(t)} = \pi, 
$$
for all $t \ge 1$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: 4 10 of arXiv:2607.12303

[Theorem thm:max_string of arXiv:2607.22291, 'Rare subtree patterns in size-conditioned Bienaymé trees: Poisson approximation and declum'] Assume that $\mu$ is critical and belongs to the domain of attraction of a stable law.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] Assume that $\mu_{1}>0$.  Set
$$t_n^* = \frac{1}{\log(1/\mu_{1})} \log n + \frac{1}{\log(1/\mu_{1})} \log(1-\mu_1).$$
For every $t \in \mathbb{R}$ we have 
$$\P\bigl(H_{1} ( \mathcal{T}^{n})  \leq \lfloor t_n^* + t\rfloor\bigr) - \exp\bigl(-\mu_1^{t+1 - \{t_n^* + t\}}\bigr)   \quad \mathop{\longrightarrow}_{n \rightarrow \infty} \quad  0$$
\item[(ii)] Let $r\ge2$ be such that $\mu_r>0$, and set
$$
  t_n^{**}=\log_r\log n-
  \log_r\left(\frac{\log(1/\mu_r)}{r-1}\right).
$$
Write $m_n=\lfloor t_n^{**}\rfloor$ and
$\theta_n=\{t_n^{**}\}$, where $\{x\} = x - \lfloor x \rfloor$ is the fractional part, and define
$$
  J_n=
  \begin{cases}
    \{m_n-1,m_n\},&\theta_n\le\tfrac12,\\
    \{m_n,m_n+1\},&\theta_n>\tfrac12.
  \end{cases}
$$
Then $
  \P(H_r(\mathcal T^n)\in J_n)\longrightarrow1$.
Moreover, if $\liminf_n\min(\theta_n,1-\theta_n)>0$, then
$\P(H_r(\mathcal T^n)=m_n)\to1$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let n ≥ 3 be odd, put m = (n+1)/2, and let u0 ∈ C^{m+1}(R^n), u1 ∈ C^m(R^n) both vanish outside the closed ball B̄(0,R). Let u be the (unique) C² solution of ∂_t²u − Δu = 0 with these data. Then u(t,x) = 0 whenever |x| > t + R (finite speed) and also whenever |x| < t − R. Equivalently: u(t,x) depends only on the data on the sphere ∂B(x,t), not on the data inside the ball B(x,t); a compactly supported disturbance produces a signal supported in the spherical shell t − R ≤ |x| ≤ t + R, which passes and leaves no residue.
n odd and n ≥ 3
u0 ∈ C^{(n+3)/2}(R^n), u1 ∈ C^{(n+1)/2}(R^n)
data supported in B̄(0,R)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Try to control the finite-cluster susceptibility above p_c via the lace expansion with a cluster-size cutoff. Result: Above p_c the finite-cluster two-point function tau^f(x) = P(0 <-> x, |C(0)| < infinity) is not directly lace-expandable because the finite-cluster condition is not local; the standard route is through the h -> 0 limit of the magnetisation, whose derivatives in h at fixed p > p_c give the finite-cluster moments. The scaling relation gamma' = gamma follows if the magnetisation M(p,h) has a scaling form M ~ (p - p_c) f(h / (p - p_c)^Delta) with the same Delta on both sides, which is the mean-field prediction; the mean-field magnetisation satisfies M ~ (p-p_c) + sqrt(h) crossover, and the finite-cluster susceptibility above p_c would then be chi^f ~ (p - p_c)^{-1}, i.e. gamma' = 1. A rigorous one-sided bound is available: chi^f(p) >= c/(p - p_c) from the differential inequality of Aizenman-Barsky applied above p_c (since dtheta/dp is bounded by chi^f up to constants and theta ~ (p - p_c)); the matching upper bound needs the finite-cluster expansion. So gamma' >= 1 in the bounded-ratio sense is rigorous; gamma' <= 1 is the open half. Similarly nu' >= nu follows from the lower bound on the finite-cluster correlation length via the same inequality chain. Key identity: dtheta/dp <= C chi^f(p) and theta ~ (p - p_c) give chi^f(p) >= c/(p - p_c), i.e. gamma' >= 1 in the ratio sense. Obstruction: No expansion for finite-cluster quantities above p_c; only the lower bounds are rigorous.

        \widetilde d^2=\chi^2=\widetilde d\chi+\chi\widetilde d=0.

Version 1, Target 1, kind bound; proofs (unaudited), 20 October 2026.

## C033: discrete-time semigroup subtraction

Let a=1/(3pi), b=1/(6pi^2), and A,B be the differential operators in C032.
One step of duration 1/n has P_n=I+A/n+B/n^2+O(n^(-5/2)) on positive
compacts. A diffusion step has exp(A/n)=I+A/n+A^2/(2n^2)+O(n^-3), for
sufficiently smooth local tests. Thus the local weak-error operator is

    C=B-A^2/2
     =(8u+a/5+b/u)D+(4u^2-3au/5)D^2.               (3)

This is an algebraic identity, not a global semigroup expansion at zero.
Direct differentiation gives

    A^2=(4u+2a)D+(14u^2+6au+a^2)D^2
                  +(8u^3+2au^2)D^3+u^4 D^4.

Subtracting half of this from C032's B proves (3); the third- and fourth-
derivative terms cancel exactly. Their inclusion before subtraction was
necessary. A global modified diffusion with this C is not asserted:
the drift b/u is singular and its second-order coefficient can be negative
near zero at finite n.

## C034: a rigorous logarithmic divergence of the limiting Duhamel functional

Use the reviewer-PASS C017 diffusion dU=(2U+a)ds+sqrt(2)U dW, U0=0,
and its semigroup P_s. Fix t>0 and f(u)=1-exp(-u). Define, for 0<epsilon<t,

    I_epsilon(t)=integral_epsilon^t E[(C P_(t-s)f)(U_s)] ds,
    D_t=(D P_t f)(0)=E[J_t exp(-U_t)],
    J_t=exp(t+sqrt(2)W_t).

Then 0<D_t<infinity, and there is a finite H_t such that

    I_epsilon(t)=(D_t/(2pi))log(1/epsilon)+H_t+O_t(sqrt(epsilon)). (4)

This statement concerns the specified cutoff integral for the limiting SDE.
It does not replace epsilon by 1/n inside a network weak-error theorem.

Proof of regularity. The solution from initial value u is U_v^u=U_v^0+uJ_v.
Consequently D^j P_v f(u)=E[J_v^j f^(j)(U_v^0+uJ_v)] for j>=1.
All these derivatives are bounded uniformly for 0<=v<=t, because Gaussian
exponentials J_v have every positive moment. Differentiation under expectation
is justified by these dominating moments. The time derivative of D P_v f
is bounded too: Af and (Af)' are bounded (polynomials times exp(-u)), and
the semigroup identity P_v f-f=integral_0^v P_r Af dr allows differentiation
in u. In particular, with h(s,u)=D P_(t-s) f(u),

    |h(s,u)-D_t|<=C_t(s+u), 0<=s<=t, u>=0.          (5)

The same bounded-derivative estimates apply to D^2 P_(t-s)f.

Proof of the entrance estimate. The explicit solution gives

    U_s=a integral_0^s exp((s-r)+sqrt(2)(W_s-W_r)) dr.

Let M_s=sup_(r<=s)|W_r| and H_s=s+2sqrt(2)M_s. Then
exp(-H_s)<=U_s/(as)<=exp(H_s). Brownian scaling and the Gaussian tail of
M_1 show, for each fixed t,

    E(1/U_s)<=C_t/s,
    E|1/U_s-1/(as)|<=C_t/sqrt(s), 0<s<=t.           (6)

For the second inequality use |1/(U_s/(as))-1|<=exp(H_s)-1 and
E(exp(H_s)-1)<=C_t sqrt(s). The moments of U_s of each fixed order are
O_t(s^j), by the same pathwise bound.

Equations (5)-(6) imply

    E[h(s,U_s)/U_s]=D_t/(as)+O_t(s^(-1/2))+O_t(1).

The nonsingular terms in C have bounded expectation near s=0, by the
derivative and U_s moment bounds. Therefore

    E[(C P_(t-s)f)(U_s)]= (b/a)D_t/s+O_t(s^(-1/2)). (7)

The difference between the integrand and (b/a)D_t/s is integrable at zero.
Integrating it proves (4), including its remainder. Finally b/a=1/(2pi).

## Consequence and the unpaid step

The natural candidate network leading correction for this bounded test is
(D_t/(2pi))log(n)/n, with a theta0-dependent constant/n at the next order.
This is a prediction, not proved network asymptotics. A proof still needs
uniform control while u approaches zero, a matching scale and remainder,
and the accumulated exact-to-regularized bounded-test comparison through
the entrance. A lower-cutoff contribution might alter or cancel a formal
coefficient unless controlled. C029's deterministic logarithmic offset is
compatible with this prediction but cannot supply that missing stochastic
matching theorem. [Theorem 3 (\cite{Kadane/OHagan:1995}, Theorem~1) of arXiv:2608.17793, 'The non-mathematical section of Kolmogorov's \emph{Grundbegriffe}'] Let $\mathcal{C}$ be any collection of subsets of a set $\Omega$
  with $\Omega\in\mathcal{C}$,
  and let $P$ be a nonnegative real-valued function on $\mathcal{C}$ with $P(\Omega)=1$.
  Then $P$ can be extended to a finitely additive probability measure on all subsets of $\Omega$
  if and only if, for all finite lists $C_{1},\dots,C_{c}$ and $C'_{1},\dots,C'_{c'}$
  of members of~$\mathcal{C}$,
  \begin{equation}
    \left(
      \sum_{i=1}^{c} 1_{C_{i}} \le \sum_{j=1}^{c'} 1_{C'_{j}}
    \right)
    \Longrightarrow
    \left(
      \sum_{i=1}^{c} P(C_{i}) \le \sum_{j=1}^{c'} P(C'_{j})
    \right),
  \end{equation}
  where $1_{A}$ stands for the indicator function of $A$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: \cite{Kadane/OHagan:1995}, Theorem~1

[Definition 10 (Two-dimensional Coulomb gas) of arXiv:2603.28734, 'Free energy analyticity of the disordered XY model and Debye screening in the 2D Coulomb g'] Fix $d=2$ and $\beta\in\R_{\geq 0}$.
    The \emph{two-dimensional lattice Coulomb gas} on $\Lambda_n$ with free boundary conditions at inverse temperature $\beta$
    is the probability measure on $q\in\Z^{F(\Lambda_n)}$
    given by
    \begin{equation}
      
        \mu_{\Coulomb,\Lambda_n,\beta}^\free[\{q=Q\}] = \frac{1}{Z_{\Coulomb,\Lambda_n,\beta}^\free} \mathbf{1}\Big[\sum\nolimits_{f\in F(\Lambda_n)}Q(f)=0\Big]\cdot e^{-\frac{\beta(2\pi)^2}{2} \langle Q , -\Delta^{-1} Q \rangle}.
    \end{equation}
    Notice that, contrary to the XY model,
    the Hamiltonian of the Coulomb gas is non-local due to the presence of the inverse Laplacian.
title: Two-dimensional Coulomb gas

[Proposition 10 of arXiv:2609.00209, 'Exit Times for Brownian Motion and Location Detection'] Let $\mathcal H$ denote the hyperbolic domain above and let $u_1(x,y)=\mathbb{E}^{(x,y)}[\tau_{\mathcal H}]$ and $u_2(x,y)=\mathbb{E}^{(x,y)}[\tau_{\mathcal H}^2]$ denote the first and second moments of the exit time from $\mathcal H$. If $a>b$, then the first moment of the exit time from $\mathcal H$ satisfies
\[
u_1(x, y)=\frac{a^2b^2}{2(a^2-b^2)}\left(\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}-1 \right).
\]
If $a>(1+\sqrt{2})b$ then the second moment of the exit time from $\mathcal H$ satisfies
\[
u_2(x, y)=\left(Ax^2+By^2+C\right)u_1(x, y),
\]
where the constants $A, B,$ and $C$ satisfy
\begin{align*}
A&=\frac{b^2(5a^2-b^2)}{6(a^4-6a^2b^2+b^4)},\\
B&=-\frac{a^2(a^2-5b^2)}{6(a^4-6a^2b^2+b^4)},\\
C&=\frac{a^2b^2(5b^2-a^2)(5a^2-b^2)}{6(a^2-b^2)(a^4-6a^2b^2+b^4)}.
\end{align*}
title: Proposition 10 of arXiv:2609.00209

\]

body:
Let $\mathcal{A} = \{A_i\}_{i \in I}$ be a finite collection of non-empty subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$. The nerve $N(\mathcal{A})$ of $\mathcal{A}$ is the simplicial complex with vertex set $I$ where a non-empty finite subset $\sigma \subseteq I$ forms a simplex in $N(\mathcal{A})$ if and only if $\bigcap_{i \in \sigma} A_i \neq \emptyset$. By the Nerve Theorem, if each $A_i$ and all finite non-empty intersections are contractible (e.g. convex sets), then the union $\bigcup_{i \in I} A_i$ is homotopy equivalent to the geometric realization of $N(\mathcal{A})$.
\mathcal{A} is a finite family of non-empty subsets in \mathbb{R}^d
title: Nerve Complex of a Collection of Sets

body:
[Proposition of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] For a permutation $\sigma\in S_p$, we have the formula
$$|\sigma|+\#\sigma=p$$
where $|\sigma|$ is the number of cycles of $\sigma$, and $\#\sigma$ is the minimal $k\in\mathbb N$ such that $\sigma$ is a product of $k$ transpositions. Also, the following formula defines a distance on $S_p$, 
$$(\sigma,\pi)\to\#(\sigma^{-1}\pi)$$
and the set of permutations $\sigma\in S_p$ which saturate the triangular inequality 
$$\#\sigma+\#(\sigma^{-1}\gamma)=\#\gamma=p-1$$
where $\gamma\in S_p$ is a full cycle, is in bijection with the set $NC(p)$.

[Lem 93 of arXiv:2609.01389, 'K-stability and birational rigidity of Fano 3-fold weighted complete intersections'] Let
\[
f (x, y) =  a (x) y^2 + b (x) y + c (x),
\]
be a polynomial in variables $x, y$, where $a (x), b (x), c (x) \in \mbC [x]$.
Suppose that $x \nmid a (x)$, $x \mid b (x)$, $x \mid c (x)$, $x^2 \nmid c (x)$ and $a (x)$, $b (x)$, $c (x)$ do not share a common component.
Then $f (x, y)$ is irreducible.

For f_r=1-2*1_(x_1=...=x_r=0) on the uniform F_2^r cube, r>=2, its squared Fourier law S has Pr[i in S]=I_i(f_r)=a=2^(1-r) for every i. The first spectral-coordinate chain entropy increment in any deterministic ordering is h2(a), and h2(a)/I_i>=r-1. Thus no absolute C bounds every chain-rule increment H(1_(i in S)|previously exposed spectral coordinates) by C I_i(f) for all Boolean f. Also sum_i h2(I_i)/I is unbounded on this family although H/I tends to 4. For distinct i,j and r>=3, Pr[i,j in S]=2^-r, whereas Pr[i in S]Pr[j in S]=2^(2-2r); spectral coordinates are dependent despite independent input bits. The assertion does not rule out adaptive or block entropy budgets.

body: [Defn def:ipvt of arXiv:2606.30517, '\textsc{Convergence towards Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations with a focus on Diestel--'] Let $X^{(\lambda)}$ be the nuclei process as in (def:PPP of the paper). Assume $\lambda_n\to 0$ is a sequence for which $\mathrm{Vor}(X^{(\lambda_n)})$ is convergent (as a point process of closed subsets). Then, the limit is called an \textbf{ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellation (IPVT)} of $(E,\mu)$. If, in addition, $\lim_{\lambda\to 0} \mathrm{Vor}(X^{(\lambda)})$ exists, it is called \textbf{\textit{the IPVT}} of $(E,\mu)$.

[Definition def:Holder of arXiv:2606.02003, 'Higher-Order Multifractional Stable Motion:\\ Definition and Fundamental Properties'] For a stochastic process $\{X(t)\}_{t \in \mathbb{R}}$ and
$t_0 \in \mathbb{R}$, the \emph{pointwise H\"older exponent} at $t_0$
is
\[
\alpha_X(t_0)
:= \sup\!\left\{
\gamma \geq 0 :
\limsup_{h \to 0}
\frac{|X(t_0+h) - X(t_0)|}{|h|^\gamma} < \infty
\;\text{ a.s.}
\right\}.
\]

[Lemma lem:real-freedman-rescaled of arXiv:2606.08683, 'Exact Fourier dimensions of dyadic Mandelbrot cascades under minimal integrability'] Let \((\mathcal H_j)_{j=0}^N\) be a filtration, and let \((M_j,\mathcal H_j)_{j=0}^N\) be a real-valued martingale with \(M_0=0\) and martingale differences \(\xi_j=M_j-M_{j-1}\).  Let \(R,V\in(0,\infty)\).  Assume that \(
\lvert \xi_j\rvert\le R\) for every \(j\) and
\[
\sum_{j=1}^N
\mathbb{E}\left(\xi_j^2\mid \mathcal H_{j-1}\right)
\le V
\]
almost surely.  Then, for every \(u>0\),
\[
\mathbb{P}\left(
\max_{0\le j\le N} M_j>u
\right)
\le
\exp\left(
-\frac{u^2}{2(V+Ru)}
\right).
\]

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.06038, 'Efron type identities\\ for stopping sets and Poisson hulls'] Let $\eta$ be as in Theorem~\ref{t:spatMarkov}. Let $(Z_n)$ be a 
  sequence of $\eta$-finite stopping sets. 
  Assume that $Z\colon \bN\to\cX$ satisfies
  \begin{align}
    
    \lim_{n\to\infty}\I\{x\in Z_n(\mu)\}=\I\{x\in Z(\mu)\},
    \quad (x,\mu)\in\BX\times\bN.
  \end{align}
  Then $Z$ is a Markov set with respect to $\eta$.
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2608.06038

[Proposition 6 of arXiv:2607.25949, 'Block-hierarchical covariance decompositions for finite-block additive functionals'] (Projection onto the marginal subspace).\\
Assume reversibility and that \(I-K^2\) is invertible on
\(L^2_0(\nu)\).  Let
\[
\mathcal M_k
=
\overline{
\left\{
a_1(X_1)+\cdots+a_k(X_k):
a_i\in L^2_0(\nu)
\right\}}
\subset \mathcal H_k
\]
be the one-variable marginal space.  For \(f\in \mathcal H_k\), define
\[
q_i(x)=E\{f(X_1,\ldots,X_k)\mid X_i=x\},
\qquad i=1,\ldots,k,
\]
and write
\[
q=(q_1,\ldots,q_k)^T.
\] 
Then the orthogonal projection of \(f\) onto \(\mathcal M_k\) is the unique element 
\(a_1(X_1)+\cdots+a_k(X_k)\), 
whose coefficient vector \((a_1,\ldots,a_k)^T\) solves the system
\[
(a_1,\ldots,a_k)^T=
(I-K^2)^{-1}
\begin{pmatrix}
I & -K & 0 & \cdots & 0\\
-K & I+K^2 & -K & \ddots & \vdots\\
0 & -K & I+K^2 & \ddots & 0\\
\vdots & \ddots & \ddots & \ddots & -K\\
0 & \cdots & 0 & -K & I
\end{pmatrix}
q ,
\]
where the factor \((I-K^2)^{-1}\) is applied componentwise. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition 6 of arXiv:2607.25949

The pair (X_G, X_L) is a bivariate random variable on Z_+^2 describing the total global and local contacts made by an infected individual throughout their infectious duration. Unlike classical models where X_G ~ Poisson(beta_G * I) and X_L ~ Poisson(beta_L * I) are conditionally independent given infectious period I, the distribution of (X_G, X_L) may be arbitrary, permitting negative correlation between global and local contacts.
(X_G, X_L) has support in Z_+^2

[Theorem of arXiv:2412.07936, 'Simple Norm Bounds for Polynomial Random Matrices via Decoupling'] (See also [Oue22:thesis] Theorem 7) Let ${\bf T} \in (\mathbb{R}^n)^{\otimes 3}$ be a random noise tensor with i.i.d. standard Gaussian entries. For $i,j \in [n]$, let $T_i$ and $T_j$ be the first-mode slices of ${\bf T}$. The pure noise matrix ${\bf M} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ associated to the melon graph has entries ${\bf M}[i,j] = \langle T_i, T_j \rangle$. Then
$$
{\mathbb E} \norm{{\bf M} - {\mathbb E} {\bf M}}_{2t}^{2t} ~ \leq ~ {\mathcal O} (n^{3t}).
$$

[Lemma 19 (McLeish) of arXiv:2608.22342, 'Completely Positive Entropy and Fourier Central Limit Theorems for Stationary Random Measu'] For each $n$, let $(X_{n,j})_{1\leq j\leq m_n}$ be a finite row of real,
square-integrable martingale differences. Suppose that, as $n\to\infty$,
\begin{align}

    \max_{j\leq m_n}|X_{n,j}|&\longrightarrow0
      \quad\text{in probability},\\

    \sup_n\E\max_{j\leq m_n}|X_{n,j}|^2&<\infty,\\

    \sum_{j=1}^{m_n}X_{n,j}^2&\longrightarrow\sigma^2
      \quad\text{in probability},
\end{align}
where $\sigma^2>0$ is constant. Then
$\sum_jX_{n,j}\dto N(0,\sigma^2)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary 5 of arXiv:2608.12451, '2608.12451'] Fix $q\geq2$.  For each $n$, let
$\big(N_{n,i,j}:1\leq i\leq m_n,  1\leq j\leq q\big)$
be independent random variables with $N_{n,i,j} \sim \Pois(\alpha_{n,i,j})$.  
Put

\noi
\begin{align}
 \beta_{n,i}
 :=\prod_{j=1}^q\alpha_{n,i,j},
 \quad
 X_n
 :=\sum_{i=1}^{m_n}
 \prod_{j=1}^qN_{n,i,j},
\AND
 \delta_n
 :=
 \max_{\substack{1\leq i\leq m_n\\1\leq j\leq q}}
 \alpha_{n,i,j}.
 
\end{align}
If
\noi
\begin{align}
 \delta_n\to0
 \AND
 \sum_{i=1}^{m_n}\beta_{n,i}\to\lambda>0,
\notag 
\end{align}
then $X_n$ converges to $\Pois(\lambda)$ in total variation, and its
first four moments converge to those of the limit.
 
Moreover, there exists a constant $C_{q,\lambda}$ depending only on $q$ and $\lambda$
 such that
 
 
\noi
\begin{align}
 \dTV\bigl( X_n, P_\lambda\bigr)
 \leq C_{q,\lambda} 
 \left(
 \left|\sum_{i=1}^{m_n}\beta_{n,i}-\lambda\right|
 +\sqrt{\delta_n}\right)
 
\end{align}
for all
sufficiently large $n$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 5 of arXiv:2608.12451

$(\gamma_n)_n\subset\Pc_p(\Xc)$ and $(\lambda_n)_n\subset\Pc_p(\Yc)$.
Assume that there exist $\gamma\in\Pc_p(\Xc)$ and $\lambda\in\Pc_p(\Yc)$ such that

\Wc_p(\gamma_n,\gamma)\longrightarrow0,

Then, for every $\pi\in\Pi(\gamma,\lambda)$, there exists a sequence
$(\pi_n)_n$ with $\pi_n\in\Pi(\gamma_n,\lambda_n)$ such that
\vspace{-2mm}
\[
\Wc_p(\pi_n,\pi)\longrightarrow0.

\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Thm robust-SPDE-thm of arXiv:2601.19145, 'Stochastic Persistence in Infinite Dimensions'] Suppose that the assumptions of (main-SPDE-thm of the paper) or (main-SPDE-thm-2 of the paper) are satisfied when $\Theta$ is replaced by $\{\theta_0\}$ for some $\theta_0 \in \Theta$. body:
[Theorem 16 of arXiv:2604.01701, '\bf Chung-type laws of the iterated logarithm for $m$-fold weighted integrated fractional '] Let $\Delta=(a,b)\subset (0,\infty)$,  $m\ge 0$, $\gamma\ge 0$, $\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_i<H+i+\gamma$, $i=1,\ldots,m$, and, $\tau=H+m+\gamma$.  Suppose   $q>1$,  
$\frac{1}{r}=\tau+1+\frac{1}{q}$,  and 
\begin{equation}\int_0^t |w(s)|s^{\tau}ds<\infty\; \text {and }\; \|w\mathbbm{I}_{\Delta}\|_{r,\tau+1,q} =\left(\sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty}2^{kr(\tau+1)} \|w\mathbbm{I}_{\Delta}\|^r_{L^q(2^{k-1},2^k]} \right)^{1/r}  <\infty.
\end{equation} 
Moreover, we assume that      $\Delta$ is bounded  when $1<q<\infty$. 
  Then
\begin{align}
 & \lim_{\epsilon\to 0}   \epsilon^{1/(\tau+1)}\log \pr\left(\left\|\int_0^tw(s)s^{\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_m}  J_{m,\bm\alpha}(I_{\gamma}B_H)(s) \right\|_{L^q(\Delta)}<a_H \epsilon\right)\nonumber\\
=& \lim_{\epsilon\to 0} \epsilon^{1/(\tau+1)}\log \pr\left(\left\|\int_0^tw(s)s^{\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_m} J_{m,\bm\alpha}(W_{H+\gamma})(s)ds\right\|_{L^q(\Delta)}< \epsilon\right) \nonumber\\
=&\lim_{\epsilon\to 0} \epsilon^{1/(\tau+1)}\log \pr\left(\left\|wW_{\tau+1}\right\|_{L^q(\Delta)}< \epsilon\right) 
=-\kappa(\tau+1,q)\|w\|_{L^r(\Delta)}^{1/(\tau+1)}, 
\end{align}
where $\kappa(\lambda,q)$ is defined as \eqref{eq:constant:2}.   In particular, 
$$ \lim_{\epsilon\to 0} \epsilon^{2/3}\log \pr\left(\sup_{t>0}\left|\int_0^tw(s)B(s) ds\right|< \epsilon\right) 
= -\kappa_{\frac{3}{2}} \int_0^{\infty}|w(s)|^{2/3}ds $$ 
whenever  $\sum_{k=-\infty}^{\infty}2^{k} \underset{t\in (2^{k-1},2^k]}{\text{ess sup}}|w(t)|^{2/3} <\infty$,  and
$$ \lim_{\epsilon\to 0} \epsilon^{2/3}\log \pr\left(\left\|\int_0^tw(s)B(s) ds\right\|_{L^2(0,1]}< \epsilon\right) 
= -\frac{3}{8} \left(\int_0^1|w(s)|^{1/2}ds\right)^{4/3} $$ 
whenever $\sum_{k=-\infty}^{0}2^{3k/4} \big(\int_{2^{k-1}}^{2^k}|w(t)|^2dt\big)^{1/4} <\infty$ and $\int_0^1|w(s)|s^{1/2}ds<\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Corollary cor:farey-sixth-order of arXiv:2609.01690, 'Iterated-sumset spectra: The complete exponent law and its rank geometry'] For each integer $N\geq1$, let $\mathrm{FV}(N)$ be the number of distinct
intersections of Farey lines of order $(N,N)$, and let $\mathrm{FR}(N)$ be
the number of connected regions into which those lines cut the open unit
square.  Then, as $N\to\infty$,
\begin{equation}
 \mathrm{FV}(N)=\Theta(N^6),\qquad
 \mathrm{FR}(N)=\Theta(N^6).
\end{equation}
The lower bound for $\mathrm{FV}(N)$ already comes from intersections in
the open triangle $0<x<y<1$.

[Lemma lem:equi of arXiv:2604.14851, 'Pool model: a mass preserving multi particle aggregation process'] Let $T_n, \ n\ge 1$ be a sequence of independent exponential random variables with $E[T_n]=c_n$ such that $c_1=\pi^{1/2}$, $c_n\downarrow 0$, while $\sum_{n=1}^\infty c_n=\infty$. Then we have 
	$$
	\frac{\sum_{k=1}^n T_k}{\sum_{k=1}^n c_k}\overset{a.s.}{\rightarrow} 1. 
	$$
title: Lemma lem:equi of arXiv:2604.14851

body:
[Definition def:block-shuffle-law of arXiv:2601.07045, 'From Continuous to Discrete: \\ a No-U-Turn Sampler for Permutations'] A random permutation $\rho\in S_n$ with law $q_B$ is generated as follows:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item Sample an offset $U\sim\mathrm{Unif}\{0,1,\dots,B-1\}$.
  \item Work in the rotated coordinates $t'=\phi_{U}^{-1}(t)$ and partition
        $\{1,\dots,n\}$ into consecutive blocks of size $B$
        (except possibly the final block).
  \item On each block, independently sample a uniform random permutation.
        Let $\Pi$ denote the resulting blockwise permutation in the rotated
        coordinates.
  \item Define the final permutation on the original labels by
        \[
          \rho(t)
          \;:=\;
          \phi_{U}\bigl(\Pi(\phi_{U}^{-1}(t))\bigr),
          \qquad t=1,\dots,n.
        \]
\end{enumerate}
title: Block--shuffle direction law $q_B$

body:
[Theorem main body of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Suppose $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Z}$ are smooth separated Deligne--Mumford surfaces, and there is a contraction $f : \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{Z}$ where the exceptional $\mathcal{C}$ is a smooth irreducible stacky curve. 
    Moreover, suppose $f(\mathcal{C}) = p \in |\mathcal{Z}|$ and $f : \mathcal{X} \setminus \mathcal{C} \xrightarrow{\sim} \mathcal{Z} \setminus \mathcal{Y}$ is an isomorphism where $\mathcal{Y} := \mathcal{B}\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal{Z}}(p)$. 
    Then, $f$ is a regular weighted blowup of $\mathcal{Z}$ with reduced center $\mathcal{Y}$. In particular, $f|_\mathcal{C} : \mathcal{C} \to \mathcal{Y}$ is a weighted projective bundle, and $\mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{X}}(\mathcal{C})|_{\mathcal{C}} \simeq \mathcal{O}_{\mathcal{C}}(-1) \otimes f^*\mathcal{L}$ for some line bundle $\mathcal{L}$ on $\mathcal{Y}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem main body of arXiv:2609.04023

body: [Cor 37 (Proposition 4.5 of \cite{Ten}) of arXiv:2609.00758, 'Deformations of Compact Calabi--Yau and Fano Varieties with Isolated Singularities'] Let $X$ be a compact log-canonical Gorenstein complex space of pure dimension $n,$ with isolated singularities and whose resolutions satisfy the $\partial\db$ lemma. Let $\pi:(Y,E)\to(X,X^\sing)$ be a good resolution. Then the natural map $H^{q-1}(X^\reg,\Om^{n-1}_{X^\reg}(\log E))\to H^q_E(Y,\Om^{n-1}_Y(\log E))$ is surjective.

[Lemma lem:Lemma5.1 of arXiv:2507.12601, 'Multi-type logistic branching processes with selection: frequency process and genealogy fo'] Let $T_K$ be a stopping time w.r.t.~the natural filtration of $\mathcal{N}_K$ and write $\tau_K := \inf\{t: N_K(t) \geq K\}$ for the time that the logistic branching reaches its carrying capacity for the first time.
Then, for $\widehat{T}_K := T_K\wedge \tau_K$, there exists a constant $c > 0$ independent of $K$ s.t.~for all $s \geq 0$,
\[
\mathbb{E}\left[ \Big( F_K^u(\widehat{T}_K) - F_K^u(s\wedge \widehat{T}_K)\Big)^2\right] \leq c\int_s^{+\infty} \mathbb{E}\left[\dfrac{\1_{\{N_K(t) > 0, t < \widehat{T}_K\}}}{N_K(t)}\right]\;\mathrm{d} t.
\]
title: Lemma lem:Lemma5.1 of arXiv:2507.12601

body: A linear map T between normed spaces is bounded if there is a constant C with ||Tx|| <= C ||x|| for all x; the least such C is the operator norm ||T||. For linear maps between normed spaces, bounded is equivalent to continuous, and to continuous at a single point. The bounded operators from X to a Banach space Y form a Banach space under the operator norm.

Every fixed-coordinate hyperplane $\set{t_i=c}$ and every coordinate-collision hyperplane $\set{t_i=t_j}$ is null for this positive product measure, and hence also for $

[Corollary cor:tailrl-binary-recovery of arXiv:2609.02987, 'Tail Likelihood Reinforcement Learning'] Suppose $r_i\in\{0,1\}$ and let
$M:=\sum_{i=1}^N\mathbf 1\{r_i=1\}$. If $M>0$, then every successful
rollout receives weight $1/M$ and every unsuccessful rollout receives weight
zero. Hence the uncentered TailRL{} estimator reduces to
\begin{equation}
g_{\mathrm{TailRL}}^{(N)}(x)
=
\frac{1}{M}
\sum_{i:r_i=1}S_i,

\end{equation}
which is the MaxRL estimator. After mean-centering, successful rollouts have
weight $1/M-1/N$ and unsuccessful rollouts have weight $-1/N$. If $M=0$,
all uncentered and centered weights are zero.

body: [Lemma lem:physical-comparison-comp of arXiv:2609.00698, 'Kinetic Wedge Layers and Diffusive Limit of Neutron Transport in Polygonal Domains'] Let $g\in L^\infty(\Omega\times\mathbb S^1)$ be a real-valued bounded mild solution of $\mathscr L_\varepsilon g=F$ with $g\big|_{\gamma_-}=k$. If $F\ge0$ almost everywhere and $k\ge0$ almost everywhere on $\gamma_-$, then $g\ge0$ almost everywhere in $\Omega\times\mathbb S^1$. Therefore, if $\mathscr L_\varepsilon g_1\le\mathscr L_\varepsilon g_2$ and $g_1\big|_{\gamma_-}\le g_2\big|_{\gamma_-}$, then $g_1\le g_2$.
title: Lemma lem:physical-comparison-comp of arXiv:2609.00698

[Theorem 1 (Asymptotic expansion of expectations) of arXiv:2604.03213, 'Asymptotic expansion for transport maps \\ between laws of multimatrix models'] Let $V \in\cC^{16k+23}(X_1,\dots,X_d)$ be a $(4k+4)$-regular potential (Definition \ref{definition:kregular}), $f\in\cC^{4k+4}(X_1,\dots,X_d)$, and $Y^N$ be a multimatrix model with potential $V$ (Definition \ref{def:randompot}).
There exist functions $f_i\in\cC^{k-i+1}(X_1,\dots,X_d)$ ($i = 0,\ldots,k$) such that if $x$ a $d$-tuple of free semicircular variables, $K > 0$, and $N \in \N$ satisfies $N>2K$, then
$$ \left| \E\left[\frac{1}{N}\Tr\left( f(Y^N) \right) \right] - \tau\big( f_0(x) \big) - \frac{\tau\big(f_1(x)\big)}{N^2} - \dots - \frac{\tau\big(f_k(x)\big)}{N^{2k}} \right| \leq \frac{C_{V,k,K} \norm{f}_{\cL^k,K}}{N^{2k+2}},$$

body:
Let $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ be a measure-preserving system on a probability space with $T$ invertible (a measure-preserving automorphism). A finite or countable measurable partition $\xi = \{A_1, A_2, \dots\}$ of $X$ is a (two-sided) generator if the smallest $\sigma$-algebra containing all the sets $T^{-n} A_i$, $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, coincides with $\mathcal{B}$ up to $\mu$-null sets; in join notation, $\bigvee_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} T^{-n}\xi = \mathcal{B}$ (mod $\mu$). For a non-invertible $T$ one uses the one-sided join $\bigvee_{n=0}^{\infty} T^{-n}\xi$ and speaks of a one-sided (strong) generator. Why it matters: by the Kolmogorov-Sinai theorem, if $\xi$ is a generator with finite entropy $H_\mu(\xi) < \infty$ then the measure-theoretic entropy of the system equals the entropy relative to $\xi$, $h_\mu(T) = h_\mu(T, \xi)$; no supremum over partitions is needed. Existence (Krieger): an ergodic automorphism of a Lebesgue probability space with $h_\mu(T) < \log k$ has a generator with $k$ atoms; a system with infinite entropy has no finite generator. Sharp edges: a partition may generate for one invariant measure and not another; the join over $n \geq 0$ alone need not generate for an automorphism (e.g. the time-zero partition of a two-sided shift does not generate one-sidedly); and 'generates' is a statement mod null sets, not about separating every pair of points, although separating points does imply generating (see the Walters entry).
(X, B, mu) is a probability space and T is measure-preserving
the partition is finite or countable and consists of measurable sets
for the two-sided join T must be invertible
title: Generator (generating partition) of a measure-preserving transformation

\[
 \|K\|_{\rm op}\le A^r(r+1)^B n^{\max\{2-g-f_R,0\}}.

\]
In particular the residual low cell $g=1,f_R=2$ has
$\|K\|_{\rm op}\le A^r(r+1)^B$.  This estimate is atomwise and is taken
before any endpoint translation is summed.

[Definition 10 (Decorated $p$-adic linear fractional stable motion) of arXiv:2606.24056, 'Decorated stable $p$-adic self-similar processes with stationary increments'] Let \(0<\alpha\le2\), \(H>0\), and
\(\psi:(\Z/L\Z)\times(\Z_p^\times/(1+p^c\Z_p))\to\R\) be any function.  For
\((s,\gamma)\in(\Z/L\Z)\times(\Z_p^\times/(1+p^c\Z_p))\), define
\[
  G_{s,\gamma}(z)=
  \begin{cases}
    \abs{z}_p^{H-1/\alpha}
    \psi\bigl(s+v_p(z)\!\!\pmod L,\gamma\omega_c(z)\bigr),&z\ne0,\\
    0,&z=0.
  \end{cases}
\]
Let \(M_\alpha\) be a real symmetric \(S\alpha S\) random measure on
\(\Q_p\times(\Z/L\Z)\times(\Z_p^\times/(1+p^c\Z_p))\) with control measure
\(m\otimes\nu_{L,c}\).  The decorated $p$-adic linear fractional stable motion is defined as
\[
  X(t)=\int_{\Q_p\times(\Z/L\Z)\times(\Z_p^\times/(1+p^c\Z_p))}
       \left(G_{s,\gamma}(t-x)-G_{s,\gamma}(-x)\right)\,
       M_\alpha(dx,ds,d\gamma).
\]
title: Decorated $p$-adic linear fractional stable motion

[Theorem 4 (Stability of the maximal EPI on compact groups) of arXiv:2608.22534, 'Entropy power inequalities in compact groups'] Let $G$ be a connected, compact and metrizable topological abelian group, 
equipped with its Borel $\sigma$-algebra. Let $X,Y$ be independent random 
variables on $G$ such that $\max{\{h(X),h(Y)\}} = h(Y) >-\infty.$ 
Put 
$$s := e^{6h(X)-2} \quad \text{and} \quad \eta_s  
:= \left(\frac{\sin(\pi s)}{\pi s}\right)^2.$$ 
Then
$$
 h(X+Y) - h(Y) \geq \min{\Bigl\{\frac{1}{4}, 
\frac{(1-\eta_s)^2}{8+\frac{16\eta_s}{s}} \Bigr\}}D(Y\|U_{G}).
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Stability of the maximal EPI on compact groups

For M linear regression tasks define L(w;m)=||X_m*w-y_m||^2/2. The population loss is L(w)=M^(-1)*sum_(m=1)^M L(w;m). For an ordering tau_1,...,tau_k and the final iterate w_k, the source’s seen-task loss is L_(1:k)(w_k)=k^(-1)*sum_(t=1)^k L(w_k;tau_t). Equivalently, if N_m(k)=#{t<=k:tau_t=m}, then L_(1:k)(w_k)=sum_m [N_m(k)/k]*L(w_k;m). Repeated task occurrences retain their multiplicity. This definition is not the uniform average over the distinct observed task indices. All the losses in L_(1:k) are evaluated at the same final iterate w_k.
Finite collection of tasks, an ordering of length k>=1, and the final iterate w_k.

Let T_v, v in Z^d excluding 0, have finite means and 0<sigma(v)^2=Var T_v<infinity; put X_v=T_v-E T_v. Define chi_a as the infimum of q such that some alpha_q>0 gives sup_v E exp(alpha_q |X_v|/|v|^q)<infinity, and chi_b as the supremum of q such that some R gives inf_(|v|>R) Var T_v/|v|^(2q)>0. Suppose some alpha>0,K<infinity give sup_v E exp(alpha |X_v|/sigma(v))<=K. Suppose also that there is chi>=0 such that for every eta>0 there are c_eta,C_eta,R_eta>0 with c_eta |v|^(chi-eta)<=sigma(v)<=C_eta |v|^(chi+eta) for ALL |v|>=R_eta. Then chi_a=chi_b=chi. This is a sufficient criterion, not evidence that the uniform variance regularity or normalized concentration has been proved for iid Uniform[1,2] FPP. It addresses fluctuation matching only, not wandering matching.

The stated two-sided variance power envelope for every positive exponent slack and every sufficiently large displacement

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2605.27212, '2605.27212'] Let \(P\) be a coordinate-replacement kernel as in
\eqref{eq:abstract-fibre-decomposition} on \(\mathcal X=S^N\), with invariant
set \(\Omega\), product law \(\mu\), stationary law \(\pi=\mu(\cdot\mid\Omega)\),
and good set \(G\subseteq\Omega\).  Assume \(\pi(G)>0\).  Suppose that the
following hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}, leftmargin=*]
    \item There is a constant \(A<\infty\) such that, for every nonnegative
    \(F:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) with \(\supp(F)\subseteq G\),
    \[
        \Ent_\mu(F^2)\le A\cE_P^\mu(F,F).
    \]
    \item There are \(t_*\ge0\), an integer \(L\ge1\), and \(\eta\ge0\) such
    that, uniformly in \(x\in\Omega\) and all integers \(s\ge t_*\),
    \[
        \Prob_x(\exists\,u\in\{0,1,\ldots,L\}:X_{s+u}\notin G)\le\eta.
    \]
\end{enumerate}
Set
\begin{equation}
    t_{\mathrm{conf}}=2A\log(e+\log|\Omega|),
\end{equation}
and define
\begin{equation}
    \zeta=\Prob(\operatorname{Poi}(t_{\mathrm{conf}})>L),
    \qquad
    R=e^{-t_{\mathrm{conf}}/A}\log|\Omega|+A\frac{\pi(G^c)}{\pi(G)}.
\end{equation}
Then, for every \(x\in\Omega\) and every integer \(s\ge t_*\),
\begin{equation}
    \left\|\delta_xP^s e^{t_{\mathrm{conf}}(P-I)}-\pi\right\|_{\TV}
    \le 2(\eta+\zeta)+\sqrt{R/2}+\pi(G^c).
\end{equation}
Consequently, if
\begin{equation}
    2(\eta+\zeta)+\sqrt{R/2}+\pi(G^c)
    +\Prob(\operatorname{Poi}(2t_*)<t_*)\le\frac14,
\end{equation}
then the continuous-time chain satisfies
\[
    t_{\mathrm{mix}}^{\mathrm{cont}}(1/4)\le 2t_*+t_{\mathrm{conf}}.
\]

[Proposition prop:invariant-dual of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] For every \(i\geq 0\),
\[
    \Pi_{\mathcal{S}}^{\perp}
    \left(
        \frac{1}{C_F}F(W_i)-\Pi_{\mathcal{S}}^{\perp}I_d
    \right)
    =
    \frac{1}{C_F}\Pi_{\mathcal{S}}^{\perp}H_i.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
    \frac{1}{C_F}F(W_i)-I_d-\frac{1}{C_F}H_i
    \in \mathcal{S}.
\]
Thus, at the end of iteration \(i\), the entire remaining violation of the
image constraint is incurred by the newly created higher-order term \(H_i\).

body: [Definition of arXiv:2411.17653, 'Exclusion processes with non-reversible boundary: hydrodynamics and large deviations'] A subset $\mathcal{A}\subset \mathcal{D}([0,T],{\mathcalboondox M})$ is said to be $I_{[0,T]}(\cdot|\gamma)$-dense if for any $\pi\in\mathcal{D}([0,T],{\mathcalboondox M})$ such that $I_{[0,T]}(\pi|\gamma)<+\infty$, there exists $\{\pi^n:n\geq1\}$ in $\mathcal{A}$ with $\pi^n\to\pi$ in $\mathcal{D}([0,T],{\mathcalboondox M})$ and $I_{[0,T]}(\pi^n|\gamma)\to I_{[0,T]}(\pi|\gamma)$.

[Theorem thm:convergenceZ of arXiv:2601.20502, 'Optimal matching under size priority'] Let $(\mathbb{T},o,w)$ be a Unimodular Bienaymé-Galton-Watson tree with reproduction law $\pi$ and i.i.d. weights of law $\omega$.
    Assume that $\pi$ and $\omega$ have finite expectation, and that the generating function $\phi$ of $\pi$ is such that the function
    \[x \in [0,1] \mapsto \phi(1-x) + \phi(1-\hat\phi(1-x)) + \phi'(1) x \hat\phi(1-x)\]
    has at most two global maxima.
    For any $\varepsilon>0$, denote by $(\mathbb{T},o,w, \mathbb{M}_{\max}^{(\varepsilon)})$ the unique (in law) unimodular matching maximising
    \[  \mathbb{E}\left[ \sum_{v\sim o}(1+ \varepsilon w(o,v)) \mathbbm{1}_{ \{o,v\} \in \mathbb{M}_{\max}^{(\varepsilon)} }\right],\]
    and by $(\mathbb{T},o,w,\mathbb{M}_{\mathrm{opt}})$ the unique (in law) optimal unimodular matching 
     given by Theorem~(maintheorem of the paper). We have the following weak local convergence
    \[(\mathbb{T},o,w, \mathbb{M}_{\max}^{(\varepsilon)}) \underset{\varepsilon \rightarrow 0}{\longrightarrow} (\mathbb{T},o,w, \mathbb{M}_{\mathrm{opt}}).\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 7 (Brownian Time Extension) of arXiv:2606.21759, 'A Note On Gaussian Random Fields \& Underlying Markov Processes Through a Central Limit Th'] Let $\{B(f,t):f\in 1_\pi^\perp, t\in\mathbb{R}\}$ denote the
temporal extension of $B$ with finite dimensional
distributions defined by Gaussian weak-convergence limit 
\begin{equation}
\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\bigg(\int_{nt_1}^0f_1(\tilde{X}_{s_1})ds_1,\dots,\int_{nt_k}^0f_k(\tilde{X}_{s_k})ds_k,
 \int_{0}^{nt_{k+1}}f_{k+1}(\tilde{X}_{s_{k+1}})ds_{k+1},\dots,\int_0^{nt_m}f_m(\tilde{X}_{s_m})ds_m\bigg),
\end{equation}
for $t_1<t_2\cdots<t_k<0<t_{k+1}<\cdots< t_m$.
 Then ${B}$ is a space-time
centered 
Gaussian random field indexed by $1_\pi^\perp\times\mathbb{R}$
with 
 \begin{equation}
 \text{cov}(B(f_1,t_1),B(f_2,t_2))
 =
 \begin{cases} (|t_1|\wedge|t_2|)(-2\langle f_1, A^{-1}f_2\rangle_\pi)
 & \text{if}\quad t_1t_2 >0\\
 0 & \text{if}\quad t_1t_2\le 0.
 \end{cases}
 \end{equation}
 Moreover, 
 the path $t\to B(f,t)$ has an
 almost surely continuous version as  Brownian motion.

[Lemma 10 (Cyclotomic fibers) of arXiv:2608.25725, 'Gr\"obner Bases for Alexander Fitting Ideals of Links'] For every divisor \(\delta\mid q\) with \(\delta>1\),
\begin{equation}
p_\delta(y)=
\begin{cases}
1,
& \delta\nmid\lcm(m,k),
\\[6pt]
\displaystyle
\frac{y^g-x_\delta^e}
 {(y-x_\delta)^{\mathbf 1_{\delta\mid k}}
  (y-x_\delta^{-1})^{\mathbf 1_{\delta\mid m}}},
& \delta\mid\lcm(m,k).
\end{cases}
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
d_\delta=
\begin{cases}
0,
& \delta\nmid\lcm(m,k),
\\[3pt]
g-\mathbf 1_{\delta\mid m}-\mathbf 1_{\delta\mid k},
& \delta\mid\lcm(m,k).
\end{cases}
\end{equation}

Let
\[
\mathcal D:=
\{\delta>1:\,\delta\mid q,\ d_\delta>0\}.
\]
If \(\mathcal D=\varnothing\), then \(I=R\).  If
\(\mathcal D\ne\varnothing\), then
\[
R/I\cong
\prod_{\delta:\,\delta\in\mathcal D}
\mathcal K_\delta[y]/(p_\delta(y)),
\qquad
\dimQ(R/I)=
\sum_{\delta:\,\delta\in\mathcal D}d_\delta\deg\Phi_{2\delta}.
\]

body: For the composition operator (C phi)(t) = sum_eps p_eps phi(eps/3 + (2/3) t) of the Bernoulli-2/3 self-similar variable D = eps/3 + (2/3) D' (eps in {0, +1, -1} with weights 1/2, 1/4, 1/4): the three branches map every disk of radius R > 1 strictly into itself, since (2/3) R + 1/3 < R, so C is compact on functions analytic there, with eigenvalue 1 on the constants; and its spectrum is exactly {(2/3)^n : n >= 0} union {0}. Proof: every branch has the same derivative 2/3, so C(t^n) = sum_eps p_eps (eps/3 + (2/3) t)^n = (2/3)^n t^n + (terms of lower degree), the leading coefficient being (2/3)^n times sum_eps p_eps = 1; C maps the polynomials of degree at most n into themselves with diagonal (2/3)^k, and on a space of analytic functions in which the monomials form a basis the spectrum is exactly these powers together with 0. In particular the second eigenvalue is exactly 2/3 (an interval-arithmetic estimate near 1/2 is wrong). Numerically, Chebyshev discretisations at 24, 40, 60 and 80 nodes give leading moduli 1, 0.666667, 0.444444, 0.296296, 0.197531, 0.131687, the powers of 2/3 to six figures and stable under refinement. Consequence: an argument for a square-integrable density of the Bernoulli convolution at ratio 2/3 needs a rate strictly below 2/3 with exponential room, and this spectral gap is exactly 2/3, so no argument whose only input is this gap can work - consistent with the equivalence, via a Fejer minorant, of the rate 2/3 exactly with square-integrability. The general lesson: for a self-similar measure whose maps share one contraction ratio, the transfer operator is triangular in the monomial basis and its gap is forced to be that ratio.

[Definition $d$-Ahlfors regular metric measure spaces of arXiv:2609.03129, 'A Closed-Form Formula for Consistent Lipschitz Regression on Metric Spaces with Sparse Neu'] Let $d>0$.  A metric measure space $(X,\rho,\mathfrak m)$ is called
$d$-Ahlfors regular if $\operatorname{supp}(\mathfrak m)=X$ and there exist constants
$0<c_{\rm A}\le C_{\rm A}<\infty$ such that
\[
    c_{\rm A} r^d
    \le
    \mathfrak m(B(x,r))
    \le
    C_{\rm A} r^d
\]
for every $x\in X$ and every
$
    0<r\le\operatorname{diam}(X).
$

[Lem 23 ({cf.~\cite[Lemma~3.9) of arXiv:2506.17979, '\large\bf A remark on subharmonicity for symmetric Dirichlet forms'] {CK}}]
Let $D$ be an open set and $u$ is a nearly Borel $\overline{\R}$-valued function on $E$. 
Then we have the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\rm(1)]
Suppose \eqref{e:2.3} and $u\in L^1_{\loc}(D;{\m})$. If $u$ is subharmonic in $D$, then $u$ is subharmonic in $D$ in the weak sense. Moreover, under ${\bf (AC)}$ for ${\bf X}$, if $u$ is a subharmonic function on $D$ without  exceptional set and is in $L^1_{\loc}(D;{\m})$, then $u$ is subharmonic in $D$ in the weak sense without exceptional set.
\item[\rm(2)] If $u$ is a nearly Borel finely continuous 
$\overline{\R}$-valued function such that $u$ is subharmonic in $D$ in the weak sense, 
then for any $U\Subset D$, $t\mapsto u(X_{t\land\tau_U})$ is a 
{\rm(}not necessarily uniformly integrable{\rm)} $\mathbb{P}_x$-submartingale for q.e.~$x\in E$. Moreover, under ${\bf (AC)}$ for ${\bf X}$ , if $u$ is a finely continuous subharmonic function on $D$ in the weak sense without exceptional set, then for $U$ above, $\{u(X_{t\land\tau_U})\}_{t\geq0}$ is a {\rm(}not necessarily uniformly integrable{\rm)} $\P_x$-submartingale for all $x\in U$.

body: [Theorem 2 (Finite-time condensation for Cai--Lu solutions) of arXiv:2609.01436, '2609.01436'] Assume \cref{ass:CL}. Let $F_0\in\mathcal B_1^+([0,\infty))$ satisfy \begin{equation} N(F_0)>0, \qquad E(F_0)>0, \qquad {\overline T}/{\overline T_c}<1, \end{equation} where $\overline T/\overline T_c$ is determined by $N=N(F_0)$ and $E=E(F_0)$ through \eqref{eq:temperature-ratio}. Then, for every fixed \(\lambda\in(1/{20},1/{19})\), there exists a conservative isotropic measure solution $(F_t)_{t\geq0}$ with initial datum $F_0$ such that \begin{equation} \|F_t-F_{\rm be}\|_1^\circ \leq C_\lambda(1+t)^{-\lambda/2}, \qquad t\geq0, \end{equation} for some constant $C_\lambda>0$. For this solution there exists a finite time $T\geq0$ such that \begin{equation} F_T(\{0\})>0,\qquad F_t(\{0\})>0, \quad t\geq T, \end{equation} and \begin{equation} F_t(\{0\})\longrightarrow N_c, \qquad \|F_t-F_{\rm be}\|_1\longrightarrow0 \qquad\text{as }t\to\infty. \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Finite-time condensation for Cai--Lu solutions

			$$\left \langle J_{n}f, g\right \rangle _{L^{2}}= \left \langle f, J_{n}g

			\item For all $\sigma\ge0$, $n\ge1$, and $f\in H^\sigma$, we have

[Theorem thm:basic_properties_of_PPPs of arXiv:2505.07145, 'Nonamenable Poisson zoo'] Let $\mathcal{X} = \sum_{i \in I} \delta_{(x,H)_i} \sim \mathcal{Q}_{\nu}^\lambda$ be as in Definition (def:Poisson_zoo_as_PPP of the paper) and given any $A \in \mathcal{Z}$ introduce the restricted measure $\nu_A(\cdot) := \nu ( \cdot \cap A)$.
	\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
		\item If $A \in \mathcal{Z}$, then the restricted process $\mathcal{X} \mathds{1} [A]$ has law $\mathcal{Q}_{\nu_A}^\lambda$.
		\item If $A_1, A_2, \ldots \in \mathcal{Z}$ are such that $A_i \cap A_j = \emptyset$ for $i \neq j$, then the restricted processes $\mathcal{X} \mathds{1} [A_1], \mathcal{X} \mathds{1}[A_2], \ldots$ are independent.
		\item Let $p \in [0,1]$ and $\{ \xi_i \}_{i \in I}$ a collection of independent $\mathsf{Bernoulli}(p)$ random variables, and consider the following decomposition:
		\begin{equation}
			\mathcal{X} = \mathcal{X}_1 + \mathcal{X}_2 := \sum_{i \in I} \xi_i \delta_{(x,H)_i} + \sum_{i \in I} (1 - \xi_i) \delta_{(x,H)_i}.
		\end{equation}
		Then $\mathcal{X}_1 \sim \mathcal{Q}_{\nu}^{p v}$ and $\mathcal{X}_2 \sim \mathcal{Q}_{\nu}^{ (1-p)v }$ in law, and they are independent of each other.
		\item If $A \in \mathcal{Z}$, then $\mathcal{X}(A)$ follows a Poisson distribution.
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:basic_properties_of_PPPs of arXiv:2505.07145

[Lemma 13 of arXiv:2607.04943, '\textbf{Approximation of Random Differential Equations Driven by Physical Brownian Motion '] For each $(x,X,y)\in\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}\times\mathbb{R}^d,$ define
	$$\Phi(x,X,y):=\sum_i\partial_{x_i}\vp(x,X)y^i+\sum_{i,j}\partial_{X_{ij}}\vp(x,X)x^iy^j,$$
	\begin{eqnarray*}
		&&\Theta^{ij}(x,X)\\&:=&\partial^2_{x_ix_j}\vp(x,X)+\sum_k\partial^2_{x_iX_{kj}}\vp(x,X)x^k+\sum_k\partial^2_{X_{ki}x_j}\vp(x,X)x^k\\&&+\sum_{k,l}\partial^2_{X_{ki}X_{lj}}\vp(x,X)x^kx^l+\partial_{X_{ij}}\vp(x,X),
	\end{eqnarray*}
	and
	$$\Xi^{ij}(x,X,y):=\sum_k\partial_{x_k}\Theta^{ij}(x,X)y^k+\sum_{k,l}\partial_{X_{kl}}\Theta^{ij}(x,X)x^ky^l.$$
	Then
	
	(i) $\frac{d}{dt}\vp(\ue_t,\bbue_t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\ep}}\Phi(\ue_t,\bbue_t,\ee_t)$.

	(iii) $\frac{d}{dt}\Theta^{ij}(\ue_t,\bbue_t)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\ep}}\Xi^{ij}(\ue_t,\bbue_t,\ee_t)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
