[Proposition prop:many-codim-L of arXiv:2608.26707, 'An Exponential Lower Bound for the Permanent\\of Random Bernoulli Matrix'] Let $L\geq1$, let $k\leq n-3L$, and condition on $\mathcal{F}_k$.
Suppose that $A_0\in\binom{[n]}{k}$ is $\lambda$-heavy, and set $q=\floor{\frac{n-k}{2L}}.$ Then, after exposing rows $k+1,\dots,n-L$, with conditional probability at least $1-Ce^{-cL}$ there exist at least $\left\lfloor q/2\right\rfloor$ $\lambda$-heavy sets
\[
 A_1,\dots,A_{\left\lfloor q/2\right\rfloor}\in\binom{[n]}{n-L}
\]
whose complements are pairwise disjoint.

  Then we define the \emph{generalized sequential gamble space} $(\Omega,\hat\mathcal{Z},T)$ to be the gamble space $(\Omega,\mathcal{Z}_T)$, as defined following eq.~(equation eq:cumulative-gamble-infinite of the paper).

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2608.30549, '\vspace{-1cm}Maximally Spread Out Measures and Implications\\{} for Phase Transitions in A'] Let $(\XX, d)$ be a quasi-metric space.
  Let $\emptyset \ne \SC \subset \XX$ be bounded.
  Then, writing $\CR^\ast := \bigl(\umd(\SC)\bigr)^{-1}$, the following holds:
  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item \emph{(A suitable codec sequence achieves every rate below $\CR^\ast$)}
          There exists a codec sequence ${\mathscr{S}^\ast = ( (E_n^\ast, D_n^\ast) )_{n \in \N}}$
          for $\SC$ such that for every $0 \leq \CR < \CR^\ast$,
          there exists $C(\CR) > 0$ satisfying
          \[
            \delta (E_n^\ast, D_n^\ast) \leq C(\CR) \cdot n^{-\CR}
            \qquad \forall \, n \in \N
            .
          \]
          In particular, $\mathcal{R}^\CR (\mathscr{S}^\ast, \SC, \XX) = \SC$.
  \end{enumerate}
  Now, assume that $\mu$ is a probability measure on $\XX$ that is critical for $\SC$,
  and set
  \[
    \CR^\sharp
    := \bigl(\lmd(\SC)\bigr)^{-1}
    .
  \]
  Then the following hold:
  \begin{enumerate}[resume,label=(\roman*)]
    \item \emph{(quantitative bound relating approximation error and number of bits)}
          Let $\CR \in (\CR^\sharp, \infty)$.
          Then there exist $c = c(\CR) > 0$ and $\eps_0 = \eps_0 (\CR) > 0$
          such that for every $n \in \N$ and every $n$-bit codec $(E_n, D_n)$ for $\SC$,
          we have
          \[
            \mu^\ast
            \Bigl(
              \bigl\{
                x \in \SC
                \,\,:\,\,
                d\bigl(x, D_n(E_n(x))\bigr) \leq \eps
              \bigr\}
            \Bigr)
            \leq 2^{n - c \cdot \eps^{-1/\CR}}
            \qquad \forall \, \eps \in (0, \eps_0)
            .
          \]

    \item \emph{(any rate above $\CR^\sharp$ is only achievable on a $\mu$-null set)}
          For every $t \in (\CR^\sharp, \infty)$ and every codec sequence
          $\mathscr{S} = \bigl( (E_n, D_n) \bigr)_{n \in \N}$,
          the set $\mathcal{R}^\CR (\mathscr{S}, \SC, \XX)$ is a $\mu$-null set:
          \[
            \mu^\ast \Bigl(\mathcal{R}^\CR (\mathscr{S}, \SC, \XX)\Bigr)
            = 0
            \quad \text{ for every $\CR\in (\CR^{\sharp},\infty)$.}
          \]
          In fact, even
          \[
            \mu^\ast
            \biggl(\,\,
              \bigcup_{\CR \in (\CR^\sharp, \infty)}
                \mathcal{R}^\CR (\mathscr{S}, \SC, \XX)
            \biggr)
            = 0
            .
          \]
  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition def_triangle of arXiv:2608.09105, 'Longest convex chains with i.i.d.\ points'] Let $f\colon[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}$ be continuous and convex.
Let us write $\mathsf{A} = (a,f(a))$ and $\mathsf{B} = (b,f(b))$.
\begin{itemize}

\item (Typical case) 
If $\partial^+f(a) < \partial^-f(b)$ and at least one of these two derivatives is finite, then we denote by $\mathsf{Tri}_f(a,b)$ the triangle bounded by the following three lines: the tangent line of $f$ at $a$ with slope $\partial^+f(a)$, the tangent line of $f$ at $b$ with slope $\partial^-f(b)$, and the secant line of $f$ between $a$ and $b$.
The vertices of $\mathsf{Tri}_f(a,b)$ are thus $\mathsf{A}$, $\mathsf{B}$, and the unique intersection point of the two tangent lines.
See Figure~(fig_tangency_triangle of the paper) (left).

\item (Degenerate case 1: flat)
If $\partial^+f(a)=\partial^-f(b)<\infty$, then we let $\mathsf{Tri}_f(a,b)$ denote the line segment between $\mathsf{A}$ and $\mathsf{B}$.

\item (Degenerate case 2: doubly infinite)
If $\partial^+f(a)=-\infty$ and $\partial^-f(b)=\infty$, then we let $\mathsf{Tri}_f(a,b)$ denote the infinite region below the secant line, defined in (equation below_secant of the paper).
\hfill\ensuremath{\square}

\end{itemize}

[Proposition 7 (Intrinsic projection for spans \(m\ge 3\)) of arXiv:2607.25949, 'Block-hierarchical covariance decompositions for finite-block additive functionals'] Let \(m\ge 3\), and let $\psi\in\mathcal H_m= L^2_0(\pi_m)$. Define
\[
L_m\psi
=
E(\psi\mid X_1,\ldots,X_{m-1}),
\qquad
R_m\psi
=
E(\psi\mid X_2,\ldots,X_m),
\]
and
\[
C_m\psi
=
E(\psi\mid X_2,\ldots,X_{m-1}).
\]
Then the orthogonal projection of \(\psi\) onto \(\mathcal I_m\) is
\[
\operatorname{Proj}_{\mathcal I_m}\psi
=
\psi-L_m\psi-R_m\psi+C_m\psi .
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Intrinsic projection for spans \(m\ge 3\)

body:
[Lemma tech cond of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Suppose $f : X \to Z$ is a birational contraction morphism between two smooth separated schemes where $Z$ is quasi-projective. 
Suppose further that there is a smooth closed subscheme $Y \subseteq Z$ where $f$ defines an isomorphism away from $Y$. 
Let $\bar{Z}$ and $\bar{Y}$ be projective schemes containing $Z$ and $Y$ as schematically-dense open subschemes respectively where $\bar{Y} \subseteq \bar{Z}$ is closed.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be a very ample line bundle on $\bar{Z}$, and let $f^*\mathcal{L}$ denote the pullback of the line bundle under the composition $X \xrightarrow{f} Z \hookrightarrow \bar{Z}.$

Then,
there exists $d \gg 0$ such that for $L := \mathcal{L}^{\otimes d}$ the finite-dimensional vector space $V := \operatorname{H}^0(\bar{Z}, L)$ satisfies the following properties.
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(a)] The restriction map $\operatorname{H}^0(\bar{Z}, L) \to \operatorname{H}^0(\bar{Y}, L|_{\bar{Y}})$ is surjective.
    \item[(b)] If $V_Y := \operatorname{im}(\operatorname{H}^0(\bar{Z}, L) \to \operatorname{H}^0(Y, L|_Y))$, then $V_Y$ is naturally identified with $\operatorname{H}^0(\bar{Y}, L|_{\bar{Y}}).$ 
    In particular, for $d \gg 0$, $\dim V_Y > r:= \dim Y.$
    \item[(c)] The sections of $V := \operatorname{H}^0(\bar{Z}, L)$ generate $L|_Z$, and the image sections $V_Y$ generate $L|_Y$.
    Consequently, the pulled-back sections generate $f^*L$ on $X$ and generate $f^* L |_E$ on $E$.
\end{itemize}

[Thm 13 (Girsanov's theorem; see, e.g.,~\cite{KS-BM}) of arXiv:2606.18877, 'Ergodic Properties of Non-Linear Density-Dependent Perturbations of the Ornstein--Uhlenbec'] Let \((\Omega, \{\F_t\}_{t\geq 0},\PP)\) be a probability space, and let \(\{\beta_t\}_{t\geq 0}\), be an \(\F_t\)-adapted stochastic process with values in \(\R^d\) such that
    \[
    \PP\left(
    \int_0 ^T \Vert \beta_s\Vert_2^2\,ds
    <\infty
    \right)
    =1, 
    \quad \forall\, 0<T<\infty.
    \]
    Then, if the process
    \[
    \mathcal{E}_t:=\exp\left\{
    \int_0 ^t \beta_s\,dW_s
    -\frac{1}{2}\int_0 ^t \Vert \beta_s\Vert_2^2\,ds
    \right\},
    \quad t\geq 0,
    \]
    is an \(\F_t\)-martingale under \(\PP\), then for any fixed \(0<T<\infty\) the process
    \[
    \widetilde{W}_t:= -\int_0 ^t \beta_s\,ds+ W_t, 
    \quad 0\leq t\leq T,
    \]
    is an \(\F_t\)-Brownian motion on \((\Omega,\{\F_t\}_{0\leq t\leq T},\widetilde{\PP})\) with \(\widetilde{\PP}\) a probability measure such that \(\frac{d\widetilde{\PP}}{d\PP}\Bigr|_{\F_T}=\mathcal{E}_T\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 1 of arXiv:2603.28702, 'Distribution of the magnetization of the critical Ising model on sparse random graphs'] Consider the Ising model on a graph $G\sim G_{n,d}$ (for $d\ge3$) at the critical temperature, $\beta_c=\tanh^{-1}((d-1)^{-1})$. Let $\mu_{n,\text{reg}}\in\mathcal{M}_1(\R)$ be the random measure defined as
$$\mu_{n,\text{reg}}(A):=\PR_{n,\text{reg}}(m\cdot n^{-3/4}\in A\ |\ G),\ \text{with}\ G\sim G_{n,d}.$$
Then, there exists a measure $\mu_{\text{reg}}\in\mathcal{M}_1(\R)$ such that $\mu_{n,\text{reg}}\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{}\mu_{\text{reg}}$ in the 1-Wasserstein distance associated to $\text{d}_{\text{KS}}$. This measure $\mu_{\text{reg}}$ has density $$f_{\text{reg}}(y)\varpropto \exp\left(-\frac{(d-2)(d-1)}{12d^2}y^4\right).$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition theorem_size_bias_coupling of arXiv:2606.03442, 'Stein's method in network analysis'] Let $X = \sum_{j=1}^m Y_j$ be a sum of non-negative random variables, with $0 < \mathbb{E} [X] < \infty$,
   and let $F_j(\cdot;y) = \mathcal{L}\bigl(\sum_{i, i \neq j} Y_i \,|\, Y_j = y\bigr)$. Let $J$ be a random index with values in $1, \ldots, m$, with $\mathbb{P}(J = j) = \mathbb{E}[Y_j] / \mathbb{E}[X]$.
   Given $J=j$, let~$Y_j^{(s)}$ be sampled from the size biased distribution of~$Y_j$; then, if $Y_j^{(s)} = y$,
    sample~$X_j^{\star}$ from $F_j(\cdot;y)$. Then $X^{(s)} = X_J^{\star} + Y_J^{(s)}$ has the size bias distribution of~$X$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition theorem_size_bias_coupling of arXiv:2606.03442

[Proposition 14 (A general upper bound on \(\EE{\Svar}\)) of arXiv:2604.13149, 'The Distributional Tail of Worst--Case Quickselect'] Let \(A>2\), and let \(L:\R\to[0,1]\) satisfy
\[
L(x)\le F(x),
\qquad x\in(2,A).
\]
Then
\[
\EE{\Svar}
\le
2+\int_2^A \bigl(1-L(x)\bigr)\,\dd x
+\frac{\exp\!\bigl(-A\log(A/2)+A\bigr)}{\log(A/2)}.
\]

body: A topological space X is path-connected if for every pair of points x and y in X there is a path from x to y, that is, a continuous map gamma from the interval [0,1] (with its standard topology) to X such that gamma(0) = x and gamma(1) = y. Every path-connected space is connected; the converse fails in general (the topologist's sine curve is connected but not path-connected).

[Corollary co:close_geodesic_small_parts of arXiv:2507.15589, 'Tightness of approximations to metrics on non-simple conformal loop ensemble gaskets'] There exist $c>0$ and $\zeta>0$ (not depending on $M,a,a_1,a_0$) such that the following is true. Fix $M,a,a_1 > 0$ such that $a,a_1$ are sufficiently small (depending on $a_0$). 
Let $\widehat{G}_{M,a}$ be the event that for every $0 \le s < t \le \infty$, the domain $D \setminus \eta([0,s]\cup[t,\infty))$ is $(M,a)$-good. Let $U \subseteq D_\eta$ be the $\delta_1^{1+a_1}$-neighborhood of $\eta$.

For $0 < \delta_1 < \delta$, let $G_{\delta_1,\delta}$ denote the event that there exists a finite collection of intervals $[s_i,t_i] \subseteq [0,\infty]$ such that
\begin{itemize}
\item if $\mathrm{dist}(\eta(t),\partial D) \le \delta_1$, then $t \in \bigcup_i [s_i,t_i]$,
\item $\bigcap_i G^U_{s_i,t_i}(r_i)$ holds for some $(r_i)$ with
\[
\sum_i r_i \le M(\delta_1/\delta)^{\zetaa_0} .
\]
\end{itemize}
Then
\[ \mathbf{P}[ G_{\delta_1,\delta}^c \cap \widehat{G}_{M,a} ] = O(M\delta^{{\alpha_{\mathrm{apr}}}-c(1+a_0^{-1})(a+a_1)}(\delta_1/\delta)^{\zeta{\alpha_{\mathrm{apr}}}}) \quad\text{as}\quad \delta \to 0.\]

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). For two independent centered Gaussian fields X, Y indexed by a common finite (or suitably truncated) set T with covariance functions C_X, C_Y, Kahane's interpolation forms Z(t,u) = sqrt(u) X(t) + sqrt(1-u) Y(t) for u in [0,1] and computes d/du E[F(Z(.,u))] for a smooth test function F, obtaining, since Z(.,u) has covariance u C_X + (1-u) C_Y, d/du E[F(Z(.,u))] = (1/2) sum_{s,t in T} (C_X(s,t) - C_Y(s,t)) E[d_s d_t F(Z(.,u))]. When C_X <= C_Y pointwise (or the relevant difference has a consistent sign) and F is chosen with matching sign of mixed partials, this yields a comparison inequality between functionals of X and Y, an approach that both generalizes Slepian-type comparisons and, in the Gaussian multiplicative chaos literature, is used to show that different regularizations of a log-correlated field, such as the two-dimensional Gaussian free field, converge to the same limiting chaos measure regardless of the approximation scheme, a key technical step in constructing Liouville quantum gravity measures. It does not apply to non-Gaussian fields, the interpolation is built from independent copies of the two fields (always available, since only their laws are compared; a dependent coupling adds cross-covariance terms to the derivative), and the sign or convexity conditions on F needed to obtain a clean inequality must be verified case by case rather than assumed. Typical failure: Running the interpolation on a dependent coupling of the two fields while dropping the cross-covariance terms, or to a family of regularizations whose covariance difference does not have a consistent sign across the whole index set, which is common when comparing regularizations of a log-correlated field near its singular set; either error breaks the monotonicity the interpolation is meant to exploit, and the resulting comparison can go in the wrong direction with no explicit error term to control it. Canonical reference: Kahane, 1986, Annales des Sciences Mathematiques du Quebec; Robert and Vargas, 2010, Comptes Rendus Mathematique; Berestycki, 2017, Electronic Communications in Probability.

existence and enough regularity of the covariance functions to differentiate the interpolated expectation under the integral
a consistent-sign comparison, or specific structural relation, between the two covariance kernels
the test functional F smooth with the correct sign of mixed partial derivatives for the interpolation identity to yield a useful inequality rather than an uncontrolled remainder

[Lemma lem:hetero_reference_realization of arXiv:2609.00193, 'Provably Efficient Federated Reinforcement Learning with Linear Function Approximation and'] For any agent $m\in[M]$, policy $\pi$, and step $h\in[H]$, define
\[
w_{m,h}^{\pi}
:=
\theta_h+\int_{\mathcal X}V_{m,h+1}^{\pi}(x')\,\mu_h(\mathrm d x').
\]
Then, for every $(x,a)\in\mathcal X\times\mathcal A$,
\[
\bigl|Q_{m,h}^{\pi}(x,a)-\phi(x,a)^\top w_{m,h}^{\pi}\bigr|
\le H\xi.
\]
Moreover, $\|w_{m,h}^{\pi}\|_2\le 2H\sqrt d$.

body: [Theorem 1.3 of arXiv:2512.17823, 'van den Berg-Kesten--type correlation inequalities for disjoint polymers in the KPZ univer'] There exist $C,c,L_{0}>0$ such that the following holds. Let $y\in\mathbb R$, $K\geq 0$, and $\mathsf{A}\subseteq\mathcal{C}([0,K],\mathbb R)$ be an increasing Borel measurable set. For any $t>0$, $L\geq L_{0}(t^{-1/6}\vee 1)$, and $M>C(L+y^{2})^{3/4}$, $\displaystyle\mathbb P\Bigl(\hat{\mathfrak{h}}_{t,2}|_{[y,y+K]}-Ct^{-1/3}\log M\in\mathsf{A}\ \Big|\ \hat{\mathfrak{h}}_{t,1}(y)=L\Bigr)$ $\displaystyle\leq\mathbb P\left(\hat{\mathfrak{h}}_{t,1}|_{[y,y+K]}\in\mathsf{A}\right)+3(K+1)t^{2/3}\exp(-cM^{2}).$ The same also holds when the conditioning is replaced by $\hat{\mathfrak{h}}_{t,1}(y)\geq L$. The same also holds under both conditionings when the processes are considered on $[y-K,y]$ rather than $[y,y+K]$.

The basic household reproduction number R_* is the expected number of global infectious contacts emanating from a single typically infected household during its entire within-household epidemic outbreak in an otherwise completely susceptible population: R_* = mu_G * mu_{out}(h), where mu_G = E[X_G] and mu_{out}(h) is the expected total number of individuals infected in the household (including the primary case). A major epidemic outbreak is possible if and only if R_* > 1.

body:
CAUTION ON THE NAME: 'Rosenblum's argument' is used for at least two different results of M. Rosenblum; this entry is the scattering-theory one, the Plancherel estimate that drives the Kato-Rosenblum theorem on trace class perturbations and the standard existence proofs for wave operators. STATEMENT: let A be a self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space H with spectral measure E, let psi in H be a vector whose spectral measure mu_psi(S) = <psi, E(S) psi> is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure with density bounded by a constant M (that is, d mu_psi / d lambda <= M almost everywhere), and let K be a Hilbert-Schmidt operator on H. Then the map t -> K exp(-i t A) psi is square integrable on R as an H-valued function and the integral over R of the squared norm of K exp(-i t A) psi dt is at most 2 pi M times the square of the Hilbert-Schmidt norm of K. Consequently the quantity tends to 0 along a sequence of times, and combined with Cook's criterion this is what produces existence of wave operators for perturbations that factor through Hilbert-Schmidt operators; note that the bound is UNIFORM over all vectors psi with the same density bound M, which is how the estimate is bootstrapped from a dense set of vectors to the whole absolutely continuous subspace. WHERE IT FAILS: (i) the bounded density is essential. If psi has any point mass, for instance if psi is an eigenvector of A, then the norm of K exp(-i t A) psi equals the norm of K psi for all t and the time integral is infinite unless K psi = 0. The lemma is a statement about the absolutely continuous subspace with a locally bounded density, not about arbitrary vectors. (ii) 'Hilbert-Schmidt' cannot be relaxed to 'bounded': taking K the identity makes the left-hand side the integral of a positive constant over R, which diverges. (iii) The constant 2 pi is tied to the Fourier convention; with the kernel exp(-2 pi i t lambda) the constant is 1. (iv) Nothing is claimed about the pointwise decay of the norm of K exp(-i t A) psi in t; only its square integrability.
H is a complex Hilbert space and A is self-adjoint on it
psi lies in the absolutely continuous subspace of A and its spectral density is bounded by M almost everywhere
K is Hilbert-Schmidt (in particular compact); boundedness alone is not enough
the Fourier convention is exp(-i t lambda), which fixes the constant 2 pi
the estimate is uniform in psi given the density bound and in K given its Hilbert-Schmidt norm

\[ f^{321}_\beta(x) := \frac12 + \frac1\beta \log\left( \frac{\textup{e}^{\beta x} + \textup{e}^{\beta/2}}{1 + \textup{e}^{\beta/2} + \textup{e}^{\beta} - \textup{e}^{\beta x}} \right) \,.\]
Then, the random permutations $\tau^{\beta,321}_{n}$ converge almost surely in the sense of permutons to the deterministic permuton
\[ \mu^{321}_\beta := \big( (X,f^{321}_\beta(X))_\# + (f^{321}_\beta(X),X)_\#  \big) \frac{\textup{d} x}{1+\exp\left(\beta(\frac12-x) \right)} 
\]
if $\beta>0$,
and to the diagonal permuton if $\beta\le 0.$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition defn:closen of arXiv:2411.10829, 'Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble and its Laplace transform'] Take $D>0$.
For any discrete blocks $(\vec p, \vec\upsilon, \mathcal H)$ of $(\hat{\mathfrak D}_{m}^{N_m})^{k_m} \cdots (\hat{\mathfrak D}_{1}^{N_1})^{k_1}$ which are valid in parity, and any blocks $(\vec \mathbf p, \vec\boldsymbol{\upsilon},\mathbf H)$ (with times $\vec \mathbf k\in \mathbb R_+^m$, and $\mathbf Q_\ell=\sum_{\ell'=1}^\ell \mathbf k_{\ell'}$ for each $\ell \in \llbracket 0, m\rrbracket$),
they are \emph{$D$-close}, or simply \emph{close} if the following conditions hold.
\begin{itemize}
    \item $u=\mathbf u$.
    \item For each $\ell\in\llbracket 1,m\rrbracket$, we have
$|k_\ell- \mathbf k_\ell N^{2/3}|<D$.
    \item For each $\ell\in\llbracket 1,m\rrbracket$, either $\upsilon_\ell=\boldsymbol{\upsilon}_\ell=\varnothing$, or
$|\upsilon_\ell-\boldsymbol{\upsilon}_\ell N^{2/3}|<D$ with $\upsilon_\ell\neq\varnothing$.
    \item For each $\ell \in \llbracket 1,m\rrbracket$ and $j\in \llbracket \ell, m+\mathbf u\rrbracket$, we have $\delta_{j,\ell}=\boldsymbol{\delta}_{j,\ell}$.
    Besides, if we denote the numbers in $\Delta_{j,\ell}$ and $\mathbf \Delta_{j,\ell}$ by $t_1<\cdots < t_{\delta_{j,\ell}}$ and $x_1<\cdots<x_{\delta_{j,\ell}}$ respectively, we have for each $i\in\llbracket 1, \delta_{j,\ell}\rrbracket$,
    \[
    |t_i - N^{2/3}x_i|,\quad |p^0(t_i)-N^{1/3}\mathbf p^0(x_i)|, \quad |\mathcal H(t_i) - N^{1/3}\mathbf H(x_i)| < D,
    \]
    and
\[
 (\mathbf p^0(x_i)-\mathbf p^0({x_i}-))(p^0(t_i)-p^0(t_i-1))>0,
\]
    and $p_j=0$ on $\llbracket Q_\ell, Q_m \rrbracket$ if and only if $\mathbf p_j=0$ on $[\mathbf Q_\ell,\mathbf Q_m]$.
\end{itemize}

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2606.14812, 'Joint convergence in Wiener chaos via transport hierarchy and Malliavin covariances'] Let $(X_N=I_p(f_N), N\geq 1)$, where $p\geq 2$ and $f_N\in H^{\odot p}$ 
	for each $N\geq 1$. Assume that $X_N$ satisfies \eqref{c1}. Consider a 
	$d$-dimensional random sequence $(\mathbb{Y}_N, N\geq 1)=((Y_{1,N},\ldots,
	Y_{d,N}), N\geq 1)$ such that for all $i=1,\ldots,d$,
	\begin{equation*}
		Y_{i,N} = \sum_{k=1}^\infty I_k(g_{k,N}^{(i)}), 
		\qquad g_{k,N}^{(i)}\in H^{\odot k} 
		\text{ for all } N,k\geq 1,\ i=1,\ldots,d.
	\end{equation*}
	Suppose that:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item There exists $\mathbb{Y}\in L^2(\Omega)$ such that 
		$\mathbb{Y}_N\to_{N\to\infty}\mathbb{Y}$ in $L^2(\Omega)$.
		\item For every $i=1,\ldots,d$, 
		$\mathbf{E}[X_NY_{i,N}]\to_{N\to\infty}\rho_i$.
		\item For every $i=1,\ldots,d$,
		\begin{equation}
			\sup_{N\geq 1}\sum_{k=M+1}^\infty k!\,
			\|g_{k,N}^{(i)}\|^2_{H^{\otimes k}} \to_{M\to\infty} 0.
		\end{equation}
	\end{enumerate}
	Then $(X_N,\mathbb{Y}_N)\xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{(d)}(Z,\mathbb{Y})$, 
	where $Z\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$ and the characteristic function of 
	$(Z,\mathbb{Y})$ is given by \eqref{phi}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: A parametric family of distributions {f(x;theta): theta in Theta subset R^k}, given as densities or pmfs with respect to a common sigma-finite dominating measure, is an exponential family if it can be written in the form f(x;theta) = h(x) * exp( sum_{i=1}^k eta_i(theta) * T_i(x) - A(theta) ), where h(x) >= 0 does not depend on theta, T_1,...,T_k are real-valued statistics not depending on theta, eta_1,...,eta_k are real-valued functions of theta called the natural parameters, and A(theta) = log( integral h(x) * exp( sum_{i=1}^k eta_i(theta) T_i(x) ) dx ) is the log-normalizing function that makes f integrate to 1. When theta is taken directly as the natural parameter (eta_i(theta) = theta_i), the family is said to be in canonical form.
title: Exponential Family

[Corollary 14 (Polynomial-size complements) of arXiv:2606.29530, 'Cutoff profiles for colored top-\texorpdfstring{$m$}{m}-to-random shuffles with growing bl'] Fix an integer $r\ge2$ and a number $a>0$. Suppose
\[
       n-m_n\sim a n^{1-1/r},
        \qquad
        k_n=r.
\]
Then
\[
        E_r^{(m_n)}\Rightarrow \Poisson(a^r),
\]
and for every fixed $p\ge1$,
\[
        \normTV{(Q_{n,p}^{(m_n)})^{*r}-U_{n,p}}\to f_p(-r\log a),
\]
while
\[
        \sepd\!\left((Q_{n,p}^{(m_n)})^{*r},U_{n,p}\right)\to
        \begin{cases}
        1-e^{-a^r}(1+a^r),&p=1,\\
        1-e^{-a^r},&p\ge2.
        \end{cases}
\]

[Lemma 22 of arXiv:2607.21374, 'Local structure at the maximum and sharp persistence asymptotics of rough fractional Brown'] Put
\begin{equation}
  \Gamma_\rho(t,u)
  :=K_H(t,u)-\frac{K_H(t,\rho)K_H(u,\rho)}{|\rho|^\alpha}.
  
\end{equation}
Fix \(0<a<R<\infty\) and \(r_*>0\).  There are
\(\rho_0,C>0\) such that, if \(0<|\rho|\leq\rho_0\),
\(s,t\in[a,R]\), and \(u\notin\{0,\rho\}\), then
\begin{equation}
  |\Gamma_\rho(t,u)-\Gamma_\rho(s,u)|
  \leq C|t-s|^\alpha\Gamma_\rho(r_*,u).
  
\end{equation}
If instead \(r_*<0\), the reflected estimate holds for
\(s,t\in[-R,-a]\), with the same quantifiers.

If \(v=1/\rho\) and
\begin{equation}
  \overline\Gamma_v(t,u)
  :=K_H(t,u)-\frac{K_H(t,v)K_H(u,v)}{|v|^\alpha},
  
\end{equation}
then, for every \(\bar r_*>0\), there are \(v_0,C>0\) such that
\[
 |\overline\Gamma_v(t,u)-\overline\Gamma_v(s,u)|
 \leq C|t-s|^\alpha\overline\Gamma_v(\bar r_*,u)
\]
whenever \(|v|\geq v_0\), \(s,t\in[a,R]\), and
\(u\notin\{0,v\}\).  The reflected far-pin estimate holds for
\(\bar r_*<0\) and \(s,t\in[-R,-a]\).  Every reference kernel on the
right is strictly positive on its displayed domain.
title: Lemma 22 of arXiv:2607.21374

[Cor degree-times-uniform of arXiv:2510.18856, 'Evolution of recursive trees with limited memory'] Let $\set{\left(\mathscr{E}_{j,k}\right)_{k\geqslant 1}:j\geqslant 0}$ be \emph{iid} copies of $\left(\mathscr{E}_{k-1\leadsto k}\right)_{k\geqslant 1}$ and $T_1$ be an exponential random variable of rate $1$ independent of $\set{\left(\mathscr{E}_{j,k}\right)_{k\geqslant 1}:j\geqslant 0}$. Then 
    \begin{equation*}
        \left(\log n - \log \lceil n U\rceil,\left(\tau_{j,k}^{\lceil nU \rceil}\right)_{k\geqslant 1}: j\geqslant 0 \right) \stackrel{d}{\longrightarrow} \left(T_1,\left(\mathscr{E}_{j,k}\right)_{k\geqslant 1}:j\geqslant 0 \right).
    \end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 14 of arXiv:2605.30560, 'Projected McKean--Vlasov Dynamics for Entropic Weak Optimal Transport'] A weak solution of \eqreftag{eq:Fokker-planck-a} is a weak continuous flow
$
    (\P_t)_{t\ge0}\subset\Pc(\Xc\times\R^d),
$ 
$
    \P_0=\pi_0,
$
together with a Borel vector field
$
    \hat A:\R_+\times\R^d\longrightarrow\R^d,
$
such that the following conditions hold.

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), ref=(\roman*)]
    \item 
    There exists \(p>1\) such that, for every \(T>0\),
    \[
    \int_0^T
    \int_{\Xc\times\R^d}
    \left|
    \hat A(t,y)
    -
    a\bigl(t,x,y,(\P_t)_x\bigr)
    -
    \nabla_y V(y)
    \right|^p
    \P_t(dx,dy)\,dt
    <\infty.
    \]

    \item 
    For every \(t\ge0\) and every
    \(h\in C_b(\Xc\times\R^d; \R)\) such that
    \(h(x,\cdot)\in C_c^\infty(\R^d; \R)\) for all \(x\in\Xc\),
    \begin{align*}
    \E^{\P_t}[h]
    =&
    \E^{\P_0}[h] 
    +
    \int_0^t
    \E^{\P_s}\!\Big[
    \nabla_y h(X,Y)\cdot
    \big(
    \hat A(s,Y)
    -
    a\bigl(s,X,Y,(\P_s)_X\bigr)
    -
    \nabla_y V(Y)
    \big)\Big]ds
    \\
    &+
    \int_0^t
    \E^{\P_s}\!\Big[ \Delta_y h(X,Y)
    \Big]ds .
\end{align*}

    \item[(iii)] 
    For a.e. \(t\ge0\),
    \[
    \hat A(t,y)
    =
    \E^{\P_t}\!\left[
        a\bigl(t,X,y,(\P_t)_X\bigr)
        \mid Y=y
    \right],
    \qquad
    \P_t\text{-a.s.}
    \]
\end{enumerate}
title: Definition 14 of arXiv:2605.30560

Let H be a complex Hilbert space and T: D(T) ⊂ H → H densely defined. Then: (a) T* is closed. (b) T is closable if and only if D(T*) is dense, and in that case T̄ = T**. (c) If T is closable, (T̄)* = T*. (d) ker T* = Ran(T)^⊥, and if T is closed also ker T = Ran(T*)^⊥ provided T* is densely defined (true for closed densely defined T). (e) If S ⊂ T (both densely defined) then T* ⊂ S*. (f) If B is bounded and everywhere defined, (T + B)* = T* + B*. In general only inclusions hold for sums and products: (S + T)* ⊃ S* + T* when S + T is densely defined, and (ST)* ⊃ T*S* when ST is densely defined; equality in (ST)* = T*S* holds if S is bounded and everywhere defined.

[Theorem thm:weighted-spatial-regularity of arXiv:2608.16119, 'Fully nonlinear parabolic equations under a fixed reference diffusion: weighted \texorpdfs'] Let $w$ be a regular weight of order $\alpha\geq0$.  Assume
Assumptions~(ass:reference-diffusion of the paper),
(ass:drift-multiplier of the paper), (ass:lipschitz-driver of the paper), and
(ass:differentiable-driver of the paper) at the same order $\alpha$.  Suppose
$C_w(X)<\infty$, $\delta_{\mathrm{sg}}>0$, and $\psi\in H^2(\mu_T)$.
Let $u^*$ be the unique order-$\alpha$ weighted Sobolev solution and set
$F^*=F_{u^*}$.  The following estimate holds with
$C=C\bigl(T,\lambda,\Lambda,M_1(a),\operatorname{osc}_\alpha(w),C_w(X),
\Lambda_b,L_x^{\mathrm{gr}},\mathbf L_f,
\delta_{\mathrm{sg}}^{-1}\bigr)>0$:
\begin{equation}
 \left\lVert D_xF^*\right\rVert_\alpha+\left\lVert D_x\mathsf G u^*\right\rVert_\alpha
 \leq C\left(
   \left\lVert m_x\right\rVert_\alpha+\left\lVert f_0\right\rVert_\alpha
   +T^{\alpha/2}\norm\psi_{H^2(\mu_T)}\right).
 
\end{equation}
In particular,
$F^*\in H_{x,\alpha}^1$ and
$\mathsf G u^*\in H_{x,\alpha}^1$.
title: Theorem thm:weighted-spatial-regularity of arXiv:2608.16119

body: In abstract algebra, an abelian group (G, +) is called finitely generated if there exist finitely many elements x_1, x_2, ..., x_s in G such that every x in G can be written in the form x = n_1 x_1 + n_2 x_2 + ... + n_s x_s for some integers n_1, n_2, ..., n_s. In this case, we say that the set {x_1, x_2, ..., x_s} is a generating set of G or that x_1, ..., x_s generate G. So, finitely generated abelian groups can be thought of as a generalization of cyclic groups.

[Lemma a24 of arXiv:2411.19926, 'Sparse Pseudospectral Shattering'] Fix $M\in{\mathbb{C}}^{n\times n}$ and $R\ge\max(2\left\|M\right\|,n/2)$. Let $N$ be a random matrix with i.i.d.~symmetric subgaussian entries. Then
\[\E\vol\Lambda_\varepsilon(M+N)
\le\pi (R + \varepsilon)^2\sup_{\left\|M'\right\|\le1.5R+\varepsilon}\Pr\mleft(\sigma_n(M'+N)\le\varepsilon\mright)
+\exp\mleft(-\Omega(R)\mright).
\]

[Proposition prop:8 of arXiv:2512.09219, 'Strong confluence of geodesics in Liouville quantum gravity'] ([GM21])
  
  For a GFF plus a continuous function $\mathtt{h}$, there exists a unique (up to a deterministic multiplicative constant) random metric $D_{\mathtt{h}}$ on $\mathbb{C}$ which is measurable with respect to $\mathtt{h}$ and satisfies the following almost sure properties.
  \begin{enumerate}
  \item 
 \textbf{Length space}: Almost surely, for all $u,v\in \mathbb{C}$, $D_\mathtt{h}(u,v)=\inf_{\eta}\ell(\eta;D_\mathtt{h})$, where the infimum is over all paths $\eta$ connecting $u,v$.
  \item 
   \textbf{Locality}: For any deterministic set $U\subseteq \mathbb{C}$, consider the induced metric $D_{\mathtt{h}}(\cdot,\cdot;U)$ defined by $D_{\mathtt{h}}(u,v;U)= \inf_{\eta\subseteq U} \ell(\eta; D_{\mathtt{h}})$,  where the infimum is taken over all paths contained in $U$. Then, for any fixed open set $U\subseteq \mathbb{C}$, the induced metric $D_{\mathtt{h}}(\cdot,\cdot;U)$ is measurable with respect to $\mathtt{h}\lvert_U$. 
  \item 
  \textbf{Weyl scaling}: For a continuous function $f\colon \mathbb{C}\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$, consider the metric $e^f\cdot D_h$ defined by $e^f\cdot D_h(u,v)=\inf_{\eta}\int_{0}^{\ell(\eta;D_h)}e^{f(\eta(t))}dt$, where the infimum is over all paths $\eta$ from $u$ to $v$. Then, for $\xi=\gamma/d_\gamma$, with $d_\gamma$ denoting the fractal dimension of $\gamma$-LQG as defined in [DG20], we a.s.\ have the equality $e^{\xi f}\cdot D_{\mathtt{h}}=D_{\mathtt{h}+f}$ simultaneously for every continuous function $f\colon \mathbb{C}\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$.
  \item 
   \textbf{Coordinate change formula}: Fix a deterministic $z\in \mathbb{C}$ and $r>0$. With $Q$ defined by $Q=\gamma/2+2/\gamma$ and the field $\mathtt{h}'$ defined by $\mathtt{h}'(\cdot)=\mathtt{h}(r\cdot+z)+Q\log r$, almost surely, for all $u,v\in \mathbb{C}$, we have $D_\mathtt{h}(ru+z,rv+z)=D_{\mathtt{h}'}(u,v)$.

  \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Proposition prop:8 of arXiv:2512.09219

[Definition 10 (Locally Lipschitz function) of arXiv:2605.18198, 'Large deviations of crowding in finite $\beta$-ensembles'] A function $F:\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^m$ is said to be \emph{locally Lipschitz}
	if for every compact set $K \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ there exists
	$L_K >0$ such that
	\[
	|F(x)-F(y)| \le L_K \|x-y\|,
	\quad
	\text{for all } x,y \in K .
	\]

[Lemma 15 (Weighted $L^2$ exit estimate) of arXiv:2608.26834, 'Small-time annealed large deviations principle for one-dimensional diffusions in a random '] Take intervals $A \subset D\subset {[-R,R]}$. Assume $v$ is a weak solution to equation (\ref{02}) on $(0,S)\times D$ satisfying $0 \le v \le 1$ and $v(0,x)=0,x \in D$. Assume
		\[
		r:=\inf\{d_W(y,z):y\in A,\ z\notin D\}>0.
		\]
		Then, for every $t \in (0,S)$,
		\begin{equation}
			\int_Av(t,y)^2\,\dd \mu_W(y)
			\le C\mu_W(D\setminus A)
			\left(1+\frac{t}{r^2}+\frac{r^2}{t}\right)
			\exp\left\{-\frac{r^2}{t}\right\},
		\end{equation}
		where $C$ is an absolute constant.

A Borel measure 
u on \mathbb{R} \setminus \{0\} is called a Lévy measure if \int_{\mathbb{R} \setminus \{0\}} \min(1, x^2) d
u(x) < \infty. In particular, 
u can have infinite total mass near the origin (infinite activity of small jumps), but must assign finite measure to sets bounded away from zero (finite activity of jumps of size > \epsilon).
title: Lévy Measure

[Theorem PCM-product of arXiv:2507.01406, '{\Large On Iterated Lorenz Curves with Applications: The Multivariate Case }'] \medskip \noindent  Let $d=2m$, and let $F$ be PCM with
continuous marginals and positive block normalizers $\mu _{r}$. Then the
Lorenz image $L_{F}$ factorizes blockwise: 
\begin{equation}
L_{F}(x_{1},\ldots ,x_{d})=\prod_{r=1}^{m}L_{r}(x_{2r-1},x_{2r}).

\end{equation}
In particular, the $i$-th marginal of $L_{F}$ depends only on the
countermonotone block containing $i$. \medskip
title: Theorem PCM-product of arXiv:2507.01406

[Proposition 11 (Impulse-response representation) of arXiv:2609.02728, 'Momentum in large-batch training: Polyak enlarges the critical batch size, Nesterov improv'] For any step $k \ge 0$, the coordinate-wise error trajectory of Polyak satisfies:
\begin{equation} 
    e_k(j)
    =
    e_k^{\mathrm{det}}(j)
    -
    \eta\sum_{m=0}^{k-1}G_{k-1-m}(j)\xi_m(j),
\end{equation}
where $e_k^{\mathrm{det}}(j)$ is the unperturbed deterministic trajectory solving:
\[
    e_{k+1}^{\mathrm{det}}(j)
    =
    (1+\rho-\eta\lambda_j)e_k^{\mathrm{det}}(j)
    -
    \rho e_{k-1}^{\mathrm{det}}(j),
\]
with initializations $e_0^{\mathrm{det}}(j) = e_0(j) = -\theta_j^*$ and $e_{-1}^{\mathrm{det}}(j) = e_{-1}(j) = -\theta_j^*$ (assuming $\btheta_0=\btheta_{-1}=\bm0$).

[Definition 16 of arXiv:2609.03976, '2609.03976'] Let $M$ be a coherent $\mathcal D_Y$-module. A V-filtration along $U \times \{0\} \subset Y$ on $\mathcal{M}$ is a decreasing filtration $V^{\bullet}\mathcal{M}$ indexed by rational numbers satisfying the following conditions.
		
		$(1)$ It is exhaustive, i.e. $\bigcup_{\alpha \in \mathbb{Q}}V^{\alpha}\mathcal{M}=\mathcal{M}$,
		
		$(2)$ It is discrete and left continuous. This means that there exists a positive integer $N$ large enough such that for every $i \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $\alpha \in (\frac{i}{N},\frac{i+1}{N})$, $V^{\alpha}\mathcal{M}$ is constant.
		
		$(3)$ For every $\alpha \in \mathbb{Q}$ and $i \in \mathbb{Z}$, we have $V^{i}\mathcal{D}_{x,t} \cdot V^{\alpha}\mathcal{M} \subset V^{i+\alpha}\mathcal{M}$.
		
		$(4)$ For every $\alpha \in \mathbb{Q}$, the operator $s+\alpha:=-\sum_{i=1}^{r}\partial_{t_{i}}t_{i}+\alpha$ is nilpotent on $\mathrm{Gr}_{V}^{\alpha}\mathcal{M}:=V^{\alpha}\mathcal{M}/\bigcup_{\beta>\alpha}V^{\beta}\mathcal{M}$.
		
		$(5)$ For every $\alpha \in \mathbb{Q}$, $V^{\alpha}\mathcal{M}$ is finitely generated over $V^{0}\mathcal{D}_{Y}$.
		
		$(6)$ For every $i>0$ and every sufficiently large $\alpha$,
		$V^i\mathcal D_Y\cdot V^\alpha M
		=
		V^{\alpha+i}M$.
title: Definition 16 of arXiv:2609.03976

[Definition 3 (i.i.d.\ random field and Bernoulli shift) of arXiv:2602.14618, 'Finitary coding and Gaussian concentration\\ for random fields'] Let $(A,\mathcal F)$ be a standard Borel space with probability law $\varrho$.
An \emph{i.i.d.\ random field} is a family $X=(X_i)_{i\in\Zd}$ of $A$-valued random variables
that are independent and identically distributed with law $\varrho$.
Equivalently, the joint law of $X$ on $A^{\Zd}$ is the product measure
$\varrho^{\otimes \Zd}$.
The associated \emph{$d$-dimensional Bernoulli shift} is the shift dynamical system
$\big(A^{\Zd},(T^j)_{j\in\Zd},\varrho^{\otimes \Zd}\big)$.

[Lemma lem:weighted-collar-monotonicity of arXiv:2608.30700, 'Convex hulls and area minimizing currents in asymptotically locally hyperbolic manifolds'] Let
    \[
        \delta(r) := C_0 e^{-r}, \qquad
        w(r) := \exp(-qC_0e^{-r}),
    \]
    and let $Z$ be an integral $p$-current of finite mass such that its associated varifold $|Z|$ is stationary in $\{a<r<t\}$. Define
    \[
        B(s):= \int_{\{a < r < s\}} w(r)\,d\left\lVertZ\right\rVert_g.
    \]
    Then $s\mapsto e^{-qs}B(s)$ is nondecreasing on $(a,t)$. Equivalently, for every $a<s<u<t$,
    \[
        B(s) \leq e^{-q(u-s)}B(u).
    \]
    If $\mathbf{M}_g(Z) \leq Le^{qt}$, then
    \[
        \left\lVertZ\right\rVert_g(\{a < r < s\}) \leq CLe^{qs}, \qquad
        a<s\leq t,
    \]
    where $C=w(a)^{-1}\leq e$.

[campaign result 2026-09-14, Author-checked only, no independent read.] This is the energy-flow extension of the restricted negative answer to the question in Chapter 4 of David Aldous and James Allen Fill's Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, unfinished monograph (2002, recompiled 2014; official source https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/RWG/book.html), recorded as intake row I0024. That question asks whether the relaxation time can be characterized exactly as an infimum over flows. Let G be a finite connected undirected graph with positive rational conductances c_e on its edges and distinct vertices a,b. Orient the edges arbitrarily and minimize E(f)=sum_e f_e^2/c_e over real flows f with divergence +1 at a, -1 at b, and zero at all other vertices. The minimum is the effective resistance R_eff(a,b). It is rational, because the electrical-flow optimality equations are a rational linear system. More generally, the same rationality conclusion holds for attained convex quadratic flow programs with rational data whose optimizing point is determined by a rational linear system. Therefore these minimum-energy constructions cannot universally return the relaxation time tau_2=1/(1-lambda_2) on rational reversible chains, since the simple random walk on the six-vertex path has tau_2=3+sqrt(5). This is an unrefereed campaign result.

[Corollary 5 of arXiv:2607.19873, 'Local limit theorem for the operator norm of products of random matrices'] Let $B$ be a compact metric space and let $\pi: E \to B$ be a 
Lipschitz vector bundle of dimension $d$ over $B$. 
Let $G$ be a locally compact group acting on $E$ by an isometric Lipschitz bundle action 
and let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $G$. 
Assume that there exists a constant $\alpha >0$ such that $\bb E ({\rm Lip}_E(g_1)^{\alpha} ) < \infty$. 
Let $\sigma_0: G \times B \to \bb R$ be a continuous cocycle satisfying \eqref{moment-assumption-02-a}.
Then, for every $\alpha' \in (0, \alpha)$ and $\gamma >0$ close enough to $0$, 
the operator $P_{\mu, z}$ is bounded on $\bf \Gamma^{\gamma}(E)$, 
and the map $z \mapsto P_{\mu, z}$
with values in the space of bounded operators on $\bf \Gamma^{\gamma}(E)$ 
is analytic on the strip $\{ z \in \bb C: |\Re(z)| < \alpha' \}$. 

Moreover, if $(G, \mu)$ satisfies the contraction property \eqref{contraction-property-on-B} on $B$,
then, for every $t \in \bb R$, 
the operator $P_{\mu, it}$ has essential spectral radius strictly less than $1$ on $\bf \Gamma^{\gamma}(E)$.
title: Corollary 5 of arXiv:2607.19873

body:
[campaign result 2026-09-14, author checked against a direct linear-algebra solve on twelve graphs, with the complete graph and the cycle as independent controls at the two extremes.] This is a sufficient-condition reduction of Open Problem 7.31 in David Aldous and James Allen Fill's Reversible Markov Chains and Random Walks on Graphs, unfinished monograph (2002, recompiled 2014; official source https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/RWG/book.html), which asks for tau_0=O(n) uniformly over distance-regular graphs other than cycles. Let G be a finite connected simple distance-regular graph with n>=2 vertices, valency k, and diameter d: for vertices at distance i, the numbers of neighbors one step closer to or farther from the target are constants c_i and b_i depending only on i. Use c_1=1, b_0=k, b_d=0. Let k_i be the number of vertices at distance i from a fixed vertex, so k_0=1, k_1=k, k_{i+1} c_{i+1}=k_i b_i, and n=sum_{i=0}^d k_i. For the simple random walk, let T_y be the first hitting time of y, measured in steps, and define tau_0=max_{x,y} E_x[T_y]; here tau_0 is the maximum mean hitting time, not the spectral Kemeny sum. Define the tail count T_i=sum_{j=i}^d k_j and u_i=k/(k_i c_i). The intersection recurrence gives u_1=1 and u_{i+1}=u_i c_i/b_i for 1<=i<d, hence tau_0/n=sum_{i=1}^d (T_i/n) product_{j=1}^{i-1}(c_j/b_j) <= sum_{i=1}^d product_{j=1}^{i-1}(c_j/b_j), where an empty product is one. A uniform bound on the last sum over noncycle distance-regular graphs would prove the requested O(n) estimate. The campaign does not prove this uniform bound, and the sufficient criterion is not asserted to be necessary. This is an unrefereed campaign result.
The graph and intersection numbers satisfy the preceding definitions.
Only indices j<d occur in denominators b_j.

body:
[Lem waf of arXiv:2412.00593, 'A new approach to strong convergence II.\\The classical ensembles'] Let $\boldsymbol{G}^N=(G_1^N,\ldots,G_r^N)$ be i.i.d.\ GUE/GOE/GSE random 
matrices of dimension $N$, and let $\boldsymbol{s}=(s_1,\ldots,s_r)$ be a 
free semicircular family. Then
$$
	\lim_{N\to\infty}
	\mathbf{E}[\mathop{\textnormal{tr}} P(\boldsymbol{G}^N)] =
	(\mathop{\textnormal{tr}}\otimes\tau)[P(\boldsymbol{s})]
$$
for every noncommutative polynomial
$P\in\mathrm{M}_D(\mathbb{C})\otimes\mathbb{C}\langle\boldsymbol{s}\rangle$.

Similarly, let $\boldsymbol{U}^N=(U_1^N,\ldots,U_r^N)$ be i.i.d.\ 
Haar-distributed random matrices in 
$\mathrm{U}(N)/\mathrm{O}(N)/\mathrm{Sp}(N)$, and let 
$\boldsymbol{u}=(u_1,\ldots,u_r)$ be free Haar unitaries. Then
$$
	\lim_{N\to\infty}
	\mathbf{E}[\mathop{\textnormal{tr}} P(\boldsymbol{U}^N,\boldsymbol{U}^{N*})] =
	(\mathop{\textnormal{tr}}\otimes\tau)[P(\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{u}^*)]
$$
for every noncommutative polynomial  
$P\in\mathrm{M}_D(\mathbb{C})\otimes\mathbb{C}\langle\boldsymbol{u},\boldsymbol{u}^*\rangle$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Weak asymptotic freeness

For $\phi: \mathbb R^d\to \mathbb R$ smooth and bounded, we define $M_t^N(\phi)$ for $t\in N^{-1}\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$ by the formula $M_0^N(\phi)=0$, and \begin{equation}M^N_{t+N^{-1}}(\phi) - M_t^N(\phi):= \mathscr B_N \int_I \phi(N^{-1/2}   x)\; (\mathcal L_N Z_N)(Nt,\mathrm d   x).\end{equation}
   Then for all $N\in \mathbb N$ and smooth bounded $\phi$, the process $M^N(\phi)$ is a martingale indexed by $N^{-1}\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}$, with respect to the filtration $(\mathcal F^\omega_{Nt})_{t\in N^{-1}\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}}$ where $\mathcal F_t^\omega:=\sigma(K_1,...,K_{t})$ for $t\in \mathbb N$ (and $\omega=(K_i)_{i=1}^\infty$ are the i.i.d. environment kernels as in Assumption \ref{a1}). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 33 of arXiv:2510.22155

body:
Let tasks z_j be iid from a fixed law. For each task let C_z be a nonempty affine subspace of R^d, and assume a common point x* belongs to C_z almost surely. Start from a deterministic x_1 and set x_(j+1)=P_(C_(z_j))x_j by exact Euclidean projection. Then for every k>=1, E[(1/k) sum_(j=1)^k (1/2)dist(x_(k+1),C_(z_j))^2]<=10||x_1-x*||^2/k. The mean counts sampled occurrences, including repetitions, and includes factor 1/2. The bound holds for arbitrary affine task ranks and is independent of task count and dimension. It is not a statement about an adversarial ordering or a distinct-label mean.
iid task samples from a fixed law
nonempty affine solution sets in finite-dimensional real Euclidean space
one common solution almost surely
exact Euclidean projection at each update
deterministic initial model

[Theorem 12 (Primitive normal-cone theorem) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] There is a natural isomorphism of normal-graded Hopf algebras
\begin{equation}
 {\operatorname{gr}}_JT(V)\cong T(Q)\#_\rho S(V)
 \cong U\!\left(V_{\mathrm{ab}}\ltimes_\rho{\mathfrak L}(Q)\right).
 
\end{equation}
The isomorphism is induced by the identity on the degree-zero primitives
\(L/D\cong V\) and the degree-one primitives \(D/[D,D]=Q\), and it
respects ordinary tensor degree.
Consequently,
\begin{align}
 J^r/J^{r+1}&\cong Q^{\otimes r}\otimes S(V),
 \\
 {\operatorname{Prim}}({\operatorname{gr}}_JT(V))_0&\cong V,
 \qquad
 {\operatorname{Prim}}({\operatorname{gr}}_JT(V))_r
 \cong{\mathfrak L}_r(Q)\cong\gamma_r(D)/\gamma_{r+1}(D),
 \quad r\geq1,
 
\end{align}
and, most importantly,
\begin{equation}
 L\cap J^r=\gamma_r(D),\qquad r\geq1.
 
\end{equation}
Thus normal order and derived-ideal ancestry agree exactly.

Own-work draft. Status: proof (unaudited), T323-SMALLBETA-001 v2; no independent audit. Fix finite n>=1 and a symmetric real 3x3 V with eigenvalues lambda_1>=lambda_2>0>lambda_3. For the self-inclusive projected sphere attention flow on (S^2)^n with Q^T K=V, there exists epsilon(V,n)>0 such that for each 0<beta<epsilon, product-volume-almost every initial configuration converges to consensus at one unit vector in the top eigenspace of V. This covers normalized and unnormalized flows. Repeated largest eigenvalues are included. Epsilon is existential and need not be uniform in n or V. Arbitrary Q,K and arbitrary beta remain unresolved. Local consensus stability was already proved by Kuehn-Yoon; the candidate increment is the full small-beta almost-everywhere classification.
Finite n>=1
V symmetric, signature (2,1)
Q^T K=V
Full self-inclusive projected continuous-time attention
0<beta<epsilon(V,n) for an existential epsilon>0

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:43dfff679777bde2aec8b50d70caba065aa1734605bc7baf904adc3af97ec957","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/43/43dfff679777bde2aec8b50d70caba065aa1734605bc7baf904adc3af97ec957.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:2943453dc6dea0c3f262e92646c951edfb84c23fb0aefe5eb0e7e4a3019d04ac","bundle_entry_key":"small-beta-draft","bundle_id":"population.t323-symmetric-attention-frontier-20261020","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"spherical self-attention dynamics","draft":"w696/bundle_001.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:analysis.dynamical_systems:t323-aligned-indefinite-attention-small-beta-consensus-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# Signature-(2,1) aligned attention: almost-everywhere consensus at small beta

T323-SMALLBETA-001 v2. Proof (unaudited). Kind narrowed; target 2.
This version includes repeated positive eigenvalues. Version 1 remains saved.

## Theorem and exact scope
Let n>=1 be finite and let V be a real symmetric 3x3 matrix with signature
(2,1). Write its eigenvalues lambda_1>=lambda_2>0>lambda_3, and let E_top
be its largest-eigenvalue eigenspace. Consider the full, self-inclusive,
normalized projected attention flow on M=(S^2)^n, with Q^T K=V:

 dot x_i = P_i sum_j exp(beta x_i^T V x_j) Vx_j / Z_i,
 Z_i = sum_j exp(beta x_i^T V x_j),  P_i=I-x_i x_i^T.

There exists epsilon(V,n)>0 such that, for every 0<beta<epsilon(V,n),
for product-volume-almost every initial configuration, every token
converges to the same unit vector u in E_top. In particular, if the top
eigenvalue is simple, the only possible generic limits are consensus at
+e_1 or -e_1. For a repeated top eigenvalue the limit is a single point
of the top-plane unit circle, not necessarily a predetermined orientation.
The same assertion holds for the unnormalized flow, omitting Z_i.

This is not a result for arbitrary Q,K, every beta, or uniformity in n.
The exceptional null set may depend on beta. No numerical lower bound on
epsilon is asserted. The source paper already gives local consensus
stability; the candidate increment is the complete almost-everywhere
small-beta classification for the indefinite family.

## 1. Energy and its regular zero-beta limit
For X=(x_i), S=sum_i x_i, set

 F_beta(X) = (1/(2 beta)) sum_ij [exp(beta x_i^T V x_j)-1],
 F_0(X) = (1/2) S^T V S.

Expanding the exponential shows joint real analyticity in beta and X near
beta=0, and uniform C^r convergence on compact M for each finite r.
Symmetry of V, including the diagonal terms i=j, gives

 grad_i F_beta=P_i sum_j exp(beta x_i^T Vx_j) Vx_j.

The normalized dynamics is its gradient ascent for the positive analytic
metric g_beta(U,W)=sum_i Z_i <u_i,w_i>; the unnormalized dynamics uses
the product metric. This is the known aligned gradient construction in
2312.10794 section 3.4. At beta=0, g_0 is n times the product metric.

## 2. Complete critical landscape at beta=0
For tangent U=(u_i), W=sum_i u_i, differentiating along product geodesics
produces the background-product-metric Hessian identity

 Hess F_0[U,U] = W^T V W - sum_i (x_i^T V S)||u_i||^2.       (H)

Criticality is P_i VS=0 for all i. The positive spectral space E_+ has
dimension two, so E_+ intersect x_i^perp always has a nonzero vector with
strictly positive V-quadratic form.

If S=0, take only one nonzero u_i in this intersection. Formula (H) is
u_i^T V u_i>0. Thus EVERY zero-mean critical point is a strict saddle.

If S!=0, invertibility gives h=VS!=0. Criticality implies
x_i=s_i u, s_i in {+1,-1}, u=h/||h||. If signs are mixed, choose i with
s_i=-1 and only u_i nonzero, again in E_+ intersect u^perp. Then (H) is
u_i^T V u_i + ||h|| ||u_i||^2>0. Every such point is a strict saddle.

If all tokens coincide at x, criticality says Vx=lambda x. When
lambda<lambda_1, a unit v in E_top is orthogonal to x. Taking every
u_i=v makes (H)=n^2(lambda_1-lambda)>0. Thus the only critical points
without a positive Hessian direction belong to

 C={ (u,...,u): u in E_top, ||u||=1 }.

C is two points when lambda_1>lambda_2 and a circle when they coincide.
At any point of C, diagonalize V in a basis starting with u. For each
transverse eigenvector with eigenvalue mu, the n-coordinate Hessian block
is mu 11^T - n lambda_1 I_n. Its eigenvalues are n(mu-lambda_1)
on the common mode and -n lambda_1 on the n-1 disagreement modes.
The only zero modes are common modes with mu=lambda_1, precisely T C.
Every normal mode is strictly negative. Thus C is a compact Morse-Bott
maximum manifold (in the simple case, two nondegenerate maxima).

## 3. No additional critical points can enter a neighborhood of C
C remains an exact critical manifold for every beta, since the weighted
sum at consensus is proportional to Vu=lambda_1 u. At C, the first
variation of every score x_i^T Vx_j vanishes on T M. Therefore

 Hess F_beta|_C = exp(beta lambda_1) Hess F_0|_C.

In particular its kernel is T C and its normal Hessian is strictly negative.
For clarity, the local isolation conclusion follows without asserting a
general persistence theorem: take tubular bundle coordinates (a,z) near C,
where a parametrizes C and z is normal. Since C is critical,
partial_z F_beta(a,0)=0 for all a and beta. The derivative in z of this
normal-gradient equation at beta=0,z=0 is the invertible negative normal
Hessian. The implicit function theorem gives z=0 as its unique nearby
solution, jointly for a and small beta. Compactness of C supplies a finite
collection of such charts and fixed U containing C, and eta>0, in which
all critical points of F_beta lie on C whenever |beta|<eta. The sphere's
normal bundle need not be trivial; this is a finite local-chart argument.

## 4. All critical points outside C stay strict saddles for small beta
K=M minus U is compact. If the conclusion failed arbitrarily near zero,
there would exist beta_j down to zero and critical X_j in K with no
positive Hessian direction. Pass to X_j->X_* in K. Uniform C^2 convergence
implies grad F_0(X_*)=0 and Hess F_0(X_*) negative semidefinite, measured
in a fixed background metric. Step 2 forces X_* in C, contrary to K
being disjoint from U. Thus some epsilon>0 works simultaneously for all
critical points: for 0<beta<epsilon the only critical points without a
positive Hessian direction are exactly C.

This compactness step gives a genuine interval, not a beta depending on
the starting point. It does not give a numerical threshold. At critical
points Hessian inertia is independent of the positive Riemannian metric.

## 5. Trajectory convergence and the null exceptional set
For each fixed beta in that interval, compactness and the real analytic
Lojasiewicz gradient inequality give convergence of every gradient
trajectory to one critical point. The metric g_beta is positive analytic;
there is no issue from normalization. A local inequality near a critical
accumulation point bounds remaining arc length by an energy gap to a
positive power; taking a sufficiently late entry traps the trajectory
there and makes it Cauchy. This also applies to a critical manifold: a
single limiting point is obtained, rather than convergence merely in
distance to C.

Geshkovski et al., 2312.10794 Appendix A Lemma A.1, states that on a
compact Riemannian manifold the initial points whose gradient-ascent
trajectory converges to a strict saddle form a volume-zero set. It does
not require isolated saddles. Apply it to F_beta with g_beta. Its volume
and product volume have positive smooth density ratios bounded above
and below on M, so their null sets agree. All remaining limits lie in C
by Step 4. This proves the statement. For USA, repeat with the product
metric throughout.

## Provenance and limits
The aligned metric and the convergence/avoidance architecture are known.
The Hessian block at simple consensus reproduces the known Kuehn-Yoon
2604.26085 Proposition 5.1; it is not claimed as new. Their Theorem 6.1
requires a common-sign initial cone and dominant absolute eigenvalue;
Theorem 6.4 requires negative definiteness and n=2. Neither supplies the
claimed almost-everywhere signature-(2,1) small-beta conclusion.

Candidate new step: classify EVERY beta=0 critical point using the
2-dimensional positive spectral space, and transport this landscape by
compactness plus normal isolation of C. No claim of independent audit
or exhaustive literature priority is made. Relevant current searches
and primary sources are recorded in logs/lit1.json through lit6.json
and SOURCES.jsonl. Full arbitrary-beta classification remains open here.

body:
[Lemma lem:global-decay of arXiv:2608.26745, 'Moderate Deviations for the Largest Eigenvalue of a Randomly Deformed Gaussian Unitary Ens'] Let $a_j=w_N-\xi_j$.  For $j=1,2$, define
\[
 g_j(t)=\Re\{f_N(C_j(t))-f_N(w_N)\},
\]
and for $j=3,4$ define
\[
 g_j(t)=-\Re\{f_N(C_j(t))-f_N(w_N)\}.
\]
Then
\begin{align}
 g_1'(t)=g_2'(t)
 &=-\sum_{k=1}^N
 \frac{2t^2}{a_k\{(a_k+t)^2+t^2\}},                    \\
 g_3'(t)=g_4'(t)
 &=-\sum_{k=1}^N
 \frac{2t^2}{a_k\{(a_k-t)^2+t^2\}}.                    
\end{align}
Consequently, uniformly over all truncated configurations (and hence on
$\mathcal G_N$), there is a constant $c>0$ such that
\begin{align}
 g_j(t)&\le-c\frac{Nt^3}{w_N^3},
 &&0\le t\le\frac{w_N}{2},                             \\
 g_j(t)&\le-cN-c\frac{N}{w_N}\Big(t-\frac{w_N}{2}\Big),
 &&\frac{w_N}{2}\le t<\infty.                                  
\end{align}

body:
[Theorem Fourier transform: convolutors \(\leftrightarrow\) multipliers, Theorem 30.3 of \cite{treves2016topological} of arXiv:2512.04371, 'Constructive Approximation under Carleman's Condition, \\ with Applications to Smoothed An'] With the above Fourier convention, the Fourier transform is a bijection
\[
  \mathcal F:\ \mathcal O'_C(\mathbb{R}^d) \xrightarrow{\;\simeq\;} \mathcal O_M(\mathbb{R}^d),
\]
and it identifies convolution operators with multiplication operators in the sense that
for every \(T\in\mathcal O'_C(\mathbb{R}^d)\) and \(\varphi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb{R}^d)\),
\[
  \widehat{T*\varphi} = (\widehat T)\,\widehat\varphi, \qquad \widehat T \in \mathcal O_M(\mathbb{R}^d).
\]
Conversely, for every \(a\in\mathcal O_M(\mathbb{R}^d)\) there exists a unique \(T\in\mathcal O'_C(\mathbb{R}^d)\)
with \(\widehat T = a\), and multiplication \(\varphi\mapsto a\varphi\) corresponds under \(\mathcal F^{-1}\)
to convolution \(\varphi\mapsto T*\varphi\) on \(\mathcal S(\mathbb{R}^d)\). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2604.21143, 'Quantitative homogenization for the critical long-range random conductance model'] For $u, v \in \Zd$ with $u \ne v$, let $\gamma_{v \to u}$ be the nearest-neighbour path from $v$ to $u$ obtained by changing coordinates one at a time in the order $1, \ldots, d$.
		Let $e$ be an undirected nearest-neighbour edge of $\Zd$, and let $z \in \Zd \setminus \{0\}$.
		Then the number of pairs $(u,v) \in (\Zd)^2$ such that $v - u = z$ and $\gamma_{v \to u}$ uses $e$ is at most $|z|_1$.
		
		More generally, for $\eps \in (0,1)$, let $e$ be an undirected nearest-neighbour edge of $\eps\Zd$, and let $z \in \eps\Zd \setminus \{0\}$.
		Then the number of pairs $(u,v) \in (\eps\Zd)^2$ such that $v - u = z$ and $\gamma_{v \to u}$ uses $e$ is at most $|z|_1/\eps$.

\qquad h\in(0,1],
\end{equation}
where
\[
\eta_{12}:=\min\{2(\alpha_1+\alpha_2)-1,\,2\}>1.
\]

[Def 18 of arXiv:2604.24189, 'Malliavin calculus and densities for chaos-driven stochastic differential equations'] The one-dimensional Hermite process $Z^{H,q}=\left(Z_t^{H,q}\right)_{t \in \R_+}$ of order $q\geq 1$ and self-similarity parameter $H \in\left(\frac{1}{2}, 1\right)$ is defined by
\begin{align}
	Z^{H,q}_t=I_q(L_t^{H, q}) \qquad \text{where} \qquad L_t^{H, q}(\xi)=c(H, q) \int_0^t \prod_{j=1}^q\left(s-\xi_j\right)_{+}^{H_0-\frac{3}{2}} ds,
\end{align}
$$
H_0=1+\frac{H-1}{q} \in\left(1-\frac{1}{2 q}, 1\right), \quad\text{and}\quad c(H, q)=\sqrt{\frac{H(2 H-1)}{q!\,\beta^q\left(H_0-\frac{1}{2}, 2-2 H_0\right)}}.
$$
Here $\beta$ stands for the Beta function and we use the convention, for each $(\theta, \alpha) \in \R^2$,
		\[\theta^{\alpha}_+:=\left\{ \begin{array}{rl}\theta^{\alpha}, & \text{if }\theta>0,\\ 0, &  \text{otherwise}. \end{array}\right. \]

Let X, Y and Z be random variables with finitely many values on one probability space, with Z = f(Y) almost surely for some function f. Then H(X | Z) - H(X | Y) = H(Y | Z) - H(Y | X, Z), and both sides equal the conditional mutual information I(X; Y | Z). Entropies use natural logarithms with 0 ln 0 = 0, and a conditional entropy averages only over conditioning values of positive probability; dividing every term by ln 2 gives the same statement in bits.

body:
Let W be an n by n real symmetric (or Hermitian) random matrix with independent entries above the diagonal having mean zero and variance 1/n (and mild moment conditions, e.g. uniformly bounded fourth moments). Then the empirical spectral distribution of W converges weakly, almost surely, to the semicircle distribution with density (1/(2 pi)) sqrt(4 - x^2) on [-2, 2].

[Theorem thm:FH10.5 of arXiv:2601.21762, 'Navier-Stokes with a fractional transport noise as a limit of multi-scale dynamics'] Let $(X,Y)=(X^i,Y^i)_i$ be a centered Gaussian process on $[0,T]$, such that $(X^i,Y^i)$ is independent of 
    $(X^j, Y^j)$ when $i \neq j$. Assume that there exists $\rho \in [1,2)$, and $\{M_i\}\in \ell^1$, such that 
    \begin{align*}
        \norm{R_{X^i}}_{\rho,[s,t]^2} &\leq M_i |t-s|^{\frac{1}{\rho}}, \qquad
        \norm{R_{Y^i}}_{\rho,[s,t]^2} \leq M_i |t-s|^{\frac{1}{\rho}}, \quad 
        \norm{R_{X^i-Y^i}}_{\rho,[s,t]^2} &\leq \epsilon^2 M_i |t-s|^{\frac{1}{\rho}},
    \end{align*}
for all $i\geq 1$ and $0\leq s \leq t \leq T.$ Then
    \begin{itemize}
        \item [a)] For every $q\in [1,\infty)$ and for all $0\leq s \leq t \leq T$,
       $$
            \mathbb{E} \left[\norm{Y_{s,t} - X_{s,t}}^q \right]^{\frac{1}{q}} \lesssim \epsilon \sqrt{\left\| M \right\|_{\ell^1}}
            |t-s|^{\frac{1}{2\rho}}, \qquad 
            \mathbb{E} \left[\norm{\mathbb{Y}_{s,t} - \mathbb{X}_{s,t}}^q \right]^{\frac{1}{q}} \lesssim \epsilon \left\| M \right\|_{\ell^1}
            |t-s|^{\frac{1}{\rho}}.
$$
        \item [b)] For any $\alpha < \frac{1}{2\rho}$ and $q\in [1,\infty)$, one has
        \begin{align*}
            \mathbb{E} \left[\left\| Y-X \right\|_\alpha^q\right]^{\frac{1}{q}} &\lesssim \epsilon \sqrt{\left\| M \right\|_{\ell^1}}, \qquad
            \mathbb{E} \left[\norm{\mathbb{Y}-\mathbb{X}}_{2\alpha}^q\right]^{\frac{1}{q}} \lesssim \epsilon \left\| M \right\|_{\ell^1}.
        \end{align*}
        \item[c)] For $\rho \in [1, \frac{3}{2})$ and any $\alpha \in (\frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{2\rho})$ , $q<\infty$ one has 
       $$ \mathbb{E}\left[\rho_\alpha(\mathbf{X},\mathbf{Y})^q \right]^{\frac{1}{q}} \lesssim \epsilon. $$
    \end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem thm:FH10.5 of arXiv:2601.21762

[Lemma 40 (Equivalence of intrinsic and fixed-chart norms) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Fix \(n\), \(m\geq2\), \(\sigma\in(0,1)\), \(\Lambda\geq1\), and \(L>0\).
Suppose that
\(\PBG_m(s;\Lambda;[a,b])\) holds and \(b-a\leq L\).  Let
\(\|\cdot\|_{X_{s,{\mathrm{fc}}}^m[a,b]}\) and
\(\|\cdot\|_{Y_{s,{\mathrm{fc}}}^m[a,b]}\) denote the suprema of the Euclidean
component norms in the fixed lifted atlas supplied by
Lemma~\ref{lem:uniform-parabolic-atlas}.  Then there is
\(C=C(n,m,\sigma,\Lambda,L)\) such that every deck-invariant tensor \(U\)
satisfies
\begin{align}
 C^{-1}\|U\|_{X_s^m[a,b]}
 &\leq \|U\|_{X_{s,{\mathrm{fc}}}^m[a,b]}
 \leq C\|U\|_{X_s^m[a,b]},                                      \\
 C^{-1}\|U\|_{Y_s^m[a,b]}
 &\leq \|U\|_{Y_{s,{\mathrm{fc}}}^m[a,b]}
 \leq C\|U\|_{Y_s^m[a,b]}.                                      
\end{align}
The analogous comparison holds for every spatial
\(C^{k,\sigma}\)-norm with \(0\leq k\leq m\).  For tensors on the universal
cover that are not deck-invariant, the same local comparison holds with the
fixed-chart side interpreted as the uniformly local norm.

[Proposition prop: Yu replace sum by min of arXiv:2411.17109, 'On the maximal correlation of some stochastic processes'] Let $X_1,X_2,\ldots,X_n$ be i.i.d. real-valued random variables. Let $1\leq \ell+1\leq m\leq n$. Then we have that
\begin{equation}
R\left(\min_{i:1\leq i\leq m}X_i,\min_{j:\ell+1\leq j\leq n}X_j\right)\leq\frac{m-\ell}{\sqrt{m(n-\ell)}}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 20 of arXiv:2606.24056, 'Decorated stable $p$-adic self-similar processes with stationary increments'] Assume \(0<\alpha<2\).  Then every decorated $p$-adic harmonizable fractional stable motion has finite minimal
spectral supremum.  On the other hand, the \(p\)-adic log-fractional stable motion with $H=1/\alpha$, the $p$-adic linear fractional stable motion with $H<1/\alpha$, and the BRW tree process with $H\leq 1/\alpha$ all have infinite minimal
spectral supremum.

[Theorem intersection.twodifferent of arXiv:2411.19145, 'On the intersection of critical percolation clusters and other tree-like random graphs'] Let $\mathcal G$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal G}$ two random graphs on the same metric space $(V,d_V)$, satisfying both the BK inequality, and respectively~(equation Halpha of the paper) and $(\mathcal H_\beta)$, for some $\alpha,\beta \in(\frac{d}{2},d)$, with $\alpha\le \beta$, and $2\alpha + 2\beta > 3d$. Let $\mathcal C_0$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal C}_0$ the clusters of the origin in $\mathcal G$ and $\widetilde{\mathcal G}$ respectively. There exsits a constant $\kappa>0$, such that

\mathbb E\Big[\exp\big(\kappa\cdot  |\mathcal C_0\cap \widetilde{\mathcal C}_0|^\gamma\big)\Big]<\infty, \quad \textrm{with}\  
\gamma = \frac{2\alpha - d}{d+ 2\alpha - 2\beta}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

We say that the triple $(X,Y,i)$ admits a Cannon-Thurston map, if
$i$ extends continuously to 
$\widehat i: \widehat Y \to \widehat X$. The continuous extension, if it exists, is referred to as a \emph{Cannon-Thurston map} for 
$i: Y \to X$.

[Theorem thm:tree-polytope of arXiv:2609.03412, 'Toughness Bounds for Fractional Hamiltonicity and Resistance Positivity'] Let $G=(V,E)$ be connected. Then $P(G)$ is the set of all
$x=(x_e)_{e\in E}\in\mathbb R^E$ satisfying:
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
    \item $x_e\ge0$ for every $e\in E$;
    \item $x(E)=|V|-1$;
    \item $x(E[S])\le |S|-1$ for every nonempty proper set
    $S\subsetneq V$, where $E[S]$ is the set of edges with both endpoints
    in $S$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Publication record. Y. Shmalo, The layer distribution of the random recursive tree and the minimum of the Poisson-weighted infinite tree (2026). The layer of a vertex of a tree is the number of rounds of leaf removal after which it is a leaf. Stepanyants, Krapivsky, Hartle and Krioukov (arXiv:2608.04303) showed that the limiting proportion of vertices at layer at least k in a random recursive tree is lbar_k = int_0^inf s_k(y) e^(-y) dy with s_0 = 1 and s_i(y) = 1 - exp(-int_0^y s_(i-1)), and conjectured that the proportion l_k at layer exactly k is exp[-k/e - (3/(2e)) log k - O(1)]. The paper proves lbar_k e^(k/e) k^(3/(2e)) -> C_* in (0, inf) and l_k e^(k/e) k^(3/(2e)) -> (1 - e^(-1/e)) C_*. The recursion is the distribution function of the minimal position M_k in generation k of the Poisson-weighted infinite tree, so lbar_k = E exp(-M_k), and the asymptotics follow from Addario-Berry and Ford (Ann. Appl. Probab. 2013) and Aidekon (Ann. Probab. 2013). It also proves the layer half of their Conjecture 2: in every finite tree the largest layer is floor(diameter/2), and for the random recursive tree on n vertices it is e log n - (3/2) log log n + O_P(1); the largest rank is not treated. Paper and code: https://github.com/yspennstate/rrt-layer-tail (commit 0f20604c8b2b). Not refereed.
title: Layer distribution of the random recursive tree: lbar_k e^(k/e) k^(3/(2e)) converges, proving Conjecture 1 of Stepanyants-Krapivsky-Hartle-Krioukov (Shmalo 2026, repository yspennstate/rrt-layer-tail)

[Theorem 2 (Mod-$\phi$ convergence for cyclotomic generating functions) of arXiv:2608.14143, 'Mod-$\phi$ convergence for random variables with cyclotomic generating functions'] Let $(X_N)_{N\in\N}$ be a sequence of random variables and consider the rescaled moment generating functions $\E\!\big[e^{zX_N/s_N}\big]$, which are of the form \eqref{eq:DefKN},
 where $s_N\to\infty$ and $b_{N,j} \ge a_{N,j}$ for all $j=1, \ldots, N$ and all $N\in\N$.  Suppose there exists a 
	non-decreasing function $f\in C^{2}[0,1]$ with $f(1)>0$ such that $b_{N,j}/s_N=f(j/N)$ for all $j=1,\ldots,N$.  Further, assume  $\delta_{N,j}:=a_{N,j}/s_N$ satisfies
	\[
	\max_{1\le j\le N} \delta_{N,j} \to 0, \qquad 
	\sum_{j=1}^{N}\delta_{N,j} \to \Sigma \in [0,\infty),
	\]
	as $N\to\infty$. Then the sequence of random variables ${X_N}/{s_N}$ converges mod-$\phi$ with parameter sequence $w_N=N$, domain $\widetilde{\mathscr{D}} = \{z\in \C: \Im z \in (-\pi/M, \pi/M)\}\cup \{z\in\C: \Re z < 0\}$ with $M := f(1)$, and normalization function and limiting function given by
	\begin{align*}
	\phi(z) &= \int_{0}^{1} \log\Bigl(\frac{e^{z f(t)}-1}{z f(t)}\Bigr)\,dt, \\
	\psi(z) &= \exp\left(
		\frac12\,\log\Bigl(\frac{e^{z f(1)}-1}{z f(1)}\Bigr)
		- \frac12\,\log\Bigl(\frac{e^{z f(0)}-1}{z f(0)}\Bigr)
		- \frac{z}{2}\,\Sigma
	\right).
	\end{align*}
If, in addition, we have $f(0) = 0$, then the same result holds on
$$
\mathscr{D} := \bigl\{z\in \C: \frac{e^{z f(t)}-1}{z f(t)}\not\in (-\infty, 0] \text{ for all } t\in [0,1]\bigr\}.
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Mod-$\phi$ convergence for cyclotomic generating functions

[Theorem 1 of arXiv:2604.07478, 'Mixing Times and Cutoff for the Rook's Walk'] Let $t_\text{mix}(\epsilon)$ with $\epsilon >0$ be the mixing time of the Rook's Walk with dimension $d$ and board-length $n$. Then,
      \begin{multline*}
       \left(\log \left(\frac{d(n-1)}{2n}\right) + \log\left(\frac{1-\epsilon}{\epsilon}\right)\right)\left(2\log\left(\frac{d(n-1)}{d(n-1)-n}\right)\right)^{-1} \\
        \leq t_\text{mix}(\epsilon)  \leq-\frac{d(n-1)}{2n}\log\left((4\epsilon^2+1)^{1/d}-1\right) 
      \end{multline*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Identify what the log n scaling comes from and whether it survives without (POS1). Result: The log n factor at delta = 1 comes from the total progeny of the critical branching process with migration delta = 1 having a tail n^{-1/2} with a logarithmic correction, so that the time to make n right excursions is of order n^2 log n, equivalently the maximum after time t is of order sqrt(t)/log t... the source's scaling sqrt n log n for X_{[nt]} reflects the backtracking being negligible at that scale. Under (6.2) the migration has finite mean and the critical tail should persist (same mechanism as C0134). Removing (POS1) allows left-pushing cookies; the walk then has non-negligible backtracking below its maximum, and the limit of X itself (not only its maximum) may differ from the running maximum; the maximum process S should still converge to the running maximum of Brownian motion since the backtracking affects only the difference S - X, whose scale is the length of a typical left excursion, of order sqrt(n) (diffusive) which is o(sqrt n log n). So the expected answer is: the theorem persists under (6.2), and without (POS1) the maximum still converges but X - S is O(sqrt n), negligible at the sqrt n log n scale, so the conclusion for X persists too. The proof would need the branching-process comparison for two-sided cookies (the branching process with migration then has both immigration and emigration), which is the source's [KM11]-type framework; not carried out. Key identity: Backtracking scale sqrt(n) is negligible against the sqrt(n) log n scale of the maximum at delta = 1. Obstruction: Two-sided branching-with-migration comparison not verified under (6.2) without (POS1).

[Proposition 64 of arXiv:2609.00567, 'Hodge--Tate splitting and Akizuki--Nakano vanishing in positive characteristic'] Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p$.
Let $X$ be a flat projective scheme over $W(k)$ and let $\mcalM$ be a coherent sheaf on $X$.
Let $X_{\F_p}$ be the closed fiber of $X$ and let $\iota \colon X_{\F_p} \to X$ be the closed immersion.
For $i \in \Z$, we have
\[
R\Gamma_{(p)}(X,\mcalM) \in \mcalD^{\geq i} \Leftrightarrow R\Gamma(X_{\F_p},Li^*\mcalM) \in \mcalD^{\geq i-1} \Rightarrow R\Gamma(X,\mcalM) \in \mcalD^{\geq i-1},
\]
where $R\Gamma_{(p)}(X,\mcalM) \defeq R\Gamma_{(p)}R\Gamma(X,\mcalM)$.

    \frac{\log n - \log \log n}{n}$. More precisely, if $x \in \mathbb{R}$
    \[
    \mbox{ for } p_{n,x} = \frac{\log n - \log \log n + x}{n} \quad  \mbox{ we have } \quad         \bP _{p_{n,x}}\left( 1 \nearrow n \right) 
        \xrightarrow[n \to \infty]{}  1 - e^{e^{-x} - x} \int_{e^{-x}}^\infty \frac{e^{-t}}{t} \mathrm{d} t.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop 5 of arXiv:2506.15341, '\bf Superpositions for General Conditional Mckean-Vlasov Stochastic Differential Equations'] Assume that Assumption \ref{assump2} is in force. Let $(\Omega,\cF,\hQ^0)$ be a probability space on which is defined a $d+1$-dimensional Brownian motion $(B^1,Y)$ and a continuous $\hF$-adapted $\sM_1(\hR^d)$ valued process $(\n_t)_{t\in[0,T]}$ satisfying SPDE \eqref{Zakai: state}. 

Then, the $\sP_1(\sM_1(\hR^d))$-valued process $\{\bP^Y_t\}_{t\in[0,T]}$ defined by (\ref{bPyt}) satisfies the following conditional Fokker-Planck equation: 
\bea

\int_{\sM(\hR^d)}F (\bn)(\bP^Y_t-\bP^Y_0)(d\bn)
&=&\int_0^t\int_{\sM(\hR^d)} \cL_s^{Y, \bm} F(\bn) \bP^Y_s(d\bn) ds \\
&&+\int_0^t\int_{\sM(\hR^d)}\bd_{\bn}F(\bn,x)\cdot \cH(t, x , Y_{\cdot\wedge s},{\bm}) \bP^Y_s(d\bn) dY_s, \qq \hQ^0\textit{-a.s.}\nonumber
\eea

where the operator $\cL^{Y, \bm}_t$ is defined as  in \eqref{FP operator}, and $F$ is a $k$-cylindrical test function. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2608.17449, 'Spectral Simplicity and Joint Eigenvalue Densities\\ for a Non-Gaussian Brownian Time Chan'] For $f\in\mathcal T$, let $\Mult_fu:=fu$.  We have
\begin{equation}
 \Mult_f(V_\mu)\subset V_\mu,
 \qquad
 \|\Mult_fu\|_{\E,\mu}
 \le C_f\|u\|_{\E,\mu},
 \qquad u\in V_\mu.
 
\end{equation}
For $f_1,\ldots,f_N\in\mathcal T$ and $z\in\C^N$, set
\[
 m_z(x):=\exp\!\left(-\frac{\gamma}{2}\sum_{j=1}^Nz_jf_j(x)\right),
 \qquad
 \Mult_{m_z}u:=m_zu.
\]
We have
\[
 \Mult_{m_z}\in\mathcal B(V_\mu^\C),
 \qquad
 \Mult_{m_z}^{-1}=\Mult_{m_{-z}}.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \C^N\ni z\longmapsto\Mult_{m_z}\in\mathcal B(V_\mu^\C)
\]
is holomorphic.

Let U_t be the source time-t departure odometer, H_t unfilled-hole indicators, m_t=E U_t(0), and K a finite nonempty set. metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:c64667de6eb6a75f773ad2bfad23ff918b0607bbec7806df5de5579d3eada5b5","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/c6/c64667de6eb6a75f773ad2bfad23ff918b0607bbec7806df5de5579d3eada5b5.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:015b5984a291f0f0923186c014a792d753f4d15ab12cd6bd72303a5a34761dbd","bundle_entry_key":"i0005-c13","bundle_id":"population.i0005-sink-capacity-and-gradient-obstruction-005","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"parking and killed random walks","draft":"w661/bundle_005.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.particle-hole:particle-hole-finite-sink-capacity-flux-and-void-identity-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# I0005-C13 v1: finite-sink void identity and capacity flux bound

Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty: KNOWN singleton result, Bou-Rabee--
Panagiotis arXiv:2609.02820v1 (50)-(51); UNCHECKED prior appearance of
this finite-set extension. This is an actual parking-process statement.

Consider the source's synchronous nearest-neighbor particle-hole process
on Z^d, d>=3, with iid P(eta=1)=P(eta=-1)=p, P(eta=0)=1-2p,
0<p<1/2. Holes have capacity one and never move. Let H_t(x) indicate an
unfilled hole, U_t(x) count departures through the source's time-t
odometer convention, and m_t=E U_t(0). Let K be any nonempty finite set.

Define a sink process by setting eta(x)=0 on K and making K permanent
absorbing sinks: any arrival there is removed; no particle departs there.
Off K use the original iid law, fresh walks/instruction stacks and the
same coupling conventions as the source. Let U_t^K be its odometer,
J_t^K the number of arrivals killed on K in the rounds corresponding to
U_t^K, and

    Lambda_t^K=(1/(2d)) sum_{s in K} sum_{y adjacent s} U_t^K(y).

Terms with y in K vanish. Let cap(K)=sum_{s in K}P_s(T_K^+=infinity),
the full-space discrete-time SRW escape-probability capacity. Then

    P(H_t(s)=1 for all s in K)=p^|K| P(J_t^K=0),
    m_t cap(K) <= E Lambda_t^K = E J_t^K <= m_t |K|.

The expectation identity and sandwich do not provide a bound on the
zero-arrival probability. In particular they do not establish C9's Palm
clustering hypothesis.

## 1. Exact void identity

All sites in K must initially be holes for the joint-hole event. This
has probability p^|K| and is independent of the signs off K and the
walk instructions. Conditional on those initial holes, the original and
sink evolutions agree until the first arrival to K, because neither
system has an initial particle or a departure there. At that first
arrival an original hole is filled, so the joint-hole event has already
failed. Hence the joint survival event is precisely the no-arrival event
in the sink process, proving the formula. No independence between the
arrivals or between individual hole-survival events is asserted.

## 2. Monotone sink comparison and the expected odometer

Through a fixed finite time t, represent each permanent sink by sufficiently
many initial holes that its capacity cannot be exhausted by that time.
There are finitely many potentially relevant initial particles in the
t-neighborhood of K and at most one at each initial site; a deterministic
capacity greater than that finite number suffices. This modified initial
configuration is coordinatewise below the original one. The source's
Lemma 2.3 comparison gives, off K,

    U_t^K<=U_t,   A_t^K<=A_t,   H_t^K>=H_t

in its coupled construction. Therefore f(y):=E U_t^K(y) is bounded by
m_t, is zero on K, and equals m_t whenever dist(y,K)>t. The last assertion
uses finite propagation: initial changes on K cannot affect such a site
before the time horizon. Expectations are finite by the source's finite-time
odometer estimates.

At y outside K, mean particle-hole conservation, or the source's (19)
with mean-zero instruction noise, yields

    (P-I)f(y)=E[A_t^K(y)-H_t^K(y)]-E eta(y)<=0.

Here P is one SRW step, E eta(y)=0 off K, and the inequality uses the
monotone comparison and E A_t(y)=E H_t(y) in the original critical law.
Thus f is superharmonic outside K.

## 3. Escape lower bound and boundary flux

Stop a free walk from y outside K when it hits K or leaves a large finite
ball containing the t-neighborhood of K and y. Superharmonicity makes
f of the stopped walk a supermartingale; optional stopping is justified
by boundedness and the almost-sure finite exit time. On K its value is
zero, while on the outer boundary it is m_t. Consequently

    f(y)>=m_t P_y(exit before hitting K)
         >=m_t P_y(T_K=infinity).

Together with f<=m_t this gives

    E Lambda_t^K >= (m_t/(2d)) sum_{s in K}
                              sum_{y adjacent s}P_y(T_K=infinity)
                  =m_t sum_{s in K}P_s(T_K^+=infinity)
                  =m_t cap(K).

For neighbors inside K the escape probability is zero, so including them
in the sum causes no error. The upper bound follows from f<=m_t and
at most 2d neighbor terms per s: E Lambda_t^K<=m_t |K|.

## 4. Compensator identity

Reveal departure instructions chronologically, revealing each only after
the preceding history determines that it is used, exactly as in the
source's Lemma 4.3 and proof of (50)-(51). Every departure from y has
conditional probability deg_K(y)/(2d) of entering K. Its killed-arrival
indicator minus that probability is a martingale difference. Only finitely
many departures can reach K through time t; finite propagation and the
bounded initial number of particles provide a deterministic finite bound
on the number of such instructions. Summing expectations gives

    E J_t^K = (1/(2d))sum_y deg_K(y) E U_t^K(y)
            = E Lambda_t^K.

## Missing estimate

The singleton case is the source's (50)-(51). For two sites the full-space
capacity is 2/(g+G(x-y)), but the identity here involves a stopping-dependent
sink process, not an independent Poisson cloud. A capacity-sized expected
arrival count does not determine P(J_t^K=0). A lower-tail/no-arrival
comparison uniform in t and separation would be needed to turn this
extension into a two-hole survival bound. The d4 logarithmic influence
convolution remains an obstacle to such a concentration estimate.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:fb8fccc578ac5b2adf0f53a9de6f6cd4ac7f55cbcca4e34b8b2f482f45071155","revision_digest":"sha256:6096b4022996cb8ce77c7b68df1a708123697db85dc0015eb22f41b41b1f5be8","source_id":"own-work:w661:I0005-C13:v1","source_revision":"v1; 2026-10-14T06:02:25.9473414+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}
