[Thm matsutomo_yor of arXiv:2412.06701, 'Matsumoto-Yor processes on Jordan algebras'] The process $Z=(Z_t \ ; \ t\ge 0)$ defined by
$$Z_t := \exp( b_t^{(\nu)} )\int_{0}^{t} \exp\left( -2 b_s^{(\nu)} \right) ds \ , \ t\ge 0,$$
is a Markov process, whose natural filtration is strictly contained in that of $b$, i.e. for all $t > 0$, ${\mathcal F}_t^Z \varsubsetneq {\mathcal F}_t^b$.

Furthermore, we have the conditional distribution
$$
   {\mathbb P}\left( \exp\left( b^{(\nu)} \right) \in dx \ | \ {\mathcal F}_t^Z, \ Z_t = z \right) 
   = \mathrm{GIG}_{{\mathbb R}_+^*}\left( \nu ; \frac1z , \frac1z \right)(dx) \ .
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm.2 of arXiv:2605.17725, 'Limit theorems for random walks with spatio-temporal drift'] Suppose that Assumption (assump of the paper) and Assumption (assump2 of the paper) are fulfilled. 
Then $n^{-A} P_u S_n$ converges to an almost‑sure limit ${W}_u$.  Furthermore, we have
$$
\begin{pmatrix}
\displaystyle \frac{P_sS_n}{\sqrt n} \\[2mm]
\displaystyle D_n^{-1}n^{-A_c}P_cS_n \\[2mm]
\displaystyle \frac{P_uS_n-n^{A_u}W_u}{\sqrt n}
\end{pmatrix}
\xrightarrow[n\to\infty]{d}
\mathcal N\left(
0,
\begin{pmatrix}
\Xi_s & 0 & 0 \\
0 & \Xi_c & 0 \\
0 & 0 & \Xi_u
\end{pmatrix}
\right),
$$
where the block‑diagonal covariance matrices are determined as follows.

\begin{itemize}
    \item $\Xi_s$ is the unique solution to the Lyapunov equation
    $$
    \bigl(\tfrac{1}{2}I - A_s\bigr) \Xi_s + \Xi_s \bigl(\tfrac{1}{2}I - A_s\bigr)^\top = P_s \Sigma P_s^\top,
    $$
    where $A_s$ is the restriction of $A$ to $E_s$.

    \item  $\Xi_c$ is given by
    $$
    \Xi_c = Q \,\mathcal{V}\, Q^*,
    $$
where $\mathcal{V}$ is the block matrix  
$\mathcal{V}=(\mathcal{V}(r,s))_{1\le r,s\le R}$, such that its $(r,s)$ block is given by
\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{V}(r,s)&=(\mathcal{V}_{i,j}(r,s))_{1\le i\le m_r, 1\le j\le m_s},\\
    \mathcal V_{i,j}(r,s)
&=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle
\frac{(-1)^{m_r+m_s-i-j}}
{(m_r-i)!\,(m_s-j)!\,(m_r+m_s-i-j+1)}
\widetilde{\Sigma}_{m_r,m_s}(r,s),
& \lambda_r=\lambda_s,\\[3mm]
0,
& \lambda_r\ne\lambda_s.
\end{cases}
\end{align*}
with $\widetilde{\Sigma}(r,s)$ being the $(r,s)$ block of size $m_r \times m_s$ of  $\widetilde{\Sigma}=Q^{-1} P_c \Sigma P_c^\top  (Q^{-1})^*$.

    \item $\Xi_u$ is the unique solution to the Lyapunov equation
    $$
    \bigl(A_u - \tfrac{1}{2}I\bigr) \Xi_u + \Xi_u \bigl(A_u - \tfrac{1}{2}I\bigr)^\top = P_u \Sigma P_u^\top,
    $$
    where $A_u$ is the restriction of $A$ to $E_u$.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Joint Central Limit Theorem for Mixed Regimes

For any non-negative measurable functions $f, g: \R^n \to \R_+$ and any non-increasing measurable function $\Omega: (0, \infty) \to (0, \infty)$ satisfying the pointwise bound:
    $$f(x)g(y) \leq \Omega^2([x,y]) \quad \text{for all } x, y \in \R^n \text{ with } [x,y] > 0,$$

[Lem 25 of arXiv:2608.05185, '\large\bf ON THE HEAT FLOW CONJECTURE FOR RANDOM MATRICES'] Let \(N\geq1\), let \(\mathbf{A}\) be a fixed \(N\times N\) complex
matrix, and regard \(z\) and the entries \(Z_{ij}\) of \(\mathbf{Z}\) as
algebraically independent variables.  For
\[
 P(z,\mathbf{Z})
 =\det\!\left(z\mathbf{I}_N-\mathbf{A}-\mathbf{Z}\right),
\]
one has the following identity in the polynomial ring
\(\C[z,(Z_{ij})_{1\leq i,j\leq N}]\):
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{i,j=1}^{N}
 \frac{\partial^2P}{\partial Z_{ij}\partial Z_{ji}}
 =-\partial_z^2P.
\end{equation}
All derivatives are formal polynomial derivatives.

[Lemma 5 (\cite{VER2020}) of arXiv:2607.21392, 'Gaussian Convexity Principles for Sharp Moderate Deviations of Gaussian Maxima and Critica'] For every $u\ge 0$,
\[
\mathbb P\bigl(|\max_{1\le i\le N}X_i-m_N|\ge u\bigr)\le 2e^{-u^2/2}.
\]
Consequently,
\begin{equation}
    | \E \max_{1\le i\le N} X_i-m_N|
\le \E|\max_{1\le i\le N}X_i-m_N|
\le \int_0^\infty 2e^{-u^2/2}\,du
=\sqrt{2\pi}=C_{\mathrm{med}}.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition 28 of arXiv:2604.01978, 'Homogenized Transformers'] Let $B\in C^{1}((\S^{d-1})^{n};\mathsf{T}(\S^{d-1})^{n})$ and
$G:(\S^{d-1})^n\times\Uptheta\to \mathsf{T}(\S^{d-1})^n$ be such that for ${\uprho_*}$-a.e.\ $\theta$,
the map $X\mapsto G(X,\theta)$ is $C^2$.
A continuous $(\S^{d-1})^{n}$-valued adapted process $(X(t))_{t\ge 0}$ with $X(0)=x$ is called a solution to the Itô SDE 
    \begin{equation} 
        \de X(t)=B(X(t))\de t+\int_{\Uptheta}G(X(t),\bm{\theta})\mathsf{W}(\de \bm{\theta},\de t),
    \end{equation}
if for all $g\in C^{\infty}((\S^{d-1})^{n})$, we have
\begin{align*}
g(X(t))
= g(x)
&+ \int_{0}^{t} (Bg)(X(s))\,\de s \\
&+ \frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{t}\int_{\Uptheta} \Hess g(X(s))[G(X(s),\theta), G(X(s),\theta)]\,{\uprho_*}(\de \theta)\,\de s \\
&+ \int_{0}^{t}\int_{\Uptheta} (G(\cdot,\theta)g)(X(s))\,\mathsf{W}(\de \theta,\de s),
\end{align*}
where $Bg=\langle \grad g,B\rangle$, $G(\cdot,\theta)g=\langle \grad g, G(\cdot,\theta)\rangle$.
title: Definition 28 of arXiv:2604.01978

[Theorem thm:fik-completeness of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] \begin{equation*}
    \textbf{FIK} = \set{ \varphi \in \mathscr{L}_{\Box\Diamond}; \forall \mathfrak{F} \in \FrameClass{\Diamond\text{-p}}\,(\mathfrak{F} \vDash^{\text{h}} \varphi) }.
  \end{equation*}
  \begin{proof}
    ($\subseteq$) By Corollary (cor:wk-completeness of the paper) and Proposition (prop:int-ik-coincides of the paper), it suffices to show that $\textsf{C}_\Diamond$ and $\textsf{wCD}$ are h-valid on any $\Diamond$-p frame.
    For $\textsf{C}_\Diamond$, it is proven similarly to Proposition (prop:separation-cdia of the paper) (1).
    For $\textsf{wCD}$, take any $\Diamond$-p model $\mathfrak{M} = (W, \leq, \sqsubset, V)$ and any $x_0, x_1, x_2 \in W$
    such that
    $x_0 \leq x_1 \leq x_2$,
    $x_1 \Vdash^{\text{h}} \Box(\varphi \lor \psi)$, and
    $x_2 \Vdash^{\text{h}} \Diamond \varphi \to \Box \psi$,
    then it suffices to show that $x_2 \Vdash^{\text{h}} \Box \psi$.
    Take any $x_3, y_3 \in W$ such that $x_2 \leq x_3 \sqsubset y_3$,
    then $x_1 \Vdash^{\text{h}} \Box(\varphi \lor \psi)$ implies $x_2 \Vdash^{\text{h}} \Box(\varphi \lor \psi)$ by persistency,
    then $y_3 \Vdash^{\text{h}} \varphi \lor \psi$, so either $y_3 \Vdash^{\text{h}} \varphi$ or $y_3 \Vdash^{\text{h}} \psi$.
    Here, the former implies the latter; if $y_3 \Vdash^{\text{h}} \varphi$,
    then $x_3 \sqsubset y_3 \Vdash^{\text{h}} \varphi$ implies $x_3 \Vdash^{\text{h}} \Diamond \varphi$.
    then we have $x_3 \Vdash^{\text{h}} \Box \psi$ by $x_2 \leq x_3 \Vdash^{\text{h}} \Diamond \varphi \to \Box \psi$ (persistency),
    so we have $y_3 \Vdash^{\text{h}} \psi$.
    Therefore, $x_2 \Vdash^{\text{h}} \Box \psi$ holds.

    ($\supseteq$) Follows from Proposition (prop:canonical-model-is-dia-p of the paper) and Truth lemma.
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: {Completeness of $\Logic{FIK}$, \cite{balbiani_natural_2024}}

body: [Thm Feldman-Moore of arXiv:2608.06644, 'Applications of the cluster graphing'] Let $\mathcal{R}$ be a countable Borel equivalence relation on a standard Borel space $(X, \mu)$. Then there is a Borel action $\alpha: \Gamma \curvearrowright X$ of a countable discrete group $\Gamma$ such that $\mathcal{R} = \mathcal{R}_\Gamma$, where $(x, y) \in \mathcal{R}_\Gamma$ if and only if $x,y$ lie in the same $\Gamma$-orbit. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let $p \in (1, \infty)$, and let $(y^n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence in a metric space $(\mathcal{Y}, d_\mathcal{Y})$. The sequence has finite weighted $p$-variation if there exists a sequence of positive weights $(b_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ such that $\sum_{n=1}^\infty b_n = 1$ and $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{b_n^{p-1}} d_\mathcal{Y}^p(y^n, y^{n+1}) < \infty$.
p \in (1, \infty)
\sum b_n = 1
title: Sequence with Finite Weighted p-Variation

body: [Proposition 1 of arXiv:2511.05218, 'On the Color Discrepancy of Spanning Trees in Random and Randomly Perturbed Graphs'] For every $\delta>0$, there exists a constant $C=C(\delta)>0$ such that, if $p=\frac{C}{n}$, then with high probability the giant component of $G\sim G(n,p)$ contains a spanning tree $T$ with $|L_{1}(T)|\geq\big(\frac{1}{3}-\delta\big)n.$

body:
Let (X, mu) be a measure space and 0 < p < infinity. Let (f_n) be a sequence in L^p(mu) that is bounded in L^p norm and converges mu-almost everywhere to a function f. Then f is in L^p and lim_n ( ||f_n||_p^p - ||f_n - f||_p^p ) = ||f||_p^p. Equivalently the L^p norm splits asymptotically into the norm of the limit plus the norm of the vanishing part - a refinement of Fatou's lemma, which alone gives only ||f||_p <= liminf ||f_n||_p.
Uniform L^p boundedness AND almost-everywhere convergence.
Without the norm bound the conclusion fails;
no convergence in norm is assumed or concluded.

body: [Proposition 12 of arXiv:2608.13358, 'Extreme points of sets of probability measures and $\phi$-divergences'] Let $(\Omega_i,\cF_i,p_i)_{i=1,\ldots, n}$ be a family of probability spaces,  $\cM:=\Pi(p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ be the set of multi-marginal couplings of $p_1,\ldots,p_n$, and $p\in\cM$ be concentrated on a marginal uniqueness set $S\in\cF$.\ Then $p$ is $\ll$-minimal in $\cM$.\ In particular, $p$ is an extreme point of $\cM$, and the blow-up \eqref{eq:blowup} of Theorem~\ref{thm:minimal:divergence} holds for every $p'\in\cM\setminus\{p\}$, every $q\in\cM$ with $p,p'\ll q$, and every convex function $\varphi$ satisfying \eqref{eq:phi:blowup}.

[Lemma 19 (Controlling the remainder) of arXiv:2604.12797, 'A free boundary problem for the mean-field limit of diffusing particles with nonlinear bou'] The remainder $r_t^\varepsilon(x)$ defined in \eqref{eq:remainder} satisfies that, for every $\theta \in (0, \tfrac{1}{2})$, there exists $\delta \in (1-\theta,1)$ and $C=C(\theta) > 0$ such that
\[
\E\big[\|r^\varepsilon_t\|_{2}^2\big]
	\leq C \varepsilon^{\frac{1}{2} - \theta} t^{-\delta},
\]
for all $t \in (0,T]$, for $\varepsilon > 0$ sufficiently small.

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] The ``normal'' law $g_t$, having as Fourier transform 
$$F(x)=e^{-tx^2/2}$$
must have all odd moments zero, and its even moments must be the numbers
$$M_k(g_t)=t^{k/2}\times k!!$$
where $k!!=(k-1)(k-3)(k-5)\ldots\,$, as usual.

Then the gradient of \(u\) exists in a classical sense and satisfies
\[
\nabla_x u\in C^{\beta/2,\beta}_{\mathrm{loc}}(Q).
\]

        \nabla_x(X,C_k)

body:
[Lemma 11 of arXiv:2609.03556, 'An Effective SPDE Model for a Schr\"odinger Equation with a Fluctuating Magnetic Potential'] For each $n\in\mathbb N$ the following holds $\mathbb{P}-a.s.$: for every
$\phi\in \mathscr{S}(\R^d)$ and $t\in [0,T]$
\begin{align*}
    i\langle \hat{\psi}^{\tau_n}_t, \phi\rangle
    &+\frac{\tau_n}{2}\langle \hat{\psi}^{\tau_n}_t,|A^n_t|^2\phi\rangle
    -2i\tau_n\langle \hat{\psi}^{\tau_n}_t,A^n_t\cdot\nabla\phi\rangle\\
    &=i\langle \psi_0,\phi\rangle
    +\frac{\tau_n}{2}\langle \psi_0,|A^n_0|^2\phi\rangle
    -2i\tau_n\langle \psi_0,A^n_0\cdot\nabla\phi\rangle\\
    &\quad+\int_0^t\langle\hat{\psi}^{\tau_n}_s,(-\Delta+V)\phi\rangle ds+\frac{i\tau_n}{2}\int_0^t
    \langle\hat{\psi}^{\tau_n}_s,\Delta(|A^n_s|^2\phi)\rangle ds\\
    &\quad+2\tau_n\int_0^t
    \langle\hat{\psi}^{\tau_n}_s,\Delta(A^n_s\cdot\nabla\phi)\rangle ds-\tau_n\int_0^t
    \langle\hat{\psi}^{\tau_n}_s,A^n_s\cdot\nabla(|A^n_s|^2\phi)\rangle ds\\
    &\quad-\frac{i\tau_n}{2}\int_0^t
    \langle\hat{\psi}^{\tau_n}_s,|A^n_s|^4\phi\rangle ds+4i\tau_n\int_0^t
    \langle\hat{\psi}^{\tau_n}_s,A^n_s\cdot\nabla(A^n_s\cdot\nabla\phi)\rangle ds\\
    &\quad-2\tau_n\int_0^t
    \langle\hat{\psi}^{\tau_n}_s,|A^n_s|^2A^n_s\cdot\nabla\phi\rangle ds+\sqrt{2\tau_n}\sum_{k\in I}\int_0^t
    \langle\hat{\psi}^{\tau_n}_s,A^n_s\cdot\sigma_k\phi\rangle dW^{k,n}_s\\
    &\quad-i\sqrt{8\tau_n}\sum_{k\in I}\int_0^t
    \langle\hat{\psi}^{\tau_n}_s,\sigma_k\cdot\nabla\phi\rangle dW^{k,n}_s.
\end{align*}

The workload diffusion has drift -beta and variance rate m2/m. If uniform-on-compacts state-space collapse Q/r-W/(rh) were established, its queue-length image would have drift -beta/h and variance rate m2/(m*h^2). For beta>0 the stationary exponential rate of this candidate is 2*(beta/h)/(m2/(m*h^2))=beta, exactly the rate obtained from P(Q>=k)=rho_r^k. This fixes the constants and reduces a proof to a precise collapse estimate. Check: For exponential service of rate mu, h=1/mu and the proposed variance rate is 2*mu, matching the birth-death generator directly. The stationary calculation is a consistency test, not an interchange-of-limits proof. Obstruction: Uniform state-space collapse for arbitrary gamma remains unproved. Equality of fixed-time marginals does not establish process convergence or tightness.

[Lemma 14 of arXiv:2609.00483, 'On Embedding Hamming Spheres with Applications to Positive Curvature'] \cite{AS} Let $M^n$ be a closed,  positively curved Riemannian $n$-manifold, $n\geq 5$. Suppose that $N_1^{n-k_1}$ and $N_2^{n-k_2}$ are two closed, totally geodesic submanifolds of $M$ with $ k_1\leq k_2$, $4k_1\leq n+3$, and $k_1+2k_2\leq n+1$. Then 
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\widetilde{N_2}$ is a cohomology sphere and $N_2$ has cyclic fundamental group, then  
 $M$ is homotopy equivalent to $S^n$, $\RP^n$, or a lens space; and
 \item If  $\widetilde{N_2}$ is cohomology complex projective space,  $2|k_1$ and $\pi_1(N_2)$ is trivial, then $M$ is homotopy equivalent to $\CP^{n/2}$.
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lem paley-zygmund of arXiv:2607.05097, 'Asymptotics of Lyapunov Exponents and Phase Transitions for Fluids with Degenerate Forcing'] Given $K \in \mathbb{N}_0$ and a sequence of elements $g_k \in \mathcal{H}^{\otimes_s k}$, let
    $X = \sum_{k=0}^K \tilde I_k(g_k)$.
Then, whenever $\|g_K\| \geq \delta$, one has
    $$\mathbb{P}\Big(|X| > \Big[\frac{K!}{2}\Big]^{1/2}\delta\Big) \geq \frac{3^{-2K}}{4} \,.$$

\noindent (i) Let $\delta>0$ and set $D_\delta=\{x\in\ER^d, d(x,D)\le \delta\}$. For every $t_0>0$, we have
$$\sup_{x\in D} \PE_x(\tau_{D_\delta}(\xi)>t_0)<1.$$

\noindent (ii)  There exist some compact sets $K$ and $\widetilde{K}$ of $D$ such that $K\subset \widetilde{K}$ and such that there exist some positive $t_0$, $t_1$, such that for all $h>0$,

$$\forall x\in D,\; \PE_x\left({\xi}_{t_0}\in K,  \tau(\xi^h)>t_0\right)>0$$ and
$$\inf_{x\in K}\PE_x( \xi_{t_1}\in K\,\textnormal{and}\,\forall t\in[0,t_1], {\xi}_{t}\in \widetilde{K}) >0.$$

body:
ONE VARIABLE. Let $a, b: (t_0, t_1) \to \mathbb{R}$ be $C^1$ and let $F(x, t)$ and $\partial_t F(x, t)$ be continuous on an open set of $\mathbb{R}^2$ containing $\{(x,t) : t \in (t_0,t_1),\ x \text{ between } a(t) \text{ and } b(t)\}$. Then for $t \in (t_0, t_1)$
$$\frac{d}{dt} \int_{a(t)}^{b(t)} F(x,t)\,dx = \int_{a(t)}^{b(t)} \partial_t F(x,t)\,dx + F(b(t),t)\, b'(t) - F(a(t),t)\, a'(t).$$

SEVERAL VARIABLES. Let $v(x,t)$ be a $C^1$ velocity field on an open set $U \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, $t \in (t_0, t_1)$, with flow $\varphi_t$ (so $\partial_t \varphi_t(y) = v(\varphi_t(y), t)$, $\varphi_{0} = \mathrm{id}$), and let $\Omega(t) = \varphi_t(\Omega_0)$ where $\Omega_0$ is a bounded open set with Lipschitz (e.g. piecewise $C^1$) boundary whose closure stays in $U$. Let $F(x,t)$ be $C^1$ on $U \times (t_0, t_1)$. Then
$$\frac{d}{dt} \int_{\Omega(t)} F\,dx = \int_{\Omega(t)} \partial_t F\,dx + \int_{\partial \Omega(t)} F\,(v \cdot \nu)\,dS = \int_{\Omega(t)} \big(\partial_t F + \nabla\cdot(F v)\big)\,dx,$$
where $\nu$ is the outward unit normal and $v \cdot \nu$ is the outward normal velocity of the boundary. Only the NORMAL component of the boundary velocity enters: two motions of the domain whose boundaries sweep the same sets (differing by a tangential reparametrisation) give the same derivative, so the formula can be stated with any $C^1$ boundary velocity having the correct normal component. The one-variable formula is the case $n = 1$, $\nu = \pm 1$ at $b$ and $a$.

WHERE IT FAILS OR NEEDS CARE. (1) $F$ must be continuous up to the moving boundary from inside; if $F$ jumps across $\partial\Omega(t)$ the boundary integrand is the one-sided limit from inside $\Omega(t)$. (2) $\partial_t F$ must be integrable over $\Omega(t)$ (continuity on a compact closure suffices); without domination, differentiation under the integral sign can fail. (3) The bounded-domain / Lipschitz-boundary hypothesis is what licenses the divergence theorem in the second equality; the first equality (Lagrangian form) needs only the change of variables. (4) If the domain is not transported by a $C^1$ flow but its boundary merely moves with a prescribed normal speed $w$, the same formula holds with $v \cdot \nu$ replaced by $w$, but the proof must build a flow with that normal speed.
F and its time derivative are continuous (F is C^1) on a neighbourhood of the closures of the moving domains
the domain is transported by a C^1 velocity field (one variable: the endpoints are C^1 functions of t)
the domain is bounded with Lipschitz boundary so that the divergence theorem applies
only the outward normal component of the boundary velocity enters the boundary term

For the deterministic predecessor chain, h_n=n-1 and the cut A={floor(n/2)+1,...,n} has total outflow1, forcing kappa>=floor(n/2)*ceil(n/2)/n, of order n. Let G be a finite undirected loopless multigraph on n vertices with positive edge weights w_e, L its weighted Laplacian, and t > 0. A spanning rooted forest is a spanning forest with one chosen root in each tree; its weight is t^|E(F)| prod_{e in F} w_e (so an unrooted forest with trees T_1, ..., T_k counts prod |T_i| times). Z(t) is the total weight of spanning rooted forests, and Q_t = (I + tL)^-1. body:
For a finite undirected graph with labeled terminal vertices and a random open-edge configuration, its terminal partition puts two terminals in the same block exactly when an open path joins them inside the graph. The boundary-partition law is the probability distribution on these terminal partitions. When the graph attaches to an exterior only through those terminals, ordinary open-path connectivity in the union is determined by this partition and the exterior connectivity.
The gadget meets the exterior only at the named terminal vertices.
Connectivity uses open paths.

Let A,Phi be real symmetric n-by-n matrices with Phi positive semidefinite. Fix z with Im(z)>0,nonzero alpha with Im(alpha)<=0,and gamma>0. For s in the open upper half-plane let S(s)=(A+s^(-1)*Phi-zI)^(-1),f_n(s)=alpha^(-1)+gamma*tr(S(s)Phi),and tr=Tr/n. Then Im f_n(s)>=gamma*Im(z)*tr(S Phi S*)>=0. More precisely,Im f_n(s)=Im(alpha^(-1))+gamma*Im(s)/|s|^2*tr(S Phi S* Phi)+gamma*Im(z)*tr(S Phi S*). For s1,s2 in the upper half-plane,write S_j=S(s_j) and d_j=(Im f_n(s_j)-gamma*Im(z)*tr(S_j Phi S_j*))/Im(s_j)>=0. Then |f_n(s1)-f_n(s2)|<=|s1-s2|*sqrt(d_1*d_2). These are normalized-trace identities and inequalities for finite matrices;no simultaneous diagonalization of A and Phi is assumed. Draft,independent review pending.

body: [Theorem completudemovimento of arXiv:2609.03909, 'Conic Pseudo-Finslerian Mechanical Systems'] Let $L \colon \mathcal{U} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a conic Finslerian metric, where $\mathcal{U}$ is a conic convex open set. Let $(M,\tfrac12 L,-\nabla^v \phi)$ be a conservative conic Finslerian mechanical system and let $\gamma$ be an $\mathcal{M}$-motion. Then $\gamma$ is defined for all $t > 0$.

body: The continuous (topological) dual X* of a normed space X is the space of bounded linear functionals f : X -> scalars, itself a Banach space under the operator norm ||f|| = sup_{||x||<=1} |f(x)|. The Hahn-Banach theorem guarantees X* is rich (functionals extend and separate points); the natural map X -> X** is an isometric embedding, and X is reflexive when it is onto.
title: Dual Space

[Proposition 13 (\cref{sec:end-analysis}) of arXiv:2608.31008, 'Stability of gravitational instantons with a bounded Killing vector field'] Let $(M^4,g)$ be a complete Ricci-flat ALF manifold satisfying
\eqref{eq:intro-end}, and let $K$ be a nonzero bounded Killing field.
After multiplying $K$ by a nonzero constant, for every
$0<\varepsilon<\frac12$ one has, on the end,
\[
 |\nabla_b^j(K-T)|_b+|\nabla_b^j(V-1)|_b
   =\mathcal O(r^{-1-j}),\qquad \text{ and }\qquad
 |\nabla_b^jF|_b=\mathcal O(r^{-2-j}),\qquad \text{for }j\geqslant0.
\]
There are global functions $u$ and $\chi$ respectively satisfying 
 $\Delta u=V+2$ and $d\chi=\iota_K(*F)$ and for every $j\geqslant0$,
\[
 |\nabla_b^j(u+r^2/2)|_b=\mathcal O(r^{1+\varepsilon-j}),
 \qquad
 |\nabla_b^j\chi|_b=\mathcal O(r^{-1+\varepsilon-j}).
\]
The symmetric $2$-tensor
 $k_K=\nabla^2u-\kappa\otimes\kappa+\frac{V+1}{2}g$ satisfies
 $$|\nabla^jk_K|=\mathcal O(r^{-1+\varepsilon-j})\qquad \text{ for }0\leqslant j\leqslant2.$$ In particular, all of the integrals used below converge: for $M_R=\{r<R\}$, we have as $R\to+\infty$
\begin{equation}
\begin{split}
 &\int_{\partial M_R}|k_K|\,|\nabla k_K|\,dA\longrightarrow0,\\
 &\int_{\partial M_R}
   |(F^+\circ F^-)(\nabla u,\nu)|\,dA\longrightarrow0,\\
 &\int_{\partial M_R}|1-V\pm\chi|\,
   |\partial_\nu(V\pm\chi)|\,dA\longrightarrow0.
\end{split}
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm 1 of arXiv:2605.07369, '2605.07369'] {\bf (Exponential inequality)}
Let $(X_n)_{n\ge 0}$ be a stochastic process taking values in $\rr$ and satisfying the stochastic approximation algorithm  (\ref{sa-0}). Assume that the conditions (\ref{sa-2}) and (\ref{g}) hold.
Then, for any $\varepsilon>0$, there exist a constant $\delta\in (0,1)$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, we have
$$
\pp\left(\left|X_{n+1}-x^*\right|\ge \varepsilon\right)\le 2 \exp\left(- \frac{C \varepsilon^2\delta n}{1-\delta}\right)\left(1+\frac{1}{1-\exp\left(- \frac{C \varepsilon^2  }{1-\delta}\right)}\right).
$$
Here $\delta$ can be chosen to satisfy
$$
0<\delta<\exp\left(-\frac{2(F+\varepsilon)}{b K_1 \varepsilon}\right),
$$
where $F=F\left(b, K_1, K_u\right)$ is a positive constant. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem thm:main-critical-level-percolation of arXiv:2609.02829, 'Quantitative explosion and percolation of the divisible sandpile'] Let $d\geq2$ and let $\nu_{0}>0$, $\theta_{0}>0$, and $K_{0}<\infty$. There are $c=c(d,\nu_{0},\theta_{0},K_{0})>0$ and $t_0=t_0(d,\nu_{0},\theta_{0},K_{0})<\infty$ such that the following holds. Suppose $(\sigma(x))_{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d}$ is an i.i.d.\ field with mean $\mathbb{E}\sigma(0)=1$, $\Var(\sigma(0))\geq\nu_{0}^2$, and $\mathbb{E} e^{\theta_{0}|\sigma(0)-1|}\leq K_{0}$. Then, for every integer $t\geq t_0$, the level set
\[
    \{x\in\mathbb{Z}^d:u_t(x)>c \, h(t)\}\, ,
    \qquad\text{where}\quad
    h(t)=
    \begin{cases}
    t^{(4-d)/4} & \text{if } d\in\{2,3\}\, ,\\
    \log t & \text{if } d=4\, ,\\
    (\log t)^{2/d} & \text{if } d\geq5\, ,
    \end{cases}
\]
contains an infinite nearest-neighbor component almost surely.

[Cor 23 (uniqueness via stochastic analysis) of arXiv:2605.25715, '2605.25715'] Let $A \in M_{d}(\mathbb{R})$ be symmetric and positive definite. Assume that $G \in M_d(\mathbb{R})$ is a Hurwitz matrix. Then, there exists a unique $d \times d$ symmetric matrix
solution $S$ to \eqref{SOHHDlinalg1}.
More precisely, the solution $S$ is real, symmetric and invertible, and has the following explicit form:
$$
S=\left(-\int_{0}^{\infty} e^{Gt}\,(2A)\,e^{G^T t}\,dt \right)^{-1}= (-P)^{-1},
$$
where $P$ is determined by the vectorized equation \eqref{vectorialmap}.
If $\tilde{S}$ is another symmetric matrix solution  to \eqref{SOHHDlinalg1}, then $S=\tilde{S}$.

\leqslant\mathcal{W}_q\big(\bm{X}^t_1,\bm{Z}_1\big)
\leqslant\mathcal{W}_q\big(\bm{X}^t,\bm{Z}\big)\leqslant
c_2\big(t^{1-q/\alpha}\1_{\{\alpha<1\}} + t^{q(1-1/\alpha)}\1_{\{\alpha>1\}}\big),
\end{equation*}
for some $c_1,c_2>0$ and all sufficiently small $t>0$.

\item[(b)] Assume $\mathcal{Q}(x,\bm{v})\!=\! c_\alpha H(x)^\alpha$ for $x>0$, $\bm{v}\in \mathbb{S}^{d-1}$ and some monotone $H\in\mbox{SV}_0\cap C^1$. Set $\varrho(x)\!\coloneqq \!\int_x^\infty H(y)^\alpha y^{-\alpha-1}\mathrm{d} y$ and let $\varrho^{\leftarrow}$ be its right-continuous inverse. Suppose $G(x)\coloneqq H(\varrho^{\leftarrow}(1/x))$ satisfies Assumption~(\nameref{asm:S}) for some function $G_2\in\mbox{SV}_0$. Then, for $g(t)\coloneqq t^{1/\alpha}G(t)$, $a(t)\coloneqq G(2t)/G(t)$ and $\bm{X}^t\coloneqq(\bm{X}_{st}/g(t))_{s\in[0,1]}$, we have
\[
\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}^t,\bm{Z})=\mathcal{O} ( G_2(t)^q),
\quad\text{as }t \downarrow 0,\quad\text{and}\quad
\max\big\{\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}^t_1,\bm{Z}_1)
,\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}^{2t}_1,\bm{Z}_1)\big\}
\geqslant |1-a(t)^q|\mathds{E}\big[|\bm{Z}_1|^q\big]/3,
\]
for sufficiently small $t >0$. The function $t\mapsto|1-a(t)^q|$ is not upper bounded by any non-decreasing function $\phi$ with $\int_0^1\phi(t)t^{-1}\mathrm{d} t<\infty$, $G$ is $C^1$ with $t\mapsto t|G'(t)|\in\mbox{SV}_0$ and there exists some $\phi\in\mbox{SV}_0\cap\mbox{SV}_\infty$ satisfying the inequality $\phi(x)\geqslant\sup_{t>0,y\in[x\wedge 1,x\vee1]}yG'(yt)/G'(t)$ for all $x>0$. Moreover, defining  $L(t)\coloneqq t|G'(t)|/G(t)$, there exist constants $c_1,c_2>0$ such that for all sufficiently small $t>0$, we have
\[
c_2L(t)
\leqslant\max\{\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}^t_1,\bm{Z}_1)
,\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}^{2t}_1,\bm{Z}_1)\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{X}^t,\bm{Z})
\leqslant c_1L(t)^q.
\]

\end{description}

The strong-log-concavity Poincare bound gives C_P(mu_y)<=t and 0<=Cov(mu_y)<=tI. These assertions also hold for nonsmooth convex potentials by log-concave approximation; they do not assert C_P(mu)<=t.

[Prop twoseed of arXiv:2606.24793, '\LARGE Random sequential nearest-neighbor coloring on trees'] Let $o'$ be a vertex of $\mathcal{T}$ such that $d(o,o')$ is odd. For $\ell > d(o,o')$, consider the coloring process on the finite tree $\mathcal{T}^{(\ell)}$ with two seeds located at $o$ and $o'$, and assume that all processes are constructed using the same sequence of arrival times. Then $
(\tilde{B}^{(\ell)},\tilde{R}^{(\ell)})_{\ell > d(o,o')}
$
converges almost surely in the local topology to some random sets
$
(\tilde{B}^{(\infty)},\tilde{R}^{(\infty)}).
$
Moreover:
\begin{itemize}
    \item[\textup{(a)}]
    $\tilde{B}^{(\infty)} \cap \{v \in \mathcal{T} : d(v,o)>d(v,o')\}$ is a.s. finite;
    
    \item[\textup{(b)}]
    $\tilde{R}^{(\infty)} \cap \{v \in \mathcal{T} : d(v,o)<d(v,o')\}$ is a.s. finite.
\end{itemize} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop twoseed of arXiv:2606.24793

body: A topological space X is connected if it cannot be written as the union of two disjoint nonempty open sets. Equivalently: the only subsets of X that are simultaneously open and closed are the empty set and X itself. A subset of a topological space is called connected if it is connected in the subspace topology. A pair (U, V) of disjoint nonempty open sets whose union is X is called a separation of X. The real interval [0,1] with its standard topology is connected (a consequence of the least-upper-bound property of the reals).
title: Connected space

body:
[Thm reg_existence of arXiv:2506.01746, '\bf Optimal Bregman quantization: existence and uniqueness of optimal quantizers revisited'] Let $r>0$ and let $\|\cdot\|$ denote any norm on  $\mathbb{R}^d$.  Assume $\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}\|\xi\|^{r}\mathbb{P}(\mathrm{d}\xi)< + \infty$.

\smallskip
\noindent $(a)$ For every $n\ge 1$, there exists at least one $L^r$-optimal quantizer $\Gamma^{(r,n)}$ of size at most $n$, solution to the minimization problem
\[
\inf_{\Gamma: |\Gamma|\leq n}  e_r(\Gamma,P,\|.\|)
\]
i.e. such that 
\[
e_r(\Gamma^{(r,n)},P,\|.\|)=  e_{r,n}(P,\|.\|).  
\]

\smallskip
\noindent $(b)$ If ${\rm card}\big({\rm supp}(P)\big) \ge n$, then any $L^r$-optimal quantizer $ \Gamma^{(r,n)}$ has full size $n$ and for every $a\!\in  \Gamma^{(r,n)}$, $P(C_a( \Gamma^{(r,n)}))>0$. Moreover, 

\smallskip
 $(i)$ if the norm $\|\cdot\|$ is smooth~(\footnote{that $\|\cdot\|$ is differentiable on $\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\{0\}$, like Euclidean norms or $\ell^p$-norms, $1<p<+\infty$.}) and strictly convex then {\em the boundary of the Voronoi partition is $P$-negligible}: for every $a\!\in \Gamma^{(r,n)}$, $P\big(\partial C_a(\Gamma^{(r,n)})\big)=0$

\smallskip
  $(ii)$ if   $r\ge 2$ and the norm $\|\cdot\|=|\cdot|_e$ is Euclidean then these quantizers are {\em $L^r$-stationarity}: for every $a\!\in \Gamma^{(r,n)}$,
\[
a = \frac{\int_{C_a(\Gamma^{(r,n)})}\xi|\xi-a|^{r-2}P(\mathrm{d}\xi)}{\int_{C_a(\Gamma^{(r,n)})}|\xi-a|^{r-2}P(\mathrm{d}\xi)}.
\]
\
\noindent $(c)$ When $d=1$  and $P=U([0,1])$, then for every $r>0$, the $L^r$-optimal quantizer is unique and 
\[
\Gamma^{(r,n)} = \Big\{\frac{2k-1}{2n},\; k=0,\ldots,n\Big\}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Proposition prop-well-posedness-approx of arXiv:2507.09922, 'A scaling limit for Vlasov equations with electrostatic fluctuations'] Assume that $f^\delta_0\in C_c^\infty (\mathbb{T}^3\times \mathbb{R}^3, \mathbb{R}_+)$. Then for any $\delta>0$, the approximate equation (equation stoch-Vlasov-approx of the paper) admits a unique probabilistically strong solution $f^\delta$, represented as
  $$f^\delta_t(x,v)= f^\delta_0 \big(\Phi^{\delta,-1}_t(x,v) \big), $$
where $\big\{\Phi^{\delta,-1}_t \big\}_{t\ge 0}$ is the inverse flow associated to the stochastic equations
  \begin{equation}
  \left\{ \aligned
  d X^\delta_t &= V^\delta_t\, dt, \\
  d V^\delta_t &= \big[E_{\rho^\delta_t}\big(X^\delta_t \big) + B V^\delta_t\times \bm{e}_3 \big]\, dt + \sum_k \sigma_k\big(X^\delta_t \big)\circ dW^k_t
  \endaligned \right.
  \end{equation}
with initial condition $\big(X^\delta_0, V^\delta_0 \big)= (x,v)\in \mathbb{T}^3\times \mathbb{R}^3$. Moreover, $\|f^\delta_t \|_{L^p_{x,v}} = \|f^\delta_0 \|_{L^p_{x,v}}$ for any $p\ge 1$.

body:
[Prop of arXiv:2507.09120, 'Chemical distance in graphs of polynomial growth'] (Russo's Formula; see e.g. [grimmett1999percolation])
   Let $f : 2^E \to \mathbb{R}$ be a decreasing function, in the sense that $\omega \subset \omega'$ implies
   $f(\omega) \ge f(\omega')$. Suppose further that $f$ only depends on a finite set of edges
   (that is, there exists $F \subset E$ finite such that $f(\omega) = f(\omega \cap F)$ for all $\omega \in 2^E$).
   Then $\mathbb{E}[f(G_p)]$ is differentiable in $p$, and its derivative is given by
   \[ 
      \frac{d}{dp} \mathbb{E}[f(G_p)] = - \sum_{e \in E} \mathbb{E}[ \Delta_e f (G_p) ],
   \]
   where for $\omega \in 2^E$ and $e \in E$ we define 
   $ \Delta_e f(\omega) := f(\omega \setminus \{e\}) - f(\omega \cup \{e\})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered prop of arXiv:2507.09120, 'Chemical distance in graphs of polynomial growth'

body:
[Proposition 4 (Excess-risk rate under semi-supervised designs) of arXiv:2608.23960, 'Learning from Uncertainty-dependent Missing Labels for Semi-supervised Classification'] Let $\theta^\star$ denote the pseudo-true parameter and let $\hat\theta$ be an $M$-estimator satisfying
\[
\hat\theta-\theta^\star=O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1/2}).
\]
Consider the plug-in classifier
\[
C_\theta(y)=\mathbbm{1}\{\mu_\theta(y)\ge 1/2\},
\]
where $\mu_\theta(y)=\tilde g^{-1}\{\eta_\theta(y)\}$ is a differentiable working regression function. Suppose that $\mu_{\theta^\star}(y)=\eta^\star(y)$ is the target regression function and that the Tsybakov margin condition holds:
\[
\Pr\!\left\{
\left|\eta^\star(Y)-\frac12\right|\le t
\right\}
\le
C_M t^\alpha
\]
for some $\alpha>0$, $C_M>0$, and all sufficiently small $t>0$. Assume also that, in a neighborhood of $\theta^\star$,
\[
\sup_y |\mu_\theta(y)-\mu_{\theta^\star}(y)|
\le
L\|\theta-\theta^\star\|
\]
for some finite constant $L$. Then
\[
R(\hat\theta)-R(\theta^\star)
=
O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(n^{-(1+\alpha)/2}\right).
\]
In particular, for the regular two-component mixture setting in
Lemma~\ref{lem:margin-two-component}, \(\alpha=1\), and hence
\[
R(\hat\theta)-R(\theta^\star)
=
O_{\mathbb P}(n^{-1}).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Excess-risk rate under semi-supervised designs

[Lemma 18 (Uniform compactly supported half-space quasimodes) of arXiv:2608.30211, '2608.30211'] There are $R_0,C>0$ such that, for every $R\geq R_0$ and
$\varrho\in[0,1]$, one can find an $L^2$-normalized function
$\Psi_{\varrho,R}$ in the $\varrho$ form domain on $\Hh^d$ satisfying
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{supp}\Psi_{\varrho,R}\subset B_{3R}(0)\cap\overline{\Hh^d},
 \qquad
 Q_\varrho(\Psi_{\varrho,R})\leq\mu_\varrho+\frac{C}{R}.
\end{equation}
At the Dirichlet endpoint the quasimode has zero trace.

body:
A sequence is Cauchy if for every epsilon > 0 there is N with |a_m - a_n| < epsilon for all m, n >= N. In R (and any complete metric space) a sequence converges if and only if it is Cauchy. The forward direction holds in any metric space; the converse is exactly completeness. This lets one prove convergence without knowing the limit.

[Definition of arXiv:2602.00853, 'Mixing times for the stochastic $p$-Laplace equation'] Let $p\in (1,2)$. We say that $\{X_t\}_{t\in [0,T]}$ is a \emph{stochastic variational inequality (SVI) solution} to (equation eq:pLaplace of the paper) for initial data $x_0\in L^2(U)$ if
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item $X\in L^2([0,T]\times\Omega;L^2(U))$ such that
\[\operatorname{ess\,sup}\displaylimits_{t\in [0,T]}\mathbb{E}\int_0^T\int_U|\nabla X_s|^p\,\mathrm{d} z\,\mathrm{d} s<\infty,\]
\item for any $z_0\in L^2(U)$, every $Z\in L^2([0,T]\times\Omega;H^1_0(U))$, and every progressively measurable $G\in L^2([0,T]\times\Omega;L^2(U))$ such that
\[Z_t=z_0+\int_0^t G_s\,\mathrm{d} s+B\,W_t,\]
we have that for a.e. $t\in [0,T]$
\begin{align*}&\mathbb{E}\left[\|X_t-Z_t\|^2_{L^2(U)}\right]+\frac{2}{p}\mathbb{E}\int_0^t\int_U|\nabla X_s|^p\,\mathrm{d} z\,\mathrm{d} s\\
\le &\mathbb{E}\left[\|x_0-z_0\|^2_{L^2(U)}\right]+\frac{2}{p}\mathbb{E}\int_0^t\int_U|\nabla Z_s|^p\,\mathrm{d} z\,\mathrm{d} s-2\mathbb{E}\int_0^t\int_U G_s(X_s-Z_s)\,\mathrm{d} z\,\mathrm{d} s.\end{align*}
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Definition 11 of arXiv:2609.02878, '2609.02878'] For \(p=[w]\in\PP^N\), define the ambient chord-square barrier
\begin{equation}
 \widehat\rho_p([z])
 :=1-\frac{|\langle z,w\rangle|^2}{|z|^2|w|^2}.
\end{equation}
It is a smooth nonnegative function, vanishes precisely at \(p\), and
the family \(\{\widehat\rho_p\}_{p\in\PP^N}\) has uniform first- and
second-derivative bounds.  Moreover, for uniform \(0<c<C<\infty\),
\begin{equation}
 c\,d_{\rm FS}(y,p)^2\le\widehat\rho_p(y)
 \le C\,d_{\rm FS}(y,p)^2,
 \qquad y,p\in\PP^N.
\end{equation}
Indeed, in the standard normalization
\(\widehat\rho_p=\sin^2d_{\rm FS}(\,\cdot\,,p)\), and the
Fubini--Study diameter is finite.

Now let \(q\in U_0\Subset U_1\Subset Y^{\rm rv}\).  Compose
\(\widehat\rho_{\iota(q)}|_Y\) with a smooth nondecreasing function
that is the identity near zero and is constant once its argument leaves
a sufficiently small sublevel set contained in \(U_1\).  The resulting
function \(\rho_q\) is called a \emph{localized squared-distance
barrier at \(q\)}.  It is the restriction of a smooth ambient function,
has zero set \(\{q\}\), is uniformly comparable to
\(d_\eta(\,\cdot\,,q)^2\) near \(q\), is bounded below on
\(Y\setminus U_0\), and has its first two derivatives supported in
\(U_1\).

[Theorem 5 of arXiv:2605.23222, 'On global solutions to the semidiscrete stochastic heat equation'] If $\beta$ is sufficiently small, the following holds: Let $\Omega' \in \Fc$ such that $Q(\Omega') = 1$ and $\theta_t(\Omega') = \Omega'$ for all $t \in \R$. Let $Z: \Z^d \times \R \times \Omega' \to (0, \infty)$ be a global stationary solution to~\eqref{eq:sSHE} such that for every $\omega \in \Omega'$ there is $\epsilon \in (0,1)$ with 
$$
\lim_{\|y\| \to \infty} \frac{\lvert \ln(Z(y,0,\omega)) \rvert}{\|y\|^{1-\epsilon}} = 0. 
$$
Then, $Q$-almost surely, for all $(y,t) \in \Z^d \times \R$, 
$$
Z(y,t,\omega) = Z_{-\infty}^{y,t}(\omega) \cdot \frac{Z(0,0,\omega)}{Z_{-\infty}^{0,0}(\omega)}. 
$$ (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 5 of arXiv:2605.23222

[Lem thm:bobkov of arXiv:2602.22342, 'Sum of Gaussian vectors and large sets'] Let $C\geq 1$ and let $\mu$ be a probability measure on $\R$ with piecewise continuous density 
$$C^{-1}\varphi(x)\leq \frac{d\mu (x)}{dx} \leq  C \varphi(x).$$
Then $\mu = F_*(\gamma_1)$ for a Lipschitz map $F:\R\to \R$ with Lipschitz constant at most $C^2$.

body:
[Lem 79 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] On the time interval $[q_0,\gamma(1)]$ let $\tilde{Y}$, $\tilde{W}$, $\tilde{w}$, $\tilde{\cF}_Y$ be as given by Lemma~\ref{l:time.change}.
It is possible to extend these to the full time interval $[q_0,1]$ such that
$|\tilde Y(1)| = 1$ almost surely, and the same conditions as before are satisfied: $\tilde{W}$ is a standard Brownian motion,
$\tilde{w}$ is progressively measurable with respect to
    \[
    \tilde \cF_Y(t) = \sigma\Big(
        (\tilde W_s)_{s\in [q_0,t]}, U', \tilde Y(q_0)
    \Big)
\]
with $\bbE[(\tilde w_t)^2] = 1$ for all $t$,
and
 \[
        \tilde Y(t) = \tilde Y(\gamma(1))
            + \int_{\gamma(1)}^t \tilde w_s\,d\tilde{W}(s)\,.
    \]

\begin{proof} Abbreviate $t_1=\gamma(1)$.
Let $Z$ be a standard Brownian motion on the time interval $[t_1,{{\infty)}}$ with initialization $Z(t_1)=\tilde{Y}(t_1)$. Let
    \[
    \bar{\tau}
    \equiv\inf\Big\{t\ge t_1 : |Z(t)|\ge1\Big\}\,,
    \]
and define the stopped martingale
    \[\bar{Z}(t)\equiv Z(t\wedge\bar{\tau})
    =\tilde{Y}(t_1)+ \int_{q_0}^t \ind\{t\le\bar{\tau}\} \,dZ(t)\,.
    \]
Then, similarly as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{l:time.change}, we define $\tilde{Y}$ to be the time change of $\bar{Z}$ satisfying the desired properties. Explicitly, let 
    \[
    \bar{\gamma}(t)
    = \E[\bar{Z}(t_1+t)^2] -\E[\bar{Z}(t_1)^2] 
    = \E \int_{t_1}^{t_1+t} \ind\{t\le\bar{\tau}\}\,dt\,,
    \]
and denote its generalized inverse $\bar{\lambda}$.
We then take $\tilde{Y}(t)=\bar{Z}(t_1+\bar{\lambda}(t-t_1))$, so that
$\E[\tilde{Y}(t)^2]=t$. As in Lemma~\ref{l:time.change}, we can express
    \[
    \tilde{Y}(t)
    = \tilde{Y}(t_1) + \int_{t_1}^t \tilde{w}_t\,d\tilde{W}(t)
    \]
where we can define explicitly    \begin{align*}
    \tilde{W}(t) 
    &=\int_{t_1}^{t_1+\bar{\lambda}(t-t_1)}
	\bar{\gamma}'(u-t_1)^{1/2}\,dZ(u)\,,\\
    \tilde{w}_t
    &= \frac{\ind\{t_1+\bar{\lambda}(t-t_1)\le\tau\}}
        {\bar{\gamma}'(\bar{\lambda}(t-t_1))^{1/2}}\,.
    \end{align*}
The claim follows.
\end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lem 79 of arXiv:2608.29416

body: [Defn def:condLBSF of arXiv:2608.30031, 'Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures'] A flow $\Phi$ is \textbf{locally branched surface finite} (\textbf{LBSF}) if for every $p\in \mathbb{R}^n$, there is a neighborhood $U$ of $p$ and a finite collection of $\Phi$-horizontal branched surfaces $\Sigma_1,\dots, \Sigma_m$ such that, up to the action of flow preserving homeomorphisms of $(M,\Phi)$ rel boundary, every $\Phi$-horizontal foliation with generalized boundary multislope in $U$ is carried by some $\Sigma_i$. Here, a generalized boundary multislope is in $K$ if some substitution of its $\aleph$ components with real numbers lies in $K$.
title: Defn def:condLBSF of arXiv:2608.30031

[Lem of arXiv:2607.19660, 'Smallest gaps between zeros of stationary Gaussian processes'] Given $x_{1}, \ldots, x_{k}$ be distinct elements in $[0, R]^{k}$, and  let $\eta=\min (x_{i+1}-x_i)$. Then one has the uniform asymptotics, 
	$$
	R^k \tilde{\rho}_{k}^{}\left(x_{1}, \ldots, x_{k}\right) \to \left(\alpha_0 \int_{A} u^{} \mathrm{~d} u\right)^{k} \left(1+O\left(\left(\|\kappa\|_{4,  \eta}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)\right).
	$$ as $R\to\infty$.  In particular, given $x_{1}, \ldots, x_{k}$ be distinct elements in $[0, 1]^{k}$,  one has the uniform asymptotics, 
	$$
	R^k \tilde{\rho}_{k}^{}\left(Rx_{1}, \ldots, Rx_{k}\right) \to \left(\alpha_0 \int_{A} u^{} \mathrm{~d} u\right)^{k}  $$ as $R\to\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Unnumbered lem of arXiv:2607.19660, 'Smallest gaps between zeros of stationary Gaussian processes'

[Definition Stochastically continuous Feller semigroup of arXiv:2505.14012, 'Ergodicity for stochastic neural field equations'] We say that $(P_t)_{t\ge 0}$ is a stochastically continuous Feller semigroup if for every $v\in H$ and every $r>0$ it follows that
\[\lim_{t\to 0} P_t(v,B(v,r))=1
\quad \textrm{ and }\quad
P_t(C_b(H))\subset C_b(H),
\]
where $B(v,r):=\{z\in H:\|z\|_H<r\}$.
title: Stochastically continuous Feller semigroup

[Lemma lem:logarithmic-derivative-support of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] For every $z\in Z$, define
\[
    A_z^+(x)
    :=
    \frac{F_z'}{F_z}(x+iY)+4\pi i,
    \qquad
    A_z^-(x)
    :=
    \frac{F_z'}{F_z}(x-iY)-4\pi i.
\]
Then
\[
    \operatorname{supp}\widehat A_z^+
    \subset[1,\infty),
    \qquad
    \operatorname{supp}\widehat A_z^-
    \subset(-\infty,-1].
\]

[Lemma lem:pair-table-cert of arXiv:2607.13990, 'Effective Resistance in Fixed-Rank External-Field Measures\\ and Constant-Stretch Correlat'] Let $\pi_{11},\pi_{10},\pi_{01},\pi_{00}>0$ with $\pi_{11}+\pi_{10}+\pi_{01}+\pi_{00}=1$, and put
\[
    s
=
    \pi_{10}+\pi_{01},
\quad
    \mu_i
=
    \pi_{11}+\pi_{10},
\quad
    \mu_j
=
    \pi_{11}+\pi_{01},
\quad
    \delta
=
    \pi_{10}-\pi_{01},
\]
\[
    v_i
=
    \mu_i(1-\mu_i),
\quad
    v_j
=
    \mu_j(1-\mu_j),
\quad
    \omega
=
    \pi_{10}\pi_{01}-\pi_{11}\pi_{00},
\quad
    h
=
    \mu_i+\mu_j-2\mu_i\mu_j.
\]
Then
\[
    \pi_{10}\pi_{01}(v_i+v_j)+\pi_{11}\pi_{00}\delta^2-sv_iv_j
=
    \omega\bigl[2v_iv_j+\omega h\bigr].
\]

[Definition def:scaling of arXiv:2512.06984, 'Infinite Dimensional Multifractal Analysis of the Wiener measure'] A family $ \mathsf{scl} = ( \mathit{scl}_\alpha)_{ \alpha > 0 } $ of Hausdorff functions is  a \emph{scaling} if for every $ \alpha > \beta > 0 $ and every $ \lambda > 1 $ close enough to $ 1 $ (say $1<\lambda <\lambda_0$), it holds: 
        \[ \mathit{scl}_\alpha ( \varepsilon)  = o ( \mathit{scl}_\beta ( \varepsilon^\lambda)) \quad \text{and}\quad \mathit{scl}_\alpha ( \varepsilon)  = o ( \mathit{scl}_\beta ( \varepsilon) ^\lambda )  \; .   \]

body:
Let $A$ be measurable and uniformly parabolic with constants $\lambda,\Lambda$ and let $u$ be a local weak solution of $\partial_tu=\mathrm{div}(A\nabla u)$ in the backward cylinder $Q_{2r}=Q_{2r}(x_0,t_0)$. Then: (a) local boundedness -- $\sup_{Q_r}|u|\le C\big(\frac{1}{|Q_{2r}|}\iint_{Q_{2r}}u^2\big)^{1/2}$; (b) interior Holder continuity -- there are $\alpha=\alpha(n,\lambda,\Lambda)\in(0,1)$ and $C=C(n,\lambda,\Lambda)$ such that $u$ has a continuous representative with $|u(x,t)-u(y,s)|\le C\Big(\frac{|x-y|+|t-s|^{1/2}}{r}\Big)^{\alpha}\sup_{Q_{2r}}|u|$ for $(x,t),(y,s)\in Q_r$. Both constants depend only on $n$ and the ellipticity constants, and on nothing else about $A$ -- this is exactly what makes the theorem the parabolic counterpart of De Giorgi's and Nash's solution of Hilbert's 19th problem and the engine behind Aronson's bounds. Estimates are interior in the parabolic sense: they hold up to the top time $t_0$ but require distance from the bottom and the lateral sides.

divergence form, no lower-order terms (with bounded lower-order terms the same holds with constants depending on their bounds and on r)

[Proposition properties-of-a0 of arXiv:2609.00425, 'Individual and Uniform Eventual Positivity of Self-Adjoint Semigroups'] Let $A_0$ be the operator on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})$ as defined above. Then the following assertions hold:
    \begin{enumerate}[\upshape (i)]
        \item The operator $A_0$ is real and self-adjoint.
        \item One has $A_0 \leq 0$ in the Hilbert space sense, and $s(A_0) = 0$ is a simple eigenvalue of $A_0$.
        \item $A_0$ has compact resolvent.
        \item Both $H_{\mathrm{even}}$ and $H_{\mathrm{odd}}$ reduce $A_0$ and one has $A_0|_{H_{\mathrm{odd}}} = -D|_{H_{\mathrm{odd}}}$.
    \end{enumerate}

[Lemma lem:hausdorff-requests of arXiv:2608.29561, 'Ball codes: A coding characterization of Hausdorff and packing dimensions'] Let \(E\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, let \(s>0\), let \(k\ge0\) and
\(m\ge1\) be integers with \(sm\ge k\), and let \(\eta>0\).  If
\[
\mathcal H^s_{2^{-(m+2)}}(E)<2^{-s-k}\eta,
\]
then there are a finite or countable index set \(I\), closed balls
\((B_i)_{i\in I}\), and natural numbers \((\ell_i)_{i\in I}\) such that
\[
E\subseteq\bigcup_{i\in I} B_i,
\qquad
0<\diam(B_i)<2^{-m},
\qquad
\sum_{i\in I}2^{-\ell_i}<\eta,
\]
and
\[
\ell_i<s\bigl(-\log_2\diam(B_i)\bigr)+1-k
\]
for every \(i\in I\).  Thus small \(s\)-Hausdorff content at scale
\(2^{-(m+2)}\) gives a cover whose balls can be requested with small total
Kraft weight and with a prescribed saving \(k\) in the requested lengths.

[Cor generic of arXiv:2606.30517, '\textsc{Convergence towards Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations with a focus on Diestel--'] Under the conditions of (def:generic of the paper), the distribution of $(\iota_{t(\lambda)}X^{(\lambda)}, \mathrm{Vor}(X^{(\lambda)}))$ is precompact for both ordered and unordered versions (discussed in (subsubsec:ipvt of the paper)). 
		Moreover, if a subsequence $(\iota_{t(\lambda_n)}X^{(\lambda_n)}, \mathrm{Vor}(X^{(\lambda_n)}))$ converges in one sense, say to $(\Phi,T)$, then it converges to $(\Phi,T)$ in the other sense as well. If, in addition, either $E$ is a graph or $\Phi$ is nondegenerate a.s., then $T=\mathrm{Vor}(\Phi)$ a.s.

[Definition 7 (Reachability and mutual reachability) of arXiv:2608.28991, 'Jigsaw-CRL: Recovering Global Latent Causal Order from Fragmented Multi-Client Interventio'] For two nodes $i,j \in \cV_k$, we say that $i$ is \emph{reachable} to $j$, written $i \rightsquigarrow_k j$, if there exists a sequence of nodes
$i = v_0, v_1, \dots, v_m = j$, 
such that for every $\ell = 0,\dots,m-1$, either $v_\ell \prec_k v_{\ell+1}$ or $v_\ell \leftrightarrow v_{\ell+1} \in \cD_k$.
Two nodes $i,j \in \cV_k$ are said to be \emph{mutually reachable} if $i \rightsquigarrow_k j$ and $j \rightsquigarrow_k i$.
title: Reachability and mutual reachability

[Definition 16 (Obstacle Problem) of arXiv:2605.18198, 'Large deviations of crowding in finite $\beta$-ensembles'] Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain and let 
	$\psi : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}$ be the obstacle. 
	Find a function $u$ such that
	\begin{align*}
		u &\ge \psi && \text{in } \Omega, \\
		-\Delta u &\ge 0 && \text{in } \Omega, \\
		(-\Delta u)(u-\psi) &= 0 && \text{in } \Omega, \\
		u &= g && \text{on } \partial \Omega .
	\end{align*}
title: Obstacle Problem

body:
[Lemma 7 of arXiv:2608.18557, 'Randomly Permuted Orthogonal Products and Fast Dimension Reduction'] Let \(b\in\R^d\) satisfy \(\sum_{k=1}^d b_k=0\), let
	\(X_1,\ldots,X_d\) be symmetric \(r\times r\) matrices, and let
	\(\pi\) be uniform on \(S_d\). Set
	\[
	\sigma^2
	=
	\frac{\norm{b}_2^2}{d}
	\left\|
	\sum_{j=1}^d X_j^2
	\right\|,
	\qquad
	M
	=
	\norm{b}_\infty\max_{j\in[d]}\norm{X_j}.
	\]
	Then
	\[
	\probb{\pi}{\norm{\sum_{j=1}^d b_{\pi(j)}X_j}\ge t}
	\le
	2r\exp\left(
	-\frac{t^2}
	{12\sigma^2+4\sqrt2\,Mt}
	\right)
	\qquad \text{for }t\geq0.
	\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 7 of arXiv:2608.18557

[Proposition (Informal) Equivalence of Chebyshev Polynomials and Concatenated Shapes of arXiv:2608.12415, 'Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting'] For a linear combination of backbone-dangling shapes, $Q = \sum_{\psi \in \mathcal{B}(Q) : \text{backbone-dangling} } c_\psi  \cdot \mathsf{M} _\psi$, provided $\mathrm{Var}(Q) =1$,
 for any $j\geq 1$,  we have
\[
    P_j(Q)
    =
    \sum_{\substack{\tau:\text{ \(j\)-fold concatenation of }\mathcal{B}(Q) \\ \tau =\psi_1\circ \psi_2\circ \ldots \circ \psi_j} }
    c_\tau \mathsf{M} _\tau + o_d(1),
\]  
up to lower-order error terms of spectral norm $o_d(1)$ and the coefficients are given by \(
c_\tau = \prod_{t\in [j]} c_{\psi_t} \).

In words,   \(P_j(Q)\) is approximated by the
weighted sum of all \(j\)-fold proper concatenations of shapes from
\(\mathcal{B}(Q)\), up to lower-order error terms. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: (Informal) Equivalence of Chebyshev Polynomials and Concatenated Shapes

body: The Riemann zeta function is zeta(s) = sum over n >= 1 of n^{-s}, absolutely convergent for Re(s) > 1, extended by analytic continuation to a meromorphic function on C with a single simple pole at s = 1 of residue 1. It satisfies the functional equation relating zeta(s) and zeta(1 - s) through the completed function xi(s) = pi^{-s/2} Gamma(s/2) zeta(s), which is symmetric under s -> 1 - s. Its zeros in the critical strip 0 < Re(s) < 1 govern the distribution of primes; the Riemann hypothesis places them all on Re(s) = 1/2.
title: Riemann Zeta Function

body: In the field of machine learning, the universal approximation theorems (UATs) state that neural networks with a certain structure can, in principle, approximate any continuous function to any desired degree of accuracy. These theorems provide a mathematical justification for using neural networks, assuring researchers that a sufficiently large or deep network can model the complex, non-linear relationships often found in real-world data.
title: Universal approximation theorem

[Proposition 8 of arXiv:2609.03238, 'Representation Defects and Cassels Pairings for Congruent Number Curves'] Let $p\ne q$ be odd primes and let $n\in\{pq,2pq\}$.  Then
\[
s_2(n)=4
\]
if and only if
\[
p\equiv q\equiv1\pmod8,
\qquad
\left(\frac qp\right)=1.
\]
For every other residue pattern one has only the general bound $s_2(n)\le3$; the value
$s_2(n)=3$ can occur.

[Theorem 11 (Total stochastic dominance characterises the fair coin) of arXiv:2601.16580, 'Coin flipping and waiting times paradoxes \\ Why fair coins are exceptional'] Let $p\in(0,1)$ and consider an i.i.d.\ coin with $\Pr(\mathrm{H})=p$ and $\Pr(\mathrm{T})=q:=1-p$.
For each finite binary string $T\in\{\mathrm{H},\mathrm{T}\}^\ast$, let $\tau_T$ be its first-hit time and
write $\prec_{\mathrm{st}}$ for the strict stochastic-dominance order on strings:
\[
T_1\prec_{\mathrm{st}}T_2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\tau_{T_2}\sdom \tau_{T_1}.
\]
Then $\prec_{\mathrm{st}}$ is a strict weak order on the set of \emph{all} binary strings
(i.e.\ every pair is comparable up to statistical equivalence) if and only if $p=\tfrac12$.

Own work draft; proof (unaudited), no novelty established. For the population DDPM score loss of an equilateral three-Gaussian teacher of small noisy radius a, centered-network GD contracts shape and plane errors toward the two-dimensional equilateral subspace at rate 1-c h a^2, locally in a fixed relative tube whose projected radius lies in [0.9a,1.1a]. The exact transverse covariance Hessian has plane coefficient 2r^2-2/3 and perpendicular coefficient 2r^2/3. Constants are independent of ambient dimension. Scope limits: This is conditional local tracking only; random entry, radial tube preservation, centroid drift for free means, and long empirical perturbations are not settled.

metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:9079094046d8c0b1e0aa17c0424af5a5640169fa1327da97b27f9fdb7d4b6377","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/90/9079094046d8c0b1e0aa17c0424af5a5640169fa1327da97b27f9fdb7d4b6377.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:9414a991b2186c148d2cb49844008a912bb9006dfe2c0e78fc1b7001dc98b71f","bundle_entry_key":"t309-c05","bundle_id":"population.t309-transverse-tracking-and-spurious-ddpm-minimum-drafts","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"probability, Gaussian mixtures, score matching","draft":"w721/bundle_002.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.learning:equilateral-gaussian-ddpm-transverse-tracking","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# T309: transverse attraction toward the equilateral family

T309-w721-C05 v1. Status: proof (unaudited). This is a local population statement for a centered student parameterization, not a solution of Target 2. No novelty is asserted.

The point of this lemma is to control the previously unpaid shape and plane directions near the family used in C03. It does not establish entry into that neighborhood from a generic random initialization. It also does not treat centroid drift of the unrestricted three-mean parameterization or finite-sample errors over the ensuing long angular stage.

## 1. Setup and statement

Fix d>=2. Let u_j, j=0,1,2, be unit equilateral vectors in a plane P, and let Q rotate P by 2pi/3. The teacher is q_a=(1/3)sum_j N(a u_j,I_d), where a>0 is sufficiently small.

Let H be the linear space of d-by-3 mean matrices M whose columns sum to zero. Train the Eq. (9) score student with equal component weights and identity covariance, parameterized on H, using the population DDPM objective. Equivalently, choose any orthonormal coordinates on H and apply Euclidean GD in those coordinates. In the original three-column coordinates, this is the centered projection of the full gradient, not unrestricted three-mean GD. This distinction is part of the assumptions.

Let L be the two-dimensional linear subspace consisting of matrices with columns Q^j z for z in P. Write Pi_L for its orthogonal projection within H. For M=v+w, where v=Pi_L M and w is orthogonal to L within H, define r by ||v||_F=sqrt(3) a r.

There are absolute constants a_0,rho,c,C>0, independent of d, such that throughout the tube

    0<a<=a_0,    9/10<=r<=11/10,    ||w||_F<=rho a,

the following hold:

    <w, grad_H F_a(v+w)> >= c a^2 ||w||_F^2,                     (1)
    ||Pi_{L-perp} grad_H F_a(v+w)||_F <= C a^2 ||w||_F.          (2)

Here F_a is the exact population excess score loss, equal to the population excess DDPM objective. Consequently, for centered GD with 0<h<=c/(C^2 a^2),

    ||w_next||_F^2 <= (1-c h a^2)||w||_F^2,                     (3)

provided the current iterate lies in the tube. For the centered gradient flow, the corresponding squared distance decays at least as exp(-2c a^2 t) for as long as the projection radius remains in the indicated interval. These are conditional local tracking estimates; (3) alone is not a proof that a trajectory stays radially confined or enters the tube.

The plane and subspace L are used only to state and analyze the error. The centered gradient step itself does not require knowing P. Centering, however, is enforced in the student parameterization.

## 2. The high-noise loss expansion in all centered directions

For a centered matrix U with columns u'_j, write C(U)=UU^T/3. Let U_* be the teacher's unit-radius matrix. Uniformly on any fixed Frobenius ball ||U||_F<=B inside H,

    F_a(aU)=a^4 ||C(U)-C(U_*)||_F^2 + O_{C^2(U)}(a^6).         (4)

The C^2 bound is in operator norm with respect to the Frobenius metric, and its constant can be chosen independently of d. The teacher is fixed at a U_* while the student varies as aU.

For completeness, the posterior mean correction in the score is

    b_U(a,x)=a sum_j w_j u'_j,
    w_j proportional to exp(a u'_j dot x-a^2 ||u'_j||^2/2).

Since sum_j u'_j=0, expansion gives b_U(a,x)=a^2 C(U)x+O(a^3). Hence the squared difference between the student and teacher scores begins at a^4, and its Gaussian leading expectation is ||C(U)-C(U_*)||_F^2. The exact replacement (a,x)->(-a,-x) makes the risk an even function of a, so the next possible order is a^6.

The integrated Taylor remainder and its two U derivatives are justified by the softmax-weight domination argument used in C01. To check dimension independence rather than hiding it in an ambient Gaussian norm, fix unit Frobenius directions D,E when taking a mixed Hessian derivative. Every logit and every directional derivative depends on x only through the span of the columns of U,U_*,D,E. Its dimension is at most 12, independently of d. All norms of these four matrices are bounded, so the derivative envelopes are fixed polynomials in a Gaussian vector of dimension at most 12, times exp(C||G||) if a derivative of the teacher density is present. Their moments are bounded uniformly. Coordinates perpendicular to that span integrate to 1 and make identical score contributions for teacher and student. This proves a common bound for all unit D,E and hence the required operator-norm C^2 remainder.

## 3. Exact transverse Hessian of the covariance loss

Choose a 3-by-2 matrix A with orthonormal columns spanning 1-perpendicular, and let E be an orthonormal basis matrix for P. Right multiplication M->MA is an isometry on H because AA^T is the projection onto 1-perpendicular. Choose the orientation of E and A so the equilateral reference has factor

    U A=sqrt(3/2) r E.

At another angular position the same calculation holds after rotating E, which leaves the teacher covariance C(U_*)=P/2 unchanged. For a centered perturbation D write its two-column factor as

    D A=E X+E_perp Y,

where E_perp is an orthonormal basis for the perpendicular complement (absent if d=2). Orthogonality of D to L says that X is orthogonal to both I_2 and the 90-degree rotation J. Every real 2-by-2 matrix orthogonal to I_2 and J is symmetric with trace zero. This follows directly by writing its four entries: its two diagonal entries sum to zero and its two off-diagonal entries are equal.

Let G(U)=||C(U)-P/2||_F^2. Its Hessian in a direction D is

    Hess G(U)[D,D]=2||DC(U)[D]||_F^2
                   +2<C(U)-P/2,D^2C(U)[D,D]>,
    DC(U)[D]=(DU^T+UD^T)/3,    D^2C(U)[D,D]=2DD^T/3.

Using the factor sqrt(3/2)r E, symmetry and tracelessness of X, and orthogonality of P and P-perpendicular gives exactly

    ||DC(U)[D]||_F^2=(2r^2/3)||X||_F^2+(r^2/3)||Y||_F^2,
    Hess G(U)[D,D]=(2r^2-2/3)||X||_F^2+(2r^2/3)||Y||_F^2.       (5)

In particular, for 9/10<=r<=11/10,

    Hess G(U)[D,D] >= (27/50)||D||_F^2.                        (6)

Indeed the plane coefficient is at least 143/150 and the perpendicular coefficient is at least 27/50; also ||D||_F^2=||X||_F^2+||Y||_F^2. This is not a dimension-count argument: it identifies and computes the two normal blocks. The exact symbolic check in scripts/check_normal.py independently expands the 3-by-2 factor perturbation and verifies (5).

## 4. Transfer of the Hessian to the exact loss

Because (5) is a polynomial Hessian with dimension-independent Frobenius operator bounds on bounded balls, there is a sufficiently small absolute rho>0 such that (6), weakened to a lower bound 2/5, holds in the fixed directions D orthogonal to L also at U+W whenever ||W||_F<=rho. The perturbation W need not remain equilateral. This is continuity in operator norm on a bounded ball, with constants bounded by the covariance polynomial itself, so it does not introduce a dimension-dependent compactness argument.

By (4), after changing from U=M/a to physical means M, the Hessian of F_a is

    Hess_M F_a = a^2 Hess_U G + O_op(a^4)

on the centered space. Choose a_0 sufficiently small that the remainder leaves at least a^2/4 of normal curvature throughout the tube and its segments v+s w, 0<=s<=1. The same expansion gives a full centered Hessian upper bound C a^2 there. Thus one may take c=1/4 after adjusting the tube and the upper constant C.

The exact symmetry in C02 implies grad_H F_a(v) lies in L at every v in L. Therefore its normal projection is zero. Integrating the normal Hessian along v+s w proves (1), while its upper bound proves (2):

    Pi_{L-perp} grad_H F_a(v+w)
        =integral_0^1 Pi_{L-perp} Hess_H F_a(v+s w) w ds.

All projections here are orthogonal in the same Frobenius metric as the parameterization.

## 5. The tracking inequalities

For centered GD, w_next=w-h Pi_{L-perp} grad_H F_a(v+w). Expanding its squared norm and applying (1)--(2) gives

    ||w_next||^2 <= (1-2c h a^2+C^2 h^2 a^4)||w||^2.

For h<=c/(C^2 a^2) this is (3). For the flow, differentiating ||w||^2 gives -2<w,grad_H F_a>, yielding the exponential estimate by integration while the tube condition holds. No probability product, independence claim, or numerical integration bound is used.

## 6. The exact outstanding bridge

For a centered generic initial triple, the leading loss in (4) is a rank-two PSD covariance-factorization problem. Reaching the tube by that leading dynamics does not automatically prove that the exact DDPM trajectory does so. A successful random-entry argument needs quantitative control of the high-noise perturbation for the entire covariance-learning phase, anti-concentration of the inherited angular coordinate away from the three saddles, radial confinement during the subsequent phase, and a finite-sample perturbation estimate over its polynomially long duration if a shrinks with d.

The finite-horizon argument in C04 cannot simply be reused with a=d^(-c): it would generally raise inverse accuracy to an exponent growing with d. This is an exact limitation of that transfer route, not an SQ lower bound or a counterexample to Target 2. Centered-network GD also must not be silently substituted for unrestricted mean GD; centroid tracking is a separate step for that architecture.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:927c5b3c33a3e77790e962beb6c27b526ea19266a9216a8fffaa1f31512a5ffe","revision_digest":"sha256:6358af5f3329a32e1d2b356901f4f3070fb108844204377c1a6abd9890f04e4d","source_id":"own-work:T309-w721-C05-v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20T20:39:18.089313","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

Every such ray hits S_n, so sum_{x in S_n}q(x)=E|T_0 intersect S_n|>=P(T_0 nonempty). If a ray exists almost surely, the sum is at least 1 for every n and sup_{x in S_n}q(x)>=1/(8n). [Lemma lem:leading-chaos-local-variance of arXiv:2606.21006, 'Law of the Iterated Logarithm for Weighted Sums of Functionals of Long-Memory Gaussian Seq'] Let
\[
    S_{n,m}:=\frac{J_m}{m!}\sum_{t=1}^n a_tH_m(X_t).
\]
Assume \(((A1 of the paper))\), \(((A3 of the paper))\), and \(((A4 of the paper))\). Let \(m\ge1\) be fixed and suppose that
\(\alpha m<1\) and \(2d+\alpha m<1\).

Then for every sufficiently small \(\eta>0\) there exists \(C_\eta<\infty\) such that, 
for all sufficiently large \(N\) and all intervals \(I\subset\{N+1,\ldots,2N\}\),
\[
    \operatorname{Var}\left(
        \frac{J_m}{m!}\sum_{t\in I}a_tH_m(X_t)
    \right)
    \le
    C_\eta A_N^2
    \left(\frac{|I|}{N}\right)^{2-\alpha m-\eta}.
\]
In particular, \(\eta>0\) may be chosen so small that \(2-\alpha m-\eta>1\).

[Lemma 10 of arXiv:2605.09372, 'Sharp weighted norm estimates for martingale square functions'] For the principal sets introduced above, we have
\begin{enumerate}[\rm (a)]
\item  The sets $E(P):=P\cap\{\tau_{P}=\infty\}$, where $P\in \mathcal P$, are disjoint.
    
\smallskip

\item   For every $P\in\mathcal P$, $P\in \mathcal F_{\kappa_2(P)}$.
\smallskip

\item   For  every $P\in \bigcup_{m=2}^{\infty} \mathcal{P}_{m}$,
$$\Big(\sum_{\kappa_1(P)<i\leq \kappa_2(P)-1}\|\widehat W_{\kappa_1(P)}^{-1}d_i(W^{-\frac1p}f)\|_{\mathbb C^d}^2\Big)^{\frac12}\leq C_\gamma\mathbb E_{\kappa_1(P)}\|\widehat W_{\kappa_1(P)}^{-1}W^{-\frac1p}f\|_{\mathbb C^d}\,\,\, \mbox{on}\,\,\,P$$
and
$$\sup_{\kappa_1(P)<i\leq \kappa_2(P)-1}\|\widehat W_{\kappa_1(P)}^{-1} \mathbb E_{i}(W^{-\frac{1}{p}}f)\|_{\mathbb C^d}\leq C_\gamma\mathbb E_{\kappa_1(P)}\|\widehat  W_{\kappa_1(P)}^{-1}W^{-\frac{1}{p}}f\|_{\mathbb C^d}\,\,\, \mbox{on}\,\,\, P.$$

\item   For every $P\in \bigcup_{m=2}^{\infty} \mathcal{P}_{m}$, $$\Big(\sum_{i>\kappa_2(P)}\|\widehat W_{\kappa_2(P)}^{-1}d_i(W^{-\frac1p}f)\|_{\mathbb C^d}^2\Big)^{\frac12}\leq C_\gamma\mathbb E_{\kappa_2(P)}\|\widehat W_{\kappa_2(P)}^{-1}W^{-\frac1p}f\|_{\mathbb C^d}\quad \mbox{on}\quad E(P)$$
and
$$\sup_{i> \kappa_2(P)}\|\widehat  W_{\kappa_2(P)}^{-1} \mathbb E_{i}(W^{-1/p}f)\|_{\mathbb C^d}\leq C_\gamma\mathbb E_{\kappa_2(P)}\|\widehat  W_{\kappa_2(P)}^{-1}W^{-\frac{1}{p}}f\|_{\mathbb C^d}\quad \mbox{on}\quad E(P).$$

\smallskip

\item   For  every $P\in\bigcup_{m=2}^\infty\mathcal P_m$, we have
    $$\mathbb P(P)\leq 2\mathbb P(E(P))$$ and $$\chi_P\leq 2\mathbb E_{\kappa_2(P)}(\chi_{E(P)}).$$
\smallskip

\item  $\lim_{N\to \infty} \mathbb P(\bigcup_{P\in{\mathcal P}_N} P)=0.$
	\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Definition 5 of arXiv:2506.16259, 'Two-dimensional Rademacher walk'] Let $a_n\in \R_+$,  $n=1,2,\dots$. We call the sequence $\{a_n\}$ {\em good}, if for each large~$n$ there is a positive integer $K_n$ such that
$$
\frac{K_n}{\log_2 a_n}\to 1\text{ as }n\to\infty,
$$
and a subset  of $\{1,2,\dots,n\}$  with $K_n$ distinct elements, say $\{ i_1,i_2,\dots,i_{K_n}\}$, such that $i_{K_n}= n$ and $a_{i_{k+1}}\ge 2a_{i_{k}}$ for every $k=1,2,\dots,K_n-1$.

[Definition Active star of arXiv:2605.19835, 'Reemergence of the Epidemic Threshold in SIRS Infections on Connected Stars'] Let $k, \ell \in \mathOrText{\mathds{N}}_{\geq 1}$, and let~$G^\star$ be a \conStar{k}{\ell}.
    Moreover, let $\varepsilon \in \mathOrText{\mathds{R}}_{>0}$ be a constant, and let~$C$ be an SIRS process on a super-graph of~$G^\star$ (over $n \in \mathOrText{\mathds{N}}_{\geq 1}$ vertices) with infection rate $\lambda \in (0, 1]$ such that $\lambda \in \bigOmega{\ell^{-1/2+\varepsilon}}$ and with constant deimmunization rate $\varrho \in \mathOrText{\mathds{R}}_{> 0}$. Furthermore, let $c=\frac{\mathOrText{\varrho}}{4(2+\mathOrText{\varrho})}$, and let $d \in \mathOrText{\mathds{R}}_{>0}$ be the largest constant such that $d \leq c/7$ and $\eulerE^{-2d/c}\geq 1-\varepsilon/2$. For each star $s$ of~$G^\star$ and each time $t\in \mathOrText{\mathds{R}}_{\geq 0}$, let $I_{s,t}$ be the number of infected vertices of $s$ at time $t$. We say that $s$ is \emph{active} at time $t \in \mathOrText{\mathds{R}}_{> 0}$ if and only if there exists a time $t' \in \mathOrText{\mathds{R}}_{\leq t}$ such that $I_{s,t'} \geq \lambda d\ell$ and for all $t^* \in [t', t]$, we have $I_{s,t^*}>0$.

An affine algebraic set V is irreducible if it cannot be expressed as the union V = V_1 union V_2 of two proper algebraic subsets V_1, V_2 strictly contained in V. An algebraic set is irreducible if and only if its vanishing ideal I(V) is a prime ideal in the polynomial ring.
V is a non-empty affine algebraic set

body: Let A be an event depending on the states of a finite set of edges, and let omega be a configuration. The edge e is PIVOTAL for A at omega if the occurrence of A is decided by the state of e alone, that is if omega with e forced open lies in A and omega with e forced closed does not, or the reverse. Pivotality is a function of the states of the OTHER edges only, so the event {e is pivotal for A} is independent of the state of e - a fact used constantly and easy to forget. The INFLUENCE of e on A under P_p is I_e(A) = P_p( e is pivotal for A ). Under the uniform measure on the discrete cube this coincides with the usual influence P( f(X) != f(X with coordinate e flipped) ) for the indicator f of A. The total influence sum_e I_e(A) is, by Russo's formula, exactly the derivative of p -> P_p(A) for increasing A, which is why influences govern the sharpness of the phase transition; and by the Kahn-Kalai-Linial theorem the maximum influence of a balanced Boolean function on n coordinates is at least of order log n / n, which is the quantitative input behind sharp-threshold results. [standard; e.g. Grimmett, Percolation, 2nd ed., Section 2.4, and O'Donnell, Analysis of Boolean Functions, Chapter 2]

[Theorem cor:condensed-completeness of arXiv:2608.29708, 'Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians'] {bozic_models_1984}}] 
  Let
  $\FrameClass{\Box\text{-con}}$, $\FrameClass{\Box\text{-bri}}$,
  $\FrameClass{\Diamond\text{-con}}$, and $\FrameClass{\Diamond\text{-bri}}$
  be the classes of all $\Box$-condensed frames, $\Box$-brilliant frames, $\Diamond$-condensed frames, and $\Diamond$-brilliant frames, respectively.
  Then,
  \begin{align*}
    \textbf{iK}_\Box &= \set{ \varphi \in \mathscr{L}_\Box; \forall \mathfrak{F} \in \FrameClass{\Box\text{-con}} \cap \FrameClass{\Box\text{-bri}}\,\, (\mathfrak{F} \vDash^e \varphi) }, \\
    \textbf{iK}_\Diamond &= \set{ \varphi \in \mathscr{L}_\Diamond; \forall \mathfrak{F} \in \FrameClass{\Diamond\text{-con}} \cap \FrameClass{\Diamond\text{-bri}}\,\, (\mathfrak{F} \vDash^e \varphi) }.
  \end{align*}
  Consequently,
  as $\FrameClass{\Box{\text{-p}}} \supseteq \FrameClass{\Box\text{-con}} \supseteq \FrameClass{\Box\text{-con}} \cap \FrameClass{\Box\text{-bri}}$,
  we have $\textbf{iK}_\Box = \set{ \varphi \in \mathscr{L}_\Box; \forall \mathfrak{F} \in \FrameClass{\Box\text{-con}}\,\, (\mathfrak{F} \vDash^e \varphi) }$,
  and
  as $\FrameClass{\Diamond{\text{-p}}} \supseteq \FrameClass{\Diamond\text{-con}} \supseteq \FrameClass{\Diamond\text{-con}} \cap \FrameClass{\Diamond\text{-bri}}$,
  we have $\textbf{iK}_\Diamond = \set{ \varphi \in \mathscr{L}_\Diamond; \forall \mathfrak{F} \in \FrameClass{\Diamond\text{-con}}\,\, (\mathfrak{F} \vDash^e \varphi) }$.
  \begin{proof}
    For the convenience, let $\heartsuit \in \set{\Box, \Diamond}$.
    ($\subseteq$)
    Trivial from Theorem (thm:ikb-ikd-completeness of the paper) and $\FrameClass{\heartsuit\text{-p}} \supseteq \FrameClass{\heartsuit\text{-con}} \cap \FrameClass{\heartsuit\text{-bri}}$.
    ($\supseteq$)
    If $\textbf{iK}_\heartsuit \nvdash \varphi$,
    then by Theorem (thm:ikb-ikd-completeness of the paper), we have a $\heartsuit$-p model that falsifies $\varphi$.
    We condense it to obtain a $\heartsuit$-condensed and $\heartsuit$-brilliant model,
    which also falsifies $\varphi$ by Proposition (prop:condensation of the paper).
  \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Let $(X, \mathcal{B}, \mu, T)$ be a probability-preserving system. For a finite (or countable, with finite entropy) measurable partition $\xi = \{A_1, \dots, A_k\}$ put $H_\mu(\xi) = -\sum_i \mu(A_i) \log \mu(A_i)$ (with $0 \log 0 = 0$), and $\xi^n_0 = \bigvee_{j=0}^{n-1} T^{-j}\xi$, the partition into sets $A_{i_0} \cap T^{-1}A_{i_1} \cap \dots \cap T^{-(n-1)}A_{i_{n-1}}$ (the $n$-step itineraries). The entropy of $T$ relative to $\xi$ is $h_\mu(T, \xi) = \lim_{n\to\infty} \frac1n H_\mu(\xi^n_0)$ (the limit exists because $n \mapsto H_\mu(\xi^n_0)$ is subadditive; it also equals $\inf_n \frac1n H_\mu(\xi^n_0)$ and $\lim_n H_\mu(\xi \mid \xi^n_1)$). The Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy is $h_\mu(T) = \sup_\xi h_\mu(T, \xi)$ over finite partitions, in $[0, \infty]$. Facts used constantly: $h_\mu(T, \xi) \le H_\mu(\xi) \le \log k$; $h_\mu(T, \xi) \le h_\mu(T, \eta) + H_\mu(\xi \mid \eta)$ for partitions $\xi, \eta$; $h_\mu(T^m) = m\, h_\mu(T)$ for $m \ge 1$; the Kolmogorov-Sinai generator theorem: if $\xi$ is a generator ($\bigvee_{j \ge 0} T^{-j}\xi$ generates $\mathcal{B}$ mod $\mu$, or $\bigvee_{j\in\mathbb{Z}}$ for invertible $T$) then $h_\mu(T) = h_\mu(T, \xi)$; and if $\xi_m$ is an increasing sequence of partitions generating $\mathcal{B}$ then $h_\mu(T, \xi_m) \uparrow h_\mu(T)$. On a compact metric space, finite Borel partitions $\xi_m$ with $\mathrm{diam}(\xi_m) \to 0$ also give $h_\mu(T, \xi_m) \to h_\mu(T)$ (for every finite partition $\eta$, $H_\mu(\eta \mid \xi_m) \to 0$), but not monotonically in general, since such partitions need not refine one another. The map $\mu \mapsto h_\mu(T)$ on invariant measures is affine, but it is NOT in general continuous or even upper semicontinuous in the weak* topology; upper semicontinuity holds when $T$ is expansive (and for $C^\infty$ maps of compact manifolds by Newhouse), which is what guarantees measures of maximal entropy exist in those cases.
mu is a T-invariant probability measure
partitions are finite or have finite static entropy

Own-work draft; T419-C025 v1, proof (unaudited), no novelty claimed. Let r>=1, m,p>=r be arbitrary integers and Delta any real m-by-p matrix of rank exactly r, with all nonzero singular values equal to1. Let any s>0 and 0<rho<1. Define

 d=rho/2, a=d/(10r^(3/2)), b=sqrt(rp/d),
 Kbar=sqrt(r)(s^2 b^2+1+4sqrt(r)).

Initialize B0=0 and A0=sG where G is r-by-p with independent standard Gaussian entries. For any one fixed eta with

 0<eta<=1/(6Kbar+1),

ordinary simultaneous GD on ||BA-Delta||F^2/2 satisfies, with probability at least1-rho, for every integer t>=1,

 ||B_t A_t-Delta||F <=sqrt(r) exp[-eta^3 s^4 a^4(t-1)/(8Kbar)].

For every 0<eps<sqrt(r), a sufficient time is

 1+ceil[(8Kbar/(eta^3 s^4 a^4))log(sqrt(r)/eps)].

The success event and the fixed step are independent of requested accuracy. This covers every positive Gaussian scale, every rank and every input/output aspect ratio, including all proper bottlenecks m,p>r. It covers condition number1, not arbitrary target spectra. No expected-risk or finite-sample claim is included. The rate is deliberately conservative; independent proof audit and any novelty judgment remain pending.
