body:
STATUS: proof (unaudited), own-work draft. For the coupled scalar two-token joint-head factored-attention logistic gradient flow, every nonzero-imbalance leaf k^2-q^2=C has a unique reduced saddle and two escaping basins. In full R^3 almost every initialization escapes with kq,v of matching infinite sign, factors O(sqrt(log |v|)), head-normalized limit +/-e_v and margin Gamma_+ or Gamma_-. The finite saddle-stable set plus balanced planes is null. Balanced k=-q, v>0 and max root<kq<0 instead collapse to uniform attention and margin min a_i, showing an actual third fate on a null surface.

# Target 1: almost-everywhere full-space factored gradient-flow classification

Version 1, proof unaudited. Own work; novelty unestablished.
This concerns continuous gradient flow, not arbitrary-step GD.

## Statement

For n>=2, b_i,kappa_i>0, 0<a_i<b_i, set
h_i(s)=a_i+b_i tanh(kappa_i s) and
L(v,k,q)=mean_i log(1+exp(-v h_i(kq))).
Let p_bar be the unique zero of mean_i h_i. For every initial point with
C=k^2-q^2!=0, the Euclidean gradient flow exists globally forward and has
exactly one of these outcomes:

1. convergence to a finite point on the stationary curve v=0,kq=p_bar;
2. v,kq->+infinity, loss->0, normalized direction (v,k,q)/norm ->(1,0,0);
3. v,kq->-infinity, loss->0, normalized direction ->(-1,0,0).

The set in outcome 1, together with the excluded balanced surfaces C=0,
has three-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero. Hence almost every finite
initialization belongs to one of the two escaping basins. Both basins
are open in the FULL parameter space, are nonempty, and have respective
normalized minimum margins Gamma_+=min_i(a_i+b_i) and Gamma_-=min_i(b_i-a_i).
The second is strictly inferior, as in claim 010. The known imbalance
invariant is used for reduction, not claimed as a new result.

We do not classify trajectories on C=0 in this theorem. They really allow
another fate: on k=q=0, v solves v_dot=mean_i a_i/(1+exp(v a_i))>0,
so v->infinity and L->0 while attention stays uniform. In fact a relatively
open subset of the balanced plane has this fate: if k=-q!=0, v>0 and
R<kq<0, where R=max_i rho_i<0, then v increases, s increases toward zero,
and k,q tend to zero. To check this, all h_i(s)>=c>0, forcing v->infinity.
If s tended to a strictly negative limit, alpha=2|s| and all h_i' would
be bounded below there; ds/dv>=c_1 v would contradict bounded s. Thus
s->0 and both factors vanish. Its normalized margin is min_i a_i.
These null sets demonstrate why the almost-everywhere qualification
must not be omitted.

## Reduction and global existence

Put s=kq, F=mean_i g_i h_i(s), G=mean_i g_i h_i'(s)>0,
g_i=(1+exp(v h_i(s)))^-1. Flow equations are

 v_dot=F, k_dot=vqG, q_dot=vkG.

Differentiating gives d(k^2-q^2)/dt=0. Also
(k^2+q^2)^2=C^2+4s^2. Thus on a fixed nonzero-C leaf,

 v_dot=F(v,s), s_dot=alpha_C(s) vG(v,s),
 alpha_C(s)=sqrt(C^2+4s^2)>0.

If H=max_i(a_i+b_i), M=max_i b_i kappa_i, then |v_dot|<=H.
On any finite time interval v is bounded, and
|k_dot|+|q_dot|<=M|v|(|k|+|q|). Gronwall gives finite factors on that
interval. The smooth full flow therefore has no finite-time blow-up,
in either time direction. Nonzero-C leaf coordinates are global charts on
each sheet: for C>0 fix sign k, solve
k=sign(k)sqrt((alpha_C(s)+C)/2), q=s/k;
for C<0 instead fix sign q and use the symmetric formula.

## Leaf saddle and trapping

Let A=H^2/4 and F_0(s)=F(0,s)=mean_i h_i(s)/2. Then
-A<=F_v<=0, F_0 strictly increases with unique zero p_bar, and G>0.
The sole reduced equilibrium is (0,p_bar), corresponding to one point
on each sheet. With u=s-p_bar, the two good quadrants v,u>0 and v,u<0
are forward invariant: s_dot has sign v; on the boundary v=0 the vector
field F_0(s) points into the respective quadrant. More explicitly, in
the positive quadrant v_dot>=-A v, so a strictly positive v cannot hit zero
in finite time, and u increases. Reflection treats the negative quadrant.

In a bad quadrant v>0,u<0, F(v,s)<=F_0(s)<0 and s_dot>0.
Both coordinates move monotonically toward their axes until one axis is
crossed or the orbit stays forever. Crossing an axis enters a good quadrant;
uniqueness excludes hitting the equilibrium in finite time. If the orbit
stays in the bad quadrant, it has a finite limit. Continuity and monotonicity
force F=alpha_C vG=0 at that limit, hence it is the saddle.
The other bad quadrant is handled by the reflected links -h_i(-s).
Nonstationary points on an axis enter a good quadrant immediately.

## Escape from good quadrants

Consider the positive quadrant. Then s increases from s_0>p_bar.
Suppose s tends to finite P. If v is bounded, compactness and
alpha_C G>0 imply integral_0^infinity v(t)dt<infinity.
Since |v_dot|<=H, the nonnegative function v is uniformly continuous;
the elementary disjoint-triangle argument gives v->0. But then
v_dot->F_0(P)>0, contradiction.

If v is unbounded, put R=max_i rho_i, h_i(rho_i)=0. If P<=R,
an example j with root R has h_j(s(t))<=0, hence g_j>=1/2;
on the compact s interval its derivative is >=d>0. Consequently
s_dot>=|C| d v/(2n). A finite P again implies integral v<infinity
and, by the same bounded-derivative argument, v->0: contradiction.
If P>R, eventually all h_i>=c>0. Then v increases without bound and

 ds/dv=alpha_C(s) v (mean g_i h_i')/(mean g_i h_i)
       >=|C| d v/H,

contradicting finite P. Thus s->infinity. Eventually all h_i>=c>0;
v increases and cannot remain bounded, since bounded v keeps every g_i
bounded below. Therefore v->infinity. Reflection proves negative escape.

For the direction, let kappa_0=min_i kappa_i. On the positive tail,
alpha_C(s)<=|C|+2s and

 ds/dv<=(4M/c)(|C|+2s)v exp(-2kappa_0 s).

Thus d[exp(kappa_0 s)]/dv <=C_1 v, because
(|C|+2s)exp(-kappa_0 s) is bounded on the positive tail.
Integration gives s=O(log v). Since k^2+q^2=alpha_C(s), both
factors are O(sqrt(log v)) and are negligible relative to v.
The negative branch is identical after reflection. Endpoint margin and
zero-loss limits follow. By fixed C and |s|->infinity, both |k| and |q|
also tend to infinity (their squared difference is constant).

## Leaf-null implies full-space-null

At the reduced equilibrium the linearization is

 [[-A_s,B_s],[alpha_C(p_bar) B_s,0]],
 A_s=mean h_i(p_bar)^2/4, B_s=mean h_i'(p_bar)/2>0.

Its determinant is negative; it is a hyperbolic saddle. The local stable
manifold is one-dimensional. The global stable set on a leaf is contained
in its countably many backward integer-time flow images, so is planar null;
the flow is a smooth local diffeomorphism (indeed globally defined here).

The full stationary curve E={v=0,kq=p_bar} is closed. The set
S={initial points whose distance to E tends to zero} is Borel: express
the limiting condition using countable thresholds and integer times.
For C!=0 our classification shows S is exactly the convergent set;
the leaf coordinate formulas also show convergence of k,q when s->p_bar.
Use coordinates (v,s,C) on the four open regions C>0,sign k fixed and
C<0,sign q fixed. Each coordinate map is a smooth diffeomorphism.
Every fixed-C slice of S is planar null by the preceding argument.
Fubini gives a null set in these coordinates; local diffeomorphisms
preserve null sets under a countable cover. Finally C=0 is the union of
the two planes k=q and k=-q, also null. This proves the asserted full-space
almost-everywhere dichotomy, without assuming independence across examples.

The escaping basins are open even at balanced initial points: any escaping
orbit eventually enters a strict region v>0,s>max(R,0) or v<0,s<min rho_i.
Those regions are invariant and escape, also when C=0, by the same proof
with alpha=2|s| bounded below there. (Requiring s>0 on the positive branch
is essential; a balanced negative product can instead collapse to zero.)
The union of their finite-time preimages
is open. For arbitrary escaping points the converse follows from divergence
of s. They are nonempty by claim 010's sign regions. No assertion that every
balanced trajectory escapes is needed.

## Literature scope and remaining obstruction

The comparisons in proof 008 apply: 2308.16898 and 2403.08699 treat
fixed-head factored attention, while this is the stated scalar joint-head
logistic family. The balance reduction is standard and is not a novelty claim.
For simultaneous GD, C_+=(1-eta^2 v^2 G^2)C, so these invariant leaves
are unavailable. Extending this full-space result to GD remains open here;
claim 010 proves only its arbitrary-step open sign basins.
n>=2, 0<a_i<b_i, b_i,kappa_i>0, h_i(s)=a_i+b_i tanh(kappa_i s), average logistic loss, continuous Euclidean gradient flow in (v,k,q). Complete leaf classification only for C!=0; open escaping basins in full space; no discrete full-space assertion.

interval. The smooth full flow therefore has no finite-time blow-up,
in either time direction. Nonzero-C leaf coordinates are global charts on
each sheet: for C>0 fix sign k, solve
k=sign(k)sqrt((alpha_C(s)+C)/2), q=s/k;
for C<0 instead fix sign q and use the symmetric formula.

## Leaf saddle and trapping

Let A=H^2/4 and F_0(s)=F(0,s)=mean_i h_i(s)/2. Then
-A<=F_v<=0, F_0 strictly increases with unique zero p_bar, and G>0.
The sole reduced equilibrium is (0,p_bar), corresponding to one point
on each sheet. With u=s-p_bar, the two good quadrants v,u>0 and v,u<0
are forward invariant: s_dot has sign v; on the boundary v=0 the vector
field F_0(s) points into the respective quadrant. More explicitly, in
the positive quadrant v_dot>=-A v, so a strictly positive v cannot hit zero
in finite time, and u increases. Reflection treats the negative quadrant.

In a bad quadrant v>0,u<0, F(v,s)<=F_0(s)<0 and s_dot>0.
Both coordinates move monotonically toward their axes until one axis is
crossed or the orbit stays forever. Crossing an axis enters a good quadrant;
uniqueness excludes hitting the equilibrium in finite time. If the orbit
stays in the bad quadrant, it has a finite limit. Continuity and monotonicity
force F=alpha_C vG=0 at that limit, hence it is the saddle.
The other bad quadrant is handled by the reflected links -h_i(-s).
Nonstationary points on an axis enter a good quadrant immediately.

## Escape from good quadrants

Consider the positive quadrant. Then s increases from s_0>p_bar.
Suppose s tends to finite P. If v is bounded, compactness and
alpha_C G>0 imply integral_0^infinity v(t)dt<infinity.
Since |v_dot|<=H, the nonnegative function v is uniformly continuous;
the elementary disjoint-triangle argument gives v->0. But then
v_dot->F_0(P)>0, contradiction.

If v is unbounded, put R=max_i rho_i, h_i(rho_i)=0. If P<=R,
an example j with root R has h_j(s(t))<=0, hence g_j>=1/2;
on the compact s interval its derivative is >=d>0. Consequently
s_dot>=|C| d v/(2n). A finite P again implies integral v<infinity
and, by the same bounded-derivative argument, v->0: contradiction.
If P>R, eventually all h_i>=c>0. Then v increases without bound and

 ds/dv=alpha_C(s) v (mean g_i h_i')/(mean g_i h_i)
       >=|C| d v/H,

contradicting finite P. Thus s->infinity. Eventually all h_i>=c>0;
v increases and cannot remain bounded, since bounded v keeps every g_i
bounded below. Therefore v->infinity. Reflection proves negative escape.

For the direction, let kappa_0=min_i kappa_i. On the positive tail,
alpha_C(s)<=|C|+2s and

 ds/dv<=(4M/c)(|C|+2s)v exp(-2kappa_0 s).

Thus d[exp(kappa_0 s)]/dv <=C_1 v, because
(|C|+2s)exp(-kappa_0 s) is bounded on the positive tail.
Integration gives s=O(log v). Since k^2+q^2=alpha_C(s), both
factors are O(sqrt(log v)) and are negligible relative to v.
The negative branch is identical after reflection. Endpoint margin and
zero-loss limits follow. By fixed C and |s|->infinity, both |k| and |q|
also tend to infinity (their squared difference is constant).

## Leaf-null implies full-space-null

At the reduced equilibrium the linearization is

 [[-A_s,B_s],[alpha_C(p_bar) B_s,0]],
 A_s=mean h_i(p_bar)^2/4, B_s=mean h_i'(p_bar)/2>0.

Its determinant is negative; it is a hyperbolic saddle. The local stable
manifold is one-dimensional. The global stable set on a leaf is contained
in its countably many backward integer-time flow images, so is planar null;
the flow is a smooth local diffeomorphism (indeed globally defined here).

The full stationary curve E={v=0,kq=p_bar} is closed. The set
S={initial points whose distance to E tends to zero} is Borel: express
the limiting condition using countable thresholds and integer times.
For C!=0 our classification shows S is exactly the convergent set;
the leaf coordinate formulas also show convergence of k,q when s->p_bar.
Use coordinates (v,s,C) on the four open regions C>0,sign k fixed and
C<0,sign q fixed. Each coordinate map is a smooth diffeomorphism.
Every fixed-C slice of S is planar null by the preceding argument.
Fubini gives a null set in these coordinates; local diffeomorphisms
preserve null sets under a countable cover. Finally C=0 is the union of
the two planes k=q and k=-q, also null. This proves the asserted full-space
almost-everywhere dichotomy, without assuming independence across examples.

The escaping basins are open even at balanced initial points: any escaping
orbit eventually enters a strict region v>0,s>max(R,0) or v<0,s<min rho_i.
Those regions are invariant and escape, also when C=0, by the same proof
with alpha=2|s| bounded below there. (Requiring s>0 on the positive branch
is essential; a balanced negative product can instead collapse to zero.)
The union of their finite-time preimages
is open. For arbitrary escaping points the converse follows from divergence
of s. They are nonempty by claim 010's sign regions. No assertion that every
balanced trajectory escapes is needed.

## Literature scope and remaining obstruction

The comparisons in proof 008 apply: 2308.16898 and 2403.08699 treat
fixed-head factored attention, while this is the stated scalar joint-head
logistic family. The balance reduction is standard and is not a novelty claim.
For simultaneous GD, C_+=(1-eta^2 v^2 G^2)C, so these invariant leaves
are unavailable. Extending this full-space result to GD remains open here;
claim 010 proves only its arbitrary-step open sign basins.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:b8deca6bc27f7f10bba8a04757e53f969a578e99c19740be9e734a928aa0de72","revision_digest":"sha256:65ea29b518db264e147ffc601a13037ce84230f2e321f234075bb47770924c02","source_id":"owner:T328:w698:claim-012:v1","source_revision":"2026-10-20 v1, unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

[Proposition 34 (Bulk confinement and one-outlier alternative) of arXiv:2608.07820, 'Linear Spectral Statistics for Entrywise-Transformed Spiked Wigner Matrices under Shifted '] Let \(M_N\) denote either \(M_N^{(4)}\) or \(M_N^f\).  For every fixed
\(\delta>0\), all but possibly one eigenvalue of \(M_N\) lie in
\([-2-\delta,2+\delta]\) with probability \(1-o(1)\).  More precisely:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
\item if \(|\theta|\le1\), then
\(\spec(M_N)\subset[-2-\delta,2+\delta]\) with probability \(1-o(1)\);
\item if \(|\theta|>1\), then there is one eigenvalue on the side determined
by \(\theta\) such that
\begin{equation}
 \lambda_{\rm out}(M_N)\longrightarrow
 \rho_\theta=\theta+\theta^{-1}.
\end{equation}
All remaining eigenvalues lie in \([-2-\delta,2+\delta]\).  In particular,
if \(0<\delta<|\rho_\theta|-2\), the outlier is the unique eigenvalue outside
that interval with probability \(1-o(1)\).
\end{enumerate}

Fix -1<a<1 and sigma_a(t)=t for t>=0, sigma_a(t)=a*t for t<0, applied coordinatewise. A depth-L network has L affine layers, activation after the first L-1 layers, and an affine final output. Its squared parameter cost is sum_ell (||W_ell||_F^2+||b_ell||_2^2). For a function f and domain Omega, R_L is the infimum of this cost over all such finite-width networks equal to f on Omega; R_L=+infinity if the class is empty. Let Omega be a nonempty bounded open subset of R^d. Suppose f=g composed with h on Omega, where h:R^d->R^k and g:R^k->R^m are continuous finite piecewise-affine functions and k>=1. Translate h by a constant vector so h(Omega) lies in the strictly positive orthant, and compensate the input of g. There exist fixed finite depths L_h,L_g and finite constant B, independent of L, such that for every integer L>=L_h+L_g, R_L<=B+k*(L-L_h-L_g). Here B is the total squared parameter cost of fixed networks realizing the translated factors. Hence limsup_(L->infinity) R_L/L<=k. For k=0, the corresponding factorization means f is constant on Omega; using zero weights and the final output bias gives R_L<=||f||_2^2 for every L. A prescribed-width version requires widths sufficient for the fixed end subnetworks and width at least k in the middle; arbitrary narrow architectures are excluded.

A homogeneous linear equation c_1 x_1 + c_2 x_2 + ... + c_k x_k = 0 with integer coefficients is partition regular over the positive integers if for every finite coloring of the positive integers N, there exists a solution (x_1, ..., x_k) in N^k where all x_i have the same color.

k >= 2

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.03821, 'Condensation and Metastability in the Supercritical Two-Species Zero-Range Process via...'] In this article, we investigate the two-species zero-range process, a multi-species generalization of the classical zero-range process. First, we analyze its condensation regime, which directly parallels its single-species counterpart. As our main result, we establish the dynamical metastable behavior of the location of the single condensate, showing that its motion is governed by a simple Markov chain on the accelerated time scale $N^{1+\alpha}$, where $N$ denotes the total number of particles in the system and the parameter $\alpha>1$ governs the attractivity of the system. Another novelty of this work lies in the proof technique, which integrates the recently developed resolvent approach with the $H^{1}$-approximation method to rigorously characterize metastability.

body: [Example 2.7 of arXiv:2110.05374, 'When Janson meets McDiarmid: Bounded difference inequalities under graph-dependence'] Let (X_1, X_2, X_3) be dependent random variables with K_3 as their dependency graph, and let (X_i)_{4≤i≤9} be independent random variables that are also independent of (X_1, X_2, X_3). Then the vertex-disjoint union G of K_3 and 6 copies of K_1 is a dependency graph for (X_i)_{i∈[9]}. If every X_i takes values in a real interval of length c ≥ 0, then for every t > 0 Janson's inequality (Theorem 1.4 of the paper, with χ_f(G) = 3) gives P(Σ_{i∈[9]} X_i − E[Σ_{i∈[9]} X_i] ≥ t) ≤ exp(−2t²/(27c²)), while Corollary 2.6 gives the better bound P(Σ_{i∈[9]} X_i − E[Σ_{i∈[9]} X_i] ≥ t) ≤ exp(−8t²/(81c²)). The second bound uses the fractional forest vertex cover with weight 1/2 on each of F_1 = {1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7}, F_2 = {1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9} and F_3 = {2, 3, 6, 7, 8, 9}: each G[F_k] is K_2 plus 4 copies of K_1, so (Σ_k w_k √(Σ_{{i,j}∈E(G[F_k])} (c_i + c_j)² + Σ_{T∈T(F_k)} c_{min,k,T}²))² = ((3c/2)·√(2² + 1 + 4))² = 81c²/4.

[Proposition prop:gen_dissip of arXiv:2609.03164, 'Energy Decay Induced by Localized Coercivity in the 3D Navier--Stokes Equations'] For every $\rho\in\mathcal P$, the operator $A(\rho)$ generates a
$\mathcal C_0$-semigroup $(e^{tA(\rho)})_{t\ge0}$ on $H$ and satisfies
\[
\|e^{tA(\rho)}\|_{\mathcal L(H)}\le1,\qquad \forall t\ge0.
\]
If there exists $\alpha_\omega>0$ such that
\begin{equation}

-\langle A(\rho)v,v\rangle_H \ge \alpha_\omega\|v\|_H^2,
\qquad \forall v\in D(A_0),
\end{equation}
uniformly for $\rho\in\mathcal P$, then
\[
\|e^{tA(\rho)}\|_{\mathcal L(H)}\le e^{-\alpha_\omega t},
\qquad \forall t\ge0,
\]
uniformly in $\rho$.

OPEN per arXiv:2609.02820v1 (Theorems 1.5–1.6, PDF pp.5–6); bounded later-work check found no settlement. In the critical iid particle–hole model on Z^4, particles take synchronous discrete-time simple random-walk steps and settle permanently into stationary holes. After immediate cancellation the iid integer-valued excess η is nonconstant, has mean zero and an exponential moment. Does P(the origin is strictly closer in ℓ1 distance to an unfilled hole than to an active particle at time t) tend to zero for every such law? The source proves yes for d≤3 and exhibits counterexamples for d≥5 with P(η=1)=P(η=−1)=p and P(η=0)=1−2p. It explicitly says simulations suggest this counterexample extends to d=4. This general particle–hole question is distinct from the original binary one-car-or-one-spot parking initial law. Novelty: KNOWN source gap; current openness not certified by zero indexed citations.

For any \( \eta >0 \) (if $Q-1/H>0$, we further require $\eta<Q-1/H$), there exists a positive constant \( C = C(a, b, M, Q, H, \mathcal{V}, \eta) \) such that
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{P}\Big(Y([a,b])\cap A\neq\emptyset\Big)~\leqslant C\ \mathrm{Cap}_{Q-1/H-\eta}(A)
\end{equation}for all compact sets \( A \subseteq B_d(o, M) \).
title: Theorem 44 of arXiv:2512.07202

body: [Lemma 19 (Aperiodicity of the minimal set) of arXiv:2607.20838, 'Long-memory Markov chains with power-law intensities'] Let $\mathrm{CM}(\Psi)$ be the deterministic control model associated with our nonlinear state-space model, and let $M = \overline{A_+((\xi,\gamma))}$ be the closure of the forward reachable set from the globally attracting state $(\xi,\gamma)$. Then $M$ is aperiodic.

body: For any integers r, s >= 1, every sequence of more than (r-1)(s-1) distinct real numbers contains either an increasing subsequence of length r or a decreasing subsequence of length s. The bound is sharp: there exist sequences of exactly (r-1)(s-1) distinct reals with no increasing subsequence of length r and no decreasing subsequence of length s. [Erdos and Szekeres (1935); see Bollobas, Combinatorics]
title: Erdos-Szekeres Theorem (Monotone Subsequences)

body:
[Lemma 8 (Affine spline loader) of arXiv:2608.31157, 'Sharp Approximation Rates for Neural Networks with Affine Latent Parameterizations'] Let $S\in\N^+$ and
$\bmy=(y_0,\ldots,y_{S-1})\in\R^S$.  There exist an architecture
$\Phi^{\mathrm{spl}}\in\Arch(5,2S+2)$ and an affine map
$\calA^{\mathrm{spl}}\in\aff(S,P_{\Phi^{\mathrm{spl}}})$, both independent of
$\bmy$, such that, after setting
\[
 \bmtheta:=\calA^{\mathrm{spl}}(\bmy),
\]
one has
\[
 \Phi^{\mathrm{spl}}_{\bmtheta}(m)=y_m,
 \qquad m=0,\ldots,S-1.
\]
Every target-dependent slot depends on at most three consecutive entries of
$\bmy$.

body:
[Proposition 1 (Dynamical fluctuation expansion) of arXiv:2604.04100, '\LARGE Learning Equilibrium Fluctuation Expansions from Overdamped Langevin Dynamics'] Let  $\varepsilon\in (0,1)$ and assume that $X_\varepsilon$ is the solution of \eqref{SDE-0}  with initial data $\xi_{\varepsilon}$ satisfying Assumption \ref{A1}. Let $(\bar{X}_m)_{0\leq m\leq n}$ be the solution of \eqref{eq-barX0-intro}, \eqref{eq-barX1-intro}, \eqref{eq-barXm-intro}, respectively. We define the remainder terms as $$
w_{\varepsilon,m}(t)
:=\frac{X_\varepsilon(t)-\sum_{k=0}^{m}\varepsilon^{k/2}\bar X_k(t)}{\varepsilon^{m/2}},
\qquad 0\le m\le n,\,\,t>0.
$$ 
Then for each $p\ge1$ and $t>0$, there exists a constant $C(p,t,n)>0$, independent of $\varepsilon$, such that for all $m=0,1,\cdots,n$,
\begin{equation*}
	\mathbb{E}\bigl|w_{\varepsilon,m}(t)\bigr|^{2p}\leq C(p,t,n)\varepsilon^{p}.
\end{equation*} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Dynamical fluctuation expansion

body: [ESTABLISHED 09-08 08:2x, REOPENS a closure I had published] Erdos-Kahane at fixed lambda = 2/3 is LIVE, not closed. By EXACT cell enumeration (no Monte Carlo) a run-pattern-aware cost gives R E[e^-2cost] decaying at R^-0.28, monotonically at every N from 11 to 30 (factor 9.1 over 19 octaves), while the per-symbol cost GROWS at R^+0.11 on identical machinery; truth is R^-0.79. The crossover is at ORDER TWO - blocks of <=2 consecutive jump symbols already decay - so the structural argument for closure ('any decaying cost must encode the cylinder geometry and is computing the integral') is false: that cost is strictly local, finite-order, combinatorial, and sits 3e5 above the true energy. The count x measure = 1 identity stands; the obstruction moves from the counting step to the FREE ENERGY of the digit process, which is not iid. Not a proof - nested octaves, sign carried by strict monotonicity. The closure report named this exact falsifier and did not run it

    $$\|D^m f(0)\| \geq \delta \quad \text{and} \quad \sup_{t \in \Delta^K(1)} \|D^{m+1} f(t)\| \leq M\,.$$

    $$\|f\|_{L^2(\Delta^K(1))} \geq C(K,m)\delta^{K/2+m+1}M^{-K/2-m} \,.$$

[Theorem 11 of arXiv:2609.03238, 'Representation Defects and Cassels Pairings for Congruent Number Curves'] Assume \eqref{eq:layer}.  The value $\Pi_2(p,q)$ is independent of the auxiliary
primitive solutions above.  The equality
\[
\Pi_2(p,q)=1
\]
holds if and only if
\[
2pq\text{ is noncongruent}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\Sha(E_{2pq})[2^\infty]\cong(\Z/2\Z)^4.
\]
Furthermore,
\begin{equation}
\frac{r_s(pq)-r_t(pq)}{32}\equiv\Pi_2(p,q)\pmod2,
\end{equation}
and therefore
\begin{equation}
r_s(pq)\equiv h(-2pq)+16\Pi_2(p,q)\pmod{32}.
\end{equation}

[Corollary 27 of arXiv:2605.02002, 'Glauber dynamics for random field Ising models on bounded degree graphs and MLSI'] Under the same assumption in Proposition \ref{proposition672}, with $\mathbb{P}_h$-probability at least $1-O_{\beta,\Delta,p_0}(\frac{1}{|V|})$, the edge field denoising process $(Y_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$ satisfies $R$- approximate conservation of variance up to time $\theta_*$ with constant 
    $$
R\leq\exp\left(\frac{16\beta\Delta\ln|V|}{\alpha_*}\right).
    $$
    Moreover, the RFIM measure $\mu_G$ satisfies approximate tensorization of variance with constant $R$.

body:
[Theorem 109 (Primitive--PBW boundary beyond finite depth) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Let finite-dimensional ancestry shells $G_m$ have cumulative rank
$M(x)=\sum_{m\le x}\dim G_m$, let $w_m\downarrow0$, and let
$T=\mathscr S(\bigoplus_m w_mI_{G_m})\mathscr S^*$ with
$\mathscr S^*\mathscr S=I+$compact.  If
\[
 M(x)\sim Ax^\delta(\log x)^\gamma,
 \qquad
 w_m\sim cm^{-\alpha}(\log m)^\eta,
\]
then, with $p=\delta/\alpha$ and $\theta=\gamma+p\eta$,
\[
 \mathcal N_T(R)
 \sim Ac^p\alpha^{-\theta}e^{pR}R^\theta.
\]
The corresponding real Mellin and Fredholm laws follow from
\Cref{cc:thm:regular-dictionary}.  For an exponentially attenuated free tower
on $q\ge2$ generators, the primitive zeta function has a logarithmic branch at
$p_0=(\log q)/\kappa_0$, whereas the PBW tower has a simple pole and its
$k$-fold tensor power has a pole of order $k$:
\[
 \zeta_{\rm prim}(p_0+\varepsilon)=\log(1/\varepsilon)+O(1),
 \qquad
 \zeta_{\rm PBW}(z)=\frac1{1-qe^{-\kappa_0z}}.
\]
The lattice spectrum generally produces log-periodic counting oscillations.

body:
[Corollaryen 7 (Exact anchored minibatch envelope) of arXiv:2608.18999, '2608.18999'] Let \(H\) be a nonzero real Hilbert space, let \(1<p\le2\), let \(n\ge1\), and let
\(X_1,\ldots,X_n\) be independent copies of an \(H\)-valued random vector
with mean \(\mu\).  Fix a deterministic anchor \(a\in H\), \(\tau>0\),
and assume
\[
M_a=\E\norm{X_1-a}^p<\infty.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat\mu_{a,\tau}
=a+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n C_\tau(X_i-a).
\]
Then, for every \(\alpha,\beta\ge0\),
\begin{equation}
\alpha\norm{\E\widehat\mu_{a,\tau}-\mu}
+\frac\beta\tau
\E\norm{\widehat\mu_{a,\tau}
         -\E\widehat\mu_{a,\tau}}^2
\le
K_p\!\left(\alpha,\frac\beta n\right)
\tau^{1-p}M_a.
\end{equation}
The constant is the smallest possible uniform constant over this class, and
its phase boundary is \(\alpha=p\beta/n\).

body:
[Lemma smash-lQ of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Let $G$ be a compact Lie group, and let ${\mathcal{F}}_1,{\mathcal{F}}_2$ be families of closed subgroups. Then
    \begin{equation}
        {-}\smashp{-}\colon (\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*)_{{\mathcal{F}}_1}\times(\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*)_{{\mathcal{F}}_2}\to(\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*)_{{\mathcal{F}}_1\cap{\mathcal{F}}_2}.
    \end{equation}
    is a left Quillen bifunctor for the model structures as indiciated.
    \begin{proof}
        Write ${\mathcal{F}}_1\times{\mathcal{F}}_2$ for the family of closed subgroups $K\subset G\times G$ such that there exist $H_1\in{\mathcal{F}}_1,H_2\in{\mathcal{F}}_2$ with $K\subset H_1\times H_2$. Then $((eq:smash-equiv of the paper))$ factors as
        \[
            (\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*)_{{\mathcal{F}}_1}\times(\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*)_{{\mathcal{F}}_2}
            \xrightarrow{\;{-}\smashp{-}\;}\big(\cat{$\bm{(G\times G)}$-Top}_*\big){}_{{\mathcal{F}}_1\times{\mathcal{F}}_2}
            \xrightarrow{\;\Delta^*\;}(\textbf{\textup{$\bm G$-Top}}_*)_{{\mathcal{F}}_1\cap{\mathcal{F}}_2},
        \]
        where the second functor is left Quillen by Lemma~(lemma:restr-equiv-lQ of the paper). We are therefore reduced to showing that the first functor is a left Quillen bifunctor.

        It suffices to verify the pushout product axiom for the generating (acyclic) cofibrations, which are of the form $(G_i/H_i\times f_i)_+$ for generating (acyclic) cofibrations $f$ of $\textbf{\textup{Top}}_*$ and $H_i\in{\mathcal{F}}_i$. The pushout product is then given by
        \[
            (G_1/H_1\times f_1)_+\mathbin{\raise.25pt\hbox{\scalebox{.67}{$\square$}}}
            (G_2/H_2\times f_2)_+\cong
            \big((G_1\times G_2)/(H_1\times H_2) \times (f_1\mathbin{\raise.25pt\hbox{\scalebox{.67}{$\square$}}} f_2)\big){}_+.
        \]
        As $\textbf{\textup{Top}}$ is a cartesian model category, $f_1\mathbin{\raise.25pt\hbox{\scalebox{.67}{$\square$}}} f_2$ is a cofibration, acyclic if at least one of $f_1,f_2$ is so. As $(G_1\times G_2)/(H_1\times H_2)$ is $({\mathcal{F}}_1\times{\mathcal{F}}_2)$-cofibrant by definition and since the $({\mathcal{F}}_1\times{\mathcal{F}}_2)$-model structure is topological, the claim follows.
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma smash-lQ of arXiv:2608.28504

body:
[Theorem 27 of arXiv:2605.17296, 'Zero correlations and averaged fields of orthonormal Gaussian Functions'] For fixed $k \ge 1$, as $n \to \infty$, 
the short-range correlations between the zeros of
 $\spec_{h_{n}}\cW(z)$ and
 $\spec_{h_{n+k}}\cW(z)$ are 
\begin{equation*}
g_{n,n+k}(z,z) = 
\begin{cases}
\disp 1-\frac{5}{4n^{2}}+O\left( \frac{1}{n^{3}}\right) <1 & \text{if $k=1$}, \\[4mm]
\disp \frac{4}{3}+
\frac{1}{12n^2}+O\left( \frac{1}{n^3}\right) 
>1 &
 \text{if $k=2$}, 
\\[4mm]
\disp 1 & \text{if $k\geq 3$}.  
\end{cases}
\end{equation*}
Thus, the short-range correlations
between zeros of $\spec_{h_{n}}\cW(z)$ and zeros of 
$\spec_{h_{n+k}}\cW(z)$ display repulsion if $k=1$, 
attraction if $k=2$, and no short-range second-order correlation in the contact
 limit if $k\geq 3$. Moreover, $g_{n,n+1}(z,z)$ increases
 with $n$ and $g_{n,n+1}(z,z) \to 1$, and
$g_{n,n+2}(z,z)$ attains its maximum at $n=2$ and then
 decreases for $n\geq 2$, 
with $g_{n,n+2}(z,z) \to 4/3$ as $n \to \infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 225 (Imprecise $L^2$ estimates for the top-order fully modified quantities) of arXiv:2609.03101, 'The emergence of the Cauchy horizon from the crease for $3D$ compressible Euler flow'] Let $N = \Ntop$,  let
$\mathfrak{P}^{(N)}$, $\angLie_{\mathfrak{P}}^{(N)}$ 
be the set of order $N$ $\nullhyparg{u}$-tangential commutator operators from
Def.\,\ref{D:STRINGSOFCOMMUTATIONVECTORFIELDS}. Let $\blowuprateofwaveWRTnumberofcommutations(N) = \blowupratetoporderwave$ denote the blowup rate of the wave variables defined in \eqref{E:BLOWUPRATEOFWAVEWRTNUMBEROFCOMMUTATORS}. Let $\varsigma_0$ be the constant featured in Lemma\,\ref{L:PRELIMINARYBELOWTOPORDERL2ESTIMATESFOREIKONALFUINCTIONQUANTITIES} (see also Remark\,\ref{R:SMALLNESSCONSTANTFORBELOWTOPORDERACOUSTICVARIABLES}).
Then if $\varsigma_1 \in (0,1]$ is sufficiently small, the following estimates hold for
$(\ubar,u) \in [\leftubar,\ubarboot) \times [\moreinterestingu_1,\moreinterestingu_2]$, where the implicit constants are \textbf{independent} of $\varsigma_0$ and $\varsigma_1$:

	\begin{align}
		\begin{split} 
			& \totalfluxcontrolimprecisefullymodifiedchi(\ubar,u)  +  (\blowupratetoporderwave + 1) \totalbulkcontrolimprecisefullymodifiedchi(\ubar,u) \lesssim  (1 + \varsigma_0^{-1}) \initialsmalldoublenull^2  \\
			& \ \ +  (1 + \varsigma_0^{-1} +  \varsigma_1^{-1}) \int_{\ubar' = \leftubar}^{\ubar}  \totalfluxcontrolimprecisefullymodifiedchi(\ubar',u) \, \mathrm{d} \ubar'  + \varsigma_1\fundbootsmall \max_{\angLie_{\tander}^N \in \angLie_{\mathfrak{P}}^{(N)}}   \int_{ \characteristicdiamondtwoarg{[\leftubar,\ubar)}{[\moreinterestingu_1,u]}}
			\left|\upmu \angLie_{\tander}^N \upchi \right|^2  \weight^{\blowupratetoporderwave} \voldiamond \\

			 & \ \ + \bulkcontrolVortVort_N(\ubar,u) +  \bulkcontrolDivGradEnt_N(\ubar,u)

+   \int_{u' = \moreinterestingu_1}^u \left\{\fluxcontrolVort_{\le N}(\ubar,u')+ \fluxcontrolGradEnt_{\le N }(\ubar,u')\right\} \, \mathrm{d} u' \\.

[Corollary 31 of arXiv:2608.30549, '\vspace{-1cm}Maximally Spread Out Measures and Implications\\{} for Phase Transitions in A'] Let $(\XX,\varrho)$ be a quasi-metric space, and let $\emptyset \ne \SC \subset \XX$.
  Let $\mu$ be a Borel probability measure on $\XX$ that satisfies $\om{\mu}(\SC)=1$
  and the small-ball condition with parameter $s>0$ on $\SC$, i.e.,
  there exist $r_0, c > 0$ such that
  \[
    \mu^\ast (\ball (x,r)) \leq \exp(- c \cdot (1/r)^s)
    \qquad \forall \, x \in \SC \text{ and } 0 < r < r_0
    ,
  \]
  where $\ball(x,r) = \{ y \in \XX \,\,:\,\, \varrho(y,x) \leq r \}$.

  Then $\mu$ satisfies the small-ball condition with parameter $s$ on $\XX$,
  i.e., there exist constants $r_1, c^\ast > 0$ such that
  \[
    \mu^\ast (\ball (x,r)) \leq \exp(- c^\ast \cdot (1/r)^s)
    \qquad \forall \, x \in \XX \text{ and } 0 < r < r_1
    .
  \]

[Theorem 5 (Algorithmic lower bound for comparison decoders) of arXiv:2606.07931, 'Pointwise Complexity for Gaussian Fields:\\Upper Envelopes, Algorithmic Lower Bounds, and '] Let \(v:T\to\mathcal H\) be an embedding into a finite-dimensional Hilbert space and set
\(d(s,t)=\|v_s-v_t\|_{\mathcal H}\). Let
\[
Y=v_\Theta+\tau Z,
\qquad
\Theta\sim\pi,
\qquad
Z\sim N(0,I_{\mathcal H}),
\]
and let \(m\in\mathcal H\) be any reference center.  Set
\[
Q_{\tau,m}:=N(m,\tau^2I_{\mathcal H}),
\qquad
\mathcal I_{\pi,m}:=\frac{1}{2\tau^2}\int_T\|v_t-m\|^2\,\pi(dt).
\]
With \(\bar v_\pi:=\int_T v_t\,\pi(dt)\), the centered choice \(m=\bar v_\pi\) gives
\[
\mathcal I_{\pi,\bar v_\pi}=\frac{\mathsf V_\pi}{4\tau^2},
\qquad
\mathsf V_\pi:=\iint d(s,t)^2\pi(ds)\pi(dt).
\]

Let \(\widehat\Theta(Y)\) be an estimator with values in \(T\).
Assume that there is a penalty \(\Omega:T\to\mathbb R\) and nonnegative, integrable comparison errors
\(\varepsilon_{\rm opt}\) and \(\varepsilon_{\rm pen}\), measurable under the true joint law, such that
\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
\|Y-v_{\widehat\Theta}\|^2+\Omega(\widehat\Theta)
\le
\|Y-v_\Theta\|^2+\Omega(\Theta)+\varepsilon_{\rm opt},\\
\Omega(\widehat\Theta)
\ge \Omega(\Theta)-\varepsilon_{\rm pen}.
\end{gathered}
\end{equation}
Let the full comparison error be denoted by
\[
\varepsilon_{\rm cmp}:=\varepsilon_{\rm opt}+\varepsilon_{\rm pen}.
\]
If, for some \(c\in(0,1)\) and \(\Delta>0\),
\begin{equation}
\mathcal I_{\pi,m}+\log 2
\le
(1-c)\log\frac{1}{\rho_{\Delta,Q_{\tau,m}}(\widehat\Theta)},
\end{equation}
then
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E_{\Theta,Y}d(\Theta,\widehat\Theta(Y))\ge c\Delta,
\end{equation}
and, for the Gaussian process \(X_t:=\langle Z,v_t\rangle\) built from the same Gaussian vector \(Z\),
\begin{equation}
\mathbb E_{\Theta,Z}\bigl[X_{\widehat\Theta}-X_\Theta\bigr]
\ge
\frac{c^2\Delta^2-\mathbb E_{\Theta,Z}\varepsilon_{\rm cmp}}{2\tau}.
\end{equation}
In particular, if \(\mathbb E\varepsilon_{\rm cmp}\le c^2\Delta^2/2\), then the right-hand side is at least \(c^2\Delta^2/(4\tau)\).  Thus the exact ghost mass gives an algorithmic lower bound on the Gaussian range sampled by the comparison decoder, up to the explicit comparison error.

Ordinary nearest neighbor corresponds to \(\Omega\equiv0\) and \(\varepsilon_{\rm opt}=\varepsilon_{\rm pen}=0\).  The unrestricted norm-regularized nearest-neighbor rule
\[
\widehat\Theta_\lambda(Y)\in
\arg\min_{a\in T}\bigl\{\|Y-v_a\|^2+\lambda\|v_a\|^2\bigr\}
\]
is also covered with zero error whenever the realized outputs have norm at least the norm of the true parameter, as in the separating example in Theorem~\ref{thm:decision-aligned-separation}. This is a canonical minimum-complexity inductive bias consistent with modern perspectives, rather than an explicit restriction of the hypothesis class. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Algorithmic lower bound for comparison decoders

[Lemma 21 (Martingale bounds on infection paths) of arXiv:2604.00630, 'The contact process on a bipartite spatial network'] Assume that~$G$ is a bipartite graph, and consider the contact process on~$G$ in which the infection rates of types~$1$ and~$2$ are~$\lambda_1$ and~$\lambda_2$, respectively. Assume that~$\lambda_1,\lambda_2 < 1/4$.
	Let $\Gamma=(\Gamma_0,\ldots,\Gamma_\ell)$ be a vertex path in~$G$ with initial vertex~$\Gamma_0$ of type~$1$. Then, the probability that there exist~$t > 0$ and an infection path~$g:[0,t]\to V$ having $\Gamma$ as its ordered trace is at most $(2\lambda_1)^{\lceil|\Gamma|/2\rceil}(2\lambda_2)^{\lfloor|\Gamma|/2\rfloor}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

TECHNIQUE CARD (drafted from a spec by a helper model, every card read and seven corrected by the Fable agent on 2026-09-07; canonical statements only, no original claim). A probability measure mu on R is moment-determinate if it is the unique probability measure sharing its full sequence of moments (m_k)_{k>=0}. The Carleman condition gives a simple sufficient criterion: if sum_{k=1}^infinity m_{2k}^{-1/(2k)} = infinity, then mu is moment-determinate. In practice this is most often invoked via a stronger, easier-to-check sub-condition, such as subgaussian or lighter tails, for instance P(|X|>t) <= C exp(-ct^2), which implies the even moments grow at most at Gaussian rate and hence satisfy Carleman's sum divergence; a common proof strategy in random matrix theory and random measure convergence is to show convergence of all moments to those of a known moment-determinate limit, such as the compactly supported semicircle law, and then invoke Carleman's condition, or compact support directly, to upgrade moment convergence to convergence in distribution. It does not hold automatically for every measure with finite moments of all orders: the classical log-normal distribution is the standard counterexample, having finite moments of every order yet failing to be moment-determinate, so other measures share its entire moment sequence, meaning that verifying Carleman's sum diverges, or invoking compact support, is a genuinely necessary step, not a formality. Typical failure: Assuming that finiteness of all moments, or even termwise convergence of a sequence's moments to a limit's moments, is sufficient to conclude convergence in distribution, without checking that the limit measure is itself moment-determinate; the log-normal-type failure of moment determinacy is the standard cautionary example, and in random matrix or random measure contexts, using the method of moments toward a limit whose determinacy has not been separately established, as happens for some heavy-tailed spectral limits, can produce a plausible-looking but invalid convergence claim. Canonical reference: Carleman, 1926, Les Fonctions Quasi Analytiques, Gauthier-Villars; Akhiezer, The Classical Moment Problem, 1965, Hafner Publishing; Anderson, Guionnet and Zeitouni, An Introduction to Random Matrices, 2010, Cambridge University Press.

$$
M_N:=\max_{1\le i\le r(N)} m_i^{(N)} =  o(n_N),

\[
\Sigma\ :=\ \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac{1}{n_N}\sum_{i=1}^{r(N)}\frac{m_i^{(N)}\bigl(m_i^{(N)}+1\bigr)}{2}
\]
exists in $\R$. Then $X_N/n_N$ converges mod-$\phi$ with parameter $n_N$, normalization function
\[
\phi(z)\ :=\ \int_0^1 \log\Bigl(\frac{e^{tz}-1}{tz}\Bigr)\,dt,

\[
\psi(z) = \exp\Bigl(\frac12\log\Bigl(\frac{e^{z}-1}{z}\Bigr)-\frac{z}{2}\,\Sigma\Bigr)
\ =\ \sqrt{\frac{e^{z}-1}{z}}\;e^{-\,\frac{z}{2}\Sigma}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem thm:introduction-lattice-induction of arXiv:2607.25616, 'Stealthy point processes and lattice induction'] The following assertions hold.

\begin{enumerate}
\item
For every $d\geq 1$, each lattice-induced
probability-preserving Borel $\mathbb R^d$-space admits a
generating stealthy Delone cross-section.

\item
Let $\eta$ be an ergodic translation-invariant point process on
$\mathbb R$ with positive intensity and local second moments. If
\[
    \int_{0<|\xi|<1}
    \frac{1}{\xi^2}\,d\sigma_\eta(\xi)
    <
    \infty,
\]
then the translation action on its configuration space has a
nonzero eigenvalue and is lattice-induced.
\end{enumerate}

Consequently, an ergodic probability-preserving Borel
$\mathbb R$-space is lattice-induced if and only if it admits a
generating stealthy Delone cross-section. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Stealthy cross-sections and lattice induction

body:
Load-bearing hypothesis: the equivalence 'admissible shock ⇔ Lax inequalities f'(u_-) ≥ σ ≥ f'(u_+)' requires the flux to be convex (genuinely nonlinear) on the range of the data. For a nonconvex flux one must use Oleinik's full chord condition, which involves f at every intermediate state, not only the two endpoint derivatives. Counterexample: f(u) = u^4 - 5u^2 (so f'(u) = 4u^3 - 10u), left state u_- = 2, right state u_+ = -2. Since f(2) = f(-2) = -4, Rankine-Hugoniot gives the stationary shock σ = 0, and the Lax inequalities hold strictly: f'(2) = 12 > 0 > f'(-2) = -12. Yet the shock is NOT admissible: the chord joining (-2,-4) and (2,-4) is the constant -4, while f(0) = 0 lies ABOVE it, so Oleinik's condition fails; equivalently the Kruzhkov inequality with k = 0 requires σ(k - u_-) ≥ f(k) - f(u_-), i.e. 0 ≥ 4, which is false. The correct entropy solution of this Riemann problem is read off the least concave majorant of f on [-2,2] (the hull construction for a decreasing jump u_l > u_r): a shock from u_- = 2 down to u* = (√7 - 2)/3 ≈ 0.2153, the point at which the line through (2, f(2)) is tangent to the graph of f, then an attached rarefaction from u* down to -u*, then, by symmetry, a shock from -u* to u_+ = -2. The two shock speeds are -(16 + 14u*)/9 ≈ -2.113 and +(16 + 14u*)/9 ≈ +2.113, and the rarefaction sweeps the speeds between them. Auditor's check: whenever a proof calls a jump admissible using only characteristic speeds, verify convexity of the flux on the interval spanned by the two states; otherwise test the whole chord.
Counterexample flux f(u) = u^4 - 5u^2 with states u_- = 2, u_+ = -2, shock speed σ = 0
Lax inequalities compare σ only with f'(u_-) and f'(u_+)
Oleinik's condition requires the graph of f between the two states to lie on the correct side of the chord at EVERY intermediate value
For nonconvex flux the Riemann solution is generally a composite of shocks and rarefactions given by the convex (or concave) hull construction
title: Pitfall: Lax's Shock Inequalities Are Not Sufficient When the Flux Is Not Convex

body: Theorem (campaign status: audited-pass): Under affine spanning, projective simplicity, and coordinate-full homogenization, an affine fibre of density greater than 27/512 cannot have old geometric distance three. Structure: homogeneous compression yields an optimal residual plane; if it descends with any slack the old distance is ≤ 2; otherwise it has the saturated shared-h pattern, the balanced local relation reduces the old support to three or five coordinates, and long directions, flag estimates, planar spectra, the m = 8 exact normal forms, and the m ≤ 7 intrinsic enumeration cover every possible effective size. In each case either the density is ≤ 27/512 or an old rank-two residual certificate contradicts distance three. Notes: Quantifier: under the distance-three hypothesis EVERY optimal homogenized plane must be exceptional, so excluding any selected one suffices. Density threshold 27/512 ~ 0.0527. Finite components certified per p.27; this is a deterministic local theorem, not the determinant conjecture.

[Definition of arXiv:2603.12774, 'Synchronization by noise for stochastic differential equations driven by fractional Browni'] Let $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$ be a probability space. 
	The space of random Lipschitz functions denoted by \(\mathrm{BL}_{\Omega}(\mathbb{R}^d) \) consists of all functions \( g : \mathbb{R}^d \times \Omega \rightarrow \mathbb{R} \) satisfying the following properties.
	\begin{itemize}
		\item For every \( \omega \in \Omega \), the function \( x \mapsto g(x,\omega) \) is continuous.
		\item For every \( x \in \mathbb{R}^d \), the function \( \omega \mapsto g(x,\omega) \) is measurable.
		\item There exists a constant \( M > 0 \) such that on a set of full measure in \( \Omega \) 
		\begin{align*}
			\| g(\cdot, \omega) \|_{\mathrm{BL}} < M,
		\end{align*}
		where
		\[
		\| g(\cdot, \omega) \|_{\mathrm{BL}} := \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}^d} |g(x,\omega)| + \sup_{\substack{x, y \in \mathbb{R}^d \\ x \neq y}} \frac{|g(x,\omega) - g(y,\omega)|}{|x - y|}.
		\]
	\end{itemize}
	Furthermore 
	\[
	\mathrm{Pr}_{\Omega}(\mathbb{R}^d) := \left\{ \nu \text{ is a probability measure on } \mathbb{R}^d \times \Omega \,\middle|\, \left( \Pi_{\Omega} \right)_{\ast} \nu = \mathbb{P} \right\},
	\]
	where $\Pi$ denotes the projection onto $\Omega$.

[DRAFT prior-art concept.] For nontrivial finitely generated groups G_1,G_2 with finite symmetric factor generating sets, independent bond percolation on Cay(G_1*G_2,S_1 union S_2) has critical parameter characterized by (chi_1(p)-1)(chi_2(p)-1)=1, where chi_i is expected root-cluster size on the corresponding factor Cayley graph. In the F_2 long-power family, G_1=G_2=Z, the b factor has chi_b=(1+p)/(1-p), and this specializes to p(2chi_N(p)-1)=1. The union-of-factor-generators assumption is essential; this formula is not asserted for arbitrary prescribed generating sets. Source: Kozakova arXiv:math/0611668v3, Theorem 1.
Nontrivial finitely generated factors
Generating set is the union of factor generating sets
Independent bond percolation
title: Published prior art: free-product critical equation for factor generating sets

body: [Abstract of arXiv:2609.02257, 'Aperiodic random walks: uniform estimates, local limits and invariance principles'] We prove uniform endpoint estimates, killed local limits, and conditioned-bridge invariance principles for triangular arrays of centered, aperiodic, integer-valued random walks with uniform exponential tails. [Lemma LEM:var of arXiv:2412.09790, 'Critical threshold for weakly interacting log-correlated focusing Gibbs measures'] Given $N \in \mathbb{N}$, let $Y_N$ be as above.
Suppose that  $F:C^\infty(\mathbb{T}^d) \to \mathbb{R}$
is measurable such that $\mathbb{E}\big[|F(Y_N)|^p\big] < \infty$
and $\mathbb{E}\big[|e^{F(Y_N)}|^q \big] < \infty$ for some $1 < p, q < \infty$ with $\frac 1p + \frac 1q = 1$.
Then, we have
\begin{align}
 \log \mathbb{E}\Big[e^{F(Y_N)}\Big]
= \sup_{\theta \in \mathbb H_a}
\mathbb{E}\bigg[ F( Y_N + \Theta_N) - \frac{1}{2} \int_0^1 \| \theta(t) \|_{L^2_x}^2 dt \bigg], 

\end{align}
	
	
\noindent
where  
 the expectation $\mathbb{E} = \mathbb{E}_\mathbb{P}$
is taken  with respect to the underlying probability measure~$\mathbb{P}$.
Here, 
$\Theta_N = \pi_N \Theta$, 
where the process $\Theta$  is  defined by 
\begin{align}
\Theta (t)  =  \int_0^t \langle \nabla \rangle^{-\frac d2} \theta(t') dt'.

\end{align}

\noindent (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

\[
\mathbb E^{\alpha,x}[(M_t^C)^2]=\int_0^t \mathbb E^{\alpha,x}[\Lambda_s] (\mu_Z^2+\sigma^2_Z) ds\leq A(\mu_Z^2+\sigma^2_Z)t.
\]
In particular, $\frac{M^C_t}{t}\to 0$
in $L^2(\mathbb P^{\,\alpha,x})$ and $\mathbb P^{\,\alpha,x}$-a.s.

For a probability space of absolutely continuous characteristic paths theta=(a,b,w), assume finite integrated squared Euclidean speed, original w learning rate one, nonnegative loss with integral_0^t E||theta_prime||^2 <= L0-Lt, L0<=E, and rotationally invariant p0=w0/sqrt(d) with E||p0||^2<=R^2. For fixed unit u and gamma_t=<w_t,u>/sqrt(d), ||gamma_t||_2 <= (R+sqrt(t*(L0-Lt)))/sqrt(d) <= (R+sqrt(t E))/sqrt(d). If P(|gamma_t|>=h)>=m>0, necessarily t E >= [sqrt(d)*h*sqrt(m)-R]_+^2. If Law(gamma_t)>=ell Lebesgue on [l,r], then replace h sqrt(m) with sqrt(ell*(r^3-l^3)/3). Hence bounded initial loss and normalized second moment exclude fixed positive unweighted mass of order-one scales in t=o(d), without pointwise bounds on parameters. This standard action-displacement application does not control amplitude-weighted exponential features, does not rule out an O(d) alignment phase, and does not prove Target 3. \[
\mathbf S_t^{T,\gamma}
:=
S_{T-t}^{\gamma}(X_t),
\qquad
t\in[0,T].
\]
is a bounded, continuous
\(\mathbb P_x^{T,\gamma}\)-submartingale with respect to
\(\{\mathcal F_t^{T,x}\}_{t\in[0,T]}\). Moreover, if
\(\mathbf S^{T,\gamma}
=
\mathbf M^{T,\gamma}+\mathbf A^{T,\gamma}\)
denotes its Doob--Meyer decomposition, then the increasing component
\(\mathbf A^{T,\gamma}\) is constant during the excursions of \(X\) away
from the origin, while the martingale component satisfies
\(\mathbf M^{T,\gamma}\in L^2(\mathbb P_x^{T,\gamma})\) and is given by
\begin{align}
\mathbf M_t^{T,\gamma}
=
S_T^\gamma(x)
+
\int_0^t
\nabla S_{T-s}^\gamma(X_s)\cdot dW_s^{T,\gamma},
\qquad
t\in[0,T].
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
For a connected finite plane honeycomb graph with f bounded faces and compatible prescribed boundary midpoint values, the homogeneous vertex-relation kernel has complex dimension f. Fewer than f additional complex linear conditions cannot determine interior midpoint values uniquely. Exactly f suffice: orient each internal edge, put J_e=(v-u)F(p_e)/2, and impose c_i^T J=0 on the real signed cycle vectors of the bounded faces. These constraints give a unique solution to the algebraic boundary problem; they are not claimed to hold for the actual SAW observable or to prove a scaling limit. This is an author-proved auxiliary result, pending full independent review.
Finite honeycomb graph; arbitrary complex midpoint fields

Let mu be a nonnegative Borel measure on R such that every polynomial is absolutely integrable and integral q(t)^2 dmu(t)>0 for every nonzero real polynomial q. Let p_k be its degree-k monic orthogonal polynomials, with p_0=1. Fix n>=1 and alpha in R, and write r_1<...<r_n for the n distinct real roots of p_n+alpha p_(n-1). There are strictly positive real numbers lambda_1,...,lambda_n such that integral f(t)dmu(t)=sum_(i=1)^n lambda_i f(r_i) for every real polynomial f of degree<=2n-2. These weights are unique. The parameter alpha is arbitrary real; no support-location restriction on the roots is added. The asserted exactness degree is2n-2, not2n-1 for arbitrary alpha. This is Lemma3.6 of Cohn-Kumar.

[Corollary of arXiv:2605.15066, 'The critical activation density in graph bootstrap percolation'] Let $A$ be a graph. 
Consider the graphs $F_e$ in 
Lemma (L_Fs of the paper). Suppose that, for some $e$ in $\langle A\rangle_H\setminus A$,

Then, for some $f$ that is added to $A$ before $e$ during the WGA, 
we have 
\[
v(F_e)/e(H)
\leqslant v(F_f)<v(F_e).
\]

[Proposition 2 (Probabilistic representation and error decomposition) of arXiv:2604.23133, 'High-Precision Framework for Expected Hitting Times Analysis in the Dice-Sum Process'] For every \(N \in \mathbb{N}\) and \(s \ge 0\), define
\[
F(s) := \mathbb{E}_s\big[\min(T,\omega_N)\big].
\]
Then, \(F\) satisfies the same recursion and boundary conditions as~\eqref{eq:ENdef}, and hence provides a solution of the truncated recursion.
Moreover,
\begin{equation}
E(s) - F(s)
\;=\;
\mathbb{E}_s\!\big[(T - \omega_N)\,\mathbf{1}_{\{\omega_N < T\}}\big].
\end{equation}
In words, \(\min(T,\omega_N)\) represents the truncated stopping time, and
\((T-\omega_N)\mathbf{1}_{\{\omega_N<T\}}\) is the additional waiting time incurred along paths that overshoot the cutoff \(N\) before hitting the target set~\(\mathcal{H}\).

	\end{equation}
	holds for some $\alpha \in (0,1)$. Let $(X_\epsilon)_{\epsilon\in (0,1)}$ be a family of $Y_\alpha$-valued random variables  that is uniformly tight in $ Y_0$ and has uniform tail estimates in $Y_1$, i.e., 
	\[\biggl(\sup_{\epsilon\in (0,1)} \mathbb{P} ( \|X_\epsilon \|_{Y_1} \ge N) \biggr)\,\to\, 0,
	\]
	as $N\to\infty$. Then $(X_\epsilon)_{\epsilon\in (0,1)}$ is also tight in $Y_\alpha$.

[Thm 6 (Universality for random polynomials) of arXiv:2608.06576, 'The Resultant Distribution Method: Universality for $p$-adic Random Matrices and Polynomia'] Let $K_1,\ldots,K_m$ be finite extensions of $\Q_p$, and let
$$
U\subseteq
\mc{O}_{K_1}^{\times,\new}
\times\cdots\times
\mc{O}_{K_m}^{\times,\new}
$$
be clopen. Suppose that
$$
P_n(x)=\xi_nx^n+\cdots+\xi_1x+\xi_0,
$$
where $\xi_0,\ldots,\xi_n$ are independent
$\epsilon$-balanced random variables in $\Z_p$. Then
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}
\E\left[
Z_U(P_n)
\right]
=
\int_U
\rho_{K_1,\ldots,K_m}^{(\infty),\poly}
(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\,dx_1\cdots dx_m.
$$
Here, the integral is taken with respect to the product Haar probability
measure on
$\mc{O}_{K_1}\times\cdots\times\mc{O}_{K_m}$, and
$\rho_{K_1,\ldots,K_m}^{(\infty),\poly}$ is the stabilized Haar polynomial
correlation function introduced above. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Universality for random polynomials

[Theorem 2.7 (van den Berg) of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186'] Suppose that $D$ is simply connected and that $\partial D$ is Minkowski nondegenerate with
Minkowski dimension $\msf d_M(\partial D)\in[1,2)$. That is,
\[0<\liminf_{r\to0}\frac{\msf{A}(\partial D_r)}{r^{2-\msf d_M(\partial D)}}\leq
\limsup_{r\to0}\frac{\msf{A}(\partial D_r)}{r^{2-\msf d_M(\partial D)}}<\infty,\]
where we define
\[\partial D_r=\left\{x\in\mbb R^2:\inf_{y\in\partial D}|x-y|<r\right\}.\]
There exists constants $c\in(1,\infty)$ and $\th>0$ such that
\begin{align}

c^{-1}t^{1-\msf d_M(\partial D)/2}\leq\msf{A}(D)-\msf M_0(t)\leq ct^{1-\msf d_M(\partial D)/2},\qquad t\in(0,\th).
\end{align} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Definition Block-reversal involutions on $\llbracket n \rrbracket$ of arXiv:2509.02996, 'Group-averaged Markov chains: mixing improvement'] Let $n=2^k$ with $k\in\mathbb{N}$. For each $j\in \llbracket k \rrbracket$ define
	a permutation $\sigma^{(j)}$ of $\llbracket n \rrbracket$ by
	\[
		\sigma^{(j)}(i) := q\,2^{j} + \bigl(2^{j}-1-r\bigr) + 1, \quad \text{where } i-1 = q\,2^{j} + r \quad (q\in \mathbb{N}\cup \{0\},\ 0\le r < 2^j).
	\]
	Equivalently, partition $\llbracket n \rrbracket$ into consecutive blocks of length $2^{j}$:
	\[
	\llbracket 1,2^{j} \rrbracket,\ \llbracket 2^{j}+1,2\cdot 2^{j} \rrbracket,\ \dots,\ \llbracket (m-1)2^{j}+1,m2^{j}\rrbracket,\ \dots
	\]
	with $m \in \llbracket 2^{k-j} \rrbracket$ and within each block reverse the order, leaving different blocks disjoint.
title: Block-reversal involutions on $\llbracket n \rrbracket$

    be an \(\alpha\)-nice function (Assumption~(assmpt: sufficiently nice function of the paper)).
    Then, for any \(0\le \underline{t}<\overline{t}\le T\) the differential equation 
    \begin{equation}
        dx_t = \sigma(t,w_t, x_t) \, dg_t

    \end{equation}
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*), font=\upshape]
        \item has a \underline{unique} solution
        \(x\) with \(x \in C^\alpha([\underline{t},\overline{t}], \banachSpace[X])\).
    \end{enumerate}
For any \(R>0\)
    there exist constants
    \[
        C_{\text{flow}}^R, C_{\text{flow,loc}}^R, C_{\text{init}}^R, C_{\text{driver}}^R, C_{\text{param}}^R

    such that for all initial conditions

[Theorem thm:intro-mixing-time of arXiv:2505.02685, 'On the Spectral Expansion of Monotone Subsets of the Hypercube'] Let $A \subseteq \{0,1\}^n$ be a non-empty monotone set. Then the random walk on
    $\{0,1\}^n$ censored to $A$ has mixing time
    \[
        t_{\mathsf{mix}} \leq \frac{2n}{\mu(A)}\cdot  \log(4\cdot 2^n \mu(A)) \,.
    \] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 5 (Rank--one structure of $\E {[}M{) of arXiv:2606.20816, 'Spectral Properties of Dense Barab\'asi--Albert Graphs'] }$]
Let $A = \left[0, c\right]$, $B = \left(c, 1\right]$, and $u \left(t\right) = \left(2 t - c\right)^{-1 / 2}$. Define the function $\phi : \left[0, 1\right] \to \R$ by
\[
\phi \left(x\right)
\ := \
\mathbf{1}_{\left\{x \in A\right\}} + \sqrt{c} \, \mathbf{1}_{\left\{x \in B\right\}} u \left(x\right),
\]
where $\mathbf{1}_{x \in S}$ is the indicator function defined as
\[
\mathbf{1}_{x \in S}
\ = \
\begin{cases}
1, & x \in S, \\
0, & x \notin S,
\end{cases}
\]
for some set $S$. Then the limiting mean kernel $F$ from \eqref{eq:FWR} satisfies
\[
F \left(x, y\right)
\ = \
\phi \left(x\right) \phi \left(y\right).
\]

Consequently, if one forms the $n \times n$ matrix
\[
F^{\left(n\right)}_{k j}
\ := \
F \left(\frac{k}{n}, \frac{j}{n}\right),
\qquad
1 \le k, j \le n,
\]
then $F^{\left(n\right)}$ is rank one, since
\[
F^{\left(n\right)}
\ = \
v^{\left(n\right)} \left(v^{\left(n\right)}\right)^\top\!,
\qquad
v^{\left(n\right)}_k
\ := \
\phi \left(\frac{k}{n}\right).
\]
In particular, by Theorem \ref{thm:mean-kernel-limit}, the expectation matrix $\E[M]$ is asymptotically a rank--one matrix.

[Lemma lem:d_P_bound of arXiv:2411.03609, 'Asymptotically optimal Wasserstein couplings for the small-time stable domain of attractio'] \noindent{\nf(a)} Let $\bm\xi$ be a random vector in $L^q$, i.e. $\mathds{E}[|\bm\xi|^q]<\infty$, for some $q\in(0,1]$. Then, 
$$\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{\xi},a\bm{\xi})\geqslant |1-a^q|\mathds{E}\big[|\bm\xi|^q\big] \quad \text{ for any constant }a \in(0,\infty).$$

\noindent{\nf(b)} Assume that the random vectors
$\bm\xi_1, \bm\xi_2, \bm\zeta_1, \bm\zeta_2$ are in $L^q$, for some $q\in(0,1]$, and that 
$(\bm{\xi}_1,\bm{\zeta}_1)$ and $(\bm{\xi}_2, \bm{\zeta}_2)$ are independent. Then the following inequality holds:
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{W}_q(\bm{\xi}_1+\bm{\xi}_2,\bm{\zeta}_1+\bm{\zeta}_2)
\leqslant \mathcal{W}_q(\bm{\xi}_1,\bm{\zeta}_1) + \mathcal{W}_q(\bm{\xi}_2,\bm{\zeta}_2).
\end{equation*}

body:
[Lemma 2605211341 of arXiv:2609.02626, 'Comparison principles and symmetry for subquadratic fractional $p$-Laplacian equations'] Let $N\ge 1$, $s\in (0, 1)$ and $p>1$. Suppose that $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^N$ is a bounded open set, and $u\in \widetilde{W}^{s,p}(\Omega)$ is a weak solution of
\[
(-\Delta)_p^s u= g\quad \mbox{in } \Omega,
\]
for some $g\in L^1_{loc}(\Omega)\cap W_0^{s, p}(\Omega)'$. Let $v\in L^1_{loc}(\mathbb{R}^N)$  satisfy
\[
{\rm dist}({\rm supp}(v), \Omega)>0, \quad \int_{\Omega^c}\frac{|v(x)|^{p-1}}{(1+|x|)^{N+sp}} {\rm d}x<\infty.
\]
Define
\[
h(x)=2\int_{{\rm supp} (v)}\frac{J_{u+v}(x, y)-J_u(x, y)}{|x-y|^{N+sp}} {\rm d}y, \quad \mbox{for a.e. }x\in \Omega.
\]
Then $u+v\in \widetilde{W}^{s,p}(\Omega)$ and it solves weakly $(-\Delta)_p^s (u+v)= g+h$ in $\Omega$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
PROOF (UNAUDITED); novelty unverified. For deterministic x in R^d with d>=1 and s=||x||^2/d in (0,1], take independent standard Gaussian U(n by d), W(n by n), v(n), with n>=1. Define h=Ux/sqrt(d), a=tanh(h), H=Wa/sqrt(n), f=v^T tanh(H)/sqrt(n). With all raw U,W,v trainable and no biases, the diagonal NTK Theta_n=||grad_U f||_F^2+||grad_W f||_F^2+||grad_v f||^2 satisfies ||Theta_n-Theta_infty||_2<=37/sqrt(n). Here F(q)=E tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2, R(q)=E sech(sqrt(q)Z)^4 and Theta_infty=F(F(s))+(F(s)+s R(s))R(F(s)). This is also a W2 bound to the deterministic NTK point mass.
Two hidden layers of common width n; one fixed nonzero input, normalized squared norm <=1; independent Gaussian initialization; tanh; raw-parameter NTK scaling as stated; no trainable biases. Uses unaudited C021 and reviewed C002 v2 scalar kernel shape.
metadata_json:
{"artifact_digest":"sha256:2e54f669559ce1276dfe40f4e7ccfcb607ea68e74c8a28015756a0133b6fdbad","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/2e/2e54f669559ce1276dfe40f4e7ccfcb607ea68e74c8a28015756a0133b6fdbad.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:f3aeefd89b9bd0bd89a56e7f3aa2fc2ce4fb878722b532ee4aa00190646ee9e0","bundle_entry_key":"t250_w712_c022","bundle_id":"population.w712-t250-c021-c022-transpose-tanh-ntk","claim_kind":"theorem","conditions":[],"domain":"Quantitative Tensor Programs and Gaussian shared-weight conditioning","draft":"w712/bundle_016.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.neural_networks:two-hidden-tanh-diagonal-ntk-rate","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# C022 v1: n^(-1/2) rate for one initial two-hidden-layer tanh NTK program

Kind: narrowed. Target: 2, one transpose-using program.
Status: proof (unaudited). Novelty unverified. This is a one-input
diagonal NTK result, not the entire NTK matrix on multiple inputs or
a quantitative Master Theorem for arbitrary transpose programs.

## Model and statement

Let x in R^d be deterministic, with d>=1 and s=||x||^2/d in (0,1].
Let U in R^(n by d), W in R^(n by n) and v in R^n have independent
standard Gaussian entries, mutually independent, with n>=1. Define

    h=Ux/sqrt(d), a=tanh(h), H=Wa/sqrt(n),
    f(x)=v^T tanh(H)/sqrt(n).

All nonlinearities are coordinatewise. Train the raw parameters U,W,v
with the displayed scaling retained in the computational graph; there
are no bias parameters. The scalar diagonal empirical NTK is

    Theta_n(x,x)=||grad_U f||_F^2+||grad_W f||_F^2+||grad_v f||^2.

For Z standard Gaussian put

    F(q)=E tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2,
    R(q)=E sech(sqrt(q)Z)^4,
    q1=F(s), q2=F(q1), r1=R(s), r2=R(q1),
    Theta_infty=q2+(q1+s r1)r2.

Then, for all n>=1,

    ||Theta_n(x,x)-Theta_infty||_2 <=37/sqrt(n).     (1)

Equivalently, W2(Law(Theta_n(x,x)),delta_(Theta_infty)) is at most
37/sqrt(n), since coupling to a deterministic point has exactly that
L2 cost. The constant is universal on 0<s<=1 and deliberately loose.
The program genuinely uses W and W^T together; the quantitative shared-
weight step is C021, not an independent-backward-weight replacement.

## 1. Differentiate the exact finite-width program

Set qhat=||a||^2/n, D=diag(sech(h_i)^4), rhat=tr(D)/n,
g_j=sech(H_j)^2, b_j=v_j g_j and Rhat=||b||^2/n. Direct differentiation
with respect to the raw parameters in the stated parametrization gives

    ||grad_v f||^2 = Qhat2:=mean_j tanh(H_j)^2,
    ||grad_W f||_F^2 = qhat Rhat,
    ||grad_U f||_F^2 = s T,
    T=b^T W D W^T b/n^2.

For the last line grad_(U_ik) f=x_k sech(h_i)^2(W^Tb)_i/(n sqrt(d));
summing its square over i,k supplies exactly s, not an additional n.
Hence

    Theta_n=Qhat2+qhat Rhat+s T.                    (2)

Conditional on h, a,D are fixed with 0<=D<=I, and a!=0 almost surely
because s>0 and tanh vanishes only at zero. W,v are still fresh independent
Gaussians. C021 with g(t)=sech(t)^2 therefore gives, conditionally and
then unconditionally,

    ||T-rhat Rhat||_2<=9/sqrt(n).                   (3)

This is the only new transpose-conditioning input, and is unaudited.

## 2. Scalar forward and derivative moments

The h_i are iid N(0,s). Since tanh^2 and sech^4 lie in [0,1],

    ||qhat-q1||_2<=1/sqrt(n),
    ||rhat-r1||_2<=1/sqrt(n).                       (4)

Given h, the H_j are iid N(0,qhat). Thus

    ||Qhat2-F(qhat)||_2<=1/sqrt(n).

The independently reviewed C002 establishes that F is increasing and
concave, with F(0)=0 and F'(0+)=1. Consequently it is 1-Lipschitz on
[0,1]. Equations (4) give

    ||Qhat2-q2||_2<=2/sqrt(n).                      (5)

Given h, the pairs (H_j,v_j) are iid and E Rhat=R(qhat). Their individual
second moment is E[v_j^4 sech(H_j)^8]<=3. Conditional variance and total
expectation therefore give

    ||Rhat-R(qhat)||_2<=sqrt(3)/sqrt(n).             (6)

We also need a Lipschitz bound for R, proved here without an inverse
variance denominator. Let psi(t)=sech(t)^4. Its second derivative is

    psi''(t)=16 sech(t)^4 tanh(t)^2-4 sech(t)^6,

so |psi''|<=20 on R. If 0<=p<=q, take independent standard Gaussians
Z,Z'. The random variable sqrt(p)Z+sqrt(q-p)Z' has variance q. Taylor's
theorem, with a pointwise remainder at most 10(q-p)(Z')^2, and conditional
centering of the first-order term in Z', show

    |R(q)-R(p)|<=10(q-p).                          (7)

All expectations of the remainder are finite; psi' is bounded, so the
centered linear term is integrable. This includes p=0 and does not move
an uncontrolled derivative or limit through an integral.

## 3. Assemble the NTK rate without factoring dependent errors

Put Ahat=qhat+s rhat and A=q1+s r1. Both lie in [0,2]. From (2)--(3),

    ||Theta_n-[Qhat2+Ahat Rhat]||_2<=9/sqrt(n).      (8)

Expand the remaining product in the following exact order:

    Ahat Rhat-A r2
       =Ahat[Rhat-R(qhat)]
        +Ahat[R(qhat)-R(q1)]+(Ahat-A)r2.

Bounding Ahat pointwise by 2, r2 by 1, and using (4), (6), (7),

    ||Ahat Rhat-A r2||_2
       <=[2sqrt(3)+20+2]/sqrt(n).                  (9)

Neither Ahat nor qhat is assumed independent of Rhat. Triangle
inequalities with pointwise bounds suffice. Combine (5), (8), (9):

    ||Theta_n-Theta_infty||_2
       <=[33+2sqrt(3)]/sqrt(n)<37/sqrt(n),

using sqrt(3)<2. This proves (1).

## Scope, prior work, and remaining question

This is an explicit bounded-smooth-activation, diagonal, single-input
example of Target2. It does not control the NTK at two distinct inputs,
the full backward row distribution, growing depth, or reuse in a general
Tensor Program. The next mathematical extension is the off-diagonal
kernel: joint forward conditioning then has rank two and may become
ill-conditioned when the input features align.

Primary-source prior-work check: Hanin--Nica, arXiv:1909.05989v1,
Theorem1, PDF page4, treats ReLU diagonal NTK moments with zero-initialized
but trainable biases and two-sided second-moment comparability. That
comparability alone is insufficient to subtract the squared mean and
deduce a variance O(1/n); no such inference is used here. This is not a
claim that an n^(-1/2) tanh NTK rate is new in the literature. Independent
novelty assessment remains pending. The elementary Gaussian conditioning
mechanism itself is standard and is not claimed new.

Load-bearing checks: the precise raw-parameter normalization in section1;
the conditional independence required by C021; qhat>0 almost surely;
bounded derivatives for (6)--(7); and pointwise rather than independence
estimates in (9). At n=1 the conditioning still includes the rank-one
term, and (1) remains valid. There is no s=0 cancellation in the proof;

body: Let X be a Banach space and A: D(A) subset of X -> X a linear operator. There exists a strongly continuous semigroup (T(t))_{t >= 0} of bounded linear operators on X with ||T(t)|| <= 1 for every t >= 0 (a contraction semigroup) whose infinitesimal generator is A if and only if: (i) A is closed and D(A) is dense in X; and (ii) every lambda > 0 lies in the resolvent set of A, with ||(lambda I - A)^{-1}|| <= 1/lambda for every lambda > 0. [standard, e.g. Pazy, Semigroups of Linear Operators and Applications to Partial Differential Equations]

body:
[Theorem thm:explicit_current_1 of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let $(X_t)_{t\geq 0}$ be an ergodic diffusion with invariant measure $\mu$ whose
symmetric part $\mathcal{L}_S$ satisfies the Poincar\'e inequality~(equation eq:poincare of the paper)
with spectral gap $\lambda_\mathrm{gap}>0$ (Assumptions~(ass:dynamics of the paper)). 
Let $\overline{J}_t(U)$ denote the empirical current according to Definition~(def:empirical_current of the paper)
with ergodic mean $\E^\mu[\overline{J}_t(U)]=\E^\mu[v_{\textrm{s}}\cdot U]= \E^\mu[W]$,
and let $\nu\ll\mu$ with $\mathrm{d}\nu/\mathrm{d}\mu\in L^2(\mu)$.
Then for all $t > 0$ and $a > 0$,
\begin{align}
  \mathbb{P}^\nu\left(\overline{J}_t(U) - \E^\mu[\overline{J}_t] \geq a\right)
  \leq
  \left\|\frac{\mathrm{d}\nu}{\mathrm{d}\mu}\right\|_{L^2(\mu)}
  \exp\left[-t\frac{\tilde\sigma_{J,1}^2}{c_{J,1}^2}h\left(\frac{c_{J,1} a}{\tilde\sigma_{J,1}^2}\right)\right],
  
\end{align}
where $h(u) \equiv 1 + u - \sqrt{1+2u}$ and we define
\begin{align}
  \tilde\sigma_{J,1}^2 \equiv
  \frac{2\mathrm{Var}_\mu(W)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}} + 2\|Q\|_{L^\infty(\mu)},
  \qquad 
  c_{J,1} \equiv \frac{\|W-\E^\mu[W]\|_{L^\infty(\mu)}}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap}}.
\end{align}

body:
[Theorem 1 (Risk Stability Under Conditional Generative Augmentation) of arXiv:2609.01410, 'On the Reliability of Generative Augmentation:\\ A Wasserstein-Based Theoretical and Empir'] Assume:

\begin{enumerate}
    \item The loss $\ell(f(x),y)$ is $L_\ell$-Lipschitz with respect to $x$.
    
    \item The hypothesis class $\mathcal F$ is measurable and induces a uniformly bounded loss.
    
    \item For each class $y\in\mathcal Y$,
    \[
    W_1(P_y,P_{G,y})
    \le
    \varepsilon_y .
    \]
\end{enumerate}

Then for any classifier $f$,
\begin{equation}
|R_{P_\alpha}(f) - R_P(f)|
\le
\alpha L_\ell \sum_{y \in \mathcal{Y}} \pi_y \varepsilon_y.
\end{equation}

If $\varepsilon_y \le \varepsilon$ uniformly, then
\begin{equation}
|R_{P_\alpha}(f) - R_P(f)|
\le
\alpha L_\ell \varepsilon.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Risk Stability Under Conditional Generative Augmentation

body:
[Cor DeepSets of arXiv:2609.03129, 'A Closed-Form Formula for Consistent Lipschitz Regression on Metric Spaces with Sparse Neu'] Let $d,K,F\in\mathbb N_+$, let
$
    \mathcal{K}
    \subseteq
    \mathcal P_{\operatorname{emp}}^{\le K}(\mathbb R^d)
$
be compact with respect to $d_\phi$, and let
$
    \phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^F
$
be a \texttt{ReLU}-MLP such that $T_\phi$ is injective on $\mathcal{K}$. 
\hfill\\
\noindent
For every $L>0$, every $L$-Lipschitz map
$
    f:(\mathcal{K},d_\phi)\to\mathbb R,
$
and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a \texttt{ReLU}-MLP
$
    \Psi:\mathbb R^F\to\mathbb R
$
such that
\begin{equation}

    \sup_{
        \nu=
        \frac{1}{\widetilde K}
        \sum_{k=1}^{\widetilde K}\delta_{z_k}
        \in\mathcal{K}
    }
    \left|
        f(\nu)
        -
        \Psi\left(
            \frac{1}{\widetilde K}
            \sum_{k=1}^{\widetilde K}\phi(z_k)
        \right)
    \right|
    <\varepsilon
\end{equation}
and the resulting Deep Set map $\big(
\mathcal P_{\operatorname{emp}}^{\le K}(\mathbb R^d),d_{\phi}\big)\ni 
    \nu
    \mapsto 
    \Psi\big(T_\phi(\nu)\big)
\in (\mathbb{R},|\cdot|)$
is $L$-Lipschitz. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Universality of Lipschitz Deep Sets with Prescribed Regularity

body: Theorem (campaign status: audited-pass): Choose an independent dominating set U in C_n of size d = ceil(n/3) whose cyclic gaps have (edge-)length two or three. Put L_u = A + B_u and R = span{L_u : u in U}; the L_u are independent. Orient the cycle: in a length-two gap u-v-u' take basis forms B_v, C_v; in a length-three gap u-v-w-u' take B_v, C_v, C_w. Together with A these are exactly n+1 full-dual forms, linearly independent by backward substitution through each gap. Modulo R: B_u = -A, C_u = B_v, B_w = C_w in the relevant gap cases, so every full-dual form has a signed basis representative with residual in R. Hence dcb(A_n) = dgeo(A_n) = ceil(n/3). Notes: Explicit optimal certificate, not just an existence bound. Form count checks: sum of gap lengths = n edges, so d gaps contribute n forms, plus A = n+1.

body:
[Theorem intro-fredi of arXiv:2412.09290, 'Asymptotics of Harish-Chandra transform and infinitesimal freeness'] (Theorem (fredi of the paper))
  
  Let $n$ be a fixed integer. Let $A$ be a random Hermitian matrix of size $N$ and assume
  that for every finite $r$ one has
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} N^{n \varepsilon} \left( \frac{1}{N} \log
    \mathbb{E}[H \text{} C (x_1, \ldots, x_r, 0^{N - r} ; \lambda_1 (A),
    \ldots, \lambda_n (A))] - \sum_{j = 0}^{n - 1} \sum_{i = 0}^r
    \frac{1}{N^{j \varepsilon}} \Psi_j (x_i) \right) = \sum_{i = 1}^r \Psi_n
    (x_i), 
  \end{equation}
  where $\Psi_0, \ldots, \Psi_n$ are smooth functions in a complex neighborhood of
  $0$, the above convergence is uniform in a complex neighborhood of $0^r$, and $0 <
  \varepsilon < n^{- 1}$. Then the $1 / N^{n \varepsilon}$ correction of the
  average empirical distribution of $N^{- 1} A$ is given by
  \begin{equation}
    \lim_{N \rightarrow \infty} N^{n \varepsilon} \left( \frac{1}{N^{k + 1}}
    \mathbb{E}[\ensuremath{\operatorname{Tr}} (A^k)] - \sum_{j = 0}^{n - 1} \frac{1}{N^{j
    \varepsilon}} \ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}^{(j)}_k \right) =\ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_k^{(n)},
    
  \end{equation}
  where for every $j \in \{0, \ldots, n\}$
  \[ \ensuremath{\boldsymbol{\mu}}^{(j)}_k := \sum_{b_1 + 2 b_2 + \cdots + j \text{} b_j
     = j} \sum_{m = 0}^{k - b_1 - \cdots - b_j} \frac{k!}{m! (m + 1) ! (k - m
     - b_1 - \cdots - b_j) !b_1 ! \ldots b_j !} \text{{\hspace{8em}}} \]
  \begin{equation}
    \text{{\hspace{14em}}} \times \left. \frac{\mathrm{d}^m}{\mathrm{d} x^m} ((\Psi'_0
    (x))^{k - m - b_1 - \cdots - b_j} (\Psi'_1 (x))^{b_1} \ldots (\Psi'_j
    (x))^{b_j}) \right|_{x = 0} . 
  \end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem intro-fredi of arXiv:2412.09290

body:
[Defn local_multiple_radial_SLE_kappa of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] The locally commuting $n$-radial $\mathrm{SLE}(\kappa)$ is a compatible family of measures 
\[
\mathbb{P}_{\left(\Omega; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, q\right)}^{\left(U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n\right)}
\]
on $n$-tuples of continuous, non-self-crossing curves $\left(\gamma^{(1)}, \gamma^{(2)}, \ldots, \gamma^{(n)}\right)$ for all simply connected domains $\Omega$ with marked points $\left(z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, q\right)$ and target sets $\left(U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n\right)$. These measures satisfy the following conditions:

\begin{itemize}
    \item[(i)] \textbf{Conformal invariance}: If $\varphi: \Omega \to \Omega^\prime$ is a conformal map, then the pullback measure satisfies
    \[
    \varphi^* \mathbb{P}_{\left(\Omega^\prime; \varphi(z_1), \varphi(z_2), \ldots, \varphi(z_n), \varphi(q)\right)}^{\left(\varphi(U_1), \varphi(U_2), \ldots, \varphi(U_n)\right)} 
    = \mathbb{P}_{\left(\Omega; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, u\right)}^{\left(U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n\right)}.
    \]
    It suffices to describe the measure when $\left(\Omega; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, q\right) = \left(\mathbb{D}; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, 0\right)$. The definition for arbitrary $\Omega$ with a marked interior point $q$ can then be extended by pulling back via a conformal equivalence $\varphi: \Omega \to \mathbb{D}$ mapping $q$ to $0$.

    \item[(ii)] \textbf{Domain Markov property}: Let $\left(\gamma^{(1)}, \gamma^{(2)}, \ldots, \gamma^{(n)}\right) \sim \mathbb{P}_{\left(\mathbb{D}; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, q\right)}^{\left(U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n\right)}$, and parametrize $\gamma^{(j)}$ by their own capacity in $\mathbb{D}$. For stopping times $\mathbf{t} = (t_1, t_2, \ldots, t_n)$, define
    \[
    \tilde{U}_j = U_j \setminus \gamma^{(j)}_{[0, t_j]}, \quad 
    \tilde{\gamma}^{(j)} = \gamma^{(j)} \setminus \gamma^{(j)}_{[0, t_j]}, \quad 
    \tilde{\Omega} = \mathbb{D} \setminus \bigcup_{j=1}^n \gamma^{(j)}_{[0, t_j]}.
    \]
    Then, conditionally on the initial segments $\bigcup_{j=1}^n \gamma^{(j)}_{[0, t_j]}$, we have
    \[
    \left(\tilde{\gamma}^{(1)}, \tilde{\gamma}^{(2)}, \ldots, \tilde{\gamma}^{(n)}\right) 
    \sim \mathbb{P}_{\left(\tilde{\Omega}; \gamma^{(1)}_{t_1}, \gamma^{(2)}_{t_2}, \ldots, \gamma^{(n)}_{t_n}, q\right)}^{\left(\tilde{U}_1, \tilde{U}_2, \ldots, \tilde{U}_n\right)}.
    \]

    \item[(iii)] \textbf{Absolute Continuity with respect to independent SLE($\kappa$)}: Let $\left(\gamma^{(1)}, \gamma^{(2)}, \ldots, \gamma^{(n)}\right) \sim \mathbb{P}_{\left(\mathbb{D}; z_1, z_2, \ldots, z_n, 0\right)}^{\left(U_1, U_2, \ldots, U_n\right)}$. Let $z_j(t) = e^{i \theta_j(t)}$, the capacity-parametrized Loewner driving function $t \mapsto \theta_j(t)$ for $\gamma^{(j)}$ satisfies
    \[ 
    \begin{aligned}
    \mathrm{d} \theta_j(t) &= \sqrt{\kappa} \, \mathrm{d} B_j(t) + b_j\left(\boldsymbol{\theta}(t)\right) \, \mathrm{d} t, \\
    \mathrm{d} \theta_k(t) &= \cot\left(\frac{\theta_k(t) - \theta_j(t)}{2}\right) \, \mathrm{d} t, \quad k \neq j,
    \end{aligned}
    \]

body: [Theorem thm: main dual of arXiv:2411.04773, 'Meeting of squared Bessel flow lines and application to the skew Brownian motion'] The process $(V(-r)+r,\, r\ge 0)$ is a homogeneous Feller process starting from $0$. For any $r>0$, $\frac{V(-r)+r}{r}$ has distribution ${\mathcal B}(\frac{\widehat{\delta}}{2},\frac{\delta}{2})$. Conditionally on $V(0)=z>0$,  the  process $V$ stays constant then jumps at time $\mathrm{x}$ where  $\frac{z}{z+{\mathrm x}}$ has distribution ${\mathcal B}(\frac{\delta}{2},1)$. [Theorem 1 of arXiv:2608.12839, 'Spiking Neural Networks with Elephant Reinforcement'] Let \(N<\infty\). Consider the process
\[
Y_t=(V_t,S_t,K_t)
\in \mathbb N^N\times\mathbb Z^N\times\mathbb N^N.
\]
Assume that site \(i\) fires with rate
\[
\lambda_i(V,S,K)
=
\mathbf 1_{\{V_i>\alpha S_i^+\}},
\qquad
S_i^+=\max\{S_i,0\},
\]
and leaks with rate
\[
\gamma\mathbf 1_{\{V_i>0\}},
\qquad \gamma>0.
\]
When site \(i\) fires, \(V_i\) is reset to \(0\), its two neighbours receive
one unit of potential, and
\[
S_i\mapsto S_i+\xi_i,
\qquad
K_i\mapsto K_i+1.
\]
Then the process is non-explosive. More precisely, if \(N_t\) denotes the
number of events up to time \(t\), then
\[
\mathbb E[N_t]\leq (\gamma+1)Nt<\infty.
\]

body:
[Lemma 12 of arXiv:2609.02193, 'State-law dynamics of McKean-Vlasov stochastic reaction-diffusion equations on $\mathbb R^'] For every $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$, $T>0$ and $u_0\in L^2(\Omega,\mathcal F_0;H)$, equation~\eqref{Eq1} has a unique variational solution $u$ on $[0,T]$. The solutions obtained on different finite intervals are consistent and therefore define a global solution on $[0,\infty)$. Moreover, $t\mapsto\mathcal L u(t)$ belongs to $C([0,\infty);P)$ and
	\begin{align}
		&\mathbb E\sup_{0\leq r\leq T}\|u(r)\|^2
		+\mathbb E\int_0^T
		\big(\|u(r)\|_V^2+\|u(r)\|_p^p\big)dr
		\leq
		C_T\big(1+\mathbb E\|u_0\|^2\big),
	\end{align}
	where $C_T>0$ depends only on $T$ and the structural data and is independent of $\epsilon\in[0,\epsilon_0]$ and $u_0$. If $u_1,u_2$ are two solutions driven by the same Brownian motion with initial data $u_{0,1},u_{0,2}\in L^2(\Omega,\mathcal F_0;H)$, then
	\begin{align}
		\mathbb E\|u_1(t)-u_2(t)\|^2
		\leq
		e^{(L_G-\bar\gamma)t}\mathbb E\|u_{0,1}-u_{0,2}\|^2,
		\qquad t\geq0.
	\end{align}
	Consequently, the law of the solution is determined by the initial law $\mathcal L u_0$.
title: Lemma 12 of arXiv:2609.02193
