[Lemma 25 of arXiv:2608.08242, 'Bang--bang representation of $3\times 3$ embeddable stochastic matrices'] For $g\in(g_{\min},0)$, the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]	
\item
The admissible endpoint for $q_g$ is
	\[
	\bar c=\frac{r+1}{r+2x}.
	\]

\item
The coefficients of $q_g$ satisfy 
	\[
	\alpha(g)=(r+2x)m(g)T_{33}(U_g),
	\qquad
	\beta(g)=-2m(g)B(g),
	\qquad
	\gamma(g)=V_{32}(U_g),
	\]
	where
	\[
	\begin{aligned}
		B(g)={}&-(r^2+rx-r-2x)\\
		&+g\bigl(yr^2+yrx-2yr-3yx-y-r^2-rx+x\bigr).
	\end{aligned}
	\]
	
\item	
	The vertex-location expression satisfies
	\[
	2\alpha(g)\bar c+\beta(g)
	=2m(g)\bigl(T_{31}(U_g)+1\bigr).
	\]
	
	
\item	
The reduced discriminant factor from
	Lemma~\ref{lem:Frydman-discriminant-factorization} is
	\[
	\widetilde H_{23}(U_g)=4\Theta(g),
	\]
	where
	\[
	\Theta(g)=h_2g^2+h_1g+x^2(r-2).
	\]
	Here
	\[
	h_2=-(r+2x)T_{21}(U)>0,
	\]
	and the explicit formula for $h_1$, together with the remaining
	polynomial identities used below, is recorded in
	Appendix~\ref{app:X23-Frydman-formulas}.
\end{enumerate}

body:
Let S be a separable metric space, and let \mu_n, \mu be Borel probability measures on S such that \mu_n \Rightarrow \mu weakly. Then there exists a single probability space (\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \mathbb{P}) and S-valued random variables X_n, X defined on \Omega such that the law of X_n is \mu_n for all n, the law of X is \mu, and X_n(\omega) \to X(\omega) as n \to \infty for \mathbb{P}-almost every \omega \in \Omega.
S is a separable metric space
\mu_n \Rightarrow \mu weakly

body:
[Defi 13 of arXiv:2608.28148, 'Flows and homotopies of Banach Lie algebroids'] An \emph{almost Lie bracket} on an anchored bundle $\left(A,\pi, M,\rho\right)$ is a sheaf of antisymmetric bilinear maps
\[
\LB_{A_U} \colon \Gamma\left( A_{U}\right)  \times\Gamma\left(  A_{U}\right)
\to\Gamma\left(  A_U\right), U\subseteq M \text{open}
\]
which satisfies the following properties
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\textbf{AL \arabic*})]
\item  the Leibniz identity:
\[
\forall\left(   \mathfrak{u}_{1}, \mathfrak{u}_{2}\right)  \in \Gamma \left(A_{U} \right)  ^{2}, \forall f \in C^{\infty}(U)
,\ \LB[\mathfrak{u}_{1},f \mathfrak{u}_{2}]_{A_{U}}=f.\LB[\mathfrak{u}_{1}, \mathfrak{u}_{2}]_{A_{U}}+df(\rho( \mathfrak{u}_{1})). \mathfrak{u}_{2}.
\]
\item For any  open set $U\subseteq M$ and any $(\mathfrak{u}_1,\mathfrak{u}_2) \in \Gamma(A_{U})^2$, the maps
\[
\mathfrak{u}_1,\mapsto \LB[\mathfrak{u}_1,\mathfrak{u}_2]_{A_{U}} \textrm{ and } \mathfrak{u}_2,\mapsto \LB[\mathfrak{u}_1,\mathfrak{u}_2]_{A_{U}}
\]
only depend on the $1$-jets of $\mathfrak{u}_1$ and $\mathfrak{u}_2$, respectively.
\end{enumerate}
By abuse of notation, such a sheaf of almost Lie brackets will be denoted $\LB_A$. The quintuple $(A,\pi, M,\rho,\LB_A)$ is called an \emph{almost algebroid}.
title: Definition 13 of arXiv:2608.28148

body:
At the regular 24-cell (vertices the 24 permutations of (+-1,+-1,0,0); facets a.x = 1 with a = +-e_i or a = (+-1/2,+-1/2,+-1/2,+-1/2)), the 144 vertex-facet incidence equations a_j.v_i = 1 in the 192 coordinates of the 24 vertices and 24 facet normals have rank 140: four of them are dependent at this point. The Zariski tangent space of the realization space therefore has dimension 52, against the expected dimension 48 (28 against 24 after quotienting by the 24-dimensional projective group), so a first-order count cannot certify the local dimension. This is why Brysiewicz and Sinn (arXiv:2609.02818) use a second-order (quadratic obstruction) test; the local dimension they certify is the expected one, 48, so the regular 24-cell is not locally projectively rigid.

Assumes: realization space in vertex and facet-normal coordinates, facets normalised as a.x = 1 (the origin is interior)

[Def frame bundle of arXiv:2609.04023, 'Characterizing Contractions and Weighted Blowdowns'] Let $\mathcal{Y} \to \mathcal{Z}$ be a degree $d$ finite \'etale morphism of smooth separated Deligne--Mumford stacks. 
Then, the {\em frame bundle} $\underline{\mathrm{Isom}}_{\mathcal{Z}}(\mathcal{Z}^{\sqcup \, d}, \mathcal{Y}) \to \mathcal{Z}$ defined as follows: suppose $T \to \mathcal{Z}$ is an \'etale morphism where $T$ is a complex scheme, then
\[
\underline{\mathrm{Isom}}_{\mathcal{Z}}(\mathcal{Z}^{\sqcup \, d}, \mathcal{Y})(T) := \underline{\mathrm{Isom}}_T(T^{\sqcup \, d}, \mathcal{Y} \times_{\mathcal{Z}} T)
\]
where $\underline{\mathrm{Isom}}_T(T^{\sqcup \, d}, \mathcal{Y} \times_{\mathcal{Z}} T)$ is the usual Isom scheme (see [SGA2]).
The frame bundle naturally defines a principal $S_d$-bundle induced by the canonical left action of $S_d$ on $\mathcal{Z}^{\sqcup \, d}.$
title: Def frame bundle of arXiv:2609.04023

body: [Definition of arXiv:2609.03988, 'A $p$-summability approach to the weak maximizing property'] Let $1 \leq p < \infty$. A pair of Banach spaces $(X, Y)$ is said to have the \textbf{weakly $p$-singular maximizing property} ($\mathrm{SMP}_p$, for short) if every bounded linear operator $T: X \to Y$ which admits a weakly $p$-singular maximizing sequence is norm-attaining.

[Lemma lem:Gsym of arXiv:2605.15545, 'Crossover from subcritical to critical decay: \\ random walk, self-avoiding walk, percolat'] Suppose the hypotheses of Lemma~(lem:perc_diagram-p1 of the paper) hold.
Let $p\in [p_c-\delta_1, p_c)$ and $\mu \in \Omega_p$, with $\delta_1$ chosen
small enough that (equation eq:perc_tilted_infrared of the paper) holds.
Then there are (explicit) functions $f_j: [0,\infty) \to [0,\infty)$, satisfying $f_j(t) \to 0$ as $t \to 0$, for which
\begin{equation}
\norm{ \hat \tau_{p,\mathrm{sym}} ^{(\mu)} - \hat \tau_p }_3
\le f_1(\abs \mu) + f_2( 1 - \hat J_p ^{(\mu)}(0) )
	+  f_3( 1 - \hat J_p(0) ) .
\end{equation}

[Lemma 35 of arXiv:2606.11758, '2606.11758'] There exist constants \(\eta_R>3\varepsilon\) and \(\eta_V>6\varepsilon\) such
that, for every \(n\ge1\), every \(\xi\in\mathcal A_n\), and every
\(d\in\mathfrak D_{\xi,n}^{\mathrm{osc}}\), the stopped prefix martingale and
every finite stopped post-bin martingale associated to \((\xi,d,n)\), ordered
edge by edge generation by generation, admit deterministic Freedman budgets
\(R_{\xi,d,n}\) and \(V_{\xi,d,n}\) satisfying
\[
    R_{\xi,d,n}
    \le
    C_\gamma2^{-sn/2}2^{-\eta_R n},
    \qquad
    V_{\xi,d,n}
    \le
    C_\gamma2^{-sn}2^{-\eta_V n}.
\]
Every martingale difference \(\Delta\) satisfies
\[
    |\Delta|\le R_{\xi,d,n},
\]
and the predictable quadratic variation of each such martingale is bounded by
\(V_{\xi,d,n}\).

body:
[Proposition nest of arXiv:2608.07236, 'Negative association of Busemann functions \\in exponential last-passage percolation'] Fix $k<m<n$.
For any vertices $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}$ above or along level $n$, we have 
\begin{align} 
G^{\textup{S}}_{m, \mathbf{x}}(h) - G^{\textup{S}}_{m, \mathbf{y}}(h) = G^{\textup{S}}_{n, \mathbf{x}}(\sigma^{n-1}\cdots\sigma^m h) - G^{\textup{S}}_{n, \mathbf{y}}(\sigma^{n-1}\cdots\sigma^m h).
\end{align}
Similarly, for any vertices $\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{b}$ below or along level $k$, we have 
$$G^{\textup{N}}_{\mathbf{a}, m}(h) - G^{\textup{N}}_{\mathbf{b}, m}(h) = G^{\textup{N}}_{\mathbf{a}, k}(\sigma_{k}\cdots\sigma_{m-1} h) - G^{\textup{N}}_{\mathbf{b}, k}(\sigma_{k}\cdots\sigma_{m-1} h).$$
title: Nested LPP property

[Cor algebraic_area of arXiv:2606.21049, '\textsc{Locality of rough path lifts}'] There exists a bilinear map
\[
\mathbb{A} \colon C([0,1])\times C([0,1]) \to \mathbb{R}^{\triangle}
\]
which satisfies Chen's identity (equation eq:chen of the paper) and is strongly local in the sense of (rem:timeloc of the paper),
i.e. if
$Z'_{s + \tau,u + \tau} = Z_{s,u}$ for all $u \in [s,t]$ then
$
\mathbb{A}_{s + \tau, t + \tau}(Z') = \mathbb{A}_{s, t}(Z)
$.
The same statement holds with the domain of $\mathbb{A}$ replaced by $\mathbb{R}^{[0,1]}\times \mathbb{R}^{[0,1]}$ and with \say{strongly local} replaced by \say{local} in the sense of (def:local of the paper).

If there exists an integer n_0 \ge 1 such that \phi^{n_0} \in L^1(\mathbb{R}), then for all n \ge n_0, the standardized sum Z_n = \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}} \sum_{k=1}^n X_k has an absolutely continuous distribution with continuous density f_n(x), and \lim_{n \to \infty} \sup_{x \in \mathbb{R}} \left| f_n(x) - \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} e^{-x^2 / 2} \right| = 0.

[Thm 3 (Endpoint atom case) of arXiv:2605.07059, 'Modified ruin probability for a Cram{\'e}r-Lundberg model driven by a compound mixed Poiss'] Assume that $\ell_1<c/\mu$, that $p_1:=G(\{\ell_1\})>0$, and that the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm:light-fixed} hold with $\ell=\ell_1$. In addition, assume that for every $\ell\in(0,\ell_1)$ there exists $R_\ell>R_{\ell_1}$ such that
\[
\psi_{\rm cl}(u,\ell)\le e^{-R_\ell u},\qquad u\ge0.
\]
If $\psi$ is continuous or monotone on $(-\infty,0)$, then
\[
\psi(u)\sim C_{\ell_1}\,\psi_{\rm cl}(u),\qquad u\to\infty.
\]

[Lemma properties-of-d of arXiv:2609.00425, 'Individual and Uniform Eventual Positivity of Self-Adjoint Semigroups'] Let $D \colon \dom D \to \ell^2(\mathbb{Z})$ be the diagonal operator as defined above. Then the following assertions hold:
    \begin{enumerate}[\upshape (i)]
        \item The operator $D$ is self-adjoint and is positive in the Hilbert space sense.
        \item $D$ has compact resolvent.
        \item Both $H_{\mathrm{even}}$ and $H_{\mathrm{odd}}$ reduce $D$, and one has $Dq_n = nq_n$ for all $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
    \end{enumerate}

Own-work draft; proof (unaudited). Uniform-origin stationarization of iid fixed-length finite-alphabet blocks is either iid (the block law is a product of identical marginals) or has rho(n)=1 for every lag. Random-length, dependent-block and hierarchical encodings not excluded. Concatenate a bi-infinite iid family of blocks with law P on S^L at fixed boundaries, then translate by an independent uniform phase in {0,...,L-1}. Distinct translated laws are separated by some finite-cylinder probability; its two directional length-L sampled empirical frequencies yield a shared tail statistic. The statement does not cover random-length or dependent blocks.

[Definition 6 of arXiv:2609.00702, 'On the Set-Valued Katugampola Fractional Integral: Properties and Regular Selections'] Let $F$ be a compact set-valued function such that $F:I\rightrightarrows \mathbb{R}$ and for each $u\in [a,b]$, $F(u)$ is compact. For any partition $\mathcal{T}=\{t_0,t_1,t_2,\ldots t_n\}\subset I= [a,b]$ and $n\in \mathbb{N},$ the total Jordan variation of $ F$ is
    \[ V_a^b(F)=\sup_{\mathcal{T}} \sum_{i=1}^nH_d(F(t_i),F(t_{i-1})), \]
    with the supremum over all partitions $\mathcal{T}$ of $I.$ If $V_a^b(F)< \infty,$ then we say that $F$ is of bounded variation on $I.$ 

 \begin{definition}
     A set valued map $F:I\to \mathbb{R}$ is said to be Lipschitz on $I$ with respect to $H_d$ if there exists a constant $C_F>0$ such that 
     \[ H_d(F(t_1),F(t_2)) \le C_F|t_1-t_2| \text{ for all } t_1,t_2 \in I \] 
     and such a constant $C_F$ is called the Lipschitz constant of $F.$

[Corollary 10 (Positive definiteness of the Mellin quotient) of arXiv:2606.18458, 'Stable size-biasing and the positive scale-mixture order of generalized Gaussian laws'] For $p,q>0$, the function
\[
\Phi_{p,q}(t)=\frac{2^{it/p}\Gamma((1+it)/p)\Gamma(1/q)}{2^{it/q}\Gamma((1+it)/q)\Gamma(1/p)}
\]
is a characteristic function if and only if $p\le q$. If $p<q$, then $\Phi_{p,q}$ is the characteristic function of
\[
\log V_{p,q}=\left(\frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{q}\right)\log 2+\log W,
\qquad
W=\left(S_{p/q}^{-1/q}\right)^*,
\]
where the star denotes ordinary size-biasing of the positive random variable $S_{p/q}^{-1/q}$. If $p=q$, then $\Phi_{p,p}\equiv1$.

[Proposition 22 of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186'] For every $\eps,\ka>0$,
the operator $H_{\ka,\eps}$ is self-adjoint on $L^2(D)$.
Its spectrum $\la_1(H_{\ka,\eps})\leq\la_2(H_{\ka,\eps})\leq\cdots$ is purely discrete, bounded below, and has no accumulation point.
Moreover, the corresponding eigenfunctions $\psi_1(H_{\ka,\eps}),\psi_2(H_{\ka,\eps}),\ldots$
form an orthonormal basis of $L^2(D)$. Finally, for any $f\in L^2(D)$,
\begin{align}

\mr e^{-t H_{\ka,\eps}}f=\sum_{n=1}^\infty\mr e^{-t\la_n(H_{\ka,\eps})}\big\langle\psi_n(H_{\ka,\eps}),f\big\rangle\psi_n(H_{\ka,\eps}).
\end{align}

[Lemma 14 (Consistency and rate for \textup{($ii$)}) of arXiv:2608.29465, 'Deciding When to Decide:\\Testing Operational Suboptimality Under Distributional Shift'] Suppose the assumptions of Lemma~\ref{lem:termI_consistency} hold, specifically that the envelope $F(X)$ and the Lipschitz modulus $L(X)$ are square-integrable under the target distribution $\mathbb{P}_1$.
\begin{equation}

|\textup{($ii$)}|
=\Big|
\min_{z\in\mathcal Z}
\rho^{\mathbb P_1}\!\big(f(z;X,\hat\theta)\big)
-
\rho^{\mathbb P_1}\!\big(f(\hat z_1;X,\hat\theta)\big)
\Big| \leq 2\,\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}\sup_{z\in\mathcal Z}\big|\rho^{\widehat{\mathbb P}_1'}\!\big(f(z;X,\theta)\big) - \rho^{\mathbb P_1}\!\big(f(z;X,\theta)\big)\big|
=O_p(\varepsilon_{m'}).
\end{equation}
In particular, if $\varepsilon_{m'}\to 0$ then $\textup{($ii$)}\xrightarrow{p}0$, and if $\varepsilon_{m'}\asymp (m')^{-1/2}$ then $|\textup{($ii$)}|=O_p((m')^{-1/2})$.
title: Consistency and rate for \textup{($ii$)}

body: [Theorem thm:continuity-alpha-LSI of arXiv:2602.17579, 'Non-equilibrium functional inequalities for finite Markov chains'] Let $M$ be a generator of an irreducible Markov chain on a finite state space $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$ and $\zeta\in \mathcal{P}_+(\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}})$, the set of positive probability measures on $\ensuremath{\mathbb{Z}}$. [Lemma 24 (Lemma A.5, \cite{MR3406823}) of arXiv:2609.02197, '2609.02197'] \begin{enumerate}
\item For every $\beta \in \mathbb{R}_+,$ there exists $\mu \in \mathbb{R}_+^*$ such that for all $\alpha \in \mathbb{R},$ $$\forall \left(r,f\right) \in \mathbb{R}_+^*\times \mathscr{C}^\alpha,\left\Vert G_rf\right\Vert_{\mathscr{C}^{\alpha+\beta}}\leq \mu\max\left(r^{-\frac{\beta}{4}},1\right)\left\Vert f\right\Vert_{\mathscr{C}^\alpha}.$$
\item There exists $\mu \in \mathbb{R}_+^*$ such that for any $\gamma \in \mathbb{R}$ and all $\left(U,f\right) \in \mathbb{R}_+\times\mathscr{C}^\gamma,$ the function $\begin{aligned}[t]
\left[0,U\right]&\longrightarrow \mathscr{C}^\gamma\\
m &\longmapsto G_mf
\end{aligned}$ is continuous on $\left[0,U\right]$ and $\sup_{r\in\left[0,U\right]}\left\Vert G_rf\right\Vert_{\mathscr{C}^\gamma}\leq \mu\left\Vert f\right\Vert_{\mathscr{C}^\gamma}.$
\item For every $\beta \in \left[0,4\right],$ there exists $\mu \in \mathbb{R}_+^*$ such that for all $\alpha \in \mathbb{R},$ $$\forall \left(r,f\right) \in \mathbb{R}_+^*\times \mathscr{C}^\alpha,\left\Vert G_rf-f\right\Vert_{\mathscr{C}^{\alpha-\beta}}\leq \mu\min\left(r^{\frac{\beta}{4}},1\right)\left\Vert f\right\Vert_{\mathscr{C}^\alpha}.$$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma A.5, \cite{MR3406823}

body:
[Theorem 3 (ADT dichotomy) of arXiv:2608.03575, '2608.03575'] Let $(G,\rho,\Theta)$ be an infinite, locally finite, simple, 
one-ended, ergodic, tame unimodular random ADT satisfying 
\emph{(Z1)--(Z4)}. If $\mathbb{E}[\deg(\rho)]<\infty$, then the sign of the expected geometric characteristic number determines 
the conformal type of the ADT:
\[
\mathbb{E}[L_\rho(G,\Theta)]=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
G\ \text{is VEL-parabolic},
\]
whereas
\[
\mathbb{E}[L_\rho(G,\Theta)]<0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
G\ \text{is VEL-hyperbolic}.
\]
Moreover, these conditions are equivalent to the corresponding
circle-pattern, amenability, and random-walk characterizations (see
Theorem~\ref{thm:dichotomya}). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Theorem inversions main of arXiv:2603.09008, 'On the statistics of random-to-top shuffles'] Let $I_{r,n}$ be the number of inversions after $r$ iterated random-to-top shuffles of an $n$-card deck, starting from the identity. Let $c>0$ be a constant. We have
    \[\frac{I_{cn,n}-n^2(1-e^{-2c})/4}{n^{3/2}}\Rightarrow_d\,\mathcal{N}\left(0,\frac{1+8e^{-3c}-9(1+c)e^{-4c}}{36}\right).\]
    If there exists a sequence $c_n\to\infty$ such that $r\gtrsim (n\log n)/4 + c_n n$, then
    \[\frac{I_{r,n}-n^2/4}{n^{3/2}}\Rightarrow_d\,\mathcal{N}(0,1/36).\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem inversions main of arXiv:2603.09008

body:
[Lemma 35 (Double-hive KL bound using a shared large-gap side) of arXiv:2607.04138, 'Hives from deformed GUE minor processes'] \lab{lem:doubleKLhive}
Let \(w,w'>0\) and \(u,u'\geq 0\). Let \(G_n,\widetilde G_n,G'_n,\widetilde G'_n\) be independent GUE
matrices, and set
\[
D_n=\operatorname{diag}(\operatorname{spec}(\widetilde G_n)),
\qquad
D'_n=\operatorname{diag}(\operatorname{spec}(\widetilde G'_n)).
\]
Let
\[
X_n=\sqrt n\,(wG_n+uD_n),
\qquad
Y_n=\sqrt n\,(w'G'_n+u'D'_n),
\]
and put
\[
a^2=w^2+u^2,\qquad b^2=(w')^2+(u')^2.
\]
Assume
\[
\frac{u}{w^2}=\frac{u'}{(w')^2}.
\]
Let
\[
\lambda_n=\operatorname{spec}(X_n),
\qquad
\mu_n=\operatorname{spec}(Y_n).
\]
Let \(L_n\) be the corrected regularized large-gap side from
\eqref{eq:corrected-large-gap}, and set
\[
N_n=L_n+\operatorname{diag}(X_n),
\qquad
P_n=L_n - \operatorname{diag}(Y_n).
\]
Let
\[
h_n^{(1)}\in H_n(\lambda_n,L_n;N_n),
\qquad
h_n^{(2)}\in H_n(\mu_n,L_n;P_n)
\]
be the two hives obtained, via Proposition~\ref{gt-rem}(iv), from the
large-gap construction applied to the two deformed minor processes arising from
$X_n$ and $Y_n$ respectively.  Paste them along the common side \(L_n\), with
the exterior sides in clockwise cyclic order
\[
\lambda_n,\qquad \mu_n,\qquad P_n,\qquad N_n.
\]
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.9, every node/.style={font=\small}]
  \coordinate (L) at (0,0);
  \coordinate (T) at (2,2);
  \coordinate (R) at (4,0);
  \coordinate (B) at (2,-2);
  \draw[thick] (L) -- (T) -- (R) -- (B) -- cycle;
  \draw[thick] (L) -- (R);
  \node[below left] at (1,-1) {\(\lambda_n\)};
  \node[above left] at (1,1) {\(\mu_n\)};
  \node[above right] at (3,1) {\(P_n\)};
  \node[below right] at (3,-1) {\(N_n\)};
  \node[above] at (2,0) {\(L_n\)};
\end{tikzpicture}
\end{center}
Decorate these four exterior sides, with
independent uniform Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns.  Let \(q_n^{\mathrm{dbl}}\)
be the resulting density on the four-boundary double-hive cone \(\mathbb D^4\).

Let \(p_n^{\mathrm{dbl}}\) be the maximum-entropy density on \(\mathbb D^4\)
whose four exterior sides, in clockwise cyclic order, have the same expected
quadratic moments as
\[
\lambda_n,\qquad \mu_n,\qquad P_n,\qquad N_n .
\]
Then
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(q_n^{\mathrm{dbl}}\Vert p_n^{\mathrm{dbl}}\right)
=O(n\log n).
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Double-hive KL bound using a shared large-gap side

[Definition 4 of arXiv:2607.10102, 'Dynamical mean-field limit and replica-symmetric free energy for the orthogonally-invarian'] Let $T>0$, let $D=\{d_1,\ldots,d_m\} \subset [0,T]$ be a finite subset,
and call \[[0,d_1),[d_1,d_2),\ldots,[d_{m-1},d_m),[d_m,T]\] 
the maximal intervals of $[0,T] \setminus D$. 

Fixing $T$-dependent
constants $K_0,K_1,K_2,K_3>0$ where $K_0,K_1$ define the above envelopes,
let $\mathcal{S}_\theta^+(T,D)$ be the space of all
pairs $(C_\theta,R_\theta)$ such that:
    \begin{enumerate}
    \item $C_\theta:[0,T] \times [0,T] \to \R$ is a positive-semidefinite
covariance kernel satisfying
\[C_\theta(t,t) \leq \Phi_{C_\theta}(t) \text{ for all } 0\leq t\leq T,\]
and for any maximal interval $I$ of $[0,T]\setminus D$,
        \begin{equation}
            |C_\theta(t,t)+C_\theta(s,s)-2C_\theta(t,s)| \leq  K_2|t-s|
\text{ for all } t,s \in I.
        \end{equation}
        \item $R_\theta:[0,T] \times [0,T] \to \R$ is a function satisfying
\[|R_\theta(t,s)| \leq \Phi_{R_\theta}(t-s) \text{ for all } 0 \leq s \leq t
\leq T, \qquad R_\theta(t,s)=0 \text{ for all } s>t,\]
and for any two maximal intervals $I,I'$ of $[0,T]\setminus D$,
\begin{equation}
|R_\theta(t,s)-R_\theta(t',s')| \leq K_2(|t-t'|+|s-s'|) \text{ for all } t,t'\in
I,~s,s'\in I' \text{ with } s\le t \text{ and } s'\le t'.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

Let $\mathcal{S}_g(T,D)$ be the space of all pairs
$(C_g,R_g)$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $C_g:[0,T] \times [0,T] \to \R$ is a symmetric function (not necessarily
positive-semidefinite) satisfying
\[C_g(t,t) \leq \Phi_{C_g}(t) \text{ for all } 0\leq t\leq T,\]
and for any two maximal intervals $I,I'$ of $[0,T]\setminus D$,
        \begin{equation}
|C_g(t,t)+C_g(s,s)-2C_g(t,s)| \leq K_2K_3|t-s|
\text{ for all } t,s \in I,
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}
            |C_g(t,s)-C_g(t',s')| \leq K_2K_3(\sqrt{|t-t'|}+\sqrt{|s-s'|})
\text{ for all } t,t' \in I,~s,s' \in I'.
        \end{equation}
      \item $R_g:[0,T] \times [0,T] \to \R$ is a function satisfying
\[|R_g(t,s)| \leq \Phi_{R_g}(t-s) \text{ for all } 0 \leq s \leq t \leq T,
\qquad R_g(t,s)=0 \text{ for all } s>t,\]
and for any two maximal intervals $I,I'$ of $[0,T]\setminus D$,
\begin{equation}
|R_g(t,s)-R_g(t',s')| \leq K_2K_3(|t-t'|+|s-s'|) \text{ for all } t,t'\in
I,~s,s'\in I' \text{ with } s\le t \text{ and } s'\le t'.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}
We denote by $\cS_g^+(T,D) \subset \cS_g(T,D)$
the subset of pairs $(C_g,R_g)$ where $C_g$ is positive-semidefinite.

body:
Let A be the infinitesimal generator of a strongly continuous (C_0) semigroup on a Banach space. Then the semigroup is UNIQUELY determined by A: if (S(t)) and (T(t)) are C_0-semigroups with the same generator then S(t) = T(t) for every t >= 0. Equivalently, the Laplace transform of the semigroup is the resolvent of A, and the resolvent determines the semigroup. The Hille-Yosida theorem says which operators are generators: A is the generator of a contraction semigroup exactly when A is densely defined and closed and every lambda > 0 lies in the resolvent set with ||(lambda I - A)^{-1}|| <= 1/lambda.
Both semigroups strongly continuous with the SAME generator including the same domain - two operators that agree on a common core but have different domains can generate different semigroups, which is precisely the non-uniqueness phenomenon for symmetric operators with several self-adjoint extensions.

\]
exists and is continuous of $x_1,...,x_n$. Furthermore, for any disjoint $S_1,..,S_n\subset\mathbbm{R}$,
    \begin{equation}
        \int_{S_1\times...\times S_n}\widehat{G}^\mathrm{Bub}_0(x_1,...,x_n)\prod_{i=1}^ndx_i=C^n\mu^\mathrm{Bub}_0\left[\prod_{i=1}^n\nu_{\gamma\cap\mathbbm{R}}(S_i)\right].

Hence, $\widehat{G}^\mathrm{Bub}_0(x_1,...,x_n)=C^n G^\mathrm{Bub}_0(x_1,...,x_n)$ where $G^\mathrm{Bub}_0(x_1,...,x_n)$ is defined in~(equation eq:def-gf-bub of the paper) and $C$ is the same constant as in Proposition~(prop:equivalence of the paper). Then $E_{\mathcal{N}}$ is the orthogonal projection to $\mathcal{N}$ with respect to the $L^2$ norms $\lVert\cdot\rVert_{\sigma,s}$ for any $s \in [0,1]$. body:
[Proposition prop: distance of arXiv:2609.00257, 'Stability estimates for the initial-to-final-state inverse problem'] Let $n\geq 2$ and $V_1, \, V_2 \in L^1((0, T); L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n))$ with $\| V_j \|_w < \infty$, for $j\in\{1, 2\}$ and weight $w:\mathbb{R}^n \to (0, 1)$. The quantity defined in (equation eq: distance of the paper) is a distance. 

In particular, fix $R_0>0$ and for $V \in L^1((0, T); L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n))$ with $\| V \|_w < \infty$ and $\| \mathop\mathrm{Im} {V} \|_w\leq \frac{1}{4T}$ set 

\[
\mathcal {T}_V := \{\widetilde{ V} \in  L^1((0, T); L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n)) : \,\, \| \widetilde{V} \|_w<\infty, \, \| \mathop\mathrm{Im} \widetilde{V} \|_w \leq \frac{1}{4T} \,\,

\text{and such that} \,\, 

\| V - \widetilde{V} \|_w \leq \frac{R_0}{2} \}.
\]

Then, if $\mathcal J$ is the set of the initial-to-final-state maps corresponding to potentials in $ \mathcal T_V$, the quantity (equation eq: distance of the paper) becomes a quasi-metric on the set $\mathcal J$.

body: [Definition definition strong on of arXiv:2607.18531, 'Doubly reflected BSDEs driven by Inhomogeneous simple Lévy processes: Applications to gene'] Let $\beta >0$, $Y \in \mathcal{S}^2_{\beta}$, and $\sigma,\tau \in \mathcal{T}_{0}^T$ such that $\sigma \leq \tau$ a.s. The process $Y$ is said to be a strong $\mathcal{E}^f$-supermartingale (resp. $\mathcal{E}^f$-submartingale) on $[\sigma,\tau]$, if for all $\sigma^{\star}, \tau^{\star} \in \mathcal{T}_{0}^T$ such that $\sigma \leq \sigma^{\star} \leq \tau^{\star} \leq \tau$ a.s., we have $\mathcal{E}^f_{\sigma^{\ast},\tau^{\ast}}(Y_{\eta^{\ast}}) \leq Y_{\sigma^{\ast}}$ (resp. $\mathcal{E}^f_{\sigma^{\ast},\tau^{\ast}}(Y_{\tau^{\ast}}) \geq Y_{\sigma^{\ast}}$) a.s. Finally, the process $Y$ is said to be a strong $\mathcal{E}^f$-martingale on $[\sigma,\tau]$, if it is both a strong $\mathcal{E}^f$-supermartingale and a strong $\mathcal{E}^f$-submartingale on $[\sigma,\tau]$.
title: Strong $\mathcal{E}^f$-(sub,super)martingale

[Proposition 3 of arXiv:2609.02218, 'Neumaier graphs of coherent rank five'] Let $n\geqslant8$ and $m\geqslant3$. 
Suppose $H$ is a Hadamard matrix of order $n$ with first row $h_1=\one^\transpose$, and let $\bL$ be a family of $m$ MALS of order $n-1$. 
For each $x\in\{1,\dots,n\}$, put
\[
 \mathcal C_x=\{(i,r,x):1\leqslant i\leqslant m,
 1\leqslant r\leqslant n-1\}.
\]
Then $\mathcal C_1,\dots,\mathcal C_n$ partition the vertex set of
$\Gamma(H;\bL)$ into cliques of size $m(n-1)$, each regular with nexus
$(n-2)+(m-1)(n/2-1)$.

[Lemma lem:spo_order of arXiv:2411.07809, 'Pirogov--Sinai Theory Beyond Lattices'] The relation $\prec$ has the following properties:
  \begin{enumerate}[nosep]
  \item It is a strict partial order on contours.
  \item If $\gamma'\prec\gamma$, then
    $\mathsf{Int} \gamma'\subsetneq \mathsf{Int}\gamma $. In particular,
      $|\mathsf{Int} \gamma'| < |\mathsf{Int} \gamma|$.
    \item If $\gamma\prec\gamma_1$,
        $\gamma\prec\gamma_2$, and
        $\{\gamma,\gamma_{1},\gamma_{2}\}$ are a
        compatible set of contours, then either
        $\gamma_{1}\prec\gamma_{2}$ or $\gamma_{2}\prec\gamma_{1}$.
  \end{enumerate}

Load-bearing hypothesis in the stability theorem: the approximating functions must be VISCOSITY sub/supersolutions and the convergence must be LOCALLY UNIFORM. Neither can be dropped. (1) Almost-everywhere solutions are not closed under uniform convergence: let u_k(x) := dist(x, (1/k)Z) on R. Then |u_k'| = 1 at every point of differentiability, 0 ≤ u_k ≤ 1/(2k), so u_k → 0 uniformly, yet the limit u ≡ 0 satisfies |u'| = 0 and solves the eikonal equation nowhere. The u_k are not viscosity solutions of |u'| - 1 = 0 (at each of their convex kinks, on (1/k)Z, the supersolution test with the touching slope p = 0 fails), which is exactly why the stability theorem does not apply. (2) The convergence hypothesis cannot be weakened to pointwise or weak-* convergence. What goes wrong in the a.e. setting is already visible in (1): Du_k = ±1 a.e. while Du_k ⇀ 0 weakly-*, and the nonlinear expression H(Du_k) does not pass to weak limits. For genuine viscosity sub/supersolutions the proof of the stability theorem uses LOCALLY UNIFORM convergence to move maximum points of u_k - φ to a maximum point of u - φ; for a family that is merely locally uniformly bounded the correct substitutes are the half-relaxed limits limsup* u_k and liminf* u_k (Barles-Perthame), which are respectively a subsolution and a supersolution but in general differ from a pointwise limit. (If the u_k are locally equi-Lipschitz, pointwise convergence already forces locally uniform convergence, so the gap between the two modes of convergence bites only in the absence of equicontinuity.) Auditor's check: any passage to the limit in a nonlinear first-order PDE that is justified only by 'u_k → u and each u_k solves the equation a.e.' is invalid.
Counterexample: sawtooth functions u_k = dist(·, (1/k)Z) for the eikonal equation |u'| = 1 on R
Viscosity stability requires locally uniform convergence of the solutions (convergence of the equations must also be locally uniform)
Half-relaxed limit techniques replace uniform convergence only when combined with semicontinuous envelopes, not with a.e. solutions
title: Pitfall: Stability under Uniform Limits Needs Viscosity Solutions, Not a.e. Solutions

[Proposition DriverSenguptaDiscrete of arXiv:2602.08591, 'The Yang--Mills measure on compact surfaces as a \\ universal scaling limit of lattice gau'] Let $M$ be a family of random variables, one for each horizontal edges with joint law
\[
\mathrm{d} \mathbb{M}_N\left(\left(M_{\theta\xrightarrow{r}\theta_+ }\right)_{\substack{\theta\in\Theta^N_-\\r\in R^N}}\right)

\]
Let $(U_i)_{1\le i\le 2g}$ be independent, uniformly distributed random variables in $G$, independent of $M$. 
Then $H(M,U)$ generates the same lattice gauge theory as the Driver--Sengupta measure.

Let $\{N_n\}$ be positive integer-valued rvs, independent of $\{a_n\}$, such that $N_n/n\stackrel{\mathbb{P}}{\to}K>0$, a constant, as $n\rightarrow\infty$.\vskip5pt
    
    \noindent (i) If $\{a_i\}$ are free then 
    $\frac{\mathcal{S}_{N_n}}{\sqrt{N_n}}
    
    \stackrel{*}{\to} s$.

\vskip 3pt
    \noindent (ii) If $\{a_i\}$ are independent then $\frac{\mathcal{S}_{N_n}}{\sqrt{N_n}}\stackrel{*}{\to} z$. 
    \vskip3pt
    \noindent (iii) If $\{a_i\}$ are half independent then $\frac{\mathcal{S}_{N_n}}{\sqrt{N_n}}\stackrel{*}{\to} r_S$.

[Theorem 24 (Chen, Theorems 2.3.2 and 2.4.1; Matsuda, Theorem 3.7) of arXiv:2507.06186, '2507.06186']

Let $x\in\mbb R^2$ and $t>0$ be fixed,
and suppose that $Z$ is either $B^x$ or $B^{x,x}_t$.
\begin{enumerate}[(1)]
\item Let $0\leq a<b\leq c<d\leq t$.
There exists a random variable $\be_{[a,b]\times[c,d]}(Z)$ such that
\[\be_{[a,b]\times[c,d]}(Z)=\lim_{\eps\to0}\be^\eps_{[a,b]\times[c,d]}(Z)
\qquad\text{in probability.}\]
\item If $0\leq a<b\leq t$, then
there exists a random variable $\ga_{[a,b]^2_\leq}(Z)$ such that
\[\ga_{[a,b]^2_\leq}(Z)=\lim_{\eps\to0}\Big(\be^\eps_{[a,b]^2_\leq}(Z)-\mbf E\Big[\be^\eps_{[a,b]^2_\leq}(Z)\Big]\Big)
\qquad\text{in probability.}\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: Let (S, A) be a measurable space and mu a sigma-finite measure on it, the intensity measure. A Poisson point process with intensity mu is a random counting measure N on S (N(A) is a random element of {0, 1, 2, ...} union {infinity} for each A in A, and N is a measure for each outcome) such that (i) for every A with mu(A) < infinity, N(A) has the Poisson distribution with mean mu(A), and (ii) for pairwise disjoint A_1, ..., A_k the counts N(A_1), ..., N(A_k) are independent. Such a process exists for every sigma-finite mu (construct it on each piece of finite measure by throwing a Poisson(mu(A)) number of independent points with law mu restricted to A and normalised, then superpose the pieces). When mu has no atoms the points are almost surely distinct; when mu is a multiple of Lebesgue measure on R^d the process is homogeneous with rate equal to that multiple. Basic calculus: the mapping theorem (the image of a Poisson process under a measurable map is Poisson with the image intensity), superposition (independent Poisson processes add to a Poisson process with the summed intensity), thinning (keeping each point independently with probability p(x) gives a Poisson process with intensity p mu), and Campbell's formula E sum_{x in N} f(x) = integral f d mu.

body: [Theorem of arXiv:2606.00325, 'Ergodicity for a class of stochastic Hasegawa-Mima equations with dissipation'] Let $G : \mathbb{X} \rightarrow R$ be collection of functions which determines measures. Assume that there exists a measurable $\mathbb{X}_0 \subset \mathbb{X}$ such that for any $(u_0,v_0) \in \mathbb{X}_0 \times  \mathbb{X}_0 $ and any $\phi \in G$ there exists a $\Gamma= \Gamma(u_0, v_0, \phi) \in \tilde C(\delta_{u_0}P^\mathbb{N}, \delta_{v_0}P^\mathbb{N})$ such that $\Gamma( D_\phi)>0$. Then there exist at most one ergodic invariant measure $\mu$ for $P$ with $\mu(\mathbb{X}_0) > 0$. In particular if $\mathbb{X}_0 = \mathbb{X}$, then there exists at most one, and hence ergodic, invariant measure. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body: [Definition Type path descendants of arXiv:2607.16911, 'Multipartite random graphs with given degrees: local limit, revisiting the giant, distance'] Consider any directed edge $e=(p(v),v)$ in $\mathbb T$ where $v\neq \varnothing$, with type $T(e)=(T_{p(v)},T_v)$. Let $s_0=T_{p(v)}$ and $s_1=T_v$, and for a type path $\pi=(s_0\rightarrow s_0s_1 \rightarrow \dots \rightarrow s_0s_1\dots s_k)$ in $\mathscr T(T_{p(v)})$, we inductively define a set $C(e;\pi)$ of descendants of $v$ as follows. If $k=2$ then $C(e;\pi)=\mathbf c_\mathbb T(v;s_2)$, while if $k>2$, then $$C(e;\pi)=\cup_{u\in \mathbf c_\mathbb T(v;s_2)}C((v,u);\pi^{(1)}),$$ where recall $\pi^{(1)}$ from (equation eq:def_pi_uppercut of the paper).

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2607.29495, 'Fast Mixing for Low-Temperature Potts Models via Poisson Trees'] Let $\theta>1$ and $\kappa,K>0$ be arbitrary reals.  Then, for all large enough real $d$,  for  all integer $q\geq d^{\theta}$, for all real $\beta > (1+\frac{1.01}{\theta})\frac{\log q}{d}$, the following holds for all large~enough~$n$.

    
      Let $T$ be a Poisson tree with parameter $d$,  truncated at level~$h=\lfloor K\log_d n\rfloor$. Then, with probability $\geq 1 -n^{-\kappa}$ over  $T$,  the Glauber dynamics for the Potts distribution $\mu^{\pl}_{T^h;q,\beta}$ with monochromatic boundary condition has mixing time $\leq |V(T)|n^{o(1)}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
Random variables X_n converge in distribution to X if and only if their characteristic functions converge pointwise, phi_{X_n}(t) -> phi_X(t) for every t. More usefully: if phi_{X_n}(t) -> psi(t) pointwise and psi is continuous at t = 0, then psi is the characteristic function of some random variable X and X_n -> X in distribution. This is the engine that turns the characteristic-function computation in the Central Limit Theorem into convergence in distribution.

Here the random variables are real-valued and phi_X(t)=E[exp(i t X)]. In the forward direction X_n converging in distribution to X implies the stronger conclusion that, for every T<infinity, sup_{|t|<=T}|phi_{X_n}(t)-phi_X(t)| tends to zero. Equivalently, for probability measures mu_n on R, weak convergence to mu gives convergence of their characteristic functions uniformly on every compact subset of R; the pointwise-convergence converse still requires continuity of the limit at 0.
for the converse, the limit function is continuous at 0

Let H and B be jointly translation-invariant disjoint binary fields on Z^d, marking holes and active sites. Use graph distance, put h=E H(0)>0, S=sum_{0<|x|<=2R}E[H(0)H(x)], T=sum_{|x|<=2R}E[H(0)B(x)], and let B_R be the graph ball of integer radius R>=1. The probability that the origin is strictly nearer a hole than an active site is at least |B_R|(h-T)_+^2/(h+S). Consequently in d=4, if h_t tends to zero, R_t=floor(b h_t^(-1/4)) for fixed b>0, S_t<=C h_t and T_t<=theta h_t eventually with C finite and theta<1, the closer-hole probability has positive liminf. {"artifact_digest":"sha256:e14d6f9533aba8111cd4fb6f84e823b67a7db654c6592746fbad34ebbd519242","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/e1/e14d6f9533aba8111cd4fb6f84e823b67a7db654c6592746fbad34ebbd519242.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:a31d174696b39217c23e18b76d86886c8a46b0b980c4086414d1bd398b3b5ce2","bundle_entry_key":"i0005-c7","bundle_id":"population.i0005-palm-reductions-and-comparisons-004","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"interacting particle systems and comparison fields","draft":"w661/bundle_004.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.particle-hole:stationary-hole-active-mixed-second-moment-covering-draft","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"# I0005-C7 v1: an overlap criterion using mixed hole–active moments

Novelty: UNCHECKED. A direct first/second-moment geometric reduction, compared against the source's isolation argument and own C2. No earlier separate source found in the limited I0005 search. This does not prove its required moment estimates in the fixed-law d4 process.

Fix d≥1. Let H(x),B(x) be jointly translation-invariant binary fields on Z^d indicating holes and active sites, with H(x)B(x)=0 and h=EH(0)>0. Distances are graph distances. For an integer R≥1, put V_R=|B_R(0)| and

S_{2R}=sum_{0<|z|_1≤2R}E[H(0)H(z)],
T_{2R}=sum_{|z|_1≤2R}E[H(0)B(z)].

The z=0 term in T is zero by disjointness. If F is the event that the origin is strictly closer to some hole than to every active site, then

P(F)≥V_R (h−T_{2R})_+²/(h+S_{2R}).

Thus a time-indexed d4 configuration with h_t→0 has positive closer-hole liminf if, for some fixed b>0,C<∞,θ<1 and R_t=floor(bh_t^−1/4),

S_{2R_t}≤C h_t and T_{2R_t}≤θ h_t

eventually. The resulting lower limit is at least (2^4/4!)b^4(1−θ)²/(1+C). Unlike C2, this criterion allows an arbitrarily large fixed finite conditional expected number of neighboring holes; it requires a separate hole–active bound instead.

## Proof

Define G(x)=H(x)1_{there is no active site within distance 2R of x}. Its intensity g satisfies g≥h−T_{2R}, by applying the union bound to H(0) together with the active-site events. Since G≥0, g≥(h−T_{2R})_+.

If G(x)=1 and w is within distance R of x, then any active site y satisfies |y−x|_1>2R. Consequently

|w−y|_1≥|y−x|_1−|w−x|_1>2R−R≥|w−x|_1.

Thus every site within radius R of a G-center is strictly nearer a hole than every active site. If the active set is empty the same conclusion holds, with its nearest distance interpreted as infinity.

Let M=sum_{x∈B_R(0)}G(x). Then {M>0}⊂F and EM=V_R g by translation invariance. Since G≤H and H is binary,

EM²≤sum_{x∈B_R}EH(x)+sum_{x,y∈B_R,x≠y}E[H(x)H(y)]
≤V_R h+V_R sum_{0<|z|_1≤2R}E[H(0)H(z)]
=V_R(h+S_{2R}).

The second inequality follows by fixing x and enlarging the possible differences y−x to B_{2R}\{0}; all terms are nonnegative. Cauchy–Schwarz gives (EM)²≤P(M>0)EM². Hence

P(F)≥P(M>0)≥V_R g²/(h+S_{2R})≥V_R(h−T_{2R})_+²/(h+S_{2R}).

The denominator is positive since h>0. If EM=0 the asserted bound is zero, so no division by a vanishing EM occurs. All sums are finite and require no independence.

Finally, V_R=(2^d/d!)R^d+O_d(R^{d−1}+1). For d4 and the stipulated R_t, h_tV_{R_t}→(2^4/4!)b^4. Substituting the moment bounds and taking lower limits proves the stated sufficient condition and constant.

## The missing input changes, rather than disappears

In the sparse particle–hole model one can bound B by active multiplicities A. Therefore it is sufficient to prove the same T-bound with E[H(0)A(z)]. The source's two-hole estimate supplies no such mixed bound in d4. A product FKG argument conditioned on initial randomness alone is not enough after averaging the walk instructions; no negative association of the full dynamics is assumed here.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:1c3dcea0c0d9581690e0b39d8bdb7899bedd14af1bcebf941ddc1ef05029982c","revision_digest":"sha256:688bd96428f9a3df4c2ae0cc3ed5e78ffcc21b789685add6b2ee28f2fdb1b8bf","source_id":"own-work:w661:I0005-C7:v1","source_revision":"v1; 2026-10-14T06:00:17.3108952+03:00","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

Let X be a real random variable with E[X^2] < infinity, G a sub-sigma-field, and Var(X | G) = E[(X - E[X | G])^2 | G]. Then Var(X) = E[Var(X | G)] + Var(E[X | G]), both terms on the right are finite and nonnegative, and so Var(E[X | G]) <= Var(X), with equality if and only if X = E[X | G] almost surely, that is, X is almost surely equal to a G-measurable variable.
(Omega, F, P) is a probability space and G is a sub-sigma-field of F
X is a real random variable with E[X^2] < infinity

[Thm Existence-r of arXiv:2506.01746, '\bf Optimal Bregman quantization: existence and uniqueness of optimal quantizers revisited'] Let $r\!\in [2, +\infty)$. Assume that  the distribution $P$ of $X$ satisfies the  moment assumption~(equation eq:Integrabilite of the paper), that  

$F$ is $C^2$ on $U$ with $\nabla^2F(x)$ (symmetric) positive definite for  every $x\!\in U$.
Assume that at every $\bar x \!\in\hat\partial U =  \partial   U$, 

\noindent either
\begin{equation} 
\nabla^2F \mbox{ can  be continuously extended at } \bar x \mbox{ and } \nabla^2F(\bar x) \mbox{ is (symmetric) positive definite}
\end{equation}
or \\
\indent the l.s.c. extensions $\phi_{_F}(\xi, \cdot)$  on $ \bar U^{\widehat{\mathbb{R}^d}}$ satisfy at $\bar x$ 
\begin{equation}

 \forall\, \xi \!\in U, \qquad \phi_{_F}(\xi, \bar x) =\displaystyle  \sup_{x\in U}\phi_{_F}(\xi,x).
\end{equation}
Finally,  if $U$ is unbounded, assume that $\bar x = \infty$ satisfies the above condition~(equation eq:Cond-rb2 of the paper).

\medskip
\noindent $(a)$ Then for every $n\ge1$ there exists an $n$-tuple $x^{(r,n)}= \big(x^{(r,n)}_1, \ldots, x^{(r,n)}_n\big) \!\in U^n$ which minimizes $G_{r,n}$ over $U^n$. Moreover, if  the support (in $U$) of the distribution $P$ has at least $n$ points then $x^{(r,n)}$ has pairwise distinct components and $P\big(\mathring C_i(x^{(r,n)})\big)>0$ for every $i\!\in \{1,\ldots,n\}$.

\smallskip
\noindent $(b)$ The distribution  $P$ assigns no mass to the   boundary of  any $\phi_{_F}$-Bregman--Voronoi partitions of $x^{(n)}$ i.e.
\[
P\left (\bigcup_{i=1}^n\partial C_i\big( x^{(r,n)})\right) = 0
\]
and $x^{(r,n)}$ satisfies the $(r,\phi_{_F})$-stationary (or $(r,\phi_{_F})$-master) equation
\begin{equation}
 x^{(r,n)}_i = \frac{ \int_{C_i(x^{(r,n)})}\xi \phi_{_F}( \xi,x^{(r,n)}_i )^{\frac r2-1}P(\mathrm{d}\xi)}{\int_{C_i(x^{(r,n)})}\phi_{_F}( \xi,x^{(r,n)}_i )^{\frac r2-1}P(\mathrm{d}\xi) } , \quad  i=1,\ldots,n.
\end{equation}
 
\noindent $(c)$ The sequence $\displaystyle G_{r,n}\big( x^{(r,n)}\big) = \min_{U^n} G_{r,n}$ decreases as long as it is not $0$ and converges to $0$ as $n$ goes to infinity. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma lem:gluing_very_good of arXiv:2508.18809, '{\bf Critical long-range percolation III: The upper critical dimension}'] Suppose that $d=3\alpha$ and that the modified hydrodynamic condition does \emph{not} hold. 
\begin{enumerate}
  \item If $\liminf_{r\to \infty} r^{-\alpha}\mathbb E_{\beta_c,r}|K| < \infty$, then there exists an unbounded set $\mathscr{R} =\{r_1,r_2,\ldots\} \subset [1,\infty)$ 
with $r_{i+1} \geq 32 r_i$ for every $i \geq 1$ such that $\sup_{r\in \mathscr{R}} r^{-\alpha}\mathbb E_{\beta_c,r}|K|<\infty$ and for each $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\eta>0$ and $n_0<\infty$ such that
\[
  \mathbb E \left[ \mathbbm{1}(0 \nxleftrightarrow{r} y)|K^r||K^r_y| \mathbbm{1}\left(\sum_{i=n+1}^{n+N} \mathbbm{1}\left(r_i \text{ is $(y,\eta)$-very good}\right) \leq \eta N\right)\right] \leq \varepsilon (\mathbb E|K^r|)^2.
\]
for every $n,N \geq n_0$, $r \geq r_{n+N}$, and $y\in \mathbb Z^d$ with $\|y\|\leq r_{n+1}$.
\item If $\liminf_{r\to \infty} r^{-\alpha}\mathbb E_{\beta_c,r}|K| = \infty$, then there exists $0<\lambda_0 \leq 1$ such if $0<\lambda \leq \lambda_0$ then there exists an unbounded set $\mathscr{R}=\mathscr{R}_\lambda =\{r_1,r_2,\ldots\} \subset [1,\infty)$ 
with $r_{i+1} \geq 32 r_i$ for every $i \geq 1$ such that for each $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\eta=\eta_\lambda>0$ and $n_0=n_{0,\lambda}<\infty$ such that
\[
  \tilde\mathbb E_{\lambda} \left[ \mathbbm{1}(0 \nxleftrightarrow{r} y)|K^r||K^r_y| \mathbbm{1}\left(\sum_{i=n+1}^{n+N} \mathbbm{1}\left(r_i \text{ is $(y,\eta)$-very good}\right) \leq \eta N\right)\right] \leq \varepsilon (\tilde\mathbb E_{\lambda}|K^r|)^2.
\]
for every $n,N \geq n_0$, $r \geq r_{n+N}$, and $y\in \mathbb Z^d$ with $\|y\|\leq r_{n+1}$.
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2606.17859, 'Full $\Gamma-$expansion for the level-two large deviation rate functionals of non-reversib'] Fix $\lambda>0$, $1\leq p\leq \widehat{\mf q}$ and a bounded function
$g\colon \mc S_p \to \bb R$. Let $\phi_{p,\epsilon}$ be the solution of
\eqref{smooth_resolvent_eq}. Then, for every
$x\in \bb T\setminus \mc M_p$,
\begin{align*}

&\Big| \,\phi_{p,\epsilon}(x) \,-\, \phi_{p,\epsilon}(m_p^-(x))
\, \bb P_x^\epsilon \big[\, \tau(m_p^-(x))<\tau(m_p^+(x)) \,\big]
\,-\,\phi_{p,\epsilon}(m_p^+(x))\, 
\bb P_x^\epsilon \big[\, \tau(m_p^+(x))<\tau(m_p^-(x)) \,\big] \,\Big|
\notag\\
&\quad \leq 2\, \Vert G_g\Vert_\infty \,\bb E_x^\epsilon
\Big[\tau(m_p^-(x),m_p^+(x))\,/\,\theta^{(p)}_\epsilon\Big]\,. 
\end{align*}
In particular, 
\begin{equation*}
\liminf_{\epsilon\to 0}\inf_{x\in \bb T}\phi_{p,\epsilon}(x)
\,\ge \, \min_{\mc M\in \mc S_p}f_p(\mc M) \,.
\end{equation*}

[Lemma 19 of arXiv:2609.02267, 'Locally Conformally Flat Manifolds with Positive Scalar Curvature: Kleinian Groups, Moduli'] Let \(\Gamma\) be a non-elementary convex cocompact Kleinian group, and let
$ C:=\mathrm{CH}(\Gamma)$
be the closed convex hull of \(\Lambda(\Gamma)\).  Then \(C\) is a
nonempty closed convex subset of \(\mathbb H^{n+1}\).  Equipped with its
intrinsic metric, \(C\) is a proper geodesic
\(\operatorname{CAT}(-1)\) space, hence a Gromov-hyperbolic space, and
\(\Gamma\) acts on \(C\) properly, cocompactly, and isometrically.
Moreover, \(\partial_\infty^{i}C=\Lambda(\Gamma)\).

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2606.15843, 'Long-time behaviour of DLRA for SDEs'] Given any invariant probability measure $\pi^*$ of Eqn.~\eqref{eq:DO}  whose second marginal $$\mu^*(A):=\int_{V_r(\bb R^d)}\pi^*(\rrm du, A), \quad\text{for any }A\in \scr B(\bb R^r),$$
    satisfies $\rrm{det}(C_{\mu^*}) \neq 0$, there exists another invariant probability measure $\widetilde\pi^*\in\scr P_2(V_r(\bb R^d)\times\bb R^r)$ that is $O(r)$-invariant. Moreover, define $$\widetilde\mu^*(A)=\int_{V_r(\bb R^d)}\widetilde\pi^*(\rrm du, A), \quad\text{for any }A\in \scr B(\bb R^r).$$
    Then we have $\rrm{det}(C_{\widetilde\mu^*}) \neq 0$.

[Lemma of arXiv:2608.28504, 'Global $\bm\infty$-categories and global Thom spectra'] Any automorphism of ${\textup{O}}(2)$ is an inner automorphism.
    \begin{proof}
        As ${\textup{SO}}(2)$ is the identity component of ${\textup{O}}(2)$, $f$ restricts to an automorphism of ${\textup{SO}}(2)$. By [broecker-tom-dieck]*{Proposition~II.8.1}, we therefore need to have $f(A)=A$ or $f(A)=A^{-1}$ for all $A\in{\textup{SO}}(2)$. As $A$ and $A^{-1}$ become conjugate in ${\textup{O}}(2)$ via the reflection $R\coloneqq\begin{psmallmatrix}-1&0\\0&1\end{psmallmatrix}$, we see that $f\colon{\textup{O}}(2)\to{\textup{O}}(2)$ preserves conjugacy classes of elements in ${\textup{SO}}(2)$. 
        
        On the other hand, any matrix in ${\textup{O}}(2)\smallsetminus{\textup{SO}}(2)$ has $-1$ and $1$ as eigenvalues and hence is conjugate to $R$. As $f$ also has to preserve ${\textup{O}}(2)\smallsetminus{\textup{SO}}(2)$, we conclude that $f$ preserves also the conjugacy class of elements in ${\textup{O}}(2)\smallsetminus{\textup{SO}}(2)$, so that it is conjugate to the identity by Lemma~(lemma:conjugate-to-On of the paper).
    \end{proof} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Lemma 26 of arXiv:2605.13512, '2605.13512'] For any fixed $(x,t)$ and $h >0$ we can find functions $d(h) \le 2e(h)=o(h)$ and a path ${\bf w} \in \mathcal H^{v_0}_{x,t- e(h)}$ such that: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item ${\bf w}(0) = (w_1(0), -v_0(w_1(0)))$ and ${\bf w}(t-e(h)) = (x, -v(x,t)),$
\item there exists a constant $C_{\max}(x,t) \in (0,\infty)$ and a $\xi_h \in [-C_{\max}(x,t), C_{\max}(x,t)]$ so that $${\bf w}(t-h-d(h)) := (x_h, y_h) = (x - h\xi_h, g^{z_0}(x_h-z_0, t-h)-v_0(z_0)),$$
where $-v(x,t) = g^{z_0}(x-z_0, t)-v_0(z_0)$,
\item we have the following equality
\be
v(x,t) \le v(x_h, t-h-d(h)) - \int_{t-h-d(h)}^{t-e(h)}\tilde c({\bf w}(s))\psi \left( \frac{w_1'(s)}{\tilde c({\bf w}(s))} \right)\,ds.
\ee
\item and 
\be 
        \sup_{s\in[t-h-d(h),\,t-e(h)]}
        \left|
        {\bf w}(s)-(x,-v(x,t))
        \right|
        \longrightarrow 0
        \qquad\text{as }h\downarrow0.
\ee
\end{enumerate}

[Proposition 24 (Heisenberg representation facts) of arXiv:2605.27212, '2605.27212'] Let \(\Heis=W\times\Fp\) be the group in \eqref{eq:heis-law}, with
\(\dim W=2m\).  For \(\xi\in W^*\), define
\[
    \chi_\xi(v,z)=\psi(\xi(v)).
\]
The following facts hold.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}, leftmargin=*]
    \item The functions \(\chi_\xi\), \(\xi\in W^*\), are exactly the
    irreducible complex representations of \(\Heis\) on which the center
    \(\{0\}\times\Fp\) acts trivially.
    \item For each \(\lambda\in\Fp^\times\), there is an irreducible unitary
    representation \(\rho_\lambda\) of \(\Heis\), of dimension \(p^m\), such
    that
    \[
        \rho_\lambda(0,z)=\psi(\lambda z)I,\qquad z\in\Fp.
    \]
    \item If \(\sigma\) is any irreducible complex representation of \(\Heis\)
    on which the center does not act trivially, then there is a unique
    \(\lambda\in\Fp^\times\) such that
    \[
        \sigma(0,z)=\psi(\lambda z)I,\qquad z\in\Fp.
    \]
    For this \(\lambda\), there is a unitary map \(U\) from the representation
    space of \(\sigma\) to that of \(\rho_\lambda\) such that
    \[
        U\sigma(g)U^{-1}=\rho_\lambda(g),\qquad g\in\Heis.
    \]
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if \(g=(v,z)\), \(g'=(w,t)\), and \(\lambda\in\Fp^\times\), then
\begin{equation}
    \rho_\lambda(g)\rho_\lambda(g')
    =
    \psi(\lambda\omega(v,w))\rho_\lambda(g')\rho_\lambda(g).
\end{equation}

[Lemma lem:positive-finite-energy-potential of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] For every finite positive Radon measure $\mu$ with $I_D(\mu)<\infty$, there is
a unique potential $U_D\mu\inH$ characterized by
\[
 \mathcal E(U_D\mu,v)=\int_D\widetilde v\,d\mu,
 \qquad v\inH.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \mathcal E(U_D\mu,U_D\mu)=I_D(\mu),
\]
and its quasi-continuous representative is given by
\begin{equation}
 \widetilde{U_D\mu}(z)
 =\int_DG_D(z,w)\,\mu(dw)
 \qquad\text{for $\mathcal E$-q.e. }z\in D.
 
\end{equation}

$$P(s)=\frac{\binom{s+a-1}{s}\binom{n-s+b-1}{n-s}}{\binom{n+a+b-1}{n}}$$
with the following convention for the quantities in brackets,
$$\binom{n}{k}=\frac{(2n+1)!!}{(2k+1)!!(2n-2k+1)!!}$$
where $M!!=(M-1)(M-3)\ldots$ for any integer $M\in\mathbb N$, as usual.

body: Both hypotheses are used, and each failure has a clean counterexample on the unit disk D. (1) The set E where pointwise convergence is assumed must have an accumulation point in the open set U, not merely on its boundary. Take a_k = 1 - 1/k^2, so that the sum of (1 - a_k) converges, and let B be the Blaschke product with simple zeros exactly at the a_k; B is holomorphic on D with |B| < 1 and B is not identically zero (B(0) = product of the a_k, nonzero). The sequence f_n = (-1)^n B is uniformly bounded by 1 and converges (to 0) at every point of E = {a_k}, a set whose only accumulation point is the boundary point 1, yet f_n diverges at every point where B ≠ 0, for instance at 0. (2) Local uniform boundedness cannot be dropped: on U = D(0,2) the functions f_n(z) = z^n converge pointwise on E = D (a set with plenty of interior accumulation points) but diverge for |z| > 1; the family is not bounded on compact subsets of U. (3) Connectedness of U matters in the same way as for the identity theorem: if U has several components, the hypothesis must be met on each component separately, since the identity theorem step is applied there. When auditing an argument that upgrades pointwise convergence of holomorphic functions to locally uniform convergence, check exactly these three things, and check that the pointwise limits are finite complex numbers rather than ∞.
title: Pitfall: Vitali–Porter needs the convergence set to accumulate inside the domain, and local boundedness

[Definition def:densities of arXiv:2411.12149, 'Airy limit for $\beta$-additions through Dunkl operators'] For $x>0$, $h,g> 0$, we define 
    \[\mathbf{F}(x;h,g)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi x}}\left(\exp\left(-\frac{(g-h)^{2}}{2x}\right)-\exp\left(-\frac{(g+h)^{2}}{2x}\right)\right).\]
    Note that (by reflection principle) $\mathbf{F}(x;h,g)$ is the transition density of a Brownian bridge from $g$ to $h$, conditioned on staying nonnegative.

    Let \[\mathbf{F}_{0}(x,h)=\frac{2h}{\sqrt{2\pi x^{3}}}\exp\left(-\frac{h^{2}}{2x}\right),\]
and let \[\mathbf{F}_{0,0}(x)=\frac{2}{\sqrt{2\pi x^{3}}}.\]

(Y^{N_j,n})_{n\ge0},
(\mathcal M^{N_j,n})_{n\ge0}
\right)
\!.
\]

\item[(ii)] We have
\begin{equation}
\left(
(\widetilde Y^{N_j,n})_{n\ge0},
(\widetilde{\mathcal M}^{N_j,n})_{n\ge0}
\right)
\longrightarrow
\left(
(\widetilde Y^n)_{n\ge0},
(\widetilde{\mathcal M}^n)_{n\ge0}
\right)
\quad \widetilde{\mathbb P}\text{-a.s. in }
E^{\mathbb N_0}\times E^{\mathbb N_0}.
\end{equation}

\item[(iii)] For every \(q\in(0,1/4)\),
\[
\sum_{n=0}^\infty
q^n\widetilde{\mathbb E}\sup_{t\le T}
\|\widetilde Y_t^n\|_{H^{-\beta_\ast}}^2
<\infty.
\]
This follows directly from \eqref{eq:weighted-apriori-bound},
\textup{(i)--(ii)}, Fatou's lemma, and the lower semicontinuity on \(E\) of
\(z\mapsto\sup_{t\le T}\|z_t\|_{H^{-\beta_\ast}}^2\). Together with
continuity in \(E\), the same bound gives weakly continuous paths in
\(H^{-\beta_\ast}\) for every \(\widetilde Y^n\).
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Skorokhod representation

body:
[Defn def-supercritical-map of arXiv:2506.18827, 'Random walk reflected off of infinity, with applications to uniform spanning forests and s'] Fix ${\mathbf{c}} \in (1,25)$, let $Q = \sqrt{\frac{{\mathbf{c}}-1}{6}} \in (0,2)$, and let $\bf q$ be a non-generic critical weight sequence of type 2 (Definition~(def-critical of the paper)). 
Also let $k\in\mathbbm N$. 
We inductively define random planar maps $\{\mathfrak M_j\}_{j\in\mathbbm N}$, each of which is equipped with a set of \textbf{holes} $\mathcal H_j \subset \mathcal F \mathfrak M_j$, as follows. 
\begin{itemize}
\item
Let $\mathfrak M_0$ be a Boltzmann map with perimeter $2k$ and weights $\bf q$ (Definition~(def-critical of the paper)) and let $\mathcal H_0$ be the set of faces of $\mathfrak M_0$ other than the external face. 
\item 
Inductively, assume that $j \geq 1$ and $(\mathfrak M_{j-1}, \mathcal H_{j-1})$ has been defined. 
Conditional on $(\mathfrak M_{j-1} , \mathcal H_{j-1})$, let $\{Y_h\}_{h \in \mathcal H_{j-1}}$ be i.i.d.\ random variables with the uniform distribution on $\{-1,1\}$, indexed by the holes $ h\in \mathcal H_{j-1}$. Conditional on $(\mathfrak M_{j-1} , \mathcal H_{j-1}, \{Y_h\}_{h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}})$, for each $h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}$, sample a ring $R_h$ from the uniform distribution on rings of outer perimeter $\deg(h)$ and inner perimeter\footnote{
The reason for the strange looking quantity $\exp\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft( \pm \frac{\pi\sqrt{4-Q^2}}{Q}  \aftergroup\egroup\originalright)$ in~(equation eqn-perimeter-ratio of the paper) is that this quantity coincides with the ratio of the LQG lengths of a CLE$_4$ loop as measured from inside and outside the loop in the coupling of~[ag-supercritical-cle4], see~[ag-supercritical-cle4]. 
}
\begin{equation}  
2 \mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft\lfloor \exp\mathopen{}\mathclose\bgroup\originalleft( Y_h  \frac{\pi\sqrt{4-Q^2}}{Q}  \aftergroup\egroup\originalright) \frac{\deg(h)}{2} \aftergroup\egroup\originalright\rfloor  .
\end{equation}  
We take the rings $R_h$ to be conditionally independent given $(\mathfrak M_{j-1} , \mathcal H_{j-1}, \{Y_h\}_{h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}})$. 
For each $h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}$, we identify the edges of the outer boundary of $R_h$ to the edges of the boundary of $h$ in cyclic order. There are $\deg(h)$ ways to do this identification. We choose one way uniformly at random. 
\item 
Conditional on $(\mathfrak M_{j-1} , \mathcal H_{j-1}, \{R_h\}_{h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}})$, for each $h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}$ such that $R_h$ has non-zero inner perimeter, we sample a Boltzmann map $M_h$ of perimeter equal to the inner perimeter~(equation eqn-perimeter-ratio of the paper) of $R_h$ (we take the maps $M_h$ to be conditionally independent). We then identify the edges of the boundary of $M_h$ to the edges of the inner boundary of $R_h$ in cyclic order (as above, we choose one of the possible ways to do the identification uniformly at random). 
\item 
We define $\mathfrak M_j$ to be the map which is the union of $\mathfrak M_{j-1}$, $\{R_h\}_{h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}}$, and $\{M_h\}_{h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}}$, subject to the above identifications. We define $\mathcal H_j$ to be the set of faces of $\mathfrak M_j$ which are also faces of $M_h$ for some $h\in\mathcal H_{j-1}$. 
\item We define $\mathcal M = \mathcal M_k$ to be the planar map which is the increasing union of the maps $\mathfrak M_j$, and call it the \textbf{supercritical random planar map of central charge ${\mathbf{c}}$ and perimeter $2k$}. We define $\mathcal L_k$ to be the collection of simple loops on the dual of $\mathcal M_k$ such that each loop traverses the faces of one of the rings in the above construction (these loops are shown in red in Figure~(fig-model of the paper)). 
\end{itemize}
title: Defn def-supercritical-map of arXiv:2506.18827

Let (M,g) be a complete, simply connected Riemannian manifold with nonpositive sectional curvature at every point (K <= 0 for every tangent 2-plane at every point). Then for any point p in M, the exponential map exp_p: T_pM -> M is a diffeomorphism. In particular M is diffeomorphic to R^n, n = dim M, and any two points of M are joined by a unique geodesic.

[Lemma 5 of arXiv:2609.02779, '2609.02779'] There exist $\rho_0,\mu,C,\lambda_0,e_0>0$ such that the following holds for
$0<\rho\le\rho_0$ and every real interval $[a,b]$.

\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
\item If $0<\lambda\le\lambda_0$ and
$Z_\lambda:[a,b]\to T^*M$ is the lift of a $u_\lambda$-calibrated curve with
\[
 d_{T^*M}(Z_\lambda(s),\Gamma)<2\rho
 \qquad\text{for every }a\le s\le b,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 d_{T^*M}(Z_\lambda(s),\Gamma)
 \le C\rho\bigl(e^{-\mu(s-a)}+e^{-\mu(b-s)}\bigr)+C\lambda
 \qquad\text{for every }a\le s\le b.
\end{equation}

\item If $Z^0:[a,b]\to T^*M$ is a conservative orbit satisfying
\[
 \dot Z^0=X_H(Z^0),
 \qquad
 H(Z^0(s))\equiv c+e,
 \qquad |e|\le e_0,
\]
and
\[
 d_{T^*M}(Z^0(s),\Gamma)<2\rho
 \qquad\text{for every }a\le s\le b,
\]
then
\begin{equation}
 d_{T^*M}(Z^0(s),\Gamma)
 \le C\rho\bigl(e^{-\mu(s-a)}+e^{-\mu(b-s)}\bigr)+C|e|
 \quad\text{for every }a\le s\le b.
\end{equation}
\end{enumerate}

body:
[Defn rational SLE of arXiv:2505.14762, 'Multiple radial SLE($\kappa$) and quantum Calogero-Sutherland system'] In the unit disk $\mathbb{D}$, let $e^{i\theta} \in \partial\mathbb{D}$ be the growth point, and let $u_1 = e^{i\theta_1}, u_2 = e^{i\theta_2}, \dots, u_k = e^{i\theta_k} \in \overline{\mathbb{D}}$ be marked points. A symmetric double divisor $(\boldsymbol{\sigma}^+, \boldsymbol{\sigma}^-)$ assigns a charge distribution on $e^{i\theta}$ and $\{u_1, \dots, u_k\}$, where
\[
\boldsymbol{\sigma}^+ = a \cdot e^{i\theta} + \sum_{j=1}^{k} \sigma_j \cdot u_j,
\quad \text{and} \quad
\boldsymbol{\sigma}^- = \overline{\boldsymbol{\sigma}^+}|_{\mathbb{D}},
\]
and the total charge satisfies the neutrality condition $(\mathrm{NC}_b)$.

We define the rational $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa[\boldsymbol{\sigma}]$ as a random normalized conformal map $g_t(z)$, with initial condition $g_0(z) = z$ and normalization $g_t'(0) = e^{-t}$. It evolves according to the radial Loewner equation:
\[
\partial_t g_t(z) = g_t(z) \frac{e^{i\theta(t)} + g_t(z)}{e^{i\theta(t)} - g_t(z)}, \quad g_0(z) = z.
\]

Let $h_t(z)$ be the covering map of $g_t(z)$, defined via
\[
e^{i h_t(z)} = g_t(e^{i z}),
\]
so that $h_0(z) = z$, and
\[
\partial_t h_t(z) = \cot\left( \frac{h_t(z) - \theta(t)}{2} \right).
\]

The driving function $\theta(t)$ evolves as
\[
d\theta(t) = \frac{\partial \log \mathcal{Z}(\theta)}{\partial \theta} \, dt + \sqrt{\kappa} \, dB_t,
\]
where the Coulomb gas partition function is
\begin{equation} 
\mathcal{Z}(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \prod_{j < k} \sin\left( \frac{\theta_j - \theta_k}{2} \right)^{\sigma_j \sigma_k} 
\cdot \prod_j e^{\frac{i}{2} \sigma_j (\sigma_0 - \sigma_\infty)\theta_j}.
\end{equation}

The flow map $g_t$ is well-defined up to the first time $\tau$ when $\zeta(t) = g_t(w)$ for some $w$ in the support of $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$. For any $z \in \mathbb{D}$, the process $t \mapsto g_t(z)$ is defined up to time $\tau_z \wedge \tau$, where $\tau_z$ is the first time such that $g_t(z) = e^{i\theta(t)}$. Define the associated hull by
\[
K_t = \left\{ z \in \overline{\mathbb{D}} : \tau_z \le t \right\}.
\]

Furthermore, the law of the rational $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa[\boldsymbol{\sigma}]$ Loewner chain is invariant under Möbius transformations $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{D})$, up to a time change, due to the conformal covariance of the Coulomb gas correlation functions. Thus, we define rational $\mathrm{SLE}_\kappa[\boldsymbol{\sigma}]$ in a general simply connected domain $\Omega$ via a conformal map $\phi: \Omega \to \mathbb{D}$ by pulling back the flow.
title: Rational SLE

[Lem lem-harmonic-compat of arXiv:2506.18827, 'Random walk reflected off of infinity, with applications to uniform spanning forests and s'] Let $\mathcal A\subset \mathcal B \subset \mathcal V\mathcal G$ be non-empty finite vertex sets.  
Let $\phi : \mathcal A\to\mathbbm R$ and let $h^\phi$ be the energy-minimizing function on $\mathcal G$ with $h^\phi|_{\mathcal A} = \phi$, as in Proposition~(prop-min-harmonic of the paper).

[Proposition 15 of arXiv:2609.02416, '2609.02416'] Let $\Omega=(\alpha,\beta)$ be bounded and assume $q\in C^1(\overline \Omega)$. Let $\phi_\Omega$ be the positive principal eigenfunction associated with $\Lp(\Omega)$. Then the formal adjoint
\[
\cA_\Omega^*v=d\left(\int_\Omega J(x-y)v(y)\,dy-v(x)\right)-(qv)'(x)+a(x)v(x)
\]
has a positive eigenfunction $\phi_\Omega^*\in C^1(\Omega)\cap C(\overline \Omega)$ satisfying
\[
\cA_\Omega^*\phi_\Omega^*+\Lp(\Omega)\phi_\Omega^*=0\ \hbox{in }\Omega,\quad \phi_\Omega^*(\alpha)=0,\quad \phi_\Omega^*>0\ \hbox{in }\Omega.
\]
If $v\in C^1(\Omega)\cap C(\overline \Omega)$ satisfies $v>0$ in $\Omega$, $v(\beta)=0$ and $\cA_\Omega v+\mu v\ge0$ in $\Omega$, then $\Lp(\Omega)\le\mu$. If equality holds and $v$ is an eigenfunction, then $v$ is proportional to $\phi_\Omega$.

conditioned on $\ell_0 = c$,

Assume that $\phi: \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be sufficiently smooth and $\int_0^1\phi(x)^2dx < \infty$.
We have:
\begin{equation}

\int_0^\infty \phi(I_x^c) dx - \frac{1}{4} \int_0^\infty (\ell_x^c)^2 \left( \frac{\phi(I_x^c)}{I_x^c} + \phi'(I_x^c) \right)dx 
\stackrel{d}{=} \mathcal{N}\left(-\frac{c \phi(1)}{4}, \frac{1}{4} \int_0^1\phi(x)^2 dx\right).

body: [Lemma lem:VHStheorem of arXiv:2411.00663, 'Ergodicity and Mixing of invariant capacities and applications'] Let $(\Omega, \mathcal{F})$ be a measurable space, and $\{P_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence  of probabilities. Suppose that  for any $A\in \mathcal{F}$ the  limits exist $\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} P_n(A)=Q(A)$. Then $Q$ is a probability. If we further suppose that each $P_n$ is absolutely continuous with respect to the probability $Q$, then the absolute continuity of the $P_n$ with respect to $Q$ is uniform in $n\in\mathbb{N}$, that is, for any $\epsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that for  any $A\in\mathcal{F}$, if  $Q(A)<\delta$ then $ P_n(A)<\epsilon$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

body:
[Lemma 53 (Finite-state stabilization for fixed-profile dyadic cutoffs) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $m_\Lambda(\xi)=m(\xi/\Lambda)$ be a fixed-profile cutoff from
Definition~\ref{def:admissible-cutoff}, with $\Lambda\in\Dyd$.  Let
$\rho_N$ be supported in an annulus
$\{\kappa_-N\le|\xi|\le\kappa_+N\}$ for $N\ge2$.  There exist integers
$k_-<k_+$, depending only on $(\kappa_-,\kappa_+,c_0,C_0)$, such that
\begin{align*}
 m_\Lambda\rho_N&=0 &&\text{if }\log_2(\Lambda/N)\le k_-,\\
 m_\Lambda\rho_N&=\rho_N &&\text{if }\log_2(\Lambda/N)\ge k_+.
\end{align*}
Consequently the restriction of $m_\Lambda$ to a fixed dyadic shell has only
$k_+-k_-+2$ possible states as $\Lambda$ ranges over the dyadic cutoffs.  The
inhomogeneous unit shell is handled separately and also has only finitely many
states.  More generally, for any fixed number of cutoff factors carried by
arbitrary dyadic shells (not necessarily comparable), their joint restriction
has a scale-independent finite number of states.  This number depends only on
the cutoff profile, the shell support constants, and the number of factors,
not on the ratios of the shell scales.

In particular, if a dyadic random block $X_{\Lambda,N,Q,M}$ depends on
$\Lambda$ only through these cutoff factors and every one of its possible
states satisfies $\|\|X\|\|_{L^p}\le A_{N,Q,M}$, then
\begin{equation}
 \left\|\sup_{\Lambda\in\Dyd}\|X_{\Lambda,N,Q,M}\|\right\|_{L^p}
 \lesssim_m A_{N,Q,M}.
\end{equation}
For every fixed block, $X_{\Lambda,N,Q,M}$ agrees with its uncut value for
all sufficiently large $\Lambda$.

Owner draft: independently checked proof (C015 v1). Suppose a d-dimensional body is decomposed up to null sets into finitely many nondegenerate d-simplices with disjoint interiors and volume fractions q_j/D, where q_j are positive integers and D=sum q_j. Then its uniform law is n-CM at n=kD whenever every k*q_j>=d+1. Take a complete mix of k*q_j uniform points in each simplex, concatenate the groups, and randomly permute all output positions. Deterministic volume-matched counts give the full uniform marginal and total n times the whole-body centroid despite differing piece centers. Rational-coordinate convex polytopes have such a rational-volume triangulation, so admit arbitrarily large commensurate-order mixes. This does not prove critical order for a multi-piece decomposition or all nonmultiple orders, and variable-order approximation cannot be passed to a fixed-order mix. Novelty UNKNOWN.

For f, g in L^1(R^n) the convolution (f * g)(x) = integral over R^n of f(x - y) g(y) dy is defined for almost every x, belongs to L^1(R^n) with ||f * g||_1 <= ||f||_1 ||g||_1, and its Fourier transform is the product of the transforms: (f * g)^(xi) = f^(xi) g^(xi) for every xi, with f^(xi) = integral f(x) exp(-2 pi i x . xi) dx (with another normalisation of the transform a constant factor appears). Dually, for f, g in L^2(R^n) (or in L^1 with transforms in L^1) the transform of the pointwise product is the convolution of the transforms: (f g)^ = f^ * g^. The same identity holds for the Fourier series of 2 pi-periodic functions (the convolution on the circle, coefficients multiply), for the discrete Fourier transform of finite sequences with cyclic convolution (the basis of fast convolution by FFT, O(N log N) instead of O(N^2)), and for the Laplace transform with the convolution on [0, infinity). Consequences: L^1(R^n) with convolution is a commutative Banach algebra without unit whose Gelfand transform is the Fourier transform; convolution with an approximate identity converges to the function (the transforms tend to 1 pointwise); a convolution operator f -> k * f is diagonalised by the Fourier transform, with symbol k^, which is how constant-coefficient linear PDE and filters are analysed.

[Prop DBMconv of arXiv:2411.10829, 'Airy$_\beta$ line ensemble and its Laplace transform'] Take $m\in \mathbb N$, $\vec \mathbf k \in \mathbb R^m_+ $, and $\vec \boldsymbol{\tau}\in \mathbb R_{\ge 0}^m$ such that $\boldsymbol{\tau}_1\le \cdots \le \boldsymbol{\tau}_m$, and $C_1>0$.
For any large enough $N\in \mathbb N$, we take $\vec k\in\mathbb N^m$, $\tau_1\le \tau_2\le \dots\le \tau_m$ satisfying (equation eq_x2 of the paper).
Then as $N\to\infty$,
\[
2^{-m}\left(\frac{\hat{\mathcal P}_{k_m}^{N,\tau_m}}{(2\beta \tau_mN)^{k_m/2}}+\frac{\hat{\mathcal P}_{k_m+1}^{N,\tau_m}}{(2\beta\tau_mN)^{(k_m+1)/2}}\right) \cdots \left(\frac{\hat{\mathcal P}_{k_1}^{N,\tau_1}}{(2\beta\tau_1N)^{k_1/2}}+\frac{\hat{\mathcal P}_{k_1+1}^{N,\tau_1}}{(2\beta\tau_1N)^{(k_1+1)/2}}\right) [1]_{x_1=\dots=x_N=0}
\]
converges to $\mathbf L_\beta(\vec\mathbf k,\vec\boldsymbol{\tau})$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop DBMconv of arXiv:2411.10829

[Prop 8 of arXiv:2609.03653, 'The derived set of multiple star polylogarithms'] For every ${\bf k}\in\widehat{\mathcal{T}}$, the sequence $H_{k_1,\ldots,k_r}$ converges locally uniformly on $\mathcal{D}$ to a holomorphic function $H_{\bf k}$.  For $|z|<1$,
\begin{equation}
H_{\bf k}(z)=\sum_{n=0}^{+\infty}A_{\bf k}(n)z^n.
\end{equation}
If ${\bf k}\in\mathcal{T}$, then the boundary value
\[
H_{\bf k}(1):=\lim_{r\rightarrow+\infty}\zeta^{\star}(k_1,\ldots,k_r)
\]
exists and is greater than $1$.
title: Prop 8 of arXiv:2609.03653

[Theorem 7 of arXiv:2606.14812, 'Joint convergence in Wiener chaos via transport hierarchy and Malliavin covariances'] Let $(X_N = I_p(f_N), N\geq 1)$ with $p\geq 2$ satisfying \eqref{c1}. 
	Let us consider a sequence $(\mathbb{Y}_N=(Y_{1,N},\ldots,Y_{d,N}), N\geq 1)$ 
	of $d$-dimensional random vectors, with components in the $p$th Wiener 
	chaos, which converges in distribution to $\mathbb{Y}=(Y_1,\ldots,Y_d)$. 
	Assume
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbf{E}\!\left[X_N Y_{j,N}\right] \to_{N\to\infty} \rho_j, 
		\quad\text{for every } j=1,\ldots,d.
	\end{equation}
	Let $\rho=(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_d)\in\mathbb{R}^d$. Then
	\begin{equation}
		(X_N,\mathbb{Y}_N) \xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{(d)} (Z,\mathbb{Y}),
	\end{equation}
	where $Z\sim N(0,\sigma^2)$ and the characteristic function of 
	$(Z,\mathbb{Y})$ is given by, for every $u\in\mathbb{R}$, 
	$v\in\mathbb{R}^d$,
	\begin{equation}
		\varphi_{(Z,\mathbb{Y})}(u,v) 
		= \mathbf{E}\!\left[e^{i\langle v,\mathbb{Y}\rangle}\right]
		e^{-\frac{\sigma^2 u^2}{2} - u\langle\rho,v\rangle}.
	\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Defini 12 of arXiv:2608.27934, 'An example of biquandle and an invariant of long virtual knots defined through it'] (Index of a crossing)\\
Let $G(D)$ be the pointed Gauss diagram of a long virtual knot diagram $D$. 
For each dashed arrow in $G(D)$, we assign symbols $+$ and $-$ to the endpoints of the dashed arrow so that the symbol assigned to the tail is the same as that of the dashed arrow and that the symbol assigned to the head is the opposite to that of the dashed arrow. 
For each classical crossing $c$ of $D$, corresponding dashed arrow in $G(D)$ cuts unique interval without the specified point $p$ from the circle. 
The signed sum of symbols on the interior of the interval is denoted by $\alpha(c)$ and called {\it the index of }$c$.
title: Definition 12 of arXiv:2608.27934

[Lemma 9 (Detection of centeredness by places) of arXiv:2607.05219, 'Random free semigroups of affine groups'] Let $\zeta$ be a probability measure on $F^\times$ and denote by $A:=\langle \supp \zeta \rangle_{\mathrm{grp}}$. Then the following are equivalent: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $\zeta$ is centered.
\item[(ii)] For every place $v\in S(A)$,
\[
\int \log|a|_v\,d\zeta(a)=0.
\]

[Lemma lemma-M_N martingale of arXiv:2505.24043, 'Weak solutions of Navier-Stokes Equation with purely discontinuous L\'evy Noise'] For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the process ${{M}}_{n}$ is a square integrable $\mathbb{F}$-martingale and 
\begin{align}

\sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}}\mathbb{E} \left[ \sup_{t\in [0,T]}\bigl\vert  {{M}}_{n} (t) \bigr\vert_{H}^2 \right]
&\leq C_2 \sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}}
\mathbb{E} \Bigl[   \int_0^{T} \int_{Y} \rvert P_n F(s, u_n(s),y)\vert_{H}^2 \, \nu(\mathrm{d} y) \, \mathrm{d}s
\Bigr]
\\
&\leq C_2 \sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \left( 1+ \mathbb{E} \left[ \int_0^T  \lvert u_n (t) \rvert^2_H \, \mathrm{d}t \right] \right) < \infty. 

\end{align}
Moreover, if Assumption F.(assum-F5 of the paper)  is satisfied,  then for every $p\in [2, 4+\gamma] $ and for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the process ${{M}}_{n}$ is a $p$-integrable $\mathbb{F}$-martingale
\begin{align}
\sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}}\mathbb{E} \left[ \sup_{t\in [0,T]}\bigl\vert  {{M}}_{n} (t) \bigr\vert_{H}^p \right]
&\leq C_p \; \sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}}
\mathbb{E} \Bigl[   \Bigl( \int_0^{T} \int_{Y} \rvert P_n F(s, u_n(s),y)\vert_H^2 \, \nu(\mathrm{d} y) \, \mathrm{d}s \Bigr)^\frac{p}2
\\
\nonumber
&\hspace{2truecm}+\int_0^{T} \int_{Y} \rvert P_n F(s, u_n(s),y)\vert_H^p \, \nu(\mathrm{d} y) \, \mathrm{d}s
\Bigr]
\\

&\leq C_p \sup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \left( 1+ \mathbb{E} \left[ \int_0^T  \lvert u_n (t) \rvert^p_H \, \mathrm{d}t \right] \right) < \infty .
\end{align}
The constants $C_2$, $C_p$ are generic positive constants which can change from line to line but which do not depend on $n$.

Then $\ev_{\mathbb S}\colon{\textup{Fun}}^\textup{L}({\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\textup{gl},{\mathcal{C}})\to{\mathcal{C}}(1)$ is the left adjoint in a Bousfield localization.
    \begin{proof}
        As a consequence of the previous proposition, $\ev_{\mathbb S}$ has a right adjoint given by the composite
        \[
            {\mathcal{C}}(1)\xrightarrow{\;\mathbb S_*\;}{\textup{Fun}}'({\mathpalette\ulhelper{{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{lvl},{\mathcal{C}})\xrightarrow{\;\smash{\raisebox{-0.25ex}{\ensuremath{\scriptstyle\sim}}}\;}{\textup{Fun}}^\text{L}({\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\textup{gl},{\mathcal{C}}),
        \]
        where ${\textup{Fun}}'({\mathpalette\ulhelper{{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{lvl},{\mathcal{C}})$ denotes the full subcategory of left adjoints factoring through the localization $L\colon{\mathpalette\ulhelper{{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}_\textup{lvl}\to{\mathpalette\ulhelper{\mathfrak d\kern-.25pt}}\hbox{\rule[-2pt]{0pt}{0pt}}{\mathfrak S\kern-.5pt\mathfrak p}_\textup{gl}$ and the unnamed equivalence is given by precomposing with a right adjoint to $L$.     \end{proof}

   \mathbf L_b[\boldsymbol k;\boldsymbol\tau].

The convergence is locally uniform in the ordered time vector
$\boldsymbol\tau$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary cor:S_n of arXiv:2604.04922, 'Elephant random walk on the infinite dihedral group $\mathbb{Z}_2 * \mathbb{Z}_2$'] For any $p \in [0, 1)$, the following hold.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \setlength{\itemsep}{5pt}
        \item[(a)] \textbf{Strong Law:} $\frac{\Delta_n^{(s)}}{n} \xrightarrow{\text{a.s.}} 0$.
        \item[(b)] \textbf{Functional Central Limit Theorem:} 
        The process $\big(\frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\Delta_{\lfloor nt \rfloor}^{(s)}\big)_{t \in [0, 1]}$ converges weakly to the standard Brownian motion $(B_t)_{t \in [0, 1]}$ in the Skorohod space of c\`adl\`ag functions on $[0, 1]$. In particular, $\frac{\Delta_n^{(s)}}{\sqrt{n}} \xrightarrow{d} N(0, 1)$. 
        \item[(c)] \textbf{Law of the Iterated Logarithm:} We have 
        \[
            \limsup_{n \to \infty} \frac{\Delta_n^{(s)}}{\sqrt{2n \log{\log{n}}}} = - \liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{\Delta_n^{(s)}}{\sqrt{2n \log{\log{n}}}} = 1.
        \]
        As a consequence, $\Delta_n^{(s)}$ is recurrent. 
        
        \item[(d)] \textbf{Quadratic Strong Law:} $\frac{1}{\log{n}} \sum_{k=1}^n \frac{(\Delta_k^{(s)})^2}{k^2} \xrightarrow{\text{a.s.}} 1$.
    \end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Thm mainthmintro of arXiv:2602.08591, 'The Yang--Mills measure on compact surfaces as a \\ universal scaling limit of lattice gau'] The sequence $(A_N)_{N\geqslant 0}$ converges in law, in the H\"older space $C_\mathrm{loc}^{-(\frac{5}{2}+\varepsilon)}(\Sigma\setminus f^{-1}(\max (f));\mathfrak{g})$ of distributional $\mathfrak{g}$-valued $1$-forms, to the Morse-gauge-fixed Yang--Mills measure on $\Sigma$.
Moreover outside the union of some finite number of closed curves, the sequence $A_N$ converges to $A$ in local anisotropic Hölder spaces of regularity $(-\frac{1}{2}^-, \frac 1 2^-)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Universal scaling limit of lattice gauge theories

body: A function f: A \rightarrow B is bijective (a bijection) if it is both injective and surjective. In this case, f has a unique two-sided inverse function f^{-1}: B \rightarrow A.
title: Bijection (One-to-One Correspondence)

body: Let W_t be a standard Brownian motion and let X_t solve the Ito stochastic differential equation dX_t = mu_t dt + sigma_t dW_t for adapted, sufficiently integrable processes mu_t, sigma_t. If f(t,x) is continuously differentiable once in t and twice in x, then Y_t = f(t,X_t) satisfies dY_t = [f_t + mu_t f_x + (1/2) sigma_t^2 f_xx] dt + sigma_t f_x dW_t, all partial derivatives evaluated at (t,X_t). Equivalently df = f_t dt + f_x dX_t + (1/2) f_xx d[X]_t, using the Ito rule (dW_t)^2 = dt. The stochastic-calculus chain rule; due to Kiyoshi Ito.
title: Ito's lemma

body:
[Definition def:propagation-of-chaos of arXiv:2606.29557, 'Propagation of chaos for Belavkin equations beyond pure states'] Let $\rho_0^N\in\mathcal S(\mathcal H_N)$ and $\gamma_0\in\mathcal S(\mathcal H)$.  Propagation of chaos is said to hold if, for every
fixed $n\ge1$ and $T>0$,
\begin{equation}
  \sup_{0\le t\le T}
  \mathbb E\left[
    \left\|
      \rho_t^{N:n}-\Gamma_t^n
    \right\|_1
  \right]
  \longrightarrow0
  \qquad
  \text{as }N\longrightarrow \infty.
  
\end{equation}
title: Propagation of chaos

body:
[Lem tree-power-residual of arXiv:2609.03856, 'Consensus time for asynchronous $\ell^p$ relaxation: graph dependence'] Let $x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_k\ge0$, let $\sigma_i\in\{-1,1\}$, and put
\[
 \rho=\left|\sum_{i=0}^k\sigma_i x_i^a\right|.
\]
If $\alpha_i>0$ and $\sum_{i=1}^k\alpha_i=1$, then, for
$0<\varepsilon\le1$,
\begin{equation}
 x_0^p\le(1+\varepsilon)
 \sum_{i=1}^k\alpha_i^{-1/a}x_i^p
 +C_p\varepsilon^{-1/a}\rho^q.
\end{equation}

[Proposition 4 (Compressible Processes are Generic) of arXiv:2607.14361, 'NeuralChaos: Optimal Adapted Approximation of Square Integrable Predictable Processes'] Let $s \in \mathbb{N}_{+}$ and let $\mu_{\vartheta,U}$ be any Borel probability measure on $\mathbb{D}^{s,2:d}_{T}$, satisfying Assumption \ref{ass:random-lp-stable-chaoslet-series}. If $\operatorname{Law}(X_\cdot)=\mu_{\vartheta,U}$, then $X_{\cdot}$ is $\big(S=\frac{1}{p_{\rm cmp}}\big)$-compressible and belongs to $\mathbb{D}^{s,2:d}_T$ $\mu$-almost surely. In particular, its best $N$-term
chaoslet approximation error is $\mathcal{O}\Big(
N^{-\big(\tfrac{1}{p_{\mathrm{cmp}}}-\tfrac{1}{2}\big)}
\Big)$.

body:
[Definition 1 of arXiv:2607.12384, '2607.12384'] Let $(\Omega, \mathcal{F}, \{\mathcal{F}_t\}_{t\geq 0}, \mathbb{P})$ be a filtered probability space satisfying the usual conditions, and let $W(ds, dy)$ be a space-time white noise defined on this space.  An adapted and jointly measurable random field
	\[
	\{u(t,x):(t,x)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb R\}
	\]
	is called a mild solution to \eqref{eq:main equation} if
	\[
	\sup_{(t,x)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb R}
	\mathbb E|u(t,x)|^2<\infty,
	\]
	and, for every
	\((t,x)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb R\),
	\[
	\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb R}
	G_{t-s}(x-y)^2
	\mathbb E\left[|\sigma(u(s,y))|^2\right]\,dy\,ds
	<\infty,
	\]
	so that the Walsh integral below is well defined in \(L^2(\Omega)\). Moreover,
	for every \((t,x)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb R\),
	\begin{equation}
		u(t,x)
		=
		1+
		\int_0^t\int_{\mathbb R}
		G_{t-s}(x-y)\sigma(u(s,y))\,W(ds,dy)
	\end{equation}
	holds in \(L^2(\Omega)\).
title: Definition 1 of arXiv:2607.12384
