body:
[Lemma 1 of arXiv:2604.10051, 'Ergodicity of the voter model with dynamic anti-voter bonds'] Let~$(\xi_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a Feller process defined on a metric space~$\mathcal C$ and~$(Z_t)_{t \ge 0}$ be a Markov chain with a countable state space~$\mathcal S$ and~$Q
$-matrix~$\{q(x,y) : x,y \in \mathcal S\}$ that satisfy
\begin{equation}
c(x) > 0, \; \forall x \in \mathcal S, \quad
\sup_{ \substack{ x,y \in \mathcal S \\ q(x,y) > 0 } } \frac{c(x)}{c(y)} < \infty, \quad \int^\infty_0 \mathds{1}_{ \{Z_{t^-} \neq Z_t\} } \cdot c(Z_t)^{-2} \; \mathrm{d}t = \infty \; a.s.,
\end{equation}
where~$c(x) = -q(x,x)$. Assume that the processes are dual with respect to a function~$D:\mathcal C \times \mathcal S \to [0,\infty)$, that is,
$$ E_\xi D(\xi_t,z) = E_z D(\xi_t,z) \quad \text{ for every } \xi \in \mathcal C,\; z \in \mathcal S,\; t \ge 0; $$
also assume that for each~$z \in \mathcal S$,
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item the map~$\xi \mapsto D(\xi,z)$ is bounded and continuous; and
    \item there exit~$M>0$ and~$\alpha>0$ such that for each~$\xi \in \mathcal C$ and~$t \ge 0$ we have that $E_z [D(\xi,Z_t)^{1+\alpha}] \leq M$.
\end{enumerate} 
Moreover, assume that 
$\mu \in \mathscr{I}_\infty$. Then,
\begin{equation}
    \int D(\xi,z)\; \mu( \mathrm{d} \xi ) = \int D(\xi,z) \; \mu S_t( \mathrm{d} \xi ) \quad \text{for any } t \ge 0 \text{ and } z \in \mathcal S.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Lemma 1 of arXiv:2604.10051

body:
[Prop role-of-shifted-a_new of arXiv:2411.03065, 'Growing conditioned BGW trees with\\ log-concave offspring distributions'] Let $d\geq1$ and $s\in\{0,\dots,d-1\}$.
	Consider $({\mathbf{a}},{\mathbf{b}})$ a $(d,s)$-non-degenerate weight pair for which $({\mathbf{a}}^+,{\mathbf{b}})$ is $(d,\overline{s-1})$-non-degenerate.
	Let $C_{nd+s}$ be a $\PComp{{\mathbf{a}},{\mathbf{b}}}{nd+s}$-distributed random composition  for some fixed $n\geq 0$.
	If we let $X_{nd+s}=\mathrm{proj}_1(C_{nd+s})$ and $C'_{nd+s}=\mathrm{proj}_{>1}(C_{nd+s})$, then when $s\neq0$ the variable $X_{nd+s}$ has distribution given by
	\begin{align}
	\Prob{X_{nd+s}=md+1}&=\frac{b_{md+1}\cdot\PFComp{{\mathbf{a}}^+,{\mathbf{b}}}{(n-m)d+(s-1)}}{\PFComp{{\mathbf{a}},{\mathbf{b}}}{nd+s}},
	\qquad
	&&m=1,\dots,n,
	\intertext{while when $s=0$ the variable $X_{dn}$ has distribution given by}
	\Prob{X_{dn}=md+1}&=\frac{b_{md+1}\cdot\PFComp{{\mathbf{a}}^+,{\mathbf{b}}}{(n-m-1)d+(d-1)}}{\PFComp{{\mathbf{a}},{\mathbf{b}}}{nd+s}},
	\qquad
	&&m=1,\dots,n-1,
	\end{align}
	Conditionally on $X_{nd+s}$, the composition $C'_{nd+s}$ has distribution $\PComp{{\mathbf{a}}^+,{\mathbf{b}}}{nd+s-X_n}$.

body: [Proposition 6.1 of arXiv:2503.23159, 'Hall's marriage theorem'] A Latin rectangle can be extended to a Latin square by adding extra rows. Clearly it suffices to show that, if m < n, then one more row can be added. The letters (a1, . . . , an) in the added row must be all distinct, and must not occur in the m elements in their column in the given rectangle; so they must form an SDR for the sets T1, . . . , Tn, where Ti is the set of letters not appearing in the ith column.
title: Proposition 6.1 of arXiv:2503.23159: Hall's marriage theorem

body: Every read-k DNF or CNF f (negations and redundant terms allowed) satisfies H(f) <= min(2.89 + 9.9k, 30 + 5.6 log2 k) I(f), so the Fourier entropy-influence constant grows as O(log k); before this only the min-entropy version was known for read-k DNFs (Arunachalam-Chakraborty-Koucky-Saurabh-de Wolf, STACS 2020). Every regular (2-monotone) Boolean function, including every linear threshold function, satisfies H(f) <= 15.1 I(f). Both classes satisfy O'Donnell-Tan's strengthened form H^+ <= C (I - Var). Threshold gates T_{t,r} = 1[y_1 + ... + y_r >= t] satisfy the biased strengthened form under every product measure (constant 526 in nats, about 760 bits; 66.4 bits when all inputs share one bias), so by O'Donnell-Tan's composition theorem every read-once formula of threshold gates of any fan-in and depth satisfies FEI. Monotone functions whose desirability preorder has width w satisfy H <= (15.1 + log2 w) I.

[Lemma l:log.likelihood.local.region.bounds of arXiv:2607.02013, 'Resolution of the Detection Threshold Conjecture for Random Geometric Graphs in the $d>n$ '] Fix $r\ge2$ and $N\ge1$. For $\Lambda_\theta=\log L_\theta$ as defined by ~((eq:logL-explicit of the paper)), we have the bounds
\begin{align}

\sup\bigg\{|\Lambda_\theta(t)|
:0\le\theta\le1
\bigg\}
&\le
C_{r}\delta U(t)\,,\\

\sup\bigg\{ \bigg|
\frac{\partial^j}{\partial\theta^j}\Lambda_\theta(t)
\bigg| : 0 \le \theta \le 1\bigg\}
&\le
C_{r,j}[\delta U(t)]^j \,,
\end{align}
for all $U(t)\le c_0/\delta$, where the second line holds for all $1\le j\le N$.

[Prop coupling2 of arXiv:2602.21277, 'A Limit in Law for the Cover Time and Last Visited Vertex of Wired Planar Domains'] If $\gamma > 0$ is taken small enough then, for any $\eta \in (0,\tfrac{1}{2})$ sufficiently small (depending only on $\gamma$) we have that, for all $k$ sufficiently large and $T \in [k,{\rm e}^k]$,
	\begin{equation}
		\mathbb{P} \bigg( \bigg\{ \sqrt{\widehat{L}_{\widetilde{v}_k}(0)} \in {\rm d} u\bigg\} \setminus \mathcal{L}^{\eta,[1,T-1]}_{\widetilde{v}_k} \bigg)=\frac{4}{\sqrt{\pi}} \cdot \frac{1}{Tk^{1/2+\gamma}}{\rm e}^{-2Tk^\gamma}\left(\widehat{u}{\rm e}^{2\sqrt{2}\widehat{u}}\right)\left(\widehat{v}{\rm e}^{-2\sqrt{2}\widehat{v}-\frac{\widehat{v}^2}{Tk^\gamma}}\right)(1+o_k(1))\,
	\end{equation} holds uniformly over $u \in \mathcal{Q}_k^\eta(0)$ and $v \in \mathcal{Q}_k^\eta(T)$, where $\widehat{u}:=u-\sqrt{2}k$ and $\widehat{v}:=v -\sqrt{2}(k+Tk^\gamma)$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop coupling2 of arXiv:2602.21277

body: [Lemma L: cumulant_calculation of arXiv:2606.18654, 'Rigidity of infinite exchangeable sequences with Gaussian marginals'] Let $\lambda$ be an infinitely divisible probability measure on $\mathbb{R}$ with finite fourth moment. Let $\kappa_4(\lambda)$ denote its fourth cumulant. Then $\kappa_4(\lambda) \geq 0$. Moreover, $\kappa_4(\lambda) = 0$ if and only if $\lambda$ is a (possibly degenerate) Gaussian law.

body:
[Theorem thm:pairwise-torsion of arXiv:2607.24705, 'Derangetropy Operators'] Let $f \in \mathcal{D}_{+}(R)$, $n \ge 3$, with all pairwise
		maximal correlations below one. Then:
		\begin{enumerate}[label=\normalfont(\roman*), leftmargin=*]
			\item the torsion decomposes into pairwise blocks: the bracket
			$[L_{i}^{a}, L_{j}^{b}]$ depends only on the $(i,j)$-marginal
			copula, with the components~(equation eq:torsion-components of the paper), and the
			$(i,j)$-block vanishes on the trigonometric family precisely when
			$X_{i}$ and $X_{j}$ are independent, so the torsion table detects
			exactly the pairwise independence graph;
			\item torsion is not a complete dependence invariant: for pairwise
			independent but jointly dependent laws, such as smoothed parity
			triples, every torsion block vanishes while the law lies off the
			product leaf, its interaction potential containing an irreducible
			three-way term detected by the three-dimensional odds ratio;

[Thm 2 of arXiv:2607.24170, '\large\bf ON NON-MONOTONICITY OF LOGARITHMIC ENERGY\\ FOR RANDOM MATRICES'] Let
$\pentry\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}1/32$ and
$\qentry\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}31/32$.  Let $\mathsf{X}$ and
$\mathsf{G}$ be independent random variables such that
\begin{equation}
 \Prob\left(\mathsf{X}=-\frac1{\sqrt{31}}\right)=\qentry,
 \qquad \Prob(\mathsf{X}=\sqrt{31})=\pentry,
 \qquad
 \Prob(\mathsf{G}\in\mathrm{d}z)=\frac1\pi\mathrm{e}^{-|z|^2}\mathrm{d}^2z.
\end{equation}
For $\varepsilon>0$, set
\begin{equation}
 \mathsf{Y}_\varepsilon\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}
 \frac{\mathsf{X}+\varepsilon \mathsf{G}}{\sqrt{1+\varepsilon^2}},
\end{equation}
and let $\mathbf{M}_{n,\varepsilon}$ have i.i.d.\ entries with law
$\mathsf{Y}_\varepsilon$.  Put
\[
 \nu_{n,\varepsilon}\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}
 \E[\mu_{\mathbf{M}_{n,\varepsilon}/\sqrt n}].
\]
Then, $\mathsf{Y}_\varepsilon$ is centered, satisfies
$\E[|\mathsf{Y}_\varepsilon|^2]=1$, and has a strictly positive real-analytic
density, all moments, and sub-Gaussian tails.  Moreover,
\[
 \cE(\nu_{n,\varepsilon})\in\R,\qquad n\geq1,\quad\varepsilon>0,
\]
and there exists $\varepsilon_0>0$ such that
\[
 \cF_{\C}(\nu_{3,\varepsilon})>\cF_{\C}(\nu_{2,\varepsilon}),
 \qquad 0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Thm 2 of arXiv:2607.24170

[Definition 8 of arXiv:2608.30859, 'Conservation Laws with Discontinuous Flux:\\ A First Application to Traffic Flow'] A vector field $H : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is said to have 
\emph{locally bounded directional variation} if, for every 
$(t_0,x_0) \in \mathbb{R}^2$, there exist $\delta>0$ and a constant $C>0$
such that
\[
\sum_{i=1}^N 
\bigl| H(t_i,x_i) - H(t_{i-1},x_{i-1}) \bigr|
\;\le\; C
\]
for every finite sequence $(t_i,x_i)$, $i=0,\ldots,N$, satisfying
\[
(t_0,x_0) \prec (t_1,x_1) \prec \cdots \prec (t_N,x_N),
\qquad t_N < t_0 + \delta .
\]
Here $\prec$ denotes the partial order on $\mathbb{R}^2$ induced by the cone
\begin{equation}
    \Gamma_M := \{ (t,x) \in \mathbb{R}^2 : |x| \le M t\}, 
\end{equation}
namely
\begin{align}
(t,x) \prec (t',x')
\quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad
|x - x'| \le M (t - t') .
\end{align}
title: Definition 8 of arXiv:2608.30859

The leading product has expectation zero by centering. The only surviving linear term is v_j*E[xi_i*sigma(xi_i)]*E[sigma_prime(xi_j)]=v_j*b_sigma^2,using Gaussian integration by parts. Since |v_j-x_i^T x_j|<=C*epsilon^2 and |b_sigma|<=lambda_sigma,this proves the off-diagonal estimate. For one coordinate,write zeta=||x_i||*Z. Lipschitz continuity bounds the mean deviation by C*lambda_sigma*abs(||x_i||^2-1). Expanding sigma(zeta)^2-sigma(Z)^2 as2*sigma(Z)*(sigma(zeta)-sigma(Z))+(sigma(zeta)-sigma(Z))^2 and applying Cauchy-Schwarz gives C*lambda_sigma*a+C*lambda_sigma^2*a^2,where a=abs(||x_i||^2-1);lambda_sigma*a<1 absorbs the quadratic term. This proves both diagonal estimates. If epsilon>=1/4,the same diagonal argument bounds Phi_ii by a universal constant. Cauchy-Schwarz bounds |Phi_ij|,and |b_sigma|^2*|x_i^T x_j|<=lambda_sigma^2*epsilon<=4*lambda_sigma^2*epsilon^2;enlarging the universal constant gives the off-diagonal bound too. At epsilon=0 the independent projections give the exact identities. [Prop three_point_upper of arXiv:2508.18809, '{\bf Critical long-range percolation III: The upper critical dimension}'] If $d\geq 3\alpha$ and $\alpha<2$ then there exists a decreasing function $h_p:(0,\infty)\to (0,1]$ decaying faster than any power such that

\[
  \tau_{\beta_c,r}(x,y,z) \preceq V_{d_\mathrm{min}(x,y,z)}  d_\mathrm{min}(x,y,z)^{-d+2\alpha} d_\mathrm{max}(x,y,z)^{-d+\alpha}  h\left(\frac{d_\mathrm{max}(x,y,z)}{r}\right)
\]
for every $r\in [1,\infty]$ and distinct triple of points $x,y,z\in \mathbb Z^d$, where we set $h(d_\mathrm{max}(x,y,z)/r)\equiv 1$ when $r=\infty$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 6 of arXiv:2606.27774, 'Variational Formulas for the Spectrum of\\ Block Wishart Matrices'] Fix $\alpha\in(0,\infty)$, integer $k\ge1$, $\nu\in\cuP_0(\sa{k}{\C})$.
Then  $\supp(\mu_\up{\alpha,\nu})\subseteq(0,\infty)$ if and only
if there exist $\bS,\bB\succ\bzero$ satisfying all of the following
\begin{enumerate}
    \item 
    $
   \alpha^{-1} \bS^{-1}\bB\bS^{-1} - 
   \int \bT(\bI+\bS\bT)^{-1}\bB (\bI+\bT\bS)^{-1}\bT\, \nu(\de\bT)\succ\bzero$
   \item
$\int \bT(\bI+\bS\bT)^{-1} \nu(\de\bT) - \alpha^{-1} \bS^{-1}\succ\bzero.$
\item $\bS^{-1} +\bT \succ\bzero$ for all $\bT\in\supp(\nu).$
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Corollary 6 of arXiv:2606.27774

body:
[Definition 4 (Finite Free Convolutions) of arXiv:2606.19115, 'Finite free perpetuities'] Let $p, q \in \tilde\pols_{\leq n}(\C)$.
\begin{itemize}
\item Their finite free additive convolution, denoted $p \boxplus_n q$, is the polynomial in $\tilde\pols_{\leq n}(\C)$ defined by its coefficients:
\[ \coef{k}{n}(p \boxplus_n q) = \sum_{j=0}^k \binom{k}{j} \coef{j}{n}(p) \coef{k-j}{n}(q) \quad \text{for } k=0, 1, \dots, n. \]

    \item Their finite free multiplicative convolution, denoted $p \boxtimes_n q$, is the polynomial in $\tilde\pols_{\leq n}(\C)$ defined by its coefficients:
\[ \coef{k}{n}(p \boxtimes_n q) = \coef{k}{n}(p) \coef{k}{n}(q) \quad \text{for } k=0, 1, \dots, n. \]

\end{itemize}
title: Finite Free Convolutions

body:
[Cor 17 of arXiv:2509.01797, 'Relation between Wick powers and excursion clusters of the 2D GFF'] For every $D\subsetneq \C$ open simply connected domain,
for every $z,z',w,w'\in D$ such that
$\vert z' - z\vert \leq \frac{1}{2}d(z,\partial D)$,
$\vert w' - w\vert \leq \frac{1}{2}d(w,\partial D)$,
$\vert z' - z\vert\leq \frac{1}{4}\vert z-w\vert$,
and
$\vert w' - w\vert\leq \frac{1}{4}\vert z-w\vert$,
we have
\begin{eqnarray*}
\vert G_{D}(z',w') - G_{D}(z,w)\vert &\leq &
\dfrac{\log(2)}{\pi}\dfrac{\vert z' - z\vert +\vert w' - w\vert}{\vert z-w\vert}
\\  && +
16\dfrac{\vert z' - z\vert}{d(z,\partial D)}
\Big(G_{D}(z,w)+\dfrac{1}{2\pi}\log \dfrac{\vert z-w\vert}{d(w,\partial D)}\Big)
+ \dfrac{\log(2)}{\pi}\dfrac{\vert w' - w\vert}{d(w,\partial D)}.
\end{eqnarray*}
title: Cor 17 of arXiv:2509.01797

body:
[Theorem 21 of arXiv:2605.21424, 'A dice game, a multinomial walk, and the inverted Dirichlet distribution'] Let \(\tau_1\) be as in Proposition \ref {thm:rep-tau1}. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item \(
\lim_{n_1\to \infty}\tau_1(n_1,\ldots,n_m)=\prod_{k=2}^m\mathbb{P}(G_k \le  n_k)\,.
\)
\item With \(X_2,\ldots,X_m\) as in Proposition \ref {thm:rep-tau1}\eqref{it:rep-tau1-1},  
\begin{align*}
&\lim_{n_m\to \infty}\tau_1(n_1,n_2,\ldots,n_m)\\
&=\int_0^{\frac{n_2}{n_1}}\cdots\int_0^{\frac{n_{m-1}}{n_1}}\int_{n_1(1+\sum_{k=2}^{m-1}s_k)}^\infty f_\Gamma(s_m)ds_{m}\ \varphi_{<m}(s_2,\ldots,s_{m-1})ds_{m-1}\dotsc ds_2,
\end{align*}
where 
\(\varphi_{<m}\) is the marginal density of \(X_2,\ldots,X_{m-1}\) and \(f_\Gamma\) is a \(\operatorname{Gamma}\Big(\sum_{k=1}^{m-1}n_k,1\Big)\) density.
\item For given \(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_m>0\)  
\[
\lim_{n\to \infty}\tau_1(\alpha_1 n,\ldots, \alpha_m n)=\int_{-\infty}^\infty \prod_{k=2}^m \Phi\Big(\sqrt{\frac{\alpha_k}{\alpha_1}}\ z\Big)\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}e^{-\frac{z^2}{2}}dz\,.
\]
\end{enumerate} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 21 of arXiv:2605.21424

Math-brain retrieval testing, 2026-08-30: the store's TEXTBOOK layer is untestable by construction, so testability lives only in its private layer. A sterile pre-registered control on famous theorems returned arms identical on every measure - credited score 25 of 39 both, false positives 4 of 39 both, discrimination +24 both, discordants three each way at p = 1.00 - and that null had room to fail, since six discordants appeared and a six-nil split would have given p = 0.031. On obscure private records the same contrast gives an untreated arm at zero discrimination against a notes arm at plus eight, plus five and plus three. So retrieval helps exactly where the solver lacks the fact and is inert where it already holds it. Of 745 unused uniquely-titled nodes, 719 are textbook material; the remaining private pool is about sixteen nodes, which ceilings near twenty pairs only under the most generous admission and multiplicity assumptions and gives about eleven at the measured 53 percent admission rate. Harvesting more encyclopedia content adds recall surface and no testability.

[Definition 3 of arXiv:2609.00087, 'Translational tiles without spectra\\ in finite abelian $p$-groups'] A set $A\subset G$ is a \emph{translational tile} if there is a set
$B\subset G$ such that every element of $G$ has a unique representation
$a+b$ with $a\in A$ and $b\in B$.  We then write $A\oplus B=G$ and call
$B$ a tiling complement of $A$.

[Corollary cor:weighted-logarithmic-estimate of arXiv:2609.00556, 'Higgs--Demailly System and Positivity of Higgs Bundles'] Let \(f\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)\), let
\(g=e^u\in\operatorname{Herm}^+(E,h_{\rm ref})\), and suppose that
\begin{equation}
 \sqrt{-1}\Lambda_\omega
 \left(
  \bar\partial(g^{-1}\partial^{h_{\rm ref}}g)
  +[\theta,g^{-1}\theta_{h_{\rm ref}}^*g
             -\theta_{h_{\rm ref}}^*]
 \right)
 +e^f u+\Psi=0.
\end{equation}
Then
\begin{equation}
 e^f|u|_{h_{\rm ref}}^2
 -\frac12\Delta_\omega^{\mathbb C}|u|_{h_{\rm ref}}^2
 +\mathscr Q_\nabla(u)+\mathscr Q_\theta(u)
 =
 -\langle\Psi,u\rangle_{h_{\rm ref}}.
\end{equation}
In particular,
\begin{equation}
 e^f|u|_{h_{\rm ref}}^2
 -\frac12\Delta_\omega^{\mathbb C}|u|_{h_{\rm ref}}^2
 \leq
 |\Psi|_{h_{\rm ref}}|u|_{h_{\rm ref}},
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}
 e^{\min_M f}\|u\|_{C^0}
 \leq
 \|\Psi\|_{C^0}.
\end{equation}

[Theorem 2 (Intrinsic volumes of weighted \(\ell_p\)-balls) of arXiv:2605.11995, 'Intrinsic volumes of \(\ell_p\)-balls and a continuum of Maxwell--Poincar\'e--Borel laws f'] Let \(1<p<\infty\), \(n\ge 2\), and let $a=(a_1,\dots,a_n)\in(0,\infty)^n$
be a vector of positive weights. Define the weighted\footnote{The notation $\mathbb{B}_p^n(a)$ should not be confused with its common use to denote the standard unit $\ell_p$-ball $\mathbb{B}_p^n$ centered at $a$.} \(\ell_p\)-ball by
\[
\mathbb B_p^n(a)\equiv \mathbb B_p^n(a_1,\dots,a_n)
:=
\left\{
x\in\mathbb R^n:\ \sum_{r=1}^n |a_r x_r|^p\le 1
\right\}.
\]
Then, for every \(j\in\{0,\dots,n-1\}\), one has
\begin{multline*}
V_j(\mathbb B_p^n(a))
=
\frac{p(p-1)^{n-1-j}}{2\pi^{\frac{n-j}{2}}\Gamma\!\left(1+\frac jp\right)}
\sum_{i=1}^n
\sum_{\substack{I\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}\setminus\{i\}\\ |I|=n-1-j}}
\\
\times \int_0^\infty \theta^{\frac{n-j}{2}-1}
a_i \mathcal K_p\!\left(a_i^2 \theta\right)
\prod_{r\in I} a_r \mathcal J_p\!\left(a_r^2 \theta\right)
\prod_{r\notin I\cup\{i\}} a_r^{-1} \mathcal I_p\!\left(a_r^2\theta\right)
\,d\theta,
\end{multline*}
where the functions $\mathcal I_p, \mathcal J_p, \mathcal K_p$ are defined by~\eqref{eq:def_I_p}. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Intrinsic volumes of weighted \(\ell_p\)-balls

Let f ∈ C^1(R;R^n) and u0 ∈ L^∞(R^n). Then: (a) there exists exactly one Kruzhkov entropy solution u ∈ L^∞(R^n × (0,∞)) of u_t + div f(u) = 0, u(·,0) = u0, and it has a representative in C([0,∞); L^1_loc(R^n)) with u(0) = u0; (b) (finite speed of propagation / local L^1 contraction) if u, v are entropy solutions with data u0, v0, K := max(||u0||_∞, ||v0||_∞) and M := max_{|s| ≤ K} |f'(s)|, then for every R > 0 and t > 0, ∫_{|x| ≤ R} |u(x,t) - v(x,t)| dx ≤ ∫_{|x| ≤ R + Mt} |u0 - v0| dx; (c) ||u(·,t)||_∞ ≤ ||u0||_∞, the solution map is order preserving (u0 ≤ v0 a.e. implies u ≤ v a.e.), and if u0 - v0 ∈ L^1(R^n) then ||u(·,t) - v(·,t)||_{L^1} ≤ ||u0 - v0||_{L^1} for every t > 0; (d) if u0 ∈ BV(R^n) then TV(u(·,t)) ≤ TV(u0) for all t. The entropy solution is also the vanishing-viscosity limit of the solutions of u^ε_t + div f(u^ε) = εΔu^ε.
f ∈ C^1 (or locally Lipschitz), u0 ∈ L^∞(R^n)
the solution is required to be an entropy solution in the Kruzhkov sense; mere weak solutions are not unique
M in (b) is the maximum of |f'| over the interval determined by the L^∞ bounds of the data, so the contraction is on backward cones with that slope
(d) requires u0 of bounded variation

[Proposition 7 (Perturbed Walks on $(\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)^n$) of arXiv:2605.19084, 'Limit Profiles for Separation Distance'] Fix $m\geq2$, and let $P_n$ be the uniform coordinate refresh walk on $(\mathbb Z/m\mathbb Z)^n$. Fix $b\in(0,1)$, set $a_n:=\frac1n-\frac{b}{n-1}$, and let $Q_n$ be the coordinate refresh walk with rates $\alpha_1:=\frac1n+b$ and $\alpha_k:=a_n$ for $2\leq k\leq n$. With $\bar t_n(c):=a_n^{-1}(\ln(n-1)+c)$, for every fixed $c\in\mathbb R$,
$$\left|s_*^{Q_n}\left(\bar t_n(c)\right)-s_*^{P_n}\left(n(\ln n+c)\right)\right|\to0.$$
Consequently, $Q_n$ has separation limit profile $1-e^{-e^{-c}}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let v be a nonzero vector in R^p. For the whitened one-hidden-neuron linear loss f(beta,a)=||beta a-v||^2/2, consider continuous gradient flow beta'=a^T v-beta||a||^2, a'=beta v-beta^2 a, with beta_0=0 and a_0^T v nonzero. Then its product beta(t)a(t) tends to v. The scalar imbalance delta=beta^2-||a||^2 is conserved and is strictly negative at initialization. More generally, in the negative-imbalance case the saddle-basin boundary is a_0^T v+(beta_0/2)(delta+sqrt(delta^2+4||v||^2))=0. For the zero-output initialization it reduces to a_0^T v=0, which has probability zero under any nondegenerate isotropic Gaussian a_0. These continuous-time solutions and basin statements are already given by Kunin, Raventos, Domine, Chen, Klindt, Saxe and Ganguli, Get rich quick, arXiv:2406.06158, Appendix A.2.4 equations (30)-(33), printed p.19, and Appendix A.2.5 equation (34), p.20. They do not themselves constitute a discrete-GD hitting-time theorem.

body:
[Corollary 10 of arXiv:2608.19744, 'Conditioned Brownian motion and local equivalence of path ensembles'] Let $K$ be symmetric positive definite, let $\sigma>0$, and let
$Q:\mathbb R^d\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous and nonconstant.  Define
\[
    A_T=\int_0^T \de s \, Q(X_s)
\]
for the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
\[
    \de X_t=-KX_t\,\de t+\sigma\,\de B_t,
    \qquad X_0=x.
\]
Let $\lambda(\beta)$ and $\psi_\beta$ be the lowest eigenvalue and
normalized positive ground state of
\[
    K_\beta=-L_K+\beta Q
    \qquad\text{on }L^2(\mu_K).
\]
For $\theta\in\Theta_Q^{\mathrm{OU}}
       =\lambda'((0,\infty))$ and $\lambda'(\beta_\theta)=\theta$,
put $v_\theta=-\lambda''(\beta_\theta)>0$ as well as 
\[
    I_Q^{\mathrm{OU}}(\theta)
       =\lambda(\beta_\theta)-\beta_\theta\theta.
\]
Then, for every fixed $z\in\mathbb R$,
\[
    \bbP_x^{\mathrm{OU}}(A_T\leq\theta T+z)
    \sim
    \frac{
      \psi_{\beta_\theta}(x)
      \langle\psi_{\beta_\theta},\mathbf 1\rangle_{L^2(\mu_K)}
    }{
      \beta_\theta\sqrt{2\pi v_\theta T}
    }
    \exp\!\left(
       -I_Q^{\mathrm{OU}}(\theta)T+\beta_\theta z
    \right).
\]
The asymptotic is locally uniform in $(x,z)$.

Moreover, on every fixed time interval, the conditioned process converges
in total variation to the ground-state diffusion
\[
    \de Y_t
      =
      \left[
        -KY_t+\sigma^2\nabla\log
        \psi_{\beta_\theta}(Y_t)
      \right]\de t
      +\sigma\,\de B_t,
    \qquad Y_0=x.
\]

Let \(\Psi \in \mathrm{U}(dL)\) be a unitary matrix. Then, with probability at least \(1 - \eta\), the scaled matrix \(m^{-1/2} \mathbf{B} \Psi\) satisfies the group restricted isometry property (group-RIP) of order \(s\) with constant \(\delta_s \leq \delta\), provided that

\[
m \gtrsim_{\tau} \delta^{-2} \left[ s^2 \mu_{\mathcal{S}}^2 \log^2 D \left( \log^2 G + g^2 \log^2 \left( \frac{s}{\mu_{\mathcal{S}}} \right) \right) + \log \left( \frac{1}{\eta} \right) \right],
\]

where $\mu_{\mathcal{S}}$ and $\boldsymbol{\psi}_i$ is denote as above.

[Corollary 6 of arXiv:2603.28226, '2603.28226'] Let $f\in L^1(\mathcal F_\infty)$ and $\lambda>0$. Then one can write
\[
 f=g+h+k
\]
with $g,h,k\in L^1(\mathcal F_\infty)$ such that

\medskip
\noindent\textup{(a$'$)}
\[
\mathbb P\Bigl(\sup_{n\ge1}|\mathbb E_n[g]|>0\Bigr)
\le \frac{2\|f\|_1}{\lambda},
\qquad
\|g\|_1\le4\|f\|_1.
\]

\noindent\textup{(b$'$)}
\[
\Bigl\|\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|\mathbb E_n[h]-\mathbb E_{n-1}[h]|\Bigr\|_1
\le4\|f\|_1.
\]
In particular, $\|h\|_1\le4\|f\|_1$.

\noindent\textup{(c$'$)}
\[
 \|k\|_\infty\le \lambda,
 \qquad
 \|k\|_1\le2\|f\|_1,
 \qquad
 \|k\|_2^2\le2\lambda\|f\|_1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Proposition 42 (Independent failure mechanisms) of arXiv:2608.08756, 'Infinite-Dimensional L\'evy Area and Spectral Ancestry'] Each part of the architecture has an independent role.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.8em]
\item Without filteredness, an algebraic order-one vector may be sent to
      singular values $N^{-1/2}$, so no finite critical upper grade exists.
\item With filteredness but proper kernel support, every nonzero probe in the
      annihilator of that support is invisible at the correct grade.
\item A full-support kernel may carry an oscillatory boundary representative;
      valuation equality then holds without an asymptotic equivalent.
\item If the grade-one boundary class is nilpotent under tensor product, one
      grade-one certificate cannot propagate to every depth.
\item If labels are discarded, equal singular-value profiles can represent
      distinct coefficient directions, so annihilator reconstruction fails.
\item A universal coefficient-pure kernel says nothing about an unrelated raw
      observable until its native readers are shown to push forward that
      kernel with full support.
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma lem:advancing-transient of arXiv:2602.21315, 'The Instability of all Backoff Protocols\thanks{For the purpose of Open Access, the author'] Fix $\lambda \in (0,1)$ and a send sequence $\overline{p}$ with $p_0=1$.  
Let $j_0$ be a sufficiently large positive integer. Let $\tau_0$ be a  non-negative integer. Let $\Psi_0$ be the   initialising high-level state with  $\tau^{\Psi_0} = \tau_0$ and $j^{\Psi_0} = j_0$. 
Let $\mathrm{hls}$ be the $\Psi_0$-backoff bounding rule from Definition~(def:backoff-bounding-rule of the paper).  
Let $V$ be a volume process from $\Psi_0$ with transition rule $\mathrm{hls}$ send sequence~$\overline{p}$ and birth rate~$\lambda$. 
Let $t> \tau_0$ be a positive integer such that $\Psi(t)$ is $j$-advancing and $\tau^{\Psi(t)} = t$.
Then there is an integer $t'$
in the range
$t < t' \le t+ 12 j^{\phi+1}W_j$ such that $\Psi(t') \neq \Psi(t)$.

[Lemma 8 (Dissipative resolvent) of arXiv:2608.08177, 'Uniform-in-Time Smoluchowski--Kramers Approximation\\ in Total Variation for Fractional SD'] Let $q:[0,\infty)\to[\lambda,L]$ be measurable and let
\[
  v_t=e^{-\int_0^tq_rdr}v_0
      +\int_0^t e^{-\int_s^tq_rdr}f_s\,ds.
\]
For every $p\ge1$,
\[
 \sup_{t\ge0}\norm{v_t}_{L^p}
 \le \norm{v_0}_{L^p}
     +\lambda^{-1}\sup_{s\ge0}\norm{f_s}_{L^p}.
\]
If $f_s$ is replaced by a locally integrable random process, then
\[
 \norm{v_t}_{L^p}
 \le e^{-\lambda t}\norm{v_0}_{L^p}
 +\int_0^t e^{-\lambda(t-s)}\norm{f_s}_{L^p}\,ds.
\]

[Lemma 18 (Extension from finite spatial blocks) of arXiv:2607.10813, '2607.10813'] Let $X_1,\ldots,X_m$ be Banach spaces obtained as the closures of subspaces
$X_1^0,\ldots,X_m^0$ of smooth finite-spatial-block paths.  If a $m$-linear
map $T$ satisfies
\[
 \|T(f_1,\ldots,f_m)\|_Y
 \le C\prod_{\nu=1}^m\|f_{\nu}\|_{X_{\nu}},
 \qquad f_{\nu}\in X_{\nu}^0,
\]
for a Banach space $Y$, then it extends uniquely to a continuous $m$-linear
map on $X_1\times\cdots\times X_m$.  The same assertion holds with
$Y$ replaced by $L^p(\Omega;Y)$ or by a Banach space of bounded operators.
If the approximating outputs have a uniform vanishing Littlewood--Paley tail,
the extension takes values in the corresponding little-Besov closure.

It also shows the two-regime structure: defect-poor blocks can never be charged locally, but they admit exactly-absorbed alternatives once ancestors have paid. Note the caveat 'once its two boundary residuals have been ancestor-paid' -- the bookkeeping semantics matter.

[Prop 31 of arXiv:2608.05185, '\large\bf ON THE HEAT FLOW CONJECTURE FOR RANDOM MATRICES'] Let \(s>0\), let \(\left|c_0\right|\leq s\), and let
\(\mathbf{A}_N=\mathbf{A}_N^*\) satisfy
\[
 \sup_N\|\mathbf{A}_N\|<\infty,
 \qquad
 L_{\mathbf{A}_N}\overset{\mathrm{w}}{\longrightarrow}\mu_0.
\]
If we define,
\[
 p_N(z)=\det(z\mathbf{I}-\mathbf{A}_N-\mathbf{Z}_N(s,c_0)),
 \qquad
 q_N(z)=
 \exp\!\left(-\frac{s-c_0}{2N}\partial_z^2\right)p_N(z),
\]
then, we have
\[
 \nu_{q_N}\overset{\mathrm{w}}{\longrightarrow}
 \mu_0\boxplus\mathfrak{sc}_s
 \qquad\text{almost surely}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop 31 of arXiv:2608.05185

W_1 X, loss ell = ||U - Y||_F^2 / 2, gradient descent in the W coordinates with step 0 <= eta <= 1. For all sufficiently large L (threshold depending on the data), if max(d_x, d_y) <= m <= L/(420 log L), then with probability at least 1 - m/L - L^{-612/8335} the loss stays in [0.4, 0.6] ||Y||_F^2 for every integer 0 <= t <= floor(exp(L/(21000 m))). Version 1 of the same argument gives m <= L/(10000 log L), horizon exp(L/(1000 m)), probability >= 1 - 1/L - L^{-47}.

[Lemma lem:measurable-Hilbert-field-calculus of arXiv:2608.02459, 'Response Calculus for Spectral Simplicity\\ and Joint Eigenvalue Densities'] From the preceding definitions we obtain the following three properties.
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)},leftmargin=*,itemsep=0pt,topsep=2pt,parsep=0pt]
 \item For every $j\ge1$, the map $\mu\mapsto e_j(\mu)\in H_\mu$ is
 measurable.
 \item For every $\mu$, $\mathcal E_\mu$ is an orthonormal basis of $H_\mu$.
 In particular, $J_N(\mu)$ is the orthogonal projection onto
 $\operatorname{span}\{e_1(\mu),\ldots,e_N(\mu)\}$ and
 \begin{equation}
  \|J_N(\mu)u-u\|_{H_\mu}\longrightarrow0
  \qquad\text{for every }u\in H_\mu.
 \end{equation}
 \item An operator field $T$ is measurable in the sense of
 (equation eq:measurable-operator-field-definition of the paper) if and only if
 \[
  \mu\longmapsto
  \langle e_i(\mu),T_\mu e_j(\mu)\rangle_{H_\mu}
  \quad\text{is measurable for every }i,j.
 \]
\end{enumerate}

[Prop 55 ({cf.~\cite[Corollary~7.8) of arXiv:2609.02561, 'NON-NEF LOCI IN MIXED CHARACTERISTIC'] {HLS}}]
Let $(R,\m,k)$ be a complete regular local ring of residue characteristic $p>0$,
and let $\Delta\geq 0$ be a $\Q$-divisor on $\Spec R$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item 
If $\ord_{\m}(\Delta)<1$,
then
$\alphabcm(R,\Delta)\geq 1-\ord_{\m}(\Delta)$.
In particular, $\alphabcm(R,0)=1$.
\item If $k$ is $F$-finite, $\lfloor\Delta\rfloor=0$, and $\Supp\Delta$ is simple normal crossing,
then 
\[ \alphabcm(R,\Delta)=1-\max\{ \text{coefficients of $\Delta$}\}. \]
\end{enumerate}

body: A map T : V -> W between vector spaces over the same field F is linear if T(u + v) = T(u) + T(v) and T(av) = a T(v) for all u, v in V and a in F. Its kernel is { v : Tv = 0 } and its image is { Tv : v in V }; both are subspaces.

[Lemma lem:poincare_density of arXiv:2609.01581, 'Concentration of additive functionals of Stratonovich-type'] Let Assumptions~(ass:dynamics of the paper) hold, such that the symmetric part
$\mathcal{L}_S$ satisfies the Poincar\'e inequality~(equation eq:poincare of the paper) with
spectral gap $\lambda_\mathrm{gap}>0$ and let $\E^\mu[V]\equiv\int V\mathrm{d} \mu$. Then for every $k$ with
$0\leq k < \lambda_{\mathrm{gap}}/\|V-\E^\mu[V]\|_{L^\infty(\mu)}$,
\begin{align}
  \Lambda^\rho(k)
  \leq
  k \E^\mu[V]
  + \frac{k^2 \mathrm{Var}_\mu(V)}{\lambda_\mathrm{gap} - k \|V-\E^\mu[V]\|_{L^\infty(\mu)}}.
  
\end{align}

body: Let X >= 0 with 0 < E[X^2] < infinity. The second moment method is the chain of consequences of Paley-Zygmund and Chebyshev. FIRST FORM: P(X > 0) >= (E X)^2 / E[X^2]. This gives only a LOWER BOUND ON THE PROBABILITY, bounded away from 0 when the second moment is comparable to the square of the first; it does NOT give an event of probability tending to 1. SECOND FORM: if Var(X) / (E X)^2 -> 0 along a sequence of models, then X / E[X] -> 1 in probability by Chebyshev, so X > 0 with probability tending to 1 and moreover X is concentrated. Confusing the two is the standard error: E[X^2] <= C (E X)^2 with C > 1 fixed gives positive probability at least 1/C, and no amount of that alone upgrades to high probability. The repair when only the first form is available is usually a 0-1 law or a sprinkling or self-improvement argument that turns positive probability into probability one, not a better moment estimate. The typical use is a counting random variable X = number of structures of a given type: the first moment method (Markov: P(X >= 1) <= E X) gives the upper threshold, and the second moment method gives the lower one, and the two match only when the second moment is not inflated by correlated pairs. [standard; e.g. Alon and Spencer, The Probabilistic Method, Chapter 4]

T250-w712-C004 v1. Target 1. Status: proof (unaudited).

This addresses the deterministic amplification factor for several inputs. It does not prove a finite-width multi-input Gaussian approximation.

Write F(q)=E tanh(sqrt(q)Z)^2. For q,r in (0,1] and u in [-1,1], define

    H(q,r,u)=E[tanh(sqrt(q)X)tanh(sqrt(r)Y)]/sqrt(F(q)F(r)),

where (X,Y) are jointly standard normal of correlation u. Then H is increasing in u and

    Lip_u H(q,r,.) <= 1+8(q^2+r^2).                (1)

For deterministic critical tanh variance trajectories q_(l+1)=F(q_l), r_(l+1)=F(r_l), and any two correlation trajectories with these same marginal variances,

    u_(l+1)=H(q_l,r_l,u_l),
    v_(l+1)=H(q_l,r_l,v_l),

one has, uniformly over depth L,

    |u_L-v_L| <= exp(48(q_0+r_0)) |u_0-v_0| <= exp(96)|u_0-v_0|.     (2)

Proof of (1). Let f_q(z)=tanh(sqrt(q)z). Its Gaussian mean is zero by oddness. Set chi(q)=E f_q'(Z)^2/F(q). Gaussian integration by parts and Cauchy-Schwarz give

    (E f_q'(Z))^2 = (E Z f_q(Z))^2 <= F(q).

Apply the Gaussian Poincare inequality to f_q':

    E f_q'^2-F(q) <= Var(f_q') <= E f_q''^2.

Since f_q''(z)=-2q tanh(sqrt(q)z) sech(sqrt(q)z)^2, the inequality |tanh t|<=|t| implies E f_q''^2<=4q^3. The lower bound F(q)>=q/4 from C002 gives

    chi(q)<=1+16q^2.

All these quantities are integrable: the first two derivatives of f_q are bounded for each q, and the displayed fourth bound uses only E Z^2=1. No limiting variance is divided by zero because q>0.

For |u|<1, Gaussian covariance differentiation (Price's identity) gives

    partial_u H(q,r,u)
      = E[f_q'(X) f_r'(Y)]/sqrt(F(q)F(r)).

Both derivatives are nonnegative. Cauchy-Schwarz bounds the right side by sqrt(chi(q)chi(r)), and the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality bounds this by 1+8(q^2+r^2). For completeness, Price's identity here follows by differentiating the bivariate Gaussian density p_u and using partial_u p_u=partial_x partial_y p_u; integration by parts twice transfers those derivatives to f_q and f_r. On every compact subinterval of (-1,1), density derivatives have integrable polynomial-Gaussian bounds and the tanh functions and their derivatives are bounded. Thus differentiation and integration by parts are justified. The representation Y=uX+sqrt(1-u^2)Z and bounded dominated convergence extend H continuously to u=+-1. The uniform interior derivative bound then implies the same Lipschitz bound on the closed interval.

Proof of (2). C002 proves F(q)<=q-q^2/6 on [0,1]. Consequently

    sum_(l=0)^(L-1) q_l^2 <=6(q_0-q_L)<=6q_0,

and likewise for r. Applying (1) at each deterministic step and using 1+x<=exp(x) gives

    product_(l=0)^(L-1) [1+8(q_l^2+r_l^2)]
       <= exp(8 sum_l(q_l^2+r_l^2))
       <= exp(48(q_0+r_0)).

This proves the depth-independent bound.

The first proposed route used an odd-Hermite spectral estimate. The proof above instead uses only ordinary Gaussian Poincare, integration by parts, and covariance differentiation. There is no need for a sharper Hermite coefficient or an additional parity lemma.

The unpaid step is stochastic. Finite-width q_l and r_l are random, and the empirical normalized correlation also has sampling noise and conditional bias. Formula (2) does not license replacing random path products by products of expected factors. A multi-input result must jointly control those random marginal variances, correlation fluctuations, and near-singular deterministic correlation matrices. None of those controls is assumed proved here.

[Theorem Gelfand of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] If $X$ is a compact space, the algebra $C(X)$ of continuous functions on it $f:X\to\mathbb C$ is a $C^*$-algebra, with usual norm and involution, namely:
$$||f||=\sup_{x\in X}|f(x)|\quad,\quad 
f^*(x)=\overline{f(x)}$$
Conversely, any commutative $C^*$-algebra is of this form, $A=C(X)$, with 
$$X=\Big\{\chi:A\to\mathbb C\ ,\ {\rm normed\ algebra\ character}\Big\}$$
with topology making continuous the evaluation maps $ev_a:\chi\to\chi(a)$.

body: In mathematics, the Poisson summation formula is an equation that relates the Fourier series coefficients of the periodic summation of a function to values of the function's continuous Fourier transform. Consequently, the periodic summation of a function is completely defined by discrete samples of the original function's Fourier transform. And conversely, the periodic summation of a function's Fourier transform is completely defined by discrete samples of the original function. The Poisson summation formula was discovered by Siméon Denis Poisson and is sometimes called Poisson resummation.
title: Poisson summation formula

[Theorem 31 (Iteration on a connected large-diameter interval) of arXiv:2608.30027, 'Under Ricci flow, a 3-torus goes flat'] Under the standing fixed-threshold application with cutoff \(c_0\), fix
\(\delta_0\geq c_0\), an integer \(N\geq2\), and \(\sigma\in(0,1)\).  There are constants \(\eta_0>0\) and
\(T_{\mathrm{p}}<\infty\) with the
following properties.  The constant \(\eta_0\) depends only on
\(K,\delta_0,N,\sigma\); the threshold \(T_{\mathrm{p}}\) may additionally
depend on the fixed Bamler tail data \(T_B(c_0)\) and
\(\eps_B^{c_0}\).  Neither depends
on the number \(D_1\) below.

Let \(I\) be a connected time interval on which
\begin{equation}
        \diam(M,g(t))\geq\delta_0\sqrt t.
\end{equation}
Suppose that \(S\in I\), \(S\geq T_{\mathrm{p}}\), and
\begin{equation}
        \diam(M,g(S))\leq D_1\sqrt S
\end{equation}
for some \(0<D_1<\infty\).  At time \(S\), choose the torus fibration from
case~\ref{item:bamler-large-slice} of
Proposition~\ref{input:bamler-fixed-threshold}, put
\[
        q_0(1)=S^{-1}g(S),\qquad r_0(1)=\overline{q_0(1)},
\]
where the average is taken in that fibration, and suppose that \(r_0(1)\) is
Riemannian and
\begin{equation}
 b_0=\|q_0(1)-r_0(1)\|_{C^{N,\sigma}(M,r_0(1))}<\eta_0.
\end{equation}

Set \(T_k=100^kS\).  Call the \(k\)th block \emph{controlled} if
\([T_k,T_{k+1}]\subset I\).  On every controlled block, the same retained
torus fibration supports stagewise families \(q_k(\tau)\), \(r_k(\tau)\),
\(1\leq\tau\leq100\), and the estimates
\begin{align}
 b_{k+1}&\leq\tfrac12b_k,                                      \\
 \|q_k-r_k\|_{X_{r_k}^N[1,100]}
        &\leq C_{\mathrm{st}}b_k,                              \\
 \|r_{k+1}(1)-100^{-1}r_k(100)\|_{C^{N,\sigma}}
        &\leq C_{\mathrm{st}}b_k.                              
\end{align}
Here and below the norm in the last line is taken relative to
\(100^{-1}r_k(100)\).  On the union of the controlled blocks these stages
assemble into a continuous piecewise smooth pullback
\(g'(t)=\Psi(t)^*g(t)\) and a right-continuous piecewise invariant family
\(h(t)\), as in Section~\ref{sec:deturck-iteration}.  There is a constant
\(C<\infty\), depending only on \(K,\delta_0,N,\sigma\) and \(D_1\), such that
\begin{equation}
        L(S^1,h_{yy}(t))\leq C\sqrt t
\end{equation}
on every controlled block, for either one-sided value at a switching time,
and
\begin{equation}
        \diam(M,g(t))\leq C\sqrt t
\end{equation}
for every \(t\in I\cap[S,\infty)\).  Thus the same theorem covers both an
unbounded persistent tail and a finite component with a terminal partial
block. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Iteration on a connected large-diameter interval

			 t^{- \frac{\gamma p}{d(1-\b)}} \mbox{\bf 1}_{\{\frac pq<\frac{d}{d+q}\}}+t^{- \frac{\gamma(q-p)}{q(1-\b)}}\mbox{\bf 1}_{\{\frac{d}{d+q} < \frac pq<1\}}&  \mbox{ if $p<d(1-\b)$},\\
 			
			
			t^{- \gamma }\log(1+t)\mbox{\bf 1}_{\{ \frac pq<\b\}}+t^{- \frac{\gamma(q-p)}{q(1-\b)}}\mbox{\bf 1}_{\{\b < \frac pq<1\}}&  \mbox{ if $p=d(1-\b)$},\\
			
			
			t^{-\gamma}\mbox{\bf 1}_{\{ \frac pq<\b\}}+t^{-\frac{\gamma(q-p)}{q(1-\b)}}\mbox{\bf 1}_{\{\b < \frac pq<1\}}  & \mbox{ if $p>d(1-\b)$}.
			
			
\end{array}\right.
\]

In particular, if $\AUNgamma$ holds for some $q>\frac{p}{\beta}$, then there exists  a finite constant $K=K_{\b,p,d,\tzero}>0$ exists such that

\begin{equation}
\big\| {\cal W}_p(\nu_t,\nu) \big\|_p=\E[{\cal W}^p_p(\nu_t,\nu)]^{\frac{1}{p}}\le {K}[{{\Mpiq}}]^{\frac 1p}\left\{ \begin{array}{ll}
 t^{-\frac{\gamma}{d(1-\beta)}}&\mbox{ if $p< d(1-\beta)$}\\
 t^{-\frac{\gamma}{p}}(\log(1+t))^{-\frac 1p}&\mbox{ if $p=  d(1-\beta)$}\\

t^{-\frac{\gamma}{p}} &\mbox{ if $p>d(1-\beta)$}.
							
							\end{array}\right.
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Let G be a finite connected subgraph of the honeycomb lattice with vertex set V and internal edge set E, and set all boundary half-edge values to zero. For each internal edge e=uv with midpoint m_e, consider complex midpoint values F satisfying at every v the relation sum_{e incident to v}(m_e-v)F(m_e)=0. The complex solution space has dimension |E|-|V|+1. An interior regular hexagonal face of side delta supports a solution with sup norm one, zero boundary values, and neighboring face-midpoint values differing by one over Euclidean distance sqrt(3)delta/2. Consequently this local equation with bounded values and fixed boundary data alone implies neither uniqueness nor mesh-uniform equicontinuity. These kernel solutions are not asserted to be SAW path-sum observables.

Let X be a random variable with E[X] = 0 and a <= X <= b almost surely. Then for every real lambda, E[exp(lambda X)] <= exp(lambda^2 (b-a)^2 / 8). Equivalently X is sub-Gaussian with variance proxy (b-a)^2/4. The constant 8 in the exponent is sharp for the two-point symmetric law on {-c, c}, where (b-a)^2/8 = c^2/2 and the bound is attained to second order. Only the RANGE enters, not the variance: for a Bernoulli variable with small p the bound is far from tight, and Bennett's and Bernstein's inequalities recover the variance. Summing the lemma over independent bounded summands and applying the Chernoff method gives Hoeffding's inequality P(sum (X_i - E X_i) >= t) <= exp(-2t^2 / sum (b_i - a_i)^2). [Hoeffding (1963); see Boucheron, Lugosi and Massart, Concentration Inequalities, Lemma 2.2]

body:
[Lemma 14 (Residual identity) of arXiv:2609.02389, 'The Class Edge-Reconstruction Number of a\\ Maximal Planar Graph Is One or Two'] Suppose the same card has completions \(G=C+e\) and \(H=C+e'\), and set
\[
                  Q=A_G(e)-A_H(e').
\]
If \(G-g\cong H-h\), then
\[
                  A_G(g)-A_H(h)=Q.                 \tag{C.1}
\]
Write \(Q=P-N\), where \(P,N\) have disjoint supports and nonnegative
integer entries.  Their common total mass \(r\) is zero, one, or two.  If
every edge card of \(G\) has a degree-sequence match among the edge cards of
\(H\), then:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)},leftmargin=2.2em]
\item if \(r=2\), every edge of \(G\) has the same unordered endpoint-degree
pair;
\item if \(r=1\), the vertices of one fixed degree form a vertex cover of
\(G\);
\item if \(r=0\), then \(Q=0\).
\end{enumerate}

[Lemma ll1 of arXiv:2608.02897, 'Local limit theorem and Edgeworth expansions for inhomogeneous random walks on $GL(d,\bbR)'] For all $\epsilon$ small enough 
there are $C_0>0$ and $\theta_1\in(0,1)$ such that for all $t\in\mathbb R$ and $g:\mathbb P^{d-1}(\mathbb R)\to\mathbb C$, 
$$ 
v_\epsilon({\mathcal L}_{j,it}^n g)\leq C_0 \left[|t|\|g\|_\infty+\theta_1^n v_\epsilon(g)\right]
$$
where $\|g\|_\infty=\sup_{x\in{\mathbb P}^{d-1}({\mathbb R})}|g(x)|$. Thus for all $T>0$ 
there is $C_1>0$ and  such that for all $t\in[-T,T]$ and $g:\mathbb P^{d-1}(\mathbb R)\to\mathbb C$, 
$$ 
v_\epsilon({\mathcal L}_{j,it}^n g)\leq C_1 \left[\|g\|_\infty+\theta_1^n v_\epsilon(g)\right]
$$

[Lem LM41 of arXiv:2608.16170, '\bf On hitting time distributions of Markov processes with sub-Gaussian heat kernel bounds'] Let $X$ be a Borel right process on $(E,d)$ satisfying (AC), (H1a) and (H1b).

Let $B\subset E$ be a nearly Borel set of finite $1$-order capacity. Then for any $\lambda>0$, there exists a unique finite, positive measure $\nu^{(\lambda)}_B$ on $E$ with $\mathrm{supp}[\nu_B^{(\lambda)}]\subset \overline{B}$ such that
\begin{equation}
     p_B^{(\lambda)}(x):=\mathbb{E}^x[\mathrm{e}^{-\lambda \sigma_B}]=\int_E u_\lambda(x,y)\nu_B^{(\lambda)}(\mathrm{d} y),\quad \forall x\in E.
 \end{equation}
In particular, for any $\lambda>0$, 
\[
{\mathbb{P}}^x\left[\sigma_B\le t\right] \ge \emph{Cap}_{(\lambda)}(B)  \inf_{y\in \overline B} \int_0^t \mathrm{e}^{-\lambda s} p(s, x, y)\mathrm{d} s,\quad \forall t>0,x\in E.
\]

[Definition 44 of arXiv:2603.24616, 'Pinning in non-critical half-space geometric last passage percolation'] Fix $a \in \mathbb{R}$ and $N \in \mathbb{N}$. We define the contours 
$$\gamma^+_N(a,0) = \{1 + aN^{-1/3} + |s|N^{-1/3} e^{\mathrm{sgn}(s)\im(\pi/3)}: s \in [-N^{1/4}, N^{1/4}] \}, \mbox{and }$$
$$\gamma^-_N(a,0) = \{1 + aN^{-1/3} + |s|N^{-1/3} e^{\mathrm{sgn}(s) \im(2\pi/3)}: s \in [-N^{1/4}, N^{1/4}] \},$$
both oriented in the direction of increasing imaginary part. We further let $\gamma^+_N(a,1)$ be the arc of the $0$-centered circle that connects the points $1 + aN^{-1/3} + N^{-1/12} e^{\im(\pi/3)}$ to $1 + aN^{-1/3} + N^{-1/12} e^{-\im(\pi/3)}$, and $\gamma^-_N(a,1)$ be the arc of the $0$-centered circle that connects the points $1 + aN^{-1/3} + N^{-1/12} e^{\im(2\pi/3)}$ to $1 + aN^{-1/3} + N^{-1/12} e^{-2\im(\pi/3)}$. Both $\gamma^+_N(a,1)$ and $\gamma^-_N(a,1)$ are oriented counter-clockwise. Finally, we set $\gamma_N^+(a) = \gamma_N^+(a,0) \cup \gamma_N^+(a,1)$ and $\gamma_N^-(a) = \gamma_N^-(a,0) \cup \gamma_N^-(a,1)$. See Figure \ref{S21} for an illustration of these contours. We also recall from Section \ref{Section4.2} that $C_r$ is the positively oriented zero-centered circle of radius $r > 0$.

[Theorem thm:int-0 of arXiv:2510.06891, 'Multivariate CLT for L\'evy processes: convergence rates without moment assumptions'] Let $\bm{X}$ be 
a genuinely $d$-dimensional L\'evy process and $\bm{Z}$ a  standard Gaussian random vector in $\mathbb{R}^d$. 

Let $\mathscr{A}$ be either $\mathscr{K}$ or $\mathscr{C}$ defined above. Then the following conditions are equivalent.
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=2.5em, nosep]
\item[{\nf(a)}] 
 $\mathds{E}[|\bm{X}_1|^2]<\infty$.
\item[{\nf(b)}] There exist measurable $\bm{A}:[1,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}^{d}$ and $\bm{B}:[1,\infty) \to \mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$, such that $\bm{B}(t)$ is invertible for all sufficiently large $t$, the limits $\bm{e}_j^\intercal \bm{B}(t)^\intercal \bm{B}(t)\bm{e}_j \to \infty$ and $\bm{B}(t)^{-1}\bm{B}(f(t))\to \bm{I}_d$ hold for all $j\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$ and non-decreasing functions $f$ with $f(t)/t\to 1$ as $t \to \infty$, respectively, and 
\[
t \mapsto t^{-1}d_\mathscr{A}(\bm{X}_t-\bm{A}(t),\bm{B}(t) \bm{Z} )\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(+\infty).
\]
\end{itemize}
Moreover,  for any function $\bm{B}$ satisfying condition~{\normalfont{(b)}}, we have $\lim_{t\to\infty}d_\mathscr{C}(\bm{X}_t-t\mathds{E}\bm{X}_1,\bm{B}(t) \bm{Z} )=0$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Theorem 9 of arXiv:2608.22597, 'Scale-invariant Optimal Sampling for Rare-events Data with Sparse Models'] Denote $\X=(\x_1,...,\x_N)$ as the full-data design matrix and $\Ds$ as a
subsample. For fixed $s_{N}$,
consider a class of subsample estimators under the true model with the following
asymptotic representation:
\begin{equation}
\htheta_{U(\cA)}=\U_{(\cA)}(\btheta_{\rt};\Ds)
+o_P\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{N_1}}\right),
\end{equation}
where $\U_{(\cA)}(\btheta_{\rt};\Ds)$ satisfies that
$\Exp\{\U_{(\cA)}(\btheta_{\rt};\Ds)|\X\}=\btheta_{\rt(\cA)}$,
$N_1\Var\{\U_{(\cA)}(\btheta_{\rt};\Ds)\} \cvp\V_{U(\cA)}$, and
$\Exp\left\{\partial\U_{(\cA)}(\btheta_{\rt};\Ds)/\partial\btheta_{(\cA)}\tp\Big|\X\right\}=\0$. 
Then the asymptotic variance $\V_{U(\cA)}$ satisfies that
$\V_{U(\cA)}\geq\V_{\ruw(\cA)}$. (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

Use the network and empirical FIM in assumptions. These limits may be assumed almost surely or in probability; the conclusion holds in the same mode. Let P=sum_(l=1)^L M_l*(M_(l-1)+1), alpha=sum_(l=1)^(L-1) alpha_l*alpha_(l-1)>0, m_lambda=Tr(F)/P, and kappa_1=(1/alpha)*sum_(l=1)^L alpha_(l-1)*qtilde_l*qhat_(l-1). Then M*m_lambda->C*kappa_1. Taking qhat,qtilde from the companion mean-field closure gives the leading formula in source Theorem1, m_lambda~C*kappa_1/M when kappa_1>0. This card makes the norm-limit premise explicit; it does not prove that premise or the backward decoupling closure for the original tied-weight network. It concerns the mean, not the second moment or largest eigenvalue.
Fixed L>=2 and fixed positive integers C,T. Widths M_l/M->alpha_l>0 for l=0,...,L-1; M_L=C. Hidden layers h_l=phi(u_l), u_l=W_l*h_(l-1)+b_l; output f=u_L is linear.

phi and phi_prime have finite squared Gaussian integrals at each recursively occurring preactivation variance. The empirical FIM normalization is F=(1/T)*sum_(t=1)^T sum_(k=1)^C grad_theta f_k(x_t)*grad_theta f_k(x_t)^T.
The explicitly stated forward/backward norm limits are assumptions. Fixed finite T,C,L; alpha_l>0; qhat,qtilde finite and common across samples and output coordinates.

[Theorem of arXiv:2608.10415, 'Continuous random variables'] Given a sequence of complex Wishart matrices
$$W_N=Y_NY_N^*\in M_N(L^\infty(X))$$
with $Y_N$ being $N\times N$ complex Gaussian of parameter $t>0$, we have
$$\frac{W_N}{tN}\sim\frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{4x^{-1}-1}\,dx$$
with $N\to\infty$, with the limiting measure being the Marchenko-Pastur law $\pi_1$.

[Corollary 28 of arXiv:2605.06556, 'Probability of Quota Violations in Divisor Apportionment Methods with Nonzero Allocations'] Let $A$ be the Modified Jefferson method with divisor function
\[
\delta(s) = \begin{cases} 0 & s = 0, \\ s + 1 & s \geq 1. \end{cases}
\]
Then, under the asymptotic uniform distribution on reduced population vectors $(1, x, y)$
with $1 < x < y$, the probability of a quota violation caused by nonzero allocations is
exactly
\[
P_M^{\mathrm{JEFF}} = \frac{1}{M-1}.
\]

[Proposition prop:ergodic of arXiv:2608.24830, 'Motion helps the contact process: survival below\\ the percolation threshold on Poisson Br'] Attaching to each particle its recovery process as a mark makes
$\widetilde{\mathcal P}=\{(X_u,\mathcal R_u):u\in\mathcal P\}$ a Poisson process on
$C([0,\infty);\mathbb{R}^d)\times\mathbb M$, where $\mathbb M$ is the space of locally finite subsets of
$[0,\infty)$ and the intensity is $\nu_\eta\otimes\Pi_\mu$. Here $\Pi_\mu$ is the law of a
rate-$\mu$ Poisson process and $\Pi_\infty:=\delta_{[0,\infty)}$, since no marks are needed at
$\mu=\infty$. This process is ergodic under the spatial translations
$\vartheta_z:(w,\rho)\mapsto(w+z,\rho)$, $z\in\mathbb{R}^d$. Consequently, if $\mathcal S$ is a
translation-covariant factor of $\widetilde{\mathcal P}$ which is a point process of positive
intensity, then $\mathcal S\ne\emptyset$ almost surely.

body: In mathematics, especially general topology and mathematical analysis, compactness is a property of a space that makes it behave in many ways like a finite set. For instance, on a finite set every infinite sequence must take some value infinitely often, by the pigeonhole principle. For subsets of Euclidean space, the analogous statement is sequential compactness: a set is compact if and only if every infinite sequence in the set has a subsequence that converges to a point of the set. Likewise, whereas every real-valued function on a finite set is bounded and attains its maximum and minimum, every continuous real-valued function on a compact space has these properties. For compact subsets of Euclidean space, this is the extreme value theorem.
title: Compact space

				\[\lim_{L\to \infty}R_{1;L,t}(\mu)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu t}},\;\; \lim_{L\to \infty}K_{L,t}(\mu)=\frac{1}{\mu^2t},\;\; \lim_{L\to \infty}K_{L,t}'(\mu)=-\frac{2}{\mu^3t}.\]

[Corollary cor: duality of arXiv:2504.04792, 'Uniqueness and Longtime Behavior of the Completely Positively Correlated Symbiotic Branchi'] Let $\dot{W}$ and $\dot{W_0}$ be two independent white noises on $\mathbb{R}_+ \times \mathbb{R}$. Let $\psi \in C_{\text{tem}}^+$ and $\phi \in C_{\text{rap}}^+$. Define $(V_t)_{t \geq 0}$ and $(\Tilde{V}_t)_{t \geq 0}$ as the unique solutions with values in $C_{\text{tem}}^+$ and $C_{\text{rap}}^+$, respectively, of equation $((eq: dual of the paper))$, driven by $\dot{W}$ and $\dot{W_0}$, respectively, with initial conditions $V_0 = \psi$  and $\Tilde{V}_0 = \phi$. Then, for each $T > 0$, the following self-duality formula holds:
\begin{equation}

    \mathbb{E}\left[e^{-\langle \Tilde{V}_T, \psi \rangle}\right] = \mathbb{E}\left[e^{-\langle \phi, V_T \rangle }\right].
\end{equation} (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Prop side condition for the giant of arXiv:2605.03151, 'Giants through Higher-Order paths in Random Simplicial Complexes'] Let $(X_n)_{n \geq 1}$ be a sequence of random finite $d$-dimensional simplicial complexes that converges locally weakly in probability to $(X, o) \sim \mu$. Assume further that 
\[  \tag{2.2.3}
\lim_{k \to \infty} \limsup_{n \to \infty} \mathbb{P} \left( \sigma_1 \overset{\scriptscriptstyle{d}}{\longleftrightarrow} \sigma_2, s_{d-1}(\mathcal{C}(\sigma_1)), s_{d-1}(\mathcal{C}(\sigma_2)) \geq k \right) = 1,
\]
where $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$ are chosen uniformly at random from $X_n$. Then, it holds that
\[
\frac{s_{d-1}(\mathcal{C}_{\max})}{s_{d-1}(X_n)} \overset{\mathbb{P}}{\to} \mu \left( s_{d-1}(\mathcal{C}(o)) = \infty \right) 
\]
and
\[
\frac{s_{d-1}(\mathcal{C}_{(2)})}{s_{d-1}(X_n)} \overset{\mathbb{P}}{\to} 0.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Prop side condition for the giant of arXiv:2605.03151

[Conjecture Thin-compression ($m/d\to0$) spike phase diagram of arXiv:2609.02155, 'Exact Limits of Random Projections for Preserving Geometry:\\ Distance Recovery, Nearest-N'] \label[conjecture]{conj:spikes}
Consider $m/d\to0$ with centered covariance variation spread across many eigendirections and with no dominant eigenvalue. First, identify conditions under which the normalized compressed traceless bulk has a universal limiting spectrum. Second, determine when a finite-rank population spike becomes distinguishable from that bulk. A semicircle transition is plausible only under additional assumptions. Under \emph{free compression}---the free-probability model for compression by a generic random projection---the compressed spectral law still depends on the population law. For example, compressing $\sigma^2I+\lambda vv^\top$ produces a scalar matrix plus rank one, with no population-level random bulk. A detection threshold must therefore depend jointly on projection dimension, sample size, and covariance, as in deformed random-matrix models, which study random spectral bulks perturbed by low-rank structure [baik2005phase]. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)
title: Thin-compression ($m/d\to0$) spike phase diagram

body: In mathematics, the uniform boundedness principle or Banach–Steinhaus theorem is one of the fundamental results in functional analysis. Together with the Hahn–Banach theorem and the open mapping theorem, it is considered one of the cornerstones of the field. In its basic form, it asserts that for a family of continuous linear operators whose domain is a Banach space, pointwise boundedness is equivalent to uniform boundedness in operator norm.
title: Uniform boundedness principle

body:
[Lem 144 of arXiv:2608.29416, 'Algorithmic threshold for high-dimensional projection pursuit I: general theory'] Recall $s$ and $s_\delta$ from 
\eqref{e:s.sqrt.fn} and \eqref{e:s.sqrt.fn.delta}.
  There exists $C=C(L)$ such that for all $t\in [q_0,1]$,
  \[
     \Big|s(t)
      -s_{\delta}(t)\Big|
  \le C\delta.
  \]

\begin{proof}
Since $p(q_0)\geq 1/L$ and $p$ is increasing, we have
\[
  s(t) + s_\delta(t) \ge s(t) \ge L^{-1/2}\,.
\]
By adjusting $C$ appropriately it suffices to show
  \[
     \Big|s(t)^2
      -s_{\delta}(t)^2\Big|
  \le C\delta.
  \]
Note that
$s_\delta(t)^2$ is the average value of $s(t)^2$ on the interval $[t_\delta,t_{\delta+}]$:
  \[
  s_\delta(t)^2
  = \frac{t_{\delta+} p(t_{\delta+})
    -
    t_{\delta} p(t_{\delta})
    }{\delta}
    = \frac{1}{\delta}\int_{t_\delta}^{t_{\delta_+}}
    (tp)'(t)\,dt
    = \frac{1}{\delta}\int_{t_\delta}^{t_{\delta_+}} s(t)^2\,dt\,.
  \]
By the mean-value theorem, it suffices to show that $s(t)^2=(tp)'(t)$ is Lipschitz, which is clear since assumption (\ref{i:IAMP-main-p}) of Theorem~\ref{thm:IAMP-main} gives that  $\|p\|_{C^2([0,1])}\leq L$.
    \end{proof}

body:
Let E be finite and f: 2^E -> R symmetric (f(S) = f(E \ S)) and submodular. With the posimodular slack P(A, B) = f(A) + f(B) - f(A \ B) - f(B \ A) and the submodular slack D(X, Y) = f(X) + f(Y) - f(X n Y) - f(X u Y), P(A, B) = D(A, E \ B) for all A, B, so f(A) + f(B) >= f(A \ B) + f(B \ A), with equality exactly when submodularity is tight at (A, E \ B). No normalization or monotonicity is needed. Symmetry cannot be dropped: on E = {1, 2}, f(empty) = f({1}) = f({2}) = 0 and f(E) = -1 is submodular, and A = E, B = {2} gives f(A) + f(B) = -1 < 0 = f(A \ B) + f(B \ A).
E is finite
f is real valued on all subsets of E
f(S) = f(E \ S) for every S
f is submodular

[Theorem 2 of arXiv:2609.01540, '2609.01540'] There exist constants \(\epsilon_0(n)>0\) and \(C(n)<\infty\) with the
following property. For every \(0<\epsilon<\epsilon_0(n)\), there are a
smooth exterior region \(E_\epsilon\subset M\) and an
orientation preserving diffeomorphism
\[
 \Phi_\epsilon:E_\epsilon\longrightarrow
 \Omega_\epsilon\subset\mathbb R^n
\]
onto a Euclidean exterior region. In the asymptotically flat coordinates,
\[
 \Phi_\epsilon(x)=x+o(r),
 \qquad
 d\Phi_\epsilon=\operatorname{Id}+o(1)
 \quad\text{as }r\to\infty.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \mathcal H_g^{n-1}(\partial E_\epsilon)
 \leq C(n)
 \left(\frac{m}{\epsilon}\right)^{\frac{n-1}{n-2}},
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{\Omega_\epsilon}
 \bigl|(\Phi_\epsilon^{-1})^*g-\delta\bigr|_\delta
 \leq C(n)\sqrt{\epsilon}.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Theorem 2 of arXiv:2609.01540

[Lemma lem: Solutions Near P_4 of arXiv:2608.30443, 'On smooth holosphere solutions to compressible Euler equation'] Assume (equation eq: Parameters of the paper). Let $\sigma_3<\sigma^*<\sigma_2$ and $w_u(\sigma)$ and $w_d(\sigma)$ be the upward and downward flow solutions respectively to (equation eq: Autonomous System of the paper) with the data $w(\sigma^*)=w_2^-(\sigma^*)$. Then:\\
 \vskip .3pc
\noindent{\em 1. Downward flow}: $w_d\in C^\infty((0,\sigma^*])$ and
 $$
 \mathop{\rm lim}_{\sigma\downarrow 0}w_d(\sigma)=0.
 $$
 Moreover, $\sigma\to 0$ corresponds to $x\to +\infty$ and there exist $(w_\infty,\sigma_\infty)\in \Bbb R\times \Bbb R_+^*$ such that
\begin{equation}

\left|\begin{array}{l} 
\sigma_d(x) = \sigma_\infty e^{-rx}\left(1+\mathcal O_{x\to\infty}(e^{-rx})\right),\\
w_d(x) = w_\infty e^{-rx}\left(1+\mathcal O_{x\to\infty}(e^{-rx})\right).
\end{array}\right.
\end{equation}
{\em 2. Upward flow}: $w_u\in C^\infty((\sigma_3,\sigma^*])$ and 
\begin{equation}

\left|\begin{array}{l}
\forall \sigma_3<\sigma<\sigma^*, \ \ w^-_2(\sigma)<w_u(\sigma)<w_2(\sigma)\\
\mathop{\rm lim}_{\sigma\downarrow  \sigma_3}w_u(\sigma)=w_3,
\end{array}\right.
\end{equation}
see Figure (fig: Phase Portrait of the paper). (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)

[Corollary 21 of arXiv:2609.02850, 'Canonical-row Chern flow on Bott--Samelson towers:\\ realizable-volume models for Schubert'] For a vector bundle $E$, put
\[
 \lambda_u(E)=\sum_{j=0}^{\rk E}[\wedge^jE]u^j\in K^0(Y)[u].
\]
Under the hypotheses of \cref{thm:chern-flow},
\begin{equation}
 \lambda_u\!\left(\bigoplus_vF_v^{\oplus b_v}\right)
 =
 \prod_v\lambda_u(F_v)^{r_v}
 \prod_e\lambda_u(E_e)^{\kappa_e}.
\end{equation}
In particular, the specialization $u=-1$ gives an equality of
$K$-theoretic Euler classes.  This identity is formal at the level of
$K^0$; the realizable-volume conclusion still uses the actual globally
generated bundle on the left and its Chow top Chern class.

[Conjecture thm:convergence of arXiv:2606.03079, 'Mean Field Limits for Stochastic, Underdamped Reactive Langevin Dynamics Models'] The sequence of measure-valued processes $\{\mu^{\gamma, \ell}_t\}_{t\in [0, T]}\in \mathbb{D}_{M_F(\mathbb{R}^{d\times d})}[0, T]$, converge in law to $\{\bar{\mu}^\ell_t\}_{t\in [0, T]} \in C_{M_F(\mathbb{R}^{d\times d})}([0, T])$ for $\ell=1,2,3$, satisfying
{\small
\begin{align}
\left \langle f,\bar{\mu}^{1}_{t}\right\rangle
&= \left \langle f,\bar{\mu}^{1}_{0}\right\rangle + \int_{0}^{t} \left \langle \mathcal{L}^{\ast}_1f, \bar{\mu}_{s}^{1}\right\rangle ds -\int_{0}^{t} \left \langle f(\xi_1) \left \langle K_{+}(\xi_1,\xi_2),  \bar{\mu}_{s}^{2}(d\xi_2) \right\rangle,   \bar{\mu}_{s}^{1}(d\xi_1)\right\rangle ds \notag \\
&\quad\quad + \int_{0}^{t} \left \langle K_{-}(\xi_3)\left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^{2d}} f(\xi_1) m_{-}(\xi_1,\xi_2|\xi_3) d\xi_1 \, d\xi_2 \right) , \bar{\mu}_{s}^{ 3}(d\xi_3) \right\rangle \, ds  \\
\left \langle h,\bar{\mu}^{3}_{t}\right\rangle
& =  \left \langle h,\bar{\mu}^{3}_{0}\right\rangle + \int_{0}^{t} \left \langle \mathcal{L}^{\ast}_3 h, \bar{\mu}_{s}^{3}\right\rangle ds- \int_{0}^{t} \left \langle h(\xi_3) K_{-}(\xi_3) , \bar{\mu}_s^3(d\xi_3) \right\rangle \, ds \notag \\
&\quad\quad+  \int_{0}^{t} \left \langle  \left \langle K_{+}(\xi_1,\xi_2) \left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} h(\xi_3)m_+(\xi_3 | \xi_1, \xi_2) d\xi_3\right), \bar{\mu}_s^1(d\xi_1) \right\rangle , \bar{\mu}_s^2(d\xi_2)\right\rangle \, ds \notag
\end{align}
}
with $\left \langle g,\bar{\mu}^{2}_{t}\right\rangle$ satisfying an equation symmetric to $\left \langle f,\bar{\mu}^{1}_{t}\right\rangle$. (Stated as a conjecture by the paper; open unless the paper says otherwise.)

[Lemma 3 of arXiv:2506.16259, 'Two-dimensional Rademacher walk'] Let $d_1,d_2,d_3\dots$ be a sequence of distinct positive integers, and let $T_k=d_1\eps_1+\dots+d_k\eps_k$ where  $\eps_i$ are i.i.d.\ Rademacher. Then for every integer $\displaystyle  m\ge \max_{1\le i\le k}d_i$ and every  $M\in\Z$ we have
$$
\P(T_k-M\equiv 0\pmod m)\le \frac{C \log k}{k}    
$$
for  some universal constant $C>0$.

On {-1, 1}^n (n >= 1) with the uniform probability measure mu, chi_S(x) = prod over i in S of x_i for S inside [n], and f^(S) = E[f chi_S] is the Walsh-Fourier coefficient of a real function f, so f = sum over S of f^(S) chi_S. For real f put W_f(S) = sum over x of f(x) chi_S(x) = 2^n f^(S). Then sum over S of W_f(S)^2 = 2^n sum over x of f(x)^2, equivalently sum over S of f^(S)^2 = E f^2. For h = 1_A, A any subset: W_h(empty) = |A|, sum over S of W_h(S)^2 = 2^n |A| and sum over S of h^(S)^2 = mu(A); every W_h(S) is an integer congruent to |A| mod 2 with |W_h(S)| <= |A|. For f with values +-1 and n >= 1, sum over S of W_f(S)^2 = 4^n (so sum over S of f^(S)^2 = 1) and every W_f(S) is even; on the one-point cube n = 0 the single sum W = f(empty word) is odd. Own work draft; proof (unaudited), no novelty established. For the equal-weight teacher q_a=(1/3)sum_j N(a E u_j,I_d), where d>=2, E^T E=I_2 and u_j are the unit equilateral vertices, unrestricted physical unit-step population DDPM mean GD admits a fast centroid/slow shape decomposition. Write M=a b 1^T+a sqrt(3/2) Z V^T, V=sqrt(2/3)U^T, P=EE^T, gamma=2a^2/3. On ||b||<=11, ||Z||<=5, b_+=(I/3+(2a^2/3)ZZ^T)b+O(a^4) and Z_+=Z+gamma[(P-ZZ^T)Z+2bb^T Z+O(a^2)]. For ||b_0||<=10 the centroid impulse in shape is O(a^2); the covariance-flow comparison error through rescaled time S is at most C a^2(1+||b_0||^2)exp(76(S+1)). Set sigma_0=1/(80 sqrt(d)), S=10 log(100/(sigma_0 rho)), and choose a^2<=c rho exp(-76(S+1)) with c and rho sufficiently small absolute constants. At N=ceil(3S/(2a^2)), the unrestricted trajectory enters a fixed equilateral tube, with normalized centroid O(a^4). For iid mean initialization N(0,3a^2/(2d)), entry with surrogate angle away from the three unstable sectors has probability at least 553/1600. In that tube the full normal error contracts by 1-kappa a^2 per step and the tangent perturbation is quadratic in the normal error. This is a dynamic lemma; an empirical learning guarantee is not asserted here.

canonical mixture-score DDPM population objective at one fixed noise time
unrestricted mean parameters; physical Euclidean unit GD step
d>=2, sufficiently small fixed tube radius rho and absolute constant c
a at the stated inverse-polynomial scale; real arithmetic

{"artifact_digest":"sha256:6d39032b1739aca3943b901fde292ae0b0b1d25d12d0379c33b897387d9da88f","artifact_path":"objects/sha256/6d/6d39032b1739aca3943b901fde292ae0b0b1d25d12d0379c33b897387d9da88f.md","bundle_digest":"sha256:673f95530dab2b490a9c4f0489c157cf47df9ca849c157d7423e598879b06cc7","bundle_entry_key":"t309-c10","bundle_id":"population.t309-free-centroid-ddpm-entry-normal-tracking-draft","claim_kind":"lemma","conditions":[],"domain":"Gaussian mixture learning and diffusion objectives","draft":"w721/bundle_006.json","evidence_ids":[],"logical_id":"math:probability.learning:equilateral-gaussian-mixture-ddpm-free-centroid-entry-normal-tracking","overlay_schema_version":1,"proof_text":"Own work draft; T309-w721-C10 v2, proof (unaudited), Target 2.

# Fast centroid relaxation releases the centering constraint in the equilateral DDPM route

This is a dynamic lemma toward the named random-initialization target. It builds on C06's free-centroid expansion and C07--C09's equilateral centered route, rather than rechecking those results. All these claims remain unaudited. The present lemma treats a centered true equilateral teacher but imposes no centroid constraint on the learned means or their initialization.

## 1. Coordinates and exact GD metric

Use the notation of C07: U is the 2-by-3 unit equilateral vertex matrix, E^T E=I_2, P=EE^T, V=sqrt(2/3)U^T and c=sqrt(3/2). Every unrestricted mean matrix has a unique decomposition

    M=a b 1^T+a c Z V^T,
    b=M1/(3a), Z=MV/(ac).

The squared Euclidean metric on means is

    ||dM||_F^2=3a^2||db||^2+c^2 a^2||dZ||_F^2.

For the exact population DDPM excess risk F_a(b,Z), physical unit-step mean GD is therefore exactly

    b_+=b-(1/(3a^2)) partial_b F_a,
    Z_+=Z-(2/(3a^2)) grad_Z F_a.                     (1)

Taking a unit step directly in b coordinates would describe a different algorithm and would miss the fast centroid rate.

## 2. Fast centroid and its impulse during covariance entry

C06 Section 5 gives, after substituting C_V=ZZ^T/2,

    F_a(b,Z)=a^2||b||^2
       +a^4[||ZZ^T-P||_F^2/4-b^T ZZ^T b]+a^6 H_a(b,Z). (2)

On ||b||<=11, ||Z||_F<=5, the remainder and any fixed finite number of parameter derivatives are bounded by absolute constants independent of d. The reason is the same finite-span Gaussian/softmax differentiation bound used in C05--C07; increasing the fixed b bound to 11 changes constants only. No analyticity assumption is needed, only the smooth Taylor remainder. We use (2) as settled input from C06, with its metric now included dynamically.

Set gamma=2a^2/3 and f(Z)=(P-ZZ^T)Z. Equation (1) becomes

    b_+=(I/3+(2a^2/3)ZZ^T)b-(a^4/3)partial_b H_a,
    Z_+=Z+gamma[f(Z)+2bb^T Z-a^2 grad_Z H_a].       (3)

For a sufficiently small absolute a and ||Z||<=5,

    ||b_+||<=||b||/2+C a^4,
    ||b_k||<=2^(-k)||b_0||+2C a^4.                 (4)

In particular initial ||b_0||<=10 keeps ||b||<11, conditional only on the shape ball. The dependence of H on b does not invalidate (4), since its b derivative is uniformly bounded throughout this ball.

Compare the Z iterates with the covariance flow of C07, on its stopped radius-5 ball. The extra forcing is bounded by C||b_k||^2+C a^2. Let e_k be the factor error and retain C07's L=76 for the leading flow. Its Euler defect is Cgamma^2. Then

    e_{k+1}<=(1+Lgamma)e_k
                    +Cgamma a^2+Cgamma||b_k||^2+Cgamma^2. (5)

The transient centroid term has total impulse

    gamma sum_{k>=0} 2*4^(-k)||b_0||^2
       =(8/3)gamma||b_0||^2=O(a^2||b_0||^2).       (6)

The constant floor in ||b_k||^2 is O(a^8). Its contribution to the geometric-series bound in (5) is O(a^8 exp(Lk gamma)), not a factor exponential in a^(-2). Thus

    e_k<=C a^2(1+||b_0||^2)exp(Lk gamma).           (7)

The usual constant-forcing geometric series also absorbs the O(a^2) remainder and Euler defect. Choosing the absolute constant in C07's bound a^2<=c rho exp(-76(S+1)) smaller accommodates ||b_0||<=10 and makes (7)<=rho/4 through N=ceil(3S/(2a^2)). The stopped bound closes induction: the exact flow has norm at most 4 and the error is less than 1, so no Z exit occurs. Together with (4), neither coordinate leaves its assumed ball.

At N, b_N=O(a^4); indeed 10*2^(-N)<=C a^4 for the specified small a and S>=1. Consequently the unrestricted means enter the same equilateral tube as C07, with an additional normalized centroid error O(a^4). The fast centroid transient changes the entry estimate by an absolute constant, not a dimension-dependent exponent or a long-time instability factor.

## 3. Gaussian initialization and its entry angle

Initialize all 3d mean entries independently as N(0,3a^2/(2d)). Orthogonal right projection onto span(1) and its complement gives Z_0 with iid N(0,1/d) entries and b_0~N(0,I_d/(2d)). In particular E||b_0||^2=1/2, so

    P(||b_0||>10)<=1/200.

Combining with C07's good centered-factor event G, of probability at least 2/5, by a union bound gives

    P(G and ||b_0||<=10)>=79/200.                  (8)

Independence follows as well from orthogonal Gaussian projections, but is not needed for this probability bound. The joint event is invariant under rotations in the teacher plane, acting simultaneously on b_0 and Z_0. The surrogate factor flow is rotation-equivariant and its planar polar factor exists on G. Thus the argument of C08 gives a uniform surrogate entry angle conditional on this joint event, in either determinant branch. Excluding delta=pi/24 neighborhoods of its three unstable angles removes exactly fraction 1/8. Hence the simultaneous entry-and-angle event has probability at least

    (79/200)*(7/8)=553/1600.                       (9)

Actual unrestricted GD inherits the small angular error via (7); its own objective has no assumed continuous rotational symmetry. The extra b_N term is normal to the equilateral subspace and does not change the projected angle.

## 4. Normal contraction for unrestricted mean parameters

Use normalized Euclidean coordinates J=M/a and the same two-dimensional equilateral linear subspace L as C08, now inside all d-by-3 mean matrices. Exact population GD preserves L. The simultaneous teacher rotation, cyclic label permutation and perpendicular reflection used in C02 still have L as their fixed space even when free means are allowed. In particular the family has zero centroid without requiring the optimization to enforce one.

Write J=v+w, v in L, w perpendicular to L. In a small fixed tube, v has radius r in [0.9,1.1] and ||w||<=rho_0. Decompose w into its centroid and centered-shape parts, using orthonormal coordinates u=sqrt(3)b and Y=cZ for the whole normalized mean space. The physical mean Hessian restricted to normal directions has blocks

    H_cc=(2/3)I+O(a^2),
    H_ss=a^2 A+O(a^2||w||+a^2||b||^2+a^4),
    H_cs=O(a^2||b||+a^4),                           (10)

where A has a dimension-independent positive lower bound and finite upper bound by C05's centered normal Hessian estimate. The centroid block follows from a^2||b||^2 in (2) and the factor 3 of the metric. The b-dependent quartic term contributes O(a^2||b||^2) to the physical shape block and O(a^2||b||) to the cross block. The sixth-order remainder contributes O(a^4). These estimates hold along normal segments within the tube.

Choose rho_0 small and then a small. Completing the square in the centroid block, whose inverse is uniformly bounded, shows that the cross-block Schur correction is O(a^4||b||^2+a^8), smaller than the positive order-a^2 shape block. Consequently, for absolute kappa>0,

    kappa a^2 I <= H_normal <= (9/10)I.             (11)

For the upper bound, the leading centroid eigenvalue is 2/3, all shape eigenvalues are O(a^2), and all remaining blocks vanish as a decreases. Bounds are in physical Euclidean mean coordinates; a single crude global Lipschitz-square estimate is not used to select the step.

Since normal gradient vanishes on L, its value at v+w equals the integral of the normal Hessian applied to w along v+t w. In physical coordinates the unrestricted unit-step normal update is therefore (I-Hbar_normal)w, with the integral block Hbar satisfying (11). Rescaling to J preserves the inequality. Hence

    ||w_+||<=(1-kappa a^2)||w||                     (12)

as long as the radial annulus and tube are retained. The unit physical step is admissible because the largest normal eigenvalue is below 1, despite the unequal centroid and shape time scales.

## 5. Tangent forcing remains quadratic

In J coordinates, use rescaled step a^2 and vector field g_a=-a^(-4)grad_J F_a. It contains a large linear centroid term of order a^(-2), so its full derivative is not uniformly bounded as a->0. However that term is entirely normal: its tangent projection onto L is identically zero. The tangent part and its first two derivatives are uniformly bounded. This follows from (2): after projection and division by a^4, the divergent centroid quadratic disappears, the quartic polynomial has bounded derivatives, and the remainder is O(a^2) with its derivatives.

Invariance of L and self-adjointness of the gradient Hessian imply Pi_L Dg_a(v)w=0 for normal w, just as in C08. Taylor's theorem applied to the tangent projection therefore gives

    ||Pi_L g_a(v+w)-g_a(v)||<=C||w||^2.             (13)

Equations (12),(13) are precisely the normal-decay and summable-tangent-forcing inputs to C08, after replacing its fixed coordinate constants by the J metric constants. They close radial confinement by the same inward leading field (1-r^2)r. Their accumulated angular impulse is O(||w_0||^2), since a^2 sum_k (1-kappa a^2)^(2k) is bounded. An a^(-2) loss from the fast centroid is not present in (13).

## Scope and audit priorities

This lemma establishes entry, entry-angle probability and full normal tracking for unrestricted means in the equilateral population case. A learning corollary is recorded separately to keep this dynamic statement distinct from its empirical concentration extension. The centered teacher, known radius, equal weights, identity covariance and equilateral geometry remain assumptions. No extension to the anisotropic trap C06 or general triangles is implied.

The least trusted steps are uniform remainder derivatives for bounded free centroid, the metric and accumulated transient in (3)--(7), and the physical-coordinate Hessian bounds (10)--(13). Exact polynomial checks can test their finite algebra only; no independent PASS or novelty finding is recorded.","release_manifest_digest":"sha256:c2890e8a61a7647f868d72341f59eff40df43d81cc19a057eadc961fc48b3af5","revision_digest":"sha256:6ce3ef4a977b35e41518277aab29962778f98dab10b5309ce032bf407965eaca","source_id":"own-work:T309-w721-C10-v2","source_revision":"2026-10-20-v2-unaudited","statement_fidelity_reviewed":false,"supersedes":[],"trust_class":"curated_secondary","truth_status":"unverified"}

body: In computational complexity, problems that are in the complexity class NP but are neither in the class P nor NP-complete are called NP-intermediate, and the class of such problems is called NPI. Ladner's theorem, shown in 1975 by Richard E. Ladner, is a result asserting that, if P ≠ NP, then NPI is not empty; that is, NP contains problems that are neither in P nor NP-complete. Since it is also true that if NPI problems exist, then P ≠ NP, it follows that P = NP if and only if NPI is empty.
title: NP-intermediate

[Proposition 55 (Optimality of the $\ell^1$ convolution bound) of arXiv:2602.14618, 'Finitary coding and Gaussian concentration\\ for random fields'] Let $b=(b_m)_{m\in\mathbb Z^d}$ be a nonnegative, absolutely summable kernel
on $\mathbb Z^d$, with
\[
\|b\|_1 := \sum_{m\in\mathbb Z^d} b_m < \infty.
\]
For any finitely supported vector $\delta=(\delta_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}$,
define the quadratic form
\[
Q(\delta) := \sum_{k,\ell\in\mathbb Z^d} \delta_k\,\delta_\ell\, b_{\ell-k}.
\]
Then
\[
\sup_{\delta\neq 0} \frac{Q(\delta)}{\|\delta\|_2^2} = \|b\|_1.
\]
Moreover, this supremum is asymptotically attained by block indicators:
if $\delta^{(L)}_k := \1_{\{k\in\Lambda_L\}}$ with
$\Lambda_L := [-L,L]^d\cap\mathbb Z^d$, then
\[
\lim_{L\to\infty}
\frac{Q(\delta^{(L)})}{\|\delta^{(L)}\|_2^2}
=
\|b\|_1.
\] (Proof in the paper; no proof environment follows the statement in the TeX.)
title: Optimality of the $\ell^1$ convolution bound

body: Record of outside readings, 14 October 2026, of Y. Shmalo, A nonergodic flow rule with Galton-Watson stationary measure (repository yspennstate/nonergodic-galton-watson-flow-rule, commit 837dd0c8da7d), which answers Lyons-Peres Question 17.18 negatively. Two readers working from fresh clones without seeing each other, one a Claude model and one a Codex model, both found the argument correct, with no fatal or major finding. They agree on the question's wording and location (Probability on Trees and Networks, 2016 hardback p. 572; Question 3 of Section 10 of Lyons, Pemantle and Peres 1995), that a flow rule may send zero flow to a child (strict positivity is the extra hypothesis of Proposition 17.17), on d_1 = 5/16 and d_2 = 1849/8192, and that GW(.|C = 0) and GW(.|C = 1) are the two ergodic components; one reader also checked stationarity on all Borel sets, the other simulated 333,300 finite trees to depth 15 with no bias after the flow step (a biased control was detected). Minor findings: 'stationary' should allow sigma-finite measures; the step from Borel coordinates to a Borel flow needs one sentence; the repository's check script reports failures but exits with status 0. The n-ray example of Exercise 17.22 gives only absolute continuity, so it does not already answer the question, and a web and arXiv search found no earlier answer (Rousselin 2017/2018 assumes strictly positive child masses). Not refereed.
title: Outside readings of the nonergodic Galton-Watson flow rule (Lyons-Peres Question 17.18), 14 October 2026: two independent readings find it correct

body:
Let X be a real random variable with characteristic function f(t) = E exp(itX) and Q(X; l) = sup_x P(x <= X <= x + l). For all l > 0 and a > 0: Q(X; l) <= (96/95)^2 max(l, 1/a) int_{|t|<a} |f(t)| dt. With a = 1/l: Q(X; l) <= (96/95)^2 l int_{|t|<1/l} |f(t)| dt. Consequently, if int |f| < infinity, X has a density bounded by (96/95)^2 int |f| (Fourier inversion gives the better constant 1/(2 pi)).

Assumes: any real random variable; l > 0, a > 0
